## The swarm lane's lag hunt (2026-10-07): a latency probe, pprof, the party-match relist, and three stalls

The user's report against the Mac mini under 7,000 swarm bots: "sometimes the server lags" (also
outside Jangan), and "nothing in party matching". Unnumbered: other lanes hold the next numbers.
All measurements are LOCAL: own server and own Postgres on the 16-thread box, the Mac's settings
(`-full-map`, which turns `-single-frame` on, so every player shares one "world" bucket; 65,321
monsters alive; monster AI, aggro, battle; `-persist-position`), 3,000 bots on the plaza with
`-walk 10`. The production server and swarms were not touched. Another lane's swarm was loading the
same box (load average about 12), so the small numbers are noisy.

- **Party matching was empty because nothing renews an entry.** An entry expires 61..62 minutes
  after its registration or last change (`party.Matcher.Sweep`, READ SM 0x4504c0) and the owner is
  told nothing: the ShardManager sends only 0x386f to its GameServer, which has no case for it; ours
  sends nothing at all. The swarm listed once. Now each bot (`cmd/swarm/relist.go`) re-sends its own
  entry unchanged as 0x706a every 52..58 minutes, which renews its time; 0xb06a [2][0x2c1c] means
  gone and the bot lists again (0x7069); a party dissolving (0x3864 kind 1) or the bot leaving one
  (kind 3, its own JID) triggers the same check 3 s later. Tested end to end against the real
  handlers with the Matcher's clock moved (`TestListerRelistsAfterExpiry`). A running swarm keeps
  the old behaviour until restarted with the new binary.
- **Party matching was O(entries^2) under the party Hub's lock.** `Hub.ListingOwner` scanned every
  listing, and the page builder (each 0x706c) and the 60 s sweep called it once per listing. At
  10,000 entries: a page 339 ms and a sweep 222 ms, before; 3.9 ms and 1.8 ms with an entry index
  (`Hub.byEntry`; `TestSweepOfManyEntriesIsLinear`). The monster AI tick takes that lock inside its
  own (`linkAggro`), so the monsters waited too. A real client opening the party-matching window
  paid the page cost per page; the sweep that expired a crowd's entries together paid it once.
- **A periodic per-player stall: the position save sat in front of the click's echo.** Two probes
  in separate processes both spiked to 8-13 ms exactly every 30 s, each on its own phase: the move
  handler's `savePositionEvery` (two Postgres commits, `-persist-position`) ran before the 0xB021
  echo and the watchers' messages. Moved after them (destmove, the old position stream, the skill
  move); the 30 s spikes are gone. Against the Mac's remote Postgres (192.168.5.25) under a crowd's
  load, each is two network round trips plus two commits, up to the 5 s timeout: a walking player
  felt it every 30 s.
- **A crowd leaving at once stalled every player.** `world.Hub.Leave` copied every entity in view
  (about a kilobyte each with slice growth) under the world's write lock: 0.80 ms and 3 MB a
  disconnect at 3,000 in one window, 2.08 ms and 8 MB at 7,000 (`BenchmarkLeaveInCrowd`). The swarm
  killed (all 3,000 sockets closing in one second) gave the probe a **742 ms** round trip, and 21
  GCs in that half minute against 3-4. Leave now returns only who watched (`[]world.Watcher`,
  sized up front): 53 us and 48 KB at 3,000, 124 us and 112 KB at 7,000; the same kill gave the
  probe **218 ms and 85 ms** (two runs). An arrival's snapshot is sized up front too: Enter at
  7,000 is 0.58 ms and 1.9 MB.
- **Steady state is not where the lag is.** 3,000 in view, 300 walking: probe p50 0.10-0.12 ms,
  p99 1-11 ms, max 13 ms, no round trip over 200 ms in ~15 minutes; 3,000 arriving at 100 a second:
  max 7 ms. Server 1.6 cores, two thirds of it socket writes; GC every 8-10 s with 0.05-6 ms
  pauses at a 400-600 MB heap; scheduler latency p99 3-5 ms, max 25 ms (the box shared). The 60 s
  sweep, the nest scheduler and the mover pass did not line up with any spike.
- **Left as a write-up** (not contained fixes): under `-single-frame` each blow on a monster, each
  respawn push and each ground-item event scans every player in the world twice
  (`monsterWatchers` -> `EntitiesInZone`, plus an AOI lock per player); the 100 ms AOI, regen and
  AI ticks each copy every entity (`AllEntities`, about 2 MB at 7,000, 30-40 times a second);
  a burst of N disconnects in one window is still N^2 despawn sends (the work is inherent; the
  lock hold is now 17x shorter); regen and party updates run per-character Postgres reads serially.
- **Tools.** `swarm probe` / `up -probe` (one bot in region 98/171, a field with no nest three
  regions from the plaza, clicking every 250 ms; p50/p99/max every 10 s and a `SPIKE` line per
  round trip over 200 ms). `-pprof-addr` / `OPENSRO_PPROF_ADDR` (off by default; pprof, mutex
  sampling, and a `runtime stats` line every 30 s). Both in deploy/README.md.

## Seven-hundred-and-forty-ninth round: moving by destination, as retail does (0x7021 / 0xB021 / 0xB023)

The full notes are in `docs/rounds/r749.md`. There were three reviews in `r749_review.md`: the review,
the exploit fixes, and an honest-play verification.
- **Retail (READ, both binaries):**
  - The client sends one 0x7021 per click: `01|region u16|i16 x,y,z` in a field, three i32 in a
    dungeon, or `00|cmd|u16 angle` for a sky run.
  - The server's `GObjPC::FUN_004b0ea0` refuses silently on its gates: the 5.0 gate, the 3x3
    regions, and the stopping states `0xc1|0x4000`.
  - An accepted move is answered with one 0xB021 to the 3x3 window, the mover included.
  - 0xB023 (`FUN_004a9430`: uid, region, f32 xyz, u16 angle) is sent only when a step is
    blocked.
  - There is no position stream while walking.
- **Server (OURS where retail's navmesh is missing):**
  - Each mover has a leg, and a 250 ms pass refiles block crossings.
  - Stop reports and placements are bounded by a clock: they are measured from a server-held
    reference, with 9 units free and up to one second of run as an allowance.
  - A named point (arrival, gate, GM `/tp`) can be used once, within 2 minutes.
  - Height is measured from the last height the client gave.
  - A token bucket on 0x7021 (30/s, burst 60).
  - Server `/unstuck` 0x00B8/0x00B9 takes the player to the zone landing, on a 60 s cooldown.
- **Client:** `MoveOrderSync` sends one order per click. A missing echo stops the walk after
  1.0 s. A correction is never answered twice. Arrivals place themselves on the graph's height.
  `OtherWalk` walks others from 0xB021.
- **Bench (MEASURED, server CPU ms per simulated second):**

  | layout | 20 Hz positions | destination moves |
  |---|---|---|
  | 1000 town | 87,688 | 5,172 |
  | 1000 field | 14,332 | 872 |
  | 10k wide | 19,976 | 1,551 |

  Bytes fall 6-14x. The mover pass at 10k holds the hub lock 1.7 ms, against 53 ms before.
- **Reviews:** chained stops moved a character 1650 units in 8 ms, and the login spot gave a free
  recall. The honest-play verification found 60 Hz correction loops after `/goto hotan` under
  `-single-frame` (6,758 in 112 s), lag-spike snap-backs and `/unstuck` pinning. All are fixed,
  and the live runs show no loops.
- **Client crowd:** 1000 walking (`dest` step) is p50 52 / p95 60 ms. The height rays cost
  5.1 ms a frame (`landing_height_at`), and round 751 takes them on.
- **Version skew:** client and server ship together. An old client walks in snaps, and new
  observers see an old client's player move.

## Seven-hundred-and-fifty-second round: party matching only ever showed one page

The full notes are in `docs/rounds/r752.md`. The user, with thousands of swarm entries listed:
"It only ever lets you see 1 page".
- **Cause (MEASURED live, and in a probe):** `UiBuilder._build_spin` wired each arrow as
  `func() -> void: _spin_step(ctrl, step)`.
  - `_spin_step` is static and the lambda is made in an instance method. Godot 4.2.2 runs such a
    lambda with a null self.
  - So every click raised `Nonexistent function '_spin_step' in base 'Nil'`. No 0x706c was sent,
    and the window stayed on page 0.
  - The warehouse's page spin is built by the same function and was broken the same way.
- **Not the cause (READ and MEASURED):**
  - the server's pages (SM `0x450d20` / `0x451630`; 300 local swarm entries page 0..13 correctly);
  - the u8 request;
  - the client's count-then-index parse (`c:0x8841f0` → `0x97b930`: `+5` count, `+4` index).
- **Fix:** the arrows call `UiBuilder._spin_step`, qualified. The party-match window now treats
  the spin as the original's `CIFSpinButtonCtrl` does (READ):
  - a page sets only its top, count - 1 (`0x73b5b0` → `0x658010`), never its number;
  - a step drops the selection, then asks for the page (`0x732630`);
  - an open starts it at "1".
- **Tests:**
  - Go: `TestMatchListPagesOverTheWire`, 50 entries over the wire, pages 0, 1, 2 (the last), 3
    and 255.
  - GD: `_test_paging` (19 checks) and `ui_builder_test`'s `_check_spin_arrows_step`. Both fail
    on the old line.
  - Live: real clicks on the box page 0 → 1 → 2 → 1, and 13 → 12.

## Seven-hundred-and-fifty-third round: no other lambda calls a static with a null self, and a lint

The full notes are in `docs/rounds/r753.md`.
- **Census (MEASURED, two scanners over all of `client/scripts`):**
  - 355 lambdas; 19 call a static of their own class by the bare name.
  - 17 of those are made in static funcs, which work.
  - 2 are made in instance methods but also use the instance, so they work too:
    `World3D.gd:21181` and `hud_panels.gd:5973`.
  - **0 are broken.** Round 752's `_build_spin` arrow was the only one, so nothing needed
    qualifying.
- **Probe (MEASURED, bare 4.2.2 project):** a lambda captures self only when it names something
  of the instance: `self`, a member, a signal, a native member, `$` or `%`.
  - Still broken: a static var, a const, a captured local, a lua-style key, a parent's static, a
    class-level `var` initialiser, an inner class's method, and a nested lambda under a
    self-using one.
  - Never broken: a reference to the static that is not a call (`var c := f`,
    `f.call_deferred()`).
  - An inner class's bare call to its outer class's static is a parse error.
- **Lint:** `ui/static_lambda_lint_test.gd` scans 546 scripts in about 0.9 s. It self-checks on a
  snippet of 9 banned and 14 allowed forms. With round 752's bare `_spin_step` put back, it fails
  on `ui_builder.gd:1287`.
- Box `check` "checked 674 scripts and 9 scenes", ALL LOAD. `tests` "ran 259 suite(s), 0
  failing". No perf gate: only a test was added.

## Seven-hundred-and-fifty-eighth round: dual axes and set daggers drew all along; the look-ahead asked for files that do not exist

The full notes are in `docs/rounds/r758.md`.
- **The user's log** (v0.1.511) printed "item `axe_11.bsr` / `eu_axe_11_set_b.bsr` /
  `eu_dagger_11_set_a.bsr` ... not found in archive". The brief's guess was that axes were not
  paired as daggers are. That guess is **false**.
- **READ:** `CObjCharacter::FUN_00a5f4f0`, `icscriptobj::FUN_009e3890` and `FUN_0080b980` all
  pair `_l` / `_r` for TypeID 3/1/6 with TypeID4 9 or 13. A woman's harp (14) is `_f`. The folder
  plays no part, so `item\etc\weapon\eu_*` pairs too. `item_models` already had this rule.
- **MEASURED (Data.pk2):** every European axe and dagger and the four Egyptian set ones are
  `_l` / `_r` pairs. No plain `axe_NN.bsr` exists.
- **The cause:** `template_paths` (round 748) always listed each `_r`'s plain fallback, so the
  template task asked for a file that is not there and logged it. A real build printed the error
  and drew both halves (2 meshes, `dual_axe` / `dagger` group).
- **The fix:** the fallback is listed only once the `_r` / `_f` fails (`_prep_task`, `_prepare`,
  `build()`).
- **Census (`tools/census_weapon_models.gd`, 6640 weapon/shield item-sex pairs):**
  - Draw misses for items whose files exist: 0 before and 0 after.
  - Look-ahead asks for a missing file: 522 before, 64 after. The 64 are the
    `*_RARE_SWITCH23` rows naming `*_23.bsr`, which the archive lacks in every variant, and a
    woman's `_f` for harp 14/16/22, which retail tries first too.
- **Tests:** new checks in `character_appearance_test.gd` and `character_template_async_test.gd`.
  NEGATIVE: the old lines put back fail 4 checks. Box `check` ALL LOAD (675 scripts); `tests`
  "ran 259 suite(s), 0 failing".

## Seven-hundred-and-fifty-seventh round: the client used one core -- the engine's hidden per-frame costs

The full notes are in `docs/rounds/r757.md`; the review is `r757_review.md`. The user's live client
(RTX 5080, 32 threads) ran a 7,000-player crowd at 6-11 fps on 3% CPU and 10% GPU.
- **READ (Godot 4.2.2 `skeleton_3d.cpp`):** `Node.duplicate()` copies `animate_physical_bones` through
  its setter, which turns on the internal physics process. So 18,035 cloned skeletons got a
  callback every physics step, and a 100 ms frame ran 6-8 steps.
  `Skeleton3DBuilder.no_physics_step` turns it off.
- **Name plates:** `NamePlateBatch`, about 28 chunk meshes, replaces one `Label3D` per player, with
  retail's 300-unit rule applied in the shader.
- **Minimap:** `MinimapSigns` uses one MultiMesh per sign kind, pixel-identical (snapped).
- **Loops:** the per-body loops are event-driven, through the `_other_moved` funnel, an awake set,
  and a sound timing wheel.
- **Heights:** walkers' landing heights are computed on `WorkerThreadPool`.
- **MEASURED, RX 7600 at 1080p, everything on:**

  | | before | after |
  |---|---|---|
  | 7000 standing p50 | 99 ms | 16 ms (GPU 80% busy, from 11%) |
  | 3000 standing | 45 ms | 11.7 ms |
  | 1000 standing | 17.4 ms | 9.3 ms |

- **Errors:** `!is_geometry_instance` is fixed: it came from a CrowdGpu scratch built with
  `duplicate()`.
- **On 4.7.2:** every `Skeleton3D` processes every frame (38 ms at this scale). The upgrade must carry
  an equivalent fix.
- **Threaded rendering:** it crashes on 4.2.2 (an `AnimatedTexture` recursion), so it stays off.
- **Merged with 756:** ghosts keyed by holder for sound, batched plates, inside the far bounds.
- **Gates:**
  - box "ran 262 suite(s), 0 failing";
  - `perf_gate.sh --sites jangan,reeds,cross`: SAME everywhere.

## Seven-hundred-and-fifty-fourth round: SPIKE -- the client on Godot 4.7.2 (branch only, not merged)

The full notes are in `docs/rounds/r754.md`. The user's choice: try Godot 4.7.2-stable (released
2026-08-18, the newest stable) in place of 4.2.2. Branch `spike/r754-godot-4.7`; 4.2.2 stays
installed and pinned everywhere else.
- **Verdict:** upgrade after three things: Compatibility's colour (+6 to +12 luma in
  sunlit views) and its +17 % frame, the crowd on the default render thread (+4 ms at 1000-3000 and
  a Forward+ deadlock when the main thread waits on RID-making pool tasks), and a 4.7.2 heap
  corruption in `table_parity.gd`. On Forward+ the perf gate is 21-27 % faster a frame at all
  three views, entries 6-9 % shorter, none slower (MEASURED, base dev on 4.2.2).
- **The port (MEASURED):** a clean first import and `check`; 12 of 258 suites failed, all fixed,
  and the branch passes 258 of 258 on 4.7.2 AND on 4.2.2. The changes that matter for the game:
  - Skeleton3D out of the tree (4.4): a pose change no longer reaches the global poses, so the
    far crowd's bake would have frozen every far body (`Skeleton3DBuilder.refresh_global_poses`);
  - reversed depth (4.3): WorldFog's sky test and the cloud layer's far-plane pin;
  - LineEdit's editing state (4.4): Escape kept the keyboard and the next Enter sent nothing
    (`KeyInput.line_edit_as_42`);
  - every un-waited WorkerThreadPool task aborts 4.7.2 at quit, and the cursor's textures outlive
    the RenderingServer: every world session crashed on quit until the waits and the new
    `ShutdownRelease` autoload.
- **The 4.2.2 workarounds:** the const-array race, the static-call-from-lambda null self and
  `Node.duplicate()` off-thread are gone on 4.7.2 (MEASURED probes); the Compatibility back
  buffer too (round 707's test passes without the anchor); the opaque sort is not (READ).
- **Threading (round 757):** nodes and resources build on pool threads on 4.7.2 (4.2.2: 72,000
  thread-guard errors a run), but Forward+ on the default render thread deadlocks when the main
  thread waits on such tasks; the separate render thread crashes 4.2.2 and runs 4.7.2 at 15.0 ms
  with 1000 players standing (4.2.2's best 17.5).
- **Visual parity:** Forward+ the same picture (world views d8 <= 1.5 %); Compatibility brighter
  by 6-12 luma in sunlit views (OPEN).
- **Spike build for the user:** `/root/opensro-g472-spike/` on the render box (Linux and Windows
  zips, own settings folder, no auto-update).

## Seven-hundred-and-sixtieth round: the client on Godot 4.7.2 -- three blockers cleared, the separate render thread, CI switched

The full notes are in `docs/rounds/r760.md`. The spike (round 754) merged onto dev with round 759
(`d2e61a2a`) and dev `0dd4a583`; 4.7.2 is now the engine for CI, the release and the tools (4.2.2
stays on the box for older revisions through `GODOT_BIN`).
- **Compatibility colour (READ, MEASURED):** the cloud layer was pinned at Vulkan's reversed far
  plane, which under GL's clip space is depth 0.5 (drawn over the far scenery); and GLES3 uploads
  DXT1 as RGB from 4.6 (cut-out openings black). Pinned per renderer (`WorldFog.far_clip_z`) and
  decoded as under Forward+. World views within 0.6 luma of 4.2.2 (Samarkand was +11.8).
  RetailBloom's Compatibility anchor removed (4.7.2 keeps the back buffer's colour; box test PASS).
  Compatibility Jangan +0.15 ms (+6 %, was +17 %), not attributed (OPEN).
- **Skeletons:** every 4.7.2 skeleton has an internal PhysicalBoneSimulator3D modifier and an Idle
  modifier process, a deferred bone backup/restore per skeleton per frame. Manual mode on every
  built skeleton: 38.7 -> 6.9 ms a frame at 18,035 (MEASURED).
- **The deadlock (READ):** a pool thread's synchronous RenderingServer call waits for the main
  thread, which `wait_for_task_completion` blocks. `PoolWait` serves the queue while it polls; every
  main-thread wait uses it (lint). Probe: plain wait hangs 5 of 5, PoolWait finishes 8 of 8.
- **Heap corruption (READ):** two 4.7.2 `ustring.cpp` bugs (an unpaired lead surrogate leaves a
  string's last character uninitialised; encoding it overflows the heap). `TextDecode.utf16`
  (lint); `table_parity.gd` 3 of 3 PASS (2 of 2 aborts before).
- **The separate render thread, adopted for Forward+** (`thread_model=2`): 10 x 300 s crowd runs with
  arrivals, walking and real zone changes, 0 crashes. **Compatibility crashed on it** (3 of 5 swarm
  boots): every Compatibility route starts the default thread (override.cfg, launchers, the native
  probe's restart).
- **Round 759's review:** F2 (GLES3's half-float custom data drew the wrong far bodies past 2,048:
  37 % of the far box off before, 0 % after) and F3 folded in.
- **MEASURED against 4.2.2:** perf gate Forward+ Jangan 1.56 -> 0.75 ms, reeds 1.41 -> 0.81, cross
  1.73 -> 0.87, entries and freezes all shorter; swarm crowd standing 19.3 -> 9.8 (1000), 24.3 ->
  12.3 (3000), 33.2 -> 18.1 ms (7000). Not better: one spawn frame of a 1000-body arrival

## Eight-hundred-and-sixty-third round, lane T: turning on a click-walk direction change -- the turn already matched; a far re-click snapped before its echo

The user: "when abruptly change directions with click walking the original gives a fluid animation and
we just snap the model to the correct position. Check it for yourself and make it like the original."
Labels: READ (`c:` sro_client.exe), MEASURED, INFERRED, OURS, OPEN. Base `4ade3371` (v0.1.629).

### What the original does (MEASURED, per frame; READ where it says so)

Ground clicks at about 45, 60-70, 90-105, 130-135, 150-175 and 180 degrees from the way the body
faced, while running (speed 50), while walking (16) and from standing; the body's heading, position
and the mover's state each frame, and frames of the body.

| What | MEASURED |
|---|---|
| Turn rate | constant, 3 pi rad/s: 180 deg in 335 ms; 172.6 deg (walking) 318 ms; 152.8 deg 277 ms; 129.2 deg 242 ms; 117.3 deg (from standing) 236 ms; 90-105 deg 169-229 ms; 47-66 deg 92-171 ms. Each frame's step is that frame's time x 9.42 rad/s (0.217 rad on a 23 ms frame, 0.30 on a 32 ms frame); no easing at either end, the last step cut to land on the heading |
| Way round | the shorter one (a 220-degree change turned -140) |
| Path | the body moves along the NEW line from the first frame of the turn: no arc, no carry along the old path (READ, `c:FUN_009e02f0`: the travel direction mover +0x68 is set to the TARGET heading by `FUN_009ec850` on every call; only the drawn heading +0x8c steps) |
| When | on this player's own echo, 65-141 ms after the click on this link; the body runs straight on the old line until then |
| Walk / run / standing | the same rate in all three; from standing the body starts along the new line at once while it turns; a body that arrives before the turn ends goes on turning where it stands |
| The clip | the walk or run loop plays on through the turn (no restart, no other clip) |
| The camera | does not follow the turn: its yaw (camera +0x374) stayed 3.14 through runs and 180-degree turns |
| Another player's view | the same: an observer's copy turned 82 deg in ~180 ms at 3 pi rad/s and walked the new line at once, speed factor 1.0 |
| A far re-click | a second click within 5 degrees of a far (>= 100) destination, after the first click's echo and while the body is still turning, snaps the heading in one frame: 90.7 deg (1.47 -> 3.05 rad) in one frame, and the mover's point moves to the new click 30 ms after it (no round trip) |

READ (re-read this round; round 637 has the rest): `c:FUN_009e02f0` steps the heading by
`elapsed_ms x 9.42477798461914 / 1000` (0xde3128, 0xd83268) toward the target, the shorter way;
`c:FUN_009e0c10` calls it each frame while mover +0xa4 is set, with the object clock less mover
+0xa0; no per-model value -- the rate is the one .rdata constant. `c:UI_SILKMALL::FUN_009eb2a0`,
the ground click's filter, measures the click against the MOVER's destination (player +0x684 =
mover +0x1c, written by the echo's `FUN_009e0550` or the snap's `FUN_009e04b0`), and its snap
branch returns 0: the snapped click is not sent.

### What OpenSRO did (MEASURED, base, real clicks: `groundclick` through the viewport, lane server)

The turn was already the original's (round 637): `RemoteFacing.turn` at 3 pi rad/s, 9.0 deg a physics
tick, the shorter way, the path on the new line at once, the run loop playing on (QA MIX: no restart at
any direction change). Own player, 1280x1024: 180 deg 318-350 ms, 135 deg 234-265 ms, 90 deg 152-200
ms, 45 deg 68-99 ms; no frame stepped more than one tick's 9 deg. An observer (with 60 ms one way of
delay): 180 deg 326-333 ms, 135 deg 246-265, 90 deg 163-199, 45 deg 94-99, catch-up x1.00-1.04. One
difference from the original in when the turn starts: here at the click (OURS, round 749: the walk
starts on the click), there on the echo.

**The snap that differed.** A second far click within 5 degrees of the first, before the first one's
echo, snapped the body in ONE frame: 115.1 deg (63.0 -> 178.1) in one frame with no delay. This
client walks its click at once and measured the next click against `_move_target`, the click it
already walks; the original measures it against the mover's destination, which is still the OLD
order until the echo comes (READ above), so there the re-click is a turn. With a delayed link the
window is the whole round trip -- a quick double click in the new direction, the usual way to change
direction in a hurry.

### What changed

- `MoveOrderSync.mover_dest` (READ): the destination the original's mover holds -- every
  destination echo of this player's own 0xB021, or a snap's re-aim (`mover_snapped`); a heading
  echo, a stop or a placement clears it; an arrival keeps it.
- `World3D._click_rule_dest`: the ground click's filter (`RemoteFacing.click_rule`) measures a click
  against it, not the click already walked; a heading run keeps its own point (OURS, SkyRun).
- QA: `OPENSRO_QA_FACING_LOG_MS` (the facing report's interval; 0 = every frame).

### QA (render box, lane server 127.0.0.1:17631, real clicks, 60 ms one way through a delay proxy)

A run toward the camera, a far click straight behind (>= 100 away), and a second far click 3 ticks
(50 ms) later within 5 degrees of it, before the first one's echo (the echo came 126-131 ms after

| | base `4ade3371` | head |
|---|---|---|
| the re-click | measured against the click walked: "snap" | measured against the mover's (old) order: a turn |
| the body | 0 -> 27 deg in 49 ms, then **149.2 deg in one frame** (+73 ms) | 0 -> 176.2 deg at 9 deg a tick, on the new heading at +338 ms |
| other turns (180, 135, 90, 45, walking, from standing) | 3 pi rad/s | unchanged: 3 pi rad/s, no frame beyond one tick's 9 deg |

Without the delay (b6, base) the same re-click 7 ticks after the first also snapped (115.1 deg in one

## Eight-hundred-and-sixty-third round, the starting message: UIIT_STT_STARTING_MSG in the chat on entering the world

The user asked for the message the original shows in the chat every time the game is entered.
Labels: READ (`c:` sro_client.exe), MEASURED, INFERRED, OURS, OPEN. Base `4ade3371` (v0.1.629).

**READ.** `CGInterface::Create` (c:0x78c910) looks up `UIIT_STT_STARTING_MSG` (0x78cf1d, 0x8c9c30) and
calls 0x777c60(0xff, 0xffdbc99b, 1, text): `vswprintf` with the text as the format, then the chat
window (interface child 1, 0x8b51f0(1, 1)) gets it through 0x7aca30 as type 0xff -- a system line,
filed in all five lists (the All list through 0x64f8a0, the four tab lists through 0x7aab40), in
0xffdbc99b, RGB (219, 201, 155). The text is the archive's own (the English column of
`textuisystem`'s row); an archive without the row adds nothing.

**MEASURED** (1280x1024, entering the world): the message fills the chat as six rows of the row's
`\n`-separated parts. Each part after a break starts at the list's left edge with only its own
leading space -- no hanging indent -- while a part too long for the list (the first, "... in a great
journey") wraps with the usual 20 px hanging indent.

**Built.** `HudChat.add_starting_message` (the text, `%%` -> `%` as `vswprintf` prints it, type 0xff,
0xffdbc99b), called by World3D right after the chat window is set up. `HudChat.wrap` now starts a new,
unindented row at a line break (a real one or the table's written `\n`); rows without a break wrap
as before. Chat lines from the network still have their breaks removed first (`format_line`,
0x876930), so they are unchanged. Test `scripts/ui/hud/starting_msg863_test.gd` (ALL PASS):
all five lists, the colour, the rows, no break drawn, nothing without the text, the wrap indent;
`hud_chat_test` ALL PASS. UI-only: no perf gate.

**OPEN.**
- Whether the message is added again after a teleport (a zone change): `CGInterface::Create`
  carries a `snd_warp` branch, which suggests it also runs on a warp's arrival, but that was not
  measured; ours adds it once per world entry.
- A text ending in a break (the Korean column does) leaves an empty last row here; the original's
  handling of a trailing break was not measured.

## Eight-hundred-and-sixty-second round, lane U: the login ID box and the chat line -- the caret is the font's point size + 2 tall, and lands on the pixel its quad covers

The user asked whether the login's ID box centres its text, and for the chat input's caret, scrolling,
length limit and sent line to be checked against the original, typing lines longer than the box.
Labels: READ (`c:` sro_client.exe; `/var/tmp/decomp_client` and `/var/tmp/sro_client.asm` on the box),
MEASURED, INFERRED, OURS, OPEN. Base `a1034d2e` (v0.1.628). UI-only lane (no world drawing changed):
no perf gate. The server is untouched (the lane server is a build of this tree's).

**What the original does (MEASURED, 1280x1024, a character typed at a time; edit-local pixels).**
- **The login ID and password are centred** (pstitle's `GDR_EDIT_ID` / `GDR_EDIT_PASS`: 135x20,
  HAlign 1, VAlign 1, ClientRect 0): empty, the caret at x 68..69 -- the edit's centre, 67.5, on its
  pixel; each character keeps the text centred and the caret at its end. A line wider than `w - 5`
  (130) has its end held at 130 and the caret at 130..131 while typing; the start runs out of the box
  and the glyph crossing the edit's left edge is cut there (drawn in part). Home puts the start at 0;
  Right walks the caret to 40 px in, then the text moves a character a step under a caret held at 40;
  End puts the end back at 130; Left walks the caret over a still text; Backspace at the end keeps the
  end at 130 until the text fits again, then it is centred. Exactly round 860's rule (`TextLayout`,
  0x637b70) -- with the long-text arm the same for an HAlign 1 edit as for the chat line. The
  password draws one `*` per character by the same rule (its 22nd character, 132 px, is the first
  past 130). The ID took 36 characters and more (no limit near the box: the class's 512, round 848).
- **The caret is 11 rows tall** in every edit of FontIndex 0 measured: the login ID and password, the
  image-code box, character create's name, the chat line. Round 859 drew `tmHeight + 2`: 16 rows on
  the box's face (15 / 14 where the edit cuts it).
- **A half pixel goes right.** The empty ID's caret is at 68, not 67; after one character 8 px wide
  the text is drawn from 63 (63.5 truncated) and the caret at 72 (71.5's pixel), a pixel right of
  the glyph boundary; every password state (`*` 6 px: `135 - 6n` always odd) has its caret at the
  ceiling of `63.5 - 3n + 6n`. Whole-pixel lefts (an odd text width) put text and caret on the same
  boundary.
- **The chat line** (`GDR_CHAT_INPUTBOX`, 360x20, ClientRect 5,4,0,0, left aligned): empty caret at
  5, rows 4..14; the end of a long line at 355 (`5 + 355 - 5`), the caret there; Left x80 walks the
  caret to 45 (5 + 40) and then moves the text under it until the start is at 5; three Rights 5 -> 28;
  End back to 355; the 100-character limit holds (34 more characters typed after 80 changed
  nothing past the 100th; 100 Backspaces emptied it). Sent, the line reads `Name:text` (no space after
  the colon), cut at the 100th character, in (255, 174, 195), wrapped between words at the box's
  width, every continuation line indented by 20 px (the first line's ink at x 30, the continuations'
  at 50), 14 px a line; the input stays open with the caret at its start.
- **Other boxes:** character create's name (left aligned) takes 12 characters, its caret 11 rows;
  the image-code box: the same caret. The chat line's `/whisper` menu entry puts `$` in the chat
  line -- a whisper is `$name text` in the same edit (ours parses it the same way); no separate name box.

**What the original's code says (READ).**
- **The caret's height is the font's point size + 2.0, not tmHeight.** 0x637ec6 `fild [edx+0x4]`
  with `edx = [esi+0x11c]`, then `fadd` 2.0 (0xe1b898). The font object (0x4927b0 allocates 0x118
  bytes) is filled by 0xbaa110: `[0]` the index, `[1]` the size argument, `lfHeight = -MulDiv(size,
  96, 72)`, and each style's TEXTMETRIC from `+0x38` (`(i + 1) * 0xe` dwords; tmHeight first --
  0x8b3040 returns `[font + (style + 1) * 0x38]`, the empty caret's tmHeight). So `+4` is the point
  size. The font table (0x469350) builds indices 0..4 at 9, 8, 12, 11, 15 points (`push 9 / 8 / 0xc /
  0xb / 0xf`): 12, 11, 16, 15, 20 px, `UiBuilder.FONT_SIZES`. 9 + 2 = 11, the measured rows.
  INFERRED: that `+0x11c` is the edit's own font object (its `+4` read as the size gives exactly the
  measured height).
- **The caret's x and top are floats** (`local_c0` = `+0x370` + the advance, `local_a8` = `+0x374`;
  the quad's vertices are those floats), while the text board is drawn at their truncation (0x6356c0).
  The quad covers the pixels whose centres it holds, centres on whole coordinates: an edge on a half
  pixel takes the next pixel (MEASURED above; INFERRED: D3D9's rule for pre-transformed vertices).

**Built.** `TextLayout.caret_rect(origin, advance, point_size)` (the quad, point size + 2 tall),
`caret_pixels` (each edge to its ceiling), `point_size(px)` (the table; else px * 72 / 96 rounded,
OURS for a size no index has). `CifEdit.placement` keeps the text where it was (LineEdit's
truncated centre; the long-text rule) and works the caret from the unrounded left and top
(`left + (w - text w) * 0.5`, `top + (h - text h) / 2`; the empty centred caret from `left + w *
0.5`), through `caret_pixels`, `caret_points() + 2` tall. The alignment census measures carets the same
way (from the unrounded origin). Every edit takes it (the chat line, whisper / stall / guild /
login / name / amount boxes: all CifEdit).
New QA hook `OPENSRO_QA_FRONT_INPUT` (`QaFrontInput`, hooked in Login): keys, clicks
(`clickfield:<edit>`), `skipintro`, `snap` / `snapfield:<edit>:<name>` and `editstate:<edit>` on a
front-end screen, as `OPENSRO_QA_INPUT` plays them in the world.

**Real client (MEASURED).** Login: `qa_shot.sh --scene res://scenes/Login.tscn` at 1280x1024, real time
(30 fps), the intro skipped, a real click on the ID box, End, 40 Backspaces, then the same 89 states as
above, each with its `editstate` and six snaps of the edit 100 ms apart (`/var/tmp/r862u/qa862front.sh`,
`front_input.py`); the password the same with 22 `x`. Chat: lane server on 17621 (in memory, navmesh),
`Long862`, Enter, the 80-character line a key at a time, Left x80, three Rights, End, 34 more, Home,
End, 116 Backspaces, then the 114-character line sent (`qa862chat.sh`, `qa862chat_input.py`); each key
followed by `editstate:HudChat`, 16 states snapped six times. Measured in the frames (the caret by
the blink's difference between the snaps, the text by its ink), edit-local:

| State | Original | Base (`a1034d2e` + QA hook) | This branch |
|---|---|---|---|
| login ID empty, caret | x 68..69, rows 2..12 | x 67..68, rows 2..17 | x 68..69, rows 2..12 |
| login ID one character, caret | 72..73 (8 px glyph) | 71..72 (7 px glyph: whole left), rows 3..18 | 71..72, rows 3..13 |
| login ID 4 characters (26 px here: left 54.5) | -- | caret 80 | caret 81 (80.5's pixel) |
| login ID long, End / typing | caret 130..131, rows 3..13 | 130..131, rows 3..18 | 130..131, rows 3..13 |
| login ID Right from Home | caret held at 40 | held at 40 | held at 40 |
| password empty | 68..69, rows 2..12 | 67..68, rows 2..17 | 68..69, rows 2..12 |
| chat line empty / End / 40-in hold / Home | 5 / 355 / 45 / 5, rows 4..14 | same x, rows 4..19 | same x, rows 4..14 |
| sent line | `Name:` + 100 characters, (255,174,195), x 30, continuation x 50, 14 px pitch | the same, continuation ink at 48 (this face's 6 spaces) | unchanged |

Every caret's x on both sides follows the rule worked out from its own text width; the remaining
x differences mid-text are the faces' advances (below), not the rule.

**Every edit (MEASURED, TextAlignCensus, 1280x720 UI, Forward+ on the box; `/var/tmp/r862u/census/`).**
Base's edits measured by this branch's census (`b100`: base + the new TextLayout and census): **17 of
18 carets off** -- 16 rows where 11 are wanted (15 / 14 where the edit cuts it; party match's 11 px
name edit was already cut to 11), and the login ID's caret 1 px left (the half pixel). This branch
(`a100`, `a200`): 0 of 18 carets off at 100 % and 200 %; 393 texts and carets, 3 off (round 860's
three bold tabs' second pass, not a misalignment), as before.

**Gates.** `remote_godot.sh check` ALL LOAD (1138 scripts, 9 scenes); `tests` "ran 431 suite(s), 5
failing" with the box at a load average of 66-83 (other lanes' renders), each of
the five a timing-bound suite: run alone, `retail_gateway_test`, `crowd_ghost_test`,

**OPEN.**
- **The face.** The glyph advances differ by face (MEASURED: 'a' 8 px and `*` 6 px in the original's

  line and every mid-text caret x differ by the font, not the rule. Ours also accumulates fractional

  advances are fractional, Godot's shaping does not round per glyph. Not changed (a face-wide

- The text's vertical place against the original's: font-dependent (ascent), not compared.

## Eight-hundred-and-sixty-first round: the ride camels and the mule were white blobs -- their models are not in this archive; drawn from the trade twins (OURS)

The user: "the camel mounts are still white blobs" (after v0.1.627, round 860 lane H's horses).
Labels: READ (`c:` sro_client.exe; `/var/tmp/decomp_client` and an objdump of the exe on the box),
MEASURED, INFERRED, OURS, OPEN. Base `ba51c71a` (v0.1.627). Client-only; no server change.

- **What was drawn (MEASURED).** Not round 860's type-6 refusal: the model itself is missing.
  COS_C_CAMEL1..3 (2194-2196) and COS_C_DONKEY (2190, "Mule") name `cos\c_camel1..3.bsr` and
  `cos\c_donkey.bsr` (characterdata column 52). The box's Data.pk2 has no such file. It has only
  the trade transports' `Res\COS\t_camel1..3.bsr` (+ `t_camel1_2011`) and `t_donkey.bsr`
  (+ `_2011`), their meshes under `Prim\Mesh\COS\` and `...\cart\`, and their skeletons. Media.pk2
  has no `icon\cos\cos_c_camel1..3.ddj` / `cos_c_donkey.ddj` either. So `_cos_build_body` got no
  model and hung its untextured `CapsuleMesh` (state line `draw [@MeshInstance3D:CapsuleMesh{none}]`).
- **In service? (MEASURED, the box's Media.pk2 and server DB).** Yes. The rows and their scrolls
  (ITEM_COS_C_DONKEY 2136, ITEM_COS_C_CAMEL1..3 2140-2142) are in characterdata/itemdata, which
  hold only Service-1 rows (33,915 and 27,859 rows, all 1). The server's `_RefObjCommon` has them
  at Service 1 too. **But nothing in the original's data hands the scrolls out.** refshopgoods,
  refpackageitem and refscrapofpackageitem name only PACKAGE_ITEM_COS_C_HORSE1..3 (the five
  stables). No row of the server's drop tables (`_RefDropItemAssign`, `_RefDropItemGroup`,
  `_RefMonster_AssignedItemDrop`) names 2136 or 2140-2142. So this version's original never puts a
  ride camel or mule in the world (INFERRED: rows ahead of their models). OpenSRO hands them out
  only through its own Test Items NPC (round 783, OURS: the "Horses" tab's
  `^ITEM_COS_C_(DONKEY|HORSE[0-9]|CAMEL[0-9]|DHORSE[0-9])$`) and the GM `/give`. The rows are in
  service, so the server is unchanged; whether the test NPC should keep listing them is the user's
  call (OPEN below).
- **What the original does with a missing model (READ).**
  - The pick: a COS takes its row's model, or its Org row's when the row has none
    (CICCos::vslot_025 c:0x9c60b0), and loads it with GlobalDataManager::FUN_009c4ec0. That draws
    `res\mob\china\mangnyang.bsr` (c:0xde1f90) only when no model came back; an empty path loads
    nothing (CCObjAnimation::FUN_00a5b4b0). COS_C_CAMEL1's Org is `xxx`, so there is no Org model.
  - A named `.bsr` that is missing goes through Map::FUN_009fe760's `r` case, then
    CResourceMgr::vslot_004 (c:0xbedc40), then ResourceMgr::FUN_00bedba0. It is looked up in the
    cache (FUN_00beacc0), then loaded (FUN_00bed8d0). When the file does not open, the loader
    returns 0, and FUN_00bedba0 asserts `"%s Loading Failed."` (ResourceMgr.h line 0x7d) for every
    type but 5 (the item type returns 0 quietly).
  - The assert is fatal in this build. Without a debugger its flags are 0x501 (0x52a in the
    `DAT_00eecc14` mode); both are set by FUN_0049e450 at c:0x8328c0. Assert_FileLineExpression
    (c:0x49e490) then calls its logger at c:0x830da0, which logs and then executes
    `mov byte [0], 0` (c:0x830dda): an access violation that goes to the crash handler (c:0x832110).
    Had it returned, bits 2 and 4 clear take `ExitProcess(0)` (c:0x49e7b3). Every assert returns
    AL = 0 (c:0x49e7bb), and the caller's `int3` follows. 0x52a throws a C++ exception at the top.
  - No step tries another name: no `_2011` variant, no `Org` path for a non-empty cell, no other
    directory, no trade model. The original client, given a ride camel from this archive, stops.
  - OPEN: the very first load of a name runs through a callback FUN_009ef120 reads at run time,
    `[0x1103d87+0x1c]`. Its object sits in .bss and is referenced only by the three `mov ecx,
    0x1103d87` in FUN_009ef0c0/FUN_009ef2f0, so the setter was not found. Map::FUN_009fe760 is the
    builder for every later instance (round 756's chain).
- **Census (MEASURED, every characterdata row, the client's own pick: column 52 piece 0, else the
  Org row's, `res\` prefixed, against the 73,139-file Data.pk2 listing).**

  | kind | model present | model MISSING | `.cpd` present | no model |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | COS | 5,166 | **4** (COS_C_CAMEL1..3, COS_C_DONKEY) | 2 | 2,100 (guild soldiers, own branch) |
  | monster | 1,999 | 0 | 5 | 5,600 (thief/hunter list) |
  | NPC | 342 | 0 | 1 | 0 |
  | siege | 2,526 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
  | structure | 46 | **25** | 0 | 0 |
  | player | 52 | 0 | 0 | 0 |

## Eight-hundred-and-sixtieth round, lane T: a long line in an edit, drawn where the original draws it

The user asked for round 859 lane C's remaining open text item: "the original's long-text rule in
edits is read and in `TextLayout` but not drawn". Labels: READ (`c:` sro_client.exe; the decomp dump
and `/var/tmp/sro_client.asm` on the box), MEASURED, INFERRED, OURS, OPEN. Base `ca24154b`
(v0.1.625). UI-only lane (no world drawing changed): no perf gate.

**The rule, read again in full (READ, CIFEdit's draw `c:0x637b70`, CIFEdit and CIFEInputChatBox
slot 13).**
- It keeps **no scroll**: every frame the draw starts from the text rect (0x652800: the control's
  `+0x40` rect less the ClientRect), puts the text by HAlign / VAlign (round 859), then, for a
  single-line edit (style bit 0x40 clear, 0x637d7c):
  - `w - 5 < text w` (0x637d85..0x637da3: `fild w - 5`, `fcom` against the text board's width,
    taken only when below; **strictly** wider -- round 859's "at least" was one pixel loose, and at
    exactly `w - 5` the alignment's own left stays): the text's end goes to `left + w - 5` and its
    left to that minus its width (0x637da5..0x637de3), whatever the alignment and the caret.
  - The caret's x is then the text's left + 0x8b3820's sum of cell advances before the caret
    column (+1 while an IME composition is open, 0x634c50).
  - When the text's left is left of the rect (`fcomp`, 0x637efb) **and** the caret x is at most the
    rect's left + 40 (the integer `left + 0x28`, 0x637f04..0x637f1a), text and caret move right by
    `min(rect left - text left, rect left - caret x + 40.0)` (the double at 0xe1b8f8;
    0x637f1c..0x637f6f): the caret ends exactly 40 px in, or the text's start at the rect's left,
    whichever is the smaller move.
- So, step by step: **typing at the end** keeps the end at `w - 5` and the caret on it (`w - 5`,
  the quad to `w - 3`). **Left** walks the caret left over a still text until the caret is 40 px
  in; from there each Left moves the text right by that character's width and the caret stays 40
  px in, until the text's start reaches the rect's left; then the caret walks on to the start.
  **Right** from Home: the mirror -- the caret walks to 40 px in, then the text moves left a
  character a step until its end is back at `w - 5`. **Home** puts the start at the left at once;
  **End** the end at `w - 5` at once. **Backspace / Delete** at the end: the end stays at `w - 5`
  and the start comes in; once the text is no longer wider than `w - 5` it is drawn by its
  alignment again. **Focus in / out** change nothing (the rule reads no focus). **An empty edit**
  has no text width: round 859's empty-caret rule. **A password**: the text board holds '*' per
  character (0x636330 with style 2), so the rule measures the mask.
- **Where it is drawn (READ).** The board is drawn at the left and top truncated (0x6356c0:
  `_ftol` = `cvttsd2si` of `+0x370` / `+0x374`, 0xb42d10) -- whole pixels. The whole draw is inside
  a viewport of the **edit's own rect** (0x6531a0 with 0xb8f420's `+0x40` rect, set before the
  draw; 0x653220 sets the full screen back after), so a glyph crossing the edit's edge is cut there
  and drawn in part, and the ClientRect's inset (the chat line's 5 px at the left) shows the
  scrolled text. INFERRED: that a D3D9 viewport clips pre-transformed (XYZRHW) UI quads -- the
  draw sets it around exactly this.
- **IME (READ / OPEN).** The composition is in the edit's buffer, drawn in the text at the caret,
  the caret one column after it (0x634c50). Its underline (0x637b70 from 0x6380bb: type 3 per
  clause -- 0 dotted 0xff969696, 1 a white bar, else a grey line; otherwise one white line from
  the composition's start to its end) takes its x from 0x635580 plus only the `w - 5` move
  (`+0x1c`, the `_ftol` delta at 0x637dda), not the 40 px pull-back; its y adds the font's `+0x38`
  and a second `+0x44` that was not traced through: OPEN, not drawn.

**Built (one place: `CifEdit`).** LineEdit's scroll has no setter, so CifEdit hides LineEdit's own
drawing (`self_modulate` alpha 0) and draws on an internal child (`CifEditInk`, `clip_contents`:
the original's viewport -- the edit's width and the layout's height, since Godot holds an edit at
least a line tall: party match's 11 px name edit stands 17 px, and the original cuts its 16 px caret
at 11): the edit's art box (normal / read-only, once: Godot's

truncations; round 859's 0 px); a long text by `TextLayout.edit_scrolled_left` on the text rect
(`rule_span`: the laid-out ClientRect, else the content margins), with the text's extent in whole
pixels (ceil, INFERRED: the GDI board's width is whole) and the left floored when the rule moved
it. The caret quad, `caret_rect()` and the new `text_left()` come from the same placement. Colours
are read from the edit's theme each draw (font / uneditable / placeholder / selected / selection),

### 2. The guild war mark (`client/scripts/effects/guild_war_mark.gd`; server `pcspawn`, `guildplate.go`, `guildwar.go`)

- **The unidentified call** (READ, round 859's OPEN): vtable slot 43 (+0xac) is `c:0x9c7a60`, which
  returns byte +0x50d -- the job state (4 no job suit). So: in the at-war set, no suit, no fortress war
  -> on; not in the set -> off; a suit or a fortress war -> left as it was (the original's quirk, kept).
- **The set** (READ): 0x30EF {u8 op, u32 guild} (op 0 add, 1 remove), the spawn guild block's war
  flag and 0x30FF's (0 add, 1 remove), 0x3109 with any war (the own guild). "At war" is at war with
  anyone, not hostile to the viewer: a guild's members wear it for everyone, its own members included
  (the original; a player may not expect it).
- **Server bug fixed (READ s:0x4e5e27 / s:0x4ea4db):** the spawn's and 0x30FF's war byte is 1 for a
  guild with no war and 0 at war; OpenSRO wrote 0 for every guild (rounds 814-859), which the original

## Eight-hundred-and-sixtieth round, lane H: the white horse was a capsule -- a type-6 body is drawn from its model

Seen in rounds 856 and 859 (lane A): "the ridden horse draws as a white body in both base and head";
the user asked for it fixed. Labels: READ (`c:` sro_client.exe, `/var/tmp/decomp_client` on the box),
MEASURED, INFERRED, OURS.

- **What was drawn (MEASURED).** Not a material or texture fault: no horse model at all. The base
  client logs `ERROR: SkinnedBsrAssembler: cos\c_horse1.bsr is not a character .bsr (type 6)` and
  `COS ... Red Horse (COS_C_HORSE1, TypeID4 1) ... -- no model: a capsule`, and the COS state line
  (round 860's `draw [...]` census, below) names what is bound: `@MeshInstance3D:CapsuleMesh{none}`
  -- `_cos_build_body`'s fallback `CapsuleMesh` with no material, which Godot draws white. The same
  at summon, mounted, unmounted, in the owner's view and an observer's, for the ride horse and the
  trade horse (`cos\t_horse1.bsr`). None of the suspects (TextureType skin, BodyMirror,
  CharacterLook, BodyPulse, ObjectLight, crowd instancing, fade twins) was involved: the body never
  had a mesh to act on.
- **Why (MEASURED).** `BsrReader` marks a file a character only for object types 0 and 1, and
  `SkinnedBsrAssembler` refused anything else unless asked (`skinned_object`, round 838, used only by
  NPCs). The horse's `.bsr` writes **type 6**: one `.bmt` (slot 0), two skinned `.bms`, the
  `c_horse.bsk` skeleton (33 bones, with `saddle`) and six clips in `default`. Census of all 8,539
  `.bsr` in Data.pk2 (skeleton / none): type 0 167/7, 1 819/19, 2 90/2502, 3 20/337, 4 44/902,
  5 874/2547, 6 77/128, 8193 0/6. Joined against the tables: **10 COS rows** have a skeletal type-6
  model -- `COS_C_HORSE1..3`, `COS_C_DHORSE2`, `COS_C_UNICORN`, `COS_T_HORSE1/2`, `COS_T_CAMEL1..3`
  (every other COS is type 0 or 1; no pet is affected) -- and **70 monster rows** a skeletal type 3
  or 6 (44 the fortress hearts and tower-defence towers, 26 the treasure boxes and
  `MOB_EVENT_PANDORA`), all drawn as capsules too.
- **The original (READ).** The resource factory `ResourceMgr::FUN_00be9250` (c:0xbe9250) is a switch
  on the type word: 0 -> `FUN_00be8d50` (ResChar), **1, 2, 3, 4, 6 and 7 -> one constructor
  `FUN_00be8dc0`** (vtable 0xe0b670), 5 -> `FUN_00be8e20` (the item). The compound factory
  `FUN_00be92b0` puts 1, 3, 4, 5 and 6 in one class too. That object's loader
  `ResObject::FUN_00be41d0` reads the sound section through `FUN_00c0b740` whatever the type, and a
  compound animates whenever its resource has a skeleton and clips (`CCompChar::FUN_00c2b930`,
  BSR_FORMAT.md). So to the original a type-6 horse is a type-1 monster.
- **The fix.** `World3D._assemble_monster_model` -- the one assembler of monster, COS, monster-ride
  and mall-model templates (`MonsterDraw.Templates`, `MallModels`) -- passes `skinned_object`, so
  any `.bsr` with a skeleton is a skinned body; a skeleton-less one is still refused (OPEN below).
  `BsrReader` keeps a skeletal body's sound sets whatever its type (items excepted, as before). The
  type word itself is unchanged (`is_character` stays 0/1), so the player-body, select-screen and
  scenery paths are untouched. Rounds 795/796 (seat on `saddle`, the cart group, facing), 809 (its
  material slot: `material_for_slot`), 828 (`BodyMirror.apply` in `_cos_build_body`), 847 and 855
  run as they do for a type-1 COS.
- **QA (box, `/var/tmp/r860h/run860h.sh`, lane server 17360 with the navmesh; real input).** The
  user joins the traders at the doctor (round 805's steps), right-clicks the horse scroll (2137) in
  the bag, rides, presses Home (the ride is deleted), wears the trader suit (the QA equip hook: a
  right-click on a suit does not wear it), right-clicks the trade-horse scroll (2130), rides, Home
  (it stays). Rendered own view with a headless observer, and the reverse; base = ca24154b plus the
  QA census only.

  | | base, own | head, own | base, observer | head, observer |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | ride horse summoned | capsule | `model cos\c_horse1.bsr` | capsule | model |
  | its pieces (state line) | `CapsuleMesh{none}` | `c_horse_part1`, `_part2`: `ArrayMesh/skin{ShaderMaterial albedo_texture 512x256}` | `CapsuleMesh{none}` | the same two |
  | mounted: clip, box | -, 6.4 x 8.0 x 6.4 | `c_horse_stand01`, 7.6 x 25.3 x 25.5 | -, capsule | `c_horse_stand01`, 7.6 x 25.3 x 25.5 |
  | trade horse | capsule | `t_horse1_part1/2`, skinned, 512x256 each, `stand01` | capsule | the same |
  | unridden trade horse | capsule, plate `< Horse >` `*Merchy` | the model, the same plates | capsule | the model |

  No `SCRIPT ERROR` in any run. Frames for a human: `/var/tmp/r860h/keep/own_before_after.png`
  (ridden, ridden, transport ridden, transport unridden; base row over head) and
  `obs_before_after.png` (the observer's); logs `keep/{h,b}_{own,obs}.godot.log`, `.second.log`,
  `.server.log`; the census `keep/census.tsv` (paths, type, skeleton and clip counts; no game data).
  In the observer's head frames the horse fades in (the appear fade, round 847's) -- not a fault.
- **Test.** `world/ride_body860_test.gd` (synthetic data): a type-6 body parses with its skeleton,

  assembler takes it as a skinned object; the world's `_assemble_monster_model` assembles it and

## Eight-hundred-and-sixtieth round, lane S: return scrolls hold you in place again, as the original's server does

The user: "new bug that was reintroduced and needs be fixed before anything with its own release.
Return scrolls and similar items don't lock you from moving and they should". Labels as before.

**What the original does (READ, SR_GameServer.exe; `server/internal/session/scrollhold.go` and
`docs/protocol/return_scroll_cast.md` section 4, "The hold", have every address).** The PC's
message pump `GObjPC::FUN_004a8ad0` (from `CMainProcess::FUN_00413b30`) asks CGObjPC vtable slot
0x610 (`GObjPC::FUN_004aa310`, vtable 0xaf59fc) before slot 0x5e0 (`CGObjPC::DispatchClientMessage`
0x50eee0) runs any client message's handler. Slot 0x610 is the message filter `GObjPC::FUN_004296a0`
over the tables `RegisterValueListFilters` (0x427d90) builds: 17 groups (0xcc3fe4, 0x1c bytes each),
one per character state, each holding an allow list (kind 0) or a deny list (kind 1) of opcodes
per state value. The scroll state (`GetTeleportState`, chardata +0x10, 0x30BF kind 0xb) is group 11
(0xcc4118; 0x429814..0x429834), and its one record is **value 1, an allow list of 0x7025 (chat),
0x704C (item use), 0x705B (the cast's cancel), 0x7005 and 0x34BF** (0x429337..0x4293ab). So while a
return scroll, a reverse return scroll or the skin change casts, the move 0x7021, the arrow keys'
0x7023 / 0x7024, the action 0x7074 (attacks, skills, pick-ups, the trace) and everything else are
refused before their handlers: the moves silently, 0x7074 with 0xB074 {3, 0x4004} (`CGObjPC::
vslot_358` 0x4ecbc0 -> `HandleCharacterActionRequest_7074` with its refused flag). The thief-den
scrolls' value 2 has no record: not held. The client holds nothing itself -- the 0x30BF value it
stores (+0x7c0) has no reader (its getter 0x9db0a0 has no caller or pointer, MEASURED), and the
delay board's busy byte is not set for kind 0 (0x7b16d4, re-read) -- it walks only on its move's
echo, which never comes.

**What removed it.** Nothing in OpenSRO's history ever held a caster (searched: every commit and
WORLD_ISSUES round naming the scroll, rounds 778-859). The user asked for the lock in round 779
("During that progress bar you can't move or cast anything unless you cancel"); round 779 read the
0x7021 and 0x7074 handlers, found that neither asks the state, and concluded the original has no
lock -- an absence claim that stopped at the handlers and missed the filter in front of them. So the
lock the user remembers from the original was never built; this round builds it.

**OpenSRO.**
- Server (`scrollhold.go`, `scrollHolds`): while the session's cast has value 1, refused are 0x7021
  and a rider's 0x70C5 move (`moveByRequest`), 0x7023 / 0x7024 and a rider's commands 3 / 4
  (`arrowStop` / `arrowTurn`), OpMove's walked positions and stops (`handleMove`; a relocation
  passes), 0x7074 ({3, 0x4004}, `ActionHandler`), and OpenSRO's own OpAttack / OpUseSkill (the
  silent end, the 0x4004's equivalent). OURS: a refused move is answered with 0xB023 to the mover at
  the server's position (retail answers nothing; OpenSRO's client walks a click at once). The hold
  ends with the cast: its end (before the warp), the cancel 0x705B, a death.
- Client (`ScrollHold`, `World3D._scroll_hold`, OURS where the retail client relies on the server):
  this player's own 0x30BF kind 0xb value 1 shuts the move gate (`_own_move_blocked`: the ground
  click, the sky run, the trace walk), the arrow keys (`_arrow_send_allowed`, and a turn does not
  turn the body), the physics walk (an approach, a pick-up walk), attacks and skills
  (`_attack_monster`, `_attack_pvp`, `_cast_skill`, `_cast_on_character`). The state's 0, a zone
  change and a death release it. `partybot -watch` prints others' moves, stops, turns and scroll
  states (QA).
- OPEN: the rest of retail's allow list -- NPC talk, inventory moves, exchange, stall, pick-up within
  reach and pet commands are not held yet.

**Verification.**
- Server: `go test ./...` passes (one unrelated timing flake, `TestMonsterSpawnPushOffIsTheOldWire`,
  passed alone 3/3 and in the full re-run). `scroll860_test.go`: during a return scroll's cast a
  click, an arrow turn and stop, a walked position, a stop report and a 0x7074 are refused, each
  move answered with 0xB023 and the server's position unchanged with no leg, 0x7074 {3, 0x4004},
  the cast still running; after the cancel a click walks; the reverse scroll holds until its end;
  only value 1 holds. NEGATIVE: with `scrollHolds` forced false the suite fails.
- Client: `scroll_hold860_test.gd` 14/14 through World3D's own `_unhandled_input` (held: a ground
  click walks nowhere, arrows send and turn nothing, an attack neither walks nor waits, a sky run is
  ignored; released by the 0; state 2 holds nothing). `remote_godot.sh check` ALL LOAD (1124
  scripts); `tests` "ran 423 suite(s), 0 failing" on the final tree (an earlier run had
  `seated_spawn_test.gd` fail once under the 16-way load; it passed alone and in the re-run).
- Live (MEASURED, render box, `/var/tmp/r860s/qa860.sh q1`: the lane server on 17390 in memory with
  `-navmesh-dir`, no trusted positions; the client in `/var/tmp/opensro-r860s` driven by its own
  input -- a right-click on the bag cell, ground clicks, the arrow keys, the bar's cancel button;
  partybot Obs860 -watch beside it). The return scroll (30 s): the client at (-9.00, 790.00) before,
  and after the use, two ground clicks, Up held and released, Left held and released: still
  (-9.00, 790.00), facing unchanged, no 0x7021 / 0x7023 / 0x7024 sent (no MOVE send line), the server
  logged no leg, and the observer saw the scroll state 1 and no move, stop or turn. The cancel
  button: state 0 for both, then one click walked to (31.00, 791.00) (server leg -9,790 -> 31,791,
  the observer's WATCH move). The instant return scroll (5 s): a ground click and Up during it moved
  nothing; at its end the zone change put the client at the return point (9.00, -409.00) (the
  server's relocated claim taken there), and a click walked from it. Frames for a human:
  `/var/tmp/r860s/q1/snap/{held,moved,arrived}.png`; logs `q1.client.log`, `q1.server.log`,
  `q1.obs.log`.
- No perf gate: no world drawing changed (input gates and a server filter).

## Eight-hundred-and-fifty-ninth round, lane C: the chat caret, and every text box and caption, where the original draws them

The user: "looks like the cursor in the chat input field is too far to the left now. Can you please
[make] sure that and all other gui items are properly aligned?" Labels: READ (`c:` sro_client.exe;
`/var/tmp/decomp_client`, `/var/tmp/sro_client.asm` and the exe's `.rdata` on the box; layouts from
Media.pk2's resinfo there), MEASURED, INFERRED, OURS, OPEN. Base `deb95be4` (v0.1.624). UI-only lane
(no world drawing changed): no perf gate.

**Why the chat caret moved (MEASURED, real client, base).** Round 848 made the chat line a `CifEdit`
laid FULL_RECT over the authored `GDR_CHAT_INPUTBOX` with `StyleBoxEmpty` styles: no inset at all. Its
text and caret started at the box's left edge (INFERRED why "now": the plain LineEdit before 848 kept
Godot's default box with its own content margin, not measured here). Lane server on 17350, `Caret859`, real Enter, typed
"hello there", Home, three Rights, End, eleven Backspaces (`/var/tmp/r859c/qa859.sh`), each state
measured in the frame (`textalign:HudChat`, below): base, 100 % and 200 % UI scale alike, **text and
caret 5 px left and 1 px high, the caret 2 px short** (14 against 16) at every column (0, 3, 11, empty).

**What the original does (READ).**
- **The text rect** (`c:0x652800`): the control's rect moved in by `+0x18c / +0x190` and shrunk by
  `+0x18c + +0x194` / `+0x190 + +0x198`: the ClientRect's left, top, right, bottom (round 630).
  `GDR_CHAT_INPUTBOX` (ifchatviewer.txt): Rect 38,378 360x20, **ClientRect 5,4,0,0**, HAlign 0,
  VAlign 0, FontIndex 0.
- **CIFEdit's draw** (`c:0x637b70`, CIFEdit and CIFEInputChatBox slot 13): the text's extent from the
  text board (`+0x4c`), then HAlign (`+0x88`) 0 left, 1 `left + (w - tw) * 0.5` (0.5 = the double at
  0xe1b7d0), 2 `right - tw - 2.0` (0xe1b898); VAlign (`+0x8c`) 0 top, 1 `top + (h - th) * 0.5`, 2
  `bottom - th` (0x637c97..0x637d64). An empty edit: VAlign 1 `top + ((h - tmHeight - 2) >> 1)`
  (0x637e54..0x637e7c), VAlign 2 `bottom - tmHeight` (0x637e3d). **The caret**: x = the text's left
  + 0x8b3820's sum of glyph cell advances before `+0x448` (plus one while an IME composition is open,
  0x634c50), quad x .. x + 2.0, from the text's top (plus the caret line's y) to + tmHeight + 2.0
  (0x637e80..0x637ee5, the quad 0x637f83..); blink as round 848 read.
- **A long single-line text** (0x637d85..0x637de3, 0x637ef1..0x637f6f): when its width is at least
  `w - 5`, its end is put at `left + w - 5` whatever the caret; then, while its start is left of the
  rect and the caret within 40 (the double at 0xe1b8f8) of the rect's left, it moves right by
  `min(rect left - text left, rect left - caret x + 40)`. In TextLayout (tested); not built (OPEN, below).
- **CNIFEdit** (`.2dt` edits, `c:0x47b5b0`, CNIFEdit slot 13): the same arms on its own fields
  (insets `+0x194..+0x1a0`, HAlign 2's 2.0, the w - 5 rule, the caret quad tmHeight + 2).
- **CIFStatic / CIFButton text** (`c:0x64d9b0`): as the edit, but HAlign 2 is `right - tw` (no 2.0).
- MEASURED, the archive's 93 edit records (CIFEdit 78, CIFEInputChatBox 15, all resinfo files): 60
  are VAlign 0, 33 VAlign 1, none VAlign 2; ClientRects 5,4,0,0 (the chat line and the supporter chat's)
  and 7,5,7,5 (9 message-box amounts, counts and coupon fields), the rest 0; the front end's (pstitle,
  pscharactercreate*, pscharacterselect*) are all VAlign 1.

**The fix, one place (CifEdit, OURS form of the READ rule).** `TextLayout` (new, `scripts/ui/
text_layout.gd`): the original's formulas, pure. `CifEdit.lay_out(client_rect, halign, valign)`: the
ClientRect and HAlign become LineEdit's content margins and alignment (HAlign 2 + 2.0); **VAlign by the
margins** (LineEdit only centres: a top-aligned text gets the room under it as bottom margin, kept on
every resize and font change, worked out for the authored rect so Godot's minimum never holds it
taller). The caret is drawn by CifEdit itself (`_draw`, `caret_rect()`): Godot's is transparent; ours
is the original's quad -- x from TextServer's caret on the same shaped text LineEdit draws (so it sits
on the drawn glyph boundary at every UI scale), 2 wide, from the text's top, tmHeight + 2 tall, hidden
until the first 200 ms flip after the edit takes the keyboard (READ 0x637b50). Every edit maker calls
it: UiBuilder._build_edit (the record's ClientRect, HAlign, VAlign), TwoDtBuilder (the record's
alignment; a `.2dt` record has no inset, zero INFERRED), the chat line (`lay_out_as` the authored box),
Login.style_login_edit, CharacterCreate's name. GDI's tmHeight is tmAscent + tmDescent and Godot's font
height ascent + descent of the same face: taken as equal (INFERRED).

**The census (MEASURED).** `TextAlignCensus` (new, `scripts/ui/text_align_census.gd`) measures where a
text is drawn against the original's rule from the frame itself: the frame with every text, with one
text hidden (its ink) and with the same string drawn by the census at the original's origin, same face
and size (the reference ink); the two inks' left / top / right edges are compared, so the face's own
bearings cancel. Edits also get their caret: the frame with it against one without, against the
original's quad. The rule comes from the archive's own record, found by name in the builder's parsed
layouts (not from what the node was given); labels with no record are measured by their own rect and
alignment (window captions, spin values) or over their control (`.2dt` texts, CNIFStatic's draw INFERRED
as CIFStatic's); a window that sets a label's alignment at run time (the party pane's leader name) is
measured against the alignment it set. `tools/window_text_census.gd` (new) opens every window
`window_hole_census.gd` opens (that tool now takes an overridable measure and scenario hook) plus the

The user: "setup a grafana/prom container on the .10.100 proxmox? Then let's add a bunch of
metrics/logs from the server so we can have full observability into it." The stack (CT 111
`monitoring`, 192.168.10.86: Prometheus, Loki, Grafana) was set up first (`62a4bf6b`); this lane is
the server's side, the dashboards and the alert rules. All OURS: the original has no such thing.
Server-only and deploy config; no client change, so no perf gate.

**Metrics (OURS).** `internal/metrics`, one private registry, served on `-metrics-addr` (env
`OPENSRO_METRICS_ADDR`, default `127.0.0.1:9469`, empty off) for Alloy on the prod host to scrape.
Every hot-path call is a pre-resolved counter/histogram child; no label names a player, and every
label is a fixed set. Placed at the chokepoints, not scattered:
- the gateway (`gateway.serveConn`, `dispatch`, `enqueue`, the writer): connections, disconnects
  by reason, send stalls by bound, bytes, packets by opcode and group, handler time and
  errors/panics by group, shared broadcast frames and their recipients. The **opcode label** is
  the hex of an opcode the code names, else `other`: `opcodes_gen.go` is generated from every
  `Op...` constant (`go generate ./internal/metrics`, 466 opcodes; `TestOpcodeTableIsCurrent`
  fails on a stale table), the group from the defining file (login, lobby, world, combat, item,
  economy, guild, social, quest, cos, gm);
- the world: players online by zone (scrape time; the zone is the named town, or in the one world
  frame the town whose centre region is nearest, a served dungeon, or other), entities by kind,
  legs started (`world.Hub.StartMove`), legs ended by a wall or the run limit (`AdvanceMovers`),
  claims taken / refused / refused_wall (round 857) / refused_state, corrections, warps by kind
  (`warpVia`'s path folded to 9 kinds), round 854's zone-change refusals by reason, deaths and
  revives, GM commands by verb;
- the loops: tick time histogram, overruns (a tick longer than its period) and the last tick's
  time for monster_ai, monster_aoi, cos, buffs, toggles, status, regen, mover, potions,
  ground_items and nest;
- combat and the economy: casts (`nextCastID`), blows and damage by target/source, monsters
  spawned/killed/removed (`combat.Hub`), ground stacks dropped/picked/expired, gold in/out (the
  character stores' `AddGold`/`DeductGold`), mall buys and silk, gacha draws, stall events,
  exchanges, lobby create/delete/restore;
- the database: `txn.OpenNamedPool` wraps the pgx connector once (`metrics.WrapConnector`), so every
  statement on the `stores` and `refdata` pools is counted by op and first table and timed, every
  transaction end counted, and `go_sql_*` exports each pool's stats; no store changed;
- faults: recovered panics by where, log lines by level (a counting slog handler), build info,
  start time, the Go runtime with the scheduler-latency histogram.

**Logs (OURS).** slog text (logfmt) kept. `err=` everywhere (about 60 `"error"` keys renamed);
`character` is a name and `character_id` an id (about 110 log calls that put an id under
`character` renamed); new one-line events: `login` (account, ip, result, never the password),
`entered world`, `left world`, `warp` (via, kind, from, zone), `lobby: character created/marked
for deletion/restored`; the gm package's `gm command` line gained `verb` and `character_id`.
`packet received` -- one INFO line per packet, most of the 847 MB prod log -- is DEBUG
(`-log-level`, env `OPENSRO_LOG_LEVEL`). `slog.SetDefault` routes the packages that log through
`slog.Info` and `log.Printf` into the same handler. Checked: no password, PIN, token or DSN in any
log call.

**Rotation: the server rotates its own file** (`internal/logfile`; `-log-file`, `-log-max-size-mb`
100, `-log-max-files` 10, `-log-compress` on). Chosen over newsyslog because launchd holds the stdout
file open: rotating it needs a rename plus a reopen the server would have to be signalled for, with
newsyslog's config in `/etc/newsyslog.d` (root), or a copy-truncate that races the writer. A file
the server opens itself rotates with no root and no signal; a file past the limit at boot is
rotated at once. launchd's stdout/stderr keep only a crash's stack.

**Dashboards and rules.** `deploy/observability/grafana/dashboards/opensro-server.json` (70 panels:
health tiles, players, gateway, loops, world, combat, economy, database, runtime; restarts
annotated) and `opensro-logs.json` (lines by level, ERROR/WARN by message, the live log filtered by
character/account/zone/level/search, logins, warps, GM, economy), generated by
`grafana/gen_dashboards.py`. `prometheus/rules/opensro.yml`: 13 rules (down, restarted, tick
overrun, loop stalled, slow ticks, error-log rate, handler errors, panics, DB errors, slow DB, pool
saturated, send stalls, scheduler latency), wired into `prometheus.yml` and mounted in compose.

**QA (MEASURED).**
- `go test ./...` passes; `GOOS=darwin GOARCH=arm64 go build ./cmd/server` builds. New tests: the
  metrics package (opcode table current, unknown opcodes share `other`, handler and loop
  histograms, overruns, teleport kinds, SQL labels, the driver wrapper against a fake driver,
  `/metrics` serving the families, the counting handler), the gateway (one session's packets,
  bytes, handler run and handler_error disconnect), the session (a login by result; a world
  entry, a refused not_gm and a granted zone change, packets by opcode and the scrape snapshot,
  over a real gateway), combat (spawn, damage, kill, removal) and the log file (rotation by size,
  keep N, gzip, an oversized file at boot).
- Lane server on the render box (`/var/tmp/r858o/srv858o.sh`: in memory, navmesh, the monster
  switches, `/metrics` on 127.0.0.1:17329, its own log file) with partybots
  (`/var/tmp/r858o/qa858o.sh`). Phase A (prod-like): Walker's walk loop, NotGM's zone change,
  BotGM's `/goto donwhang` and back, BotGM2's `/spawn`, `/notice`, `/hour`; A0 -> A1:
  logins ok +4, world entries +4, players_online 4 (zone jangan), sessions 4/4/4,
  move_legs destination +14, move_leg_ends wall +10, teleports gm +2, zone_change_refused not_gm +1,
  gm_commands goto 2 / level 2 / spawn 1 / notice 1 / hour 1, broadcasts 62 to 94 recipients,
  monsters_spawned +55,362 (the nests filling, 66,854 alive), every loop ticking (monster_ai 482
  ticks, p99 under 0.1 ms; nest p99 under 5 ms; 0 overruns); A1 -> A2 after the bots left:
  disconnects client_closed +3, read_error +1, connections 4 -> 0. Phase B (trust, the pick-up
  run, 3 kills): damage events +6 (3,093 HP), monsters_killed +3, items_dropped gold +3,
  items_picked player gold +3, gold in +469, claims taken +3.
- Lane server on this host against a scratch Postgres DB (`opensro_r858o`): statements by pool
  (`stores` 32 series, `refdata` 5 at boot), ops select/insert/update/delete/with/ddl, 11 commits
  and 1 rollback for one bot's account, character and world entry; `go_sql_*` for both pools; one
  db_errors (the bot's second register of an existing account, a real unique violation). A
  4 MB `server.log` at boot was rotated to `server.log.1.gz` at once.
- Grafana on .86: both dashboards provisioned in the OpenSRO folder; all 98 panel queries parsed
  by the live Prometheus and Loki (`/var/tmp/r858o/checkq.py`; no data yet: prod's Alloy is the
  user's); `promtool check rules`: 13 rules.

**What prod needs** (the user deploys): the new binary (`-ldflags "-X main.version=<tag>"`),
`export OPENSRO_LOG_FILE=$HOME/opensro/logs/opensro.log` in `run.sh`, Alloy tailing that file and
scraping 127.0.0.1:9469 with `job="opensro-server"`, `instance="prod"`; archive the old
`server.log` at the restart; on .86 `docker compose up -d` (the rules mount).

**OPEN.** The `gold_total` counter counts a credit inside an economy transaction that later rolls
back. A query's time is to the driver's first answer, not through the rows. Guild operations are
counted as the guild group's inbound packets, not by outcome. The dashboards were checked for
loading and query parsing, not against live data (none flows until Alloy runs on prod).

### What was built

**The kill orbs (`client/scripts/effects/exp_orbs.gd`, `ExpOrbs`; READ unless marked).**
- Who: 0x3056's handler `Client_ApplyExpAndLevelUp` (`c:0x8a97c0`) -- when the source object is in
  view and a CICharactor (`c:0xef1a5c`) -- adds `count_for(exp / unit)` to its byte +0x759 and
  `count_for(sp / 100.0)` to +0x75a. The unit is the player's level record's +0x28: RefParse_leveldata
  (`c:0x97aab0`) stores the sixth token (column 5, the exp unit) at the object's +0x30 and
  `FUN_00937f20` returns object + 8 (MEASURED 24 at level 1, 47 at 2, 5170 at 80).
- How many (`FUN_008a65b0`, from its x87 code): f >= 1: 10 at 64 or more, one fewer per halving,
  4 at [1, 2); below 1: `3 - int((1 - f) * 5.0)`, at least 1; at most 10.
- When: a CICNPC (`c:0xef1ac4`) launches at once; any other body at its DEAD state's event 100
  (`c:0xa59e30`), or at its destructor (`GlobalDataManager::FUN_009d2900`). 100 is the animation
  mixer's clip-end call (READ: `AniMixer::FUN_00c53e80` at `c:0xc53f01` / `0xc5400c` and
  `CCompChar::FUN_00c53c90` at `c:0xc53d87` call the owner's callback slot 0 with (100, the
  animation, 0)); that the DEAD state's argument is that one is INFERRED. MEASURED
  (`client/tools/census_die_events.gd`, 8,309 bodies under res\ in Data.pk2, 583 die clips): no die
  clip carries a key event of type 100 (2 carry a type 1), so it is no key event. So a monster's
  orbs leave as its die clip ends.
- Gate (`FUN_009cb7c0`): the display row's +0xd below 2 drops them (INFERRED Effect Quality, whose
  "See All Effects" is 2).
- The flight (`ICPlayer::FUN_009d9400`, `CICPlayer::FUN_009d8820`, the mover `FUN_009eaaa0` /
  `FUN_009eac50`, all from the x87 code): from the monster's `Bip01` (its position without one) to the
  player's `Bip01 Spine1` (`c:0xde2d18`; 10 above its feet without one, `c:0xe1b840`), re-aimed every
  frame; kept fly effects hwan_g (EXP) / hwan_y (SP); an angle of `(rand() % 120 - 60)` degrees; the
  start velocity away from the player, turned by that angle (its z takes the NEW x -- the original's
  arithmetic, kept), lifted `rand() % 400 / 1000 + 0.1`, normalised, `rand() % 25 + 50` units a
  second; a still wait of `rand() % 800` ms; then acceleration `k * 78.4` toward the player until the
  velocity's cosine to the aim passes `k * 0.5`, then homing at `k * 392` along half velocity, half
  aim (the aim itself above 0.93), arriving when a step reaches the target; past 2.2 s it homes
  straight, past 3.5 s it is there. `k = rand() % 400 / 1000 + 0.9`. On arrival the fly effect is
  freed at once (slot 2), hwn_blue / hwn_red_indraft plays at the point once, and
  `prim\snd\ui\hyanget.wav` there (the sound manager's +0x30 with 1.0).
- OURS: only a monster's orbs (a player or COS source is not drawn); the world's z is mirrored at
  the mover's edges (`to_orig`), so its turns come out as the original's.

**The hit's blood (`SystemEffects.blood_*`, World3D `_play_skill_hit_effect_on`).** READ
(`FUN_00a49290`'s disassembly, its stack arguments counted): inside the block that draws the skill's
DamageEfp -- entered when the display row's +0xd is not 0, the decoration has a DamageEfp and an
attacker -- a second effect is made with the same transform when the blood argument is set (cleared
for a kind-7 wall entry): the TARGET's characterInfo record +0x1c (`hiteffect\<BloodType>.efp`,
column 9) or, with the option byte +0x12e clear, +0x20 (`hiteffect\hit_2_greenblood.efp`, which the
parser `FUN_00a9ae80` fills for every row that names any). The argument is the skillaniset2 row's
+0xfa -- column 26, "피 나올래?" (blood?), stored `!= 0` by the loader `c:0x00a9c470` -- or 1 when the
decoration has no row (`FUN_00a4bdd0`); the end-of-cast apply (`IDecoSkill::FUN_00a4f720`) passes 1.
MEASURED: BloodType hit_2_redblood 862 rows, none 262, greenblood 116, stone 114, wood 63, ice 27,
