## Eight-hundred-and-fifty-eighth round, lane O: the server's metrics and logs, for Grafana

The user: "setup a grafana/prom container on the .10.100 proxmox? Then let's add a bunch of
metrics/logs from the server so we can have full observability into it." The stack (CT 111
`monitoring`, 192.168.10.86: Prometheus, Loki, Grafana) was set up first (`62a4bf6b`); this lane is
the server's side, the dashboards and the alert rules. All OURS: the original has no such thing.
Server-only and deploy config; no client change, so no perf gate.

**Metrics (OURS).** `internal/metrics`, one private registry, served on `-metrics-addr` (env
`OPENSRO_METRICS_ADDR`, default `127.0.0.1:9469`, empty off) for Alloy on the prod host to scrape.
Every hot-path call is a pre-resolved counter/histogram child; no label names a player, and every
label is a fixed set. Placed at the chokepoints, not scattered:
- the gateway (`gateway.serveConn`, `dispatch`, `enqueue`, the writer): connections, disconnects
  by reason, send stalls by bound, bytes, packets by opcode and group, handler time and
  errors/panics by group, shared broadcast frames and their recipients. The **opcode label** is
  the hex of an opcode the code names, else `other`: `opcodes_gen.go` is generated from every
  `Op...` constant (`go generate ./internal/metrics`, 466 opcodes; `TestOpcodeTableIsCurrent`
  fails on a stale table), the group from the defining file (login, lobby, world, combat, item,
  economy, guild, social, quest, cos, gm);
- the world: players online by zone (scrape time; the zone is the named town, or in the one world
  frame the town whose centre region is nearest, a served dungeon, or other), entities by kind,
  legs started (`world.Hub.StartMove`), legs ended by a wall or the run limit (`AdvanceMovers`),
  claims taken / refused / refused_wall (round 857) / refused_state, corrections, warps by kind
  (`warpVia`'s path folded to 9 kinds), round 854's zone-change refusals by reason, deaths and
  revives, GM commands by verb;
- the loops: tick time histogram, overruns (a tick longer than its period) and the last tick's
  time for monster_ai, monster_aoi, cos, buffs, toggles, status, regen, mover, potions,
  ground_items and nest;
- combat and the economy: casts (`nextCastID`), blows and damage by target/source, monsters
  spawned/killed/removed (`combat.Hub`), ground stacks dropped/picked/expired, gold in/out (the
  character stores' `AddGold`/`DeductGold`), mall buys and silk, gacha draws, stall events,
  exchanges, lobby create/delete/restore;
- the database: `txn.OpenNamedPool` wraps the pgx connector once (`metrics.WrapConnector`), so every
  statement on the `stores` and `refdata` pools is counted by op and first table and timed, every
  transaction end counted, and `go_sql_*` exports each pool's stats; no store changed;
- faults: recovered panics by where, log lines by level (a counting slog handler), build info,
  start time, the Go runtime with the scheduler-latency histogram.

**Logs (OURS).** slog text (logfmt) kept. `err=` everywhere (about 60 `"error"` keys renamed);
`character` is a name and `character_id` an id (about 110 log calls that put an id under
`character` renamed); new one-line events: `login` (account, ip, result, never the password),
`entered world`, `left world`, `warp` (via, kind, from, zone), `lobby: character created/marked
for deletion/restored`; the gm package's `gm command` line gained `verb` and `character_id`.
`packet received` -- one INFO line per packet, most of the 847 MB prod log -- is DEBUG
(`-log-level`, env `OPENSRO_LOG_LEVEL`). `slog.SetDefault` routes the packages that log through
`slog.Info` and `log.Printf` into the same handler. Checked: no password, PIN, token or DSN in any
log call.

**Rotation: the server rotates its own file** (`internal/logfile`; `-log-file`, `-log-max-size-mb`
100, `-log-max-files` 10, `-log-compress` on). Chosen over newsyslog because launchd holds the stdout
file open: rotating it needs a rename plus a reopen the server would have to be signalled for, with
newsyslog's config in `/etc/newsyslog.d` (root), or a copy-truncate that races the writer. A file
the server opens itself rotates with no root and no signal; a file past the limit at boot is
rotated at once. launchd's stdout/stderr keep only a crash's stack.

**Dashboards and rules.** `deploy/observability/grafana/dashboards/opensro-server.json` (70 panels:
health tiles, players, gateway, loops, world, combat, economy, database, runtime; restarts
annotated) and `opensro-logs.json` (lines by level, ERROR/WARN by message, the live log filtered by
character/account/zone/level/search, logins, warps, GM, economy), generated by
`grafana/gen_dashboards.py`. `prometheus/rules/opensro.yml`: 13 rules (down, restarted, tick
overrun, loop stalled, slow ticks, error-log rate, handler errors, panics, DB errors, slow DB, pool
saturated, send stalls, scheduler latency), wired into `prometheus.yml` and mounted in compose.

**QA (MEASURED).**
- `go test ./...` passes; `GOOS=darwin GOARCH=arm64 go build ./cmd/server` builds. New tests: the
  metrics package (opcode table current, unknown opcodes share `other`, handler and loop
  histograms, overruns, teleport kinds, SQL labels, the driver wrapper against a fake driver,
  `/metrics` serving the families, the counting handler), the gateway (one session's packets,
  bytes, handler run and handler_error disconnect), the session (a login by result; a world
  entry, a refused not_gm and a granted zone change, packets by opcode and the scrape snapshot,
  over a real gateway), combat (spawn, damage, kill, removal) and the log file (rotation by size,
  keep N, gzip, an oversized file at boot).
- Lane server on the render box (`/var/tmp/r858o/srv858o.sh`: in memory, navmesh, the monster
  switches, `/metrics` on 127.0.0.1:17329, its own log file) with partybots
  (`/var/tmp/r858o/qa858o.sh`). Phase A (prod-like): Walker's walk loop, NotGM's zone change,
  BotGM's `/goto donwhang` and back, BotGM2's `/spawn`, `/notice`, `/hour`; A0 -> A1:
  logins ok +4, world entries +4, players_online 4 (zone jangan), sessions 4/4/4,
  move_legs destination +14, move_leg_ends wall +10, teleports gm +2, zone_change_refused not_gm +1,
  gm_commands goto 2 / level 2 / spawn 1 / notice 1 / hour 1, broadcasts 62 to 94 recipients,
  monsters_spawned +55,362 (the nests filling, 66,854 alive), every loop ticking (monster_ai 482
  ticks, p99 under 0.1 ms; nest p99 under 5 ms; 0 overruns); A1 -> A2 after the bots left:
  disconnects client_closed +3, read_error +1, connections 4 -> 0. Phase B (trust, the pick-up
  run, 3 kills): damage events +6 (3,093 HP), monsters_killed +3, items_dropped gold +3,
  items_picked player gold +3, gold in +469, claims taken +3.
- Lane server on this host against a scratch Postgres DB (`opensro_r858o`): statements by pool
  (`stores` 32 series, `refdata` 5 at boot), ops select/insert/update/delete/with/ddl, 11 commits
  and 1 rollback for one bot's account, character and world entry; `go_sql_*` for both pools; one
  db_errors (the bot's second register of an existing account, a real unique violation). A
  4 MB `server.log` at boot was rotated to `server.log.1.gz` at once.
- Grafana on .86: both dashboards provisioned in the OpenSRO folder; all 98 panel queries parsed
  by the live Prometheus and Loki (`/var/tmp/r858o/checkq.py`; no data yet: prod's Alloy is the
  user's); `promtool check rules`: 13 rules.

**What prod needs** (the user deploys): the new binary (`-ldflags "-X main.version=<tag>"`),
`export OPENSRO_LOG_FILE=$HOME/opensro/logs/opensro.log` in `run.sh`, Alloy tailing that file and
scraping 127.0.0.1:9469 with `job="opensro-server"`, `instance="prod"`; archive the old
`server.log` at the restart; on .86 `docker compose up -d` (the rules mount).

**OPEN.** The `gold_total` counter counts a credit inside an economy transaction that later rolls
back. A query's time is to the driver's first answer, not through the rows. Guild operations are
counted as the guild group's inbound packets, not by outcome. The dashboards were checked for
loading and query parsing, not against live data (none flows until Alloy runs on prod).

**Why Help would not come back (MEASURED, base 09763587).** HelpWindow is a full-rect root with the
authored frame (`HelpFrame`, a HudWindow) inside. The frame's X runs `HudWindow._on_close_pressed`,
which hides the **frame** and emits `closed`; Help then hid its root. Every opener (H through
`_run_key_action("help")`, System > Help, the console's `/help`) called `open()`, which showed only
the **root**: the frame stayed hidden, so the second open drew nothing while the key log said "help
opened". The real client against the lane server (`/var/tmp/r858/qa858.sh before`, Help858, real
H and a real click on the X at (672, 62)): H opened it (frame 348), the X closed it, H then logged
`H -> help 9: help opened` and frame 548 shows no window; after Escape (System menu) H "opened" it
again and nothing showed.

**What the original does (READ).**
- H: `0x79f690` -- if child 0x20 (GDR_GAMEGUIDE) exists, `0x79b140(0)` and the helper `0x79a7e0`
  on the System window 0x62; else `0x79b140(1)` and the helper on the guide.
- `0x79b140(1)`: when the guide does not exist, builds the "GameGuide" registry section
  (`0x425ae0("GameGuide")`, `0x8b5580`), calls its slot 0x98, shows it (slot 0x5c) and runs the
  helper (snd_window_open); `0x79b140(0)`: hides it, the helper (snd_window_close), and **destroys
  it** (`0x8b59f0`). So every open makes the window afresh.
- The X: CIFMainFrame's close button -> vslot_043; `CIFGameGuide::vslot_043` (`0x765680`) is
  `0x79b140(0)`.
- Escape: `0x79d620` checks, after the System window and before the world map, whether the guide
  exists and is shown (`0x79d744..0x79d77f`: `0x8b51f0(0x20,1)`, `0xb8f530`) and calls its
  vslot_043, then the helper on 0x62. The base did not close Help on Escape (the hud_panels comment
  said so, "open").

**The fix (help_window.gd, World3D, hud_panels).** `open()` shows root and frame together, raises,
and -- when it was closed -- starts as a new window (the first tab, the first document at its top,
centred: OURS place, the original's is the registry rect) and sounds snd_window_open; `close()`
hides both and sounds snd_window_close; `is_open()` / `toggle()`. The X, H (`toggle`), Escape
(`HudPanels._escape_close`, after System and before the world map, through `help_window`) and
System > Help all go through them. Live after (`qa858.sh after`, the same steps plus `helpstate`):
open by H -> X (root false, frame false) -> **H reopens** (root true, frame true) -> tab 2 ->
Escape closes -> H reopens on tab 0, document 0 -> H closes -> Escape raises System -> its Help
button opens it. Frames: `/var/tmp/r858/evidence/qa_after/` (a_open1 .. g_system_help) and
`qa_before/`.

**The box at the side panel's top-left (READ).** The side panel is GDR_GUIDE_MENU, a CIFGGMenu.
Its Create (`CIFGGMenu::vslot_010`, `0x7685a0`) loads `resinfo\ifggmenu.txt` (`0x7685d9`/`0x7685fd`:
the scroll manager, TILE_2 and TILE_1 at 69,16 128x128), then makes **three tabs** with the window
factory (`0x7686c9`): class `0xee96c0` (CIFSelectableArea, the stall window's tab class), IDs
0x64 + i, at x = (i * 31) * 2 + 0xe, y 0xc, 0x3c x 0x18 -- (14 + 62 i, 12) 60 x 24 --, font 0,
art `com_tab_on.ddj` / `com_tab_off.ddj` (`0x768767`/`0x76878c`), tab 0 on (`0x64cc30(1)`),
captions UIIT_STT_GAMEGUIDE / UIIT_STT_GAMEEVENTGUIDE / UIIT_STT_QUESTGUIDE1 (`0x7687cd`,
`0x768813`, `0x76884c`; "Help", "Guide", "Quest" in the archive's English). A press on another tab

## Eight-hundred-and-fifty-seventh round: walking into a rock or a building no longer lets you in

The user: "something is up with the collision and I can sometimes clip into buildings and other parts
of the map and then I can't escape. I have to teleport or unstuck to fix it ... match the original
game exactly. You check my character Pain since he's stuck right now", then a screenshot (Pain riding
into a big rock at Tarim Ferry, readout X:1621 Y:-350, `/speed 10` and "Teleport to [Donwhang]area"
in the chat) and "I believe this occurs at any speed too". Labels: READ (`c:` sro_client.exe, `s:`
SR_GameServer.exe; decomp dumps and objdump on the render box), MEASURED, INFERRED, OURS, OPEN.
The reading is in `docs/protocol/opcodes/movement.md`, "Where a mover stands, and how it was let
into a rock (round 857)".

**Where Pain is (MEASURED; prod DB and log read only, nothing written).** `characters` id 12: zone
donwhang, frame 97/168, pos (-48153.125, -73.165, 13925.859), i.e. region **90/143** (Tarim Ferry;
`worldmap.FromWorld` with the frame's origin x 97, y 168 -- not 104/142) local (806.875, 474.141).
`server/cmd/navstuck` on the user's export: that point is **0.01 north of outline edge 5 of
`oas_tarim_rock_l_03`** (object 3 at local (835.14, -72.97, 349.54), yaw -0.9425; its mesh is its
footprint: 24 flat cells at -73.17, **9.1 under the terrain** (-64.05 there), every outline edge
0x03), and on its cell 4: the save's y is the footprint's own -73.165. The readout X:1621 Y:-350
(hud_minimap's formula) is local x 850..860, z 340..350: the rock's east lobe by edge 16, i.e. Pain
walked (rode) inside the footprint from the north edge to the far side. From the save, 36 of 72
escape directions are blocked at zero length (every way out, 0x02) and the other 36 walk on into
the rock. The log: `/speed 10` at 16:09:30, a return scroll, the Eu gate to Donwhang at 16:10:23,
then nothing logged for him (moves are not logged at INFO).

**How a player gets in (MEASURED, base e06e1ccc).**
1. **Any wall stop beside a footprint under or just above the ground, at any speed, on foot or
   riding.** OpenSRO's settle (`Graph.SurfaceAt` / `NavGraph.surface_at`) took the first object cell
   under the point over the terrain however far below it lay (and the highest within 12 above). A
   wall stop is ContactPush (0.01) short of the crossing, and a long cell's 0.0001 barycentric
   tolerance reaches past 0.01 once its altitude is over 100, so the stop lay "on" the footprint.
   The server settles each leg anew (one `World.Walk` per 0x7021), and the client after a correction
   (0xB023 or a far 0xB021), a teleport or a region change, so **the next leg started on the
   footprint**: every way out blocked, every way in open. Live (`/var/tmp/r857/qa857.sh b1`, Tess857
   at Pain's rock, real clicks): the click into the rock stopped at local z 475.109; the click away
   was a zero-length walled leg (`move: leg ... from_y=-61.56 ... wall=true end_z=13924.89`) and
   the client was put back; the next click walked into the rock (`from_y=-73.165`, Pain's exact y,
   `wall=false end_z=13980` = local 420) and the client settled on `oas_tarim_rock_l_03`; every
   later click away stopped at the inside of the edge, on foot, riding the horse, at `/speed 10`
   and on a sky-click run (which crossed the whole rock to its south edge, local z 359.4). At
   Jangan (`rail.sh rb`): an Up-key run at /speed 10 into **cj_luxury**'s north wall (stop 0.01
   short of its outline edge 0, whose floor is 9.06 over the ground) put the client on the building
   (`wall ... on object cj_luxury`) and the server's next leg back was a zero-length wall.
   - The census (`navstuck -census`, all 6,178 regions of the export): 46,614 placements with a
     mesh, 44,575 walled both ways (1,707 kinds; 21,918 of them mostly 1 or more under the ground:
     trees, rocks, cliffs, walls, Baghdad and Petra pieces); walks at each from 16 directions:
     506,174 wall stops, **32,977 of them settled inside by the old settle (24,089 on a footprint
     under the ground, 8,888 above it), at 9,649 placements**. With the new settle: 2,746, of which 2,742
     are stops whose own height is off the ground -- the walk was already on that object, entered
     through an open outline edge, and stopped at its own wall from inside -- and 4 at the ground's
     height on an object flush with it (within 0.01).
2. **The heading run was not walked by the server** (round 812's list): a sky-click or Up-key run
   was a straight line through every wall until 0x7023 or 60 s; the client's own stop report, taken
   within the claim slack, usually brought it back (MEASURED `rail.sh rb`: every run's claim was
   taken at the client's wall), but the server's position ran on beyond the wall until it came,
   and a 0x7023 before it (or a lost or refused report) stopped the character there.
3. **A claim past a wall stood** (OURS since round 749): a stop report within 9 plus the banked
   second was taken wherever it lay -- a client whose own walk had gone in put the server in too.
Not ways in (MEASURED): **tunnelling** -- the server walks a unit at a time with a segment test and
the client a frame at a time with one (`/speed 10`: 1,075 a second, the stop at Pain's rock was the
same 475.109 at 1x and x10, riding and on foot); **arrivals** -- the gate and return-scroll points
are named and settle at the client's own landing height (`relocated` claims); a region crossing
re-settles the same way as a leg (fixed with it).

**What the original does (READ).**
- **The record carries the footing.** `CRegionManagerBody::vslot_012` (c:0x412660, s:0x98b300)
  walks the record `{+0 cell, +4 object (0: terrain), +8 region, +0xc x, +0x10 y, +0x14 z}` cell by
  cell through each mesh's resolver, at most 7 meshes a step (`local_88 < 7`, else refused,
  0x10000000), and a step over a region span (1920.0, `0xe1b800`) on either axis is refused; the
  record that comes back names the cell and object it ended on. Nothing re-derives the footing from
  the height between steps: a segment walk, not an end-point test.
- **The point resolve** (`vslot_011` c:0x412530 / s:0x98b1d0 -> `CRTNavMeshTerrain::vslot_003`
  c:0x403dd0 / s:0x99fd90): the terrain cell first, then each object the cell lists whose cell lies
  under the point, taken only when STRICTLY nearer the asked height (c:0x403e8c..0x403eaf). Used
  where a mover is placed with no walk: a new record (`FUN_009e0d50`), and a server-named point
  the record could not walk to (c:0x9e11e0: with a record the client walks it there, slot 12, and
  for 0xB021's source and 0xB023 falls back to the resolve when refused or blocked).
- **Inside an object**: the object walk blocks leaving through 0x02 / 0x10 outline edges whenever
  `+0x38` is not 0 (s:0x9b55ac; 1 on every object, round 851), so a mover whose record is on a
  sealed footprint stays there in the original too; the 0.2 nudge toward the cell's centre
  (`FUN_004472d0`, double 0xe1b850 = 0.2) is the terrain wall's stop in the terrain cell the mover is
  in, never a move off an object. No push-out was found (INFERRED from the three walks read; OPEN:
  the dungeon and `.cpd` walks). So the original's escape is a teleport (a return scroll, a gate);
  what keeps players out is that its record never lands on such a footprint.
- **Heading runs** step through the same query as every mover (round 851, READ).

**What changed.**
- **The settle is the original's point resolve** (server `Graph.SurfaceAt`, client
  `NavGraph.surface_at`): the terrain first, an object only when strictly nearer the mover's
  height; OURS kept: nothing more than 12 above. The exit hand-off (`seamObjectAt` /
  `_seam_object_at`) takes an object only when nearer than the ground too. A dungeon's surface pick
  is unchanged (its resolve is not read).
- **The server walks a heading run** (`world.WallFunc`, `session.navRunWall`,
  `world.Hub.WalkHeadingRuns` / `WalkHeadingRun`): two seconds of run (at least 20 units, OURS) are
  walked ahead, the 250 ms mover pass walks on, a run never goes past what was walked, and the
  first wall ends it with a 0xB023 as a walled 0x7021 leg; a turn (0x7024) and a speed re-base keep
  it walked.
- **A claim past a wall is corrected** (`world.Bound.Unreached`, `session.claimUnreached`, OURS):
  the server walks from where it has the character to the claim; a wall more than 0.5 short of it
  refuses the claim (a named point still takes it).
- `server/cmd/navstuck` (new): a stuck point's cell, edges, objects and escape probe; `-census`.

**QA (render box, real client, lane server 127.0.0.1:17300: in memory, `-navmesh-dir`, no
`-trust-client-positions`; `/var/tmp/r857/qa857.sh`, `rail.sh`, `pics.sh`; analyser `ana857.py`,
reports `b1.ana.txt` / `h1.ana.txt`).**

## Eight-hundred-and-fifty-sixth round: the state colour's guards -- berserk and the Roc's frenzy, not riding

Round 855 reported that `FUN_009cd5e0` skips a state's colour when "the riding byte" `+0x2c2 == 1` or
the kind byte `+0x448 == 2`, and asked whether to keep ours or match; the user: "keep the original".
Labels: READ (`c:` sro_client.exe, `s:` the server), MEASURED, INFERRED, OURS, OPEN. The reading is
`docs/protocol/status_effects.md`, "The colour's guards".

**What the guard covers (READ, `FUN_009cd5e0` and its disassembly `c:0x9cd640..0x9cdb68`, esi = the
object whose mask it is).**
- Only the colour calls. On: the `+0x48` of FB, ES, BU, PS, ZB, DN, STUN, each behind its own test
  (`0x9cd74a`, `0x9cd7df`, `0x9cd84d`, `0x9cd8b7`, `0x9cd969`, `0x9cd9d1`, `0x9cda37`). Off: the `+0x4c`
  (`0x9cdb35..0x9cdb56`, and the FB case).
- Not guarded: the `PARAM_` aura's start `FUN_00a54020` (`0x9cd723`) and end `FUN_009cd2b0`
  (`0x9cdac0`); FB's and SLOW's clip speed `+0xc0` (`0x9cd7bf`, `0x9cd95e`; off `0x9cdb01`,
  `0x9cdb2d`); FZ's motion state 9 and `+0xbd` (`0x9cd7ce`, `0x9cd7d3`; off `0x9cdb0b`).
- Tested per bit, inside each bit's case, on the object itself. **DN's end tests `+0x2c2` alone:**
  `0x9cdb35 cmp byte [esi+0x2c2],1` jumps to the `je` at `0x9cdb56`, past the `+0x448` compare at
  `0x9cdb4f`.

**`+0x2c2 == 1` is berserk, not riding (READ).** The byte's one writer is the body-mode setter
`FUN_009cf880` (`[this+0x2c3] = extra; [this+0x2c2] = mode`); the constructor
`CICharactor::FUN_009d2ad0` zeroes it. Callers: 0x30BF kind 4 (`FUN_008a80a0` case 4, any object in
view), the spawn (`FUN_009d17e0`, `GlobalDataManager::FUN_0052dc70`: the state block's `+0x470`) and a
debug command (`FUN_005470f0`). Mode 1 runs `FUN_009dd620(1, ...)`, the hwan decoration (0x80000000 /
`SYSTEM_CH_HWAN2MODE`); mode 4 draws the body at alpha 0x50. So the guard is on any body whose body
mode is 1 -- this player's, another player's, any object the server says is berserk. Mounting writes
neither byte: **a rider's colour is not guarded.** Round 785's StateLook header ("the player riding")
and round 855's entry were wrong.

**`+0x448 == 2` is the Roc's frenzy (READ + MEASURED).** Writers: `FUN_00a53850` (a skill decoration's
start) and `FUN_00a54be0` (a cast's action read) write 2 on the decoration's object (`deco+0x58`) when
its skill ref (`deco+0x154`) has a non-zero `+0x110`, which the client's skilldata parser
`FUN_009bbca0` fills for Param code `0x6d6f6d`, `mom`; `FUN_00a54be0` writes 1 when `+0x114` (`pmhp`)
reads 100; `FUN_00a53120` (a decoration's end) writes 0 for a `mom` skill. MEASURED on the box: Media.pk2's
ENC skilldata decrypted with the executable's own tables (61,330 rows) -- one skill has `mom`,
`MSKILL_RM_ROC_ATTACK10` (id 31102), skilleffect.txt's "괴조 로크 광폭화", the Roc's frenzy, whose ACT_L
row carries its own colour `SCT_MAT,170,30,0,235,155,0,1000`. The server's `SkillAction_Buff`
(`s:0x5830b0`, ref `+0x57c`) re-arms its stat stacks every value[0] ms.

**Why (INFERRED from the two).** Both guarded bodies hold a decoration colour of their own in the
one slot (berserk's red, the frenzy's orange): a state may neither replace it nor end it. The
decoration's end (`+0x4c`, `CIDecoSkill::FUN_00a53dd0`) ends whichever colour is on. So in the
original:
- a state begun before berserk and ended inside it: berserk's colour stays, and its end leaves none;
- a state begun inside berserk draws no colour; when berserk ends first, the state runs on uncoloured;
- the same for the frenzy; and a `mom` decoration drawing no colour of its own would keep a state's
  colour begun before it past the state's end (the quirk round 855 described) -- in the data the one
  `mom` skill does draw one, so the quirk cannot show with retail's tables.

**A kept decoration's colour (READ), built with it.** `IDecoSkill::FUN_00a513a0` hands any row with
SCT_MAT (flag 0x800) to the compound's `+0x48` and keeps it (`+0x180`); the decoration's destructor
`CIDecoSkill::FUN_00a53dd0` calls `+0x4c` when one was kept, with no body-mode or kind test. 22 rows
carry SCT_MAT (MEASURED): berserk's three, `PARAM_STONE`, the frenzy, five petrify attacks, two
`SKILL_EU_CLERIC_REBIRTHA_SPECIAL_*_BUFF`, seven `EFFECT_AM_*` marks, the two event thieves' marks, and
the white snake's READY. OpenSRO drew only berserk's: with the kind-2 guard alone a frenzied Roc would
have kept a poison's green for good. Now `SkillEffects` draws a buff aura's and a state aura's SCT_MAT
in the body's slot (`DECO_WHO`) and ends it when the aura ends, after its rows' longest Fade (INFERRED:
the decoration is freed at its fade's end).

**The change (client-only; `82f19eb3`, `8499dd9c`).**
- `StateLook.walk(old, new, look, guard)`: `guard_of(body_mode, kind)`, `colour_guarded` (body mode 1
  or kind 2; DN's end the body mode alone); a guarded bit's colour event is left out, its aura, clip
  speed, freeze and the look's own tint are not.

  character's), kind 2 from the owner's running buffs (`_fx_owner_buffs`, a skill whose Param block has
  `mom`: `SkillBuffCatalog` "mom"). A guarded walk logs `state colour left as it is (body mode m, kind k)`.
- `SkillEffects`: rows with SCT_MAT are kept even without an effect file (`parse_mat`, `mat_of`);

- Round 855's rule is intact: BodyPulse paints only its own copies; no shared material is painted
  (every test and live sample below: `shared 0`).

**Behaviour changes a player may notice.** (1) A berserk player who is poisoned, burnt, shocked,
frostbitten, zombied, darkened or stunned keeps berserk's red; the state's end does not take the red
away; berserk's end takes all colour away even while a state still runs (before: the last start won

not change the colour (not reachable on OpenSRO's server today, below). (3) The other SCT_MAT
decorations draw their colour while they last (the Cleric rebirth special buff, the petrify marks).
Riding changes nothing: a rider's state colour starts and ends as before.

## Eight-hundred-and-fifty-fifth round: a status colour that lingered -- the pulse painted a shared material

The user: "Can you also fix the bug where the status effect color lingers when it shouldn't".
Labels: READ (`c:` sro_client.exe), MEASURED, INFERRED, OURS, OPEN. The reading is
`docs/protocol/status_effects.md`, "A state's colour: one slot on the body, never in a material", and
`docs/protocol/berserk_look.md` (the end).

**What lingered (MEASURED).** Not the state, the message or the aura (round 847 measured those on
time, and they still are): the colour pulse's last colour, left in a material that is not the
body's own. `StateLook` (round 785) gave each mesh a copy of its material and painted whatever the
mesh drew every frame. `CharacterLight` rescans a body every 8th visit and swaps each object material
for ObjectLight's shared per-level copy -- it skipped berserk's copies, not a state's. On a terrain
tile (any level but the object floor's 0.6) the copy was swapped out within frames, StateLook painted
the shared level copy, and at the state's end it "restored"... that same painted shared material.
The body kept the colour, and so did every body at that level wearing the same pieces -- in the
observer's client its own, never-poisoned body pulsed green with the poisoned player's. It went only
when the body stepped onto another level or the material was freed. Round 847's runs stood on the
Jangan plaza deck (an object, 0.6), where nothing is swapped, which is why they saw the colour end on
time.

- Headless (`r855_probe`, base `6b1b1223`): a poison on a level-153 body, one CharacterLight rescan,
  the end: the shared level copy's `object_tint` stayed `(0.166, 0.260, 0.108, 1)`; a second body at
  that level drew it.
- Live, real client, base + the probe (`99c9b5a9`): see the table.

**What the original does (READ).** The colour is a flag on the character's compound object, never
in a material: `+0x48` (`CObjRendererVS::FUN_00c25800`) sets `+0x1ec`, the two colours, the ms and
the elapsed 0; `CCompChar::FUN_00c33430` steps it (`FUN_00c26ff0`); every part drawn reads its
compound's flag (`CObjRendererVS::vslot_038`, `c:0xbf5830`) and draws the pulse colour in place of the
material's and the object's (`FUN_00c27180`); `+0x4c` (`FUN_00c258b0`) clears the flag and nothing
else. One slot: a second start overwrites it. Its callers: the mask setter `FUN_009cd5e0` (a tinted
bit on: +0x48; off: +0x4c -- `c:0x9cdb5d`, guarded only by the riding byte `+0x2c2` and the kind byte
`+0x448`, not by another bit still on) and berserk's decoration end `CIDecoSkill::FUN_00a53dd0` (flag
0x800, SCT_MAT), both on `[obj+0x9c]+4`. So a part rebuilt mid-pulse draws it, the end restores
nothing, the last start wins, and any end ends the colour whoever set it.

**The fix (`BodyPulse`, OURS method for the READ rule; `0633a130`).** One colour slot per body,
`client/scripts/effects/body_pulse.gd`, which both `StateLook` and `BerserkLook` use:
- it paints only copies it made; each frame a mesh drawing its copy is painted, one whose material
  something else replaced (an equipment glow, a fade's end) has that material taken as its own and a
  fresh copy made (never painted itself), one on a fade twin keeps it (a cohort's shared twin is never
  painted; a twin of the copy -- a despawn mid-pulse -- is the mesh's own and pulses, and is unpainted
  at the end);
- `CharacterLight` leaves a pulsed mesh alone (the pulse stands in for the object colour, READ), and
  the end puts each mesh back on its own material at the body's level then;
- `StateLook.walk` reports the walk's last tinted event (`pulse`: start, end or nothing), as
  `FUN_009cd5e0` calls +0x48 / +0x4c; berserk starts it and its end ends it once (not again when its
  size is back);
- a body with a colour on is not drawn by the far crowd (`_crowd_eligible`: "pulse"), whose instances
  would keep the copy.

**Two behaviour changes to the original's rule (READ; a player may notice).**
1. Two tinted states, one ends: the colour ends while the other runs (it was already so here; now
   stated and tested). The original does the same.
2. Berserk and a state: before, berserk kept its colour over a state's (round 785's review, finding 8,
   OURS). Now the last start wins and either end ends the colour: a berserk player who is poisoned
   pulses green, and when either ends no colour is drawn while the other runs.

**QA (render box, lane server 17270 with prod's flags, in memory; real input through
`OPENSRO_QA_INPUT`; scripts `/var/tmp/r855/{srv855,qa855,run855}.sh`).** The actor QaB855 on a terrain
tile of 97/168 (levels MEASURED with `OPENSRO_QA_CHARLIGHT`: local 1002,760 is shadow byte 153 ->
0.398, local 1360,660 byte 255 -> 0.664; the plaza deck at the spawn is an object, 0.6), the watcher
Watch855 beside it. Schedule: a poison left to expire; a burn and a poison, the poison expiring
first, then the universal pill right-clicked in the bag for the burn; a poison while walking (two
ground clicks); a poison while right-clicking the sword in the bag (it did not equip: OPEN below); a
poison across a `/tp` to the other tile's level; a poison and a bleeding death. `OPENSRO_QA_TINT_PROBE=1` (`99c9b5a9`) logs,
per frame on change and every 30th, each body's meshes and how many draw a pulse colour (TintProbe:
their material's `object_tint`), whether BodyPulse holds a colour on it, and how many shared level
copies carry one. Own view rendered (the afflicted player) with the observer headless, then the
observer rendered with the afflicted player headless.

Two spots: run 1 at local 1002,760 (0.398; the camera behind a wall there, so its frames show
nothing) and run 2 at local 1360,660 (0.664), every path in each. `QA TINT` summaries
(`/var/tmp/r855/sum.py`; logs in `/var/tmp/r855/{b1,a1,b3,a3}_own`):

| | owner, base | owner, head | observer, base | observer, head |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| poison expires | 14 of 15 meshes still green (56,81,38) at the next sample, and at every sample until the next state | 0 the same frame | 14 still green | 0 |
| poison ends beside a burn | 14 stuck on the poison's frozen green while the burn runs | 0 (READ: the end ends the colour) | 14 stuck | 0 |
| the burn cured by the universal pill (bag, right-click) | 14 | 0 | 14 | 0 |
| poison during a walk (two ground clicks) | 14 | 0 | 14 | 0 |
| poison across a `/tp` to another level | 14 (59,85,41) | 0 | 14 | 0 |
| poison and a bleeding death | 14 | 0 | 14 | 0 |
| samples drawing a colour with no colour on (run 1 / run 2) | self 60 / 58 | 0 / 0 | **the observer's own, never-afflicted body 1,100 of 1,209 / 1,065 of 1,181**; the afflicted 520 / 489 | 0 / 0 |
| shared level copies carrying a colour, most at once | 14 | 0 | 28 | 0 |

While a state runs, head draws it as base did (14 of 15 meshes, the poison's 29,51,16 -> 63,90,45

121 of its 130 samples, f183 to f3781; head 0). Evidence: `/var/tmp/r855/keep` (logs, scripts,

**Tests.** `client/scripts/effects/body_pulse855_test.gd` (pure: the level copy and CharacterLight's
rescan -- NEGATIVE on `6b1b1223` as the probe shows; a level change mid-pulse; a material replaced
mid-pulse; pieces put on, taken off, freed; a rebuilt skeleton; a fade-in begun before the colour with

**Gates.** Client-only (the server is not the cause: it ended every state on time, round 847, and
nothing server-side changed). `remote_godot.sh check`: ALL LOAD (1107 scripts); `remote_godot.sh
tests`: "ran 416 suite(s), 0 failing". The perf gate (`perf_gate.sh --base 6b1b1223 --head 2d8c94b1
--sites jangan --frames 24000`; BodyPulse's tick is a dictionary walk with no colour on, and the probe
returns at once unless `OPENSRO_QA_TINT_PROBE` is set). A first attempt without `--frames` returned

|---|---|---|---|
| frame ms | 0.90 | 0.90 | SAME |
| entry ms | 8891 | 8822 | SAME |
| freeze ms | 2782 | 2757 | SAME |
| hitches | 5 | 4 | SAME |

**OPEN.**
- The riding byte (`+0x2c2 == 1`) and the kind byte (`+0x448 == 2`) guard both +0x48 and +0x4c in
  `FUN_009cd5e0`; OpenSRO has never applied them (a state on a rider pulses here). In the original a
  state that started before mounting and ended while mounted would keep its colour -- not built, as the
  user asked for the colour not to linger; the user's call.

  colour) is not read; here the slot stays on the body node and its rebuilt pieces take it.
- The live equip step did not equip: a right-click on the sword in the bag answered "that item cannot
  be used" and left the equipment as it was (MEASURED), so a piece put on mid-pulse is covered by the

- A monster's state goes the same way (StateLook on its body, CharacterLight on its level copies --
  shared by the whole species at a level, so before the fix one poisoned monster on terrain coloured

## Eight-hundred-and-fifty-fifth round, lane P: the pet strip draws under the player block, as the original does

The user: "When a pet is spawned and it shows up below the player frame it also appears on top
when it should be behind it." Their screenshots: ours drew the growth pet's strip (its round
portrait and box) over the player block's race mark and stat button. The original draws the
block's race mark, stat button and orbs over the strip. Labels: READ (`c:` sro_client.exe, the
decomp dump and the disassembly on the render box), MEASURED, INFERRED, OURS, OPEN. Base
`6b1b1223` (v0.1.619). UI-only lane: no world drawing changed, so no perf gate.

**The cause.** `HudPetMiniInfo.attach_to` hung the strip with `player_info.add_child(self)`. That
made it the block's last child, drawn after (over) the frame and the whole layout root. Godot
draws children in tree order, and nothing in the block sets a z_index (checked by the test).

**What the original does (READ).**
- **A window draws its own art, then its children in list order.** The render `c:0xb8f210`
  (shown byte +0x61, and +0x63) calls vtable +0x34 (the own draw; CIFStatic's `c:0x6550c0` for
  this block), then +0x38 = `c:0xba0300`, which walks the child list (+0x78, head +0x7c) from the
  first node forward and draws each shown child the same way, then +0x3c.
- **A resinfo section's controls join that list in reverse file order.**
  - The parser keeps them in file order: `CIFTDocument::FUN_00b3dea0` links each control after the
    last (first +0x84, last +0x88, next +0x4c, prev +0x50).
  - `CIFTSection::vslot_000` (`c:0xb3dcb0`) lists the names from the last (+0x88) back through
    +0x50.
  - `c:0x82c1d0` makes one record per name in that order (a push_back).
  - `c:0x8b5580` (CIFPlayerMiniInfo::Create's "Create" section) creates the windows in record
    order through `gwnd::FUN_00ba20b0`.
  - `gwnd::FUN_00ba20b0` hands each window to the parent's AddChild, vtable +0x1c = `c:0xb90a80`,
    a push_back.
  - So the file's first control is drawn last, on top. UiBuilder's "back to front" reversal (its
    comment said the draw loop was not found) is now READ.
- **Where control 100 sits (MEASURED, Media.pk2 `resinfo\ifplayerminiinfo.txt`).** 53 controls.
  `GDR_PMI_PET_MINI_INFO` (CIFPetMiniInfo, id 100, Rect 53,55,154,40) is the 52nd. Only
  `GDR_PMI_SELECT` (id 200, the selection glow) comes after it. The order is RACE_MARK, PARTY_LEADER,
  BTN_STATUP, BTN_CINFO, HWAN_EFF_FACE, DECO_HWAN_SLOT4..0, the 20 stat-panel labels,
  STA_CINFOBG, FORFEIT, BATTLE_GRADE, FORTRESS_INFO, PK, BTN_JAHWAN, PICTURE, CIRCLE4..0,
  TXT_MP, TXT_HP, TXT_LEVEL, TXT_ID, GAUGE_MP, GAUGE_HP, EFFECT_MP, EFFECT_HP, HWAN_EFF_GLOW,
  PET_MINI_INFO, SELECT.

## Eight-hundred-and-fifty-fourth round, lane U: UI Scale is a dropdown in Option > Video, in Windows' steps

The user: "Let's make UI scale a dropdown in the graphics settings. Let's use the same percentages
that Windows supports to keep simple yet powerful." Labels: READ (`c:` sro_client.exe), MEASURED,
INFERRED, OURS, OPEN. Base `df8ba2cb` (v0.1.618). UI-only lane: no world drawing changed, so no
perf gate.

**The game's minimum (READ / MEASURED; the brief asked to verify 1024 x 768 rather than assume it).**
- READ: the Video tab's resolution list keeps only modes with `799 < w && 599 < h` (c:0x5fef70, the
  decomp's mode loop): **800 x 600 is the smallest screen the original lays its interface out on**,
  not 1024 x 768. (1024 x 768 is only the record constructor's default mode, c:0x5f75e0.)
- MEASURED: the original places its windows at run time, not from a design resolution -- all 92
  window records in `resinfo\ginterface.txt` carry zero rects (three have 2..12-pixel offsets).
  Its largest windows fit 800 x 600: the item mall `GDR_RENEWAL_ITEM_MALL` 800 x 600 (round 838),
  this Option window 700 x 500 (optionwnd.2dt, MEASURED earlier).
- So the minimum is `VideoOptions.MIN_VIEW` (800 x 600), the same one round 696 already used for
  the resolution list.

**Built (OURS, from the original's parts).**
- `UiScaleChoices` (new): the list 100 / 125 / 150 / 175 / 200 / 225 / 250 / 300 / 350 / 400 / 450 /
  500 %. A scale is offered only when the view (window / scale) is at least 800 x 600, as Windows
  hides a scale below its minimum; 100 % is always offered. Exact in integers: 150 % needs
  1200 x 900. What that offers:

  | window | offered up to |
  |---|---|
  | 800 x 600, 1280 x 720 | 100 % |
  | 1024 x 768, 1366 x 768 | 125 % |
  | 1600 x 900 | 150 % |
  | 1920 x 1080 | 175 % (Windows offers the same there) |
  | 1920 x 1200 | 200 % |
  | 2560 x 1440, 3440 x 1440 | 225 % |
  | 3840 x 2160 | 350 % |
  | 5120 x 2880 | 450 % |
  | 7680 x 4320 | 500 % |

- **The row.** A "UI Scale" row is in the Video tab's list (the tab the user calls the graphics
  settings: its sub-tabs read Graphic 1 / Graphic 2). It is the list's 22nd entry and fills the
  last line's empty right-hand slot -- the original's CNIFVideoOptionSlot (label 216, the
  original's combo 217 through `make_combo` / ComboList), white label in font 0. So no squeezing:
  the slot was empty before (frame below). It scrolls into view as the last line, like the other
  OURS rows (renderer, Job Titles).
- **Filtering.** The row is filtered against the size the window will have: the Resolution picked
  in the tab, the screen for Full screen, else the window now. It is filtered again on every
  resize while the window is open (`OptionWindow._on_view_resized`).
- **A choice that no longer fits.** It is kept saved, and the largest scale that fits is used. The
  label says which: "UI Scale (150% won't fit)" fits the 141-wide label record at 1280 x 720
  (frame). The tooltip names the 800 x 600 minimum and the size. When the window grows back, the
  saved choice comes back.
- **Applying.** As the tab's other rows: on Apply / Confirm (nothing changes before), saved as
  [ui] scale (round 672's key, a factor).
  - A scale too large for a new Resolution is lowered before the window is resized, so
    `window_placement` places the window for the new scale. A larger scale goes in after the resize.
  - `UiScaleChoices.apply_saved` then watches the window's size and re-fits on every resize.
  - At start-up (Boot) the saved scale is applied as far as the saved Resolution allows, before the
    display, and fitted after it.
  - Default (the tab's button) puts 100 % back (OURS).
- **The Resolution list** now lists every size at least 800 x 600 at 100 %. Round 696's review
  listed only sizes that fit the scale in force, because a window too small for the scale stranded
  the Option window's buttons off screen. Now the scale follows the window, so no size strands
  anything (OPTION_VIDEO.md updated).
- **Below 100 % and odd values.** The old `/uiscale` allowed 0.5..3; nothing below 100 % is offered
  now (the original's size is the smallest, its fonts drawn 1:1). A saved or typed value is
  snapped to the nearest listed step, ties to the smaller: 0.5 -> 100 %, 1.3 -> 125 %, 1.95 -> 200 %,
  2.75 -> 250 %, above 5 -> 500 %.
  - `/uiscale` stays and snaps: "150", "150%" and "1.5" all mean 150 %. It answers with what is
    used, e.g. "UI scale 150% saved; a 1280x720 window fits up to 100%, so 100% is used until the
    window is larger."
  - The dev panel's slider steps through the list.
  - `ClientSettings.apply_ui_scale` now allows up to 5.0.
- **Departure, disclosed.** The original has no UI scale at all (it draws 1:1); the whole row is
  OURS.

## Eight-hundred-and-fifty-fourth round, lane W: the free zone warp is closed (OpChangeZone is a GM's tool)

The user, on hearing the server accepts a free zone warp: "Free warp? why do we want this? It's not
in the original game I never asked for it". It was a security hole, flagged in round 848 and left
open: `handleChangeZone` (OpChangeZone 0x0026, OpenSRO's own message) warped any living player to
any zone, with a landing spot, checking only alive / not already there. Since round 849 the
developer panel (Shift+F3, on in every build) put that warp behind buttons any player could click.
Labels: READ (`s:` SR_GameServer.exe, objdump and the decomp dump on the render box), MEASURED,
INFERRED, OURS, OPEN.

**What the original does (READ).**
- The original's GM moves are sub-commands of one message, 0x7010
  (`GObjPC_MsgHandler_SpecialCommand::DispatchCommand`, s:0x51de90; `docs/protocol/gm_commands.md`:
  0x10 "MoveTo", 0x08 "MoveToPlayer", 0x1f `OnCommandMoveToNpc`). Its first act, before the
  switch, is a permission test of the selector: s:0x51dee3..0x51def2 calls CGObjPC vtable +0x634
  (slot 397, s:0x4e5960, in the table at 0xaf59fc) with the selector; that calls s:0x40b7c0
  (`[PC+0x188]`'s byte +0x3d and the selector, on the singleton at 0xd6aa1c) -> s:0x82a070: the
  selector is looked up in a table (s:0x607520); not found refuses, found compares the entry's
  byte +0xe with s:0x82a0e0 of the account's byte (`required <= level`). A refusal answers 0xB010
  with error 0x1403 (s:0x51def8..0x51df04) and runs nothing. So a GM's warp is a server-side move,
  gated per command on the account's level. Which account field that byte is (INFERRED: the
  shard's security level) is OPEN.
- Every other relocation the original server makes has a server-side reason (the gate 0x705A
  `HandleTeleportUse` s:0x513590, the scrolls, the revive 0x7053, the walk-ins). Not claimed: a
  proven absence of any client zone message -- `handler_payloads.tsv`'s GObjPC table (163 rows) has
  none, but it does not list the movement handlers either, so it is not a complete census.

**Built.**
- `handleChangeZone` refuses any account outside `-gm-accounts` before it reads the request
  (`zoneChangeAllowed`, world.go): `OpChangeZoneResult{OK: false, Reason: "zone change is a GM
  tool"}` (wording OURS), a `WARN zone change refused: not a GM account account=<name>` log line,
  and nothing moves -- not the hub, not anyone's view. A malformed request from a non-GM gets the
  same refusal. A GM's OpChangeZone is unchanged (the developer panel's zone box and town buttons).
- A GM's `/goto <zone>` is now the server's own warp (`GMCommandHandler` -> `warpVia` "gm /goto",
  arrival guard on or off) at the zone's landing (`changeZoneLanding`, the point a client-asked
  change landed at); the reply names no zone, so no client message carries it. Before, the reply
  named the zone and the client sent OpChangeZone, which any account could send. This is the
  cleaner of the two: the zone a GM lands in is the one the GM command resolved on the server, as
  with the original's 0x7010 moves, and OpChangeZone is left only as the developer panel's GM tool.
- Client: a refused zone change that answers this client's request puts "Zone change refused:
  <reason>" on the system line (World3D `_on_change_zone_result`). The refusal never showed a
  loading screen (it goes up only for an accepted result) and consumes its request.
- partybot: `-zone` documents the GM requirement and prints a refusal with where the bot still
  is; `-zone-after` (QA aid) delays the request. The developer panel's town buttons are named
  `DebugGo<Town>` and QA `node:` looks in the shown panel, so a run clicks them.
- The suite opens OpChangeZone for its older tests (TestMain `zoneChangeAnyone`; no flag sets it,
  as with `-trust-client-positions`); `changezone854_test.go` shuts it for its own.

**Every zone move checked (server tests with OpChangeZone shut, a plain account unless named):**

| Path | Code | Test |
|---|---|---|
| OpChangeZone from a non-GM (town, known spot, arbitrary spot, dungeon, malformed) | `handleChangeZone` | refused, unmoved, the other player sees nothing (`TestRound854NonGMChangeZoneIsRefused`) |
| GM `/goto` from a non-GM | GM gate | refused, unmoved (same test) |
| OpChangeZone from a GM (developer panel) | `handleChangeZone` | warps (`TestRound854GMChangeZoneStillWorks`; `TestRound786EveryTeleportPathIsHeld` "zone change") |
| GM `/goto <zone>` | `GMCommandHandler` -> `warpVia` "gm /goto" | lands at the zone's landing, guard off and on (`TestRound854GMGotoZoneIsTheServersWarp`) |
| GM `/tp`, `/goto <monster>` | `GMCommandHandler` | unchanged (`TestRound786EveryTeleportPathIsHeld` "gm /tp") |
| Gate teleport 0x705A | `teleporter.use` | moves (`TestRound854LegitimateMovesNeedNoZoneChange`) |
| `/unstuck` | `handleUnstuck` | moves (same) |
| Revive at the return point; respawn after a kill | `returnToPoint` / `returnAfterKill` -> `warpHome` | move (same) |
| Return scroll, reverse return scroll, return then reverse to the recall point | `ScrollCaster.complete` | move (same: `TestRound786ScrollsAreHeld`, `TestRound778ReturnThenReverseToTheRecallPoint`) |
| Gate into a dungeon; walk-in portal; walk-in by a reported walk | `teleporter.use` / `walkIn` | move (same: `TestRound773TeleportIntoADungeon`, `...WalkInFiresOnEntering`, `...WalkInFiresOnAReportedWalk`) |
| Guild recall | `handleRecallAnswer` | moves (same: `TestGuild844RecallAnswer`) |
| Relog arrival | `enterOwned` (OpEnterWorld) | each rig's own entry, with the gate shut |
| Walking across region and zone boundaries | 0x7021 / OpMove claims | no zone message: the client sends OpChangeZone only from `_request_zone_change`, reached from the GM reply (now only a guard-off `/goto <monster>` in another zone, a GM's) and the developer panel |

`TestRound786EveryRelocationGoesThroughWarpVia` now expects `GMCommandHandler` twice among
`warpVia`'s callers.

**Other client messages that choose a position (checked, not changed).**
- OpMove 0x0022 (a stop, a placement, an older client's walk): with `-trust-client-positions` off
  a claim is taken only within the server's own leg's reach (`world.Hub.Claim`, `claimBound`) or
  at a point the server named (`landingTake`, `warpLandingAdmits`); otherwise the mover is
  corrected (0xB023). With the flag on every position is taken (the startup log warns "QA only").
  Prod runs without it (INFERRED from the rounds that measured "with prod's flags (no
  `-trust-client-positions`)", e.g. round 847; prod itself was not read, per the brief).
- 0x7021 click move: the server paths it (destmove.go).
- Ghost Walk / Teleport / Sprint ('tele', 'tel2', 'tel3'): the ground point is clamped to the
  skill's limit (`teleportDestination`, READ c:FUN_005862e0).
- `/unstuck`: the server picks the point (`unstuckTarget`), once a minute.
- The developer panel's "Teleport" box moves the player on the client only; it sends no message
  of its own, and the next claim is bounded as above.
- Nothing else found that lets a player pick a zone.

## Eight-hundred-and-fifty-second round: a pet's run plays at its speed; other bodies stop at walls on an observer's screen

The user: "Fix those last two open items" -- round 851's two: a pet's run animation did not scale with
its speed, and on another player's screen a rider (and any other player's body) pressed into a wall
before snapping to the stop. Labels: READ (`c:` sro_client.exe: the decomp dump and objdump on the
render box), MEASURED, INFERRED, OURS, OPEN.

**1. A pet's gait and clip rate (READ, `CICCos::vslot_009` c:0x9c59c0; docs/protocol/pets.md "Round 852").**
- It is the COS's per-frame tick: it calls the characters' tick `FUN_009d1d60` (CICharactor slot 9),
  which steps the mover (`FUN_009e0e60`) and advances the body's clip by ROUND(+0xc0 x the frame's
  ms) (`FUN_009c4180`, c:0x9c41c1 -> `FUN_00a5acb0`). So **+0xc0 is the clip rate** (round 785 had it
  INFERRED from frostbite's 0.5) and the rule below runs **every frame**.
- **Which kinds:** only an object whose type word is TypeID 1/2/3 with TypeID4 3 or 4
  (c:0x9c59d0..0x9c5a07): growth and ability pets. Horses and transports (their walk or run is the
  rider's, round 798), soldiers, players, monsters and NPCs never take it -- their clips play at 1.0
  but for the abnormal states.
- **The speed:** s = run speed (+0x670, which 0x30D0 sets) x the mover's speed factor (+0x6f4 = the
  mover's +0x8c, round 846's catch-up factor from `FUN_009e0550`); stored as the walk speed (+0x66c)
  too (c:0x9c5a09..0x9c5a1d).
- **The gait:** against 20.0 (float 0xd88108): s <= 20 -> `FUN_009ca430(2)`, walk (+0x678 0; a moving
  state 9 is restarted, so the clip changes mid-leg); s > 20 -> `FUN_009ca430(3)`, run.
- **The rate:** 1.0; s / 50.0 (double 0xd8f0b0) when s > 20 and the moving state is on (+0x65c bit
  9); x 0.5 (double 0xe1b7d0) under frostbite (+0x2c4 bit 1); at most 1.5 (float 0xd819ec), no lower
  bound. Walking, 1.0 whatever s is. Written every frame, so on a pet it overrides the abnormal-state
  setter's own +0xc0 (`FUN_009cd5e0`: slowness 0.75 is lost on a pet -- built as read).
- **Built:** `PetGait` (`client/scripts/world/pet_gait.gd`) and `World3D._cos_pet_tick`, every frame
  a pet moves and once as it stops, through the clip-speed book the abnormal states use
  (`_set_skeleton_clip_speed`; `_step_clip_speeds` now finds each body's entry from where it was last
  frame, OURS, instead of scanning every body's clip every frame while a pet runs). A COS's leg is now
  an `OtherWalk` leg with round 846's 50-unit resync and catch-up factor (READ: the 0xB021 handler is
  every object's; before, the monsters' 32 and no factor), so s is run x factor as the original's is.
  Before (base 5f7f420b): the gait was chosen once at a leg's start by its speed, a 0x30D0 mid-leg
  changed nothing, and every clip played at 1.0.

**2. Other bodies at walls (READ; movement.md "Round 852: every body an observer draws").** The mover
tick `FUN_009e0e60` runs for every character that does not ride and asks the collision query at
c:0x9e0fca, flag 1 only for the own player (CICPlayer 0xef1b44) and an own COS (CICCos 0xeef6f0 owned
by DAT_00eef5ec), 0 for everyone else. The client's `CRegionManagerBody::vslot_012` (c:0x412660)
passes both arguments to the navmesh walk (c:0x41290a..0x41291c); the terrain walk
`CRTNavMeshTerrain::vslot_002` (c:0x4047a0) tests the flag's bit 0 at three places only -- c:0x404ab9,
c:0x404c30, c:0x404f20, the cell-object re-checks, the same three as the server's (round 851) -- and
hands it down unread elsewhere; the object walk takes the second argument, always 1 (round 644). So an
observer's client stops another player on foot, its ridden horse or transport (the rider's body walks
the mount's legs), a following COS and a monster at the same trunks and railings as the server, and
draws them there; a bit-0 stop ends the movement (`FUN_009e0e60`: `param_1[0x21] = 0`).
- **Built:** `BodyWalk` (`client/scripts/world/body_walk.gd`; round 851's `CosWalk` made general and
  renamed), one walker for `_step_other_legs` (players and riders), `_cos_step` (COS) and
  `_step_monster_bodies`. Each leg is walked once when it starts (`BodyWalk.plan`,
  `World3D._plan_body_leg`): clear -> the straight step as before; walled -> its end becomes the wall's
  stop; a heading run, a leg with no graph yet or leaving its region, and a terrain wall's send-back
  are walked through the graph a frame at a time (`BodyWalk.step`).
- **OURS, and why (MEASURED, `tools/walk_probe.gd --bench-legs=3000` on Jangan 97/168, new):** a
  frame-by-frame walk costs 97 us a body a frame in GDScript (p99 411) -- every walker in a crowd would
  cost tens of ms a frame -- while one plan costs 140 us at the median (p99 625, max 973), once a leg.
  The one walk gives the frame-by-frame walk's stop: of 400 walled legs the plan could answer, 397 end
  within 0.01 of it, the worst 0.052 (54 more were left to the frame-by-frame walk). A frame spends at
  most 1.5 ms on plans (`BODY_PLAN_BUDGET_USEC`); a leg over it walks straight and is planned from where
  it is drawn on a later frame. The flag's three re-checks are not modelled (INFERRED to matter only
  where a terrain wall and an object wall fall in one step, as round 851 found for the server).

## Eight-hundred-and-fifty-first round, lane C: collision per kind of mover; a following transport stops at the trunk

The user: "Please match the exact behavior of pets following you. Especially trade transports. Trade
transports aren't supposed to be able to go through walls and can [get] stuck so it requires careful
movement sometimes to make sure you don't get on walls or even trees. Reference the movement/collision
info though for kind of mount and match it exactly". Lane C owns what blocks a mover; lane F the
follow rules. The reading is in `docs/protocol/opcodes/movement.md`, "Collision per kind of mover".

- **READ: one collision for every kind.** The server's step (`CGObjMobile::Update` s:0x48b8c0 ->
  slot 305 -> slot 231 -> s:0x485740) asks `CRegionManagerBody::vslot_012` (s:0x98b300) with two
  inputs from the mover: IsPC || IsCOS (IGObj slots 7 and 11) and its `+0x38`, which
  `CGObj::vslot_000` sets to 1 (s:0x48492a). MEASURED: no other store to `+0x38` on a game object
  (953 dword and 1,322 byte/word register stores scanned and mapped to their functions). `+0x38`
  makes object walls block (s:0x9b51e9, s:0x9b55ac); the flag only gates three re-checks of the
  cell's objects in the terrain walk (s:0x9a0a43, 0x9a0bd2, 0x9a0eb8) and never reaches the object
  walk (s:0x9b5a80). A blocking edge is flags & 3 (s:0x9a7810). No radius, no BCRadius, no
  characterdata column, no model collision. A ridden horse or transport is the mover (s:0x4d2b20
  steps the COS and seats its rider; a riding PC does not step, s:0x4ef300). So a horse, a trade
  transport and a pet stop where a player on foot stops. The client's step does the same
  (c:0x9e0fca; flag 1 for the own player and own COS, 0 for others), so it predicts the stop.

## Eight-hundred-and-fiftieth round, lane E: the weapon and shield go away for the emotes and the stall

The user: "when doing action emoticons the weapon is supposed to disappear for most if not all, check
the original code to verify" and "stalls open with weapons too when they shouldn't".

**The switch (READ, sro_client.exe).** One function hides a character's held items:
`CCompChar` vtable slot 22 (`0x00c29bd0`, the render model `[[character+0x9c]+4]`, called through
`+0x58` with `(hide, which)`). For every part whose resource is an item (type 5) it reads the part's
attachable kind -- `CResAttachable` slot 3 (`0x00be60e0`) returns `+0x314`, and `+4` from it is the
word at `+0x318`, the trailing block's second word (`BsrReader.Attachable.kind`, meaning OPEN since
round 687) -- and for `which` 0 sets the part's draw flag `+0x98` to `!hide` when the kind is 6, 7, 14
or 15 (1: 7 and 15; 2: 6 and 14; no caller below passes them). The part's attached effects follow
(`FUN_00c44f40` -> `FUN_00c7b3a0` per effect of that part); a hide clears the afterimage (slot 35,
`0x00c275a0`). No fade: the flag is set in the call.

**MEASURED, what those kinds are** (`client/tools/census_attach_kind.gd`, every item model the item
table names, plain, `_l`, `_r`, `_f`, on the box's Data.pk2): kind 7 = every right-hand weapon
(swords, blades, spears, glaives, one- and two-handed swords, staves, rods, crossbows, a dual axe's or
dagger's `_r`; 3/1/6/2..16), kind 6 = every bow, harp, shield (3/1/4/1-2) and a dual axe's or dagger's
`_l`; kind 15 = two crossbow files; no item model carries 14. Armour, accessories, job suits and
avatars carry 0-5, 8, 16 or -1, never 6/7/14/15. So "the weapon" is exactly the weapon and the shield
models, both hands, and nothing worn (wings, dresses, hats stay).

**Who throws it (READ: all 15 calls of the dispatcher `FUN_009c92a0`).**
- **op 3, a body state's enter/leave** (`FUN_009c8900(phase, mask, byte)`):
  - **State 13, the emote** (mask 0x2000; enter `0xa59bc0` plays type 0x32+byte and calls it with
    phase 1, leave `0xa59c40` stops the clip with a 200 fade and calls phase 2): enter hides, leave
    shows -- **except Rush** (byte 2, action 4004): `0x9c897d` applies byte 2 only under the dev
    console's `Camera` toggle (`[0x110f80c]+0x3ce`, command string "Camera" registered at `0x5598f5`
    -> `0x542300`) or when a skill visual change keeps the weapon hidden (below). So Hi, Smile,
    Greeting, Yes, Joy and No take the weapon and shield away; Rush keeps them. Every player's emote is
    state 13 (`FUN_008a7950`: IsKindOf CICUser `0xef1bc0`, whose runtime class `CICUser::vslot_000`
    `0x9dc100` returns), so this client's own and another's alike.
  - **State 15, the vendor pose** (mask 0x8000; enter `0xa5a330` plays ANI_VENDOR01, type 80, leave
    `0xa59c90`): hide on enter, show on leave, for a CICUser only (`0x9c8957`) -- every stalling player,
    never a jinn pet in the same pose.
  - CICharactor slot 54 (`0x9db180`) runs the same leave for a state ended from outside.
  - When the state ends: its clip's end (`0xa59c30`, `push 0xd; call 0x9c8810`, a callback, INFERRED
    to be the clip-end one from its shape), or a new state whose clear mask (the record's last word,
    table `0xec5fb8`, MEASURED in .data) holds bit 13: states 1 (0xffcf), 9 (0x21a0), 12 (0x2004), 15
    (0xfffe). Which state a move is was not read (OPEN).
- **op 0** (`0x9c9630` / `0x9c9650`, from `CharacterVisualChange::Condition_SkillCodeName` /
  `Condition_Skill` slots 4/5, `0x4e92f0` / `0x4e8e20`, when the condition's `+0x10` is set): bit 0 of
  `+0x768`, "the weapon stays hidden" -- a state's leave then keeps it hidden, and Rush shows it.
  OpenSRO has no skill visual changes (OPEN).
- **op 1**, six skill decorations (`0xa4d660`, `0xa534d0`, `0xa53610`, `0xa53dd0`, `0xa54f00`,
  `0xa557f0`) by a byte of their skill data (`+0x60`, `+2`): not modelled (OPEN).
- **op 2**, `CCObjCharacter` slot 7 (`0xa5bcd0`), called from the clip starts `0xa5a930` / `0xa5b550`
  with (animation group, action type): shows the weapon, hides it for the groups `avatar_nasrun1..3`
  (the std::string globals `0xec6408/24/40`, initialised at `0xd77898..0xd778e8`), and leaves it alone
  for ANI_DAMAGE1 (3), ANI_DAMAGE2 (9) and ANI_PICK (38) -- the clips that can play inside an emote or a
  stall. Not modelled (OPEN: no nasrun avatar group in OpenSRO's look).
- **Not covered** (no call from their states): sitting, the pick-up (state 10), the fidgets, death,
  the job and transport states. The ride hides the same items by another rule (round 796,
  `CObjItem::vslot_003`).

**Built.**
- `HeldItems` (`client/scripts/world/held_items.gd`): the READ rule as pure functions
  (`state_effect`, `emote_hides`, `kind_hidden`), and `set_shown` / `state_of` on a body skeleton (by
  the node's attachable kind, `CharacterAppearance.ATTACH_KIND_META`, new; by its visual slot for a
  node without one).
- World3D: per character a set of reasons (`ride`, `emote`, `stall`; OURS) -- the held items are drawn
  when none holds. The emote's comes with 0x3091 (own and others', all but Rush) and goes when its clip
  is over or no longer on the body (the clip clock, not the wall's); Rush clears it (its enter is the
  previous emote's leave). The stall's follows `StallWorld.stalling` in `_stall_refresh`. Round 796's
  ride is now the third reason (`_set_held_items_shown` delegates). A re-dress -- a weapon swap or any

  skeleton is installed, `_step_held` as a backstop), so the new weapon never shows early and is

## Eight-hundred-and-fiftieth round, lane Q: the quest's map marks after a normal open

The user: "when seeing quest locations, they persist after closing the quest map and opening a normal
map. You're not supposed to see that when opening a normal map window." Labels: READ (sro_client.exe,
the decomp dump and objdump on the box), MEASURED, INFERRED, OURS, OPEN.

**OURS at merge (the user's call).** The lane built the original: the marks survive a close and M,
and only the first ground click brings the map back to the player. The user's case is exactly
"close the quest map, open a normal map", which the original still showed with marks. So
`HudWorldmap._close_quest_view` (on any hide outside the teleport selection) drops the quest's
marks and, if the quest's map left auto-move off with the stale flag, turns auto-move back on; the
next open is the player's own map with no quest on it. The quest stays tracked. The ground-click
rule stays as READ for a walk with the window open. `worldmap_quest850_test.gd` was rewritten to
check the OURS close (ALL PASS on the box's Media.pk2).

**When the original drops the marks (READ).** `0x61a620` (clears +0x229c0 areas, +0x229b0 painted
colours, +0x229d0 signs; nothing while +0x229ad is 0) has exactly five callers: `0x6256e0` (the next
quest's map button), `0x622dd0(1)` (the teleport selection), `0x624f40(m, 0, ..)` (a monster picked
in the guide list, `0x628f10` -> `0x628d30`; it also unchecks box 31), `0x6255c0` (box 31, the level
box: message-map entry `0xeb5600` -> handler `0xeb5610`, written by the init at `0xd6a130`) and the
destructor `0x621ed0`. +0x229ad is written only by `0x6256e0`, `0x624f40(.., 1, ..)`, `0x6255c0`
(set), `0x61a620` and the constructor `0x620c80` (clear). No code address holds a pointer to
`0x61a620`, `0x6256e0` or `0x624f40` (a byte search of the image), so there is no indirect caller.
- **Not cleared:** ShowWindow (`CNIFWorldMap::vslot_023` `0x624550`): its hide side only leaves the
  teleport selection, its show side refreshes the map; the close button (`vslot_043` = CNIFWnd
  `0x46d7c0` -> ShowWindow(0)); M (`0x780610` case 0x4d -> `0x79abe0` -> `0x46d740`); Escape
  (`0x79d620`); the quest list's button when the window is open (`0x6e51e0`, vslot 0x50); the
  quest's completion or abandon (`0x778d10` drops only the tracked id `DAT_00eeae70`).
- **What the original shows on a normal open:** ShowWindow(1) switches to the player's map only
  with auto-move on (`0x623060`), and centres only with it on. The quest's button turns auto-move off
  with the stale flag (+0x229ac = 1, +0x7b1 = 0). **The world's ground click turns it back on**:
  `0x793570` (CGInterface's left press), its no-object branch, after the walk `0x78f8d0` at
  `0x793a7d`, runs `0x793a84..0x793ad8`: outside the selection (`0x60fc40`, +0x9990 = 0), stale set
  (`0x60fc20`) and auto-move off (`0x60fc00`) -> `0x60fc30(0)`, `0x60fc10(1)`, written directly (button
  20 not redrawn). The only other writes of +0x7b1 = 1 are `0x616b80(1)` from the world set-up
  `0x786f30` and button 20. From then the render (`vslot_013`, `0x6243f8..0x62452a`) and ShowWindow
  put the player's own map up, centred on the player.
- **Where they draw:** `0x61e700` (areas) and `0x61e890` (signs) draw only in mode 0 (+0x97d0, the
  world map) or 2 (a floor), on their own map id. A local map (mode 1) never shows them.
- **So the original keeps the marks in three cases, built here as READ:** M (or the close button and
  M) straight after the quest's map, with no ground click between, shows the same map, scroll and
  marks; the world button (`0x6231e0`) brings them back on the world map; and in the field, where
  the player's map is the world map, they still draw where they are once the map follows the player.
- **The tracked quest** (`DAT_00eeae70`): the world map draws its NPCs (`0x61bac0`, each NPC of the
  0x30D5 list at its npcpos spot, the window's sign texture +0x7f4, every mode); the minimap draws them
  too (`CIFMinimap::vslot_013`, built in round 785). The world map's draw is not built (OPEN).

**The bug.** This client never had the ground click's branch: after a quest's map, auto-move stayed
off for good, so every later M showed the quest's world map at its scroll with the marks, however far
the player walked.

**Changed.**
- `HudWorldmap.ground_clicked` (0x793a84's rule), called from `World3D._dispatch_left_click`'s ground
  branch (after `_try_set_move_target`; items, characters and NPCs are objects there and do not pass).
  With the window shown it follows the player at once (the render's step).
- `_refresh_quest_marks`: marks only in mode 0 and 2 (READ above).
- QA: `quest_layer_counts()`, `quest_report` adds `stale=` and `layers=`; OPENSRO_QA_INPUT `wmquest`
  (the report) and `hit:<x>,<y>` (every Control that would take a press there -- it found the quest
  window swallowing a first ground click in the QA).
- `docs/protocol/quests.md` section 9 has the reading.

**Tests.** `worldmap_quest850_test.gd` (rules everywhere; the real Media.pk2 on the box): the click's
rule (selection, stale, button 20), and on the real map at Jangan: the quest's map (1/1 signs, 3/3
areas, auto off, stale), close keeps them, M straight after shows the same map and scroll, the ground
click then M shows map 1 centred as before (0/1, 0/3 shown), a mark on the local map's id stays hidden,
the world button shows them again, the next quest and the selection clear them. ALL PASS.

**Live QA** (render box, lane server 17200 in memory with the quest catalogue, character Qaq850, real
input through OPENSRO_QA_INPUT: `/level 5`, a click on Herbalist Yangyun, talk lines "Talk to this
person" -> "Yangyun's Anxiety" -> Accept -> OK, Escape, Q, row 5's button 18, the map's X at

| Button 18 | map 0, canvas (-3584, -266), 1/1 signs, 3/3 areas, auto off, stale | the same |

**Gates.** `remote_godot.sh check` ALL LOAD (1093 scripts); `tests` ran 410 suites, 0 failing. The

**OPEN.** The world map's tracked-quest NPC signs (`0x61bac0`) are not built. The guide list and box

had gated the debug panel on `DevTools.enabled()`, which defaulted to `OS.is_debug_build()`, so a
release download (`--export-release`) had no panel and Shift+F3 was retail's F3, page 3.

  still forces them on). The build type is no longer consulted. When the game ships to players,

  checks both sides of the toggle. MEASURED: 409 suites, 0 failing (render box,
  `/var/tmp/opensro-r849`). UI-only, no perf gate.

## Eight-hundred-and-forty-eighth round, lane T: native tooltips, scroll bars and context menus

The user: "Can you investigate all the cases where use the native gui and not the original gui?
Please find and fix all instances of this and make sure you match original as close as possible."
Lane T's part: Godot's tooltip popup, its scroll bars and its right-click menus, across the whole
client. Labels: READ (`c:` sro_client.exe, the decomp dump `/var/tmp/decomp_client` and
`/var/tmp/sro_client.asm` on the box), MEASURED, INFERRED, OURS, OPEN.

**What the original's tooltip is (READ).** Not a Windows tooltip: every CIFWnd / CNIFWnd keeps a
help string (`0x653dc0` / `0x46d7d0`) and style bit 0x80, and the interface has ONE help window,
`CIFHelperBubbleWindow` (GInterface +0x730; Create `0x776ea0`: `com_tooltip_corner.ddj` /
`com_tooltip_edge.ddj`, both borders 8 -- the same window the item and skill tooltips use, round
731's `CNIFHelperBubbleWindow` being its CNIF twin, `0x46cdf0`). Each frame `0xba5600` takes the
window under the cursor and `0xb9dbb0` sends 0x400a / 0x4009 on a change; `0x652fb0` / `0x46cee0`
answer 0x4009 on a bit-0x80 control with the show slot (`0x6528c0` / `0x46cdf0`) and 0x400a by
hiding the bubble. **No delay** (Godot's is 0.5 s). The show slot resizes the text box to 200
(`0x54(200, 1)`, INFERRED a wrap width), writes the text white (0xffffffff, font argument 1,
`0x7769a0`), sizes the window (14 px for one line, 18 a line for more, `0x777020`) and places it
from **the control's own rect**, not the cursor (`0x776c00` = `0x497350`): right of it with the
frame touching its edge, top aligned; flipped left when the box's right edge would come within 4 px
of the screen's (`x + w + width + 0x14 > screen`); a low box 7 px above the bottom
(`>= screen - 0xf`); no clamp on the left or the top. The CIF bubble hides itself while the cursor is
inside it (`0x776bb0`). Full record: `docs/protocol/item_tooltip.md`, "Round 848".

**The fix.** `HelpTips` (`client/scripts/ui/help_tips.gd`, autoload `NativeGuiGuard`): every frame
it takes Godot's hovered control, walks to the tooltip's owner the way Godot's own
`_gui_get_tooltip` does (so every `tooltip_text` and `_get_tooltip` site keeps its owner), and shows
the text in an `ItemTooltipBubble` on its own top layer (121) at once, white rows, wrapped at 200;
new text on the hovered control shows at once (`0x653dc0`); it hides on leave and while the cursor is
inside it. Godot's own popup is held off (`gui/timers/tooltip_delay_sec=1e+06`). Controls with
HudPanels' own item / skill bubble (metas `item_tip`, `bubble_tip`) are left to it.
`HelpTips.set_tip(control, rows | Callable | String)` gives a control coloured rows. One shared
placement: `ItemTooltipBubble.place` is now the READ `0x776c00` for items, skills and help alike
(round 731 had it OURS: flipped at the edge exactly, kept on screen at the bottom and left).

**Text inputs (READ).** The original's edit boxes are Win32 EDIT windows made at (-100, -100),
200 x 14 (`CIFEdit::Create 0x637a60`, `CNIFEdit::Create 0x47ae00`), subclassed (`0x637a30` ->
`0x636cd0`, which handles Ctrl+A/C/V/X/Z and the paste); the box a player sees is drawn by the
client, so a right click on it reaches the game window: **no context menu**. HelpTips turns off
Godot's context menu on every LineEdit and TextEdit as it enters the tree, and the middle-button
paste (X11 primary; the original's middle button is quick slot 0, `0x77c4cc`).

**Scroll bars (READ).** `CIFVerticalScroll::Create` (`0x65a9c0`) builds ifverticalscroll.txt's parts
over `com_scroll_bar.ddj` and gives the bar **the control's own rect height** as its length
(`0xb8f420` then `0x65a390(height, 0, 100, 1)`) unless the window's Create sets another -- which
makes `party_match_window.gd`'s "length is the record's 232 (INFERRED)" READ. `OriginalScroll`
(`client/scripts/ui/original_scroll.gd`) hides a native bar (zero width, nothing drawn, no clicks;
it still scrolls) and drives it from `HudChat.ChatScroll` (CIF) or `VScroll2dt` (CNIF), a line a step.

## Eight-hundred-and-forty-eighth round, lane H: the in-world HUD's boxes and inputs are the original's

The user: "Can you investigate all the cases where use the native gui and not the original gui?
Please find and fix all instances of this and make sure you match original as close as possible.
Make no mistakes." Lane H's area: the in-world HUD windows and their inputs (`ui/hud/*`,
`help_window.gd`, and the edits UiBuilder / TwoDtBuilder make). Labels: READ (`sro_client.exe`,
`/var/tmp/decomp_client` and `/var/tmp/sro_client.asm` on the box; wide strings read from the exe's
`.rdata` by section mapping), MEASURED, INFERRED, OURS, OPEN. Tooltips and native scroll bars are
lane T's; the debug panel and World3D are lane W's.

**What the original's edit is (READ).** `CIFEdit` keeps its own text buffer (`+0x5474`, at most
0x1000 characters) and caret; its Create (0x637a60) makes a hidden Win32 EDIT at (-100, -100) only
to own the keyboard and the IME, subclassed by 0x637a30 -> 0x636cd0. Keys (0x637290): End, Home,
Left, Right (one character each, 0x635460) and Delete; WM_CHAR Backspace, Enter, Tab / Escape (to
the parent with style 2) and characters from 0x20. No range selection, no word moves, no caret
placed by the mouse: a left press inside only gives the edit the focus (case 0x201 -> 0xb9d9f0).
With Ctrl, A / C / X / Z are swallowed; V pastes only with style 0x200, which only the developer
console sets (`push 0x1302` at 0x54170b); Shift+Insert is swallowed. Shift+Home / Shift+End set a
whole-text mark (`+0x41a`, 0x635030) drawn on background 0xff3b457a (0x635044); Home / End / Left /
Right clear it; Delete empties a marked edit (0x6354e0); a character or Backspace first empties it
(0x635720). The caret (draw 0x637b70): a quad 2.0 wide (`0xe1b898`) in the edit's FontColor
(`+0xa0`), tmHeight + 2 tall, shown while the blink flag `+0x3ec` is set and the edit has the focus;
the flag starts clear (0x637b50) and flips on each tick of a CETime set to 5 a second (0x637b3c ->
0xba9aa0(5): 200 ms). CIFEInputChatBox (the chat line) shares the draw and handlers; its Create
(0x65cf30) sets style 2 and a limit of 100 (0x634f80(100)).

**The hidden EDIT, checked against the stock control (READ, the coordinator's question).** Create
subclasses the EDIT (`SetWindowLongA(hwnd, GWL_WNDPROC, 0x637a30)`, the old procedure at `+0x384`);
0x636cd0 calls the stock EDIT (`CallWindowProcA`) only on its fall-through and returns 0 for
WM_PASTE 0x302, WM_UNDO 0x304, Ctrl + A / C / X / Z / V keydowns (V pastes, through its own
clipboard read 0x636bd0, only with style 0x200: the console's) and Shift+Insert. Ctrl+Left,
Shift+arrows, WM_CHAR 0x16 and EM_SETSEL do reach the stock EDIT -- an off-screen window
((-100, -100)) that is never drawn and never read back: the draw 0x637b70 reads the client's own
buffer, caret and mark, and the class (0x634300..0x638300) has no GetWindowText, WM_GETTEXT or
EM_GETSEL. The visible caret moves one character for Left / Right with or without Ctrl or Shift
(0x637290 cases 0x25 / 0x27, 0x635460: 1, or 2 for a surrogate pair); WM_CHAR 0x16 is below 0x20
and is not inserted. So CifEdit's no-paste, no-range-selection and one-character rules stand as
READ. Corrected: the limit (`+0x3fc`, 0x634f80) is compared with `+0x434`, the text's length in
**bytes** of the ANSI code page (0x4fc870 WideCharToMultiByte(CP_ACP) at 0x636416; the check
0x6375e6, the cut-back 0x63642a -> 0x6362d0), so CifEdit now holds `max_length` as bytes (the
player's code page INFERRED from the OS locale: two bytes a CJK character for ko / zh / ja). OURS:
Ctrl+Backspace deletes one character (the original's WM_CHAR 0x7f is inserted as U+007F). OPEN:
the Apps key (falls through to the stock EDIT's DefWindowProc).
