## Eight-hundred-and-forty-seventh round, lane B: a status effect's look ends with the status

The user: "sometimes the status effects cast on the players (maybe more?) lingers even after it's
been removed naturally or through pills. It eventually goes away but it takes awhile." Labels: READ
(`c:` sro_client.exe), MEASURED, INFERRED, OURS, OPEN. The reading and the numbers are
`docs/protocol/status_effects.md`, "How a state's look ends".

**How it was measured.** A lane server with prod's flags (no `-trust-client-positions`, the navmesh,
in memory) and two real clients on the render box: QaB847 afflicted with `/afflict` (typed through
the console at fixed ticks, the bag opened with `I` and the pills right-clicked in it) and Watch847
beside it, once with the afflicted player rendered and the observer headless, once the other way
round. Each run: a poison left to expire, a burn ended by the universal pill (ITEM_ETC_CURE_ALL_01),
a darkness ended by the purification pill (ITEM_ETC_CURE_RANDOM_01), a confusion left to expire, and
a bleeding on 1 HP that kills. Timing lines (commit `50467b69`): the server's "status sent" per
character mask, the client's receipt frame, and when each of the ended aura's effects stopped
drawing. Evidence: `/var/tmp/r847b/keep` (logs and contact sheets per path, before and after).

**The cause (MEASURED).** The server ended every state on time and told the owner and the observer
in the same pass (the status pass, the pill, the death); both clients took the message at once, and
the icons, the colour pulse and the clip speed ended with it. What lingered was the state's body
effect: the client let the `PARAM_` aura go (`EfpEffect.release`, round 785) and it played its
particles out -- by the probe (`client/tools/state_aura_release_probe.gd`) 0.5-4 s per state, and
confusion's `status_bad_temptation.efp` never ends by itself, so it drew until the 30 s one-shot
guard. Live, base: the observer drew poison 1.04 s, burn 2.47 s, darkness 1.54 s, bleeding 1.50 s
and confusion 29.97 s past the message; the owner's frames 40, 181, 90, 289 and over 1,042.

**What the original does (READ).** `c:FUN_009cd5e0` ends the bit's decoration through
`FUN_009cd2b0` -> `FUN_00a53120` -> `IDecoSkill::FUN_00a4ffe0` -> `FUN_00a4db00`, which starts an
alpha fade over the row's Fade first value (`FUN_00a48690` -> `FUN_00a48190`) and clears the keep
flag; `CIDecoSkill::vslot_014` frees the effect at alpha 0. Every `PARAM_` row's Fade is 300 ms
(MEASURED). So a state's look ends in 300 ms, fading, and the brief's "the moment the state ends"
is that fade -- the pulse, the speed and the icons are immediate.

**The fix** (`d915f9a5`): `SkillEffects._end_kept` -- a kept effect's end releases it and, with its
row's Fade (`EfpEffect.end_fade_ms`), fades it out over that many ms and frees it. Every state aura
and every buff aura (0xB072 and the grace end) goes this way; a row with no Fade still plays out
(87 of the 146 ACT_L AT_LOOP rows). **After**, the same schedule: every aura on every path gone 18
frames (300 ms) after the message, owner and observer, confusion included; headless 297-332 ms.

**Tests.** `server/internal/session/status847_test.go`: expiry (and none before its time), the
universal pill, the purification pill, a death by a bleeding tick, and a renewal ending at its own
time, each reaching the owner and the observer. `client/scripts/world/state_end847_test.gd`: the
same paths through World3D's `_on_object_status` on this player and on another player's body (fade
at 150 ms, gone at 300, the pulse gone at once, a cure of one of two, a renewal keeping one aura);
`skill_effects_test.gd`: a buff aura's Fade end and the grace end.

**OPEN.** A cast's kept loops (`SkillEffects.stop_all`) take the same `FUN_00a4ffe0` path in the
original and are still only let go. The buff bar's own abnormal icons are not drawn by OpenSRO (an
older OPEN). OURS: another player's 0x3057 waits behind a player group being spawned. The target
and party windows' icons refresh every 1000 ms, READ, as the original's. Teleport: OpenSRO's server
drops a character's states when a pass finds her out of the world and the client clears its books on
the zone change; whether the original keeps them through a teleport is not read.

**Gates.** `go test ./...` ok; `check` ALL LOAD (1073 scripts); `tests` 403 suites, 0 failing;
perf (`--base f2a20b92 --head d915f9a5 --sites jangan --frames 24000`, median of 3):

| jangan | base | head | |
|---|---|---|---|
| frame ms | 0.87 | 0.87 | SAME |
| entry ms | 10204 | 10077 | SAME |
| freeze ms | 2773 | 2790 | SAME |
| hitches | 5 | 5 | SAME |

control master. The gate was rerun with ssh unmultiplexed.)

## Eight-hundred-and-forty-seventh round, lane A: the select screen draws a model switcher's model, and one CharacterLook for every body

The user: "another bug to fix: the character selection doesn't reflect model changers. Make sure it
shows what it's supposed to show from now on. Shouldn't there be a class or something that is
basically the visual rep of the character and things can call it so we're not changing it in 30
places?" Labels: READ (`sro_client.exe`, `/var/tmp/decomp_client`), MEASURED, INFERRED, OURS, OPEN.
The reading, the model and the census of sites are `docs/protocol/character_look.md`; the switcher's
side is `docs/protocol/item_switchers.md` 3b.

**What retail's select screen draws (READ).**
- The 0xB007 list handler (`FUN_0085f840`) reads a count and the records (`FUN_0085e620`) and dresses
  each model (`PSCharacterSelect::FUN_0085a580`); nothing is read after the last record.
- Per worn item the record carries a u32 RefItemID and a u8 plus (at most 9: equip slots 0..8, the job
  suit's slot 8 among them); per avatar a u32 RefItemID and a byte the client discards (at most 5).
- Each item is installed with `InstallEquipVisual(vslot, id, plus, 0)` (0xa61010), which keeps the plus
  beside the slot; when the item's resource has loaded, `FUN_00a60a90` calls `FUN_00a5f3e0` with both:
  the glow row and the seal's and +8 sparkle's particles, the world's path. **So the select screen draws
  the glow and the seal** (`charselect.md` had it INFERRED). The job suit is installed into vslot 8 like
  any item (no job-state test). Only 3/1/13 avatars are attached (`FUN_00a60ef0`, no plus); a devil's
  spirit is not. The scale byte goes through `FUN_00a5b960`, as in the world.

**The cause (MEASURED).** OpenSRO's list builder (`lobbyhandler.go` `record`) named each worn item's own
row, so a switched item was drawn as its original model, where the world, the doll and the previews
drew the model (rounds 838 and 843). The record has no room for the own id.

**The fix (OURS).**
- The record names the drawn row (`displayRef`), as the spawn record and 0x3038 do.
- The list carries the own ids in a trailer after the last record, only when some item is switched:

## Eight-hundred-and-forty-sixth round, lane M: every step another player takes, walked

The user: "if I take small steps it doesn't register on another client. It only registers when I take
a large step and it shows that I teleported away", and "it only seems to happen at a higher /speed but
it might be part of underlying bug". Labels: READ (`c:` sro_client.exe, `s:` SR_GameServer.exe),
MEASURED, INFERRED, OURS, OPEN. The reading is `docs/protocol/opcodes/movement.md`, "How an observer
keeps up, and every step reaches it".

**How it was measured.** A lane server with prod's movement flags (no `-trust-client-positions`,
`-navmesh-dir` with round 812's meshes, `-full-map`, in memory), two real clients on the render box: a
headless actor walking real ground clicks (`OPENSRO_QA_WALK_TO` -> `_issue_walk`, the click's own
path) and arrow keys (`OPENSRO_QA_INPUT down:Up`, `up:Up`, `down:Left`) at `/speed` 1, 2, 5, 7 and
10, and a rendered observer in real time (`QA_SHOT_REALTIME=1`, 60 fps), each through a delay proxy
(OURS, QA only: 40 ms ± 20 ms, then 100 ms ± 40 ms each way). Per frame: the actor's position
(`MOVE self`), what it sent (`MOVE send`), what the observer heard (`MOVE recv`) and drew (`MOVE
body`), lined up per step on the 0x7021 and the 0xB021 naming the same point
(`/var/tmp/r846m/keep/ana846.py`). The schedule: per speed a 30-unit click, eight small clicks
(1-5 units) 1.5 s apart, the same 0.33 s apart, eight 0.1 s apart, a 20-unit click with a click near
its end, a 40-unit click, three Up taps (0.1 s, 0.25 s, a hold), a Left turn and an Up tap.

**The causes (MEASURED, base `857ec7be`).** The server took and echoed every step that reached it
(the observer heard 127 of 130 0x7021, the 3 after its run ended), the observer walked every echo it
heard, at the speed `/speed` set (the token-less `OpBuffEnd`; a late observer reads the spawn record's
run speed), and no frame jumped further than 3.2x the speed. The faults were in what the mover did
with its own steps:

1. **The mover's own walk ended 2.39 short of every click** (`MOVE_TARGET_STOP_DISTANCE`, OURS since
   round 649 for every walk), while the server and every observer walked to the point. Small steps
   1.5 s apart at 1x: the actor moved 1.17 on average, the observer drew 3.36, all 10 ended apart;
   2x 1.83 / 3.22, 10 of 10; 5x 2.18 / 2.85, 5 of 11; 10x 2.53 / 2.88, 3 of 11. A click under 2.39 away
   moved nobody and sent nothing: in the 0.1 s bursts the actor moved 0.00-0.71 while the observer drew
   2.4-3.2 a click. READ (`c:FUN_009e0e60`, round 649): retail's mover lands on its destination.
2. **A click within 5.0 of the point still being walked to was walked here and never sent** (the
   server would refuse it, READ `s:0xb45b28`): the mover stood up to 5 from where the server and the
   others had it, until a stop put it there in one jump. READ: retail's server refuses it and its
   client walks only on its echo, so nothing moves.
3. **A click near the point just reached reached the server while its leg still ran** -- this client
   walks at once, the server one transit later -- and was refused silently; a second later
   (`ECHO_TIMEOUT_MS`) the walk stopped and the stop went out as a `0xB023`: no step, then a jump.
4. **An observer put a body on the 0xB021's source whenever it was more than 32 from it** (the
   monsters' rule) and walked every leg at the bare speed.

So the difference from the user's words: the observer did draw the small steps it was told of, but
the mover's own screen and the others' disagreed on almost every small step (by up to the 2.39 stop
plus a truncation, 1.6-2.7 units), the mover's sub-2.39 clicks did nothing at all, and a click near the
last point, at any speed, could vanish and come back as a jump a second later. INFERRED: those are
what read as "doesn't register" and "teleported"; at a raised `/speed` a 30-40 unit step is drawn in
4-8 frames on every client, the original's included, which reads as a jump by itself.

**What the original does (READ, re-read this round).** `c:NetProcessInNavAndSkill::FUN_008a5750`
puts the flag-1 source through `FUN_009e11e0`, which moves the mover's record (`+0x4c`) and re-places
the drawn object only when `FUN_009e1050` finds the two more than 50.0 apart (double `0xd8f0b0`;
`FUN_009ecdb0`, a 3-D distance); `FUN_009e0550` then sets the mover's speed factor `+0x8c` to the drawn
object's ground distance to the destination over the record's, at most 3.0 (float `0xd8adc4`; 3.0
when the record is on the point, `0xe1b808`), 1.0 when the object is no farther; the tick
`FUN_009e0e60` multiplies the walk/run speed by it. INFERRED: a body drawn behind walks on and arrives
with the server's mover. The server (`s:GObjPC::FUN_004b0ea0`) refuses a destination within 5.0 of the
one it walks to and takes every other; nothing is sent per step or on arrival. A correction to
movement.md: flag 1 does not snap the object or clear its order on the ordinary branch.

## Eight-hundred-and-forty-fifth round, lane K: the quest detail's colours and the quest list's map button

The user: "fix the bug where ready quest text on its special window is white and unreadable. It's
supposed to be color coded. Usually orange headers and black regular text. Also the map icon in the
quest menu for each quest should show where the quest area is. If not it will throw an error in the
log window on the right." Labels: READ (sro_client.exe, `c:`), MEASURED, INFERRED, OURS, OPEN. The
readings with every address are `docs/protocol/quests.md` sections 8 and 9.

**Which window.** The quest detail -- the parchment the quest list's content-view button (row control
19) opens: CIFQuestReward on `resinfo\ifquestreward.txt`, its text the quest's `SN_PAYCON_<Q>` in the
CIFPML 18. Round 785 drew that markup as plain text in a Godot RichTextLabel whose default colour is
white, on the white parchment (MEASURED on the old build's frame: 2870 white text pixels, no other text
colour, in the contents box). The reward window OpenSRO opens on 0x3514 is drawn on the same paper
(OURS since round 785) and had the same white text.

**What the original does (READ).**
- The text is `<sml2>` markup (MEASURED, textquest_otherstring: 997 strings; tags `sml2`, `br`,
  `font`, `strong` only): headers `<strong><font color="255,226,74,0"> ◈ Mission</font></strong>`,
  the plain lines with no `<font>`, the scenario inside `<font color="255,44,15,1">`.
- CIFPML's parser (0x9b2160 / 0x9b23e0 / 0x9b1e40) reads a colour as A,R,G,B; the draw (0x8b48b0)
  replaces the alpha with its own. So headers RGB (226, 74, 0), the scenario (44, 15, 1).
- A run outside `<font>` takes the control's own colour: the layout (0x64b2c0) starts its state stack
  from the window's +0xa0, which the ResInfo loader fills from the record's FontColor (0x82c7c1,
  0x8b56c5 -> 0x8b2b70) -- `GDR_QUESTREWARD_CONTENTS` FontColor 255,0,0,0: **black**.
- `<strong>` pushes the state with style 2 (0x9b0f6b), the face's weight-600 variant; the title 17 is
  in that face too (CIFQuestReward OnCreate 0x6e4fa4: 0x8b44b0(5, 2)) and white (its FontColor).
- Lines: a run's height is its face's tmHeight (0x8b3040), the line margin 5 (0x64b2c0), so text lines
  are tmHeight + 5 apart and a `<br><br>` adds only 5 (an empty line is 0 tall). Word wrap at the
  box's width after the last space (0x8b3ef0).
- The scroll: pixels, range 0..content - 247, step 1, the wheel 6 px a notch (0x649c30, vslot_036); the
  scroll bar 15 with gd_scroll_up / gd_scroll_down / gd_scroll_button and the track qst_scroll_line,
  length 247 - 48 (0x6e5020..0x6e50b5, 0x65a390).
- The data's 20 doubled-quote colours (`color=""255,226,74,0""`, QEV_ALL_BASIC3_*) read A = 0 and

## Eight-hundred-and-forty-fourth round, lane V: guild war

The user (2026-10-29): "Add guild storage and all other guild functionality." Guild war is lane V's part:
the original's war, both sides, built exactly. Labels: READ (s: SR_GameServer.exe, m: SR_ShardManager.exe,
c: sro_client.exe), MEASURED (Media.pk2), INFERRED, OURS, OPEN. The full reading, every address and every
byte: [docs/protocol/guild_war.md](protocol/guild_war.md).

**What the original does (READ unless marked).**
- **Where and who.** The guild window's tab 73 "Guild rel." > sub-tab 88 "Hostility" (CNIFHostileGuild 2000,
  `guild_r.2dt`) lists the hostile guilds (name, "-", the crest) with a details pane (the leader and member count
  always "Unconfirmed"); its 52 "Request to start the war" is the master's only, 53 "Request to end the war" the
  master's with a war and no countdown (c:0x5bca80). Tab 74 "Combat" (CNIFGuildWar 548, `guild_w.2dt`) shows
  the war: the enemy, both scores, the victory points, the stakes, the time left, the members' contribution.
- **Declaring.** CIFRequestGuildWar's three states (`ifguildwarrequest/confirm/agree.txt`): the name, the victory
  points (Unlimited or 5000..300000), the period in days / hours / minutes (each "Unlimited" too) and a stake up to
  500,000,000; client refusals SELFWAR, name length, the filter, LIMIT_COMPENSATION; 0x7110 {str, u8 0, u32
  period, u8 index, u32 stake}. The server (s:0x5c6b60): the target master online **within 300.0** (the masters
  meet), then the ladder (0x4c0d, 2, the master 0x4c1e, gold 0x4c43, the cap 0x4c5e, 50 wars 0x4c3e / 0x4c3f,
  already 0x4c3a, the union 0x4c41). The target master gets 0x3080 kind 10 and an Agreement box (OK disabled
  below the stake), 30 s; his {1, 1} begins the war and **both masters pay the stake**; LodgedGold is both.
- **During.** 0x3109 / 0x38F5 0x19 put the enemy in the hostile map: its guild lines **red** 0xffff0000, its
  members' **names 0xffff6262**, its members **enemies without Alt** (the hostile sword), the level-20 rule
  waived; the server lets them fight **anywhere but towns**, before the PK rules (s:0x5293a0). A kill scores
  **15 d + 100** (1 at d <= -6, 251 above 10; d = victim's level less killer's), counts kills / deaths /
  contribution, tells both guilds (0x1d, KILLNEWS banner); a victim above level 10 loses 20 x the exp unit.
- **Ending.** By time (past the end with the scores apart; a tie runs on), by the victory points, or by the
  end proposal, which is a **surrender**: 0x7112, a minute of countdown (0x1a / 0x1b, ENDCOUNT and "Until the end
  of war (%d seconds left)"), then the other guild wins. 0x1c: Won / Lost in a box, the lines back. The
  winner's guild keeps both stakes as booty: the master's guild manager line 0x1b "War reward gold received"
  (0x7114, any member may ask; 0x7113 the master claims). A guild at war cannot disband (0x4c46).
- **Persistence.** The ShardManager keeps _GUILDWAR (a wall-clock end, points per kill) and _GUILD.Booty.

**The user's description against the original.** Nothing to report: the user asked for "all other guild
functionality"; war is the original's own feature, built as read.

**What we built.**
- Server: `guild/war_rules.go` (the rules, the wire), `war_store.go` + `sqlstore_war.go` (MemStore and SQLStore:
  `guild_wars`, `guild_war_booty`, self-created; the members' counters), `session/guildwar.go` (0x7110 and its
  question, the answer in the 0x3080 chain, kills from the PvP blow, the 1 s end check and the 60 s time sync,
  the surrender, the reward, 0x3109 after every guild block, the disband refusal, the war cache read per blow),
  `jobs.AttackCode`'s hostile argument, the KilledByPlayer death multiplier, lane U's `unionHostile` (0x4c42)
  answered by the war, `/union` refused at war. OURS QA aids: `/guildwar`, `/guildwar end <guild> [s]`,
  partybot `-war-answer`, `-war-declare`, `-war-surrender-after`.
- Client: `GuildWarNet`, `HostileData` (in GuildData), `GuildWarPanes` (the two panes), `GuildWarRequestBox`
  (three states), `GuildWarUi` (the boxes, the banners, the countdown, the reward), the red lines and enemy names,
  IsEnemy and the level waiver (`JobPvpNet`), the master's NPC line 0x1b.

## Eight-hundred-and-forty-fourth round, lane H: the guild storage

The user's ask: "Add guild storage and all other guild functionality." This lane is the guild storage
(the guild warehouse), end to end. Labels: READ (sro_client.exe `c:`, SR_GameServer.exe `s:`),
MEASURED, INFERRED, OURS, OPEN. The whole reading, with every address, is
`docs/protocol/guild_storage.md`.

**What the original does (READ).**
- **Where.** The guild manager (interaction 0x0f; Jangan's Guild Manager Leebaek), talk line 0x1d
  "Use guild storage. (level 2 or above)" for every member, drawn 0xffff4a4a below guild level 2
  (`FUN_006fcd60`). The line sends 0x7046 {npc, 0x0f}; its 0xB046 sends 0x7250 {npc}; 0xB250 {1}
  opens GDR_GUILDSTORAGEROOM (ID 0x91, the personal storage's CIFStorageRoom and ifstorageroom.txt,
  "Guild storage") with the inventory beside it, then 0x7252 lists it as 0x3253 {u64 gold}, 0x3255
  pieces, 0x3254 (u8 size, u8 n, n x {slot, item record}).
- **Who.** The master, or a member with permission bit 0x08 (0x4c1e "You are not authorized."); a
  guild of level 2 or more (0x4c4a "Guild level must be 2 or higher to use guild storage."). Sizes 30 /
  60 / 90 / 120 by level (the table s:0xc6b5f0).
- **One at a time.** The ShardManager's job 0x24 holds the guild's holder; a second member gets
  0x4c48 with the holder's name ("At the moment guild member %s is using guild storage, so it cannot
  be opened."). The holder cannot leave or be expelled and the guild cannot be disbanded (0x4c48), and
  bit 0x08 cannot be taken from the holder (0x4c4c). A disband takes the items with it
  (UIIT_MSG_GUILD_BREAK_ANOTHER_EXPLAIN).
- **Moves.** 0x7034 types 0x1d (inside: move, merge or swap; no split), 0x1e (bag -> storage: the
  whole stack, never merged, the fee **half** the warehouse's: `KeepingFee x count x 0.5`, 1 to
  10,000,000), 0x1f (storage -> bag, free), 0x20 / 0x21 (gold in / out, INTERACTMODE 6). The deposit
  refuses quest and event items (3/3/9) and untradeable ones (0x1843).

**What was built.**
- Server: `internal/guildstorage` (the rules, `Service` over the bag, the storage container keyed by
  guild id, the purse and the guild's gold, each action one transaction; `Locks`; the mem and SQL gold
  stores, `guild_storage_gold` and `guild_storage_slots` created by the schema code);
  `session/guildstorage.go` (0x7250..0x7252, the 0x7034 types, the disconnect release,
  `GuildStorageHolder` for the other guild requests); the leave, expel and disband refusals
  (guildops.go, four small checks); `/guildperm` (GM test tool, OURS); partybot `-gstore`.
- Client: `GuildStorageNet` / `GuildStorageState` (the wire, the kept list), `GuildStorageController`
  (the window with the shared slot code -- `_set_item_slot_fx`, tooltips, the held icon -- the
  deposit, withdraw and gold boxes at the original's purposes 0x10..0x13, Escape and the X sending
  0x7251), the talk line and its red, World3D's 0x0f arm and QA actions `gscell`, `gsgold`,
  `gsclose`, `gsreport`.

**Live QA (MEASURED; real input, Mate a partybot master, QaWin the rendered member; frames in
/var/tmp/r844h/keep on the render box).**

## Eight-hundred-and-forty-fourth round, lane G: the guild window, the guild manager and the member highlight

The user (2026-10-29): "Add guild storage and all other guild functionality. Also when selecting members in a
guild on the guild window there's a yellow highlight around the name. We don't have that. replicated that
behavior."

Labels: READ (c: sro_client.exe, s: SR_GameServer.exe), MEASURED, INFERRED, OURS, OPEN. The full readings are in
docs/protocol/guild.md, "The guild window and the guild manager (round 844, lane G)". The census of every guild
opcode, window and NPC line, with each one's owner lane, is docs/protocol/guild_census.md.

**What the original does.**
- **The highlight (READ, MEASURED).**
  - A guild row is a CNIFBarWnd. A left press selects it (c:0x5b8790, message 0x201 only).
  - The selected row's art becomes `com_bar01select_` and every other row's `com_bar01_` (c:0x5b7090).
  - The select art is the plain bar plus a 1-px (255, 178, 82) frame inset 2 px. It is a frame, not a fill.
  - Nothing changes on hover. A refill keeps the selection on the same member (c:0x5b8580).
  - The friend list does the same (c:0x5a8700).
  - The party matching and the stall network already swap or overlay the art correctly.
- **The window.**
  - Headers 400..403 sort the list by name, level, class or GP (c:0x5ba310).
  - Button 23 cycles the shown name: name, grant name, fortress position (c:0x5ba970).
  - Scroll 21 scrolls the list.
  - The notice bar opens the body's view 1200; its pencil opens CIFGuildNotifyWrite (0x70F9).
  - Button 38 opens the permission pane CNIFGuildGrantPow (0x7104: invite, expel, union chat, storage,
    notice; union chat holds 12 at most).
  - Button 250 opens CIFGuildPointUp: SP becomes GP (0x7258).
  - Button 41 is the fortress positions (0x70FF), out of scope.
  - There is **no right-click or double-click on a member**: the row handles 0x201 only. So the original's
    guild list has no whisper and no party invite.
- **The guild manager** (FUN_00700440).
  - The master's lines: 0x17 promote (CIFGuildLevelUp, 0x70FA), 0x14 disband, 0x18 transfer leadership
    (CIFGuildMasterLeave, 0x7103), 0x1b the war's reward gold.
  - Every member's lines: 0x19 / 0x1a the master-release vote, 0x1d the storage, 0x43 GP usage history.
- **The hand-over (READ s:0x5c46e0).**
  - The new master gets class 0, mask 0xffffffff and siege role 1; the old one gets 10, 0 and 0.
  - It goes out as 0x38F5 type 0x16 mask 0x54.
  - This settles round 821's INFERRED masks: master all bits, member 0.
- **Agent A's reading** (0x70F6 dead, 0x7202 / 0x7203 not guild, every 0x38F5 type) is in the census.

**What was wrong.** `GuildWindow._mark_row` added the select bar and moved it to index 0, which put it
**under** the row's own opaque `com_bar01_` bar, so nothing showed. The guild and friend lists share that code.
The window had no order, name modes, scroll, notice view or write, permission pane or donation. The guild manager
had no level-up or hand-over line.

**What we built.**
- **Server (`guild/manage.go`, `wire_manage.go`, `memstore_manage.go`, `sqlstore_manage.go`,
  `session/guildmanage.go`):** the five requests in the original's order of checks, with their replies and
  0x38F5 broadcasts; the 0x38F5 types 0x14 and 0x16.
  - The notice applies the chat ban and the quote drop, then the byte limits 0x80 / 0x800.
  - Lane H's storage hook for 0x4c4c is `session.GuildStorageUser`.
  - SP comes from the skill store; `main` calls `SetGuildDonateSkills`.
  - There is no schema change: the stores use round 821's columns.
- **Client.**
  - `GuildWindow`: the art swap, the order, the name modes, the scroll, the notice view, the permission pane,
    the button rules.
  - The windows `GuildNoticeWrite`, `GuildDonateWindow`, `GuildLevelUpWindow`, `GuildMasterLeaveWindow`.
  - `GuildManageNet`, `GuildData` 0x14 / 0x16, and the NPC lines 0x17 / 0x18 (`NpcServiceReader`).
  - QA input `guildnode:`, `hudnode:`, `guildreport`.
- **OURS.**

## Eight-hundred-and-forty-fourth round, lane U: unions for players

The user's ask (round 844): "Add guild storage and all other guild functionality." Lane U's part: unions
complete for players -- the request and the Agreement box, leave, expel and the union broken, the union
tab in the guild window, union chat, the union's messages and its emblem, the GM's /union kept. Labels:
READ (`c:` sro_client.exe, `s:` SR_GameServer.exe, `sm:` the ShardManager's decompile on the box),
MEASURED, INFERRED, OURS, OPEN. The whole reading: `docs/protocol/guild_union.md`.

**What the original does (READ unless marked).**
- **Request.** Only the union tab's Apply (51) sends 0x70FB {u32 the selected object} (`c:0x8201b0`, its
  one caller the tab's dispatcher `c:0x57d060`; a pet stands for its owner); no target-menu route. The
  server (`s:0x5170b0` -> `s:0x5c6550`): reach 3, dead 0x4c07, no guild 0x4c0d, not the master 0x4c1e, **a
  requester in a union led by another guild 0x4c1e**, own level < 2 0x4c2a, target 3 / no guild 0x4c25 /
  hostile 0x4c42 (INFERRED from `UIIT_MSG_QUESTION_GUILD_RESPECT_ALLY_NOTALLY`) / same guild 0x4c26 /
  level < 2 0x4c2b / in a union 0x4c28 / not its master 0x4c24; then 0x3080 {6, requester} to the target
  and nothing to the requester. Refusals 0xB0FB {2, code}, shown through the guild category (0x4c2e,
  0x4c10, 0x4c2f, 0x4c30 have no row: nothing).
- **Agreement box 0x1d** (`c:0x88afb4`, `c:0x647a01`): 470 x 144, "Apply", "The leader of [%s] guild
  proposed an alliance with you. Do you accept?", the line 0x4c right, OK / Cancel 0x51 right, its timer;
  Yes {1, 1}, No **{2, u16 0}** (`c:0x798667`). The answer (`s:0x5c8510` kind 6): No 0x4c2e to the
  requester; Yes the ShardManager's join (`sm`: 0x4c0d, 0x4c25, 0x4c28, 0x4c24, **0x4c29 when the union's
  eight slots are full** -- raised by the ShardManager, not the GameServer, which round 717's alliance.go
  searched); no 0xB0FB on success; 30 s -> 0xB0FB {2, 0x4c10} to the requester only.
- **Told.** Formed: both guilds 0x3102 (no line); joined: the new guild 0x3102, the others 0x38F5 0x0d
  ("An alliance with [%s]guild has been formed."); out: {0x12, how, guild} to every guild including the one
  leaving, 0xB0FC / 0xB0FD {1} to the asker, and **{0x12, 3} "Guild alliance has been broken." to those

## Eight-hundred-and-forty-fourth round, lane G (part 2): the leader vote, GP usage history, the guild recall and the guild goods

This part builds what the census still listed as missing in lane G's area.
- Labels: READ (c: sro_client.exe, s: SR_GameServer.exe, sm: the ShardManager), MEASURED, INFERRED, OURS, OPEN.
- The full readings are in docs/protocol/guild.md, "The vote, the GP history, the recall and the guild goods (round
  844, lane G part 2)".
- docs/protocol/guild_census.md now marks these rows built.

**What the original does.**
- **The master-release vote** (0x7105-0x7107, 0x3908; lines 0x19 / 0x1a; CIFGuildMasterElection).
  - Who may start it, READ from s:0x5c6ac0 and the procedure `_Guild_Master_Election_Available`: any member, once
    the master is offline and last logged out **45 days** ago or more.
  - Who is listed, READ from `_Guild_Is_Master_Candidators`: the members online or last seen **7 days** ago or
    less, the master excluded.
  - It lasts 600,000 ms, checked every 10 s.
  - A candidate wins the moment `votes * 100 / n >= 60.0`, where n is the list's size (READ sm:0x461a50).
  - The winner takes the guild through the hand-over's path. With no winner, the vote breaks.
- **GP usage history** (line 0x43; 0x7501 / B501; `res_ui\guild_gp.2dt`, READ).
  - It records GP spent only: the level-up (kind 5) and guild items (kind 6). The fortress kinds are out of scope.
  - It keeps the newest 100 entries from the last 30 days.
- **The guild recall** (itemdata 9267; 0x7030 / 0x7031 / B031, READ).
  - Only the master can use it, with the guild at level 5 or more, in a town, outside the thieves' town and the
    instance worlds. It can be used once an hour.
  - Every online member is asked for 180 s. A yes moves the member to the master's spot after 0.1 s.
- **The guild goods**, READ from CheckCurrencyRequirement s:0x617360.
  - They cost gold and the guild's GP, and only the master can buy them (0x18c4 / 0x18c5).
  - The tooltip and the buy box show the GP price.
  - The store refuses to open below guild level 3.
- **Union chat** needs permission bit 0x04 (the master always has it), and at most 12 members can hold it.

**What we built.**
- **Server** (7f9152b6, 4d544a78):
  - `guild/vote.go`, `gphistory.go` and `gpspend.go`, each with a mem and a SQL store. The schema code adds
    `guild_members.last_logout` and creates `guild_gp_history`.
  - `session/guildvote.go`, `guildgphistory.go`, `guildrecall.go` and `guildgoods.go`.
  - `mall`'s new "npcgp" rows carry the goods' GP prices.
  - The hand-over shares `handOver` with the vote's win. While a vote runs, leaving and expelling are blocked.
  - Each logout is recorded.
  - Test tools (OURS): `/guildabsent <member> <days>` and `/guildgp <n>`.
  - partybot flags: `-guild-recall-answer`, `-quit-after` and `-guild-perm`.
- **Client** (6ac7a953 and the docs commit):
  - `GuildPart2Net`, `GuildElectionWindow` and `GuildGPHistoryWindow`.
  - The member lines 0x19 / 0x1a / 0x43.
  - The recall question box and its gauge.
  - The goods' GP tooltip line and buy-box row, and the level-3 store gate.
  - The event box's caption, UIIT_STT_EVENTGUIDE "Alarm".
  - QA input actions `cmd:`, `storebuy:` and `storetip:`.
- **INFERRED / OURS.**
  - The day count uses UTC calendar days (INFERRED).
  - The vote is kept in memory only (OURS, like the ShardManager's).
  - A ballot with an index out of range gets error code 2 (OURS).
  - The recall box's English text is empty in the archive, so a stand-in is shown (OURS).
  - The constants are `guild.VoteMasterAbsentDays` (45), `VoteEligibleDays` (7), `VoteDuration`,
    `VoteWinPercent` (60) and `VoteTick`.

## Eight-hundred-and-forty-third round, lane Q: the quest scroll's flicker

The user's ask: "Can you please also remove the flickering quest icons that appear above NPCs", with a
2.1 s clip of the golden scroll over Stable-Keeper Machun (Jangan) whose glow jumps between bright and
dim from frame to frame, camera still. Reading: the original does draw these marks (round 785), so
"remove the flicker" means drawing the mark as the original does. Labels: READ (sro_client.exe, c:),
MEASURED, INFERRED, OURS, OPEN. The reading with every address is `docs/protocol/EFP_FORMAT.md`, "The
order of one effect's particles".

**The mark (MEASURED, `efpcensus -show`).** `system_questmark_start.efp` is a holder (1 frame), then
`quest_sign_shine.ddj` (SRCALPHA/ONE, colour 0xFDBE02 with alpha keyed 0x8C -> 0x48 -> 0x8C over 30
frames: the original's slow pulse) and `quest_sign_a.ddj` (SRCALPHA/INVSRCALPHA, scale (5, 5, 1)), two
billboards at one point. `_end` is the same with `quest_sign_c`; `_start_r` has the scroll first and the
shine second; `_going` is its scroll alone.

**The cause.**
- MEASURED, the user's clip (65 x 55 box on the scroll, 63 frames): mean 128.9, sd 4.17, frame-to-frame
  jumps up to 9.5; the bright-pixel count is bimodal, 61-75 in 21 frames and 226-335 in the other 42. The
  dim frames show the scroll crisp, its ink and rolled ends dark, with the halo still around it; the
  bright ones show the shine added over the scroll. That is the shine drawn under or over the scroll,
  not a glow switched off (no occlusion toggle, no restart: the halo stays).
- MEASURED on the box, one still view (`qa843.sh`, local NPCs, `OPENSRO_QA_QUEST_MARKS=0`): a movie
  run drew the shine over the scroll (bright pixels 259-399), a real-time run (`QA_SHOT_REALTIME=1`,
  xcapture, 481 distinct frames over 25 s) under it (95-138). Same build, same view, opposite orders.
- Why: each node is its own MultiMesh with the same transform and cull box (`DRAW_AABB`) at one render
  priority, so Godot's transparent depth sort ties them, and its sort is not stable (OURS reading of
  the engine: an introsort). INFERRED: in a live town, things moving around change the sort's input
  every frame, which flips the tie; the box's still scenes keep one order a run (also with damage
  numbers or casts in view, `xc3c` / `xc4c`).
- Ruled out: the mark is a plain effect (QuestMarks), not an ambient glow, so round 807's occlusion
  test and the glow pass never touch it; its fog fade is steady with the camera; the loop restarts on
  the 30-frame period, not at random.

**What the original does (READ).** The effect's particles sit on one list in spawn order (c:0x00c8878d,
the list at +0x258). The update (CEFEffect::vslot_000 -> c:0xcaeff0; `DAT_00edbd44` is 1 in .data and
nothing writes it) walks it from the tail, newest first, filing particles by texture then RenderState,
new groups last; the draw (CEFEffect::vslot_001) draws the groups in that order. Children run in the
child list's order (c:0xc86cd0, CEFUpdater::vslot_002; INFERRED the file's). So the scroll draws first
and the shine is added over it, every frame: the bright look, pulsing slowly. For `_start_r` the
scroll is over the shine.

**What we built (OURS).** `EfpEffect.DRAW_ORDER_STEP`: every plate, mesh and Link draw of an effect
gets `sorting_offset = -0.001 x its template index`, the file's first node on top, which decides only
draws that otherwise tie; `EfpDisplayPass.draw_before` breaks its equal distances the same way (the
objects' ambient effects). `OPENSRO_QA_FX_NODE_ORDER=off` drops both for an A/B. The shine's pulse is
kept as the file keys it. `QuestMarks`' header records the finding.

**MEASURED after** (the same real-time view): bright pixels 259-399 throughout (the original's order),
mean 91.5, sd 3.46, largest step 1.07 between 50 ms effect steps, none above 2: the sd is the keyed
pulse (period 30 effect frames, 1.5 s), no frame-to-frame jump.

**Other effects.** A night lamp view (97/167, 21:00, the display pass with its glows): frames 150, 200,
299 identical with the order on and off (max channel difference 1). A cast view (skills 3, 30, 47, 1381

## Eight-hundred-and-forty-third round, lane S: the item slots' effects in the stall and everywhere

The user (2026-10-29): "one other bug to report, make sure item icons show any effects in the stall, so
if it's a seal weapon show the spinning stars. It shows it in the stall network but not the stall
itself", with the standing rule to match the original's colours and behaviour exactly. Labels: READ
(sro_client.exe, `c:`), MEASURED, INFERRED, OURS, OPEN. The reading is `docs/protocol/item_seal_edge.md`
§6-7 and `docs/protocol/stall.md` §12.

**What the original does (READ).**
- A stall slot is an ordinary item slot. CIFStallSlot's fill (c:0x6cada0) runs the CIFSlotWithHelp's
  SetItem (`0x6871d0`, c:0x6cb011) on the entry's record. The owner's list (0xB0BA types 2/3 ->
  0x872290) and a visitor's (0xB0B3, c:0x874208) both read records with `0x8be4f0(stream, 1)`, so
  `+0x28` is set and SetItem starts the seal star (`0x666610`), owner and visitor alike. The user's
  report matches the original; nothing differs.
- The visitor's dim while the stall is modified is the icon's alone. The slot alpha 0x80
  (c:0x6bad9a -> `0x655460`, byte +0x12d) goes through TFACTOR in the icon's draw (`0x655ca0`), and
  `0x6554c0` resets the alpha op before the overlay pass `0x67cfb0`. That pass draws on FVF 0x104
  (no vertex colour), so the star is not dimmed.
- "Any effects": `0x67cfb0` draws four more from the item itself, on every slot kind, for a record
  whose `+0x28` is set:
  - the awake devil's spirit's edge: `icon_edge_nasrun.ddj`, 12 cells, 80 ms, any slot but the
    mall's 0xa7;
  - the summoned pet's edge: `pt_edge_effect.ddj`, 9 cells, 50 ms;
  - the blue wash `0x80004b7e`: RGB (0, 0x4b, 0x7e) at half alpha, for a dead pet or a spirit whose
    awakening ran out;
  - the pet's one-shot life flash: `pt_life_effect.ddj`, 8 cells, 80 ms, bag and bag quick slots
    only; on a revival or a longer rent.
  0x3040 drives them: mask 0x40 via `0x6b4390` and `0x60a940`, mask 0x80 via `0x6b4500`. Mask 1 (a
  switcher's new RefItemID) flashes the bag or worn slot with `icon_mall_transgender.ddj` (16
  cells, 48 x 48 at -8).
- No plus glow: nothing in SetItem or the pass reads OptLevel. One sheet serves every seal, Star to
  Nova.
- A rental's half-black wash exists, but OpenSRO has no rentals.

**MEASURED (the archive, through the client's own loader).** `icon_edge_nasrun` 512 x 32,
`pt_edge_effect` 288 x 32, `pt_life_effect` 256 x 32, `icon_mall_transgender` 128 x 128: each matches
its draw's divisor (1/512, 32/288, 1/256, 1/128).

**What we built.**
- The stall: `StallWindowView._draw_slots` gives each of the ten slots its effects on every redraw
  (`HudPanels._set_item_slot_fx`) and clears them on an empty one. The visitor's 0x80 is
  `self_modulate`, so the star stays bright.
- `ItemStateEdge` (new) draws the spirit's edge, the pet's edge, the life flash and the wash with
  the original's sheets, cells, timers, phases and order.
- `HudPanels._set_item_slot_fx(icon, id, inst)` puts the star and those on a slot from its
  ItemInstance. It is used by the bag, the worn and avatar slots, the warehouse, the exchange, the
  stall, the stall network, the alchemy and grant windows and the pet / transport bag, which had no
  star before.
- The quick slots: `HudUnderbar.set_slot_states` on every bar change and bag list. The held icon
  copies the slot's effects.
- 0x3040 redraws the bag and the bar, plays the life flash (`HudPanels.bag_item_state_changed`) and,
  for mask 1, the switch flash (`HudPanels.flash_switched`, `RepairFlash.play_switch_on`;
  `CosNet.decode_item_state` now returns the ref).

## Eight-hundred-and-forty-third round, lane W: a model switcher keeps the glow and the seal

The user: "also when using the model switcher, the seal and + glow/effects need to stay and they
currently don't", then (the coordinator's brief) "the model switcher effect should show up in the
item mall character preview and it does not. It shows up in the inventory preview though".
`docs/protocol/item_switchers.md` §3a has the whole reading.

- **The cause (MEASURED).** The user's own switched item (prod DB, read only): character 12's
  `ITEM_EU_TSWORD_11_A_RARE_ACTIVE` +12 with model `ITEM_EU_TSWORD_11_A_RARE_SWITCH13`. The
  glow and the effects are chosen by the drawn row (READ, `FUN_00a5f3e0`: RefID and plus only),
  and the archive's twins are made from the LOCKED Seal of Nova rows, which no table lists. Round
  838 drew an unlocked item with its locked row's twins, so it lost its glow type, its three Nova
  seal effects and its +8 sparkle. The census of the 960 twins the mall's switchers reach: the
  plain D11 A and the two Egyptian sets' twins carry their own rows (unchanged here); the 240
  locked twins carry none, which is right for a locked item and wrong for an unlocked one.
- **What a glow type is (MEASURED).** `itemtypenumber.txt`'s types 1-4 share colours and
  periods; they differ in the option texture's scroll, the alpha-test flag and type 1's +9
  texture. The archive sets the type per model: the plain, locked and set twins of one model draw
  the same `.bsr` (240 of 240) and agree on the type in 310 of 330; the plain and unlocked base
  rows share it on all 22 bases. The twins' description: "Model Switched Item / Model: Degree N /
  Glow: Default".
- **The fix (OURS).** `CharacterAppearance.glow_sources`: a drawn row with rows of its own keeps
  them; one with none, worn by an item that has rows, takes the item's own seal and sparkle and
  the glow type of the plain twin of the same model (`_A_RARE_SWITCHnn` -> `_A_SWITCHnn`), else
  the item's own. A locked item's twin stays plain. The Nova effects keep the item's own scale on
  the new model (INFERRED; the archive has no Nova row for it, OPEN).
- **Other players (OURS wire).** The record and the 0x3038 name the model's row (round 838). The
  server now adds the item's own id after the plus of a 0x3038 for a switched item
  (`EquipBroadcast.Own`; every other 0x3038 is retail's bytes) and sends one such 0x3038 per
  switched worn item after a spawn record (`look.switched`, among the spawn's state frames). The
  client keeps it per player and slot (`World3D._other_fx`), clears it on a 0x3039 or a plain
  0x3038, redraws the body when it changes, and carries it into the crowd's kinds and far recipes.
- **The previews.** The item mall's preview (`MallModels.build_body`) and the skin-change
  preview (`_skin_preview_body`) read the worn items' own ids, so they showed the item's original
  model. Both now take them as the Equipment window draws them (`_display_equipped`, `_player_fx`).
  The original's mall preview copies the Equipment window's dress with each slot's plus (READ
  `0xa617d0` mode 0, `item_mall.md` §4a), so it shows the model, the glow and the effects.
- **Live (box, port 17020, real clicks through OPENSRO_QA_INPUT).** A level-110 China man was
  given the unlocked Seal of Nova sword 62605 and shield 62610 at +12, used model switchers 05 and
  13 on them (right-click the tool, click the item, the box's OK), equipped the sword, opened the
  mall, tried the wedding dress 22916 on and pressed Original. The tooltips read "Reaper Ghost
  Sword (+12) ... Model Switched Item / Model: Degree 5 / Glow: Default", the plus and the stats
  kept. The body, the doll and the mall preview each drew `ITEM_CH_SWORD_11_A_RARE_SWITCH05 with
  ITEM_CH_SWORD_11_A_SWITCH05's glow type and ITEM_CH_SWORD_11_A_RARE_ACTIVE's effects +12 (row
  +12, 4 effect(s))`, the dress on and off included. A watcher saw the actor (a second client)

  frame) and put the shield on (`... slot 7 item 62207 plus 12 own 62610`); after a relog the
  actor's own body drew both with glow and effects. The v0.1.607 build, the same steps:
  `ITEM_CH_SWORD_11_A_RARE_SWITCH05 +12: no glow (no glow type in itemoption.txt) and no
  particle row`, a plain switched sword, and the mall preview drew the original sword. Its
  other-player frame was not captured (in three tries the two characters did not stand in view of

- **Tests.** Server `go test ./...` passes (`switcher843_test.go`: the trailer's bytes, the

## Eight-hundred-and-forty-third round, lane P: Magic POP's own bag, every page

The user (2026-10-29): "also another bug fix, the magic pop doesn't show inventory pages so you can't
get pop cards from other pages. Please read exactly what does for magic pop and fix it. make no
mistakes", with the standing rule to match the original's colours and behaviour exactly. Labels: READ
(sro_client.exe, `c:`), MEASURED, INFERRED, OURS, OPEN. The whole reading is
`docs/protocol/magic_pop.md` §3a; the census row is `window_companions.md` row 19.

**What the original does (READ).**
- Magic POP opens no inventory. `c:0x79c060(1)` creates the window hidden (so its toggle helper sounds
  snd_window_close) and its Create shows the select window. The window draws the bag itself.
- The Start's build (`c:0x749560`) makes, from IFInventory's own counts, **a page tab per bag page**
  (`c:0x748790`: ID 500 + i at (475 + 62 i, 55), 60 x 24, `com_tab_on/_off.ddj`, "Page 1" then
  UIIT_STT_INVENTORY_EXTENSION_TEB **"Page 2" for every other page** -- a third page reads "Page 2"
  too) and **a cell per bag slot** (ID 200 + i, each page's 32 on the same places, `pt_block.ddj` and
  disabled past the size). A tab shows its page (`c:0x747a40`), busy or not. The user's report is the
  original's behaviour missing from ours: round 838 built the first 32 cells and no tabs.
- The cells take the bag slot's own record (`c:0x749030`), so the seal star and the pet and spirit
  edges show as in the bag (lane S's OPEN item); counts as the bag's rule; the purse on
  GDR_CHACHA_STA_MONEY, grouped, uncoloured. Prizes: a fresh record with +0x28 set (a seal prize's
  star), no count, not pickable.
- The card goes in by the held icon -- click it up, click it down. `CIFGhaCha::vslot_028`
  (`c:0x749a30`) takes every put-down in the window, only in state 1 (a prize chosen, no card); its
  check `c:0x7478c0` loops over **the first 32 cells only**: a page-1 card is taken only on the card
  slot, a page-2 or page-3 card wherever in the window it is put down (a quirk of the original, kept).
  The card slot put down empties it. The card slot follows its bag slot (emptied unless a coupon).
- The chosen prize turns the pet-edge sheet (`0x666680(1)`, the draw at `c:0x67ea55`), not a tint.
- PLAY: snd_gacha_move and snd_gacha_turn, the DECO over the card slot plays `alcm_effect_prepare`
  (additive, 64 x 64, 16 frames); the effect static holds 08 for ten ticks and 15 for fourteen; at
  tick 41 it resets, and a win plays `ga_effect_sucess.ddj` (64 x 81, 15 frames) to frame 14. A loss
  leaves the global tick at 1, so the next run holds 07 and 14. The result: snd_gacha_win or
  snd_gacha_end; the coupon's arrival (0x3040 mask 1) flashes the cell and the bag slot.
- Closing is refused while busy; the close sounds snd_window_close.

**The cause.** `GachaWindow` (round 838) built 32 cells at the pane's places and no tabs (its own OURS
line: "the inventory pane's page tabs (500+i) are not built"), so bag slots 32..95 were never drawn
and a card there could not be registered.

**Built** (`client/scripts/ui/hud/gacha_window.gd`; small hooks in `World3D.gd` and `hud_panels.gd`):
the tabs and every page's cells per the reading, the locked cells, the purse, the held-icon put-down

a press over a tab passes through, so a held card can be carried across pages), the card slot's
following rule, the chosen prize's marker, the item effects on cells, card slot and prizes, the
DECO, the effect's timing and quirk, the five sounds, the coupon flash, the close refused while busy.
Gone OURS of round 838: the click that registered a card, the 32-slot pane, the tint, the

- a visitor's 0xB0B5, likewise (c:0x872450);

The owner and a visitor behave the same, since it is one class. A modify only adds its state line
(c:0x878486).

## Eight-hundred-and-forty-second round, lane P: guild colours and the stall plate

The user (2026-10-29, on v0.1.604): "When someone is in the same guild their guild name should show orange
like your own, not blue. If they're in a union with you it should show green." and "the background around
Tobi's name widens when opening a stall and it should not". Their prod picture: Pain's own
`[OFWS * RatSlayer]` orange, Tobi's `[OFWS * Pengis]` (the same guild) light blue, and the box behind "Tobi"
about as wide as the stall title `[[Tobi]'s stall.]` above it. Labels: READ (c: sro_client.exe, s:
SR_GameServer.exe), MEASURED, INFERRED, OURS, OPEN. Full reading: docs/protocol/guild_plate.md "Colour".

**What the original does.**
- **Colours and rule (READ).** A guild line is one plate item per guild NAME, shared by every character of
  that guild (the guild manager 0xeeef70's refcounted map, c:0x9a4f40 makes, c:0x9a4650 releases). At its
  making it is 0xffa0fe68 (160, 254, 104) when the name is in the union map (c:0x996d60, CDD+0x148 map
  +0x94, "IsAllianceGuild"), else 0xffff0000 when it is in the hostile list (c:0x992a90, +0xa4,
  "IsHostileGuild(sGuildWarDef...)", fed by 0x3109), else 0xff66b9ff (102, 185, 255). The own player's line
  (c:0x9dc460, an exact CICPlayer) recolours ITS entry 0xfffead2e (254, 173, 46) at c:0x9dc4d4, so **every
  member of your guild is orange like you** -- the user's description is the original's. c:0x9a4450
  recolours every entry (lists, then the own entry orange) after 0x3102, 0x3109, 0x34B4 and 0x38F5 types 2,
  3, 0x0d, 0x12, 0x19, 0x1c, 0x23 (the switch tables at c:0x888b00 / c:0x888ab4). The extra relation is
  red, guild war; OpenSRO has no wars.
- **Union data (READ).** 0x3102 (c:0x87fd00 -> 0x99a810; s:0x5c4550 -> 0x5b8eb0 to each member guild's
  local members): u32 union id, u32 crest revision, u32 slot 0's guild (INFERRED the leader), u8 n x {u32
  id, str name, u8 level, str master, u32 (INFERRED the master's model), u8 (INFERRED members)}; 0x38F5
  type 0x0d adds a guild (UIIT_MSG_GUILD_ALLY_JOIN_RESULT); type 0x12 {u8 1 left / 2 expelled + u32, 3
  broken} clears the union when the guild is the own one or the map held fewer than two (c:0x988a60), else
  takes that guild out.
- **Pets (READ).** No COS calls c:0x9a4f40 (its callers: fortress structures, guards, c:0x7891f0 and the
  users): a pet's owner line takes no guild colour; nothing to change.
- **The stall title (READ, MEASURED).** Its item (+0x474) gets 0xFFFEB5FF and the name setter's
  0x40000000 box (c:0x9c89c2 / c:0x9c89ca), so its box is drawn where the title is. Its text is "[" + the
  stall's name + "]" (c:0x9dc3a0), and the default name is UIIT_STT_STALL_DEFAULT_TITLE (MEASURED in the box's
  Media.pk2: "[%s]'s stall.") formatted with the own name (c:0x641f40 purpose 0): `[[Tobi]'s stall.]` is the
  original's own double bracket. Nothing to change there.

**What was wrong.**
- The client coloured only the own line orange (round 814's reading stopped at the constant), and OpenSRO had
  no unions at all.
- `StallWorld.apply` fitted the title's NameBox when the title was made, at the name's line, then raised the
  text 37 px: the title-wide box stayed behind the name (and a rename kept the old width).

**What we built.**
- Client: `GuildLineColour` (the rule and the four ARGB), `UnionData` (0x3102, 0x38F5 0x0d / 0x12 inside
  GuildData, cleared with the guild), `World3D._guild_line_colour` / `_recolour_guild_lines` (on the own line
  changing and on the union changing), `UserSpawnNet` / 0x30FF keep the union id; `StallWorld.apply` refits
  the title's box after placing it. QA: `OPENSRO_QA_GUILD` also prints `QA PLATE` (each name and stall title
  box size and height, with the frame).
- Server: `guild/union.go` (the record, 0x3102 / 0x38F5 encoders), MemStore and SQLStore unions
  (`guild_unions`, `guild_union_members`, slots kept, a union under two guilds dissolved -- INFERRED from the
  client's rule -- a disbanded or emptied guild leaving its union), `session/union.go` (0x3102 after every
  guild block, to the union on a join; 0x0d to the others; 0x12 to the whole union on a leave, an expel, a
  disband), the union id in pcspawn and 0x30FF. OURS: `/union <guild>`, `/union leave`, `/union expel
  <guild>` (GM, a test tool; the original's request flow 0x70FB..0x70FD is not built). partybot:
  `-gm-timed`, `-guild-delay`. Prod needs no flag; the schema adds its tables itself.

**Live (render box, lane server 16970 in memory; the rendered QaWin with real chat input; partybots Mate
(OFWS master), Tobi (OFWS, stall), Ally (Beta), Other (Gamma), Solo (no guild, stall), Late (joins OFWS in

## Eight-hundred-and-forty-first round, lane X: the exchange portraits' motion

The user: "Also I think the exchange window character portraits are supposed to be animated. Verify
that." They are: retail's two busts breathe in their stand clip for as long as the window is open.
Ours (round 836) posed the clip's first key and rendered once.

**What the original does (READ, sro_client.exe).**
- **Set-up, once per exchange.** `0x7b3180` stores the partner (`+0x372c`) and calls `0x7b2a20`; its
  two callers are `0xB081`'s success (`c:0x880330`) and `0x3080`'s accept (`c:0x88aa60`). For each
  side, `0x7b2a20`:
  - dresses the clone, a `CCObjCharacter` embedded at `+0x33e4` (own) / `+0x3588` (partner), from the
    body (`0xa61c30` -> `0xa619e0`: the body's model and equipment lists into `InstallEquipVisual`,
    then its slot 8 `0xa61c60`: the animation group, the equipment visuals, one step);
  - plays type 0 on it: slot 3 (`0xa5faf0`, vtable `0xde5fd8`) with `(0, 0, 0, 0, 1.0, 1.0)` ->
    `0xa5b550`: the group's type-0 clip, no fade, speed 1.0, weight 1.0;
  - reads `Bip01 Head` (`0xa5ace0`), moves the model (`0xa5a880`), and steps the clip 1 ms (the
    object at `+0x33e8` / `+0x358c`, its vt+0x38 `(1, 1, 0.0)`).
- **Every frame.** CIFExchange's vtable (`0xdbce4c`) slot 12 is `0x7b2210`: `0xa5ac80(1, 0.0)` on
  both clones, which is vt+0x38 with the int at `0x110f7f8`. That int is the frame's milliseconds,
  written at `0xba4106` and clamped to 3000 (`0xba410d`), set to 1 when 0 (`0x84c349`). Slot 12 is
  the window tick: the main frame's tick runs `CGWndBase::vslot_012` (`0xb92070`), which recurses
  into every shown child at `0xb923f0` (READ earlier, the quick-slot key numbers' entry). Slot 15
  is `0x7b21b0`: both clones are rendered into their rects through `0x4ffc50`, with no dirty flag.
  That it runs every draw is INFERRED from its place beside slot 14 (CGWnd's child draw
  `0xba0300`). The character window's doll (`CIFEquipment::vslot_012` `0x6ab6b0`), the item mall's
  preview (`0x7bd0f0`) and the race view are stepped by the same call.
- **The clip.** Type 0 is the stand, looked up in the clone's own weapon group, then `default`.
  Whether it loops is decided by its `.ban` IsCyclic (the mixer, `animation_mixer.md`), not by the
  caller. MEASURED live: `chinaman_fighter_standcity`, 2333 ms, cyclic.
- **What does not reach a bust.** The partner sitting, emoting or walking: the clone is a separate
  object playing its own type 0. A change of dress: the clone is dressed only at set-up. Every
  reference to `+0x33e4..` / `+0x3588..` in the disassembly is one of these: the constructor
  (`0x7b2074` / `0x7b2085`), the destructor (`0x7b2128` / `0x7b213b`), the render, the tick and the
  set-up. Item moves are refused during an exchange anyway (`0x1834`, round 834).
- **The other portraits.** The player block's face is rendered once per dress, in ANI_POSE stepped
  once (`FUN_007b7740`, `player_mini_info.md`). It is not animated, and it is unchanged here. The
  character window's doll is stepped every frame, as ours has been since round 144.

**Ours, before (MEASURED).** Live, client and partybot. The bot asks; the client accepts with a real
click on the box's Accept. Frames were then taken every 5 ticks from tick 400 to 1990 (318 pairs,
26.5 s of game time). The busts' rects are (707,182) and (707,326), each 96 x 100, and the face's is
(19,14) 48 x 48.
- The own bust changed in **0 of 318** pairs.
- The partner bust changed in 236, all from the red stranger pulse behind it. At one pulse phase,
  frames 1000 and 1054 are identical in both busts (max 0).
- `xbust`: no clip; `Bip01 Spine1` was (0, -0.0741, 0, 0.9973) at every tick from 175 to 1975.

**Changed.**
- `PlayerPortrait.animate` (off by default) is on for the exchange's two busts only
  (`HudPanels._install_exchange_extras`).
- A new body starts the clip at 1 ms. While the picture shows, `_process` adds the frame's
  milliseconds, clamped to 1..3000 as `0x110f7f8` is, and poses with the clip's own IsCyclic. It
  renders that frame (`UPDATE_ONCE`).
- A hidden window steps nothing. A one-shot clip holds its last pose and is not drawn again.
- The player block's face does not set it: one render per dress, as before.
- QA steps:
  - `xans:c<1|0>`: a real click on the request box's Accept or Refuse;
  - `xbust`: each bust's clip, clock, `Bip01 Spine1` and head pose and screen rect, and the face's
    rect.

**After (MEASURED, the same run).**
- The own bust changed in **318 of 318** pairs; the partner bust in 318.
- `xbust`: `chinaman_fighter_standcity` 2333 ms cyclic. The clock goes 234.3 / 567.7 / 901.0 /
  1234.3 ms at ticks 315 / 335 / 355 / 375 (20 ticks = 333.3 ms of game time) and reaches 27901.0 ms
  at tick 1975 (11.96 loops). The spine moves every sample.
- Frames 1000 and 1054 (the same pulse phase):
  - own bust mean 4.80, 13.0 % of pixels off by more than 8;
  - partner bust mean 4.47, 12.9 %;
  - the window outside both portrait boxes mean 0.01 (0.01 %, the same as the before run's pair);
  - the face mean 0.53, max 4 (the same as before).
- Regression check, frame 1990 before against after:
  - the face max 1;
  - the window outside the busts max 1.

  The face drifts by up to 94 between ticks 400 and 1990 in both runs alike (before 15.07 mean, after
  14.16). That is not this change, and it was not looked into.

**Evidence** (box, `/var/tmp/r841x/keep`): the window crops `before_win_1000/1054.png` and
`after_win_1000/1054.png`, with `win_montage.png` holding all four; the HUD corners
`*_hud_1990.png`; the full frames at 1000; the `QA BUST` / `QA SOCIAL` lines (`*_qa.log`); the bot
logs. The recipe is `/var/tmp/r841x/run841.sh` + `qa841.sh`. The before build is this branch less
the one `animate` line (`/opt/opensro-client-r841x-before`).

**Tests.**

## Eight-hundred-and-forty-first round, lane W: the windows that open alongside

The user: "there's a lot of times when the inventory or pet inventory window should open alongside
an operation but it doesn't. Like buying trade goods or opening a stall or buying from a stall".
This lane took a census of every opener of the inventory (the main popup's inventory tab) and of the
COS window (the pet / transport window) in sro_client.exe, and of everything that closes them, then
built each one OpenSRO has. `docs/protocol/window_companions.md` has the full table with every
address. Labels as there: READ c: sro_client.exe, MEASURED, INFERRED, OURS, OPEN.

**How the census was taken (READ).**
- The inventory tab is selected only by `0x6a1f70(0x46)`. All 31 calls of the selector were listed,
  and so was every reader of the popup pointer (`+0x728`) and of its getter `0x798d00` that shows the
  popup.
- The COS window is created and shown only by `0x79bcd0(1, ...)`, from the command `0x7a0980(0)`.
- No absolute pointer to any of the openers exists in the image, so the direct calls are all of
  them.
- The openers that go with an operation: `0x79af20` (its callers: the alchemy window's OnCreate
  c:0x592635, the stall window's show c:0x6b9780, the fortress smith c:0x6fff15, Gori c:0x703336,
  CIFAlchemyBox c:0x722ba8, the grant window c:0x888fff, the guild storage c:0x88f6b1), the store /
  storage open `0x79dbd0`, and the exchange open `0x79df10`.
- No operation's end hides the inventory. Its only hides are the keys, Escape, the store's pre-hide
  and the world-entry reset.

**What the original does that OpenSRO did not.**
- **The stall window's show opens the inventory** (CIFStall::vslot_023(1), c:0x6b9730), for the
  owner's 0xB0B1 {1} and a visitor's 0xB0B3 {1} alike. It destroys the alchemy window first, then
  calls `0x79af20`, which raises the inventory over the stall. Its hide re-enables the bag's cells
  and leaves the inventory. OpenSRO opened nothing.
- **The specialty store opens the transport's window, not the inventory** (c:0x79dbd0).
  - The store open first hides the main popup (`0x7992c0`).
  - The interaction lock (CGInterface `+0x4fc`, which the 0xB046 handler fills, "Lock : %d") picks
    the companion. Lock 1 shows the inventory again. Lock 0xc runs `0x811130(1)`: a transport made
    current, the first in summon order when the current COS is not one.
  - Then `0x811310(0, 0xff)` -> `0x7a0980(0)`: command 0, the COS window's **toggle**. It opens on
    the Inventory page at its saved position or centred, and closes when it was already open.
  - With no transport, nothing opens. OpenSRO opened the inventory beside it.
- **Gori's exchange opens the inventory** before 0x7119 (c:0x703330..0x70333b). OpenSRO did not.
- **The grant window's inventory sounds** the helper's snd_window_open (`0x79af20` -> `0x79a7e0`).
  OpenSRO's was silent.
- **Escape closes the stall through its X.** In `0x79d620` GDR_STALL comes after the NPC window and
  before the exchange. Its vslot_043 sends the owner's 0x70B2 or a visitor's 0x70B5. OpenSRO's
  Escape only hid the window and left the stall open on the server.
- **Escape closes the COS window** after the main popup. It was not in OpenSRO's Escape list.

**Unchanged, confirmed:** the store (lock 1), the storage, the exchange (its end leaves the
inventory), the alchemy window. The placement beside the store and storage stays OpenSRO's own
(rounds 513 / 593); the original only moves the popup to its tab's side (x = W - 388 - 0x50, the y
kept) and never places one window relative to the other.

**What we built.**
- `HudPanels.inventory_companion` (0x79af20).
  - Used by the alchemy window, the grant window, the stall window's show (`open_stall_window`, which
    also closes the alchemy window) and Gori's exchange (`World3D._gacha_exchange`).
- `open_shop`'s lock branch: `specialty_lock` comes from SpecialtyFlow (`store_npc != 0`), and
  `hud_cos` is set by World3D.
- `HudCos.specialty_store_opened` (0x811130 / 0x7a0980(0)) and `HudCos.escape_close_window`.
- `HudCosWindow.open_for`'s `unsaved_at`.
  - OURS: with no saved position, the transport's window takes the bag's place right of the
    centre. The original's centre lies under this client's store.
- `_escape_close` gains the stall's X and the COS window step.
- New QA steps `npcclick:<code>` (a click on the server's NPC where it is drawn; off screen it
  refuses) and `talkline:<n>` (the talk line's own rect: the pointer comes first and the click a
  few frames later, as a hand moves).
  - A press in the same frame as a fresh hover is missed by the talk box's link: the hover
    re-renders the label. MEASURED at the blacksmith's first line; recorded as a side finding.

the labels are its own (READ s: SR_GameServer.exe / c: sro_client.exe / sm: SR_ShardManager.exe and

## Eight-hundred-and-fortieth round, lane B: stall booths, the owner's pets and the stall refusals

The user's ask for round 840: finish round 839's stall OPEN items. This lane: the decoration booths'
own animation, what the original does with the owner's pets, and the stall refusals that lacked state
(the trade and chat bans, the quest block, the title's word filter), with S+0x49, an owner under
attack and the title's height settled. `docs/protocol/stall.md` section 11 has the whole reading;
labels as there (READ s: SR_GameServer.exe / c: sro_client.exe, MEASURED on the box's archives,
INFERRED, OURS, OPEN).

**What the original does.**
- **The booth moves (READ, MEASURED).** FUN_009dd040 plays the booth through its CCObjAnimation's slot
  3 at once (c:0x9dd14f..0x9dd16a: group `default`, type 0, no fade, speed 1.0, looping as the
  `.ban` says) -- the map objects' rule. The four decoration booths each carry one cyclic default
  type-0 clip (5000 / 5000 / 3333 / 5000 ms, 3 / 9 / 3 / 15 bones); `cj_store` and
  `euro_streetstall01` have no skeleton.
- **The owner's pets (READ, MEASURED).** Only when the stalling character is the client's own
  player, each COS of the player's COSDataMgr in the world whose `default` group has a type-80 clip
  enters state 0xF (the vendor loop); at the close every such COS enters state 3 (stand). Nobody
  else's pets, in any client. Of 8,539 `.bsr`s only `cos\p_jinn.bsr` and `p_jinn_02.bsr` (the
  COS_P_JINN growth pets) have one: every other pet and ride keeps its pose.
- **S+0x49 / type 4 (READ):** written by type 4 and echoed, read by nothing on either side (the client
  overwrites it before use and its type-4 reply only reads the byte). A vestige.
- **An owner under attack (READ, INFERRED):** no attack, skill or target code reads INTERACTMODE;
  the owner's death closes the stall 0x3c0e and the open protects its items from the death drop: an
  owner can be attacked like anyone. OpenSRO already behaves so.
- **The title's height (READ):** the name pass moves the plate point up 20 px for a character out of
  a suit (the guild line's place), then the title is drawn half its 14 rows plus 10 px above that:
  37 px over the name, 17 over the guild line. Ours was an OURS 22, which sat on the guild line.
- **The bans (READ):** two restriction slots per player (3 trade, 4 chat) set by the account side from
  the operator console's punishments; FUN_004f0a00 answers 0x3405 {kind, packed end} and the caller
  drops the request. Trade: the exchange request, the stall open and enter, the consignment, the
  item drop. Chat: every chat line, the global chatting item, the stall name at the open (CharName
  plus one of eleven suffixes), the guild notice, letters, the academy notice. The client shows the
  line in the warning banner and the system window; MEASURED: the archive misspells the trade row's
  key (`..._TRADE _BLOCK`), so the original shows nothing for a trade ban.
- **The quest block (READ):** a mask on the PC (QB_* slots 143..145); 0x200 refuses the open (0x3c32)
  and the enter (0x3c33); the only setters OR 0x60000, so no quest of this server sets 0x200.
- **The title filter (READ, MEASURED):** the abuse filter's fourth flag, tested only in the client's
  title box (c:0x8c3f10) for the first title and a rename; a refusal shows 0x3c38 and the window's
  X sends 0x70B2. The server loads the lists and never reads them. Group 4: 82 stall substring words,
  0 whole; group 5 (the box's Media.pk2 language): 38 and 217.
- **Not built** (no OpenSRO system): the murderer refusal 0x3c39 and the arena / flag world 0x3c16 --
  one hook each, `session.stallMurderer` / `session.stallWorldRefuses`, OPEN.

## Eight-hundred-and-thirty-ninth round, lane P: transport bags, spirits, fellow pet names, Gold Time across restarts

The user: close round 838's known gaps. Round 838 lane 4 (pets, spirits, premium) left six open;
this lane traced each in SR_GameServer.exe / sro_client.exe before changing anything.

- **Transport bags: one slot is retail (READ, MEASURED).** `s:0x4d1a50` is min(level cap,
  ref+0x224), and ref+0x224 is `_RefObjChar.InventorySize` (RefObjChar_ExtractData `s:0x6a58f0`:
  ID, Lvl, CharGender, MaxHP, MaxMP, 32 four-byte resists, then that byte). The cart's storage is
  made only by CGObjCOS vslot_349 (`s:0x4d1bd0` -> `s:0x4b7680`: maximum +0x1c = InventorySize,
  passed in ecx; usable +0x20 = the bag); the owner's 0x30C8 writes +0x20 (CGCOSInventoryOP slot
  29, `s:0x4ba720`); a level change only ever grows it (GObjPC_SetLevel `s:0x4e4f0a` ->
  `s:0x4fc960`, 0x30C9 type 2); the client draws 28-cell pages with `pt_block.ddj` past the size
  (`c:0x7a7e90`). InventorySize is 1 on all 47 COS_T rows of the archive and on the same rows of
  the private server's own `_RefObjChar` (only its client-less COS_T_SCORPION* 50..177 and
  COS_T_TEMP* 99 are larger; the box's SR_GameServer.exe is byte-identical to the private
  server's). So a level-110 trader's donkey holds one stack in retail too; OpenSRO already
  matched. Nothing changed but the notes (`specialty/scale.go`, `cos/rules.go`) and a test. OURS:
  the level-up growth is not modelled (it cannot fire with InventorySize 1). If more slots are
  wanted that is a design choice against both data sets, not a retail fix (the user's call).
- **The spirits' tables are the shard's (MEASURED).** SR_ShardManager.exe loads
  `_REFABILITYBYITEMOPTLEVEL`, `_REFMAGICOPTBYITEMOPTLEVEL` and `_REFSKILLBYITEMOPTLEVEL` from the
  shard DB for the game server (the names are its strings; the game server's "Can`t attach passive
  skill on _RefAbilityByItemOptLevel Table!"); the lookup is the exact (RefItemID, OptLevel) key
  (`FUN_00498160`, "Invalid find key inserted!"). The restored shard (CT 104, exported to

  archive's text has 266 / 505 / 335. They agree on abilities 1..159 except 89. `export-refdata
  -mode itemoptlevel` now also reads the shard's three CSVs (header = the DB's columns), and the
  deploy CSV is made from them.
- **Angel's Spirit +6..+10 (INFERRED, OURS, the user's decision).** Neither source has option rows
  for W_AMALRUN, M/W_AMALRUN_YELLOW and M/W_AMALRUN_BLUE at +6..+10 (their ability rows and

  exactly the devil's spirits' rows). The export fills each empty ability as kind `optinf` from
  every sibling spirit whose option rows equal the item's own at each level both have rows for,
  when those siblings agree (here M_AMALRUN and the six non-unique NASRUN items: 75 rows). The
  server applies them unless `-item-opt-level-inferred=false` (boot log `inferred_rows`). The
  +6..+10 MOBDEFENCEIGNORE skill (31152 on the devil's spirits) is not inferred: even M_AMALRUN,
  which has the options, has no such skill row.
- **The event spirits' rows (MEASURED).** Not a column shift or an encoding: the archive carries
  110 abilities (160..269) for the ten event spirits that the shard never had, and reuses ability
  89 (ITEM_EVENT_AVATAR_M_NASRUN +0) for them. Their option rows follow the angel's +0..+5 pattern
  by level; their skill rows do not -- they use only ability ids ending 0..6 (75 rows, never x7..x9)
  while the abilities run consecutively, and only 18 of the 110 get the skill set their level's
  pattern predicts (33 none). No clean transform recovers them (OPEN). The shard's rows are what the
  server reads: ITEM_EVENT_AVATAR_M/W_NASRUN +0 give +5 % HP / MP and SKILL_EVENT_NASRUN_

- **Spirit expiry under a running buff (READ).** refskill +0x65 is Basic_Activity
  (`docs/protocol/skill_fields.md`). `GObjPC::FUN_0059f0e0` (`s:0x59f0e0`) re-checks every
  self-cast running record's reqi list: kind 14 value 1 is the avatar storage's index-4 item that
  is not an expired 3/1/14 (vtable +0x584(4) -> `0x4a6910` on pc+0x1c34, `FUN_00498610`); a
  failing active record ends (`FUN_0059eff0(0)`) unless its Basic_Code holds
  "SKILL_CH_FIRE_SHIELD_"; a passive one only loses its params. It runs after equipment and avatar
  moves (`s:0x50f53f`) and durability changes (`s:0x4e71a2`), but not at a worn spirit's expiry:
  the 10-second rental check (`s:0x4a707b` -> `0x4b9060` -> DetachAbilityByItemOptLevel
  `s:0x4bbd60`) removes the params and skills and sends 0x3078 {3, slot} and nothing else. So a
  spirit's buff outlives its expiry until its own end or the next move. MEASURED: the 23 kind-14
  skills are all "14:1", active, 300/600/1800 s. OpenSRO re-checks the kind-14 lists after every
  avatar move (`session/buffreqs.go`). OPEN: the equipment-move and durability triggers for the
  weapon, shield and armour kinds (a weapon swap would then end weapon-bound buffs: a visible
  change, left for the user).
- **Fellow pet names (READ, MEASURED).** The 13 Celestial Fellow pets (COS_P_ANCIENT_TRIBAL_BEAR,
  BLOOD_ARMOR_DINO, CELESTIAL_TIGER, DARK_GRIFFIN, GOLD_HORN, HALF_MOON_JAGUAR, KLOX,
  LAVA_ROAR_HOUND, NIGHT_FANG, RUBINO_PHOENIX, SILVERBACK, SOUL_TAIL, YELLOW_SPARKLE_OSTRICH; 1,820
  rows; scrolls 50864..50876) have NameStrIDs with no row in any of the archive's 377 textdata
  files. CICCos::vslot_034 (`c:0x9c6d27..0x9c6d8d`) settles a COS's name at spawn: its own; else,
  for an owner in no job (byte 4), UIIT_STT_COSNEWUI_TITLE -- so "< No name >" is retail's for any
  unnamed pet; else the ref's text, which for a key with no text is the text manager's static empty
  string (`FUN_008c9b20` -> `c:0xec3b70`), and the spawn then skips the name setter (`c:0x9d19d6`):
  no name line. Ours showed "< SN_COS_P_KLOX >" for a job-suited owner (UiTextTable answers a
  missing key with the key). `CosSpawnNet.display_name` follows the engine. OPEN: retail writes the
  substitute once at spawn; ours rebuilds the label when it is redrawn.
- **Gold Time across a restart (READ).** CTJ_PremiumKeeper keeps retail's `_TIMEDJOB` words:
  TimeToKeep = into << 8 | days (into, the seconds into the job's day, runs on the keeper's Tick
  `s:0x6529d0`, so only while the owner is in the world), Data1 the start, Data2 prev << 16 |
  today, Data3 extra days, Data4 paused (getters +0x68..+0x80; `_ADDTIMEDJOB` `s:0x650980`). The
  load (vslot_012 `s:0x6525bf..0x6526fe`) compares R = (Data3 + 1) x 86400 + P1 - (now - start)
  with T = (days + 1) x 86400 - into: R <= 0 zeroes the job and sends nothing, and the first tick
  ends it with the end form; otherwise into += T - R, then one roll per whole day. So days away and
  a server's downtime are spent on the job's own boundaries (start + k days), and **the "+1 day" is
  the carry day after the period**. Data3 has no writer in the engine (INFERRED: the only type-3
  creator, `s:0x49c6b4`, passes 0; the keeper never calls the setter). OpenSRO stores those words
  (V1/V2/V3), runs the Tick's day clock and the load's catch-up, sends the short form {3, 1, ref, 0,
  0} when the period and both halves are 0 (`s:0x65285b..0x6528e4`), and reads round-838 rows
  unchanged. OURS: Data3 is not kept; a crash loses up to 60 s of drained time.

## Eight-hundred-and-thirty-ninth round, lane S: player stalls

The user's ask for round 839: close round 838's known gaps. This lane: retail's player stalls, so a
player opens a stall, lists items with prices, others see the booth and the stall's name, enter it, buy,
and the owner closes it -- and round 838's stall decorations (stored, never drawn) now draw as the booth.
The Stall Network is out of scope. `docs/protocol/stall.md` has the whole reading with every address;
the labels are its own (READ s: SR_GameServer.exe / c: sro_client.exe and the archive on the box,
MEASURED, INFERRED, OURS, OPEN).

**What retail does (READ).**
- **Wire:** 0x70B1 open {str}, 0x70B2 close, 0x70B3 enter {u32}, 0x70B4 buy {u8}, 0x70B5 leave, 0x70BA
  the owner's update (types 1 price, 2 add, 3 remove, 4 a byte with no client sender, 5 open/modify, 6
  greeting, 7 rename); 0xB0Bx the answers, 0xB0BA's success to every participant; 0x30B7 to the
  participants (1 left, 2 came, 3 sold with the list), 0x30B8 / 0x30B9 / 0x30BB to the owner's view
  (opened with the booth's u32, closed with the reason, renamed). A list is slot, the item record, bag
  slot + 13, count, price, then 0xFF. The spawn record carries `str name, u32 decoration` after the guild
  block when the interaction byte is 4 (s:0x4e5ee6, c:0x9de103). 0x30BA and 0xB0B6..0xB0B9 do not exist.
- **Rules:** no zone or distance test at the open (only the arena / flag world refuse, 0x3c16); the
  world check (alive, INTERACTMODE 0, not in a stall, no party being set up), riding 0x3c34, murderer
  0x3c39, a job suit 0x3c3b; INTERACTMODE 4 for the owner, 2 for a visitor; ten slots, seven visitors;
  whole stacks only; price 0..9,999,999,999 (the client's box 1..); not tradable / trade goods 0x3c2d, a
  summoned pet's item 0x3c3a, an awake spirit 0x3c55, the item's group from `fmntidgroupmapdata.txt`
  (c:0x938370, 0 refused 0x3c3c); edits only while modifying (0x3c2b), buying only while open (0x3c2e);
  nobody moves; every item operation refused at INTERACTMODE 4 (s:0x50f7c0, 0x1834).
- **The sale:** no tax; the stack to the buyer's first empty slot; 0x304E to both; 0xB0B4 {1, slot},
  0x30B7 kind 3; **no 0xB034** (the clients move their own copies); the DB job `_STRG_MOVEITEM_NEW` and
  both golds; a failed job closes the stall 0x3c2f and logs both out.
- **Lifecycle:** 0x3c17 by the owner, 0x3c15 warp / logout / disconnect, 0x3c0e death; a visitor's is a
  leave without 0xB0B5; nothing closes it on an attack. The BFI1 override is cleared at every close; the
  booth is the decoration item's `.bsr` or the race's default (round 838's StallBooth).
- **The client:** one window for owner and visitor (CIFStall, GDR_STALL 467x490, ifstall.txt + ten
  CIFStallSlots + the chat module, chat type 9), its title / greeting boxes and register / price / buy
  boxes; the title "[name]" in 0xFFFEB5FF over the head, the vendor loop (state 0xF, type 80), the 0xa3
  cursor, a click within 100.0 enters; the owner's client closes an emptied stall itself.

**What we built.**
- Server: `internal/stall` (the hub: stalls, members, modes; the `stall_sales` record, its own
  idempotent DDL, SQL and memory stores), `session/stall.go` (every handler and refusal in retail's
  order, the close paths on death / zone change / disconnect, the spawn record's block, chat type 9),
  the trade hub's gates fed the stalls' INTERACTMODE (`trade.Hub.SetModes`). The sale is one transaction
  with a ledger claim (OURS): the stack, both golds and the sale row, or nothing.
- Client: `StallNet`, the spawn block (`UserSpawnNet`), `StallWorld` (booth, title, vendor loop, click,
  approach), `StallController` + `StallWindowView` (the window from the archive), the boxes
  (`HudCosBox.build_stall_input`, `StoreMessageBox` STALL_*), the Stall action (1009) with the avatar
  stall's question and 0x7160. A stalling owner is never a GPU ghost (OURS). QA steps playerclick,
  stallicon / stallmodify / stallslot, bagempty, actionslot, stallclose; partybot -stall-open / -items /
  -visit / -buy / -chat and -bot-race.

**Live (render box, lane server 16880 in memory; real clicks and keys through OPENSRO_QA_INPUT,
partybot as the other players; evidence in `/var/tmp/r839s/keep`).**
