## Eight-hundred-and-thirty-eighth round, lane 6: the title scrolls are the hwan level, and the Random Wing Scroll

The user: "let's make all the items in the item mall functional ... Make no mistakes." This lane:
ITEM_TITLE_1 .. ITEM_TITLE_255 (3/3/13/14, no Param block) and ITEM_RANDOM_WING (3/3/13/1). Both are the
private server's rows; what they do is OURS (`session/titlescroll.go`), how a title is carried and drawn
is the original's.

**What a title is (READ).** Retail's _CHAR.HwanLevel (charData +0xf2). Server: CGObjChar::UpdateHwanLevel
(0x004a9f40) keeps it (+0x1c58), GObjPC::FUN_004a9e20 asserts it is within the table and writes the row
(dirty bit 0x2000), FUN_004a9f70 sends 0x30DF {u32 object id, u8 level} to the view. Client: 0x30DF
(FUN_008a7630) and the spawn record's byte (slot 22 -> DAT_00ef1bb8 -> slot 27 0x9dbcc0; 0x3013 reads it
too) both call FUN_009ca930(level): +0x764 = level, then FUN_00941000 -- hwanleveldata.txt's row, its
Title_CH70 / Title_EU70 key by the body's race (ref +0x9d), the text table's line ("" on a miss) -- into
the title slot (vslot 30, c:0x9c28a0): left of the name, #FFE65B, emptied while a job suit is worn. The
private server's own _RefHWANLevel.csv (the box's /opt/sro-files/db/csv) and the archive's
hwanleveldata.txt have rows 0..255, row N naming UIO_SECOND_HWAN_CH_NAME_LEVEL_N; textuisystem's FIRST row
for each key is that server's title (MEASURED: 1 "Ambassador" .. 97 "YouTuber", 196 "SRO Lover", 200-204,
232-239, 246-255 "Custom"), and ITEM_TITLE_N's name is that title + " Title". So ITEM_TITLE_N gives hwan
level N. The procs in /opt/sro-files/db/procs hold nothing about titles.

**Built.**
- Server: `character.TitleStore` (characters.hwan_level, custom_title; Mem and SQL), the spawn record's
  HwanLevel from a cache filled at entry, 0x30DF to everyone in view on a use, and to the arrival after
  OpSelfID (OURS: OpenSRO has no 0x3013). The title scrolls go through the service-scroll dispatch.
- OURS, the use: the title is given and the scroll spent; a new one REPLACES the old (the custom scroll's
  text: "the old one will be lost"); the same title again is refused and the scroll kept.
- OURS, ITEM_TITLE_255 "Custom Title Scroll" ("A window will open where you can enter your custom
  title"): the bag right-click opens the naming box with "Enter your custom title." (20 characters),
  the use carries the text (option 0xC7, u16 + UTF-8), the server keeps 1..20 characters of ASCII
  letters, digits, single spaces and `-_.'!#&+?:()`, stores level 255 + the text and sends it as 0x01A8
  {u32 uid, str} before the 0x30DF, and on every spawn. A use without the text is refused, kept.
- Client: `TitleNet` (0x30DF, 0x01A8, the spawn byte), `_job_plate_decor` draws the title in the title
  line for job state 4 (the OURS class title keeps the suited line), lane 3's title colour applies.
  `UiTextTable.keeps_first_row` now covers UIO_SECOND_HWAN_*: the joined-table rule (round 725) had drawn
  the stock "Captain" for level 1, while the client's TextStringManager keeps the first row (READ
  0x8ca120) and the scroll is the "Ambassador Title".
- OURS, the Random Wing Scroll: claimed before the skill item path -- its Desc128_1,
  SKILL_CELESTIUS_SILK_SCROLL_10, is a placeholder (cbuf, dura 1000 ms, no effect; MEASURED) that lane 1's
  path would have cast. One of 20 wing visuals, evenly, goes to the item chest: VSROEDITORCOM_VISUAL_09,
  10, 12 and 17..33 (the mall's Wings tab); 11 "Wings of Blood" is out, its USU1 casts VISUAL_01's horns.
- The same placeholder is named by ITEM_ACCESSORY_UPGRADE, ITEM_RACE_CHANGE, ITEM_SANTA_BOX,
  ITEM_SET_UPGRADE, the four ITEM_ELIXIR_COUPON_* (SILK_SCROLL_2500), the five ITEM_CRATE_* and
  ITEM_SILK_LOTTERY / ITEM_NAME_CHANGE (lane 3's). `isSkillItem` now leaves those skills out, so an

ifexchange.txt's own. `ch_red.ddj` (MEASURED from Media.pk2): 4 x 4 cells of 128, 9 frames, red
only in each cell's top-left 100 x 104, alpha 0, 0, 51, 85, 119, 153, 119, 85, 51 -- a pulse,
which is why some screenshots show the stranger's portrait on black. The log's background strips
300 / 301 fill the body the frame leaves open (the first live frame showed the world through two
holes exactly at their y); their x is INFERRED (centred).

**The busts.** READ `c:0x7b2a20`: the clone plays animation 0 (ANI_STAND1), reads "Bip01 Head"
and moves the model by (0, -h^2/34, -425/h) (17.0, 0.5, 25.0), then renders through a camera
object (`+0x33e8`) whose field of view was not read. So the framing is OURS, fitted to the
screenshots: distance 15, 30 degrees, the target 1.0 over the head bone (the player block's READ
lift), no yaw -- the head mid-height and about the screenshots' size (face about 25 px wide
against their 26). Transparent background, so the red pulse shows behind the model.

**Built.**
- `HudWindow.build`: registry `rects` / `size` overrides applied to a copy of the cached layout
  (`with_rects`); the controls are built and settled from their defs as any other.
- `HudPanels`: `EXCHANGE_FULL_RECTS` / `_SIZE`; `_install_exchange_extras` (the log as a
  `HudChat.ChatList` -- pitch 14, lines from the top and no hanging indent, both READ from the
  log's Create; the red pulse's 9 frames at 100 ms; the tooltip; the two `PlayerPortrait`
  busts); `set_exchange_portrait`, `exchange_trust_effect`, `exchange_log_*`; the log fed by
  `exchange_line` / `exchange_warning`. The Extra Settings row (on by default; Default restores
  on) rebuilds the window, at once or when the exchange in progress ends.
- `PlayerPortrait.set_framing` / `set_transparent` (the player block's values unchanged);
  `ChatList.stack_from_bottom` / `hanging_indent` / `clear`; `HudChat.wrap` without the indent.
- World3D `_exchange_portraits`: both bodies as the world draws them, copied (cloth and
  particles cleaned as the player block's copy) and posed in their stand clip; a partner not yet
  dressed is dressed from its spawn.

**DPI.** Everything is built in UI units from the layout, so it scales with the UI scale like
every window; the busts render at the picture's physical size (ViewportPixels), the text with
the UI's own fonts. A canvas without room for 365 x 500 (plus 8 a side) -- a high UI scale on a
small screen -- gets retail's compact window instead, decided at each opening.

**Tests and live runs.**
- `exchange834_test`: retail's compact window unchanged with the option off; with it on, 365 x

- Live (client + partybot, real clicks): UI scale 1.0 -- the whole exchange, frames compared

## Eight-hundred-and-thirty-fifth round: the exchange's blue grid at the start and the second side's Confirm

The user tried v0.1.594's exchange with another player: "It shows blue at the beginning when it
shouldn't. Then won't [let] the other player confirm their trade." Both were real, and both were
departures from the original that round 834's tests missed.

**1. The opponent's grid was blue from the start (READ).** `CIFExchange::Create` fetches
GDR_EXCHANGE_USER_NAME (ID 153, a CIFStatic at the opponent grid's rect, 21,72,212,68, with
`effect\icon\icon_effect1.ddj`) into `+0x33e0` and hides it at once (c:0x7b29c0..0x7b29dd,
vslot `+0x5c` with 0, the same call the academy's picture uses at 0x6e9848) -- the only control
Create hides. exchange.md listed it "hidden at Create", but HudPanels never hid it, so its dark
art covered the opponent's grid whenever the window opened. MEASURED on the live run: the top
grid's cells read (0, 7, 41) from the first frame the window showed, the bottom's (0, 0, 0).
Fix: `HIDDEN_AT_CREATE["exchange"]`. `0x7b2210` shows it again only while `0x81a620` holds for
control 14 (`+0x7c4`); what sets that state is still OPEN, so it stays hidden.

**2. The side that had not confirmed could not confirm (READ).** `0x3086` runs `0x7b2670(1)`:
`+0x7be` = 1, the opponent's gold grey and grid blue, and **if** `+0x7bd` (`0x7b2310`) the button
is enabled (`0x655ec0(1)`); otherwise the button is not touched. ExchangeController set it to
`enabled = mine_confirmed`, so whoever confirmed second found "Confirm" disabled and the exchange
stuck. Round 834's live runs missed it because the QA step `xbtn` called `press_button()`
directly, which a disabled button does not stop.

**Built.**
- `ExchangeController.on_partner_confirmed` enables the button when this side confirmed and
  leaves it alone otherwise (`HudPanels.exchange_button_enabled`, the state without the caption).
- `xbtn` is now a real mouse click at the button's centre and logs its caption and state.
- partybot `-exchange-confirm first|second|never` (second: after the partner's 0x3086) and
  `-exchange-hold`, so QA can play either order.
- exchange.md: the 0x3086 row and OPEN 8 corrected.

**Tests and live runs.**
- `exchange834_test`: USER_NAME hidden at Create; a new exchange starts with neither grid blue;
  the opponent confirming first leaves "Confirm" enabled, and our Confirm and Approve then go out.
- Live, client + partybot, real clicks, both orders: the bot confirms first and the client then
  confirms and approves; and the client confirms first and the bot second. Both reached 0x3087.
  Frames: both grids dark at the start, each turning blue at its own side's confirm (cells
  (35, 42, 63) / (38, 44, 64)), as the user's screenshots show.
- No perf gate: UI only.

The user asked for full friend support in the game and its windows, the right-click target menu as

wrong claims, corrected at the top of each spec before anything was built.

**Read, the parts that decide behaviour.**

  Confirm and Approve test only the session's state; the deal runs on the second Approve, incoming
  items to the receiver's first empty slots in bay order; `0x3087` done, `0x3088 {code}` closed
  (cancel, refusal, the 30 s timeout, death, a warp, logout). Retail 1.188's layout parks the

## Eight-hundred-and-thirty-third round: the Option window's Key Map tab

The user asked for key mapping in the settings, from a picture of the Option window's Key Map tab
(a private server's client: its fifth tab reads "Extra Settings", so ours does now too).

**Read (sro_client.exe; a fork's reading, addresses in `ui/hud/option_key_page.gd` and `ui/key_names.gd`).**
- **The page.** Pane 109 holds:
  - radios 110 / 111 with labels 189 / 190;
  - fourteen CNIFKeyOptionSlot rows (two a line), each a key box 211 and a label 212;
  - scroll bar 20, over lines 0..10;
  - "Custom shortcut", a lone tab with no pane.
  Row i is key slot i, and line L shows rows 2L and 2L + 1.
- **Rebinding.**
  - A left press on a row selects it, and its key box shows `opt_key_select.ddj`.
  - The next key-down the row takes (0x5fb460's table: no digits, F1-F12, arrows, Esc, numpad,
    NumLock / ScrollLock, PrintScreen or Pause) unbinds any other row holding that key -- no
    swap, no message -- and is the row's.
  - The row stays selected for the next key until another row is pressed.
  - Esc is refused; its WM_CHAR closes the window.
  - The box text is 0x6ed9e0's switch ("Tab", "C/L", "Space", "PgUp", "F1".., the OEM signs, else
    the VK's character).
- **The mouse radios** are GI+0x4f9:
  - mode 0 (default): the middle button fires the mouse quick slot and the right button turns the
    camera;
  - mode 1: the other way round (CGInterface::vslot_017 0x77c260).
- **Default** (0x5fcda0): mode 0 at once, the rows back to the defaults.
- **Apply / Confirm.** Apply stores the current tab only (0x5fe670); Confirm stores every tab.
- **The checked tab's caption** is semi-bold (0x47a950: flag 2, lfWeight 600) -- in every window.

**Built.**
- **KeyMap:** live keys over the defaults (`key_of_slot`, `set_keys`, saved in ClientSettings
  `keymap/slots`). Every key path already asked KeyMap, so a rebinding reaches all of them.
- **`OptionKeyPage`:** the tab, over the file's controls; the scroll bar is the Video tab's.
- **`KeyNames`:** the accept table and the names, on VK codes, with a Godot-keycode map.
- **Capture:** KeyInput hands a key to the page first (`KeyMap.capture`) while the tab is up and a
  row is selected (OURS: such a key is not also run by the game; whether the original's dispatcher
  sees it is OPEN).
- **Mouse mode:** World3D and the hotbar's body follow the mode (`set_mouse_mode`). The target
  menu opens on the camera's button, as the original's WM_MBUTTONUP path does in mode 1.
- **Checked tab caption:** semi-bold via HudNotice's weight-600 path (the face's bold file, or the
  glyph again one pixel right).

**Departures, disclosed.**
- Alt is refused: it arrives as WM_SYSKEYDOWN, which the window does not take (INFERRED, so the
  original never binds it although its table would).
- The keys are saved per PC in ClientSettings, not in `SROptionSet.dat`.
- Slots 25-28 and 31-32 can be bound now, but their features are still not built.
- The reference picture's scroll bar is longer than the file's record (198 px); ours keeps the
  record.

**Tests.**
- `option_key_page_test` covers, on the real Media.pk2:
  - the accept table and names;
  - live keys;
  - the mode-1 camera drag;
  - the fourteen rows and their text;
  - select, take, unbind the other row, refuse a digit, leave Esc;
  - the end of the scroll;
  - nothing in force before Apply, no capture on another tab;
  - Apply (keys and mode), Default (mode at once, keys not);
  - the semi-bold caption.
- The full run: 367 client suites, 0 failing.
- Live render: the tab against the user's picture (rows, radios, header tab, the selected row's
  box, the bold caption).
- Perf gate (`--frames 60000`, base 0a9dffcc): every number SAME (jangan 0.86 / 0.86 ms a frame,
  reeds 0.85 / 0.85, cross 1.02 / 1.02). Client only: no server change, no prod restart.

## Eight-hundred-and-thirty-second round: Trace, the right-click target menu, and the Option window's Extra tab

The user asked for trace "exactly how the original game has it", then for an Extra tab under
Esc -> Option with check-mark add-ons, the first a draggable Ping / FPS box like a private server's
(their video). The whole reading is in `docs/protocol/trace.md`.

**Trace (READ, both binaries).**
- **The request.** The client sends 0x7074 `[01 03 01 <selection>]` from the action window, a
  hotbar slot or the target menu, and checks nothing about the target.
- **The server's handling.**
  - It queues a kind-3 action on `CGCharAutoCommandActor`.
  - Every 30 ms it tests the target: a player, not dead, within the 3 x 3 regions.
  - Its walker (`0x4b0490`, every 100 ms) runs the tracer to both BCRadius + 50 short of the
    target, and only walks again past both + 80.
  - It leaves alone a walk that already heads within 15 degrees of the target.
  - It steps back out of the other body.
  - Past 1000 units it stands still (the trace stays).
  - It posts 0x704f `[03]` (run) after each forward walk.
- **The end.** The trace never finishes on arrival. 0xB074 `{2, 0}` ends it:
  - on the target's death or departure;
  - on the client's 0x7074 `[02]`, which the ground click sends;
  - on sitting, stun, sleep or freezing, a trade, mounting, death, a warp or logout.
  A new action replaces it silently. A buff (Basic_Activity other than 2) leaves it running.
- **No text.** Trace shows no message at all: the server sends no code the client prints.

**Built.**
- **Server:** `session/trace.go` answers 0x7074 and runs the 30 ms test. `cancelActions` ends a
  trace everywhere it already ended the auto-attack, except on moves (`moveCancelsActions`): the
  client's own trace walks are moves.
  - Freezing, sleep and stun landing now call `cancelActions`, as their appliers do.
  - So do a trade being established and a mount.
  - The attack, a Basic_Activity 2 cast and a pick-up drop the trace silently (Push).
- **Client:** `world/trace_follow.gd` is the walker line by line. World3D runs it every 100 ms
  (OURS: the place; OpenSRO's server does not move players), sends the cancel on a ground click,
  and keeps the action byte GI+0x620.
- **The target menu:** `ui/hud/target_menu.gd`, built from `res_ui\targetmenu.2dt`. It opens on a
  right click over a player when "Activate action short cut" is on (retail's option byte +0x1a,
  Default off), top-left at the cursor. Its five buttons do what the original's handlers do.
- **The Extra tab (OURS):** a fifth tab copied from the Game tab's button one step (125) to the
  right. Its pane is built from the Game pane's frame and CNIFGameOptionSlot rows.
  - Row 1, "Show the Ping / FPS counter": `ui/hud/ping_fps_counter.gd`, 87 x 54 with the reference
    video's three-line border (MEASURED on its 2x capture). It can be dragged anywhere and is saved
    where it is left. FPS refreshes every 0.5 s. Ping is an echo (OURS opcodes 0x00FC / 0x00FD,
    `session/ping.go`) sent every 5 s.
  - Row 2: the action short cut, until the Game tab is built.
- **QA aid:** partybot `-walk-loop` walks a bot round waypoints, so a trace has a moving target.

**Live** (`/var/tmp/r832q/qa832.sh`; bot Tracee runs a 160 x 120 loop round the client, 5 s a leg):
- **The action window's Trace:** `0x7074 [01 03 01 1]`, then `started on 1 (stop 58, walk again
  beyond 88)`. The tracer re-aims as the bot turns and holds 75-109 units behind a target that
  keeps running (stop 58 + the bot's lead).
- **The ground click:** the cancel, `trace ended (a click walk cancelled it)`; the click walk
  follows.
- **The target menu:** right click on Tracee opens the menu at the cursor (name box empty: he was
  already selected, as retail's select request is skipped then). Trace there starts it again.
- **No target selected** (the first run, the bot out of view): sent as 0, started and ended at
  once, as retail's IsPC refusal does.
- **The Extra tab and the box:** rendered (the box beside the minimap; the ping there is the
  offline movie writer's frame time, not the network).

**Tests.**
- Server: `trace_test.go` covers the layout, regions, death, an unknown id, the double answer to a
  cancel, sit, Push's silent drop and another kind refused. `ping_test.go` covers the echo.
- Client:
  - `trace_follow_test` checks every walker branch at its exact edges.
  - `trace832_test` checks the wire, the target choice and the box's ping and arithmetic. On the
    real Media.pk2 it also builds the Extra tab, switches tabs, runs Apply and Default, and builds,
    opens and presses the target menu.
  - The full run: 366 client suites, 1 failing -- `buff_persist_test`, the known timing-sensitive
    one (this file, the 282-suite run). It passed twice on its own. Server: `go test ./...` passes.
- **Review fix:** the walker's "already heading within 15 degrees" now uses a heading run's own
  heading too (an arrow-key or sky-click run), as the server's pc+0x24 does; it first read a
  heading run as standing.
- **Perf gate** (`--frames 60000`, base b82d70ad), median of 3:

  | view | frame ms | entry ms | freeze ms | hitches |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | jangan | 0.89 / 0.89 SAME | 8822 / 8800 SAME | 2804 / 2783 SAME | 5 / 5 SAME |
  | reeds | 0.86 / 0.86 SAME | 7876 / 6467 FASTER (load noise) | 1472 / 1470 SAME | 2 / 2 SAME |
  | cross | 1.04 / 1.04 SAME | 9555 / 9567 SAME | 2825 / 2825 SAME | 5 / 4 SAME |

  The gate's head copy predates the review fix (one branch in a 100 ms tick).
- **Prod:** the server half (0x7074, the ping echo) needs the new server; deployed with this round.

## Eight-hundred-and-thirty-first round: a quick swap shows no T-pose and no plate flicker; the release badge

The user (videos, ours against a private server's): "when quickly swapping weapons/shields the
character tposes and the name plate + guild text flicker". In our video, on a swap, the body stands
one frame in its bind pose with its arms out, and the plate (name and guild line) is gone for one
frame. The reference shows neither.

- **Cause, the pose.** Every equipment change rebuilds the body
  (`_apply_player_equipment_visual`, and `_redress_other` for others). The new `Skeleton3D` enters
  the tree in its bind pose and is posed at the next animation step. A worn list handled between
  that step and the draw put the bind pose on screen for a frame.
- **Cause, the plate.** The redress re-makes the own plate (`_refresh_player_name_plate`), and the
  plate sweep hides a new plate until it first measures it (`NamePlates.Sweep.add`). The guild line
  is the plate's child, so it went with it.
- **Fix (OURS; the original swaps the item on the same character object, so it has neither frame,
  INFERRED from InstallEquipVisual).**
  - `Skeleton3DBuilder.copy_pose(old, new)`, by bone name, before the old body is freed, on both
    paths.
  - A plate re-made over a shown one stays shown, and the sweep takes it from there.
- **The release badge.** v0.1.589's run finished 4 minutes after v0.1.590's, and GitHub marked
  v0.1.589 Latest. The user saw "the release isn't there". v0.1.590 was marked Latest by hand.
  `release.yml` now sets `make_latest` only when the tag is the highest `v*` tag (`sort -V`).
- **The original's swap, read** (the user: "check the original game code how it handles the switching
  to match it exactly"; `animation_mixer.md`, "A weapon change", has the addresses).
  - 0x3038's handler installs the item on the same character object: no new body, no new plate.
    Ours rebuilds the body, so it carries the old pose (copy_pose) and keeps the plate shown.
  - The animation changes only when the weapon's group does (`RefreshAnimationGroup`). A new group
    re-enters STAND / IDLE (or SIT, or MOVE).
- **Correction to round 808 (READ):** IDLE plays the stand or the battle stance with a fade-in of
  0, not 200. `0xa592f0` pushes `(type, 0, 200, ...)`, and A is a loop's fade-in all the way down
  (CCompChar slot 29's record → AniMixer `0xc55360` → the layer's `+0x88`). The old loop still
  fades out over 200, so the new stand starts at half weight in the mix.
  - `ClipMixer.IDLE_IN_MS = 0`, used by `_loop_in_ms` for stand and stance on every body (player,
    others, monsters) and on another player's stand-up.
  - The walk (200), the run (100) and the sit (200) were read right.
- **Same clip, new group:** a group change whose stand resolves to the clip already playing restarts
  it from frame 0 (the mixer's replay). `_mix_loop` is forgotten for the player; another player's
  loop entry is restarted.
- **Other players' redress.** Their clip entries now move onto the new body (`_repoint_animated`),
  so an unchanged group's clip runs on. Before this round every swap restarted it from frame 0 with
  no blend.
- **OPEN:** a weapon change while moving. The original re-enters MOVE before STAND is back, so
  MOVE's needs fail there (read); what the mover does next is not read. Ours restarts the run in the
  new group with its 100 ms fade.
- **Live** (`/var/tmp/r830q/qa830.sh` with `OPENSRO_QA_MIX_LOG=1`; sword 71 and shield 251 worn,
  bow 215 on key 1; keys 1, 3, 2, 1 at ticks 700 / 740 / 780 / 820).
  - Sword → bow → sword: the group changes, and both groups' stand is `chinaman_fighter_standcity`,
    so the stand restarts from frame 0 (t = 317 ms 20 ticks after each press).
  - The shield (group unchanged) leaves the clip running.
  - Frames 695..860: no one-frame jump (the frame-difference spike test), and the name plate is in
    every frame.
  - The round 829 build did not show the T-pose on the box either: there the worn list lands
    before the frame's pose. The user's video shows it over the network to prod. The fix does not
    depend on that timing: the new body never has a bind-pose frame.
- **Tests:** `skeleton3d_builder_test` (copy_pose: bones matched by name, extra bones kept). 364 client
  suites, 0 failing. Client and CI only: no server change.
- **Perf gate** (`--frames 60000`, base 4a3367f9 vs the working tree, 1280x720, median of 3): every
  number SAME. Frame ms: jangan 0.86 / 0.86, reeds 0.85 / 0.85, cross 1.02 / 1.02. Entry: jangan
  +84, reeds -19, cross -1256 ms. Freeze: -39, -5, +2 ms. Hitches: 5 / 5, 2 / 2, 4 / 5. Exit 0.

## Eight-hundred-and-thirtieth round: a hotbar swap emptied the previous item's key

The user (video): "When switching to a new item from the bar the previous item disappears." Each
key press put its item on, and the key of the item that came off emptied. A bow's key also emptied
the shield's key, since the bow pushes the shield into the bag.

- **Cause (MEASURED).** An equip gets two replies: the worn list, then the bag list that the client
  asks for right after the equip. Round 829 re-checked the bar on the worn list, still against the
  bag from before the equip. There the item that came off is neither worn nor in the bag, so its key
  was cleared, and the bar saved without it. On the render box both replies land in the same frame,
  so round 829's live check passed. Over the network to prod the worn list arrives first.
- **Fix (OURS).** `EquipTarget.quick_slot_binding` decides where a key's item binding goes. The worn
  list's re-check passes `bag_fresh = false`: an item missing there stays on the bar, inert, and only
  a bag list can clear a key. The original re-binds from the move reply itself (0x60e540), which names
  both slots, so it never has this gap.
- **QA hook.** `OPENSRO_QA_BAG_LIST_DELAY_MS` holds each bag list back by that many milliseconds.
- **Live** (`/var/tmp/r830q/qa830.sh`, delay 300 ms). Sword 71 and shield 251 worn, bow 215 in the
  bag; keys 1 bow, 2 shield, 3 sword; pressed 1, 3, 2.
  - **Fixed:** key 1 puts the bow on, and keys 2 and 3 follow the shield and sword into the bag.
    Pressing 3 puts the sword back on, and key 1 follows the bow. Pressing 2 puts the shield on. All
    three icons stay on the bar.
  - **Control** (the same run with the re-check marked fresh): pressing 1 logs "quickslot 2 cleared"
    and "quickslot 3 cleared", and keys 3 and 2 then do nothing. That is the user's video.
- **Tests:** `equip_target_test` (the swap and the displaced shield, against a stale bag and a fresh
  one). 364 client suites, 0 failing. Client only: no server change, no perf gate.
- **Not recoverable:** a key cleared before this fix stays cleared (the bar file was saved without
  it). Put the item on the key again.

### Round 830, second fix: the portrait showed the back of the body (a round 828 regression)

The user: "the character portrait at the top left is off now. It shows the body, not the head"; then
"almost looks like it's looking at the back and upside down".

- **Cause.** `PlayerPortrait.set_character` copies the world body and keeps its scale. Since round
  828 that scale is BodyMirror's (-h, h, h), and the portrait stage mirrors itself (`_mirror`, z ->
  -z). Two mirrors make a half turn, so the camera faced the body's back. Setting the avatar's yaw
  then decomposed that reflection into a negative scale on every axis: the user's "upside down".
- **Fix.** The copy takes the unsigned scale (`skeleton.scale.abs()`), as before round 828.
- **The other body copies** were checked: the paper doll and the party portraits build fresh,
  unmirrored bodies; a skill's afterimage copies the world transform, mirror included, which is right.
  Only the player portrait copied a world body into a stage of its own.
- **Live:** `/var/tmp/r830q/p1`, frame 690: the face, front-on and upright. It matches round 826's
  frame and not round 829's.
- **Test:** `player_portrait_test` dresses a BodyMirror'd copy and an unmirrored one. They must
  match: the same basis, upright, the same camera.
- **Round 828's miss:** its check of every `.scale` read missed this one, which takes the scale
  whole rather than as a size.

## Eight-hundred-and-twenty-ninth round: gear from the hotbar, the equipment window's drop rule, the held count, the repair flow, worn-out marks and the gear figure

The user asked for five things: weapons and shields on the hotbar that are put on when pressed;
dropping an item anywhere on the character area to equip it (rings went wrong); a carried stack
keeping its count; the repair flow as in their video (https://i.imgur.com/svVTDIk.mp4), confirm box
included; and the broken-item look ("red and flashing", plus a figure on the main screen). Three
research passes read the client; everything below is READ from sro_client.exe unless marked.

- **The equipment window's drop (`CIFEquipment::vslot_028`, 0x6ad180).**
  - It takes a held bag slot (kind 0x46) only; anything else is put back and nothing is sent.
  - It never looks at what is under the cursor. Every worn slot hands the drop to its parent
    (`CIFSlotWithHelp::vslot_028` 0x666560), and so does the picture. The item's TypeIDs pick the
    slot, then 0x7034 type 0 is sent:
    - 3/1/7: 8;
    - avatars: their storage;
    - weapons: 6;
    - shields and ammo: 7;
    - armour by TypeID4 (jump table 0x6ad594): 1 → 0, 2 → 2, 3 → 1, 4 → 4, 5 → 3, 6 → 5;
    - earring: 9; necklace: 10;
    - **ring: 11 if 11 is empty, else 12 if 12 is empty, else 11** (0x6ad502..0x6ad516).
  - Ours sent the slot under the cursor: a ring on a filled ring slot swapped it even with the other
    empty, and a drop on the picture did nothing. `EquipTarget.worn_slot_for` is the rule;
    `HudPanels.equip_from_bag` sends it. A worn item dropped on the window now stays worn (it was
    unequipped).
- **Gear on the hotbar (0x60b850 case 0x46, 0x60b94f..0x60ba95).**
  - The bar takes any bag, worn or avatar item (`CNIFUnderMenuBar::vslot_028` 0x60e950: no type
    filter).
  - Pressing a bag item that is not 3/3/x (ammo aside) or 3/2/x goes through that same handler: the
    slot is held, CIFEquipment's vslot 28 is called, then the slot is let go. Ours sent a use.
  - The binding follows the moves: `FUN_0060e540`, run by every 0xB034 reply over the 0x33 slots,
    moves a slot pointing at the source to the destination, swaps the destination's onto the source,
    and clears only on an item gone.
  - So a weapon put on stays on its key, **inert** (a worn binding breaks out of 0x60b850's switch).
    The weapon it swapped lands in the bag slot just emptied, and that weapon's key works.
  - Ours: a worn item keeps its slot at bag slot -1 (`World3D._resync_quickslot_items`; in-flight
    equips and the first worn list guard the race). The original matches the bag slot plus the
    RefItemID; ours matches the id anywhere in the bag. The outcome is the same for these moves.
- **The server's two-hander rule (INFERRED from the original server's `CGObjPC::AttachEquipItem`
  0x524cd0).** A two-hander put on over a shield takes the shield off into the bag, and a shield
  under a two-hander takes the weapon off. Ours refused both, which would have broken the swap.
  `twoHandedDisplaced` now unequips the other hand first. OPEN: the arrows moved to 7 with a bow,
  and the original's fallback to the weapon's own bag slot when the bag is full (ours refuses).
- **The held count.** The held slot is drawn by its own draw (0xb9d810 → 0x685e50), which draws the
  count (0x67bd70), so the count belongs on the cursor. Ours copied the texture only.
  `HeldIcon._carry_count` copies the slot's `CountLabel`.
- **The repair flow** (CIFStore control 0xb → 0x6cea60, 0xc → 0x6cfc00):
  - **Repair All** quotes on the client: worn slots 0..7 and the whole bag. An item counts if it is
    3/1, not an accessory, can be repaired (0x8bd0e0: no MATTR_NOT_REPARABLE, no MATTR_REPAIR ≤ 1)
    and costs more than 0.
    - The cost (`SOItem::FUN_008bacc0`): a broken item is CostRevive (column 28) plus the points
      from 1; then trunc(missing × clamp(CostRepair (col 27) / max, 1, 9.99e37)).
    - A total of 0 says UIIT_MSG_STRGERR_THERE_IS_NO_ITEM_TO_REPAIR and opens nothing.
    - Otherwise CMessageBoxManager purpose 0x0C opens (`RepairBox`, MsgBoxINIF, the geometry from
      0x646400..0x64671a). The client never holds the total against the purse.
  - **Repair** toggles the hammer cursor 0x96: forced cursor 0x777e70, new `GameCursor.forced_id`,
    which also refuses the pick-up. A worn or bag slot clicked under it:
    - CanRepair (col 22) 0: nothing;
    - unrepairable: 0x1c11;
    - full: nothing;
    - otherwise it repairs at once, with no box. Hiding the store ends the hammer.
  - **The reply.** Success shows nothing (ours wrote "Repaired for X gold."). A refusal goes to the
    system window.
  - **Per item whose durability rose:** snd_repair (from 0: snd_revive), and the slot's flash
    (`RepairFlash`): `icon_mall_repair.ddj`, 20 cells of 32 × 32 at 50 ms, drawn 72 × 72 at
    (-20, -20).
  - **Server.** It repairs the bag too (bag slots as 13 + n), stops at the first 0x1c07, and charges a
    broken item's restore fee before mending it as from 1 (`HandleRepairRequest`,
    docs/protocol/durability.md). The fee needs the new `ReviveCost` column: itemdata col 28, CSV
    column 91, `items.revive_cost`.
  - **The client's table.** The item table gained CanRepair, CostRepair and CostRevive, in both
    readers (`repair_ints`; TABLE PARITY PASS).
- **Worn-out marks** (the slot draw, 0x67dfb8..0x67e2c7; `DurabilityMark`).
  - The icon is never darkened (ours greyed a broken one).
  - **Broken** (0 with a maximum): `icon_item_broken.ddj`, a still red box.
  - **Low** (1..6 on equipment that is no accessory): `icon_item_warning.ddj`, 16 frames of 16 × 16,
    n = ftol(c / 17 × 16). c is the interface counter: 80 ms steps (timer 3, 0x7872b0), wrapping at
    17, a 1360 ms loop.
  - On the bag and the worn slots, and on a quick slot (frame 0, which has no counter). OPEN: the
    `icon_disable.ddj` overlay for an item unusable for another reason too.
- **The gear figure** (`CEquipStateImg`, ginterface.txt GDR_EQUIP_STATE_WND, `EquipStateImg`).
  - 68 × 96 at (width - 200, 74).
  - One `com_re_*` overlay per worn slot 0..7, in `_y` (1..6) or `_r` (0), on the `com_re_avatar`
    knight (0x65cc50 / 0x65cb40).
  - Hidden when nothing is worn out; no flashing.
- **Live wear (0x3052).**
  - The original sends `{u8 slot, u32 durability}` on every change. Ours saved and logged wear and
    sent nothing.
  - The server now sends it on every wear step (`notifyDurability`). The client handles it
    (`NetClient.durability_changed`): the stored lists, snd_eqbreak at 0 and snd_eqdanger at exactly
    6 on a worn item (the table authors them with each other's .wav), the slot's mark and the figure.
- **Live** (`/var/tmp/r829q/qa829.sh`, the Jangan smith; a China level-30 character with sword 71,
  mail 899, helm 791 and shield 251 put on through the equip message, then `/durability` weapon 3,
  mail 0, helm 20).
  - **Before the repair:**
    - the weapon slot pulses;
    - the mail slot shows the red box;
    - the figure shows the knight with a red chest and a yellow sword.
  - **Repair All:** "Repair All quotes 522 gold". The box has "Agreement window", the "Repair all"
    bar, the sentence, "522 Gold", and Yes / No.
  - **Yes:** "repaired 3 item(s) for 522 gold". The quote matches the charge, the revive fee
    included; before the fee was built it was 521 quoted against 351 charged.
  - **After:** snd_repair and snd_revive play; the sparks show on the three slots; the marks and the
    figure clear.
  - **Hotbar** (keys 1 and 2, two swords):
    - 1 puts on sword 71, and key 1 goes inert;
    - 2 puts on 3632; 71 lands in bag slot 0, and key 1 follows it;
    - 1 puts 71 on again.
- **Tests:**
  - `equip_target_test`, `repair829_test`, `durability829_test`;
  - `held_icon_test` (the count, and the doll's mail drop by type);
  - `error_text_test` (repair refusals to the system window);
  - server: `TestEquipTwoHandedClearsTheOtherHand`, `TestRepairHandlerMendsTheBag`,
    `TestRepairChargesTheReviveFee`, `TestEncodeDurabilityChanged`, refdata column 91.
  - 364 client suites, 0 failing; the server suite passes; native 87.
- **Deploy:** a server change and the items table re-imported for `revive_cost` (deploy/README.md,

## Eight-hundred-and-twenty-eighth round: bodies drawn the right way round, seal effects on both hands of a dual weapon

The user: "the two handed sword in the original game is held in the right hand not the left like
ours. Double check which hands all weapons / shield should be in. Also ... double axes only show the
seal effect on just one axe, same with daggers."

- **Which bone each weapon names (MEASURED, all 3,455 item `.bsr` of the archive; the attach is the
  file's own, READ `CCompChar::FUN_00c4fc70`).**
  - `Bip01 R HandMid`: swords, blades, spears, glaives, the two-handed sword (30 of 31), crossbows,
    dark and light staves, and the `_r` of dual axes and daggers.
  - `Bip01 L HandMid2`: the two-handed staff, the harp, and the `_l` of dual axes and daggers.
  - `Bip01 L Hand`: bows (21; 5 on `L HandMid2`) and shields (Europe: 19, and 6 on `L HandMid`).

  `tools/probe_weapon_hands.gd` confirms that our build hangs each model from exactly that bone. So
  the bone was never the fault.
- **The body was a mirror image (MEASURED, READ).** The readers keep the files' left-handed
  coordinates as written, and round 61's z -> -z sits on the terrain group only. Bodies hang outside
  it.
  - An unmirrored CHAR_EU_MAN_NOBLE faces -Z (right foot to right toe) with `Bip01 R Hand` at
    x -6.96, on its left: (R - L) . right = -13.92.
  - The PI turn of round 31 faced the body forward. It cannot undo a reflection.
  - So every right-hand weapon showed in the left hand and every shield on the right arm. NPCs,
    monsters and pets were mirrored too.
  - The paper doll, portrait, select and create screens were right already: each has a `D3DSpace`
    node with scale.z = -1.
- **The fix (OURS): `BodyMirror.apply`** negates the body skeleton's own x where a body enters the
  world: the player, other players (both build paths), NPCs, monsters, monster rides, pets, and the
  crowd ghosts' local transform. An x mirror in the body's frame is the world's z flip composed with
  a turn of PI, so the -Z front and every heading read off it (`SkillEffects.heading_of`,
  `MonsterMotion.facing_yaw`) stay. With the mirror the probe reads +13.92: the right hand on the
  right. Effects at bones inherit it (`EfpEffect` already flips its cull for a mirrored host, as the
  terrain's objects need).
- **What the mirror touched:**
  - **CrowdGpu.** A far instance's transform is the identity, so Godot cannot flip its cull. Its twin
    shaders now cull the other face (`mirrored_cull`: back <-> front, disabled kept, none -> front),
    and it refuses an unmirrored body instead of a mirrored one.
  - **Scale reads.** A mirrored basis's `get_scale()` is negative, and so is the scale of a node
    whose transform was set whole. Six readers now take `absf`: skill effects' body scale, BsrEffect,
    the NPC bounds, the monster label height, the far plate height and a QA helper.
  - **Monster rides.** The seat takes the rider's size alone (the saddle pose carries the ride's
    mirror). A dummy ride's root is the rider's transform less its mirror, since the ride's own
    skeleton carries one: `BodyMirror.unmirrored`, in `MonsterRide.place` and the slope tilt's copy.
- **Seal effects on both hands (READ).** `CObjCharacter::FUN_00a60a90` calls `FUN_00a5f3e0` at
  0xa60bde and 0xa60bff, once each for the visual record's +4 and +8. Those are the `_r` and `_l`
  models of a dual axe or dagger (`FUN_00a5f4f0`: TypeID4 9 or 13; a plain model and 0 otherwise).
  Each call puts the glow and every particle row on its own part. A 0 part does nothing.
  - Ours put each row on the first model with the bone (`_bone_host`), so the left axe and dagger
    went bare. `EquipGlow.bone_hosts` now gives one host per model, in `EquipGlow.apply` and the far
    recipe (`_far_fx_row`).
  - A ghost's host id gains the model, since the two models carry the same rows on the same bone
    index.
  - This closes weapon_glow.md's OPEN 4. Other weapons have one model, so spears, glaives and
    two-handed staves are unchanged, as the user expected.
- **Live** (`/var/tmp/r828/qa828.sh`, no server, the Jangan spawn, four sides):
  - **The two-handed sword:** seen from behind, it is in the right hand.
  - **Pain's own kit (prod's character 12):** body 14878, the degree-11 Nova set +12, and from the
    bag the Nova axe, dagger, two-handed sword, and sword with shield, all +12.
  - **Dual weapons:** `QA EQUIPFX` logs the axes' three `eternity_11_nova_bow` rows and the +8
    `system_enchantbow_a_01` 28 times each, on two hosts. The dagger's `eternity_11_nova` rows do the
    same. One-model weapons log 14, one host.
  - **Shield:** the shield is on the left arm, seen from behind.
- **The far path, drawn both ways (MEASURED, `tools/crowd_gpu_probe.gd --mode=pixels`, Forward+,
  1280 x 720; its bodies mirrored as the world's).** 8 Figures with kits, both races and sexes, the
  weapon and shield at +13: 8 of 8 drawn far, `refused={}`. Near against far (`frame_ab.py`) gives
  d2 = 0.00000, dmax 5 at t = 0.37 and dmax 2 at t = 1.13. The far bodies draw solid, not inside out.
- **Perf gate** (`--base 5a4e52e1 --head 60681194 --sites jangan,cross --frames 60000`, 3 runs, exit 0):

  | site | frame ms | entry ms | freeze ms | hitches |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | jangan | 0.87 / 0.87 SAME | 9995 / 8610 FASTER (the base's first run, 9995 against 8685 and 8650) | 2760 / 2753 SAME | 3 / 5 SAME |
  | cross | 1.01 / 1.01 SAME | 9351 / 9327 SAME | 2767 / 2766 SAME | 4 / 4 SAME |

- **Not checked (OPEN):** an effect placed in world space with only the caster's heading (not hung
  from a bone or the body's basis) is still drawn from the raw left-handed file, so a chiral one (a
  spiral's turn) may spin the other way. Bone-hung effects and BsrEffects follow the body's mirror now.
- **Tests.** `crowd_gpu_test` (bodies mirrored as the world's; `mirrored_cull`; F9 now refuses an

## Eight-hundred-and-twenty-seventh round: the hotbar's selection frame fades out over 4 seconds

The user reported that the gold frame on the last used quick slot fades. Round 826 had read the call
in `FUN_0060a820` as "alpha 255" and left its other arguments OPEN; they are a fade.

- **The call (READ, 0x60a86e..0x60a88f).** `0x46ca80(255, 0, 4.0, 0.0, 0)` on child 103: start alpha
  `+0x130` = 255, current `+0x131` = 255, end alpha `+0x132` = 0, length `+0x134` = 4.0 (`0xd8ada8`, read
  from the exe's .rdata), time gone `+0x138` = 0.0, hide-at-end `+0x18c` = 0.
- **The fade (READ, the CGWnd part at +0x84; its fields there are +0xac..+0xb4).** The window's
  vslot 12 (`0x46cd80`) hands vslot 1 of that part (`0x470780`) the frame's seconds `DAT_0110f7fc`. A
  length of 0 does nothing. Otherwise gone += seconds. When gone > 0, `0x470a00` sets the alpha: the
  end alpha once gone >= length, else `trunc(from x (1 - gone/length) + to x gone/length)` (the x87
  control word forced to chop, 0x470a65). When gone <= 0, the start alpha. Then, once gone >= length,
  gone and length go to 0 and vslot 7 (`0x46cd10`) runs: message 0x8064, and a hide only when
  `+0x18c` is 1 and the end alpha is 0. Here `+0x18c` is 0, so the frame stays shown at alpha 0.
  The next use starts it again from 255.
- **The seconds (READ; the unit INFERRED).** `0xba4117` copies the app's float `+0x9c` into
  `DAT_0110f7fc`, capped at 3.0 (`0xd8adc4`), beside `DAT_0110f7f8` = the ms delta `+0x98` capped at
  3000 (0xbb8). The paired caps make it seconds. The writer of `+0x9c` was not traced.
- **The user's round 826 video (MEASURED again, `hotbar_vid/gold.txt`).** Its longest hold is 1.73 s
  (slot 1, 2.67-4.40 s), with the gold at 99 -> 102 throughout. Under the code above it would be at
  57 %. That client (another server's, with its own bar art) does not fade; ours follows the binary.
- **The user's second video (MEASURED, https://i.imgur.com/7yoGsft.mp4, 30 fps, slot 7's top edge
  luma over x 520..569, y 46..47).** The frame appears at 0.23 s and is back at the slot's own border
  (luma 49.2, from 217.1) 4.0 s later. Its alpha, (luma - floor) / (start - floor), stays within 0.02 of
  1 - t/4 throughout: 0.82 at 0.80 s (linear 0.80), 0.47 at 2.13 s (0.47), 0.20 at 3.20 s (0.20),
  0 at 4.00 s.
- **OURS:** `HudUnderbar.step_slot_frame(seconds)` with `_process` passing `min(delta, 3.0)`;
  `set_process` only while a fade runs. `modulate.a` = alpha / 255. Godot's float64 stands in for the
  x87 float32 (at most one alpha step at a boundary).
- **Tests.** `hud_underbar_test.gd`: 255 at the use, 191 at 1 s, 95 at 2.5 s, 255 again on a new use,
  6 at 3.9 s, 0 (still shown) past 4 s and after. 361 suites, 0 failing.
- **Live** (`qa826.sh`, HOTKEY=470:1, 60 fps movie, `/var/tmp/r827/s1`). The gold of slot 1's top
  edge (R - B over x 342..379, y 485..488):
  - 3.8 before the use;
  - 61.4 at frame 490, falling about 2.45 every 10 frames (51.6 at 530, 37.0 at 590, 22.4 at 650,
    10.2 at 700, 5.5 at 720);
  - back to 3.8 at 730.

  That is a straight line over ~242 frames, about 4.0 s. The frame first shows about 16 frames after
  the scripted key tick (the QA hook's input path, as in round 826).
- UI only: no perf gate, no server change, no prod restart.

## Eight-hundred-and-twenty-sixth round: the camera shake, falling AT_TARGET movers, the pick-up's lock, the hotbar's frame and cooldown figures, item re-use, the strip bar under windows

The user (2026-10-25): "there's some screen shake effects for certain skills like Bash under Warrior. Can you
verify this effect and implement it for any skills that do that and any other similar effects"; "when picking
up items our game does it instantly but I think the original waits on the animation"; "add hotbar item
selection highlighting" (a video, https://i.imgur.com/EYII52x.mp4); "items / skills show the time during
cooldown ... match the style and font"; "When equipping a job item there's a yellow countdown timer bar ...
That yellow bar appears over open GUI windows and it shouldn't."

- **The camera shake (READ, docs/protocol/camera_shake.md).** One shake at a time on the game process
  (`FUN_0078db50`): a strength that falls linearly over 500 ms, redrawn on a 20 or 25 ms timer as
  `(rand() % 2s - s) / 100` on the look-at point's x and height. Started by a skill row's Script
  SCT_SHAKECAM0..3 when it plays and SCT_SHAKECAM_MOV0..3 when its mover lands (strengths 50 / 200 / 300 /
  400), unless the caster is another player (an exact CICUser test); and by this player's own blows: a
  critical 50, any blow in berserk 50, a critical in berserk 200. Bash (SKILL_EU_WARRIOR_TWOHANDA_DASH_A)
  is SHAKECAM0 on its SHOT/1 row. 391 rows carry one (MEASURED). Not built: the fortress structures'
  shake (no structures) and the developer command `/cs`.
- **AT_TARGET movers (READ, FUN_00a51bc0 case 3).** An AT_TARGET row with a non-zero MovTypeSpeed speed
  falls from the target + StartOffset to the target + TargetOffset (world axes) and lands the group's hit;
  231 rows (the China force bolts) had hung 100 units over the target and never landed their ObjName2.
- **The pick-up (READ).** The click filter `FUN_009ec240` refuses a walk while `[player+0x65c] & 0x2476`
  is set, and the state enter sets bit 1 << state (`0x9c9a19`), so the pick-up's state 10 (0x400) refuses
  ground clicks until its 533 ms clip (MEASURED) ends; G does nothing in state 10 (`0x793d1f`). The item
  itself goes into the bag at once in the original too (the server's `FUN_00526090`): no delay was added.
- **The hotbar's frame (READ, `FUN_0060a820` / `FUN_0060bb80`).** Child 103 (`ub_slot_arrow.ddj`) moves to
  the page slot of the last use numbered 1..10 -- a number key, or a right-click on a first-page slot -- at
  (x - 4, y - 3), and stays (no hide; no fade in the user's video, MEASURED over 324 frames -- but the binary fades it, round 827; its bar art from
  another client, the frame the same texture).
- **Cooldown figures (READ, `0x67c920`).** A quick slot's time left: the veil `icon_effect.ddj` and white
  seconds up to 60 s, yellow (0xffe1e700) minutes up to 3600 s, the `int_effect.ddj` veil and blue
  (0xff000ca9) hours above, in the 8 x 12 bitmap figures `cool_time_0..9.ddj` (no font), centred. Quick
  slots only: the skill window and the bag show none.
- **Item re-use (READ, CItemReuseDelayManager; `Item_OnUseItemResult 0x87a7b0`, `0x67cbf0`).** The client

## Eight-hundred-and-twenty-fifth round: the region-crossing pause measured -- NPC placement, not shaders

The user (2026-10-25): "Would shaders help us reduce the short pauses during regions?" No: a crossing
compiles no shader at draw time, and the pause is one frame placing a region's NPCs.

- **Method.** A throwaway probe (an autoload in a box-only copy, `/var/tmp/r825`, not committed) printed
  every frame over 25 ms and every frame whose `Performance.PIPELINE_COMPILATIONS_*` counters moved,
  beside the client's own `cell x/y built in` lines. Forward+, Godot 4.7.2, 1280 x 720, offline with
  `OPENSRO_QA_LOCAL_NPCS=1` (the server's NPC records fed the same `_npc_records` path), a QA walk;
  `XDG_DATA_HOME` per run so the shader cache was empty (cold) or the previous run's (warm).
- **MEASURED.**

  | walk | worst frame | its cost | draw-time compiles at the crossing |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | 97/166 -> 97/165 (row 163 streams: five sparse cells) | 25.5 ms | 9-14 ms a cell | 0 |
  | 97/165 -> 97/166, cold cache (row 168: Jangan) | 450 ms | cell 97/168: npcs 358, objects 70 ms | 0 |
  | the same, warm cache | 458 ms | npcs 363, objects 71 ms | 0 |

  98/168 (122 objects) cost 87-88 ms (place 50). The world entry's ~75 draw-time compilations
  (`PIPELINE_COMPILATIONS_DRAW` 74-80 at the end of the drain) all fall under the loading screen.
- **Why (READ, World3D).** `_try_spawn_region_npcs` places every held NPC record of a region in the
  frame its cell commits, and a model's first use runs `SkinnedBsrAssembler.assemble_from_archive` on
  the main thread. Online play takes the same path (records from the server's spawns wait in
  `_npc_records` until their region stands).
- **What would help (not done).** Placing a region's NPCs a few a frame (the monster build queue's
  budget) and assembling the models off the main thread; spreading a dense cell's object placement the
  same way. Re-measure with the same walk (`run.sh` there: `MAPM='97\165.m' AT=1700,1020 HEAD=90`).
- **OPEN.** Compatibility (OpenGL) has no pipeline counters and was not measured; its shader
  compilation can add pauses of its own.

## Eight-hundred-and-twentieth round: the compiled quests' missions, and quests no monster can finish

- **The exporter (MEASURED).** A compiled quest can allocate a helper object (0x24 bytes) before
  its mission (`CQNO_TQ_BAEKRYOUNG_10::DeclareQuestContent`: `FUN_009dd2bc(0x24)`, then
  `FUN_009dd2bc(0xa7)`, the dialog, then `FUN_009173b0`). `ParseDecomp` filed the mission under the
  first allocation's class (0x24, unmodelled): 24 quests. The mission is now the last allocation
  before `FUN_009173b0`. Coverage: playable 618 -> 626, reachable 564 -> 577.
- **Quest-spawned monsters (READ, MEASURED).** Six of the eight quests that became playable kill
  `MOB_QT_*` monsters that no nest spawns (`MOB_QT_TQ_TOMBGENERAL4`, `MOB_QT_CH_SOLDIER_01_1`, ...):
  the original spawns them from the quest's own handlers (`QNO_TQ_STONEBOARD_4::OnAfterActivated`
  and its kin), which OpenSRO does not model. OURS: `Catalog.HideUnspawnedQuestMonsters` takes out
  of play a quest whose kill or gather mission names only `MOB_QT_*` monsters nothing here spawns
  (the server measures it from its own spawn slots at boot, and logs the codes). Before this,
  QNO_EU_ADVENTURER_1 and QNO_EU_FERRY2_1 (`MOB_QT_01_CRAB`) were offered and could not be
  finished.
- **A data gap, not changed (MEASURED).** The operator's nest tables (the shard dump's
  `tab_refnest`, the same on the box and prod: 16,381 rows, 11,853 nests hatched) have no nest for
  many field species with tactics rows: `MOB_CA_MONKEY` (tactics 28500), `MOB_RM_ROC` (35600),
  `MOB_SD_PETBE` (38460), and `MOB_EU_KYKLOPES` has no tactics row. 174 offered quests name such a
  monster. They stay offered: the gap is the dump's (a full shard database would fill it), and
  hiding them is the user's call.
- **Tests.** `TestParseCompiledHelperAlloc`, `TestHideUnspawnedQuestMonsters`.

## Eight-hundred-and-nineteenth round: the quest talk as the original's -- OK closes it

The user (2026-10-24): "When I hit confirm on the quest it doesn't close the window. Not only that
let's fully support quests". This round is the first quest step; the gap list (a read of both
binaries) orders the rest (docs/protocol/quests.md).

- **Cause (READ).** The server answered a closing page's OK with nothing (`answer()` had no case
  for it), and the client ignored 0xB04B (`NpcTalkNet.ended` was connected to nothing). The
  original's CBasicQuest conversation (`s:0x920110`) runs TerminateMenu on every OK (CGObjPC vslot
  0x154 -> EndInteraction `s:0x5107c0`, 0xB04B {1}), and the client's `0x886ac0 -> 0x79e350`
  closes the NPC talk, store and storage windows by ShowWindow(0), whatever the result.
- **Fix, server.** Every quest page is the original's type-4 list with the quest's
  `SN_TALK_COMMON_*` lines (an offer [Accept, Refuse], responses 5 and 6; every other page [OK]);
  the OK ends the talk (`endInteraction`, factored out of the 0x704B handler: the trader and
  caravan hooks run as EndInteraction's own code does); after an accepted quest it first sends the
  quest's `MIDDLE_ACHIEVED` as a 0x30EC notice. The reward take ends the talk on every path, then
  sends `SN_TALK_COMMON_END` (0x30EC) and 0xB515.
- **The rest of the conversation (READ).** `NOT_PARTY` for a party-only quest (divide type 1)
  out of a party sharing EXP and items (`s:0x9261d0`); `COUNT_LIMIT` for a `LuaSetRealTime` quest
  at its limit; `ACCEPT_AFTER_ONE_CLEAR` for a `LuaSetDifferentString` quest cleared before;
  `INVENTORY_FULL` before the reward window when the reward does not fit; Accept reads
  `SN_TALK_COMMON_MAXQUEST` at 33 quests (and still accepts: nothing else reads the count). The
  setters, from the binary's own registration table: `LuaSetDivideType` 0x86bb20 (builder +0x826,
  quest +0x2e), `LuaSetRealTime` 0x86ba00 (mask |= 0x100000), `LuaSetDifferentString` 0x86b200
  (+0x85d); the compiled quests write +0x2e and the condition block's +0x1d directly. Exported as
  two new catalogue columns (an older catalogue still loads).
- **Party-only kills (READ).** `s:0x9210a0` runs the party check before any kill or gather
  mission: a party-only quest counts nothing out of a sharing party.
- **0x30D5 (READ).** Byte +9 is the divide type (it was 1 for every quest), the mission index the
  mission's +1 (`s:0x91be70`).
- **Give up (READ, `s:0x571b80`).** No reply for a quest with no record; {2, 2} for one not under
  way (status 1, 7, 8); {2, 5} while an NPC talk is open; else {1, id}.
- **Fix, client.** 0xB04B closes the NPC windows silently (no 0x704B back), the reward window
  hides the talk box silently (`c:0x884ca0`), 0x30EC shows in the quest info notice with
  `snd_quest_end` for `SN_TALK_COMMON_END` (`FUN_00884a30`), and a quest line is answered once
  until the next page (CIF_NPCTalk +0x7f0).
- **Measured in the user's data** (the re-export): 58 `LuaSetRealTime` quests, every one limit 1;
  divide types 0 x564, 5 x105, 1 x26, 4 x1 (QNO_RM_MEETROC_6, which the party check never
  passes, in retail too); 40 different-string quests.
- **Live (`/var/tmp/r819/q1`).** At the Jangan smith: list -> [Accept, Refuse] -> accepted ->
  `AT_ACCEPT` [OK] -> OK at tick 720 -> the talk window is gone at 780 and the smith carries the
  quest mark.
- **OPEN.** Which offers the first talk menu lists; the start branch's other COUNT_LIMIT test;
  where the row's colour bar draws (OpenSRO draws none yet).
- **Tests.** `quest819_test.go` (7: refuse, party-only, repeat limit and after-one-clear, the
  MAXQUEST line, the update header, a full bag, party-only kills), `csvio819_test.go` (2), the

## Eight-hundred-and-eighteenth round: the mouse no longer reaches the world through a window

The user (2026-10-24): "when I'm interacting with menus in the game like scrolling it also affects the game
behind it like I'll zoom in and out at the same time or move around".

- **Cause 1, the wheel (MEASURED).** Godot (4.3 on) gives every Control `mouse_force_pass_scroll_events`,
  default on: a wheel event goes up through a STOP control to its parent and on to `_unhandled_input`. A
  STOP square in `audit_input_bleed.gd`'s probe took the motion and still let the wheel through, so every
  wheel step over any window zoomed the camera. Fix: `World3D.wheel_over_window`, a STOP control on the
  chain of the control under the mouse, asked in `_input` before the GUI has the step (a list the step
  scrolls can move the row out from under the mouse: the skill board did, 5 points).
- **Cause 2, clicks and motion past a window's rect (MEASURED).** A window stops the mouse over its own
  rect; the guild and community windows' side tabs (`MainFrame176` Static1300, 223, 224, 314 points), the
  alchemy window's (Static2, 208) and the character pane's HP/MP text (6) are drawn past it, so a click
  there walked the player. Fix: `HudWindow.catch_overhang`, on each show: a bare PASS control on each
  drawn control's rect that reaches past the window, the window's first child (hit-tested last, so it
  never takes a button's click) handing the point to the window.
- **Retail (READ, round 697):** a window under the mouse that is not the interface itself takes the
  message (`FUN_00b9dc00 != CGInterface`); the world gets nothing under a window.
- **Tool.** `client/tools/audit_input_bleed.gd` opens all 21 windows and pushes a motion (routed as a
  click is) and, with `--wheel=1`, a wheel step at every 4-6 px of every on-screen drawn control; a sink
  at the root's end counts what reaches `_unhandled_input`. Before: 6,060 on-screen points (motion) plus
  every point (wheel); after: 0 and 0. Controls parked off the screen (the exchange's at x 10832) are not
  sampled.
- **Test.** `input_bleed_test.gd` (12 checks). `check` ALL LOAD, `tests` 354 suites, 0 failing. UI-only:
  no perf gate.

## Eight-hundred-and-seventeenth round: the plate box hangs from the baseline, as the original's

The user (2026-10-23): "the name plates on everything. There's slightly too much padding between the top and
the text. Check the original and the screenshots I sent you", then "also looks like there's 0 padding at the
bottom of some plates? Double check them all".

- **MEASURED, the original** (the user's 2x private-server picture, `svm`): every boxed plate is 16 rows, 4
  above Tahoma's 9-row caps and 3 under the baseline; `< Monkey >`'s "y" ends one row above the box's bottom.
  **Ours** (the user's v0.1.577 capture, 2x): 4.5 rows over the caps, 2 under the baseline; the "y" of
  `< Jeremy >` ran one row past the box (0 padding).
- **The original (READ).** The text item's h (`+0x4e`, `FUN_008b3910`) is its line gap `+0x30` (5, set by the
  constructor `FUN_008b46d0`) plus the font's `+4`, the point size GNFontChar keeps (9 for font 0;
  `FUN_00baa110` makes the 12 px em from it): 14 rows, so the box (`FUN_008b48b0`, 1 px round the item) is 16.
  Each glyph cell is drawn from the item's y down (`FUN_008b2290`, no per-glyph rise), so the box's top is one
  row above the cell's, and the cell's top is the face's tmAscent above the baseline.
- **Cause.** `NamePlates.box_rect` centred the 16-row box on the label's line (Godot's ascent + descent) and
  raised it a row (round 673's measurement, under the Arial fallback). Under Tahoma (ascent 12, descent 3)
  that is half a row high.
- **Fix.** The box hangs from the baseline: top = cell ascent + 1 over it. The cell ascent is GDI's tmAscent
  (`NamePlates.cell_ascent`): OS/2 usWinAscent / unitsPerEm x em, rounded to nearest (INFERRED as GDI's rule,
  MEASURED to match: Tahoma 12 px gives 12, and the picture's caps sit 4 rows down). Godot's own ascent is
  FreeType's rounded UP (Tahoma 2049/2048 x 12 = 12.006 -> 13), a row too many. Every plate takes it: names,
  titles, pets, NPCs, monsters, the guild line and the batched crowd plates; the job mark stays top-aligned with
  the box.
- **The guild line's box (READ, against the picture).** `FUN_009dea30` sets the guild line through

## Eight-hundred-and-sixteenth round: a skeletal model's boneless pieces stand still (the storage chests)

The user (2026-10-23): "can you fix the bug where the storage chest moves up and down. It's been a long
standing bug", then "Also some storage models are bugged into their chest, fix that too".

- **Cause (MEASURED).** The storage keepers' `.bsr` files carry the chest (and on the China and West China men
  a chain) as mesh pieces with **no bone palette** (`dump_bms_skin.gd`: `chinasystem_warehousekeeper_box.bms`
  150 vertices, palette of 0 bones; `_chain` 1216 vertices, 0). `SkinnedBsrAssembler` hung such a piece
  rigidly off the bone nearest its centroid: the China man's box off `Bip01 R Clavicle` (6.07 away), the chain
  off `Bip01 L Clavicle`, so both rose and fell with his breathing; the Khotan and Central Asia women's box off
  `Bip01 R Calf`, so it swung with the leg she sits with and she sank into it (renders at idle frame 30).
- **The original (READ).** `ResObject::FUN_00be2f80`, with the mesh's skin array (`+0xc4`) empty, writes
  palette entries 0/0 at blend weight 1.0 for every vertex (`LAB_00be3436`). The skinning shader
  (`shader\vss2.c`, Data.pk2) reads entry `i` at `c[3i + 26]` (`VSC_COMMON`) and then applies
  `VSC_WORLD_VIEW_PROJECTION` only; `CObjRendererVS::FUN_00bf0310` uploads the bones from register `0x1d`
  (entry 1) on, and `0xbeeaa0` uploads the identity at `0x1a` (entry 0). So such a piece is drawn still, at its
  own coordinates in the model's space; nothing ties it to a bone. This also turns round 626's INFERRED "entry
  0 is the object's own space" into READ (BMS_FORMAT.md, BSR_FORMAT.md's OPEN row answered).
- **Fix.** `SkinnedBsrAssembler.still_piece_mesh`: the piece is skinned wholly to `OBJECT_SPACE_BONE` (the
  still bone `build_skin` already adds for entry 0), canonical or not. It stays a skinned piece, so MonsterDraw's
  clone and CrowdGpu take it as any other; the rigid path is left for a palette naming bones the skeleton lacks.
  Test: `still_piece_test.gd` (8 checks: weights, the kept arrays, still under a posed root and clavicle, the
  canonical index).
- **Reach (MEASURED, `census_unskinned_pieces.gd`).** 75 of Data.pk2's 1,252 animated skeletal models carry 365
  bare pieces: the storage keepers' boxes (China, West China, Khotan, Central Asia, Arabia, the SD areas), the
  stablemen's tongs, the smiths' trees, the village headman's chair, the gambler's stick, the shaman's tiger,
  the stall booths, tower-defence crystals, Celestius `demonwarrior` (two pieces, no skinned one: it now stands
  still as the original draws it), and `pet2` / `COS` placeholders whose other pieces do not parse.
- **The keeper on the chest is retail.** Jangan places `NPC_CH_WAREHOUSE_M` (Storage-Keeper Wangu) and

## Eight-hundred-and-fifteenth round: a pet's owner line follows the suit; grant names at any guild level

The user (2026-10-23), on v0.1.575: "I don't see the guild name above me for the guild Verzion? Also my pet
still shows my trader name above it instead of my regular name after I took off my job suit", then "Grant
name can now be any guild level", and "I'm 575 still".

- **The guild line** is round 814's, in v0.1.576; the user was on v0.1.575, whose spawn reader reads the
  guild fields and draws nothing. The v0.1.576 release build was still queued for a runner. No code change.
- **The pet's owner line (READ, OPEN, OURS).** The client builds a COS's owner line (`ICCos::FUN_009c5ea0`,
  `"*" + alias` while the owner's job state is not 4) only at the COS's spawn (`CICCos::vslot_025`, its one
  caller); 0x30CA's handler (`FUN_008a7690`) stores the job byte through slot 44 (`+0x50d`) and nothing
  else; slot 15 draws the stored label. So the original's refresh after a suit change is OPEN. OpenSRO's
  client also ignored 0x30CA (decoded, never connected), and the server only sent 0x30CA. Fix (server only,
  so the v0.1.575 client takes it): `setJobState` also spawns each owned COS again in place
  (`cosAnnounce(o, cosSpawnTypeKnown)`, no summon effect), whose record carries the owner's name or alias
  as the job now is; the client's in-place update re-labels it (`_on_cos_spawned` -> `_cos_label`).
  Test: `TestRound815SuitChangeRespawnsTheCOS` (an ability pet: the alias in the suit, the name out of it).
  Not checked live (a suit needs an alias and a town); the client half is the existing in-place path.
- **Grant names at any guild level (OURS, the user).** `guild.CheckNickname` drops the level test (READ
  `GetLevel() < 4` -> 0x4c51); `ErrNicknameGuildLevel` and `MinLevelForNickname` are gone; tests changed.

## Eight-hundred-and-thirteenth round: monsters and mounts lean with the slope; a chaser swings between passes

The user (2026-10-23), on v0.1.574, with an original and an OpenSRO screenshot of a mount on a hillside:
"Have mounts respect slopes ... it doesn't look like the character does but monsters do? Verify against the
game code please and make it similar to the original as much as possible and make no mistakes." Then a clip
of a Black Tiger running at a fleeing player's back without swinging, and: the Go module still named
OpenSRO ("It's supposed to be TheOpenSRO").

- **Slope tilt (READ, docs/protocol/slope_tilt.md).** The original leans a character only if it IsKindOf
  CICMonster or CICCos (the appear, `FUN_009d17e0`): characterdata column 80 gives the factors (pair 0 =
  bytes 3 and 2 / 100), the normal is the cell's under the character (terrain: the tile triangle's face
  normal, flat on a solid plane at its height; an object: its cell's face normal, never flipped; a
  dungeon: up), eased over 0.3 s from every position or heading change, the factors over 0.1 s from 0,
  and the matrix (`FUN_009c9400`) scales forward's height by factor 0 and side's by factor 1. Players,
  NPCs and guards are never tilted (their `+0x74c` stays 0). A rider is set on its mount's saddle after
  the tilt (`FUN_009d05d0`): it leans with the mount; a monster seated on its own ride does not lean;
  a dummy ride copies its rider; the die model keeps the matrix (0xa59cc0). MEASURED: 0x64146414
  (1.0 forward, 0.2 sideways) on every horse, tiger, pet and transport; 0x14141414 on 6,403 monsters;
  0 (never) on 621.
  - Built: `SlopeTilt`, `NavGraph.ground_normal_at`, `NvmCollision.terrain_normal`,
    `NpcTableReader.parse_slope_tilt`, `SlopeTiltBody` (a move or a turn files the body as hot, the
    original's events), World3D's `_step_slope_tilts` over the hot bodies only (ridden mounts in
    `_cos_place_riders`, before the rider is seated); MonsterRide's dummy ride takes the rider's
    current transform. The model node under the body leans about the feet; the body keeps its yaw.
    OURS: no tracked cell, so the surface nearest the body's height.
  - Tests: `world/slope_tilt_test.gd` (37 checks: the bytes, pitch atan(k tan a), roll, the eases,
    the mirror, the triangle split, the plane, object winding, dungeon, the body's move and turn events). NEGATIVE: against v0.1.574
    SlopeTilt does not exist.
  - Live (render box, real server, `OPENSRO_QA_SLOPE`): the client's normals equal a Go computation
    from the heightmap at three points (38.9, 0.0, 0.4 deg); a ridden pegasus leaned 11.43 deg up an
    11.4 deg slope and 5.04 deg across a 12.9 deg one, 38.7 on 38.9 facing up it; black tigers 9.25 on
    9.3; a 0x14141414 monster 1.80 on 8.9 (atan(0.2 tan 8.9) = 1.79).
  - MEASURED, OPEN: 646 of the export's 78,483 object cells (28 meshes, 12 wound downward on every cell,
    placed in field regions) face down; the original would turn a body standing on one over, and so
    do we. Whether anything stands there in the original is not known.
  - Perf gate (`--base c323ad10 --sites jangan,crowd --frames 60000`, median of 3): the first build,
    which looked at every tilting body every frame, was SLOWER at the crowd view (2,500 monsters):
    3.02 -> 17.03 ms a frame. Made event-driven (SlopeTiltBody, the hot set), it is SAME everywhere:

    | site | frame ms | entry ms | freeze ms | hitches |
    |---|---|---|---|---|
    | jangan | 0.86 -> 0.86 | 8638 -> 8572 | 2752 -> 2713 | 4 -> 4 |
    | crowd | 3.09 -> 3.18 | 12040 -> 11361 | 3297 -> 3493 | 5 -> 5 |

  - QA note: a GM `/spawn` in or beside Jangan is sent away again within a second (the town rule,
    round 674): use `/goto mangyang`.
- **The chase (READ).** The original tests reach every frame (`Tick_UseSkill` phase 1 `0x4ae590` ->
  `Action_IsTargetWithinReach` `0x4ad4a0`) at the target's current place; ours once a 100 ms pass after
  the step, so a chaser that met its leg's end mid-step stood while the runner ran on and never swung.
  `reachedDuringStep` swings when the step's closest approach was in reach (monster_ai.md, round 813).
  INFERRED from the read rules: the clip's 75-speed tiger behind a straight 50-speed runner settles about
  32.7 away against reach 30 and never swings in the original either; a faster chaser now does (it never
  did). OPEN against the original running.
- **The module.** `server/go.mod` is `github.com/TheOpenSRO/OpenSRO/server` (the repo moved 2026-10-13);
  the local `opensro` remote is gone.

The user (2026-10-22), on v0.1.572: "Let's make NPC thieves a toggable feature and let's disable it for now.
Also let's fully implement collision like the original game", then "Also fix the bug where mobs keep attacking
you and they jitter. It's supposed to be stop, 1 attack animated with damage, then chase and attack, rinse and
repeat until they give up following you. Check how the original game does it", with a 5-s video (two White
Tigers at the user's ox, 30 fps: crouched sliding for about a second between pounces).

- **NPC thieves behind `-npc-thieves` (OURS, off by default).** A trader's caravan keeps its clock; its wave
  logs `caravan: wave skipped` and spawns nothing. NPC hunters unchanged. Prod deployed (boot log
  `npc_thieves=false`). `TestRound804CaravanWave` checks both.
- **The swing holds the monster (READ).** `Handler_0e8` (0x5472a0) posts a 0x7070 skill command (0x5411a0),
  and the command's phase 3 stands for CastingTime + ActionDuration (PreparingTime folded in by the server's
  table load; `auto_command.md`). `combat.MonsterSkill.ActionMs` (skilldata cols 7-9: Mangyang 2400, White
  Tiger 1500, MEASURED), `brain.actionUntil`: BATTLE neither chases nor swings until it ends. Before, a target
  out of reach was chased the next tick, mid-swing.
- **The chase's re-aim (READ 0x4b0490):** at most every 100 ms; standing, or the walk 0.2618 rad or more off
  the line -> a new leg (`ChaseOffLine`). Round 554's own 1-unit rule (`ChaseReaimDistance`) re-legged every
  tick behind a moving target.
- **The back-off (READ 0x4b0653..0x4b07d9):** closer than the two radii less 4 with the stop beyond them, the
  follower walks the two radii straight back (`BackOff`). MEASURED live: two tigers `/spawn`ed 6 units from
  the player backed off to 22, then swung every 1.5 s with no other leg.
- **What the user's video is (INFERRED).** Our client moves a monster only by the server's legs (it turns it
  to face, `_play_monster_swing`), so the sliding was server legs: prod ran round 554's re-aim and no swing
  hold. A standing, mounted player in a box repro (`/goto mangyang; /spawn white tiger 2`, a horse) drew no
  legs at all on the old server, so the exact trigger in the user's fight is not reproduced (OPEN); the
  three READ rules above remove both ways a fight produced them.
- **Server collision (the user: "go ahead").** READ (docs/protocol/opcodes/movement.md): the original
  server steps every mover on its own navigation mesh and stops it at a blocking edge. OpenSRO's server
  had no geometry. Built:
  - `server/internal/navmesh`: the `.nvm` reader, the `.bms` collision section, and a port of the
    client's `NavGraph` field walk (`place`, `build`, `surface_at`, `landing_height_at`, `step_tracked`
    with the in-object cell walk and the no-slide terrain stop). Parity MEASURED: the client's own
    `walk_probe --sweep=200` on 97/168 and 98/168 (300 one-unit steps each, sliding) replayed in Go --
    395 of 400 end within 0.05 on the same footing with the same wall count; the five others are long
    wall slides drifting by float precision (Godot's 32-bit Vector2). Heights agree (`--column`).
  - `World.Walk`: world frame -> region-local (worldmap.FromWorld; a world +Z is a local -Z), a unit
    at a time with the footing carried, settled on each region crossing (`WalkStep`, OURS: MEASURED,
    one 69.5-unit segment over cj_luxury stopped at 56.1 where one-unit steps walk on -- the client
    steps a frame at a time). A 150-unit walk about 60 us.
  - `cmd/export-navmesh` (6,279 `.nvm`, 773 MB, 2,044 of 3,307 objects with a mesh, a second);
    `-navmesh-dir`; `cmd/navprobe`.
  - Monsters: every leg ends at the first wall (`startLeg`, `navClipLeg`); the wander's 30-unit probe
    reverses from a wall (READ 0xb45e58 / 0xb45e68, `ai.PickWanderLeg`). Live: a field leg stopped
    at a wall (`stops at a wall`).
  - Players: a 0x7021 leg ends at the wall (`world.MoveOrder.Wall`), its arrival a 0xB023 to the
    window (`AdvanceMovers` `Ended`). `OPENSRO_MOVE_TRACE=1` logs legs, claims and wall arrivals.

The user (2026-10-22), on v0.1.571: "Also player names should be in a box likes mobs, bigger, and seem like they

### The plates

- **Every character's plate is the monsters' (READ).** The name setter every CICharactor shares (slot 29,
  FUN_009cbb90) and the title setter (slot 30, FUN_009c28a0) render through FUN_008b3bd0: font 0 and the box
  colour 0x40000000 (+0xc); the text draw FUN_008b48b0 fills the item's rect + 1 px with it (texture factor,
  SRCALPHA / INVSRCALPHA) before the glyphs, and FUN_008b4d90 centres the item on its point. So players, NPCs
  and COS have the box the monsters had since round 673, at FontIndex 0's 12 px drawn 1:1 -- ours drew them
  with NAME_PLATE_PIXEL_SIZE 0.0004, a few pixels tall, outlined. MEASURED in the user's picture (upscaled 2x):
  the name's cap 9 rows, 1-px stems, no shadow -- the monsters' 12 px face. `_retail_plate_look`; the box's
  geometry is `NamePlates.box_rect` (round 673's MEASURED pad, height and raise), its alpha now the READ
  64/255 (round 673 measured 0.29). NamePlateBatch draws it for other players (one quad of a white texel a
  plate, its own material one priority under the text).
- **A player's name is white (READ, c:0x9cfd50 `FUN_009c1920(0xffffffff)`)**; the pale NAME_PLATE_COLOUR was
  ours and stays only on NPCs (their colour is not traced, OPEN).
- **Title and name are centred together (READ, FUN_009d0a80 c:0x9d0c1d..0x9d0d2b; 0xde24f8 = -0.5, 0xe1b7d0 =
  0.5 read out of the PE).** The title from point - (title w + name w + 2) / 2, the name 2 px after it, after
  the title's trailing L" " (0xe19330, appended by the title setter). Round 805 centred the name alone and hung
  the title left, which put the whole plate left of the rider: the "is the mount the centre" the user saw. The
  point is the rider's own position (+0x90..+0x98), which is the mount's while riding. One box runs under both
  (the original's two boxes touch: 2 px apart, 1 px each).
- **The title is bold with a shadow (READ: style flags 3, FUN_008b4400(5, 3); bit 0 draws each glyph at +1, +1
  in black first, FUN_008b2290; bit 1 selects the font's style 2 in FUN_008b39e0, INFERRED the weight-600
  face, MEASURED 2-px stems and a dark pixel right and below in the picture).** OURS: FontOversampling.bold at
  1.4 and 1 px of glyph spacing (the picture's "Amateur Trader" is 98 px, 87 emboldened alone); the shadow is

- **Sitting (READ; `motion.md`, "Round 808").** Retail's world click `0x78f8d0` tests the sit bit before
  its pick and only sends `0x704f [04]`; the basic attack `0x791d40` does the same after its target
  lookup; the move gate `0x9eb140` never lets a `0x7021` out seated. Ours walked off at once with no clip

## Eight-hundred-and-seventh round: the effects' range, fog and walls

The user (2026-10-21), after round 806: "They basically pop out of view too early and it's a jarring
effect. Let's make the effects visible a little past the fog but hide it behind the fog ... all of those
lighting effects show through walls and other objects while they shouldn't. They seem go away after a bit
though when behind something. Also if the fog is disabled have the effects render out as far as the
landscape lets you"; then "Some of these effects including animated waterfalls can be seen even when
behind the fog". All three depart from the original on purpose (OURS); `docs/protocol/night_lights.md`
"Range, fog and walls (round 807, OURS)" has the detail.

- **Why they popped (READ, round 786).** A lists[2] object's effects play within 480 units and the 3 x 3
  sectors around the camera -- the lamps and burners are lists[2] -- a lists[1] object's within the
  object range (view distance - 480 = 2020 by default). The fog starts at 784 (Hotan) .. 1897 (Jangan's
  .759) and ends at 2500, so a lamp vanished well short of it, and a lists[1] effect at 1500..2020 drew
  unfogged (the original's particles turn FOGENABLE off) over half-fogged surroundings -- the waterfalls.
- **Range.** `WorldAmbientFx.fx_reach` (set by `World3D._apply_fx_reach` with the fog and the far plane):
  a host plays while its view depth less its radius is below the fog's end + 100 (`FOG_MARGIN`), or
  below the far plane with "Fog (temporary)" off; the READ rules stand when it is 0 (tests).
- **Fog.** Every effect fades by the world's fog (`WorldFog.SHADER_FN`'s planes or the dungeon's EXP fog):
  Godot's effect shaders scale the source alpha; `EfpDisplayPass` fades each draw at its vertices toward
  the source its blend pair leaves the screen unchanged with (`fog_fade_mode`), from a 32-byte uniform
  buffer of `WorldFog.last_params` / `last_height`.
- **Walls.** The original's glow draws with ZENABLE off and asks one occlusion query every 500 ms, then
  fades 1.5 alpha a ms: up to ~670 ms through a wall. The same point (`query_point`) is now tested
  against the scene's depth every frame on the GPU (`EfpEffect.glow_anchor`, the glow twin's
  `GLOW_TEST_*`; `EfpDisplayPass`'s push constants grow 80 -> 112 bytes with the anchor and the fade
  mode); a glow whose point is covered is not drawn. The ray and the fade still set the alpha.
- **Tests.** `water_fx_test` (the depth rule: a lamp at depth 2550 in, 2650 out, one 3354 away at depth
  1500 in, the radius, behind the camera), `efp_draw_order_test` (the 112-byte push constants, the fade
  modes, both shaders' fog and glow test), `ambient_particles_test` (the pass hands the glow its point).
- **QA (render box, offline, clock 21:00, 960x540, frame 580; `/var/tmp/r807/qa807.sh`).**
  - Jangan from 2,000 units up (97/167 (1455, 1010), yaw 0, pitch -24): 50 hosts in range, 115
    effects built, 69 stepping (v0.1.565: 5, 28, 9); the far lanterns show as dim glows in the fog.
    `OPENSRO_QA_FX_FOG=off` against on, same frame: 961 pixels the fog dims (the brightest
    233,235,184 -> 152,153,143, the fogged ground around it), 42 brighter.
  - Through walls (yaw 0, pitch -28, 900 up; `OPENSRO_QA_GLOW=noquery`, every glow taken as just
    turned to): the GPU test removes 11,004 pixels of glow drawn through roofs and canopies (8,763
    under Compatibility); the lanterns in plain view still glow. The same view from outside the town
    wall: 115 effects built behind it, nothing through it.
