## Eight-hundred-and-sixth round: the night lights

The user (2026-10-21): "Could you add effects and lights that only turn [on] during the night? Find all
the effects this applies to and what exact times they trigger." Round 786 had left this OPEN (the night
flag's two readers). `docs/protocol/night_lights.md` has every address, the times and the full census.

- **The night flag and its exact times (READ).** `SWorld::vslot_004` (0xa2cf60), every world frame with
  no dungeon or zone test before it, shifts the day phase by a quarter (phase + 0.75 below 0.25, else -
  0.25; the float stored at +0x26a7) and sets the effect manager's +0x1a8 (0x1112fb0) to `0.5 <
  shifted` (0xa2d17c..0xa2d1c6, thunk 0xbbdbf0 -> 0xbc0fe0). Night is a phase below 0.25 or above
  0.75: **clock 20:00:01 to 03:59:59**, day from 04:00:00 through 20:00:00 (MEASURED over every second
  of a day with the clock's own float arithmetic, `game_clock_test.gd`; it agrees with the sound's flag
  at every second). In real time from the server's start: night 0:00-4:48.000 and 24:00.020-28:48 of
  every 28 min 48 s cycle. The title's fixed hours: 5 and 23 o'clock are night, 14 and 18 day.
- **Night-only particles (READ).** `CRTModParticle::FUN_00c81450` tests the entry's byte +0x51 bit 0
  (its copy +0x91, 0xc81493) and returns by day before placing, stepping or drawing; it creates the
  effect at the first night frame (0xc814aa) and steps it by the frame's own time, so a held effect
  freezes and resumes; the glow pass skips it by day (0xc431f7, 0xc43586).
- **Night-lit layers (READ).** Every `CObjRendererVS` draw path (0xbf0fa0, 0xbf144b, 0xbf1a2b,
  0xbf2c03, 0xbf40ad) picks light mode 2 for a layer whose flag word has 0x8 at night; the shader key
  (`FUN_00bf05e0`) makes that `NOLIGHT` (defines at 0xbf6bb4..0xbf6c0e: DIRECT, PLIGHT, NOLIGHT) and
  fog `NO`; `vss0.c` / `vss2.c` (extracted on the box): `mov oD0, c[VSC_UTIL].x` = 1.0. `FUN_00c42a60`
  adds stage 0 MODULATE (0xc42aef). So at night the layer is its own texture, unlit. **Fog: unchanged**
  -- the field draws with table fog (0xa276fa..0xa27714: region id bit 15 clear -> FOGVERTEXMODE NONE,
  FOGTABLEMODE LINEAR), which ignores oFog. (A stencil exemption from WorldFog's pass was probed --
  it works in both renderers, and a transparent surface over a lamp keeps its mark -- and dropped once
  the table fog was read: nothing to exempt.)
- **Census (MEASURED, `client/tools/night_census.gd`, `mapobjcensus -dumpplaces`).** 304 models: 385
  night-only entries (all in `ambient` sets), 359 night-lit meshes (flag words 0x148 / 0x149 / 0x348 /
  0x349). 185 are placed in the field, 1,557 times: Constantinople 380 (the street lights), Baghdad 348
  (the houses' windows), the regions refregion calls ARABIA_DUNGEON 265, Jangan 121 (the palace and
  field lanterns, the adult district's windows and lanterns), Alexandria 107 (windows; the lighthouse
  beam `alex_paros`), the Jangan fortress 79, ... Dungeons: Qin-Shi tomb floors 3 and 6 (the crystals)
  and the four demon dungeons. Unplaced: the event sets, and the gold on the ground
  (`drop_ch_money_*`), `yeoha_muhan` (a monster), `t_horse2_2011` (a transport).
- **What changed (client).** `GameClock.is_night_phase`; `World3D._night_tick` every frame (before the
  title return), `EfpEffect.set_night` + the shader global `srr_night`, a log line on each change.

## Eight-hundred-and-third round: the COS status slots of a session that ended

The user (2026-10-20, on v0.1.560, with a screenshot): "The pet icons at the top right by the minimap are
stuck there even though none are spawned and I tried reconnecting and they're still there. It seemed to
happen after the server restart." Released on its own.

- **MEASURED (prod).** The server held no summoned COS for the character: `char_cos` had no row owned by
  it, and its pets' rows were stored (state 1, not summoned). Nothing on the server named the three COS.
- **Cause (client).** `NetClient.cos_own` -- every 0x30C8 told this client, kept so a world scene that
  comes up after the message still learns its COS -- was never cleared. A server restart (or any lost
  connection) sends no 0x30C9 removal, so the next entry's world scene re-added every COS of the old
  session as a status slot (`_hud_cos_setup`: "This character's COS told before this world came up").
- **Fix.** The cache is emptied when the client disconnects and at every world entry request
  (`_forget_session_lists`); the entry's own COS arrive with their 0x30C8 after it.
- **Tests.** Client compile check, hud_cos and cos_net suites. Client-only: the server is not restarted.

## Seven-hundred-and-ninety-eighth round: a walking rider's mount walks

The user (2026-10-20, on v0.1.558): "when you walk instead of run with them they might have a different
animation. Example in the original game pegasus will fly a little while running but will not when
walking. Ours has pegasus flying even while walking". Released on its own, at the user's request.

- **READ.** Retail puts a rider's Walk/Run on the mount: 0x30BF kind 1 (`FUN_008a80a0` case 1) resolves
  the object through `FUN_009cec60`, the mount while the body rides (`FUN_009ce930`, +0x2ac), and
  `GlobalDataManager::FUN_009ca430` sets its run flag +0x25d and speed index +0x678 (0 walk, 1 run),
  restarting its moving state. The mount then moves at its walk speed (+0x66c) with its walk clip.
- **Ours.** `_cos_place_riders` played TYPE_RUN whenever the rider moved. It now plays TYPE_WALK while
  the rider is in Walk (`_rider_walking`: `_walk_mode`, or `_other_walking` for another player), falling
  back to the run clip for a model with none (`_cos_mount_gait`). A walking rider's legs also moved at
  the rider's own foot walk speed (16); they take the mount's WalkSpeed now (`_gait_speed`,
  `_other_speed`, `_rider_walk_speed`), as the server already did (motion.go). INFERRED: one who mounts
  while walking keeps walking (the server's speed agrees).
- **MEASURED** (box, a level-30 GM, the pegasus scroll 22933, click moves; `OPENSRO_QA_COS` gained
  `walkrun`, the state line the mount's clip): running `c_pegasus_run` at 150/s; after Walk
  `c_pegasus_walk` at 45/s (379 -> 469 in 2.0 s); Run again `c_pegasus_run`.
- **Tests.** UI/animation only (the mount's clip and speed): no perf gate.

## Seven-hundred-and-ninety-seventh round: the pet's name in brackets, and the owner line's gap

The user (2026-10-19, on v0.1.557, with screenshots): "The names are still colliding" (ours: "deadass3"
over "Jeremy" and over "Blood Dinosaur"), "it does look like pet names have the "< >" even in iSRO"
(an iSRO picture: "Noyze" over "< Wolfinho >"), and a 2010 one: "< sylph >" -- "they're in a job suit
which hides the pet name".

- **The brackets (READ; round 796 was wrong).** `GlobalDataManager::FUN_009cbb90`, vtable slot 29 (the
  name setter every CICharactor shares), builds a CICCos's plate text as L"< " (0xde2480) + name +
  L" >" (0xde2478) when it has a name; the COS's slot 27 (0x9d17e0) calls it with the plate flag 1 at
  0x9d1a01 as it spawns. Round 796 searched the client for a "<%s>" format string, found none and
  told the user vSRO had no brackets. `CosSpawnNet.plate_text`.
- **No name (READ).** `CICCos::vslot_034`: with no name, an owner in no job (job byte 4) shows "No name"
  (UIIT_STT_COSNEWUI_TITLE) and any other the ref's own name -- the job suit's "< sylph >". Ours tried the
  ref name first.
- **The gap (ours).** Round 796 converted the 20 screen pixels through FontOversampling only; a COS plate
  is sized by NAME_PLATE_PIXEL_SIZE, not the monsters' screen-exact size, so at the user's 1262-row window
  the gap came out about 7 screen pixels. `_cos_owner_offset` now divides the screen pixel
  (`_monster_plate_pixel_size()`) by the plate's own pixel size, and the monsters' re-fit on a window,
  UI-scale or fov change re-fits the owner lines too. MEASURED (a 1280x720 frame): "Kilo" 20 pixels
  over "< No name >".
- **Tests.** cos_net_test (the brackets, the job byte); `tests` "ran 340 suite(s), 0 failing"; `check`
  ALL LOAD. UI-only (plates): no perf gate.

## Seven-hundred-and-ninety-fifth round: pets, horses and the mall's rides

The user (2026-10-19): "Alright, let's get pickup, growth, and ability pets working and added. Be
sure to add them to the test item npc so we can test. Also make sure horses and other item mall
rideables work like tigers, beetles, ostriches, etc". And: "Make sure you match the original code.
Let's prep to the item mall working next."

Labels: READ (sro_client.exe vSRO 1.188, SR_GameServer.exe), MEASURED, INFERRED, OURS.
docs/protocol/pets.md "Round 795" has every address; this entry is the summary.

- **What a COS is (READ).** Every summoned pet, ride, transport and guild soldier is one client
  class, CICCos. Its characterdata row's TypeID4 picks the kind: 1 ride (`COS_C_*`), 2 transport
  (`COS_T_*`), 3 growth and fellow pets, 4 ability (pickup, "silk") pets, 5 guild soldiers. The
  spawn record writes them as kind bytes 0, 1, 3, 2, 4.
- **Summoning (READ).**
  - Growth / fellow (3/2/1/1) and ability (3/2/1/2) items are kept. The item's Data word holds
    the COS record.
  - A ride or transport scroll (3/3/3/2) is used up. Its row is Desc1 + "_" + the largest level
    bracket at or under the owner's level, from Desc2 (col 121, now exported), with 1 and 255
    added.
  - Refusals: level under 5 (0x186c), a pet above the owner (0x18a5), a second pet of the same
    kind (0x18a9), a second ride or riding (0x185c), a transport without a job suit (0x1849),
    a dungeon (0x1879). Using an out pet's item recalls it within 100 (0x1897 past that, 0x1896
    when ridden).
- **Riding (READ).**
  - Mount: standing, within 30, a ride or transport. The rider's record carries ride state 1 and
    the mount's uid after the battle byte (pc_spawn.md row 25a).
  - While mounted the client moves the mount: 0x70C5 {mount, 1, the 0x7021 body}. The server
    drops the rider's own 0x7021 and echoes 0xB021 under the mount's uid. The rider takes the
    mount's speeds (0x30D0), and blows on the rider land on the mount.
  - Dismounting a ride deletes it; the owner's death deletes the ridden COS.
  - The client seats the rider: its skeleton's global = the mount's skeleton global x the
    "saddle" bone's pose, playing the "cart" animation group.
- **Pets (READ unless marked).**
  - Follow from 65 away, to a point selfBC + 4 + rand(1..10) off the owner, settling within
    selfBC + 50.
  - An ability pet picks up client-side: the nearest eligible item within 500, one request a pet.
    Flags 0x80 on, 0x40 everything, 1 gold, 2 equipment, 4 other. The server takes it within 10
    and gives up past 1000. Gold, quest and untradeable items go to the owner, the rest to the
    pet's bag (0x18b4 full; 0x18b5 the owner's bag full). The bag is 28 slots (OURS until the
    extension's rows are read).
  - A growth pet in AI mode 1 attacks what its owner attacks, with its col-83 skill, at half rate
    under 30% HGP.
  - Pet EXP: recomputed at the pet's level; it levels only below its owner and below 110, by
    swapping to the col-6 next-level row (type 7, and 0x3054's effect).
  - Hunger 1% every 5 minutes, regen 1.6% every 4 s, rent checked every 30 s.
  - Naming once (1-12 characters, no space), settings (0x7420 kind 1 AI, kind 2 pickup flags),
    unsummon, terminate, and the pet bag moves (0x7034 0x10 / 0x1a / 0x1b).
  - An out pet's item cannot be sold (0x18b7), traded (0x18b6) or stored (0x18b2).
  - The item record's tail by type: a pet item's state, ref, name and rent seconds; the rest of
    3/3 and 3/2/2 as retail reads them (`cos.ItemTail`; `ItemInstance._read_tail`).
- **OURS departures**: COS uids 0x7e000000+n; a 100 ms server tick; a 5 s corpse; the 400-unit
  warp leash; monsters do not target pets; logout keeps a COS summoned; the use-item option 0xC5
  carries a pet consumable's target; a COS shows and hides with its owner (in the owner's spawn).
- **Built.**
  - Server: package `cos` (rules, a store with an SQL table `char_cos`, the wire); session
    `cosworld`, `cossummon`, `cosride`, `coscommand`, `cosai`, `cosexp`, `cosuse`, `cosbag`,
    `cositem`; `-cos-csv` (`export-refdata -mode cos`, 7,272 rows); the pet bag in
    `cos_inventory`.
  - Client: `CosSpawnNet`, `CosNet` (every request and reply), `CosTable`, the bodies, riders,
    the pick scan and the growth pet's attack in `World3D`; the HUD's status slot, pet mini info,
    COS window, command bar and the pet bag (`hud_cos*.gd`); tooltips for pet items. The pet keys

  - The Test Items NPC's three new lines: "Purchase Growth and Fellow Pets", "Purchase Ability
    Pets and Pet Items", "Purchase Horses, Rides and Transports" (10-21 goods a tab).
- **Measured live** (`/var/tmp/r795/qa1.sh` on the box, `OPENSRO_QA_COS`).
  - The level-30 Fierce Tiger (`COS_C_TIGER_30`, item 23277): summoned, mounted at once, the

  - A wolf cub (item 7488) and a rabbit (item 10365) followed, took the name "Rex" and the

  - The wolf struck a mangyang the owner attacked (32 damage, killed). The rabbit, flags 199,

## Seven-hundred-and-ninety-fourth round: Dynamic Animation -- the cloth, and what a worn item plays

The user (2026-10-19): "Let's add support for dynamic animations now. The option is there but not
used. Let's make sure we account for all things that use dynamic animations like flags, weapons,
armor (all types), etc. Also make sure you deal talisman animations and glows/effect if they have
them." And: "Make sure you're comparing against the original code".

Everything is READ from sro_client.exe or MEASURED across the retail archives;
docs/protocol/CLOTH.md has every address. Five research passes (the data survey; DYVERTEX and the
step; DYJOINT, DYLATTICE and the gate; scenery and rigid cloth; worn items) are summarised there.

- **What the option is (READ).** Case 0xe sets renderer +0x19c (default on). Every compound
  object's update (`c33230`) then runs a per-vertex cloth, `CCompChar::FUN_00c0d010`, on every mesh
  whose `.bms` carries hdr[2] (amount, pinned) and the hdr[3] links. It runs in 50 ms steps, with the
  count capped at 200, at LOD 0.
  - Position Verlet: gravity `g * -5 * (k a + 1)`, a random gust (`rand() % n == 0`) of
    `(p' + 100) * (k2 a + 1) * wind`, the velocity kept, then h^2 = 0.0004.
  - Up to 7 passes of stretch-only links in the file's order, split by the two amounts.
  - The 36-byte tail of hdr[3], never decoded before, is the parameter block.
- **What carries it (MEASURED).**
  - Only DYVERTEX is used: 1,235 `.bsr`, one identical header each. The runtime mod is a stub; the
    mesh's own data decides.
  - 801 cloth meshes: robes, dresses, capes, wings, hair (every China-man body, and the women's and
    Europe's), spear and glaive tassels, plumes, mount trappings, flags, banners, tents and cobwebs.

## Seven-hundred-and-ninety-third round: the select screen's pick box leaves out the weapon

The user (2026-10-18, on v0.1.553, with a screenshot): "That's better but still not quite right. If it
includes the weapon in the hit box it should not. I have to go right of the spear to select Pain
still." And: "It looks like the weapon is used as the boundry on all characters but there is some
layering it seems." In the screenshot the third character holds a spear across her body whose head
reaches over Pain, the fourth.

- **Cause, MEASURED** (`/var/tmp/r791/sel.sh`, now with Charlie holding a spear, item 143, after the
  shield comes off): round 792's posed box took every shown mesh, the weapon and shield too. With the
  default kit's sword and shield every box was 8-10 units wide; a spear reaches past the next
  character, and since the first box hit wins (READ), the "layering" the user saw is that order: the
  character holding the weapon takes the click.
- **Fix, OURS (the user's call):** `CharSelectStage.posed_box` leaves out the nodes of the weapon and
  shield worn entries (`_held_nodes`, slots 6 and 7). **OPEN:** whether retail does: `FUN_00c2b2d0`
  walks every part in the `+0x94` map and a weapon is a part (`vslot_067`), so retail's box may take it
  in; not settled.
- **After, MEASURED** at 1280x720: every box 5.9-6.0 units wide (Bravo's dress 8.4); x 252..394,
  469..579, 678..829, 874..1014 (were 182..417, 428..605, 664..848, 852..1081). Charlie's full model
  box is 21 units deep with the spear, her pick box 5.9 wide; a click on each body picks it.
- **Test:** `charselect_test.gd` `_posed_pick_box`: a 30-unit spear under the skeleton is left out
  when skipped and widens the box when not.
- **QA:** `OPENSRO_QA_EQUIP_BAG` takes `<tick>:<slot>=0` to take a slot off (the shield, before a
  two-handed weapon goes on).

### Corrections to what the project believed

- **Storing `.ddj` in a converted pack is not a 10x read win.** At the merge the coordinator first
  credited deflated textures with a tenfold slowdown; re-measured (20,000 native reads of Data):
  deflated 2,636 ms, stored 2,076 ms, `Data.pk2` 241 ms. Storing buys ~21 % for 0.63 GB more
  (2.59 vs 1.96 GB); most of the gap to `.pk2` is the inflate of meshes and tables. The plan's
  choice (store) was kept; `-deflate .ddj` gives the smaller pack.
- **Two dress rows do not hide the helm**, though the research said so: charactervisualchange
  says they don't, and the client follows the table (lane AC).
- **Whether the default wear shows under an avatar** was OPEN (lane X); charactervisualchange hides
  it, and the client follows the table (lane AC, frames `/var/tmp/ac789/xcmp_*.png`).

### The coordinator's merge fixes

- **`custom/` sits beside the archive folder for the Go tools too** (lane G had
  `<archives>/custom`), so both sides find the same folder (the client's since round 678).
- **A symbolic-link entry in a pack is refused by the Go reader** as the client already did
  (`assetfs.TestSymlinkEntryRefused`).
- **Stored extensions** (`assetfs.StoredExtensions`) match between the converter and the docs:
  `.ddj` and the already-compressed types.
- **Conflicts** in `orphans_test.go`, `server/README.md`, `docs/TODO.md`, `asset_packs.md`: kept
  both sides (lane K's rules text, lane X's index-file item).

### Lane E's fixes (found live)

- **The grant window's rows were invisible**: its five bars were built after the list and covered
  it, clicks too (`GrantMagicAttributeWindow.raise_list`; rows over bars INFERRED).
- **The selected grant row never lit**: the select bar texture was placed under the bar's opaque
  pieces; it now replaces them (`apply_bar`).
- **NPCs vanished after a same-zone teleport** (GM `/tp`): the old nodes, queued for deletion, still
  counted as placed, so "0/3 NPC(s) placed" and the server never resent them
  (`World3D.npc_holder_standing`, `npc_rezone_test.gd`).

## Seven-hundred-and-eighty-sixth round

### Round 786 (part): Waterfall sparkles and glow match the original

**The report.** The user (v0.1.547) said "the splash effects are there but they don't seem quite
right". Two pairs of pictures, ours against the original:
- **The north Hotan palace waterfall.** In the original, blue-white glints cover the falling sheet,
  under a soft bright haze beneath the arch, and the sheet is a translucent grey. Ours was a white
  sheet with almost no glints.
- **The Jangan golden dragon.** In the original a bright white splash with glints sits where the
  streams land in the pool. Ours was faint.

The coordinator's review of a first fix asked for the proper one: blend the effects in display
values exactly, as Compatibility and Direct3D 9 do, measured on four sites. Branch
`feat/sparkle787`. Labels: READ (sro_client.exe, address given; the box's
`/var/tmp/decomp_client`), MEASURED, INFERRED, OURS, OPEN.

**The objects (MEASURED; `water_census.gd`, `dump_bsr_particles.gd`, `efpcensus -show`).**
- **Hotan (93/134, 93/135):** `oa_ho_waterfall01` and `cj_waterfall02`.
  - Their effects are `map\multugu-b`, `pokpomulbangul(-m)` and `pajang-b`.
  - The glints are `pokpomulbangul`'s additive node on `s-light-sb.ddj`: blue RGB, with the dots in
    its alpha.
  - The haze is the white `smoke.ddj` plates, which mix.
  - The sheets are MTRL mods: SRCALPHA/INVSRCALPHA, ZWRITE off, MODULATE2X.
- **Jangan (97/168):** `cj_wf_dr`.
  - Four `map\multigi.efp` sit at the foot of the streams. Each has a mixing smoke node and an
    additive `01sparkles.ddj` node.
  - The streams are SRCALPHA/ONE, and they land in the map water.
- **Alexandria:** the aqueduct falls (`dun_waterfall_big01` / `small01`, `dun\dun_waterfall_b1.efp`,
  which has an `01sparkles` cloud and an `oura_14` halo). These were the user's first guess.

**Ruled out (MEASURED, `OPENSRO_QA_WORLD_FX_DETAIL=1`):**
- **Every effect was built, in range, shown and stepping,** at 60-120 particles each. That rules
  out the range rules, the 9 sectors, the warm-up, the cull box and the particle cap.
- **The textures** (`01sparkles`, `oura_14`, `smoke`, `s-light-sb`) are DXT3 with no mip chain, in
  retail and here.

**Where an effect draws (READ; EFP_FORMAT.md, "Where an effect draws in the frame").**
- **A placed object's effects** draw right after its own meshes, blended ones included, unsorted:
  `CObjRendererVS::vslot_038` 0xbf5830, then `CRTModParticle::vslot_003`.
- **A character's decorations** draw after its body (`FUN_009d20d0`).
- **The map water** draws before every above-water object (`Map::FUN_00a24e30`).
- **Depth:** effects are depth-tested, with no depth write (`EFEffect::FUN_00cabda0`).

Every effect material now draws at `EfpEffect.RENDER_PRIORITY` = 1, after object surfaces (0), the
water (-3) and the fog pass (-1). This alone moved the boxes by at most 0.2 (MEASURED).

**The cause (MEASURED): blending in linear space.** Direct3D 9 blends in the values the screen
shows, in an 8-bit back buffer. Forward+ blends in a linear float buffer.
- **The effects.** Rounds 722 and 774 gave each effect node a twin that blends against Godot's
  screen copy, and that copy is taken before the transparent pass. Over a waterfall sheet or the
  pool the twin blended against the rock or the pool floor, and the effects' share came out a
  tenth of Compatibility's at Hotan and half at Jangan.
- **The sheets themselves.** A mixing MTRL sheet blends linearly in Forward+. The Hotan sheet's box
  mean was 167 against Compatibility's 126, while the rock beside it was 50 against 52. That is
  the white sheet: the original's is grey and translucent, as Compatibility's is.

**The fix.**
- **`EfpDisplayPass`** (new), a CompositorEffect after the transparent pass, on the world camera.
  EFP_FORMAT.md, "Display-value blending under Forward+", has the details.
  - The colour under the effects goes into an 8-bit display-value buffer.
  - Every effect plate and mesh is drawn into it with its own Direct3D SRCBLEND/DESTBLEND, its
    stage ops and a depth test, then turned back.
  - The objects' ambient effects (world, gates, dungeons) use it. Link nodes keep their twins.
  - Skills and equipment are unchanged.
- **The MTRL sheets:** a mixing or adding MTRL pass with no depth write gets a display-value tail
  (`ObjectLoader.display_blend`).
- **The first fix's exception is dropped.** The per-object rule that switched a sheet's effects to
  Godot's blend (`COVER_META`, `WorldAmbientFx.covers`) is gone.

**MEASURED against Compatibility** (`/var/tmp/sparkle/c1/<site>_<config>`, `lum.py`; the effects'
share, frames 60-99, against each side's own effects-off run):

| site | before | after | Compatibility |
|---|---|---|---|
| Hotan palace waterfall | +0.25 | +2.3, +2.7 (two runs) | +2.3 |
| Jangan dragon | +1.4 | +2.5, +2.4 | +2.7 |
| Alexandria library fountain | +4.9 | +4.2, +4.0 | +5.1 |
| Qin-Shi tomb lv.1 hall | +1.0 | +1.3 | +1.5 |

- **Compatibility tone-maps the effects' own colour.** With no post-process, its scene shader
  applies the filmic curve, which lifts mid values; Direct3D has no tone map. With the tone map
  linear on both sides (`|tonemap=0`), the Alexandria shares agree (+4.4 against +4.6).
- **The Hotan sheet box (effects off):**

  | | filmic | linear tone map |
  |---|---|---|
  | before | 167 | |
  | after | 115 | 104 |
  | Compatibility | 126 | 115 |

  The remaining -11 is overlapping blended passes (the sheet's pieces, and its back-then-front
  passes), each blended against the opaque scene (OURS, OPEN).

**Census (MEASURED).**
- **The pass:** the world's ambient sets name 170 placed effect files, 122 with an additive drawn
  node, and every one of them goes through it. Only `map\guild\light_gate_blue.efp` (3 nodes) has
  a mesh node with Direct3D culling, and its front face is INFERRED.
- **The MTRL tail:** every mixing or adding MTRL mod with ZWRITE off. 69 placed models carry
  ambient effects and a live MTRL mod; the tail is not counted per model.

**OPEN.**
- **Order.** Effects draw after every transparent surface, characters' blended meshes included. The
  original orders a placed object's effects before a later-queued object's blended meshes.
- **Water depth.** The original's plain water writes depth (READ, 0xa22c39); ours does not.
- **Overlapping MTRL passes,** the -11 above.
- **A sheet over the water** blends against the opaque scene, not the water.
- **Mesh culling** in the pass: front faces INFERRED; one world file, untested.

**Perf gate** (`perf_gate.sh --base 4093492d --head 76a56e98 --sites jangan,crowd,hotan,alex --frames 40000`,
1280x720, Forward+, median of 3, native readers off): every number SAME.

| site | frame ms | entry ms | freeze ms | hitches |

### Round 786 (part): Monsters appear on time, and attacks register promptly

The user (2026-10-13, playing deadass3, level 140, in the bandit fields and Jangan): "the mobs
appear to pop up way later than they should and sometimes my attacks take awhile to register."
Everything read and measured is in `docs/protocol/spawn_attack_latency.md`; the short form:

**The server is not where the time goes (MEASURED, READ).**
- **The view window is retail's.** Re-read in `SR_GameServer.exe`: the block division
  (`CRgnTerrain::vslot_006` 0x53ad30, **320.0** at 0xb45ae8, 1920.0 at 0xb45ad0), the 8
  neighbours (table 0xc64090) and `CMsgBlock` slot 2's loop over them (0x534340: 0x5343b8..0x534419,
  `FUN_00533e70` / `FUN_00533f70`). A player holds the 3 x 3 blocks of 320 around its own, so a
  monster first shows 320-640 units ahead -- in retail too. `sro_client.exe` holds nothing back
  and drops nothing by distance (0x3015 -> `FUN_008a6bd0` at once, round 676; removal only by
  0x3016 or the world reset; the draw's 800.0 at 0xd83080 is a mesh LOD), and fades every spawn in
  over 2.0 s (0xd86ecc). **The distance was never the bug.**
- **Enter timing** (`partybot -mode latency -walk 30s`, this tree's server with the Mac mini's
  flags and data, 67,266 monsters, a bot running 105 units/s through the bandit fields): 25-40
  enters a run, 320-621 units ahead (p50 420-483), **27-96 ms** after the bot's block crossing
  (p50 47-71): one area-of-interest tick (100 ms, OURS; retail answers in the move).
- **The AI tick** at 67k monsters, sleep on: p50 0.007-0.08 ms, max under 0.3 ms. OpAttack
  request->result on the server alone: under 1 ms (partybot, 40 attacks, 67k monsters, one player
  online as on prod); with 300 more bots moving around it (`-crowd 300`): p50 0.8 ms, max 1.1 ms
  (27 attacks), enters p50 70 ms after the crossing, the AI tick p50 0.13-0.17 ms, max 0.65 ms.
- **Prod** (Mac mini log, read only): the user's sessions' send queue peaked at 8,363 bytes and the
  send debt at 246 us; one player online, no swarm since 2026-10-12. The arrival guard held the
  user's arrivals 1.6-3.3 s, each released at the client's 0x3012 (the loading screen), as round
  786's protection meant.

**The client was (MEASURED, render box; the full-map server above on loopback, the QA client
in real time, Forward+ 1280x720, `OPENSRO_QA_LATENCY=1`).**
1. **Every pushed monster body cost 21-25 ms**, nearly all of it waiting for the render thread:
   `duplicate()` reads a `GeometryInstance3D`'s property list, which asks the rendering server
   (`thread_model=2`) and waits for it to finish drawing the last frame -- 12-25 ms for the first
   `duplicate()` of a frame, 0.3 ms for the next ones (`QA LAT dup`; INFERRED which call: Godot's
   `GeometryInstance3D::_get_property_list`). The name plate's look, the lighting's copy and the
   fade's twins wait the same way when they come first (`QA LAT build` laps).
2. **So a burst of N monsters took N frames**: the network's 8 ms read budget (OURS) counted the
   wait as its own work and read one push a frame. Every packet behind the burst -- an attack's
   result -- waited those frames too.
3. **Nagle's algorithm** was on (`StreamPeerTCP`'s default): the walk into reach ends with the stop
   report (unanswered by the server) and the attack, back to back, and the attack waited for the
   server's delayed ACK -- 40-52 ms a click against the Linux server. On the Mac mini it mostly does
   not: prod's own log has the attack 0-5 ms after the stop report in 607 of 643 cases since
   2026-10-06 (macOS acknowledges at once).
4. Kept, as retail does them: the first monster of a species waits for its model (98-277 ms,
   round 661: a hitch otherwise); a click inside the base attack's re-use delay is answered when
   the delay ends (round 785, READ), 578-1,184 ms in the fight runs right after a kill.

**What changed (OURS, client only).**
- `MonsterDraw.clone_tree`: a body built node by node from its template, resources shared as
  `duplicate()` shared them, no property list read (pinned against `duplicate()` field by field).
- `RenderSync.wait_once`: the frame's one render-thread wait taken up front in the first body
  build and credited to `NetClient`'s read budget and the build pump's, so the rest of a burst is
  read and built in the same frame.
- TCP_NODELAY on the game socket (`NetClient.no_delay_wanted`; `OPENSRO_NAGLE=1` restores
  Nagle). Retail sets none (READ: `sro_client.exe`'s six `setsockopt` calls, IAT 0xd80624, and
  `SR_GameServer.exe`'s three, IAT 0xad942c, are all `SOL_SOCKET` 0xffff) -- but retail sends one
  request per action (0x7074, the server walks the player), OpenSRO's client two.
- QA: `LatencyProbe` (`QA LAT mob|atk|build`), the A/B switches `OPENSRO_QA_DUPLICATE=1`,
  `OPENSRO_QA_NO_RENDER_SYNC=1`, `OPENSRO_NAGLE=1`; the QA fight waits out the arrival's
  protection and takes `OPENSRO_QA_FIGHT=<range>`; `tools/nagle_probe.gd`; `partybot -mode
  latency`; `tools/clone_parity.gd` (`clone_tree` against `duplicate()` on the archive's
  templates).

**Before and after** (one build, A = the A/B switches on = before; B = after; runs
`/var/tmp/latency/run/`: fights in the Mangyang field (-1000, 3000) at level 80 and the bandit
fields at 140, walks east through the bandit fields; `fight_base` is the instrumented tree before
any fix):

| | A (before) | B (after) |
|---|---|---|
| a pushed body, recv -> drawn | p50 22 ms, p95 24 (n = 54 + 599) | p50 1 ms, p95 23 (n = 319): the 23 is the frame's one render wait, now in the first body only |
| the body's instance (template copy) | p50 21.2-22.2 ms, max 25.0 | p50 0.14-0.17 ms, max 0.4 (3.6 once) |
| bursts of 3+ pushed bodies | 21 / 10 / 12 / 8 / 14 bodies over 3 / 13 / 12 / 8 / 14 frames, 98-326 ms first to last (`mfightA1`); 19 / 7 / 8 over 12 / 10 / 8 frames, 207-255 ms (`fightA4`) | 37 of 42 bursts in one frame (1-6 ms), the rest 2-5 frames, max 112 ms (27 bodies) (`mfightB1`) |
| where a monster first shows, from the player | p50 426-508, 4-841 (4: a respawn beside the player) | p50 485-525, 92-840 (the server's window, unchanged) |
| an attack, send -> result (Linux server) | p50 50-51 ms; 114 of 140 between 20 and 60 ms (`fight_base`, `mfightA1`) | p50 2 ms; 71 of 87 under 20 ms (`mfightB1`) |
| an attack, its tail | 13 + 1 over 200 ms: re-use delay deferrals, and results behind a burst | 8 over 200 ms: the re-use delay deferrals (retail's) |
| the bare socket, stop + attack (`nagle_probe.gd`, 200 rounds) | 40.9 ms p50, 199 of 200 over 20 ms | 0.3 ms p50, 0 over 20 ms |

On the user's PC (60 fps, a 23.4 ms frame in his own diag file) a burst of ten monsters stood
in ten such frames before -- about a quarter of a second for the last to start fading in, and an
attack result behind it as long (INFERRED from the box's numbers; not measured there).

**Tests.** GD `scripts/world/monster_spawn786_test.gd` (75+ checks): `clone_tree` against
`duplicate()` on a template shaped as the assembler makes one (bones, poses, pieces, twin, bone
attachment, metas; the skeleton path resolving in a tree), the probe's records, `RenderSync`'s

`cmd/partybot/latency_test.go` (the latency mode's wire reading). Before the round the GD test

**Gates.** `go test ./...` passes. Client `check` ALL LOAD (804 scripts, 9 scenes); `tests` "ran

`GODOT_LOCK=/var/tmp/latency/lock`). Perf gate (`--base f54ea367 --sites jangan,crowd,mobs`):

### Round 786 (part): the Test Items NPC's gear is +12, full blue, 100%

The user: "can you make the Item NPC shop gear all +12 full blue at 100% stats?" (OURS throughout:
retail has no such item; the rules below build the best item the operator's own tables allow.)

- **Where**: the Test Items NPC's free buy (round 783) of an equipment item (TypeID 3/1) now
  creates it with a made instance (`session/testshopgear.go`, `shop.Service.BuyFreeInstance`)
  instead of a fresh roll. The same item bought from any other NPC, or with gold, is ordinary;
  stackables (stones, elixirs, potions) are unchanged.
- **+12**: OptLevel 12.
- **100%**: every one of the twelve 5-bit variance groups at 31 (`durability.GroupMax`), so each
  white stat sits at the top of its range.
- **Full blue** (`magicopt.FullBlue`): every option the item kind's assign row lists that can drop
  (a '+' row, as `RollDrop`'s pool) and whose row allows the item, at the item's degree
  ((ItemClass-1)/3+1; the highest level below it when the degree has no row), at the row's
  highest value (the six-value pool's largest, the range's max, the single value), in the assign
  order, no more than column 158 (MaxMagicOptions). Left out: Immortal, Steady, Lucky and Astral
  (special stones that guard reinforcing, not stats) and MATTR_REPAIR (drop weight 0).
- **Durability**: the max the full variance gives, raised by the item's DUR option
  (`alchemy.MaxDurability`, READ in round 768).
- **MEASURED** over the 94 equipment goods with the Mac mini's tables (degree-11 Seal of Nova):
  4..7 options each, none capped (cap 9). Weapons STR 7, INT 7, DUR 200%, HR 60%, EVADE_BLOCK
  100; armour STR 7, INT 7, DUR 200%, ER 60%, plus HP 1300 / MP 1300 on helm, chest and legs;
  shields STR 7, INT 7, DUR 200%, EVADE_CRITICAL 100; accessories STR 7, INT 7, the five
  resists 20.
- Tests: `magicopt/full_test.go`; `TestTestItemsNPCSelectOpenBuyFree` now also checks the bought
  sword and helm (+12, full variance, STR 7, DUR 160 from its fixture), the plain stone, and a
  paid sword that stays plain.

### Round 786 (part): effects that drift off the body

The user: "Seal and skill effects will float or fly off from that character and they shouldn't.
Please fix and make no mistakes." Their screenshot: a level-140 Chinese character just after
"Teleport to [Jangan] area" (from Donwhang), the ground ring under the feet, pink sparkles on the
ground about 3 m to its left, a pale swirl far off to the upper left, a yellow streak across the
body. Then: every rule changed must come from the binary.

**The cause (MEASURED).** This client builds each zone's grid in that zone's own frame (round 570:
(0, 0, 0) is the zone centre region's middle). A gate teleport from Donwhang's gate point
(teleportdata GATE_WC, 102/153 (957, 1508)) to Jangan's (GATE_CH, 97/168 (969, 1369)) therefore
moved the body by **141.3 units** in Godot (`QA FXDRIFT MOVE`), under EfpEffect's `ANCHOR_JUMP`
(400, OURS since round 621), so the effects took it as one frame of motion: every particle that
does not follow (u6 = 0) stayed where the body had stood, 140 units beside it, and a follower of an
ancestor that died on that frame carried the whole move on every frame after (round 785's frozen
move, READ) -- flying off. The way back (Jangan -> Donwhang, 555 units) was over 400 and carried,
which is why it showed going to Jangan. That the screenshot's ground sparkles are
the left-behind particles and its far swirl a flying orphan is INFERRED from these numbers.

**What the original does (READ, sro_client.exe).**
- A change of the player's region moves every effect whole. `CICPlayer` slot 37 (0x009d5900):
  when the new position's region differs, the map's slot 7 (+0x1c) gives the offset between the
  old region and the new into a vector, slot 1 makes the new one the centre, and every object of
  the object list (DAT_00ec4b84) gets it through its slot 14 (+0x38): `CIObject`'s
  (`GlobalDataManager::FUN_009c4230`) passes it to its renderer (+0x9c -> +4, slot 11,
  `CCompChar::FUN_00c2a980`, each particle mod: `CRTModParticle::FUN_00c81150`), `CICharactor`'s
  (`FUN_009cd390`) also to each skill decoration it holds (+0x288, `CIDecoSkill::vslot_016`
  0x00a4fdb0, each effect of its list). The effect takes it through IEasyFxEffect slot 6
  (`CEFEffect::vslot_006`, 0x00ca9f20): added to its placement (-0x90) and old placement (-0x19c),
  and `CEFEffect::FUN_00c865a0` adds it to every particle's position (+0x1b0) and old position
  (+0xa4), node by node. The flag it tests (+0x48) is set by the effect's update (vslot_000), so
  every running effect moves. Into a dungeon (the new region's bit 0x8000) the offset stays 0.
- Nothing is updated while the loading screen is up (`CPSMission::vslot_012`, 0x0084c300, returns
  while +0xe4 is set; round 785), so the arrival reaches an effect as one placement.
- A placement has no distance test (`CEFEffect::vslot_007` 0x00caa020, `vslot_008` 0x00ca9460):
  a move of any size is motion. Rounds 621-785's `ANCHOR_JUMP` disagreed with the binary.
- Checked, unchanged: a newborn's velocity is its owner's minus its u6 ancestor's and its position
  its owner's (`FUN_00c88490`, round 621's reading holds); effects simulate in world space over
  the effect's scale (round 621).

**The fix.**
- `EfpEffect.shift_effects(effects, by)` (the slot-6 shift: the effect's anchor and last placement
  move, so every particle does) and `placed_under(root)` (the effects placed in the old frame);
  `World3D.zone_frame_shift(old frame, old anchor, new frame, new anchor)`, the offset every cell
  of the grid moves by between two frames (`_group_position` of `_cell_offset`; 102/153 -> 97/168 is
  (-28800, -96.6, -9600) with the two height anchors). `_on_change_zone_result` takes the old
  frame's effects before it places the player and moves them once the new grid is built, field to
  field; into a dungeon nothing (READ); out of one OPEN (nothing moved).
- `EfpEffect.pause_world` holds the effects that place themselves (`_process`) from the zone
  change's start until its arrival is laid out (READ, the loading screen). OURS in scope: EquipFx's
  masters (placed rigidly, at the origin) and a dungeon's ambient effects (static) keep stepping;
  a world torn down mid-load releases the hold.
- `ANCHOR_JUMP` removed: a move of any size is motion (the 60-unit re-centre, invisible, stays).
  So a GM move, `/unstuck` and the other re-placements inside a zone are motion, as in the
  original. `OPENSRO_QA_FX_BEFORE786=1` runs the old rules for a before render (QA only).
- With the shift the arrival is the true move -- about 30,000 units from Donwhang's gate to
  Jangan's -- so what does not follow is left there, out of sight, as in the original.
- OURS: the shift moves the effect's node, so a dead ancestor a particle still follows moves too;
  `FUN_00c865a0` walks only the nodes' live lists.

**The instruments.** `efp_probe.gd --drift` (scenarios `stand`, `jump` -- one frame's move as
motion --, `zone` -- the frames' offset first, `--frame`, then `--jump` --, `walk`, `turn`;
`--equip` adds the 74 equipment glow files; a particle is PAST beyond its still spread + 10 and
NEAR when also within 2,000 units) and, in the live client, `OPENSRO_QA_FXDRIFT` (`FxDriftProbe`:
the player's real auras and seal glaive, sampled every 5 ticks over stand, walk, stop, turn and the
real `_on_change_zone_result` of two gate arrivals; `/var/tmp/r786-fx/drift.sh` on the box).

**MEASURED, the live client** (auras 8150 `lightning_gyeonggong_keep_c`, 8214
`fire_gigongta_keep_e` at Bip01 R Finger2, 8239 `fire_ganggi_keep_e` at Bip01, 8253
`fire_hwabyeok_keep_c`; ITEM_CH_TBLADE_11_C_RARE +9; 640x360 movie run):

| phase | before (rules of 785) | after |
|---|---|---|
| arrival in Jangan (141.3-unit re-placement) | 57 samples, 2,009 particles beside the body, farthest 142.7 (gigongta, still spread 3.7) | 0 in sight; the old ones 30,415.7 away |
| arrival in Donwhang (555 units) | 0 (carried by the old 400 rule) | 0 in sight; the old ones 30,766 away |
| standing after each arrival | 0 | 0 |
| walking / stopping / turning | worst +77.4 / +57.9 / +19.7 | +79.0 / +54.2 / +19.6 (unchanged) |

**MEASURED, the census** (1,433 runs: every skilleffectset file, kept or not, and the 74
equipment files; a 194.4-unit move; 20 frames a second): `jump` -- 440 runs leave particles past
their spread and in sight (290,769 particle-frames), 55 of the 74 equipment files among them;
`zone` -- 10 runs (3,335 particle-frames), no equipment file. 8 of the 10 also pass their spread
standing still (`stand`, 12 runs: effects still growing after the 4 s lead-in); the other two are
monster effects (`skill_jupiter_at05_ground`, `skill_jupiter_authority_crown_amb`, 24 and 33
particle-frames; OPEN). Before the round's code the same `jump` census gave 385 of the 1,359 skill
runs (the equipment files were not in it).

**Not changed, measured.** Walking leaves u6 = 0 trails (`fire_hwabyeok_keep_c`'s ring +77) and a stop lets
orphans run on with the last frame's move (+54): both READ in rounds 621 and 785. Turning at
180 degrees a second, 21 of the 1,433 runs pass their spread (worst
`water_resurrection_effect_a` +117, also one of the growing ones): the bone and follow rules of
rounds 621 and 785, not changed here.

**The yellow streak (INFERRED).** In the render the +9 seal glaive's glow runs along the glaive
held across the body, and EquipFx places its holders at the weapon's bone every frame (MEASURED
round 741: 0.005 off the blade). The user's yellow streak with a pink end is taken to be their

**OPEN:** out of a dungeon, the original's offset (its map slot 7 with a dungeon region) was not
read -- nothing is moved; whether the original rebuilds the player object on a teleport (its
effects would then restart rather than move) was not read -- the position change's rule is the one
followed; the two Jupiter files above; the vertical part of the offset is this client's height

**Pictures** (render box, Forward+ RX 7600, 1280 x 720, the frame after the Jangan arrival):

### Round 786 (part): effects that drift off the body in ordinary play

The user, on v0.1.534 (the part above merged): "it does it all the time". Their picture (16:15:41):
deadass3 standing in an open field, the ground ring under the feet, and a full copy of the large
pale blue/green ring several body heights away, a purple swirl to the right. The prod server's log
for those 20 s: only 0x7021 moves every 250-500 ms (click-walking) and a few buff casts -- no zone
change. Asked: re-derive what keeps a particle on its body from sro_client.exe, measure ordinary
play, fix it.

**Ordinary play, MEASURED** (`OPENSRO_QA_FXDRIFT`, the live client, auras 8150 / 8214 / 8239 /
8253 and the +9 seal glaive, a click every 500 ms in a zigzag, 60 frames and 60 ticks a second;
farthest drawn particle past its effect's still spread, and why):

| phase | worst | what |
|---|---|---|
| standing, recasting the four buffs | 0 | -- |
| walking 50 a second | +164 | `fire_gigongta_keep_e` #13 (smoke, followed holder dead), `lightning_gyeonggong_keep_c` #12 (the wind ring, same) |
| stopped | +78 | the wind ring's orphans; `fire_hwabyeok_keep_c`'s sparks (nodes with u6 = 0) |
| turning in place, 360 degrees a second | +60 | the wind ring's orphans |
| walking 150 / stopped | +278 / +372 | the same, three times as far |
| walking 300 / stopped | +496 / +876 | the same |
| walking 50 with three server corrections (40-unit snaps) | +570 | the same |

Attacking was not measured (no monster in a server-less QA run; OPEN). So the parts that leave
the body are (a) particles whose followed ancestor has died ("orphans"), carrying that ancestor's
last move, and (b) nodes that follow nothing (u6 = 0). The ring in the picture is
`lightning_gyeonggong_keep_c` #12 "wind-master" (a mesh living 50 frames under a holder #11
living 20): its orphans; the purple swirl is not identified (OPEN; no seal file the client draws
for this glaive runs its own simulation in these runs).

**What the original does (READ, sro_client.exe), re-derived:**
- *Which nodes follow what.* `CEFCLinkMode::vslot_003` (0x00cbb0f0) reads a node's LinkMode
  controller (four u32), and `CEFCLinkMode::vslot_005` (0x00cb9370) writes them as the levels u6
  (+0x168), u2 (+0x158), u3 (+0x15c), u4 (+0x160) -- each clamped to the levels the node has above
  it, u3 = -1 kept -- and sets b1 (+0x155) on the node u6 names, b0 (+0x154) on the ones u2/u3/u4
  name; the body's own block is read by `FUN_00cc3500`. MEASURED (`tools/efp_linkmode_census.gd`,
  1,369 files, 33,015 nodes, 28,640 with a LinkMode): the levels the client reads from the body
  block equal what the controllers give in every node. The loader is right.
- *Follow pass.* `CEFUpdater::vslot_002` (0x00c85f20, the update) and `EFEffect::FUN_00c863a0`
  (the draw's, from `FUN_00cabda0` when the placement flag +0x28b or +0x60 is set): per particle,
  u2 orbit about the ancestor's old position, u3/u4 turns, then `pos += A.pos - A.old` for the u6
  ancestor A, with no test of A's dead flag. A is resolved once into the emitter
  (`CEFGroup::vslot_004`, 0x00c86db0).
- *A dead ancestor stays in memory and is still followed.* A death (`CEFElement::vslot_001`,
  0x00c87a20) unlinks the particle and kills its child emitters (`CEFGroup::vslot_001`, 0x00c879b0),
  which do not kill their particles; an emitter holds its owner (+1 at 0x00c86d54) and each
  particle holds its emitter (+1 at 0x00c8875e); both are released only at count 0
  (`CEFGroup::vslot_002` 0x00c879f0, `CEFElement::vslot_002` 0x00c87aa0). The extinct executor
  (`FUN_00c84e20`) reads the life through the emitter and kills nothing else. So round 785's
  reading holds: an orphan goes on with its dead ancestor's last per-pass move and turn.
- *A kept effect* (`CEFEffect::vslot_000`, 0x00caf550) revives the root updater's queued deaths
  only; a child holder like the wind ring's #11 dies every cycle.
- *One placement and one pass per frame.* `CIDecoSkill::vslot_014` (0x00a503f0) places each
  following entry every frame (`IDecoSkill::FUN_00a4ddc0` -> `FUN_00a4a680`, the animated bone,
  -> `CEFEffect::vslot_007` 0x00caa020), then updates it; the draw runs the pass on a frame without
  an update. The character moves every one of those frames.

**The cause found (MEASURED).** This client moves the player in `_physics_process` (60 ticks a
second) and placed its effects in `_process`, every rendered frame. At 144 or 240 frames a second
most frames see no move and one in 2.4 or 4 sees a whole tick's, so a holder that died on a quiet
frame left its orphans still (a trail), and one that died on a tick frame left them adding a whole
tick's move every frame -- 2.4 or 4 times the body's speed. Headless, `efp_probe.gd --drift`, 50
a second, the body moved on 60 Hz ticks:

| effect, scenario | 144 fps before | after | 240 fps before | after |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| lightning_gyeonggong_keep_c, walk then stop | +83.0 | +49.2 | +378.3 | +48.4 |
| lightning_gyeonggong_keep_c, zigzag | +22.1 | +98.7 | +428.3 | +97.9 |
| fire_gigongta_keep_e, walk then stop | +63.2 | +15.6 | +192.3 | +15.9 |
| fire_gigongta_keep_e, zigzag | +31.8 | +64.5 | +254.5 | +59.3 |

The "after" column equals the body moved every frame (+49.2 / +14.6 at 144 fps with no ticks):
what the original's rules give. (At 144 fps the zigzag's "before" is smaller only by chance --
there its holders happened to die on quiet frames and their orphans stood still, left behind.)
Census, every skill file and the 74 equipment files, kept as their rows say, walk then stop at 144
fps over 60 Hz ticks: drawn particles past their spread in 413 runs (410,641 particle-frames)
before, 316 (218,675) after; equipment files 52 -> 38.

**The fix.** `EfpEffect` places an effect on a host -- and runs its follow pass and steps --
once per physics tick (`tick_gate`, which World3D holds through `gate_ticks`; `tick_of` lets a tool
count its own ticks); a frame with no tick only redraws for the camera. The tick is this client's
stand-in for the original's frame (OURS; the per-frame placement and pass are READ above).
QA: `OPENSRO_QA_FX_NOGATE=1` (before), `OPENSRO_QA_PHYSICS_TICKS=<n>` (physics slower than the
movie writer, so a render shows a fast screen's case).

**Not changed, READ.** What stays: an orphan carries its holder's last move after the body stops
or turns (the wind ring up to 50 frames, `fire_gigongta_keep_e`'s smoke up to 30), and nodes with
u6 = 0 (`fire_hwabyeok_keep_c`'s sparks) stay where they were born. Both follow from the addresses
above; with the body moving every frame the in-client numbers above are those rules. The user
reports retail does not leave rings behind; the binary as read says these particles keep their
last motion. If the user's retail sight still disagrees after this fix, the difference is not in
any function read here (OPEN, for the user to decide on an OURS departure).

**Screenshots** (render box, 1280 x 720, Forward+, `OPENSRO_QA_PHYSICS_TICKS=24`, the zigzag
walk): `/var/tmp/r786-fx/keep/walk_before_f480.png` / `walk_after_f480.png` (walking) and
`walk_before_f560.png` / `walk_after_f560.png` (after the stop). In that run (2.5 frames a tick)
the particles past their spread fell from 1,545 to 1,168 while walking and from 3,481 to 2,787
after the stop; its worst single particle is noise (+43.5 -> +153.5: which frame a hand-bone holder
dies on).

### Round 786 (part): a dead holder is not frozen -- the orphans stay on the body

The user, who knows retail well, on the part above: seal glows and buff auras (Grass Walk's
`lightning_gyeonggong_keep_c`, `fire_gigongta_keep_e`, `fire_hwabyeok_keep_c`) leave copies of the
ground ring and swirls several body lengths away "all the time"; retail never does. The part above
had concluded that this is the original's behaviour. An independent re-read of the same functions
(decompiled and disassembled from `sro_client.exe` on the box) found one reading wrong.

**The departure (READ).** A particle is linked into four lists at its init (`FUN_00c88490`,
0x00c8874c-0x00c8878d): its node updater's **motion list** (updater +0xb0: head +0xd8, next offset
at +0xc8), its emitter's list (+0x30), the updater's **executor list** (+0x48: head +0x70, next
offset at +0x60) and the effect's **draw list** (+0x258). Its death (`CEFElement::vslot_001`,
0x00c87a20) unlinks it from three of them -- the draw list (0x00c87a3c), the executor list
(0x00c87a4e) and the emitter's (0x00c87a5a) -- kills its child emitters and sets its dead flag (+4).
It leaves the motion list only when it is **released** (`CEFElement::vslot_002`, 0x00c87aa0: the
unlink at 0x00c87aaa with ECX = updater +0xb0), at reference count 0 -- while any child emitter of it
still has a particle. Both follow passes walk the motion list with no dead or dying test
(`CEFUpdater::vslot_002` 0x00c85fa0-0x00c862ff, the draw's `FUN_00c863a0`), as does the shift
`FUN_00c865a0`. So a dead holder still held keeps running the motion: `old = pos` (b1, 0x00c85fe3),
its own u2/u3/u4 follows, `pos += A.pos - A.old` for its own ancestor (0x00c86217), its rotation
velocity, `pos += velocity` (0x00c86294-0x00c862bb, the last velocity: no command reaches it), and
its turn (0x00c86316). What it loses: drawing, aging (the life executors 0x00c84e20 / 0x00c84d80
walk +0x70) and commands (the program runner 0x00c84f90 walks +0x70). Its followers' `A.pos - A.old`
is therefore what the holder does now -- the body's motion through the holder's own follow -- not
the frozen last move. Round 785 read the death as "out of every list, its state frozen"; rounds 785
and the part above built on that.

**The seven questions, each checked in the binary:**
1. *Order, and old on dead particles* (READ): each `vslot_002` flushes the death queue first
   (0x00c85f28-0x00c85f5a), runs the executors at node +0x90 / +0xb4 / +0xd8, then the motion loop
   over the motion list -- `old = pos` for every member including dying and held dead -- and the
   life test runs last (node +0x12c, 0x00c8638b). The draw pass does the same `old = pos` per member.
   So a held dead particle's old is refreshed on every later pass; it stops only at release.
2. *What A is* (READ): `CEFGroup::vslot_004` (0x00c86db0) sets emitter +0x64 to its owner particle
   (+0x28) and walks up `[[A+0x14]+0x28]` (the owner's emitter's owner) u6 - 1 times: a particle
   record (+0xa4 old position, +0x1b0 position, the layout `FUN_00c88490` writes), or the effect
   itself at the top (CEFEffect has the same layout: `vslot_007` writes +0x1b0, `vslot_000` +0xa4).
   Not a node frame and not the placement matrix.
3. *Dead as a follow target* (READ): no test of +4 or +0x30 on A in either pass (A's +0x60 is
   tested for u2/u3/u4 only); A is not removed from the list the passes walk until released (above).
   No pointer is cleared on death. **This is where the earlier reading was wrong.**
4. *One pass a frame* (READ): `+0x28b` is the placement flag -- set by `vslot_007` (0x00caa020) and
   `vslot_008` (0x00ca9460) with +0x60, cleared by `CEFEffect::vslot_000` after the update
   (0x00caf550: this is the IEasyFxEffect sub-object at +0x240, so its +0x4b / -0x1e0 are +0x28b / +0x60) and by the draw after its pass (`FUN_00cabda0`). So a
   frame runs either the update's pass or the draw's, never both; ours runs one (set_origin's
   `step_due`). The draw sets the world transform to the effect's scale only (the diagonal from +0x1c8 at
   0x00cabe1d, SetTransform(D3DTS_WORLD 0x100) at 0x00cabe52-0x00cabe7e; the pass gate +0x28b at 0x00cabe80): particle positions are world positions over the scale.
5. *u6 = 0* (READ): emitter +0x64 = 0 (0x00c86217 skips the translation follow), and the newborn
   copies its owner's position (`FUN_00c88490`); with the draw in world space (4.), such a particle
   stays where it was born while the body moves: a trail in the world, not local to the effect.
   Unchanged (`fire_hwabyeok_keep_c`'s 17 spark nodes are u6 = 0).
6. *Kept effects* (READ): `CEFEffect::vslot_000` revives only the ROOT updater's death queue
   (+0x254 -> +0xa0: dying flag and age cleared); a child holder (the wind ring's #11) dies every
   cycle. Unchanged -- and harmless now: its orphans follow it while it is held.
7. *Server corrections* (READ): 0xB021's source position goes to `FUN_009e11e0`, which places the
   object at once (a snap, no interpolation): either through the object's slot 37 (`FUN_009e0d50` ->
   `+0x94`; the region-change shift of `CICPlayer::vslot_037` only when the region differs) or by
   writing the mover's position (+0x4c..). No effect is shifted inside a region; the next frame's
   placement of each effect carries the snap as motion, which the followers -- and now the orphans
   -- follow; u6 = 0 particles stay.

**The fix.** `EfpSim` keeps every particle still in memory in `_order` (live, dying, and dead with
a live descendant, in spawn order: retail's motion list); the step's and the pass's motion and the
shift walk it, commands only the live ones; `_flush_deaths` drops a dead particle once no live
descendant holds it. The native `Sim` does the same with its reference counts (`order`, kept while
`rc > 0`). Round 785's zombie machinery (`_zombie_follow`, `_still_pass`, the frozen shift) goes: a
still frame's pass now moves nothing, so `take_pass_moved` is always false. `EFP_API` 3 (an older
library steps by the frozen rule and is refused). The tick gate stays (OURS, fewer placements); it
no longer changes where orphans are drawn.

**MEASURED, `efp_probe.gd --drift --physics=60 --physics-effects`, 50 a second** (the farthest drawn
particle past its still spread; `walk` runs 2 s then stands 4 s, `zigzag` turns 90 degrees every
0.5 s; the probe now splits the particle-frames past the spread into orphans and u6 = 0 trails):

| effect | mode | 144 fps before | after | 240 fps before | after |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| lightning_gyeonggong_keep_c | walk + stop | +49.2 (72 orphan) | +0.0 (0) | +48.4 (70) | +0.0 (0) |
| lightning_gyeonggong_keep_c | zigzag | +98.7 (208 orphan) | +0.0 (0) | +97.9 (203) | +0.0 (0) |

### Round 786 (part): hotbar slot numbers and quantities

The user, on v0.1.536 (Windows and Mac): "The hotbar is supposed to show the slot number at times
and show the item quantity when applicable." Their F4 bar showed the number only on the empty slot
5, none on a skill or item, and no quantity on the potions; then "Seems like it kind of works on
F1, but still not item quantity. Make sure it's working for all of them." An earlier render on
v0.1.534's code showed F1's filled slots 1-3 drawing "1", "2", "3". Nothing in the bar changed
between the two releases (`git log v0.1.534..v0.1.536 -- hud_underbar.gd` is empty): it depends
on the page.

**Retail (READ, `sro_client.exe`, the decompile and the asm on the box):**
- **The key numbers are the bar's own pictures, not the slot's.** `nifundermenubar.2dt`'s records
  96..105 are CNIFStatics 92..101 on `ub_number_1`..`_0` (and 102 `ub_number_m`), 8x12 at each
  slot's bottom-right corner, x = slot + 24, y = slot + 22, hanging 2 px below it (MEASURED, the
  real file on the box). They come after the slots (records 33..42) in the file, children are
  appended in load order (`0xb90a80`), and `0xba0300` (CGWnd slot 14) draws the child list first
  to last. So the number is drawn over the slot whatever it holds, on every page.
- **The pages' other slots go under them.** The OnCreate (`0x60df30`) makes quick slots 11..50
  (`0x60e0d0..0x60e17a`) and calls `0xb90c30` on each (`0x60e159`): mode 2 at +0x28, order at
  +0x29. The main frame's tick (`CGFXMainFrame::vslot_011` -> `CGWndBase::vslot_012` `0xb92070`,
  recursing into every shown child at `0xb923f0`) moves a mode-2 child to the FRONT of its parent's
  list (`0xb92228` -> map `0x110f650`, inserted before the first node at `0xb92373..`); mode 1
  (`0xb90bd0`) goes to the back (`0xb92261` -> `0x110f65c`, `0xb922f7..`). Every page's slots
  therefore sit under the key numbers.
- **The quantity is the slot's own draw.** `CIFSlotWithHelp::vslot_013` (`0x685e50`): the icon
  (`0x6550c0`), the overlays (`0x67cfb0`: seal edge, re-use display, ...), then, when `0x680da0`
  holds, the count with `0x67bd70`: `item_number_0..9.ddj` digit pictures (loaded at +0x5a0 by
  `vslot_010` `0x66b460`) at the slot's TOP LEFT, as round 728 read for the bag (ItemCountLabel).
  No font, no colour of its own. `0x680da0`'s quick-slot case (kind 0x0c, sub-kind 0x46 an item):
  `0x538410` on the item's type word -- not bionic, TypeID1 3, TypeID2 3 -- and a non-zero count
  (+0x9c, `0x8ba460`; a count of 1 is drawn); a zero count clears the slot (`0x67ece0`).
  `0x67bd70` also needs the slot's +0x679: 1 from the constructor (`0x673c80`), then set by the
  SetItem every bar item goes through (`0x60c430` -> `0x6871d0`) to `max stack > 1` (`cmp
  [ref+0x1c0], 1; setg` at `0x6875cd..0x6875d7`; +0x1c0 the max stack, round 726's reading of
  `0x68a6c0`). So: a STACKABLE expendable with a count, a 1 included.
- **The count is the bag's, live.** `0x60c430` (called on bag moves and item results) finds every
  quick slot bound to the bag slot and sets it from the bag's item (`0x6871d0` stores the bag's own
  SOItem at +0x390), so the bar draws that bag slot's stack each frame -- not a total over the bag.
- **The two never collide:** the count is top-left, the number bottom-right.

**The cause (OURS, `hud_underbar.gd`, `World3D.gd`):**
- The made slots 11..50 were added at the END of the bar's children, after the number pictures,
  so on F2..F4 an icon covered its number (the empty slot showed it). F1's authored slots come
  before the numbers in file order, so F1 "kind of worked".
- No caller ever passed a count: every `set_slot_item` call in World3D gave only an icon, and the
  slot's count was a font Label at the bottom right (under the number) shown only above 1.

**The fix:**
- `_build_slots` sends each made slot to the front of the bar's children (`move_child(node, 0)`),
  as `0xb90c30` does: under every other child, over the bar's own art.
- The slot's count is an `ItemCountLabel` (the digit pictures, top left); the slot is unclipped (the
  original clips nothing; four digits start 1 px left of the slot); the re-use display is kept
  under the count (`0x67cfb0` before `0x67bd70`).
- `HudUnderbar.item_counts` / `apply_item_counts`: every item slot on every page draws its bound
  bag slot's stack when `HudPanels.bar_shows_count` (`ItemCountLabel.shows_on_bar`: max stack
  > 1, 3/3, not bionic, a count) says so, every other slot none. World3D calls it (`_refresh_quickslot_counts`) on every bag list (after a use --
  manual or auto potion --, a pick-up, a drop, a trade, a quest), every bag move, every bar change
  (`_save_hotbar`) and the login restore. `set_slot_item`'s count defaults to 0.
- QA (OURS): `OPENSRO_QA_AUTOPOT` gains `skill:<slot>:<id>` (a skill's icon on any slot) and
  `counts` (each filled slot's drawn count, `QA HOTBAR`); its `bind` now saves the bar as a drop
  does.

**Tests (failing first, 7 FAILURES before the fix):** `hud_underbar_test.gd` -- every page's slots
under the key numbers 92..101 (the fixture gains the ten number records, structure only); the count
an `ItemCountLabel` on an unclipped slot; the bar's rule (`shows_on_bar`: a 1 drawn, not for max
stack 1, bionic, gear or 0); `item_counts` (7, 7, a 1 drawn, 0 for a non-expendable and
for a missing bag slot); after F3, F4 and F1 each shown slot draws its count; a use takes the shown
F3 slot and the hidden F1 slot bound to the same stack to 6; a stale count goes from a slot no item
is bound to; the re-use display under the count.

### Round 786 (part): Uniques show their own minimap sign

The user: "uniques should show a special icon on the minimap so it's easier to find them" -- they
found Lord Yarkan only by searching by hand. Every monster had the one red monster sign. The
reading is `docs/protocol/minimap.md` ("The signs and the arrow").

**Retail (READ, `sro_client.exe`, the decompile and the asm on the box):**
- **The art.** `CIFMinimap::Create` (`0x660f70`) loads `interface\minimap\mm_sign_unique.ddj`
  (string `0xda0e20`, pushed at `0x6610ab`, loaded by `0x5008f0`) and stores it at `+0x3b0`
  (`0x6610d7`), between the monster sign (`+0x3ac`, `0x661082`) and the NPC sign (`+0x3b4`,
  `0x66112c`). MEASURED (`Pk2Reader` + `DdjReader` over the box's Media.pk2): the file is there,
  12x12, its opaque pixels a purple (mean 130, 37, 178) where the monster sign's are red.
- **Which monsters.** vslot_013's sign loop (`0x6636d2..0x6639af`) tests each entity with
  `IsKindOf` (`0xb94b90`): a CICMonster (`0xef1a84`) whose byte `+0x7ac` is 3 or 8 takes `+0x3b0`
  (`0x663790..0x6637a6`), any other CICMonster `+0x3ac`. The quad is the same +-4 for every kind
  (all branches join at `0x66382f`; `0xe1b860`), so the 12x12 art is drawn at 8x8.
- **`+0x7ac`.** `CICMonster::vslot_025` (`0x9d3850`), the monster's spawn reader, reads one byte
  (`0x9d38c4`) and stores its low nibble at `+0x7ac` (`and cl,0xf`, `0x9d38e1`), its high nibble
  at `+0x7ad` (the party flag, round 660). INFERRED: that byte is characterdata's Rarity
  (column 15), which is what our server sends; MEASURED over the box's characterdata's 6,850
  monster rows, rarity 3 is on 605 of them, the uniques among them (`MOB_TK_BONELORD`, "Lord
  Yarkan", is 3), and rarity 8 on 18 boss rows of `TQ` / `RM` (`MOB_TQ_TOMBGENERAL`,
  `MOB_RM_DEVILSAYTAN`, ...).

**Client:**
- `HudMinimap.SIGN_TEXTURES` gains `"unique"` -> `mm_sign_unique.ddj`, and
  `HudMinimap.monster_sign_kind(rarity)` is the rule (`"unique"` for 3 or 8).
- `World3D._build_monster_body` decides a body's sign once, from the snapshot's rarity, into
  `_minimap_unique_bodies` (id -> body, a subset of `_monster_bodies`, dropped in
  `_free_monster_body` and at the zone change). `_minimap_fill_monsters` (both the field's and the
  dungeon's refresh) fills `_minimap_monsters` without the uniques and `_minimap_uniques` from the
  subset; `update_signs` takes the second list as a new `uniques` argument (default empty).
- OURS: the cost. The skip is looked up only for a body already inside the sign reach, and only
  while a unique is loaded; with none, the per-frame walk over the monsters (up to 7,000 bodies,
  round 757) adds one bool test a body in reach.
- OURS: `MinimapSigns` draws a kind at a time (round 757); the `unique` kind is drawn last, over
  every other sign. Retail draws each entity's sign in the order of its one entity list
  (`0xec4cec`, next at `+0xc`), so a unique can be under a neighbour's sign there.

**Tests:** `hud_minimap_test.gd` (rarity 3 and 8 -> unique, 0, 1, 4, 5, 6, 7 -> monster; the art
paths), `minimap_signs_test.gd` (the rarity-3 and rarity-8 monsters drawn with the unique art and

icon. Then: the skill window (the skill menu) showed no cooldown at all. The whole reading is
`docs/protocol/skill_reuse_display.md`; the code `client/scripts/ui/skill_delay_overlay.gd`
(`SkillDelayOverlay`, new).

**Retail (READ, `UI_SILKMALL::FUN_0067cfb0`, from `CIFSlotWithHelp::vslot_013` `0x685e50`; the
doubles read at their addresses in `sro_client.exe`):**
- The sweep: `frame = ftol(239.0 - r * 239.0)` (0xda3760), r = `FUN_009bb9c0` (left / total),
  column `frame & 15`, row `frame >> 4`; UVs `column * 32.0 (0xd99a60) * 0.001953125 (0xda3768)`,
  the same for the row -- each cell **1/16 of the sheet**, drawn over the slot's whole quad with
  +0x620 (`skill_delay.ddj`, loaded by `vslot_010` `0x66b460`).
- The flash: `frame = ftol(15.0 - f * 15.0)` (0xd878a0), f = `FUN_009bbb60`, column `& 3`, row `>> 2`,

- MEASURED (Media.pk2, the JMXVDDJ's DDS header and payload size): `skill_delay.ddj` is
  **256 x 256** A8R8G8B8, no mips -- 16 x 16 cells of **16 pixels**, 240 used (row 15 empty), black at
  alpha 185 where time is left, the clear part growing clockwise from 12 o'clock; `skill_charge.ddj`
  64 x 64 A8R8G8B8, 4 x 4 cells of 16 pixels.
- **The skill window has it.** `ifskill_slot.txt` ID 1 is `GDR_STMS_SLOT_SKILL:CIFSlotWithHelp`
  (MEASURED); `CIFSkillSlot::Create` (`0x6a0980`) keeps it at +0x3ac and sets its kind to 0x49
  (`push 0x49; call 0x6666f0`, `0x6a09e5`); SetSkill `0x6a15f0` gives it the skill id

**The cause (OURS, round 785):** `hud_underbar.gd` read `32 * 1/512` as "a 16 x 16 sheet of 32-pixel
cells on 512 x 512" and cut a 32-pixel region; on the real 256 sheet that is 2 x 2 cells -- the
GIF's four small sweeps. The charge sheet's 16-pixel cut happened to be right. The skill window
(`SkillBoard`, round 781) drew no overlay.

**The fix:**
- `SkillDelayOverlay.cell_region` takes the cell as 1/16 (1/4) of the loaded sheet, as the UVs do;
  `apply` stretches one cell over the icon. `HudUnderbar.set_slot_cooldown` uses it (still under the
  count); `SkillCooldowns`' comments corrected.
- `SkillBoard.set_cooldowns` puts it on every learned slot (meta `skill_id`) over the 32 x 32 icon;
  `HudPanels.apply_skill_cooldowns` keeps the board's callable so a refilled board draws the running
  sweeps at once; World3D's `_tick_skill_cooldowns` feeds the bar and the window from the one
  `SkillCooldowns` (`_skill_cooldown_frames`: the skill's own record or its group's).
- INFERRED: in the skill window the overlay sits over the icon and under the level badge and button
  (the slot child's order against `ifskill_slot.txt`'s other children was not traced).
- QA (OURS): `OPENSRO_QA_AUTOPOT` gains `cool:<skill id>:<ms>` (arms the re-use time, no cast) and
  `coolboard:<ms>` (every learned skill on the open skill window, staggered).

**Tests (failing first):** `hud_underbar_test.gd` seeds the builder's cache with 256 x 256 and 64 x 64
sheets: delay frame 17 is `Rect2(16, 16, 16, 16)`, frame 0 `(0, 0, 16, 16)`, the overlay's rect is
the slot's, charge frame 6 `(32, 16, 16, 16)` -- on round 785's code "2 FAILURES" (`(32, 64, 32,
32)` and `(0, 0, 32, 32)`). `skill_delay_overlay_test.gd` (new): the cell arithmetic at the measured
sizes, every frame `SkillCooldowns` can pick inside its sheet, the node's place and life.
`skill_board_test.gd`: only learned slots are asked, one 16-pixel cell over the icon's 32 x 32 (not

### Round 786 (part): Party members on the minimap in dungeons, and on the world map

The user: "While in a party and dungeon the minimap is broken for party member dots", and "I don't
think I can track party members on the map anymore." Two client bugs; the server was right. The
reading is `docs/protocol/party_gui.md` section 9 and `docs/protocol/minimap.md` ("The signs and
the arrow").

**Root causes (MEASURED on dev `2f0f01c8`):**
- **The dungeon minimap never placed the party's marks.** `World3D._refresh_dungeon_minimap`
  (round 773) did the tiles, the player, the signs and the world map, but never called
  `HudMinimap.update_party`, so the marks stayed as the last field frame left them: frozen at old
  offsets after a teleport in, or none when the party formed inside. Live on the box (Aria and three
  partybots in the Donwhang cave, Cara beside her, Eve 191 south, Dex 662 away): `map marks minimap
  [] world map []` at every `maplog` (`/var/tmp/partymap/base_dg.out`). The new world suite on the
  base prints `got 'dot@(8.0,0.0)'` -- the field's mark, frozen.
- **The world map lost the party for the session once a dungeon floor was shown.** Round 775's
  `show_dungeon` (`449ec093`) sets `_current` null; round 717's `update_party` then sent every dot
  to (-1e9, -1e9). A Control's offsets are 32-bit floats, which cannot hold -1e9 and -1e9 + 16
  apart, so each pooled dot's size became 0x0, and nothing ever set it back. On the base: the dot
  is at (365, 256) on the world map, a floor is shown, and back on the world map it reports
  `(357,248) dot size (0.0, 0.0) visible true` -- drawn at nothing. Any floor does it: M in a
  dungeon (auto-move follows to the floor) or a click on a dungeon icon. The field path itself was
  intact (live, `MODE=field`: Dex's and Eve's dots at (4047,548) and (4027,532), round 717's place).
- **Not the server.** Since round 773 the records carry the dungeon's rid and its own-space x, y, z
  (`party.partyPosition`, `dungeon773_test.go`); live, Dex's record read `r128/1 x654 z-1420`
  after his `/tp 654 1420`. No server change, no deploy.

**Retail (READ, `sro_client.exe`, the decompile and the asm on the box):**
- **The minimap** has one party loop for the field and a dungeon (`CIFMinimap::vslot_013`,
  `0x6643a0..0x664ad1`). Each record goes to `UI_SILKMALL::FUN_009d5520(record region, &record
  x/y/z)` (`0x6643de..0x664419`): 1 for a field region while the player is in the field; else 1
  only for the player's own dungeon region (`cmp di, [ecx+0x7c]`) when the block under the record's
  position (region manager `[0x111a02c]` slot `0x2c`) has the floor of the player's block (`+0x74`
  slot `0x14` of `+0x78`), both through `[0x1103cc6]` slot 1 and the block's slot 2 -- the chain
  `ICPlayer::FUN_009d7880` reads the floor name with. The offset is the position less the player's
  `+0x80`/`+0x88` (`0x66448f..0x6644ba`), both the dungeon's own space in a dungeon.
- **The world map** (`CNIFWorldMap::FUN_0061eec0`, `0x61f8c0..0x61ffce`; `0x61f9e7..0x61fd48` the
  branches): on a field map a dungeon member is drawn at its dungeon's field point
  (`0x60fa90(member region)`, offset zeroed, `0x61fa44..0x61fa6d`); a field member from the
  player's marker by its offset (`0x61f94d..0x61f9b7`), or with the player in a dungeon from the
  dungeon's field point by the record's offset from the instance entry (`0x61fa8e..0x61fbfb`; the
  entry's `+0x30` is its field region, loader `0x953777..0x9537a3`) -- either way its own field
  position. On a floor's map (`+0x97d0 == 2`, `0x61fc00..0x61fd42`) a field member is not drawn,
  a dungeon member only with the floor row's region id (`[0x62c030() + 0x84]`, row `+0x88`), and
  in the cave (region 1, four floors in one region) only in the floor's height band:
  `CNIFWorldMap::FUN_00610ed0` puts the record's y under 70.0 (`0xd990a8`), 210.0 (the double
  `0xd990a0`) or 350.0 (`0xd9909c`) into levels 0..3 and wants `floor (+0x40) - 1`.

**Client:**
- `PartyMapMarks.region_visible` is `0x9d5520`; `minimap_draws` takes the player's region and the
  floor answer; `worldmap_draws` no longer drops dungeon records; `cave_level` and
  `floor_map_draws` are `0x610ed0` and the floor test.
- `World3D._fill_party_marks` fills the minimap's list in the player's own frame (region-local in
  the field, dungeon space in a dungeon: a spawned body through `DungeonWorld.to_dungeon`, else the
  record) and hands the world map each member's region word and position, y the record's.
  `_party_minimap_draws` asks the floor of the block under the record (`DungeonWorld.block_under`,
  cached per member until the record moves) against `_dungeon_block`'s. INFERRED: the block's
  slot 2 is `DofReader`'s floor index (as the floor name, round 774).
- `_refresh_dungeon_minimap` now fills and places the marks, and gives the world map its party.
- `HudWorldmap.update_party(regions, positions, names, job)` places each by `party_pixel` (the
  branches above); `update_player_dungeon` no longer clears the dots. `place_party_dots` leaves a
  dot it hides where it is and sets the size whenever it shows one.
- OURS: on a field map, a dungeon member whose region has no instanceinfo point has no dot; the
  world map's "less 0.5" stays out (round 717); a floor shown with the player in the field marks no
  one (OPEN below).

**Live** (`/var/tmp/partymap/live.sh`, `MODE=dungeon`: server and partybot from this branch; Aria
rendered at the cave's entry, dungeon (1011, -862); Cara beside her; Eve `/tp 1011 1053`, dungeon
