### Round 778 (part): the camera

The user: "the original camera lets me look up more, you can even get close to the character body
that makes it even fade away. Please check the original code on how the cameras work so I can
inspect better."

**What the original does (READ, `sro_client.exe` on the box: the decompile in
`/var/tmp/decomp_client` and `objdump` of the same bytes; `.rdata` values read from the PE).** The
game camera is the object at `0x110f7d0`; its CGFXVideo3d sits at +0x33c, so the look-at point is
+0x34c, pitch +0x370, yaw +0x374, distance +0x37c (the CGFXVideo3d fields round 635's portrait read: +0x10, +0x34, +0x38, +0x40).
The interface (`CGInterface`, `0x110f80c`) holds the zoom: +0x3e8 asked for, +0x3ec in force,
+0x3f8 the collided distance (+0x3f4 set while it applies).

| What | Value | Where |
|---|---|---|
| Pitch limit | +-1.0707964 rad = **+-61.35 deg**, looking down AND up | floats 0xdb8d70 / 0xdb8d64; WM_MOUSEMOVE in `CGInterface::vslot_017` 0x77c330..0x77c3fa |
| Drag | **0.005 rad (0.2865 deg) a pixel**, pitch and yaw; mouse down raises the camera | double 0xd986e8 (`fmul qword` 0x77c351) |
| Zoom range | **10 .. 150** | floats 0xd81a88, 0xdb8d74 (150 applies while +0x3cf is set: 1 from the constructor `FUN_0078d050`, toggled only by a console command at 0x53a970) |
| Wheel | distance -= delta / 20: **6 a notch** (WHEEL_DELTA 120), forward zooms in; asked-for = in-force at once | `CGInterface::vslot_036` 0x77b460, reached from `CGWndBase::vslot_017`'s `cmp esi, 0x20a` with the wParam high word; double 0xe1b830 |
| Smoothing | **none**: zoom, drag and the third-person yaw all apply the same frame | `FUN_0078dc50` writes the camera directly |
| Look-up limit | below level, distance <= **40 + 110 (1 - sin(1.5708 x (-pitch) / 0.9))**: 150 level, 62.9 at 30 deg up, 40 at 51.57, 44.85 at 61.35; back out to the asked-for distance when level or down | `FUN_0078dc50` 0x78dd21..0x78ddc3; doubles 0xe1b8f8, 0xdb97f8, 0xd83a98, 0xe1b8f0; `FUN_00b44b40` is `fsin` |
| Look-at point | over the feet, **14.2 + (d - 150)(14.2 - (h - 3.8)) / 140**: 14.2 at 150, 16.2 at 10 (d = the collided distance while it applies) | `FUN_0078dc50` 0x78ddc9..0x78de58; doubles 0xd83068, 0xd83060, 0xd83058, 0xd83078 |
| h (the character's +0x228) | 20 x size x 0.5 x scale = **20** for a player | `FUN_009c7780` (0xe1b830 x `FUN_009c7740`); size is column 3 of `textdata\skilleffect.txt` `characterInfo`, read by `FUN_00a9ae80` x 0.5 (0xe1b7d0) |
| Collision | a ray from 5 out to the distance (SWorld::vslot_030: terrain cells and objects' own meshes); on a hit the camera sits at **\|hit - target\| - 5** | `FUN_0078def0` 0x78df10..0x78e09d, double 0xd81950; on while +0x3cc is set (1 in the constructor, 0x78df10) |
| Own-model fade | each drag calls `FUN_009d54c0(pitch < -0.9)` on the player: a ramp of its alpha from where it is to **0** (looking up past **51.57 deg**) or back to 255, **t += 2.0 x dt** (0.5 s), alpha = start + t x delta, truncated | callers 0x77c39e, 0x7790ed, 0x77b19a (only three); double 0xdb8d68; ramp step `FUN_009d4e80`, rate 0xd86ecc set by `CICPlayer::CICPlayer` 0x9da6d0; applied by `CICPlayer::vslot_009` through the model's slot 5 (the compound alpha the appear fade sets) |
| Views (+0x3e4) | 0 free: drag turns both; 1 third person: yaw = (1.57 - heading) + 1.5707963 every frame (behind, no easing), drag turns the pitch; 2 quarter: drag turns the yaw only, the pitch stays -- no view writes a pitch | 0x77c31d, `FUN_0078dc50` 0x78dcef..0x78dd1b (doubles 0xdb9800, 0xe1b8f0), `FUN_00780590` / 0x780420 |
| Keys | none turn the camera: the arrows run and turn the character (`FUN_0077b070`); the arrow/WASD camera of `FUN_0078e0e0` is the developer free camera (+0x3ce, console only) | |

So there is no distance fade: the character fades because looking up past 0.9 rad pulls the camera in
(the look-up limit, then the ground cuts it to ~14) and the pitch test fades it. Only the player's own
model fades (all three callers pass `[0xeef5ec]`); monsters, NPCs, other players and the name plate
keep theirs (the plate draws at full alpha whatever the model's, round 673).

**Contradicted and corrected.** Our `CAMERA_PITCH_MIN/MAX` were -80/-10 (the 2026-08-26 sign fix: no look
up at all), the zoom 20..90 by 15 (the fifty-fifth round, "an openly-declared framing choice ... no real
camera-distance data has been found"), the drag 0.3 deg a pixel, the look-at point a fixed 14.34
(the scene's arm height), the quarter view a fixed -55 pitch and the third-person view an easing of
360 deg a second (both ours), and the third-person view took no pitch drag. Both old entries now carry
a "Superseded (round 778)" line. `SHADOW_MAP_DISTANCE` follows its own rule (300 from the player plus
the farthest camera, round 702): 400 -> **460**.

**Built (`client/scripts/world/retail_camera.gd`, `RetailCamera`; World3D's `_place_camera`,
`_camera_wheel`, `_input`'s orbit, `set_camera_view`).** The arm's pitch is the negative of the
retail pitch and its yaw the retail yaw + pi (DERIVED: the arm puts the camera at d (cos a sin w, -sin
a, cos a cos w), the retail eye is d (-cos p sin y, sin p, -cos p cos y)), so the drag signs are the
retail ones. The SpringArm3D's own spring and sphere cast are off (`set_physics_process_internal(false)`,
re-checked each step since the arm turns it back on when it re-enters the tree); `_place_camera` runs
the placer and the ray once a physics step on the arm's `collision_mask` (QA_FREE still clears it)

### Round 778 (part): the reverse return scroll

The user: "please get reverse return scrolls fully working including map icons that it provides and
original gui popup when you use it. Read how it works with the original code. It should even let me
select the floor of the cave." `docs/protocol/reverse_return_scroll.md` has every address; this is
the summary.

**READ.** A right-click on a 3/3/3/3 item (ITEM_MALL_REVERSE_RETURN_SCROLL 3795 and its three
siblings) does not send the use: `IFSlotWithHelp::FUN_00676570` opens message box kind 0x21, built
by `UI_SILKMALL::FUN_00644c90` (0x647dff..): 300 x 204, `UIIT_STT_CONFIRM_BOX`, the question, and
four `com_return_button.ddj` buttons -- "Move to the last recall point." (option 2), "Move to the
place where you died." (3), "Move to certain location at the map." (control 203, created there) and
Cancel. The map button (0x63b9a0) puts the world map in its selection mode (`CNIFWorldMap`
0x622dd0): the refoptionalteleport rows whose map-point byte is 1 drawn as `xy_returnicon.ddj`
icons (a 64 x 32 two-frame atlas swapped every 500 ms by timer 0xd, `_focus` under the mouse,
`_press` picked), a click opening a `map_return.ddj` popup that lists the point -- or, for a group's
flag, the rows of the group that are not map points: the Donwhang cave's floor. A popup button sends
the use with option 7 and the row's id (0x60f5f0); hiding the map cancels everything (vslot_023).
On the server `FUN_004a00c0` refuses in a fixed order with category-1 codes (0x18f5, 0x187a,
0x185f, 0x185d, 0x1875, 0x185e, 0x1885, 0x1886, 2, 0x18fd), starts the scroll state with
`(float)Param1` as its delay, and the state's job resolves the destination when it expires: the
recall point (`SaveCurPosAsLastTelPosition`, which the ordinary return scroll calls when used), the
death point (`FUN_004e0330` on death), or the table row's point exactly.

**The floor of the cave.** Selecting a floor is the popup under the cave's flag, not the floor
spinner (in selection mode the spinner is hidden and a click never opens a dungeon map). This
archive's table has one row under the Donwhang flag -- `SN_ZONE_23002` "Donwhang Stone Cave", the

so the cave offers one floor and the tomb none, exactly as the original client would. A table with
more rows in a group lists them all.

**OURS / OPEN.** The delay's unit is OPEN (the job counts seconds, which would make Param1 1000 a
thousand seconds; the tooltips say "immediately"): Param1 is milliseconds here. OpenSRO's wire is
OpUseItem with retail's {u8 option, u32 id} tail and a {u16 code, u32 cast_ms} reply tail. The
world, PK, quest, cart and fortress refusals have nothing to refuse in OpenSRO; an unplaceable
destination answers 0x18f5. The ordinary return scroll now works too (records the recall point,
returns to the return point after Param1) -- the reverse scroll's option 2 has nothing to read
without it. Thief-den scrolls stay refused.

## Seven-hundred-and-seventy-seventh round: the glows back, the portals' layers, the dungeon minimap's room

The user, after v0.1.523: "the teleporter effects inside the dungeon should probably a be a little
bit brighter", "make sure the minimap locations are correct in the dungeons. It just seems to show
the general floor you're located on when the locations are more precise than that", and "looks
like the glow effect for at least the Jangan teleporter stopped working, that needs fixed too.
Make sure you avoid regression."

**The glows (a round-774 regression, fixed).** Round 774 made `AmbientParticles.update` skip an
effect that was not `visible`, so a dungeon's culled effects queued no glow. But a glow effect
hides itself while its glow alpha is 0 and fades in only when the pass sees it
(`EfpEffect.set_glow_alpha`): no glow anywhere could fade in -- the Jangan gate's, every town gate's,
the dungeon flames' glow halves. The culling now sets `EfpEffect.culled`, the pass skips only
that, and `ambient_particles_test` holds both (a hidden glow is queued; a culled one is not).
Verified: `OPENSRO_QA_AMBIENT=1` at the Jangan gate, `cj_pal_potal_blue.efp a255 vis,
w_cd_potal_blue_g.efp a255 vis`, and the glow drawn. Tests ran green in v0.1.523 because none
covered a glow at alpha 0 against the new test.

**The portals (OURS, calibrated).** Measured at the tomb's entry portal, 50 frames each, the
ring's median / 90th percentile: Forward+ (57,71,160) / (84,100,194); the same frame under
Compatibility, which blends in display values exactly as Direct3D 9 does, (94,128,247) /
(161,207,255); the user's retail frame (98,116,200) / (177,231,255). `system_dungeonpotal` is 19
additive layers drawn over each other, and under Forward+ each layer blends against the opaque
scene alone (`EfpEffect.display_shader`, round 722), so the linear differences of overlapping
layers add up to less than the display-value sum (the curve is convex). Now each layer of an
additive class adds `(lin(d + n s a) - lin(d)) / n`, n = min(the effect's additive layers, 8)
(`DISPLAY_STACK_DEFAULT`): exact for a one-layer effect, and for n equal layers lying over each
other. 8 against 4 and 19, MEASURED: the ring (102,129,219) / (156,187,244); the hall's lamps
516 -> 602 warm pixels a frame (Compatibility 856) at the same brightness. `OPENSRO_QA_FX_STACK=1`
turns it off. Also MEASURED: the user's retail frames are brighter overall than ours by about the
game's own Brightness option at "Light" (its gamma ramp, OPTION_VIDEO.md: our floor (29, 30)
-> (52, 53) against their (54, 58)), so the floor's difference in round 774's entry is most likely
their setting, not the lighting.

**The dungeon minimap (READ, `UI_SILKMALL::FUN_00661ce0`'s dungeon branch).** The area label is
the text of `ICPlayer::FUN_009d7830` -- the player's block's room name, the block's room index
into the `.dof`'s room list -- set only when the block has one (a block without keeps the last);
the floor badge (child 10, `vslot 0xb4`) takes the text of `FUN_009d7880`, the floor name. Both
are textzonename rows keyed by name (MEASURED), which `TextZoneNameReader` skipped as not
numbers; it keeps them now (`text_for`). Rendered at the user's spot: "Audience Chamber" over the
minimap and "B1" in the badge, as in their retail frames. OURS: the badge's text style (the area
label's).

**Cost.** Tomb B2 with every glow fading in again: p95 work frame 7 ms (place 0.3, simulate 2.2,
draw 1.7, glow pass 2.6 ms). `check` ALL LOAD; `tests` 279 suites, 0 failing (round 776 merged).

**Perf gate** (`--base 2e057030 --head 954a3c0a --sites jangan --frames 40000`, 1280x720, median
of 3): every row SAME -- frame 0.75 -> 0.75 ms, entry 8747 -> 8473 ms, freeze 2735 -> 2719 ms,
hitches 5 -> 5.


## Seven-hundred-and-seventy-sixth round: the world map's names -- every text over every icon, centred, bold and shadowed as the client draws them

The user: "the map changes are great but some names are slightly misaligned or missing entirely.
Let's make sure the map is 100% accurate" (the private server's unique markers -- the orange-red
"(CH)" labels, red dots, the checkbox and the footer line -- are a mod and ignored). UI lane, client
only. Labels: READ (sro_client.exe, md5 2a5794b72c90908d945be8b3f3f2edd4), MEASURED, INFERRED, OURS.
The reading is `docs/protocol/WORLDMAP_FORMAT.md`, "The text signs (round 776)".

**What the original does (READ).**
- **Draw order.** The render (vslot_013 0x624380 -> 0x61c360) walks the sign list twice: every
  picture sign with a texture first, then every text sign with text (0x8b48b0). Round 775 drew
  them in file order, and the town's name `SN_ZONE_22001` ("Jangan", region (168, 97) + (15, 10))
  is listed before the icon `city_jangan.ddj` (64 x 64, region (167, 98) + (16, 2)) whose painted
  plate it lands on -- so the icon covered it: **the empty plate**. (All the world map's text rows
  come before its picture rows in the file; Jangan's is the one in this view that sits on an icon.)
- **The text's style (0x6210b0, asm 0x6211d4..0x62126c).** Column 14 is the font index
  (0xba5460), columns 15..17 the colour (0x8b2b70), then column 18 sets or clears text flag 1,
  column 19 flag 2, **column 20 flag 1 again** (`push 1; push 5` before 0x8b44b0 / 0x8b4560 at
  0x621219 and 0x62125d). So the "Blur" byte, not the "Shadow" byte, decides the drop shadow.
  Flag 2 is the weight-600 face (0x8b39e0, made in 0xbaa110), flag 1 the one-pixel black shadow
  drawn glyph by glyph before each glyph (0x8b48b0 -> 0x8b2290). Round 775 drew none of it.
- **Place.** The text is measured after the flags (0x8b3b60 -> 0x8b39e0 -> 0x8b3910: the sum of
  the glyphs' advances) and put at `origin + anchor.x - width / 2` (int division), `origin +
  anchor.y`; 0x8b48b0 draws the glyph cells from that top, the baseline at the face's tmAscent
  below it (GFontChar 0x8b0a00 places each glyph's black box at `tmAscent - gmptGlyphOrigin.y`;
  0xbaa110 stores GetTextMetrics per variant).
- **Picture signs** are top-left quads, `w` x `h` (unchanged and right: MEASURED below).
- Nothing else hides a sign: no zoom levels (one tile grid), every sign of the map shown is built;
  the map area clips them.

**MEASURED, before and after.** The user's picture of the original (2564 x 1494, the game at 2x)
and of ours (3818 x 2054, 2x) and two QA renders of the box at Jangan (1280 x 720, 1x,

one translation to the pixel (median abs difference 0.33 / 0.00 / 0.00 levels for the two PNGs, 4.7

**What changed (client).**

The user: "fix the map for dungeons. You should be able to click the dungeon and open up the

2a5794b72c90908d945be8b3f3f2edd4), MEASURED (the retail archive on the render box, nothing

  floor). A press records the link of the first picture sign under the mouse
  (+0x9800, 0x6232e4), the release opens it if the first picture sign under the mouse has the same
  link: up to 2000 a local map (0x622b60(1, id)), above 2000 a dungeon floor (0x6217e0), never a
  fortress (0x6238e2); then the view centres (0x61cc30).

  `(bottom-92)*192 .. ((top-92)*3+3)*64`; the floor spinner (record 4) set to the row's floor and
  shown when the dungeon has more than one; the floor's own signs; the caption 0x6145e0 -- the zone

  shown, which goes back (0x6231e0). Columns 1 and 2 of the `Dungeonmap` row (the dungeon's name and

  whose floor label is the text of the player's floor name (0x623060 -> 0x614280 -> 0x612920). The
  arrow is `px = (x/10 + (count_x/2)*192 - (maxX-minX)) / upp_x + draw_x`,
  `py = draw_y - ((0x80-92)*192 + z/10 - minY) / upp_y` of the `.dof`-space position (0x60f660),

  field point from `worldmap_instanceinfo.txt` (0x60fa90; loader 0x9536a0 expands each row's

## Seven-hundred-and-seventy-fourth round: dungeon fog, light maps, ambient effects, walk-in glows

The user, with retail and OpenSRO screenshots of the tomb's B1: "Some teleporters have glowing
effects like Jangan but I can't see it so it makes it hard finding where the teleporter is, fix
that. Additionally it looks super foggy in the dungeon. ... please check the original code to
verify and match exactly. Also the original game has a bunch of pretty lighting around, please
support all of that and fix the lighting and coloring." Then a frame of B1 fogged solid past
about 1,000 units.

**What was wrong (READ; docs/protocol/dungeon.md section 3 has the addresses).**
- **The fog.** Round 773 drew the block record's start/end (-200 .. 1000) as linear fog. In a
  dungeon the landscape step sets no table fog and the object shader's EXP variant
  (`Map::FUN_00a26f60` 0xa27722); `Shader\vss0.c` (Data.pk2, assembly text) computes
  `2^-((z x density)^2)` (base-2 `exp`), min'd with the height term
  `1 - A3 (|y - A0| - A1) / A2` from the block's A record (`vslot_015` 0xbeec30: four floats, c22).
  Start and end are never used. The frame clears to the fog colour, not black.
- **The light.** Rooms are light-mapped: `.bms` flag 0x400 at 0x40 = 52-byte vertices with the
  light map's coordinates at 0x20, and the light map's file after the vertex array
  (`CPrimMesh::FUN_00c1bb20`); `FUN_00bf1250` draws stage 0 MODULATE, stage 1 MODULATE2X of the
  light map. Round 773 drew only the flat block ambient (the purple wash).
- **The glows and lamps.** Every dungeon room and object `.bsr` carries an `ambient` particle set:
  the portals (`system\system_dungeonpotal.efp`), flames, lanterns, crystals, sunbeams (MEASURED:
  every object of the served dungeons; `dump_bsr_particles.gd --ambient-index`, new). Only the
  town gates played theirs. The cave's `lamp.bsr` / `404_sunbeams.bsr` have empty mesh and
  material lists and BsrReader refused them (the "64 lamp.bsr build nothing" of round 773).
- **The field walk-ins.** `w_cd_dondunenter.bsr` (the cave's mouth; its portal effect 1,056 from
  its origin) and `cj_jin_entdoor01_01.bsr` (the tomb's door) carry the portal effect but have no
  teleportbuilding row, so nothing matched them.

**What changed.**
- `WorldFog`: a dungeon mode (`set_dungeon_globals`, `srr_fog_height`), the READ formula in the
  pass and in the self-fogged shaders; the pass paints empty pixels the fog colour in a dungeon.
  OURS: per pixel with the current block's record (the original: per vertex, per block).
- `BmsReader.lightmap_path` / `lightmap_uvs`, `ObjectLoader._prepare_lightmap` /
  `_commit_lightmap`, object.gdshaderinc's `LIGHTMAP` variant. By the mesh's flag, so the field's
  1,133 light-mapped building meshes (Jangan, Donwhang, Hotan, ...) are light-mapped too, as the
  draw path READ does it; `OPENSRO_QA_NOLIGHTMAP=1` for the A/B.
- `World3D._attach_dungeon_effects`: every room's and object's ambient set; OURS: the 400 nearest
  the camera run, re-chosen every 250 ms, stepped as one batch (`EfpSimBatch`, native sims,
  `EfpEffect.static_host` skips re-placement); `AmbientParticles.update` skips hidden effects'
  glows. `BsrReader._empty_table` keeps effect-only objects.
- `ObjectStringReader` (navmesh\objectstring.ifo) and `World3D._walk_in_pairs_around`: a walk-in
  centre (an objectstring point named after a teleportdata codename) pairs the object one of whose
  ambient entries stands within 30 of it. `TeleportReader.point_by_code`.
- `DofReader.Block.height_fog` (the A record).
- QA: `OPENSRO_QA_PIXEL_RAYS`, `OPENSRO_QA_DUNGEON_FX`, `OPENSRO_QA_NOLIGHTMAP`.

**Verification (render box).**
- Tomb B1 at the user's spot by the B1 -> B2 portal (dungeon (-250, 6450)), radius 1: the hall's
  far end blue and misty with the statue's silhouette, the rows of lamps lit, the portal ring
  glowing; the near floor reads (29, 30, 74) against the user's retail frame's (54, 58, 93) --
  OPEN: the original's bloom in a dungeon was not read; their client's own settings unknown.
- `QA PIXEL` rays: the B1 shapes round 773 drew black are walls 8,800-10,500 away, past the QA
  run's 7,680 far plane, over the clear colour; they now show the fog colour.
- Field: `gate GATE_JINSI_OUT -- Obj_cj_jin_entdoor01_01_45 ... at 2.7 from its walk-in centre`,
  `gate GATE_DUNGEON_DH_IN -- Obj_w_cd_dondunenter_0 ... at 0.8`; both glows render.
- Jangan with and without light maps: the palace's door recesses and the railings' undersides
  darken; nothing else changes.
- Cost, tomb B2 (4,216 effects, the densest): p95 work frame 2 ms with no ambient effect, 12 ms
  with 400 effects in their own `_process`, 7 ms after the batch, the native sims, the static

| site | frame ms | entry ms | freeze ms | hitches |

## Seven-hundred-and-seventy-first round: V hides the whole crowd

The user: "When I press "V" almost all characters don't seem to disappear, maybe a few but all of the
names go away. All characters, pets, transports, and monsters need to disappear. Check the game code
on what it exactly does and implement it properly."
- **The original (READ):**
  - While V is held (`DAT_00eef5f4`, only three readers), the predicate `0x9d0560` fails these
    objects:
    - other players (exactly `CICUser`);
    - monsters, `CICMonsterNPC` and `CICRide`;
    - every COS but the ridden one.
  - The character's draw `0x9d20d0` then skips that object's body (`0x9c4aa0`), its attachments
    (`+0x288`) and its name (`0x9d0a80`).
  - Its vslot `0x50` (`0x9d11c0`) makes it unpickable. `CICUser::vslot_010` skips the stall booth.
  - The minimap's sign loop (`0x662bd0`) and the target window ask vslot `0x54` (`0x9c75a0`), which has
    no V test, so both keep a hidden object. Round 608 left the minimap as OPEN.
  - The selection ring on a hidden target is cleared for good (`CIODecal::vslot_009`, round 698).
- **The cause:** round 608 hid the holders of `_other_bodies` and `_monster_bodies`. Since the crowd
  rounds (737-764) every other player past the 16 nearest is drawn by CrowdGpu's MultiMeshes, which
  never read a holder's visibility, so they stayed. The ghosts' weapon effects (EquipFxBatch) stayed
  too. The names went, because the plate batch does read the holder.
- **The fix:**
  - `CrowdGpu.set_hidden`: every group's layer mask is set to 0. This covers far bodies, ghosts and
    departures fading on the GPU.
  - `EquipFx.ghosts_hidden` / `EquipFxBatch.set_ghosts_hidden`: natively, the ghost tables are sent
    empty; in the fallback, the draws are zeroed.
  - Departing players and monsters are hidden too (`_departing_bodies`); only what V hid is shown
    again.
  - A body made while V is held starts hidden.
- **MEASURED** (400 swarm bodies at the Jangan spawn, `OPENSRO_QA_INPUT` holding V; the renderer's
  own counts five frames on):

  | V | objects | primitives | draw calls | crowd groups masked off |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | held | 1,254 | 608,920 | 761 | 1,321 of 1,321 |
  | released | 2,580 | 2,677,188 | 2,087 | 0 |

  The frames show the plaza empty with V held, the NPC stall and the player kept.
- **Not drawn by this client, so not touched:** pets, COS, rides and stalls.
- **Test:** `scripts/world/hide_objects_test.gd`.

## Seven-hundred-and-seventieth round: monster drops carry blue options

A monster's equipment drop now gets blue options the way SR_GameServer.exe's `_AddMagicOptions`
(0x7276a0) gives them (`docs/protocol/magic_options.md`, "Drops"):
- **The rules:** 31 in 101 drops, and every Seal item (Rarity 2); the count is the least of four
  1-6 draws, capped by column 158.
- **The option list:** the item kind's `magicoptionassign.txt` row, '+' options only.
- **Each option:** its level by the weighted roll over the option's rows, then its value from the
  record's generator.
- **New data:**
  - `export-refdata -mode magicoptassign` and `-magic-option-assign-csv` (74 rows);
  - the magic option export gains the Sign column and drops Service 0 rows, as the server's loader
    does;
  - items gain Rarity (column 87).
- **Correction to round 768:** the range generator truncates (the x87 chop mode at 0x72fcbb); it did
  not round.
- **OPEN:** which level a STR-type option drops at. Every level has probability 1, so the first
  row loaded wins, and the server loads in database order. This build takes `magicoption.txt`'s order
  (level 7 for STR, INFERRED); id order would be level 1. The answer is in the shard backup on the box,
  which holds player data and was not read without the user's approval.
- **Not built:** the drop's plus (`_RefDropOptLvlSel`, server-only; its distribution is recorded)
  and the special drop tables.
- **OURS:** the options are rolled at pick-up, where OpenSRO creates the drop's instance.
- **Tests:** `drop_test.go` (the chance, the first row of an equal group, the weighted levels, the
  wasted draws, '+' only) and `dropoptions770_test.go` (a Seal sword picked up with its STR).

## Seven-hundred-and-sixty-ninth round: a worn item's plus and blue options count

Round 768 made the plus and the blue options something a player can change. Neither moved a stat:
`OptLevel` reached no formula, and no option was aggregated. Both are wired now, each rule READ
from SR_GameServer.exe (`docs/protocol/item_magic_options.md`, "Round 769"):
- **The plus:** `Inc * plus` on each white stat before anything rounds. Itemdata columns 67, 70,
  73, 78, 81, 99, 104 and 115 are exported as item columns 79-86. Physical and magical attack take
  it on both ends, and so do the defences. MEASURED: parry and attack rate have no increment in
  retail data.
- **The effective plus:** OptLevel, the advanced elixir, and a 'rein' option.
- **Str and Int:** each is the total, the character's own plus its worn options. It feeds the
  damage ranges, the panel and max HP/MP; flat 'hp' / 'mp' are added after the level growth
  (`character.Bonus`, cached and cleared when the worn items change).
- **Critical and block:** `round(white) + 'cri' / 'bri'`. The weapon's critical now reads its
  variance group 6, where it used to read the low end.
- **Hit rate and parry:** 'hr' / 'er' scale them by `(1 + v/100)` after the plus.
- **Evasion:** 'evcr' / 'evbl' are the player's evasion terms. The four disclosed zeros of round 406
  are gone, and `TestNoPlayerEvasionSourceExists` retired as its own text asked.
- **Side finding:** `stat_graph.md`'s params 58/59 come from the worn armour's PDStr/MDInt, not from
  characterdata.
- **Tests:** `equipstats769_test.go`:
  - a +3 sword with STR / crit / attack rate options, a +2 mail with parry / HP options, and a
    shield with block / evade crit;
  - the critical through group 6, a 'rein' option, a broken piece, 'int' / 'mp' / 'evbl', and the
    magical defence's plus;
  - a failed bonus read is not cached;
  - the unequip handler clamps the HP.
- **Review:** `docs/rounds/r769_review.md`. Every finding was taken:
  - the SQL refills (level-up, respawn) carry the bonus;
  - the stored HP is clamped when a lower max leaves it above (unequip, swap, break, the GM edits);
  - a failed read is not cached;
  - potions, `/level` and the lobby use the totals;
  - the evasion sums are cached in the bonus, and its lock is read-mostly;
  - critical and block sum every worn item's option;
  - the panel shows a broken weapon as bare hands.
- **Deploy:** re-export and re-import the items (columns 79-86), and keep `-magic-options-csv`
  set.
- **Not built:** the absorbs (params 7/8), the regeneration / resist / avatar options, and 'hpna'.

## Seven-hundred-and-sixty-seventh round: seal effects on the character select screen again

The user: the seal effects are not visible on the character select screen any more.
- **Reproduced on the box** (RX 7600, Forward+). Three QA characters each carried a seal sword:
  `OPENSRO_QA_FAKECHARS=3` with the new QA hook `OPENSRO_QA_FAKECHARS_WEAPON=4014`
  (ITEM_CH_SWORD_01_A_RARE). Their purple `system_raretype_a_step1.efp` particles:
  - with the native library (the user's client): none;
  - without it: all three.
- **The cause** (round 764's review F1, commit d29f3b40):
  - World3D's `_ready` set `EquipFx.batch_viewport` to its viewport unconditionally.
  - The select and customize screens' harbour is a World3D in title mode (round 678). It shares
    the root viewport with the select stage's characters.
  - So with the native library, every dressed character's effect host there was registered with
    the batches (`EquipFx._batching_dressed`). The batches step only with a CrowdGpu
    (`EquipFxBatch.step` returns at once when it has none), and a backdrop has none.

The user: "make it available everywhere". Round 765's star now shows on every slot this client

    `ItemSealEdge.copy_phase` gives it the slot's counter and timer.

## Seven-hundred-and-sixty-fifth round: the seal star round an item slot (icon_edge_rare.ddj)

The user asked for the "Seal of *" icon effect, a star running round the slot (their gif
`UK9786Q.gif`), replicating the original's code. The full notes are in
`docs/protocol/item_seal_edge.md`.
- **READ: it is a sprite sheet stepped by a timer, not a moving sprite.**
  - The art: `CIFSlotWithHelp` loads `icon\item\etc\icon_edge_rare.ddj` (`0x66b460`, +0x63c).
  - The start: SetItem (`0x6871d0`) calls `0x666610` for an item passing `0x8ba600` (Rarity 2 or
    6) that came off the wire (SOItem +0x28) or sits in a buy-back slot (kind 0x45).
    `0x666610` sets the counter to `rand() & 31` and starts timer 3 at 40 ms.
  - The step: `vslot_005` counts 32 down to 1 and wraps.
  - The draw: `0x67cfb0` draws cell `32 - counter` (8 x 4 grid; UV doubles 32, 1/256, 1/128)
    over the slot's own quad, after the icon and before the count.
- **MEASURED:**
  - The sheet is a 256 x 128 DXT3. Its per-cell alpha centroids trace the orbit: top-left, down
    the left, along the bottom, faint up the right and across the top. That matches the gif.
  - The timer list (`0xb933d0`) fires once a tick when 40 ms have passed, then restarts from that
    tick. At 60 Hz our client steps every 48-51 ms. The gif's lap is 1,440 ms / 32 = 45 ms a step.
- **Client:** `ItemSealEdge` is a child of the slot's `ItemIcon`. It is on the bag, worn,
  warehouse and buy-back slots.
- **OURS:**
  - a refill of the same item keeps its phase (HudPanels refills whole windows);
  - a hidden edge does not tick;
  - the edge inherits a broken item's grey.
- **OPEN:**
  - the NPC store's goods and the quick slots (`+0x28` not read for either);
  - the slots not yet built (exchange, guild storage, stall, alchemy);
  - `+0x64c`.
- **Gates:** `check` ALL LOAD (710 scripts); `tests` "ran 271 suite(s), 0 failing", without the
  native library. This is a UI-only round, so no perf gate. `tools/seal_edge_frames.gd` drew a
  real seal sword (ITEM_CH_SWORD_01_A_RARE, id 4014) on the RX 7600 (Forward+) for a human to

## Seven-hundred-and-sixty-third round: EquipFx's effect simulation in Rust, with no global particle cap

The full notes are in `docs/rounds/r763.md`; the review is `r763_review.md`, and its fixes are in §9.
- **Rust:** `SrEfpSim` and `SrEfpBatch` (`native/src/core/efp_*.rs`, `gd_efp.rs`) step EquipFx's masters
  with Godot-exact f32 maths and RNG. They write the MultiMesh buffer and links directly.
  `EfpSimNative` is the GDScript side.
  - Without the library, or with an old one, the client falls back to `EfpSim`.
  - `OPENSRO_EFP_NATIVE=0` turns native off.
- **Parity (MEASURED):** bit-exact on Linux over 420k sim-frames. The Windows (mingw) build may
  differ in the last digit of sin/cos. That is cosmetic: never networked, never mixed.
- **USER DECISION 2026-10-09:** native masters have no global cap. The per-effect 300 remains, so the
  worst case is files x 300. The GDScript fallback and other effects keep 2,000.
- **Threads:**
  - The pool is min(4, cores, setting) and the main thread takes part (`OPENSRO_EFP_THREADS`).
  - Batches under 4,000 particle-steps run inline (`OPENSRO_EFP_POOL_MIN_WORK`), because helpers
    preempted on a busy machine cost 1-3.6 ms against a 0.08 ms gain.
- **Crash safety (review M1):**
  - Every step runs under `catch_unwind`, and poisoned locks are recovered.
  - A panic returns an error, and the client drops to GDScript for the session.
  - The review also fixed duplicate sims, the refusal loop, interval 0, mixed batches and the
    retained job (L1-L6).
- **MEASURED:**
  - EquipFx went from 3.7-4.5 ms to about 1.7 ms a frame.
  - Swarm 4,000 standing: 2,317 particles uncapped, frame 11.1 ms, p95 15.3-15.6 ms, GPU-bound.
  - perf_gate jangan: SAME.

## Seven-hundred-and-forty-eighth round: crowd scale, async templates and the const-array thread race (lane B)

The full notes are in `docs/rounds/r748.md`; the review is `r748_review.md`.
- **Template builds off the main thread:** body and item templates are built on WorkerThreadPool
  tasks (at most 2), on bones-only scratch skeletons, and adopted onto the layout's shared skin.
  The dressing pump follows the frame (`HITCH_TARGET_USEC` 90 ms, OURS).
- **The crash the review found (READ, Godot 4.2.2):**
  - GDScript `const` arrays are read-only. Reading an element copies it into one shared slot
    (`array.cpp:84-98`), so a worker and the main thread reading one const array race unlocked
    and corrupt the heap.
  - Measured: 18 of 19 stress runs crashed.
  - Fixed: 25 constants in worker-reachable code became `static var`, some already in released
    builds (`IDLE_ANIMATION_HINTS`, `VERTEX_REC_SIZE_CANDIDATES`, the inflate tables, and others).
  - A lint suite (`const_array_lint_test.gd`, 61 scripts) keeps it out.
  - After the fix: 5 x 300 s stress runs, 0 crashes.
- **Other fixes:**
  - EquipFx keeps one master per effect file. Every weapon showing a file shows the same particles
    at the same moment (OURS, disclosed).
  - The driver runs after the player's pose.
  - Templates and efp waits are never stranded.
  - A freed-weapon guard.
- **`FrameSplit`** (QA): READ, `TIME_PROCESS` includes the render.

  layer (round 744's SolidPlanes, not a placed object), only the flat quad is drawn, at the
  point's height + 0.1. Ordinary water and ground are unchanged.

  suite(s), 0 failing". No render (the user tests it live).

## Seven-hundred-and-forty-third round: every value-moving action is one Postgres transaction (M1; the trade dupe)

    advisory lock;

## Seven-hundred-and-forty-fourth round: standing on Karakoram's frozen lake -- the .nvm floor plane

The full notes are in `docs/rounds/r744.md`; the rule is in `docs/protocol/NVM_FORMAT.md`
("PlaneTypeMap: bit 1 is a floor").
- **The bug:** the player walked through the ice of "Karakoram Ancient Remains" (regions
  88-92 / 124-130, ice at height 800; `/goto hotan` then `/tp -15360 3840` is 90/127 local
  960, 960). Our walk took its ground from the heightmap alone, which is the lakebed, 260-300
  units under the ice. The heightmaps themselves are right (`.nvm` = `.m` on all 9,409 vertices
  checked).
- **The original's rule (READ):** `CRTNavMeshTerrain::vslot_001` (0x004051b0) interpolates the
  heightmap, then tests `PlaneTypeMap[row*6+col] & 2` (0x405319) for the 320-unit block. When
  the bit is set and the block's plane height is above the ground, the plane height wins
  (0x405333-0x405347).
- **Census (MEASURED, all 4,704 regions):** the bit is set on exactly 955 still-surface blocks
  (type 3: 844; type 2: 111, which are not drawn). Ordinary water, type 1 (35,045 blocks), stays
  wadeable.
- **Fix:**
  - `NvmCollision.terrain_height` is used everywhere `sample_height` was: the walk, landing,
    Ghost Walk, QA.
  - One two-sided 320x320 collision quad per floor block (`SolidPlanes`), so clicks, the camera
    and monster placement stop at the ice. That the click ray hits the ice is OURS.
  - The server has no navmesh and takes positions from the client, so it is unchanged.
- **Tests:** `nvm_collision_test` `_solid_planes` and `nav_graph_test` `_walk_on_the_ice`. With
  the old height function swapped back in, the walk test fails 5 times at y 505.81.
- **Gates:** box check ALL LOAD; tests "ran 245 suite(s), 0 failing". No render or perf gate (the
  user tests it live; the added cost is one small collision shape per ice region).

  A flag-0 type draws **without** the alpha test. That is READ: `FUN_00bf0e20` runs the mod before
  `FUN_00c42a60`, which skips the item's test when `0x20000000` is set. The `0x80000000` bit binds
  the item texture to stage 1 (`0xbf10ce`, closes OPEN 9).
- **Particles from +8:** rows with min ≤ plus ≤ max on the row's bone, scale col3/100 × the body's
  height factor. They are drawn by `EquipFx`, one shared simulation per (efp, scale), with holders
  at the bones. Its limits are all OURS:
  - the nearest 64 weapons in view within 800, re-chosen over 10 frames;
  - always shown within 30 units;
  - every weapon in step, and the followers don't turn with the weapon.
  
  `CEFEffect::vslot_010`'s factor at `*(this+4)+0x264` is OPEN, not applied.
- **Every dressed view glows:** the world, other players, character select (its list's plus, READ
  `FUN_0085a580`), the equipment window and the portrait. The last three keep the glow and the
  item's alpha test after the review's F1, which MEASURED `alpha_ref` 0.502 where it had been 0.
- **Seals:** no seal-specific effect exists in the data (round 733, MEASURED). Per the user's
  decision "follow the data", none was invented.

## Seven-hundred-and-thirty-second round: item instance data (tooltip epic, lane B)

Each item's own data — plus, white-stat variance, durability, blue options, advanced elixir — is
stored on the server and sent to the client in the original's item record. The "(+x%)" maths and
the blue-option formats are read from the client and exposed for lane A (round 731), which owns the
tooltip window and its line composition. Marks: **READ** (from the binary), **INFERRED**, **OURS**,
**OPEN**.

### The item record (READ, client `SOItem::FUN_008be4f0`, equipment branch TypeID 3/1; server writer `gs:CInstanceItem::vslot_010` 0x42e230)

| Field | Wire | Item field | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| Rent block | u32; bit 0 adds u16, u32, u32 (period), bit 1 adds u16, u32 | | c:0x8bb130 at 0x8be52c; gs:0x845b30 writes 0 when there is no rent object (gs:0x862960). **Added after the review (F1).** |
| RefItemID | u32 | +0x34 | 0x8be549; gs:0x4958c0 |
| OptLevel (the plus) | u8 | +0x8c | 0x8be647; setter 0x8ba4e0 |
| Variance | u64, twelve 5-bit groups | +0x90 | 0x8be657; setter 0x8ba4f0 |
| Durability | u32 | +0x98 | 0x8be667; getter 0x8ba4a0. For TypeID3 14 (time-limited gear) this word is the period `active<<31 \| seconds` (c:0x8be600, gs:0x42fd30) |
| MagParamNum | u8, ≤ 12 | | 0x8bcdf0 assert `m_btMagicParamNum <= MAX_MAGPARAM_PER_ITEM`; server gs:0x459d30 |
| MagParam × N | u64: low u16 magicoption id, high u32 value | | 0x8bcdf0; gs Item_DecodeMagicOption 0x4904f2 |
| Binding block × 2 | u8 type, u8 count, count × entry; type 1 then type 2 | | gs:0x846280 writes the order; c:0x8bb070 reads exactly two |
| — entry | u8 nSlot, u64: low u32 `nOptID \| nOptLvl<<16`, high u32 nOptValue (type 2) or nParam1 (type 1) | | gs:CInstanceBindingOptionWithItem::vslot_009 0x825a40; columns from gs:0x85e4e0 |
| — type 1 (socket) | | slot id/value at +0x74/+0x78 | 0x8bb070 |
| — type 2 (advanced elixir) | the high u32's low byte | u8-added onto +0x8c, kept at +0x71 | 0x8bb070 |

The layout is READ; these values are OURS:
- The rent word is 0, because OpenSRO has no rentals.
- A time-limited item's period word is 0, the original's "not active" form, because OpenSRO has no
  expiry.
- The advanced-elixir entry's nSlot, nOptID and nOptLvl are 0, because the elixir's option row is
  not modelled yet.
- There are no sockets.
- An untracked durability goes out as the variance's max.

Only equipment is listed. The COS and stackable records are not sent (OPEN).

### Where it travels (OURS container, retail record)

The bag list, the bag move reply, the warehouse list and the equipment list are OpenSRO's own
messages. Each gains a trailing block, **u16 count, then per entry a u32 container slot and the
record**:
- The bag and warehouse lists (`StorageListResult`) carry it after the capacity u16.
- The equipment list (`EquipmentResult`) carries it after the durability block.

An older client stops reading before the block.

**Frame limit (review F8).** A full warehouse is 210 slots of equipment, each with 12 options and an
advanced elixir. That does not fit one frame (`proto.MaxPayload` 32,767): the list carries 199
entries in 32,755 bytes. The other 11 follow in **`OpItemInfoMore` 0x00FB** (OURS; 0x00FB was free on
both sides). Its payload is a u8 container (0 bag, 1 worn, 2 warehouse), then the same block, in as
many frames as needed (`TestWorstCaseStorageListSplits`). The bag (at most 100 slots) and the worn
slots always fit. `fitItemInfos` guards every list, so the list itself is never lost.

### Storage (OURS schema)

- Columns `opt_level SMALLINT`, `mag_params BYTEA` (8 bytes LE each) and `adv_elixir SMALLINT` were
  added to `inventory_slots`, `account_storage_slots` and `equipment_slots`.
- They are added by `ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS` with defaults, so existing rows read +0 with no
  options.
- `inventory.Instance` carries the new fields, and every move path copies them: split, swap, equip
  and unequip, deposit and withdraw, buy back, trade and ground.
- Steps are in `deploy/README.md`.

### GM hooks (OURS)

- `/give <id> [qty] [plus]` names the bag slots it filled.
- `/item <slot> plus <n> | var <u64> | quality <0-31> | opt <id> <value> | adv <n> | clear`.
- Magic-option rolling on drops is not built.

### The (+x%) (READ, `0x66c5b0` + its x87, `0x8bd980`)

The effective plus is +0x8c (with the advanced elixir) plus the byte at +0x70. The writer of +0x70
is OPEN, and the stat builder adds it only when ref+0x1d4 ≠ 0.

- **Whole-number stats** (attack, hit, parry, block, critical): `trunc((U−L)·q/31.0 + L +
  trunc(inc·plus))` (0x8bdb75). Durability uses the same formula with no plus term (0x8bdfdc).
- **Fractional stats:** `plus·inc + q/31·(U−L) + L`, stored as a float. The reinforce stats carry
  no plus term.
- **Range line (attack):** each end is `f = (v − TRUNC(inc·plus) − L)/(U−L)` as a float, or 1 if
  U = L. The percent is `trunc((f_lo + f_hi) × 0.5 × 100)`:
  - 0.5 and 100.0 are at 0xe1b7d0/d8.
  - The truncation is `cvttsd2si` (FUN_00b42d10).
  - The spec's "ROUND" is a fistp under a control word or'd with 0xc00, which **truncates**.
  - This settles spec OPEN 8: **both** ends are averaged.
- **Reinforce range:** the same average, with no plus off.
- **Single line:** `trunc((v − inc·plus − L)/(U−L)·100)`, or 100 if U = L.
  - The plus comes off only for phys/mag defence and absorption (inc ref +0x1e8/+0x214/+0x200/+0x220).
  - Hit, parry, critical, block and reinforce pass plus 0, although hit's stat includes a plus term.
- **Durability:** `trunc(q / 0.31)`, where q is the byte at item +0x137 (0x8bd980 case 0). The
  divisor is the double at 0xda1aa0, 0.3100000023841858. **A perfect 31 shows 99%.**
- **Variance groups per kind** (0x8bd980):

  | Kind | 0 | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 |
  |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
  | Weapon | durability | phys reinforce | mag reinforce | hit | phys attack | mag attack | critical |
  | Armour | durability | phys reinforce | mag reinforce | phys def | mag def | parry | |
  | Shield | durability | phys reinforce | mag reinforce | block | phys def | mag def | |
  | Accessory | phys absorption | mag absorption | | | | | |

### Blue options (READ `0x670dd0`)

- **Percent:** `max(0, trunc((value − min)/(max − min)·100))`.
  - min is the high u16 of the row's first range word.
  - max is the last non-zero u16, walking hi, lo, hi, lo… through 3 words.
  - Those words are magicoption.txt columns 8..10, READ from the row parser
    `RefParse_magicoption` (c:0x97b0b0) per review F6. Example: ER degree 10 reads 5, 10, 20, 30,
    40, 60.
  - An empty range shows (+0%): the division is unguarded and the clamp turns the inf or NaN into 0
    (review F5).
- **Row selection (READ, review F6):** the row's degree is compared with `(ItemClass−1)/3+1`,
  where ItemClass is ref +0x1d0. When they differ, the client takes min and max from the same
  MATTR code at that degree (`0x926b30`, c:0x670ebd). This is `MagicOptionTable.range_row` and
  `option_pct`.
- **Formats:** per MATTR code, in `MagicOptionTable.FORMATS`.
  - The sprintf string arguments are the keys in **reverse fetch order**. That rule is checked on
    "HP/MP recovery … Increase" and "Steady(1Time/times)".
  - The reinforce timer, 3rd-job, avatar and Nasrun formats are OPEN.

### Client API for lane A

| Call | Gives |
|---|---|
| `net_client.last_inventory_instances` / `last_equipment_instances` / `last_storage_instances` | `{slot: ItemInstance}` |
| `ItemInstance` | `opt_level`, `adv_elixir`, `effective_plus()`, `variance`, `variance_group(k)`, `durability`, `option_count()`, `option_id(i)`, `option_value(i)` |
| `ItemQuality.int_stat(L,U,q,inc,plus)` / `float_stat(...)` | the instance stat |
| `ItemQuality.range_int_pct(vLo,vHi,Llo,Ulo,Lhi,Uhi,inc,plus)` / `range_float_pct(...)` / `single_pct(v,L,U,inc,plus)` / `durability_pct(q)` | the (+x%) |
| `ItemQuality.group_for(kind, stat)` | the variance group a stat reads |
| `MagicOptionTable.shared.row(id)`; `.option_pct(id, value, item_class)` | the magicoption row; the blue (+x%), from the row at the item's degree (ItemClass = ref +0x1d0) |
| `MagicOptionTable.format_line(row.code, value, pct, MagicOptionTable.shared_text)` | the blue line |

Lane A's reader still needs the U ends and per-plus increments: itemdata 96/98/99 and so on, as
`server/cmd/export-refdata` documents.

| F3 | Time-limited gear (TypeID3 14) was sent durability | It now sends the period word `active<<31 \| seconds` as 0, the original's "not active" form (gs:0x42fd30; OURS value, since OpenSRO has no expiry). Test: `TestTimeLimitedGearSendsThePeriodWord`. |
| F4 | GD summed the advanced elixir's whole u32 | Now `& 0xff` with a u8 wrap, as c:0x8bb070 does (GD test: 200 + 100 gives 44). The Go reader already matched. |

The overflow goes in the new `OpItemInfoMore` 0x00FB (OURS), and `fitItemInfos` guards every list. The client merges it (`net_client.gd`). Test: `TestWorstCaseStorageListSplits`. |

## Seven-hundred-and-thirty-first round: the item tooltip, lane A (the window and its lines)

Builds `docs/protocol/item_tooltip.md` lane A. Every item tooltip is now the original's
CNIFHelperBubbleWindow drawn in the HUD's own canvas, replacing Godot's `tooltip_text` popup (which
was blurry at DPI 2.0). Its lines are composed in the binary's order. Labels: **READ**,
**MEASURED**, **INFERRED**, **OURS**, **OPEN**.

### What was built

- **`ItemTooltipBubble`** (`client/scripts/ui/hud/item_tooltip_bubble.gd`), the window:
  - **Frame:** `com_tooltip_corner.ddj` is the top-left corner, mirrored for the other three. `com_tooltip_edge.ddj` is the left edge, mirrored for the right and turned for the top and bottom (orientation MEASURED from the texels).
  - **Lines:** 18 px apart, or 14 for a one-line box (READ, `0x496c90`). The width is the widest line plus the 8-px frame.
  - **Text:** in the client's face at 12 px through round 672's crisp path (NEAREST), with a black drop shadow at (+1, +1) (MEASURED: 3,336 of 3,336 shadow neighbours in `XjjJyA5.png` are black).
  - **Name icon:** `com_itemsign.ddj`. The name is padded past it by ceil(12 / space) + 1 spaces (READ, `0x776d20`).
  - **Font 3** (name, seal, set, adv. elixir) is the same face with 2-px stems (MEASURED: same 9-row cap height). It is drawn with FontVariation embolden 1.4 (OURS).
  - **Alpha:** frame and fill at 200/255 (MEASURED 0.77–0.78 from three texels over known ground; the byte at `+0x131` is not read). The text is opaque.
  - **Placement:** right of the slot, top aligned (MEASURED, one screenshot). The clamp to the screen is OURS. The frame is NEAREST-filtered (OURS).
- **`ItemTooltipLines`**, the composition: the four equipment builders' skeleton, keys and colours of the spec, plus:
  - **Order (USER DECISION, binary order):** re-checked. `0x776d20` → `FUN_0064f8a0` appends each line at the list's end. The font argument (record `+0x24`) goes to `FUN_008b4400(5, font)`, which sets the line's font in all four style slots; it is not a section key. Nothing re-orders, so seal and set sit directly under the name.
  - **Advanced elixir:** "Able to use Advanced elixir." is **grey `0xffc8c8c8`**, bold (READ, `0x66fd60`). The spec said white.
  - **The Int line prints the Str requirement** (READ: `0x67eec0`'s `"%s %d"` with PARAM_INT reads ref `+0x1c8`). This is reproduced; the line's colour compares the player's Int.
  - **"(+x%)":**
    - A store's goods are reference items (variance 0): 0 %, or 100 % on an empty range. A min ~ max line averages its two ends, round 732's reading.
    - An owned item shows the instance's values and percentages when the server sent its record (round 732).
    - Without that record it shows no percentage (OURS: it would be invented).
  - **Other items** (consumables…): name, sort of item, requirements, price, in the same bubble. Their builders are not read (OURS, OPEN).
- **`ItemTypeNames`:**
  - **"Sort of item":** a group join, INFERRED (the review: the client's own lookup maps are unread, OPEN 8). `fmntidgroupmapdata.txt` (service, group, TypeID1–4; parser READ `0x6d5570`) is joined on its group to `fmncategorytreedata.txt`'s key column. The join is 1:1 over the archive's 138/72 rows (MEASURED).
  - **Set names:** `refsetitemgroup.txt` col 4 gives the key, which resolves in **`textdata_equip&skill.txt`**, not `textdata_object.txt`. `textdataname.txt` lists both files for the client (MEASURED): SN_ITEM_11_SET_A_WEAPON = "Power", the user's green line.
- **`ItemTooltipInstance`:** lane B's ItemInstance / ItemQuality / MagicOptionTable turned into the instance fields: plus = effective plus, stats, percentages, blue lines and adv. elixir.
  - It reaches those classes **by path**, because this branch could not merge lane B (the merge was refused by the session's permission check). The coordinator merges.
  - It was probed against lane B's real files in a scratch box copy. A +5 D11 spear at q = 31 read: "Phy. atk. pwr. 2113 ~ 2462 (+100%)", "Durability 90/103 (+99%)", "Critical 17 (+100%)".
  - Blue options whose format lane B lists as OPEN show "code value" (OURS stand-in).
- **Sites:** every item `tooltip_text` in `hud_panels.gd` goes through `_set_item_tip`: store (with price), buy back, storage, bag (with durability) and equipment. The equipment clear now clears the tooltip too.
  - There is no stall window in the client.
  - The hotbar never had an item tooltip; adding one needs World3D to pass the slot's item id (OPEN).
- **Columns** (both readers and `table_parity`): rarity 15, item class 61, set id 62, durability upper 64, ReqStr 59, ReqInt 60, max magic options 158, parry 68/69, absorption 71/72 and 79/80, per-plus increments 67/70/73/78/81/99/104/115, and the upper ends 96/98, 101/103, 106/108, 110/112, 114, 117. The old hard-coded English `Item.tooltip_lines` and `WEAPON_SORT` are removed.
- **QA hook:** `OPENSRO_QA_ITEM_TIP="<id>[:where[:cur/max[:price]]],..."` shows the bubbles side by side at tick 45 and logs `QA ITEM_TIP`.

## Seven-hundred-and-thirtieth round: item tooltips specified from the client (spec only)

The user asked (2026-10-05) for item descriptions like the original's: gold names for seal items, blue
for items with blue stats, legible text at DPI 2.0, and full descriptions; their necklace showed only
its name. This round is documentation only. The spec is `docs/protocol/item_tooltip.md`.

### Findings

- **The window** is `CNIFHelperBubbleWindow` (`0x496910`), built from `ifhelpbubblewindow.txt`.
  - It holds a text box, three 12x12 sign icons and an 8-px frame from `com_tooltip_corner.ddj` / `com_tooltip_edge.ddj`.
  - The frame's texels decode, from the outside in, to black, light blue (107,132,206) and a navy fill (25,33,66).
  - Line height is 18 (14 for a single line), and the width is the widest line.
- **Dispatch:** the equipment tooltip dispatches on TypeID3 (`0x685f20`). Armour, shields, accessories and weapons share one builder skeleton:
  1. the name;
  2. seal and set;
  3. Sort of item, armour position and degree;
  4. the stat block;
  5. requirements;
  6. max magic options;
  7. magic options;
  8. advanced elixir;
  9. prices.
  
  Every format and key is in the spec.
- **Colours:**
  - the name is gold `0xffffd953` for Rarity 2/6 seal items (pink `0xffff75f2` in a case not yet read), cyan `0xff00eaff` with magic options, white otherwise. The user's rule, now READ;
  - the labels are beige `0xffefdaa4`;
  - unmet requirements are red `0xffff4a4a`;
  - the set line is green `0xff6ce675`;
  - the magic options are cyan.
- **"(+x%)"** is (base − ref lower) / (ref upper − lower) × 100, with base being the instance stat minus the plus bonus.
- **Why ours is blurry at DPI 2.0 (INFERRED):** Godot's built-in `tooltip_text` popup is a separate viewport that root font oversampling doesn't reach, and it uses the default theme font.
- **Why the necklace is empty:** our `tooltip_lines` has no absorption, parry or blocking lines, no requirement block, and no max magic options. The item reader doesn't read those columns.
- **Server:** it stores variance and durability but no opt level, magic params or advanced-elixir count, and sends only durability.

### Open

- The seal and set order differs between this binary and the user's Esro screenshot; it needs reading, then possibly a user decision.
- The window alpha and placement, the rule drawing, the magic-option formats (`0x670dd0`), the non-equipment builders, the pink-seal test, and the retail instance layout. See the spec's OPEN list.

### Lanes

Lane A (client bubble and text) and lane B (instance data on the server and the wire); see the spec.

No separate review: the spec was checked area by area by the two implementation rounds' independent reviews, which corrected it in place. **USER DECISION 2026-10-05:** the line order follows the binary (seal and set lines under the name), not the Esro screenshot's.

## Seven-hundred-and-twenty-ninth round: building textures flickering as the camera moves -- the world camera's near plane is retail's 1.0

The user (2026-10-05): "certain textures in the game seem to flicker when I move or move the camera
... you can see the windows on building kind of glitching" (`/root/opensro-handoff/world_refs/
flicker_jEfh158.png`, an Alexandria house wall, native Linux build on RADV Navi33, Forward+,
3840x2004, far 11,520 in their log).

### The cause (MEASURED)

**The layers.** `tools/probe_coplanar.gd` reads a model's overlay meshes and, for each triangle,
the nearest parallel, overlapping structural triangle behind it. `alex_minga02` (the Alexandria
house in the user's view):

| overlay mesh | triangles over a structural face | separation min / median / max | against |
|---|---|---|---|
| `window` (grilles) | 30 / 54 | 0.0696 / 1.0090 / 1.7266 | wall02, wall03, wall08, wall01, wall07 |
| `window_alpha` | 20 / 20 | 0.2270 / 1.1469 / 1.2853 | wall02, wall03 |
| `dark` (insets) | 24 / 150 | 0.0099 / 1.0827 / 1.7121 | column02, inside03, column01 |
| `door01` | 16 / 139 | 0.0098 / 0.8815 / 1.8403 | column02, wall08, wall07 |
| `dark01`, `door02`, `door03` | none within 2.0 | | |

**The depth buffer.** OpenSRO's world camera kept Godot's default near plane, **0.05**; retail's is
**1.0** (READ, round 648: `fld1` in the camera constructor `FUN_00bae0a0`, never written again;
`docs/protocol/MAPM_FORMAT.md` "Depth"). With a standard-z depth buffer (Godot 4.2 has no reversed
z, which arrived in 4.3 -- INFERRED from the release history, not read in its source), the depth
step it can tell apart at view distance d is about d^2 x 2^-24 / near:

| layers apart | fight beyond, near 0.05 | fight beyond, near 1.0 (retail) |
|---|---|---|
| 1.0 (the median window) | ~920 units | ~4,100 units |
| 0.07 (the closest grille) | ~240 units | ~1,080 units |
| 0.01 (the closest inset/door) | ~90 units | ~410 units |

(d = sqrt(separation x near x 2^24): where the depth step reaches the layers' separation.) The
measured house stood about 955 units from the camera (`QA LOOK`, `Obj_alex_minga02_16`): there the
0.05 near cannot separate layers closer than ~1.09 units, which is almost every window, inset and
door layer above; the 1.0 near separates everything above ~0.054.

**The flicker, measured on one build** (`OPENSRO_QA_CAMERA_NEAR` sets the near for measurement
only). The view is region 90/48 at local (452, 864), yaw 90, pitch 4 (the house with the flower
boxes). Eight shots step the camera back 0.02 units at a time, which moves the building's edges by
about 0.004 px, so any pixel that changes is a depth decision flipping, not motion. The pixels
changing by more than 15 % between consecutive shots, inside the building's box (280 x 110 at
460, 195):

| near | per step | total over 7 steps |
|---|---|---|
| 0.05 (before) | 268, 440, 250, 294, 502, 296, 286 | **2,336** |
| 1.0 (after) | 26, 27, 21, 11, 12, 21, 9 | **127** |

The residue at 1.0 is the swaying flower boxes. The same camera rendered at both near planes differs
in 1,460-2,150 pixels, all on that house's balcony and window layers and on distant building edges.

**A negative, recorded:** the Jangan shop fronts (97/168 local (300, 1100), yaw 270) give the same
flip count at both near planes (38,966 vs 38,358 over the upper 420 rows, all animated things), so
that view has no fighting layers. A first 0.15-degree yaw sweep measured nothing either way, because
2 px of motion per step swamped it; the distance sweep replaced it.

### What the original does for coplanar layers (READ)

Nothing beyond its depth precision and draw order:
- **No depth bias.** A census of every immediate state passed to the render-state wrapper
  `FUN_00471360` (679 calls) finds ZENABLE, ZWRITEENABLE, ZFUNC, cull, blend, alpha test, fog,
  lighting, colour write and the rest, but never `D3DRS_DEPTHBIAS` (195) or
  `D3DRS_SLOPESCALEDEPTHBIAS` (175). The seven other `push 0xc3` sites in the image are UI and sound
  calls (`0x469020`, `0x468c50`, `0x65a390` with `ecx = 0x115dd40`), not render states. A state passed
  in a register is not covered by the census.
- **ZFUNC is LESSEQUAL.** Both ZFUNC writes (`0x9f4adc`, `0x9f514a`) set 4.
- **Near 1.0, far the view distance, a 24-bit depth buffer** (round 648, above).

### The fix

`CameraPlanes.NEAR = 1.0` (`client/scripts/world/camera_planes.gd`), set with the far plane in
`World3D._apply_camera_far_plane`. The water reflection and overlay cameras copy the main camera's
planes, so they follow. The cloud layer sits at z = w (round 628) and does not depend on the near
plane.

**Close geometry (the caveat round 648 left open).** The camera arm sweeps a radius-3 sphere with a
5-unit margin (`World3D.tscn`), so no collider reaches the near plane's corners: 1.39 / 1.54 / 1.60 /
1.77 units out at aspect 4:3 / 16:9 / the user's 1.92 / 21:9 (`camera_near_test.gd`). Rendered at the
minimum zoom (20) in seven tight Jangan views (the spawn at four headings, the gate, the shops, and a
camera looking up), the same camera at the two near planes differs in 0-536 of 921,600 pixels, all on
distant building edges. Nothing near the camera is clipped.

### Tests

- `client/scripts/world/camera_near_test.gd` (new): the near is 1.0, and the near plane's corners lie
  inside the arm's sphere at four aspects. ALL PASS.
- Box (`RENDER_DIR=/opt/opensro-client-r729`): `check` loads 621 scripts and 9 scenes; the full suite
  runs 238 suites, 0 failing.

### Perf gate

`client/tools/perf_gate.sh --sites jangan,reeds,cross --frames 12000`, base `d7af294b` vs the working
tree (`8f2e2525` plus these notes), 1280x720, Forward+ on the RX 7600, median of 3 runs: all SAME.

| site | frame ms | entry ms | freeze ms | hitches |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| jangan | 1.55 -> 1.53 | 9734 -> 9579 | 3357 -> 3385 | 5 -> 4 |
| reeds | 1.41 -> 1.41 | 7180 -> 7155 | 1994 -> 1991 | 2 -> 2 |
| cross | 1.71 -> 1.70 | 10653 -> 10463 | 3362 -> 3408 | 5 -> 4 |

### OPEN

- Whether Godot 4.2's depth attachment on RADV is D24 or D32F: either way it is standard z, and the
  precision rule above holds. Not read in Godot's source.
- Layers 0.01 apart (`dark`, `door01`) still fight beyond about 410 units, as they would in retail.
- Other models' overlay layers were not censused; `probe_coplanar.gd` takes any model folder
  (`--dir` with `|` for a space, `--model`, `--overlay`).

**Review** (coordinator, light at the user's request): the change is the camera's near plane 0.05 -> 1.0, READ in round 648 (`fld1` in `FUN_00bae0a0`); the flicker metric (2,336 -> 127 changed pixels on the user's house) and the close-geometry sweep are in the notes.

Perf gate (jangan, reeds, cross), all SAME -- the table is in the notes.

## Seven-hundred-and-twenty-eighth round: stack counts drawn as the original draws them, splitting a stack, buy back, and the warehouse deposit fee

NPC GUI epic. The user asked (2026-10-05) for buy back, splitting stacks and the storage deposit fee,
and for the stack count at the item's top left "like the original game". Their references are in
`/root/opensro-handoff/npc_refs/`: `qty_Pp886X3.png` (counts), `split_z4uFWIL.png` (the split
box), `3Gw7Ene.png` (the store's buy-back row) and `MKtR5Kd.png` (a deposit box showing price 1).
The tax line is left until fortress war is supported (the user's call).

### The stack count (READ; `client/scripts/ui/item_count_label.gd`)

- **Images, not a font.** `CIFSlotWithHelp::vslot_010` (0x66b460) loads
  `interface\item_number\item_number_%d.ddj`, ten 8x8 RGBA images. The glyph sits at the image's
  top-left and the image has a dark rim on its right and bottom. That rim is the "black border"
  the user saw.
- **Position.** `FUN_0067bd70` writes the count with `_itoa_s` and draws it from the last digit:
  - the first quad's left edge is `x0 - 2 + 4n`, and each next one is 5 px further left;
  - every digit is drawn at `y0 + 2`;
  - each quad spans (x - 0.5)..(x + 7.5), i.e. exactly 8x8 pixels.

  So the digits overlap by 3 px, and a 4-digit count starts 1 px left of the slot.
- **When.** `vslot_013` (0x685e50) draws the count only when `FUN_00680da0` holds: the item is an
  expendable (not bionic, TypeID1 3, TypeID2 3) and its stack is non-zero. A count of 1 is drawn
  too.
- **Square item slots are no longer clipped** (`UiBuilder._build_slot`). The clip cut off the
  first column of a 4-digit count. Row slots stay clipped.
- **Measured against `qty_Pp886X3.png`** (live run 2, frame `09_deposit_box`, bag slot 1 = 5000).
  - In both images the white glyph pixels of "5000" start **2 px left of the icon's light frame**
    and **1 px below its top row**.
  - The reference's rows 294-300 and ours, rows 234-240, are the same character strings, pixel
    for pixel.
  - In the reference, a 1-digit "9" starts at frame + 1, which is the 3 px the formula predicts
    between 1 and 4 digits.
  - The first run, with the clip still on, lost the '5's first column. That is how the clip was
    found.

### Splitting a stack (READ unless marked)

- **The trigger.** Shift+click on a bag stack (`CIFSlotWithHelp` click 0x681903 calls fill
  0x6b3fa0). It only opens for a stackable item (`0x538410`) with a count of 2 or more.
- **The box.** `CIFMessageBox` mode 5, `MsgBoxDivideCount` (`0x640020`), built as the
  inventory's one box (+0x390).
  - Size 300x183 (`push 0xb7; push 0x12c`), titled `UIIT_STT_INPUT_BOX` ("Input window").
  - Members: 11 icon, 12 name board, 15 retained count, 17 edit, 220 OK, 221 Cancel.
- **The fill.**
  - Retained count = the whole stack.
  - The edit's style is 3, its text "1" (`0xd87bdc`); it takes focus.
  - No minimum; the maximum is the stack - 1 (`0x634f20`).
  - The name goes on the board.
- **OK** (`0x63d920`) reads the edit as a 64-bit number and posts 0x8076, flagged 0 when the edit
  is empty or 0. In that case nothing is sent: the owner `c:0x6b62d0` sends only on 1 (READ).
- **What OK sends (READ, round 728 review).** The typed count moves into the bag's first empty
  slot (`c:0x6b6280`); with no empty slot, or the 0 flag (`c:0x6b62d0` sends only on 1), nothing
  is sent. The request is the retail **0x7034 type 0** `{u8 src+13, u8 dst+13, u16 count}`
  (`session/itemop.go`, `ItemOpNet`); the first version's invented count on OpenSRO's own move
  message is gone.
- **The server (READ, gs:0x4b2450).** A count below 1 refuses **0x1829**, an empty source
  0x1809; into an empty slot the whole stack moves, a count above the stack refuses **0x1814**
  (no whole-stack fallback), a smaller count splits (`inventory.Splitter`, mem and SQL, one
  transaction, the instance kept); onto an occupied slot it merges or swaps. The success is
  0xB034 type 0 `{src, dst, u16 count, u8 0}`; the client then re-reads the bag (OURS: the
  original applies the record itself).
- The layout matches `split_z4uFWIL.png`, down to "Retained numbe5000Distributed numb" running
  together as the original's statics do. The edit is held to its authored 42 px (review F8:
  Godot's LineEdit had grown it to ~53 by its theme's `minimum_character_width`).

### Buy back (reworked onto the retail messages by the review)

- **The list is the client's (READ).** It is never requested. Every 0xB034 type-9 (sell) result
  carries a trailing byte: the book's size after the sale (1..5), or 0xFF when the item is not
  booked. On anything but 0xFF the client (`c:0x87f370` → `c:0x78d900`) drops the oldest entry
  when five are held and appends the sold item at the back (`ItemOpNet.book_sale`). The row is
  drawn newest at the left (`c:0x6d4360` walks the list backwards); an index counts from the
  **oldest**.
- **The row's counts (READ).** `c:0x680da0` lists kind 0x45, the buy-back row, with the bag kinds
  under the same expendable test.
- **The box (READ).** A buy-back slot (kind 0x45) put on the bag goes `CIFInventory::vslot_028`
  0x6b5b80 → fill `0x6b0520`: the inventory's box (+0x390), mode 6, purpose 0x14, priced "%I64d"
  of the item reference's +0xb8 (the sell price) times the slot's count. The count is the
  entry's, fixed: 0x7168 carries no count and the server restores the stored item whole (READ,
  not OURS as the first version said).
- **The request (READ).** **0x7168** `{u32 NPC unique id, u8 index}`. Success is an **0xB034 of
  type 0x22** `{u8 dst+13, u8 index, u16 count}`, on which the client erases that entry
  (`c:0x784fe0`); failure only is **0xB168** `{u8 2, u16 code}`.
- **The server (READ, gs:0x42aae0, gs:0x6194e0, gs:0x42af00).**
  - The book is a vector on the PC object, appended at the back, the front dropped at five; it
    is serialized only by `CGObjPC` vslot 291/292. There is **no DB table for the book**:
    `AQ_StorageUpdater::RestoreSoldItem` writes the restored item's row. Ours is in memory per
    character; that it survives a relog is OURS.
  - A sale is booked unless the item is in the never-booked set (`gs:0x61b820`, filled by
    `ReferenceData::0x6b2950`): TypeID 3/3/8 unless bionic, any 3/2/x, 3/1/13, or a CodeName
    starting `ITEM_QNO`, `ITEM_QTUTORIAL`, `ITEM_QSP`, `ITEM_QCX`, `ITEM_ETC_E`,
    `SN_ITEM_EVENT`, or equal to `SN_ITEM_ETC_TAIWAN_50000_GOLD` (`shop.NeverBooked`). The
    server does not test the bionic exception (refdata carries no Bionic column); an itemdata
    row with TypeID1 3 is taken to be non-bionic (not counted).
  - An entry's price is max(the gold actually paid, SellPrice x count). With no tax that equals
    the sale.
  - The buy back, in order: an index past the book **0x18d3**; no empty bag slot **0x1807**
    before any gold moves; short of gold **0x180f**; the item into **the first empty slot,
    never merged** (`inventory.Placer`); not creatable 0x1842; a DB failure 0x1811.
  - **The NPC gate (OPEN).** Retail requires a live NPC interaction (`gs:0x511860`,
    `HasAvailableInteraction`, answering 3). That needs round 727's NPC interaction state, which
    has not landed on `dev`; the NPC uid is carried and not checked. The same holds for the sell
    and the deposit.
- **The Ctrl+sell warning (READ).** `CIFSlotWithHelp::vslot_029` looks the item up in a set
  (`UI_SILKMALL 0x67cf30`) and, when it is there, asks through `GInterface 0x788270`
  (MsgBoxSimple, 360x151 -- `push 0x97; push 0x168` inside 0x788270 -- style 1 Yes / No,
  caption `UIIT_STT_CONFIRM_BOX`, the text `UIIT_MSG_CANNOT_BUYBACK_ITEM_SELL` formatted with the
  item's name; 0x6814ae..0x681597). Built from round 714's `PartyMatchConfirm` (the same generic
  box); Yes sells. The set is taken to be the server's never-booked one
  (`ItemOpNet.never_booked`); that the client's own set (`c:0x67b3d0`) holds the same items is
  INFERRED, not compared.
- **Refusals** go to the system channel (OURS: where the original shows them), with the
  client's own lines: 0x180f `UIIT_MSG_STRGERR_NOT_ENOUGH_GOLD`, 0x1807
  `UIIT_MSG_STRGERR_INVENTORY_FULL`, 0x18d3 `UIIT_MSG_ERROR_RE_BUY_OBJECT_CANT`, 0x183b
  `UIIT_MSG_STRGERR_CANNOT_DEAL_AT_SHOP`.
- **The sell** is now the retail **0x7034 type 9** `{u8 src+13, u16 count, u32 NPC uid}`; its
  result `{src, u16 count, u32 NPC uid, u8 book}`. Refusals: CanSell 0x183b (READ); an empty slot
  0x1809, a count below 1 0x1829, anything else 0x1811 (OURS: the sell's own codes not mapped).

### The deposit fee

- **The column (READ).** itemdata **column 30, KeepingFee**: `RefObjCommon_ExtractData`
  (`gs:0x6a3090`) reads columns 26..31 into +0x9c Price, +0xa4 CostRepair, +0xa8 CostRevive,
  +0xa0 CostBorrow, **+0xac KeepingFee**, +0xb0 SellPrice, and the deposit's unit fee
  (`gs:0x523650`) is ref +0xac. The client's +0xcc was not separately mapped.
- **The box (READ, round 726).** It shows max(1, the fee x the count), no cap.
- **The server (READ, gs:0x524160, move type 2).** The request is **0x7034 type 2**
  `{u8 src+13, u8 dst warehouse slot, u32 NPC uid}` -- **no count**: the server moves and prices
  the **whole stack**, KeepingFee x stack clamped to **1..10,000,000** (`gs:0x524300`;
  `storage.DepositFee`). Short of gold refuses **0x180f** before anything moves; the item moves
  first and the gold is taken **only after the move succeeds** (`storage.DepositStack`). So above
  the cap the box shows more than is charged -- 30 real items (review F2), e.g.
  `ITEM_ETC_ARCHEMY_ATTRSTONE_ER_11` 2,500 x 10,000 shows 25,000,000 and is charged 10,000,000.
  The first version's "the server charges what the box shows (INFERRED)" was wrong.
- **The destination (OURS).** The client names the warehouse's first empty slot; the original
  names the slot the item was put down on.
- **The data paths.** The column is in refdata (`Item.KeepingFee`, CSV column 72,
  `items.keeping_fee`, the export), the client's `ItemTableReader` (GD and the native port,
  `keeping_fees`; an older native library reads 0), and now `table_parity`'s comparison.
  `deploy/README.md` has the production steps (re-export, import, restart, check id 8 = 11).

### What is on the retail wire now, and what is not

| Flow | Request | Result |
|---|---|---|
| split | 0x7034 type 0 | 0xB034 type 0 |
| sell | 0x7034 type 9 | 0xB034 type 9 + book byte |
| buy back | 0x7168 | 0xB034 type 0x22 / 0xB168 |
| deposit | 0x7034 type 2 | 0xB034 type 2 |

OpenSRO's other item moves -- bag to bag without a count, the doll, buy, withdraw, and the
warehouse gold -- stay on OpenSRO's own messages. They live in separate handlers from the new
`ItemOpHandler`, so moving them is a matter of adding their 0x7034 types to it and the client's
`ItemOpNet`; **that is the next step**. The server refuses any 0x7034 type it does not handle
with 0x1811 (OURS).

## Seven-hundred-and-twenty-seventh round: the NPC menus from the server's interaction ids, on the retail NPC opcodes (lane C1 of the NPC GUI epic)

This round builds lane C's first part of `docs/protocol/npc_gui.md`. The spec's new §8 has the
protocol, the id sources and the OPEN items. The labels are the spec's: READ (from the exe, with the
address), MEASURED, INFERRED and OURS. The store's and warehouse's item messages (buy, sell, buy
back, split, deposit fee) belong to lane 728 and were not touched. The tax line was left as it is,
by the user's decision: it waits for fortress war.

The round changes no drawing, loading or world code. Its client changes are the talk flow and the
menu builder, so it runs no perf gate.

### Server

- **The interaction ids** (`npcspawn.Interactions`):
  - **id 1** comes from the NPC owning a shop (the NPC init `0x4c7920` → `AddAvailableInteraction(1)`
    at `0x4c7996`, READ);
  - **id 2** comes from the quest census, `npcspawn/questtalk.go`, 89 codenames:
    - the pushes are READ: `FUN_00926ed0` and `FUN_00927040` walk each quest's mission-NPC block,
      and three classes push directly;
    - that every listed quest is in service is INFERRED;
  - **id 8** comes from the teleport links, a stand-in (disclosed);
  - **0x11 no longer goes to shops.** Its registrar reads another map (`FUN_004ccb70`), so the
    herbalist does not get the gacha line.
  - The whole set now reaches the select reply even when the flag byte is 0, as the ferry seller's
    {7, 9} does.
- **The opcodes** (`internal/npctalk`, `session/npctalk.go`): `0x7045`→`0xb045`, `0x7046`→`0xb046`
  and `0x704b`→`0xb04b`. Every field and refusal code is READ (npc_gui.md §8).
  - INTERACTMODE is 5 for ids 2 and 10, none for 0x23, and 6 otherwise.
  - The reach is 300, in 3-D, from the player to the NPC's spot in the player's frame.
  - Trading counts as busy (OURS: through the trade hub).
- **OpenSRO's `0x0050`–`0x005d`** stay. They are all store or warehouse item messages (lane 728's),
  and `0x7046` replaces only the open, for which OpenSRO had no message.

### Client

- **`NpcTalkNet`** (new) holds the codecs and the state.
  - It never sends `0x704b` while a `0x7046` is in flight. That is READ: the close slot `0x7040b0`
    asks `0x841780` first.
- **World3D:**
  - A server NPC's click (or a talk approach's arrival) sends `0x7045`. The talk window opens on
    `0xb045` with the server's set.

  - The warehouse line sends `0x7046 {3}` before the hide.

    (`HudPanels.npc_window_hidden`). The store and storage closes are READ, closing OPEN 4.

  tokens. The codename derivation `services_for` is removed, along with its `GUILD_PATTERNS` and

    - the keeper's store gate `FUN_00989d20`, a string compare whose strings are not read;
    - the academy membership byte, taken as 0;
    - 0x1e's `FUN_006f98d0` lines;
    - 6 (item 0xb, which has no text).
  - Clicking a line with no system behind it says "not available yet" (OURS, as before).
- **Gates** are client-placed and have no uid, so their set comes from their teleport point
  (`gate_ids`, OURS). With no server, an NPC's window shows its greeting and the end line.

### What id 2 and id 10 do (as corrected by the review fixes below)

- **Id 2:** `0x7046 {2}` is answered `{1, 2}` with INTERACTMODE 5. The talk window stays.

NPC GUI epic, lane B (spec: round 724, `docs/protocol/npc_gui.md` §4 and `message_box.md`). Our own
panels (BuyConfirm, SellConfirm, DepositConfirm, WithdrawConfirm, GoldDialog) are replaced by
`StoreMessageBox` (`client/scripts/ui/hud/store_message_box.gd`), which builds each box from
`resinfo\ifmessagebox.txt`, `ifitemmallconfirmbuy.txt` and `ifitemmallconfirmslot.txt` under the
defines `config\define.txt` sets. HudPanels keeps only the trigger and network functions.

### The boxes (READ unless marked)
