## Seven-hundred-and-twenty-fifth round: the NPC window, the store and storage in their registry frames, the talk text, and the chaining (lane A of the NPC GUI epic)

This round builds lane A of round 724's spec, `docs/protocol/npc_gui.md` §1–§3, §5 and §6.
Labels are as in the spec: READ (exe or layout, with the address or file), MEASURED, INFERRED and
OURS. The confirm boxes and the buy/sell gestures belong to lane B, and the opcodes to lane C. This
round is UI only, so it runs no perf gate.

### What was built

#### The NPC window (READ structure, `NpcTalkView`, new)
- **The window.** It is `GDR_NPCWINDOW`, built as a registry window from `if_npcwindow.txt`: 386x451,
  with the `mframe_wnd_` chrome, caption and close button. Its `GDR_NW_NPCTALK` at 11,48 is the
  `npc_conversation_window_` 8-slice.
- **The talk box.** `NpcTalkView.compose` builds `if_npctalk.txt`'s Create inside the window, since
  `CIF_NPCTalk::Create` (0x6fa110) loads it with itself as the parent. It holds the `com_bg_tile_d`
  panel, the text at talk-box 23,23 (window 34,71, 302x343) and the scroll bar at 336,27. The quest
  parchment is hidden.
  - When the archive lacks `if_npcwindow.txt`, the old self-framed `if_npctalk.txt` window is the
    fallback (`PANEL_FALLBACKS`).
- **The scroll bar.** It is `HudChat.ChatScroll` (the CIFVerticalScroll), with a length of 320, READ
  from `push 0x140` at 0x6fa1c9 into 0x65a390. One step is one line, and the wheel scrolls it too.
- **The line pitch.** It is 18, READ from `push 0x12` at 0x6fa1e1 into 0x638c20, the chat's 14-pitch
  setter. Wrapped lines take the same pitch, which MEASURED 18 px in `tcHCl0v.png`. The label gets
  `line_separation` = 18 − the font's height.
- **The title.** It is the NPC's name. The store's is too (0x704050 → the ref name, READ).

#### The talk text (READ: `FUN_00700440`, `FUN_006fcd60`, `FUN_006fb630`)
- **The greeting** is white `0xffffffff`.
- **The tax line** is `SN_FORTRESS_SHOP_TAX` in green `0xffd6ff7e`, followed by a blank line.
  - The fortress name comes from `textdata_object` (`SN_FORTRESS_JANGAN` → "Jangan Fortress").
    `World3D._resolve_any_text` now also tries the object-name table, which is the only one that
    holds it.
  - **Which NPCs get the line, and the rate, are OURS.** `NpcTalkView.fortress_strid_for` maps
    `_CH_` → Jangan and `_KT_` → Hotan, the two fortresses in `siegefortress.txt`, and the rate is
    0%. The server sends no fortress data, and the original's test (`+0x18c`, `+0x800`) is unread.
    This holds until lane C reads the message (spec OPEN 1).
- **The menu lines** are "`%d. `" + caption:
  - beige `0xffefdaa4` normally;
  - orange `0xffff8a00` for the other two states (INFERRED to be hover and press; the RichTextLabel's
    meta-hover re-renders the line);
  - no underline (`meta_underlined = false`);
  - "End conversation." last.
- **The menu comes from the id set, in the spec's order.** The ids are derived client-side from the
  tables and codenames (OURS until lane C reads them from `0xb045`).
  - **One store line per tab group.** The line is worded by its group's `SN_STORE_*` name: READ,
    `FUN_006fb630` walks the NPC's tab groups and `refshoptabgroup.txt` [4] is the name.
    - `ShopReader.store_lines_for` / `tabs_for(code, tabgroup)` follow the chain refshopgroup →
      refmappingshopgroup → refmappingshopwithtab → refshoptabgroup.
    - The key is `shop:<TABGROUP>`, and the store opens with that group's tabs only.
  - **Ids 2 ("Talk to this person.") and 10 ("Withdrawing Skill") are not offered.** Their
    registrar is absent from `CGObjNPCNPC::Create` (0x4c6350; it registers no 2 or 10 through
    `[vtable+0x164]`). So the herbalist's menu has two lines fewer than `tcHCl0v.png`'s (spec
    OPEN 7).
- **"Select teleport area"** replaces the menu in place (round 603's list, now in `NpcTalkView`).
- **A gate's greeting.** `NpcServiceReader.parse_greetings` dropped every `npcchat.txt` owner that
  is not an `NPC_` code, so a Dimensional Gate greeted with "...". The original greets with
  `STORE_CH_GATE_BS` (`1llywhJ.png`, verbatim), so the filter is gone.

#### `config\define.txt` (READ: `CGame` 0x848210 → 0x6441b0)
- **Reading it.** `UiBuilder.archive_defines()` reads the file once from Media.pk2, once the
  archive is open; an earlier call is not cached.
- **Parsing it.** `UiBuilder.parse_define_txt` parses it as the client does (READ, from the
  review). Each line is split on `=`, `"`, `,`, space and tab, and its first token is a name.
  - Every listed name counts as defined, `NAME = 0` included.
  - There is no comment handling, so `//` becomes a name, which is harmless.
  - The archive's copy gives 22 names.
- **The parser reads the same table (READ, from the review).** The layout parser's `#ifdef` reads
  the map that `define.txt` fills, at `0xeed4e0`.
- **The store.** It builds with those defines (`ARCHIVE_DEFINE_PANELS`, and the registry frame's
  `archive_defines`). That selects the `RENEWAL_SHOP_SYSTEM` + `RESTORE_SOLDITEM_INSHOP` branch:
  `CIFStoreForPackage`, 254x370, with the buy-back row.
- **The NPC window** is marked `archive_defines` as well, but `if_npcwindow.txt`, `if_npctalk.txt`
  and `ifstorageroom.txt` hold no `#ifdef`, so their builds are unchanged and their cache keys stay
  plain.
- **The only window whose build changed this round is the store.**

**Census of the `#ifdef` layouts (34 `resinfo` files).** Every symbol they test is in `define.txt`
except these four:

| Symbol | Layout | Original | OpenSRO |
|---|---|---|---|
| `EVENT_FESTIVAL` | `ginterface.txt` | off | read (all branches) |
| `PROVIDE_ITEM_BY_COUPON` | `ifmessagebox.txt` | off | read (all branches) |
| `EU_QUESTWINDOW_IMPROVE_SECOND` | `ifquestslot.txt` | off | read (all branches) |
| `APPLY_GNGWC_SYSTEM_2007` | `pstitle.txt` | off | read (all branches) |

OpenSRO's difference from the original here is OPEN 11. The store's and the NPC window's registry
entries are parsed from `ginterface.txt` with the archive defines, so that parse differs from the
one every other registry entry gets.

The other windows keep their hand-picked defines (`HudChat.LAYOUT_DEFINES`, `PANEL_DEFINES`) or
read-all-branches. Moving them all to `define.txt` is a follow-up, since each one's build would
change and needs its own check.

### USER DECISION (2026-10-05): the stock English wording
The coordinator relayed the decision after the review.
- **The archive.** The box's `textuisystem.txt`, which is also the user's, is two tables joined:
  - lines 1–6955: a private server's reworded English, 16 columns;
  - lines 6956–13915: the stock English, 19 columns.
  
  The first table holds 5,960 keys and the second 6,088. 5,167 keys are in both, and 433 of those
  read differently.
- **The conflict.** The binary keeps the first row (READ, 0x8ca120), so with this archive it would
  show the reworded block. The user's screenshots show the stock wording.

**The implementation (`client/scripts/ui/ui_text_table.gd`):**
- **One rule for both readers.** `UiTextTable.select_rows` decides which row of a key is kept, for
  the native reader's rows and the GDScript loop's alike. The native reader returns rows before
  that choice, so `native/src/core/tables.rs` needed no change.
- **The stock row wins when the file is two joined tables.** `joined_table_start` detects that by
  structure, not by a line number:
  - the file's opening keys restart in order for at least 8 rows (here 89 do);
  - at least half of the keys before the restart come back after it (here 5,167 of 5,960).

  Both thresholds are OURS.
- **A single table is unchanged.** It never restarts, so it keeps every first row exactly as
  before, and so does a file with a stray repeated key.
- **OURS: a stock row with no English does not replace an English one.** 109 of the 433 are
  Korean-only stock rows, such as `UIO_MSG_AUTOLOGIN` and the DirectX checks; they keep the
  reworded English instead of going blank.
- **Labels.** The rule is labelled USER DECISION and a departure. The keep-first rule stays
  documented as READ.

**Census of the other text tables (box archive):**

| File | Joined? | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `textuisystem.txt` | **yes** | the only joined one |
| `textdata_object.txt` | no | its first key never recurs; its 382 width-16/18 duplicate pairs are not a second table |
| `textdata_equip&skill.txt`, `textdata_equipskill.txt` | no | the first key recurs after a 4-row preamble, 1 of whose 4 keys returns; both rules reject it |
| `textquest_*` (otherstring, queststring, speechname, speech&name) | no | no duplicate keys |
| `textzonename.txt` | no | 10 duplicates, no restart |
| `texthelp.txt`, `textevent.txt` | no | no duplicates |
| `textquest.txt` | no | no service-1 rows |

**The font follows the rule.** `UIC_STT_FONTNAME` is the first key of both tables: "Arial" in the
reworded one and "Tahoma" in the stock one. So OpenSRO now asks for Tahoma.
- **On the box** Tahoma is not installed, so the log reads "UI face 'Tahoma' … disclosed fallback
  vplus\vfont.ttf (Arial)". The box's drawing is unchanged.
- **On a machine with Tahoma** (Windows, CrossOver) the UI draws in Tahoma.
- **The original's face is wider than Arial** (MEASURED on `tcHCl0v.png`, as Tahoma is wider):
  - the herbalist's first greeting line is 286 px in the original and 279 px in OpenSRO's Arial;
  - the tax line is 253 px against 244.
  
  That is a hint, not a proof.
- **The login screen asks for the same face as the world.** It scans for only this one row, and
  now goes through the same rule whenever the key appears more than once.

**Tests:**
- `ui_text_table_test` checks that:
  - a joined table takes the stock row;
  - a Korean-only stock row does not replace English;
  - keys found in only one table keep their row;
  - `joined_table_start` is found;
  - `keep_first` false still keeps the last row.
- Its NEGATIVE cases: a single table with a stray stock-shaped repeat keeps the first row, and a
  3-key restart is not a second table.
- `table_parity.gd` ran on the box with this lane's freshly built native library (`native/build.sh`,

- The full suite and `check` are in the round's final commit.

## Seven-hundred-and-twenty-third round: a gate's effects attach when its model sits in a neighbouring region

The user, after v0.1.494 (2026-10-05): Samarkand and Donwhang still show no glow, with every video
option on except bloom (screenshots `/root/opensro-handoff/teleport_refs/ours_iurb7RC.jpeg`,
`ours_tcxFdYo.png`). Their own client log (native Linux build on a Steam Machine, RADV Navi33,
copied to the render box as `/root/opensro_full.log`) settled the cause. It was not the drawing.

### The cause (MEASURED, the user's log)

- **Samarkand never attached.** On the user's teleport into Samarkand (`teleport accepted -- to
  SN_ZONE_22005`), no `World3D: gate STORE_CA_GATE -- ... plays N of its M ambient effect(s)` line
  appears and no `gate effect(s) preloading` line for `107\107`. Jangan (`STORE_CH_GATE`), Hotan
  (`STORE_KT_GATE`) and Constantinople (`STORE_EU_GATE`) each logged theirs in the same session.
- **The row is on the region's edge:** `teleport gate STORE_CA_GATE clickable at 107/107 local
  (1917, 250, 108)`, 3 units inside a 1920-unit region.
- **The model was placed by a neighbour.** The arrival is `in RealTerrain_106_108`, which loaded
  before 107/107. 107/107's load line reads "9 already placed by a loaded region, 7 owned by a
  neighbour and placed in its frame". The gate's model `samarkand_center_01` is listed by several
  sectors and is placed once, by whichever loads first, so it sat in a neighbour's container.
- **`_attach_gate_effects(rx, ry)` searched only `_object_containers["_rx_ry"]`**, the row's own
  region, and `_gate_points_for` gave a job only its own region's rows. So a gate whose model lives
  in another container never played anything.
- **Donwhang's row has the same shape:** `STORE_WC_GATE clickable at 103/153 local (962, -35, 8)`,
  with z = 8 on the region's edge. The user's log has no Donwhang visit after v0.1.494 to confirm
  it there; the live run below covers it.
- **Why the rounds 720-722 renders showed the glows:** they booted with the gate's region as the
  `--region`, so it loaded first and owned the model.

### The fix (`GateEffectMatch`, `World3D._attach_gate_effects` / `_gate_pairs_around` / `_gate_points_for`)

- **Search the neighbourhood.** A row is matched against the objects of its region and its eight
  neighbours, horizontally, within `GATE_EFFECT_RADIUS` (30, OURS as before).
- **One frame.** Everything is matched in the committed region's local frame:
  - a neighbour's row by its grid offset: region (x + dx, y + dy)'s local origin is at
    (dy * 1920, dx * 1920) before the world's z mirror (region y → world X, region x → world Z;
    `World3D._cell_offset`);
  - a container's objects through the containers' chain transforms.
- **Any load order.** The match runs on every region's commit, for that region and its neighbours.
  Whichever region loads last finds the pair. An object still plays once (`META_GATE_EFFECTS`), and
  an object near two rows pairs once.
- **Preload covers neighbours.** A job's gate points now include the neighbours' rows in its own
  frame, so a model placed here for a gate next door is preloaded on the worker as before.
- **The log line now names the holder:** `gate <code> -- <object> (in <container>) at <d> ...`.

### Tests

- `scripts/world/gate_effect_match_test.gd` (10 checks, 0 failures):
  - the frame offsets on both axes;
  - Samarkand's shape in both load orders: the row's region first, then the model's; and the
    model's region first;
  - once per object;
  - the radius across the boundary;
  - the neighbourhood's extent.
- Box `check`: 613 scripts and 9 scenes, ALL LOAD.
- Full suite on the box (`RENDER_DIR=/opt/opensro-client-r723`): 235 suites, 0 failing.

### Live (the user's path: a teleport from the Jangan gate)

Stock `qa_shot.sh --server --region '97\168.m' --radius 1 --at 1230,1380 --teleport <id>` with
`OPENSRO_QA_CLICK=gate` (the retail teleport CSVs; `/var/tmp/r723/run.sh`, logs in
`/var/tmp/r723/tp25/` and `tp2/`). The player clicks the Jangan gate and takes its Move.

**Samarkand (25):**
```

World3D: 106\107.o -- 1 gate effect(s) preloading on a task
World3D: gate STORE_CA_GATE -- Obj_samarkand_center_01_55 (in RealMapObjects_106_107) at 1.0 from its row plays 2 of its 2 ambient effect(s), built in 629 us
World3D: teleport arrival in RealTerrain_106_108 at local (270.0, 1421.0) ...
```
The gate's model is held by **106/107's** container, a neighbour of the row's region 107/107,
exactly as the cause predicted. Under round 722's code it would have played nothing, as in the
user's log.

**Donwhang (2):**
```
World3D: teleport accepted -- to SN_ZONE_22002, 0 gold charged, waiver 1: Teleport to [Donwhang] (no cost).
World3D: 102\153.o -- 2 gate effect(s) preloading on a task
World3D: gate STORE_WC_GATE -- Obj_w_cd_portal_71 (in RealMapObjects_102_153) at 3.3 from its row plays 3 of its 3 ambient effect(s), built in 947 us
```
Donwhang's row is at 103/153; its model `w_cd_portal` sits in **102/153**, a neighbour too. So
Donwhang had the same fault.

**Other checks:**
- The preload now runs in the neighbour's job, because its gate points include the row next door.
- Jangan's own gate attaches as before.
- The attach cost is unchanged: 629-947 us, against 538-2185 us in the user's log.

**Not shown in a frame:** after arrival the camera faces away from both gates
(`/var/tmp/r723/tp25/f00000899.png`, `tp2/f00000899.png`), so these frames show neither glow. The
glows' look is round 722's, unchanged here. This round changes which gates attach, and the log lines
above are the measurement of that.

No perf gate: no per-frame code changed. The match runs once per region commit over nine containers'
children, at the cost shown above.

**Review** (coordinator, kept light at the user's request to save usage): the diff matches the rows of the
committed region and its eight neighbours against the objects of all nine containers in one frame, on every
commit, so either load order pairs them. The live pairs' distances (Samarkand 1.0, Donwhang 3.3) equal round 720's
same-region census, which checks the cross-region offsets on the region-x axis both gates straddle; the region-y
axis offset is covered by the unit test only. No perf gate: no per-frame code.

## Seven-hundred-and-twenty-second round: the gates' animated water (TEXANI), and their glows blended in display values as Direct3D 9 blends

The user (2026-10-04), after v0.1.493: "Samarkand and Donwhang don't have glow effects and they
should. Also Hotan's teleporter is like a fountain with its own water or water-like texture that is
supposed to be animated but it's not." Then two screenshots of the original
(`/root/opensro-handoff/teleport_refs/orig_donwhang_7iPG5Cm.png`, `orig_samarkand_ZlvBrQo.png`).

Labels: READ (sro_client.exe, address given; the archive's own shader sources), MEASURED, INFERRED,
OPEN, OURS.

### 1. Hotan: TEXANI, read and built

**READ.**
- **The data**: `ModDataTexAni::vslot_004` (0xc5c5a0) reads the IModData header and then data
  +0x24..+0x34 = mode, method, fps, rows, columns, plus 16 floats at +0x38 (BsrReader._read_texani).
- **The runtime** (`CRTModTexAni`):
  - Its constructor 0xc82a00 sets the 4x4 matrix at +0x48 to the identity and fills a two-entry
    table: +0x90 = 0xc82640 (the frame-grid step), +0x94 = 0xc82830 (the rate step).
  - `vslot_002` calls the entry that data +0x28 picks, with the frame's milliseconds.
  - **The rate step** turns ms into seconds (/1000.0, the double at 0xd83268) and grows m00, m01,
    m10, m11, m20 and m21 by data +0x38, +0x3c, +0x48, +0x4c, +0x58 and +0x5c times the seconds.
    Nothing wraps.
  - **The grid step**: period trunc(1000/fps) ms; trunc(acc/period) frames; loop, ping-pong or
    clamp by header bytes +0x20..+0x22; then FUN_00c825f0 sets the translation to
    (frame % cols / cols, frame / cols / rows).
- **The draw**: `vslot_004` (0xc82970) uploads the matrix to vertex constants 23..25 for the
  material the mod names (+0x14).
- **The shader** (corrected by the review): the object shader the client assembles is
  `shader\vss0.c` / `vss2.c` (pushed at 0xbf6a5a / 0xbf6a8a), with a define list built at
  0xbf6c3f..0xbf6d34: TEXTURE0, SPEC, MULTITEX, TEXANI0, TEXANI1, TEXANI1R.
  - The renderer picks the UV variant from the draw flags (0xbf0f70..0xbf0f93), and
    `CRTModTexAni::vslot_004` sets 0x400000 for mode 1 (data +0x24) and 0x8000000 otherwise
    (0xc8299f..0xc829ad).
  - **TEXANI0** (mode 0): `m3x3 oT0.xyz, r1.xyz, c23` with r1 = (u, v, 1), so u' = dot((u,v,1), c23)
    and v' = dot((u,v,1), c24) on texture stage 0.
  - **TEXANI1** (mode 1): oT0 passes through as authored and **oT1**, the second stage's
    coordinates, is animated.
  - The matrix is transposed on upload: 0xaa3afe is D3DXMatrixTranspose (READ, the review), so
    c23 = (m00, m10, m20).
  - The archive's `vertexshader0texani.c`, which round 722 first cited, equals TEXANI0 but is not
    a file the client loads.

**MEASURED, the census** (`client/tools/dump_bsr_particles.gd --census`, now with a TEXANI section):
- 359 `.bsr` carry a TEXANI mod, 358 of them in the `ambient` set.
- All but one use the rate step (method 1); the frame grid appears once (`flame_adjutant`).
- The gates: Hotan's `oas_hot_portal` material 3 (`Oas_hot_potal_water`), v +0.48/s.
  Constantinople's `euro_esteuro_fountain01` material 6, with the 2x2 part growing
  (+0.02, +0.03, -0.02, +0.03 /s). The guild `charge_gate` material 3, v -0.7/s.

**Built.**
- `BsrReader` reads the mods: `texani_mods` and `texani_for(index)`, with the ambient set and
  MTRL's dispatch rule.
- `TexAni` (`client/scripts/world/tex_ani.gd`) runs both steps as read.
- `ObjectLoader` binds a placed object's material to its mod.
- The object shader (`object.gdshaderinc`) and the MTRL mod shader apply the two rows in vertex().
  The identity is the default, so every other material is unchanged.
- World3D ticks it every physics step.

**Live** (`/var/tmp/r722/a7hotan`, the QA TEXANI line):
- Hotan's water reads v +0.16 at tick 20 and +0.48 at tick 60, i.e. 0.48 a second.
- 11 materials animate in Hotan's 3x3 regions, the town's `bigwaterfall` objects among them: every
  placed object's TEXANI now plays, not only the gates'.

**Mode 1 (the review's finding 1).**
- 186 of the 370 mods are mode 1, which animates stage 1 only.
- Round 722 first slid the base texture for them, for example `alex_library_01`'s fountain water
  (91/49) at -0.88/s. A mode-1 mod is now not bound (`TexAni.animates_base`), so the base texture

- What these materials' second stage holds (a second texture, its stage ops) is not read, so
  whatever the original moves on stage 1 does not move here: OPEN.
- Live (`/var/tmp/r722/a8lib`): see "Review fixes" below.

**Notes (the review's finding 7):**
- The frame grid (method 0) is unexercised by placed data. Its one user, `flame_adjutant`, is set 1,

- The matrix grows with no wrap (READ: `vslot_007` resets the frame and direction, never the

- Float32 precision degrades after about 10 hours on the fastest scroll (`cj_wf_dr_01`, -2.78/s:
  |v| ~ 10^5, a step of ~0.008 of a texture).
- All of this is as the original's accumulator does; its only difference is its LOD gate, which

**OURS:**

  sits behind the LOD gate 0xc43780).
- The skinned character and item path (SkinnedBsrAssembler) is not bound: OPEN.

**Not built:** Hotan's ambient MTRL mod. It is the existing MTRL path (round 625:

### 2. Samarkand: the glow is there; Forward+ blended it away

**MEASURED.**
- Samarkand's `samarkand_center_01` carries two `map\cj_pal_potal_blue.efp`, glow byte 0, drawn
  with the scene.
- Their plates (`efpcensus -dumpone`) are two single big billboards, 70x90 and 50..70x60..90 units:
  `00illusion_basic.ddj` (ARGB 200, 62,130,254) and `01blurred2.ddj` (150, 101,144,253). Both are
  SRCALPHA/ONE additive and centred in the arch at y 55.9 and 81.8.
- They draw (the QA screen log: on screen, particle extents in the arch). Over the bright sky behind
  the open arch, though, Forward+'s additive blend in its **linear** buffer adds almost nothing.
  Direct3D 9 adds in the **display values** the screen shows (no D3DRS_SRGBWRITEENABLE, round 705),
  where blue on sky saturates toward white: the white glow in the user's picture.
- Compatibility blends in display values (WORLD_ISSUES "Blending space", MEASURED), so it is the
  reference for the original's arithmetic. Same view, mean of the arch's open area
  (110x80 px, `/var/tmp/r722/a4`, `a5`):

| render | R G B |
|---|---|
| effects off (both renderers) | 164 210 205 |
| Forward+ before (linear blend) | 175 220 238 |
| **Forward+ after (display blend, this round)** | **208 229 240** |
| Compatibility (display values, the D3D9 arithmetic) | 214 233 243 |

  The original's arch, behind the crystal: 173 183 233 and 177 199 238 (different sky and hour;
  the shape is the point).

**Built: `EfpEffect.display_shader`** (OURS method, the READ blend).
- Under Forward+ a node's shader reads the colour underneath (`hint_screen_texture`: the opaque
  scene, before the transparent pass).
- It turns that into the displayed value through Godot's tone map forward (ObjectLight's tonemap
  vector and filmic curve), makes the D3D blend of the class on display values (SRCALPHA/ONE adds
  s*a; SRCALPHA/INVSRCALPHA mixes), and writes what Godot's blend and tone map turn into that: the
  difference with ALPHA 1 for an additive class, the colour whose linear mix lands on it for a
  mixing one.
- Under Compatibility nothing changes.
- **Scope (OURS):** only the objects' ambient effects (`AmbientParticles.attach` calls
  `use_display_blend` before `make_glow`). Every other EFP (skills, auras) still blends linearly; the
  same switch would serve them (a decision for the user: the look of every skill changes).
- The display twins (and their glow twins) are added to `EfpEffect.warm`.
- **Limits (OURS):**
  - Overlapping particles each blend against the opaque scene and their differences add, which
    undercounts where they overlap and saturate.
  - A transparent surface underneath is not in the screen texture.

### 3. Donwhang: the low glow is hidden by its own platform, by the original's rule too

**MEASURED** (the QA lines; the camera on the bridge at 135 and 188 units):

- **What the user sees as Donwhang's glow** is the scene-drawn `w_cd_potal_blue` (two big additive

## Seven-hundred-and-twenty-first round: the Alexandria gate portals' rings spin about one centre -- map objects bind to the `.bsk`'s stored inverse binds where those are only a root shift

The user (2026-10-04): "Alexandria North and South gate teleporters are slightly broken. The rings
don't spin around the same axis it seems." Their screenshot of our client
(`/root/opensro-handoff/teleport_refs/alex_OyBVAZa.png`, native Linux build) shows the two inner
rings' centre offset from the outer ring's.

Labels: READ (the client decompile and asm on the render box), MEASURED, INFERRED, OURS, OPEN.

### The object

Both gates draw `res\bldg\north africa\alexandria\alex_portal.bsr` (Data.pk2):
- **Skeleton:** `alex_portal.bsk`, 9 bones.
- **Clip:** `alex_portal.ban`, the `default` type-0 entry.
- **Ring pieces:** six skinned pieces, each on one bone. `Alex_Portal_ani01_01/02` → Bone03,
  `ani02_01/02` → Bone01, `ani03` → Bone05, `ani04` → Bone07.
- **Base:** eight still pieces, centred at x ≈ 0.

It animates through `MapAnimation` (round 645).

### Cause (MEASURED, `client/tools/probe_map_anim_pose.gd`, extended this round)

**Root rest against the clip's root key.**
- The `.bsk` root stores a local translation of **(19.754, 0, 0)**.
- The clip keys the root at **(0, 0, 0)**.
- Every child's stored bind puts the root at the origin (`census_bsk_bind.gd`: "stored root local
  (19.75354, …), children imply (-0, 0, 0)").

**The bind.** `Skeleton3DBuilder.build_skin` bound each piece to the inverse of the rest composed
from the locals, which includes the 19.75. At the clip's first key the root sits at 0, so:

| piece | still centre | posed centre, t = 0 (before) |
|---|---|---|
| `ani01_01` (outer ring, Bone03) | (0.00, 169.14, -0.01) | (-19.76, 169.14, -0.01) |
| `ani02_01` (Bone01) | (0.14, 169.02, 0.22) | (-19.62, 169.02, 0.22) |
| `ani03` (Bone05) | (-0.04, 169.03, 0.05) | (-19.79, 169.03, 0.05) |
| `ani04` (Bone07) | (0.00, 169.07, 0.04) | (-19.75, 169.07, 0.04) |

**The spin.** Every ring was drawn 19.75 off its mesh and off the base, and each spun about its
bone, whose pose is at x ≈ 0:
- The outer ring spins about an axis along x, so its centre stayed at -19.76.
- The inner rings orbited the bone at radius 19.75. `ani02_01`'s centre went (-19.62, 0.22) at
  0 s, (-11.60, -15.69) at 1 s, (5.99, -18.55) at 2 s and (15.92, 11.59) at 4 s.

That is the screenshot.

### What the client does (READ)

`BSK_FORMAT.md`, "How the client skins with those three matrices" (round 648), and re-read this
round:
- **The bone update** is `RTSkeleton::FUN_00c49f20` (and `FUN_00c4bcb0` for the first bone).
- **A bone's local** comes from the blended keys when a track touched it (`+0x98` ≠ 0), otherwise
  from the prim's stored local.
- **The world matrix** is `W = L x W_parent`.
- **The palette** is `P = InvBind_file x W`, where the inverse bind is the prim's third matrix, read
  from the record's **third** (quaternion, vector) pair. It is never recomputed.
- **The skeleton scale.** For the first bone, `FUN_00c4bcb0` multiplies the 3x3 by a scale when it
  is not 1.0 (`param_3`, from skeleton `+0xa4`). On map objects it is **1.0** (READ, the review:
  the RTSkeleton constructor `FUN_00c513c0` stores `fld1` there, and the map's object build never
  calls `CCompChar` slot 9 `FUN_00c25460`, its only other writer).

### The fix

`Skeleton3DBuilder.consistent_stored_binds` (new):
- **What it reads.** Each bone's stored inverse bind (`stored_inverse_bind`: the third pair, at
  0x38/0x48, +4 on the root's 92-byte record; finite, unit rotation, inside
  `ROOT_TRANSLATION_LIMIT`).
- **When it uses them.** Only when every non-root bone's stored bind equals its composed rest moved
  by the one rigid shift that re-seats the root where its children put it
  (`root_rest_from_children`), within 0.05 units and 1°. Otherwise it returns `{}`.
- **The root** keeps its own stored bind (a vertex on the root binds as the client binds it).

`build_skin(..., world_binds)` binds a bone to the inverse of its stored world bind when the
dictionary has it. `MapAnimation.commit` passes the consistent binds; characters, monsters and items
(`SkinnedBsrAssembler`) do not, so they are unchanged.

Where the condition holds, the skin is exactly the client's (`P = InvBind_file x W`, with `W` from
the same keys and locals). Where it does not, the composed bind stays (OURS, below).

**After (MEASURED, the same probe).** Every ring's posed centre stays within 0.4 of (0, 169, 0) at
t = 0, 1, 2, 4 and 7 s; at t = 0 the posed centres equal the still ones.

### Renders, before and after (Forward+, RX 7600, stock `qa_shot.sh` on the shared lock)

**Setup.**
- `/var/tmp/r721/run_rings.sh` and `run_north.sh` run dev's client (`/opt/opensro-client-r721base`)
  and this branch's (`/opt/opensro-client-r721`).
- `OPENSRO_QA_FREE=1` and `NOUI`/`NOFOG` are set.
- Each gate gets one run per build, standing at the gate's teleport point.

**South gate** (`90\48.m`, point 612/1089; shots s1-s3 at yaw 0, pitch -3, distance 600; frames
13/41/69).
- **Metric:** the rings' silhouette against the sky, a 240x95 window above the rooftops
  (`-crop 240x95+520+95`, gray, threshold 50 %, trim), and its horizontal centre.
- **Frames 41 and 69:** dev 623.0 / 621.5, this branch 643.0 / 643.5, a shift of 21 px.
- **Expected shift:** at 600 units with the 60° vertical field of view at 720 px, one unit is
  ≈ 1.04 px, so 19.75 units ≈ 20.5 px. That is the measured cause. Frame 13 is cut by the window's
  edge in both builds.
- **Frames:** `/var/tmp/r721/{base,head}_south/f00000041.png` and the crop `hs41c.png`. The rings
  are centred over the pedestal on this branch and sit left of it on dev.

**North gate** (`92\50.m`, point 1719/760; yaws 0/90/180/270, distance 500).
- Only yaw 0 (frame 13) frames the portal, small, behind an arcade. The pair
  `/var/tmp/r721/north_pair.png` (dev left, this branch right) shows the horizontal ring band
  running left of the arch on dev and centred on it here.
- That is a picture, not a measurement. The measurement for the north gate is the probe's above:
  it is the same `.bsr`.

### Why the third pair, and why only a root shift (MEASURED)

`client/tools/probe_map_bind.gd` (new) builds all 144 animated map models as the world does. At the
clip's first key it prints the largest vertex move between the old bind and the new, and each
bind's mean distance from the authored mesh. Three passes:

1. **Inverting the second pair (the stored world bind):** 41 of 144 move. It fixes the portal, but
   moves `rock_mt_ship` (0.002 → 6.90), the horses, the sheep and 9 map NPCs off their meshes; in
   those files the second pair is stale.
2. **The third pair (the client's):** the ship, the horses, the sheep and the NPCs are back to 0.
   `tre_willow03` (0 → 58.4), `tre_tree01_big` (0 → 32.6), `demon_wall_deco*` (→ 0.54),
   `oas_hot_tree_stone` (→ 0.48) and `tre_bamboo04` (→ 0.57) still move.
   - The willow's stored chain is its composed chain **scaled by 1.793 below its first bone**.
     Bone01→Bone02 is (6.11, 80.14, 7.12) composed against (10.95, 143.71, 12.77) stored, and
     Bone02→Bone03 has the same ratio.
   - Its mesh agrees with the scaled one: the leaves sit at height ~404, Bone03 is stored at 426
     and composed at 238.
   - The skeleton scale is 1.0 on the map path (above), so by our readers the client's rule draws
     the willow 58 off its mesh. Either retail does, or one of our readers is wrong: unexplained,
     OPEN.
3. **The third pair, only where it is a root shift (shipped):** 9 models move, each onto its own
   mesh. The other 135 do not move (≤ 0.001).

| model | mean off the mesh, before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `alex_portal` | 19.754 | 0.000 |
| `quest\teleport01` | 31.714 | 0.000 |
| `dun\demon\demon_altar_deco` (and `_fire`, `_death`, `_poison`) | 54.758 | 0.001 |
| `fortress_ct_fort_in_door01` | 89.483 | 0.000 |
| `fortress_ct_fort_out_door01` | 44.606 | 0.000 |
| `arabianf_bujok03` | 481.339 | 8.699 |

### OURS / OPEN

- **OURS:** the condition itself. The client takes the stored binds always; this takes them only
  where they are a root shift of the locals and every non-root bone's third pair is usable. Where
  it does, the skin is exactly the client's (the review's probe: 0.000 against the client's rule).
- **OPEN, unexplained:** 8 models -- `tre_willow03`, `tre_tree01_big`, `tre_bamboo04`,
  `oas_hot_tree_stone` and the four `demon_wall_deco*` -- whose stored binds are not a root shift.
  By our readers, the client's rule would draw them off their meshes (58.4, 32.6, 0.57, 0.48, 0.54),
  with nothing to undo it (scale 1.0). Either retail draws them off, or one of our readers is
  wrong; to settle against retail. They keep the composed bind meanwhile.
- **OPEN:** `arabianf_bujok03`'s remaining 8.7.
- **Character path (pre-existing):** 35 monster skeletons are the portal's own case and are drawn
  offset today (`mustafa` 50.17, `event_winter_whiteknight` 48.16, …); 313 item, 3 COS and 3
  artifact skeletons have the mismatch too. Its own `docs/TODO.md` item.

### Review fixes (independent review `0b2809ba`, `docs/rounds/r721_review.md`)

| 1 | the skeleton-scale explanation is refuted: the map's scale is 1.0 (READ) | recorded READ; the explanation removed from these notes, BSK_FORMAT.md, `skeleton3d_builder.gd`, its test and TODO.md; the 8 models are now unexplained (OPEN, settle against retail) |
| 2 | the root-shift condition is OURS | labelled OURS in `map_animation.gd` (commit's doc) and BSK_FORMAT.md |
| 3 | the TODO undercounted the mismatch | its own TODO item: 35 monsters drawn offset (largest shifts listed), 313 item, 3 COS, 3 artifact |
| 4 | a bone without a usable third pair mixed two bind spaces | `consistent_stored_binds` returns `{}` when any non-root bone lacks a usable stored bind |
| 5 | the probe's column said "stored bind" | renamed "new bind" (the bind as built); the header says passes 1 and 2 used temporary edits |

## Seven-hundred-and-twentieth round: the teleport structures' glows and effects, played as the original plays an object's `ambient` particle mods

The user (2026-10-04): "Most, if not all, of the town teleports have special glows or effects to
them. Find them all in the original code and implement that."

Labels: READ (sro_client.exe), MEASURED (the user's archives, renders), INFERRED, OPEN, OURS.
The full reading and the census are `docs/protocol/teleport_effects.md`.

### What the original does (READ)

- The effects are not a teleport feature: a `.bsr`'s mod section carries **particle mods**
  (`0x30000`, `ModDataParticle::vslot_004` `0xc643b0`), and a placed object plays those of its
  **`ambient`** set: `ModPalette::FUN_00c0b060` gives the set named exactly `ambient`
  (case-sensitive) kind 2, which routes it into the palette's own slot (`FxModManager` `0xc7fcea`),
  the set an object plays with no clip running; a LOD gate (`0xc43780`, 0.9 against the host's
  `+0x7c`) is INFERRED open for buildings (corrected by the review: round 720 first cited
  `FUN_00c7b540`). Every teleport structure's model carries one.
- Each entry: a mode (0 = at a bone, else at an offset in the object's frame), the `.efp`, the
  bone, the offset, a rotation from three angles (`FUN_00c67500`), and a **glow byte** at `+0x50`
  (`CRTModParticle::vslot_001` `0xc77a20`, `FUN_00c81820`, `FUN_00c818c0`, `FUN_00c81190`).
- **The glow pass** (`FUN_00c43100`): an entry with a glow byte is tested every 500 ms with a D3D
  occlusion query (`CVisibleChecker::vslot_002`: one depth-tested point, colour writes off) at its
  position moved toward the camera by (byte - 1); its alpha moves by trunc(ms x 1.5) a frame
  toward 255 or 0 (`FUN_00c81080`); it is drawn with ZENABLE off while the alpha is above 0, and
  the alpha scales each particle colour's alpha byte (`EFEffect::FUN_00c893f0` `0xc8affd`). The
  pass is the **Light Effect** video option (the manager's `+0x1a4`, set through the thunk
  `0xbbdad0` from `SWorld::vslot_043` case 0xb -- round 720 first read it as always on); off, the
  effect draws as an ordinary particle. A test point behind the eye or off screen is clipped and
  counts hidden. Only effects whose object is drawn this frame are stepped.

### Census (MEASURED)

Every town gate carries ambient effects; Jangan's are on `cj_portal_stone` beside `cj_portal`.
Glow bytes: Jangan 25/13, Donwhang 41/49, the thief village 15, Constantinople's
`euro_constan_center` 95; Hotan, Samarkand and Alexandria's are 0 (drawn normally). The guild
gates (fort, charge, glory, revival) carry their own (`guild\gate_potal`, `light_gate_blue` turned
four ways, ...). Table in teleport_effects.md. Across the archive 1,300 `.bsr` carry an `ambient`
set (lamps, torches, fountains...).

### What was built

- `BsrReader.ParticleMod` / `ParticleEntry` / `particle_mods()`: the reader (the skip it replaces
  measured the same length).
- `ObjectLoader`: a committed object keeps its `ambient` entries as meta.

## Seven-hundred-and-nineteenth round: a character pending deletion is one translucent sheet on the select screen (blended in Godot's linear buffer, not in the original's display values)

The user (2026-10-04), on the native Linux build: "There also seems to be some rendering issues
when deleting a character that weren't there original. When they sit some parts of them become
transparent." Their two screenshots of our client show the select screen with a character pending
deletion, seated: arms, dress, face and a shoulder strap show the harbour through them, unevenly.
They run the native `opensro-linux.zip` (Godot Forward+ on Vulkan), the renderer the render box
uses, so the box reproduces it.

Labels: READ (the client exe, with addresses), MEASURED, INFERRED, OURS, DEPARTURE.

### What the original does (READ, sro_client.exe)

- **The pending alpha.** `FUN_0085def0` sets a pending character's target alpha to **0xcc**
  (`+0x298`; 0xff otherwise), fading over 1.0 s (round 684). The per-frame update
  (`0x85dc8a..0x85dd17`) hands the current byte (`+0x29a`) to the model through its vtable `+0x14`:
  **`CCompoundObj` slot 5, `CCompChar::FUN_00c25590`, `+0x4c = alpha << 24`**.
- **How a model below 0xff is drawn: `CObjRendererVS::FUN_00c428c0`** (objdump), called by the
  object draws (`0xbf110b` and four more sites) with the colour (`[esi+0xc8]+0x40` when that
  object exists, else the compound's `+0x4c`) and the layer's flag word (`material + 0x70`):
  - at `0xff000000` it returns at once;
  - otherwise ALPHABLENDENABLE 1, SRCBLEND 5 (SRCALPHA), DESTBLEND 6 (INVSRCALPHA), TEXTUREFACTOR =
    the colour; with alpha testing on, ALPHAREF = `ref x a >> 8`;
  - stage 0 alpha: flag `0x40000000` gives ALPHAOP SELECTARG2 (ARG2 TFACTOR: the fade alone);
    without it, ALPHAOP MODULATE of TEXTURE and TFACTOR (texture alpha x fade);
  - **ZWRITEENABLE is not touched**: the body writes depth, mesh by mesh in its own order.
  - In `CObjRendererVS::FUN_00bf0e20` the object's mods (`FUN_00c451e0`), then the flag word's
    states, then the fade are set in that order, so the fade's blend and stage-0 alpha override an
    MTRL mod's own (round 719's review, finding 6).
- **Where `0x40000000` comes from** (the review, READ in Data.pk2 and the asm): no `.bmt` layer of
  `Prim\Mtrl\Item` or `Prim\Mtrl\Char` has it (3,263 layers). Its sources are runtime mods:
  `CRTModEnvMap::vslot_004` ORs `0x60000000` into every material of an env-mapped object, and
  `CRTModProgEquipPow::vslot_004` ORs `0xe21f0000` for enhanced gear. So a plain body or item layer
  is drawn at `tex.a x 0.8`, and an env-mapped or enhanced one at 0.8 exactly.
- **Not a render mode.** `appear_fade.md` said `FUN_00aac913` "picks a render mode" from the
  compound's `+0x4c`. The code at `0xaacafd` compares a bitmap header's channel masks to pick a
  texture format: there **0x20 = D3DFMT_A8B8G8R8, 0x21 = D3DFMT_X8B8G8R8** (B mask 0xff0000, G
  0xff00, R 0xff; A8R8G8B8 0x15 / X8R8G8B8 0x16 are the other branch, `0xaaca92`/`0xaaca7a`).
  Unrelated to the model's alpha; corrected in `appear_fade.md`.
- **The shadow of a character at 0xcc** is not read (`appear_fade.md`, OPEN).

### The cause (MEASURED)

Since round 684 the select screen set `GeometryInstance3D.transparency` on every mesh. The bodies
wear PlayerPortrait's materials (`unshaded, <cull>, depth_draw_opaque`, no blend). Instance
transparency sends each mesh to Godot's transparent pass, where `depth_draw_opaque` writes **no
depth**, sorted mesh by mesh: far pieces of the body blend over near ones and two-sided cloth shows
its back faces. Measured below as the linear-sheet residual of the "before" rows.

### The fix

`CharSelectStage._apply_alpha`: below 255 every mesh draws through a pair made from its own
material (`fade_code`, `_fade_pair`):
- a **depth pass** (the material's shader with `blend_mix, depth_draw_always`, `ALPHA = 0.0`, alpha
  test kept) at render priority **0**, so the terrain's overlays and water (-3) and the shadow
  catcher (-2) are drawn first and stay behind her;
- its **colour pass** as `next_pass`, at the source's priority **+ 1**: `blend_mix` (also over a
  mod's own blend, READ above), `depth_draw_never`, and the original's stage-0 alpha: `ALPHA =
  mix(1.0, t.a, select_use_tex) * select_fade` -- texture alpha x fade, or the fade alone for an
  object with an env-map mod (`SkinnedBsrAssembler.ENV_MAPPED_META`, set from the BSR's
  `env_map_flags`, carried by PlayerPortrait's copy). A blending layer that writes no depth gets the
  colour pass only; a blending mod that writes depth keeps a depth pass.
- a **shadows-only twin** of each faded mesh on its own materials, so the body keeps its shadow
  (OURS: as before this round, at full strength; the original's is not read).

At alpha >= 254.5 every mesh gets its own material back and its twin is freed.

**DEPARTURE: the blend is in Godot's linear buffer, the original's in display values.** The
original mixes `0.8 x O + 0.2 x B` in the D3D9 back buffer; Forward+ blends before its Filmic tone
map. Doing the original's arithmetic in the colour pass would need what lies behind her in display
values: `hint_screen_texture` is captured after the opaque pass (INFERRED from Godot 4.2's
documented behaviour, not read in its source), so the transparent water, overlays and shadow catcher
behind her would be missing from it -- finding 1's error again. Not done; measured below.

ProgEquipPow (enhanced gear) is not drawn by this client, so an enhanced item takes `tex.a x 0.8`
where the original takes 0.8: OPEN.

### Measurements (MEASURED)

`OPENSRO_QA_PENDING_PROBE=1` selects the pending character, holds pose and camera, and saves one
frame hidden (bg1), at 255 (O), at 0xcc (P), at 1/255 and hidden again (bg2).
`OPENSRO_QA_SELECT_INSTANCE_FADE=1` draws the old way on the same build. QA_Aria (woman, dress,
seated) pending, hour pinned (`OPENSRO_QA_TITLE_HOUR`), bloom off (`OPENSRO_QA_VIDEO=bloom=0`), box
RX 7600 Forward+ 1280x720. Body pixels: |O-B| >= 90 (RGB sum) with a still background. Residuals are
|P - prediction|, RGB sum. Script: `/var/tmp/r719/r719_alpha.py`.

| hour | drawing | one sheet (linear): median / p90 / p99 / >15 | original's mix 0.8 O + 0.2 B: median / p90 / p99 / >15 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0.5833 | before | 1.4 / 33.7 / 181.5 / 19.4 % | 17.0 / 50.0 / 183.0 / 54.2 % |
| 0.5833 | after | **1.0 / 4.5 / 25.3 / 1.7 %** | 13.6 / 31.6 / 56.2 / 45.3 % |
| 0.75 | before | 1.3 / 32.6 / 173.7 / 18.0 % | 17.4 / 39.6 / 180.6 / 56.5 % |
| 0.75 | after | **1.0 / 4.6 / 23.5 / 1.7 %** | 14.6 / 29.2 / 50.2 / 48.2 % |
| 0.9583 | before | 1.5 / 17.7 / 118.4 / 12.0 % | 9.8 / 24.8 / 132.8 / 26.2 % |
| 0.9583 | after | **1.1 / 4.1 / 23.9 / 1.4 %** | 8.2 / 19.4 / 40.4 / 17.2 % |

- **One sheet.** After the fix the frame is one sheet blended in Godot's linear buffer to within 25
  levels (RGB sum) in 99 % of body pixels at every hour; before, 12-19 % of pixels were off by
  more than 15 (the pieces drawn over each other). The numbers no longer depend on the hour.
- **The original's own blend** (DEPARTURE): after the fix 17-48 % of body pixels are more than 15
  from `0.8 O + 0.2 B`, median 8-15; that is the linear-vs-display difference, largest at bright
  hours.
- **The 1/255 check** (the review's finding 1): at alpha 1/255, inside the body, no pixel is off the
  background by more than 15 at any hour (the review measured 1,010 with the depth pass at -100);
  257 / 151 / 29 pixels exceed the strict 1/255 allowance by a few levels, which the linear blend's
  dark-end gain explains.
- **The shadow** (`OPENSRO_QA_VIDEO=bloom=0,shadow_detail=2`, `OPENSRO_QA_PENDING_SHADOWS=1`, hour
  0.5833): at 0xcc no pixel the body changes at 255 is back at the bare ground (0, as before the
  round; the review measured 2,679 without the twins); 14 shadow twins. At 1/255 the shadow is
  still at full strength in both old and new (3,190 / 3,189 pixels off by more than 15): kept, not
  faded (OURS above).
- **Fade-in frame time** (`OPENSRO_QA_SELECT_FADEIN_FRAMES=1`, the longest wall-clock frame over the
  first 3.0 s after the scene is usable, movie-maker mode writing PNGs): before 188.8 / 192.4 /
  196.6 / 196.2 ms, after 193.0 / 190.3 / 195.2 / 187.3 ms. The pairs add no measurable hitch above
  the frame the scene already has at that point; the first "after" run (cold for the new shaders)
  is 4 ms above its "before".
- The first measurement of this round (before the review) did not pin the hour; its table and its
  "four-fold" claim are withdrawn.

### Texture alpha on the bodies tested (MEASURED, `QA PENDING TEXTURE`)

Over each texture image (not its UV surface): QA_Aria's clothes have no alpha; skin and face
average 0.991. The sword's texture (an atlas, `sword1_2_3.bmt`, layer flag `0x340`: 128 alpha test)
averages 0.330 over the whole image, and the hair (`0x341`: alpha-tested, two-sided, not blended)
0.781 -- those are mostly the cut-out areas, not what is drawn. The kept texels' alpha over the
UV surface was not measured; with the fix they draw at `tex.a x 0.8` as the original's do.

### Review fixes (independent review `ef5cab72`, `docs/rounds/party719_review.md`)

| # | finding | fix |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | depth pass at -100 hides the water, overlays and shadow catcher behind her | depth at 0, colour at source + 1; the probe's 1/255 shot checks it: 0 pixels off by more than 15 |
| 2 | no shadow from the pairs | shadows-only twin on the own materials (full strength, as before; OURS until the original's is read); measured with Shadow Detail on |
| 3 | measurement compared different hours | re-measured at three pinned hours, bloom off, against the linear-sheet prediction; old table and "four-fold" withdrawn |
| 4 | linear vs display blend | not feasible with the screen texture (it lacks the transparent background); labelled DEPARTURE with the numbers; the title corrected |
| 5 | texture alpha, flag 0x40000000 | colour alpha = `tex.a x fade`, the fade alone for an env-mapped object (READ rule); ProgEquipPow OPEN; hair/sword wording corrected |
| 6 | fade overrides a mod's blend | the colour pass is `blend_mix` whatever the layer's blend; a z-writing mod keeps a depth pass |
| 7 | D3DFMT names | A8B8G8R8 / X8B8G8R8 |
| 8 | stale header comment | points at `_apply_alpha`'s pairs |
| 9 | unfade relied on the lerp landing on 255 | unfade at alpha >= 254.5 |
| 10 | fade-in cost unmeasured | measured: no hitch above the existing ~190 ms frame; the depth pass keeps the full fragment (not shortened) |

### Regressions checked

- Only the select screen draws this way: it is the only writer of `GeometryInstance3D.transparency`
  on a body in `client/scripts`; in-game characters (sitting included) and the world's fades are not
  on this path. This round also adds one `set_meta` per body material built from a BSR with an

## Seven-hundred-and-eighteenth round: the user's party-matching report -- the stale listing, the ticked borders, the low digits, the Purpose value

The user's report (2026-10-04), with a screenshot of OpenSRO's Party Matching window
(`/root/opensro-handoff/party_refs/bug2_tcT9woa.png`) against their screenshots of the original
(`02_BQfjkpc.png`, `06_ZQRvaFg.png`, `07_YbXSuv5.png`):

> the name input field, the bottom border appears inaccurate. It shows vertical lines when it
> should be horizontal. The same goes for the bottom of the window for the party listings and
> level input fields. Also the numbers should be centered in the black boxes but they're too
> low. Also in the purpose tab the original game has the text aligned to the right and then
> hides the left of the text that would overflow ... let's replicate it for now. I also found a
> bug ... if I character add a party to listing while viewing the party matching then have a
> player leave and join (the party is supposed to be removed from matching and it was) and that
> new player creates a party in party matching so you see two parties. You can delete the first
> because it says it doesn't exist anymore and even hitting refresh or reopening the window does
> fix it.

Read as: the stale first entry **cannot** be deleted ("doesn't exist", `0x2c1c`), and Refresh or
reopening does **not** clear it. Labels: READ, MEASURED, INFERRED, OURS.

### 1. The stale listing: the client never let go of its own registration

**Cause (READ).** OpenSRO's `PartyMatchState` keeps the player's own registration pinned to the
top of the list (`0x97b950`) and cleared it only on a `0xb06b` for its own number or an empty
page. Nothing cleared it when the party went away. A leader whose party dissolved -- which the
server answers by dropping the entry, as the user saw -- kept the old row pinned; a page whose
row 0 is someone else's leaves the pin (`0x8841f0`), so Refresh and reopening kept it; and
Delete entry sent the old number, which the server refuses `0x2c1c` ("doesn't exist").

**What the original does (READ, `UI_PARTY::FUN_00886b10`, the `0x3864` handler).** Every clear is
`0x97c960(0)` -> `0x97c3b0`; the argument is 0 because `ebp` is zeroed at `0x886b64` and pushed
unchanged at `0x886ea4` and `0x88719f` (and `push 0` at `0x886f6f`):

| `0x3864` | the registration |
|---|---|
| kind 1, dissolved | cleared (`0x8871a7`); its number leaves the window's list and the window redraws (`0x73a700`, `0x73a770`) |
| kind 3, the player left | cleared (`0x886eaa`); the number is NOT dropped from the list (the `*piVar5 == 0` test skips `0x73a700`; review F7) |
| kind 3, someone else left, the player out of a party | cleared and dropped from the list (`0x886f76`, `0x73a700`, `0x73a770`) |
| kind 3, someone else left, still in a party | its member count becomes the party's (`+9` <- `0x986f50()+0x10`, the source the echo `0x97c530` fills the count from), and its row redraws (`0x73a980`) |
| kind 2, joined | the same count update |
| kind 9, new leader | renamed: the new leader's name into the registration's `+0x10` Name, then its row redraws (`0x8871d0`..`0x8872a2`; the review's F1) |

The list steps are gated on `0x799680` (= `0x8b51f0(0x82, 1)`, the matching window as a child of
the interface), which the original builds once with the interface, so they always run there.
None of these paths calls the Set lock `0x6d5ab0` (its four callers are `0x79c252`, `0x79c2fd`,
`0x880268`, `0x884040`), so Set stays as it was.

**Fix.** `PartyState` signals each applied event (`party_event(kind, jid)`, not for kind 6);
`PartyMatchWindow` passes it to `PartyMatchState.on_party_event`, which applies the table above.
Disconnected in `dispose()` with the window's other hooks (round 714's B6).

### 2. The ticked bottom borders: a six-piece frame's top and bottom are its sides turned on their side

**Cause (READ + MEASURED).** The black boxes are `com_blacksquare_` CIFStretchWnds: the three
search boxes (99,75,90,20; 394,75,36,20; 443,75,36,20) and the list (25,119,735,305). That set
has six pieces -- no `mid_up`/`mid_down` -- and the builder reused `left_side` for the top and
`right_side` for the bottom, tiled **upright**. `right_side` is 4x4 with a grey column 3
(`#7B797B`; MEASURED from the archive's DDS) and black elsewhere, so tiled along the bottom it
put a grey dot every 4 px: the "vertical lines". (`left_side`'s column 0 is near-black,
`#080808`, so the top's ticks were invisible.)

**What the original does (READ).** CNIFStretchWnd's two UV slots (`0x49b1e0`, `0x49b200`; no
direct callers, so virtual) both call the corner UVs `0x49a140` with mode 2 and the edge UVs
`0x49a410` with mode 3. `0x49a410` is a jump table at `0x49a7b8` (cases `0x49a417`, `0x49a4f8`,
`0x49a5f1`, `0x49a6b0`); the quad layout `0x499e10` puts quads 0-3 at the corners (LT, RT, RB,
LB) and 4-7 on the edges (left, top, right, bottom), each vertex 6 floats with u, v at +0x10 and
+0x14. Decoded by simulating the x87 stack over the asm:

| mode 3 (`0x49a6b0`) | TL | TR | BR | BL |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| left | (0,0) | (1,0) | (1,1) | (0,1) |
| top | (0,1) | (0,0) | (1,0) | (1,1) |
| right | (0,0) | (1,0) | (1,1) | (0,1) |
| bottom | (0,1) | (0,0) | (1,0) | (1,1) |

The top and bottom are the texture turned 90 degrees clockwise (a texture column becomes a
screen row), and the sizes are copied across swapped (`[0x788]=[0x784]`, `[0x78c]=[0x780]`,
`[0x798]=[0x794]`, `[0x79c]=[0x790]`): the top's thickness is `left_side`'s width, the bottom's
`right_side`'s. Mode 2's corners are each drawn upright with their own texture. So the bottom
strip's last row is `right_side`'s grey column: a line.

**Fix.** `UiBuilder._build_frame` turns a reused side piece 90 degrees clockwise
(`rotated_cw`, cached per texture) for a six-piece set's top and bottom, at that side's width.
Every six-piece base in the archive's layouts is a CIFStretchWnd (MEASURED over all 248
`resinfo` files: `com_blacksquare_` 105 CIFStretchWnd + one CIFGuildGrantPower + one
CIFMultiLetter; `com_lattice_outline_` 14; `com_square_` 1). `com_lattice_outline_` -- the
border around the inventory's, storage's, exchange's and store's item grids -- had the same
fault: its sides are vertical stripes (`#100C10 #393839 #101410 #000000` by column; MEASURED), so
its top and bottom were drawn as fine ticks, and are now horizontal bands, matching its own
`left_up` corner, whose row 1 is the band (`#313431`).

### 3. The low digits

**Cause.** Two separate things:
- The edits (Name, the two Level boxes) were Godot LineEdits with Godot's default style, a padded
  box whose minimum height (content margins plus the 17 px line) is taller than the layouts'
  11-15 px edit rects. Godot clamps a control's size to its minimum, so the edit grew and
  centred its text 4-5 px low. The client's edit draws no box of its own (every one sits on art:
  here `com_bg_tile_e` inside the black frame), and the layouts give VAlign 0.
- The page spin's value label is set to its READ rect (16,4) 18x12, but a Godot Label is never
  shorter than its line (17 px), so it grew downward and its centred text sat low.

**Fix.** `UiBuilder._build_edit` gives a CIFEdit no box (StyleBoxEmpty for normal, focus and
read_only, as `TwoDtBuilder._edit` already did) and the layout's FontIndex face, size and
colour, so it settles at its line with the text from the rect's top. The spin's label is laid by
`place_label` on its rect (the client's centred overrun, as every static's text is). How CIFEdit
applies HAlign was not read, so the edits' horizontal alignment is unchanged.

### 4. The Purpose value

The user's description of the original: right-aligned, an overflow hidden on its LEFT. The
combo's drawing code was not read; this follows the description, labelled so. A Godot Button
clips a too-long text on its right, so the OptionButton keeps the clicks and the list and draws
no text, and the value is a Label in a clipping box over the combo's READ text rect
`{5, 0, W-30, H}` (`OptionVideoPage.combo_text_rect`), its right edge on the box's.

### Tests

- `party_match_test.gd`: the stale-listing mechanism (a page of someone else's rows leaves the
  pin), every event branch above, and `PartyState` signalling kind 1. All pass.
- `party_match_window_test.gd`: after a dissolve only the new entry is listed; a CIFEdit's three
  styles are empty and pad nothing; the Purpose value's right edge is the text rect's and a
  too-long value overflows on the left inside the clip. All pass.
- `ui_builder_test.gd`: a synthetic six-piece set whose `right_side` has a grey column 3 draws
  its bottom strip with a grey last ROW (not a column), and `left_side`'s column 0 as the top's
  first row. Passes.

## Seven-hundred-and-seventeenth round: party members on the minimap and the world map

The user (2026-10-04, after v0.1.490): "showing party members on the minimap and map ... Basically
you can see a greenish big dot on the map. The minimap will show an arrow on the edge of the minimap
in the general direction of where each party member is to you. They get their own arrow. Then when
you're close enough you'll see that big green circle again but on the minimap." Their three
screenshots of the original are `/root/opensro-handoff/party_refs/map_*.png`.

Read from the client first (`docs/protocol/party_gui.md` section 9 has every address), then built.

### What the original does (READ unless marked)

- **Minimap** (`CIFMinimap::vslot_013` `0x662bd0`, the party loop `0x6643a0..0x664ad1`):
  - **Who:** every member but the player, **with the player's world id** (record `+0x68`
    against `player +0x20e4`), in a region the player can see (a field region from the field, or
    the player's own dungeon: `0x9d5520`).
  - **Position:** the spawned object's position when this client has one, else the record's
    `(x, 0, z)` in its region.
  - **Offset** in map pixels: `(dx, -dz) / 1920 x zoom`.
  - **Dot or arrow:**
    - under **47.0** px (`0xda0ef0`): the 8x8 `mm_sign_party.ddj` at the offset;
    - 47 or more: the 16x16 `mm_sign_partyarrow.ddj`, centred on a fixed 47 px rim along the
      offset, turned by `-(theta + pi)`.
    - In screen terms that turn is `atan2(oy, ox) - pi` (`0xb47c50` acos, `0xb44a10` cos, `0xb44b40`
      sin, all read in the x87 fallbacks).
  - **Per member and order:** each member has its own mark, redrawn every frame, after the other
    signs and the academy marks, then the quest marks (none in OpenSRO), then the player's own
    arrow. All of them draw over the frame and under the buttons (review finding 1).
- **World map** (`CNIFWorldMap::FUN_0061eec0`, the party loop `0x61f8c0..0x61ffce`):
  - **Who and position:** every member but the player (**no** world-id test), at the same position
    source.
  - **The dot:** the 16x16 `wmap_sign_party.ddj` centred on its map pixel, drawn before the
    player's marker.
  - **Hover:** the first member whose dot holds the mouse has its name drawn centred above the dot,
    right after it. The hit area is L + 2 ..= L + 13. In a job party the name reads `*Name`. All
    READ, review findings 2, 3, 5, 6, 10.
- **Measured** (the DDS headers in Media.pk2): `mm_sign_party` 8x8, `mm_sign_partyarrow` 16x16,
  `wmap_sign_party` 16x16, each the size of its quad.

### What was built

- **`client/scripts/ui/hud/party_map_marks.gd`** (`PartyMapMarks`): the rules as pure functions.
  They cover the offset, dot or arrow, the rim centre, the turn, a record's region-local position,
  who each map draws, and the hover rectangle.
- **`hud_minimap.gd`**: `update_party(player_local, members_local)` places one pooled TextureRect
  per member, from two pools. Both sit in one unclipped `MapMarks` root over the window's frame,
  under its buttons, in vslot_013's order: `PartyMarks` (the dots), then `PartyArrows`, then the
  player's arrow (review finding 1).
  
  Every mark is mirrored (`flip_h`) and turned a further -90 degrees, which is the quad's
  transposed texture (see below). `party_marks_report()` serves the QA log and the tests. The old
  comment saying party signs were not drawn is corrected.
- **`hud_worldmap.gd`**:
  - a `PartyMarks` layer under the player's marker (kept there when the place labels are rebuilt);
  - `update_party(region_x, region_y, members_local, names)`, with pooled 16x16 dots placed by the
    player's own world-map rule (`party_world`);
  - the hover name, as a Label;
  - `party_dots_report()` and `party_hover_text()`.
- **`World3D.gd`**:
  - `_fill_party_marks` builds the three per-frame lists (minimap positions, world-map positions,
    names). It counts first, so the packed arrays change size only when the party does. Positions
    come from the spawned body (`_party_body_for_board`) or the record (`PartyMapMarks.record_local`).
  - `_refresh_minimap` passes the lists on.
  - Two QA party steps: `maplog` (both maps' marks in the log) and `wmap` (opens the world map).

### Two things the first live runs caught

- **The quads draw their texture transposed.** The first frame had the north-rim arrow pointing
  east. Each party quad's corners go top-left, top-right, bottom-right, bottom-left with texture
  coordinates (0,0), (0,1), (1,1), (1,0), so screen (x, y) samples texture (y, x) (READ: `fldz` /
  `fld1` at `0x664544` and `0x664720`, the world map's at `0x61f9ee`). The arrow's art points up
  (MEASURED), so it draws pointing west unturned, and the client's turn then sends every arrow
  outward, as in the user's `map_JXHQtcH.png`. A Control does the same with `flip_h` and a further
  -90 degrees (`PartyMapMarks.TRANSPOSE_TURN`); the test checks that an east member's tip points
  east.
- **The rim arrow was hidden.** Centred 47 px out in a 105 px aperture, it was cut by the map's
  rectangular clip and covered by the frame's ring. The user's screenshot shows the original's
  arrow over the ring, so the arrows now draw over the frame (INFERRED, see OURS).
- **Test placement, not a code bug:** the first run placed the bots with `/tp` offsets of 120 and
  100, taking them for the minimap's display units. `/tp` takes the server's world units (z
  mirrored), so the marks showed 10 px and 8.3 px south. The logged inputs matched them exactly.
  The bots were then placed 1200 east and 1000 north.

### OURS

- A dungeon record (`region & 0x8000`) is not marked: OpenSRO sends no dungeon positions.
- The minimap's world test compares against the player's **own party record's** world id, which
  stands in for the player's `+0x20e4`. Without that record nothing is compared.
- A world-map dot off the current map is clipped by the map area (the original's clipping was not
  traced).

## Seven-hundred-and-sixteenth round: every receiver of a share is told what it gained -- retail 0x3056, 0x304E's gold total, and the client's 0x3068 line

The party epic's follow-up to round 712, which left two gaps on the wire: a party member who never
hit a monster gained its share of EXP and skill EXP in silence (its client's gauge did not move
until the next character load), and the client could not read the Item Auto Share notice `0x3068`
the server already sent. The user's standing instruction: as close to the original as possible.
Labels: READ, INFERRED, OPEN, OURS.

### What the original does (READ, both binaries)

Full tables in `docs/protocol/party_protocol.md`, "Rewards: 0x3056 and 0x304E".

- **0x3056** is written at the end of `GObjPC_GainExpAndLevel` (CGObjPC slot 92, `gs:0x4e5250`,
  appends `0x4e583c..0x4e58fa`) and read by `Client_ApplyExpAndLevelUp` (`c:0x8a97c0`) with the
  same widths: u32 source object id, u64 EXP (signed), u64 skill EXP, u8 flags, then two optional
  training-camp blocks keyed on the flags, then a **u16 RemainStatPoint only when the call raised
  the level** (`0x4e58df`). The kill reward calls slot 92 once per receiver with the victim's unique
  id as the source (`0x4eabd2..0x4eabd5`), so **every member a kill pays gets its own 0x3056**.
  Nothing is sent when both amounts are zero (`0x4e5393..0x4e53a1`). At level 110 the EXP in the
  message is clamped to what fits (`0x4e5365..0x4e5390`).
- The client prints, type 1: `UIIT_MSG_STATE_GAIN_EXP` / `_LOSE_EXP` / `_GET_SKILL_EXP`; it floats
  the gain from the source object if it can find it (`+0x759`/`+0x75a` counters).
- **A party gold share** is told with **0x304E kind 1**, not 0x3068: the split `gs:0x5bc7f0` calls
  `CGObjPC::OffsetGold` (slot 91, `0x4e4b60`) with `(amount, 0, 0x17, 1, 1)` for every share,
  which sends `FUN_004e3fb0` kind 1: u8 1, u64 the new total, u8 show. The client (`c:0x8a70d0`)
  prints `UIIT_MSG_STATE_GAIN_GOLD` "[%d]gold gained." with the rise when shown.
- **0x3068 on the client** (`c:0x873990`): the recipient's name from the party list, the item's
  from its name key; `UIIT_MSG_PARTYGET_ITEM_EXPENDABLE` "Item [%s %d pieces]is distributed to
  [%s]." type 4 for another member (every non-gold class), `UIIT_MSG_STATE_GET_ITEM_EXPENDABLE`
  type 1 for the player's own JID, `UIIT_MSG_PARTYGET_GOLD` type 4 for gold.

### What changed

**Server**
- New `server/internal/charmsg`: the 0x3056 and 0x304E kind-1 codecs (flags always 0: OpenSRO has
  no training camp).
- `session/rewardnotice.go` + `killshare.go`: `distributeKill` sends 0x3056 to **every receiver,
  the killer included**, with the EXP its row actually rose by (`expAdded`, the level-cap clamp),
  its skill EXP, and its stat points after a level-up. OpAttackResult's own EXP tail (round 639)
  stays on the wire, so an older client still prints its line; this client no longer reads it for
  that.
- `session/grounditem.go`: gold-share members other than the picker are sent 0x304E kind 1, shown.
  **OURS:** the picker is told by OpenSRO's own pick-up reply, which already prints its line; the
  original sends the picker 0x304E too. The old comment there ("the client prints
  UIIT_MSG_PARTYGET_GOLD") was wrong: that line belongs to 0x3068's gold form, which this server
  never sends.
- `cmd/partybot`: `-mode share` now checks the 0x3056 each bot receives; bot mode gains `-kill
  SPECIES -kill-after D` (once in a party, kill one monster with a real blow).

**Client**
- New `net/reward_notice.gd` (`RewardNoticeNet`): decoders for 0x3056 and 0x304E kind 1, and the
  original's lines as static functions. `PartyNet.decode_item_notice` + `PartyState.item_notice`
  for 0x3068. `NetClient` signals `exp_gained` and `gold_total`.
- `World3D`: prints the gain lines from 0x3056 (not from the attack result any more, so the killer
  is not told twice), the gold line from 0x304E, the 0x3068 line, and refreshes the EXP gauge and
  purse from the server's stats.
- **OURS:** 0x3056's stat-point u16 and 0x3068's item class are taken from the bytes left, where
  the original runs its level arithmetic and item table (equal for every message this server
  writes); the gauge and purse are refreshed from the server rather than advanced locally.

**Fixtures** (`gen_fixtures.py`, the other 60 byte-identical): `3056_kill`, `3056_levelup`,
`3056_lose`, `304e_gold`.

### Tests

- **Go:** `charmsg` round trips; `party` wire test encodes the four new fixtures byte for byte;
  `session`: every share receiver (killer and the member who never hit) gets 0x3056 with its
  payout, a level-up carries the row's stat points, an outsider gets none, a zero award sends
  nothing, a gold-share member gets its total. `go test -count=1 -p 1 ./...`: all packages pass
  (after `DecodeGold` was explained in the orphans gate).
- **GD** (`net/reward_notice_test.gd`, 24 checks): every fixture decoded and re-encoded, the lines,
  the gold clamp, the short-packet drops, PartyState naming the 0x3068 recipient. On the box:
  `check` ALL LOAD (602 scripts), full suite 230 suites, 0 failing.
- **Live, server** (the real binary on the box, in memory, retail leveldata, the round-712
  monsters.csv with ExpToGive, `partybot -mode share -level 18`):

```

[psMate] <- 0x3056 source 26 EXP 29 skill EXP 133 level-up false
[psKill] <- 0x3056 source 26 EXP 29 skill EXP 133 level-up false
    killer +29 EXP, mate +29 EXP; want both trunc(54 x 0.55) = 29
--- 3: an Exp Free-For-All party of two; one member kills
[psFfa] <- 0x3056 source 27 EXP 55 skill EXP 249 level-up false
    killer +55 EXP, idle member +0 EXP; want trunc(54 x 1.03) = 55 and 0
--- all share steps passed
```

  (The idle free-for-all member received no 0x3056, which the scenario now checks.) The scenario's
  ×0.55 check holds only for a monster fewer than 5 levels above the bots (round 712's note); at
  the default `-level 10` against level-20 chakji the party gap bonus applies and the check fails
  by design, so the run uses `-level 18`.

- **Live, client** (`/var/tmp/r716/live.sh` on the box; the stock `qa_shot.sh --server` on the shared
  lock, CLIENT_DIR `/opt/opensro-client-r716`): Bram is the rendered client, levelled to 5 so it may
  create a party, and teleported beside the partybot Killa (level 1). Bram invites Killa (the
  settings' READ defaults give type 0x05, EXP share), Killa accepts and, 8 s later, kills a
  mangnyang with a real blow. Bram never hits. Killa's log:

```
[Killa] <- 0x3080 kind=2 inviter=1 flags=0x05
[Killa] <- 0xb067 [1] jid=2
[Killa] <- 0x3056 source 25 EXP 4 skill EXP 21 level-up false
[Killa] killed MOB_CH_MANGNYANG #25 (HP 54): EXP +4, SP +21
```

  Bram's client log (`/var/tmp/r716/live/godot.log`):

```

SYSLOG [1] [24]skill experience point gained.
World3D: 0x3056 from 25: EXP 9, skill EXP 24
```

  The member who never hit got its own share and its client printed the original's two type-1
  lines. (Bram, level 5, out-levels the level-1 killer by 4 against the same monster, so its share
  is larger.) Getting there took five attempts, each a set-up fault, none the code: the bot
  invited before Bram's `/tp` landed (refused 4, too far), the bot's `/spawn` read its own stale
  `/tp` reply (fixed: queued GM replies are drained before `-kill`), chakji is not in the hand
  roster without a monster table, a level-18 kill of a mangnyang pays 0 (so, as the original does,
  nothing is sent), and a level-1 creator is refused by the level-5 rule. Server log: no errors.
  The frames were deleted; the logs stay on the box.

### Review fixes (independent review `83c7e77e`, `docs/rounds/party716_review.md`)

No BUG and no REGRESSION; six DEPARTURE/MINOR findings, all fixed as close to the original as read.

| # | finding | fix | test |
|---|---|---|---|
| F1 | 0x3056 went out before the level-up announcements; the original sends it last (`GObjPC_SetLevel` 0x4e4d90 sends 0x3054 and the HP/MP update first) | `distributeKill` sends a non-killer its OpLevelUp, then 0x3056; the killer's 0x3056 rides on its AttackResult (an unencoded field) and the attack path sends it after OpAttackResult and OpLevelUp (`combat.go`, and the status-tick kill in `status.go`). OpLevelUp is OpenSRO's own 0x0067 rather than 0x3054 | `TestKillShareSendsExpGainToEveryReceiver` reads Bram's packets in wire order: OpLevelUp before 0x3056; the killer gets none from `distributeKill` |
| F2 | the 110 clamp is keyed on the STARTING level (`0x4e52c7`); `expAdded` also clamped an award crossing into 110 | `killPayout.startLevel`; `expGainFor` sends the award, and `expAdded` only when the receiver started at `MaxCharacterLevel` | `TestExpGainClampsOnlyAtTheCap` |
| F3 | the gold line's base was overwritten by every stats reply, including unprompted regen pushes that can land between the split's credit and its 0x304E | `NetClient` counts its own stats requests (`last_stats_reply_requested`); the base is seeded by the first reply, then moved only by 0x304E and by replies this client asked for, never by a push. **OURS** beyond the original's purse (gold messages only): OpenSRO's shop, trade and storage still change gold without a 0x304E, and their requested refresh keeps the base true | box suite; reasoning recorded in `World3D._on_world_stats` |
| F4 | the killer sent two or three stats requests per kill | `_request_world_stats` is coalesced to one deferred request a frame (as `_refresh_stat_panel`) | box suite |
| F5 | the original also sends 0x304E kind 1 on a solo gold pick-up, unshown, and the split credits the picker too | READ and sent: a solo pick-up's credit `gs:0x4eaca0` calls `OffsetGold(amount, 0, 0x19, 1, 0)` (unshown); the split calls `OffsetGold(share, 0, 0x17, 1, 1)` for **every** share, the picker's included (shown). Both are sent now; the spec carries the table. The picker's own item-move reply (`0xB034`, `FUN_004e9480`) prints GAIN_GOLD from its own u32 (`c:0x87bedc..0x87bf20`); whether that is the pile or the share was not traced (**OPEN**), so OpenSRO's pick-up reply keeps printing the share | `TestGoldPickUpTellsEveryShare` |
| F6 | no handler-level test of the gold split | `TestGoldPickUpTellsEveryShare` drives `GroundItemHandler` (added to the party test world): an Item Auto Share pick-up of 1001 gives the picker 501 and both members one shown 0x304E with their rows' totals; a character outside the party hears nothing; a solo pick-up sends the picker an unshown one. A share that failed to credit is not driven (the memory store cannot be made to fail one credit) | itself |

After the fixes: the first full Go run caught two things, both fixed. `TestGroundDropAndPickUpFlow`
read the solo gold pick-up's new 0x304E as its pick-up result (the credit's 0x304E comes first),
so it now checks the unshown 0x304E and then the result. And the orphans gate flagged
`sendExpGain`, unused once F1 moved every send onto a session in hand, so it was removed. Then
`go test -count=1 -p 1 ./...` all packages pass; on the box (shared lock) `check`
ALL LOAD (602 scripts) and the full suite 230 suites, 0 failing; `partybot -mode share -level 18`
passes again (the mate's 0x3056 29/133 equals its row's rise, the idle member gets none). No
orphaned processes.

### Left open

- The gain floated from the source object (`+0x759`/`+0x75a`, a log-scale bucket): not built.
- The death penalty still refreshes from stats instead of sending its negative 0x3056.
- 0x304E's other kinds (2 skill points, 3 stat points, 4 the berserk count, 0x10) are not spoken;
  the client still learns those from OpenSRO's stats reply.
- What u32 the original's `0xB034` gold pick-up reply carries for a split picker (pile or share).

No perf gate: a message handler and system lines, no per-frame code.

**Review** (kept beside the notes): `docs/rounds/party716_review.md` (no BUG or REGRESSION; six departures and minors -- the level-up/0x3056 order, the 110 clamp, the gold line's base, coalesced stats requests, the solo 0x304E, a handler test -- all fixed).

No perf gate: no per-frame code changed (message handlers and system lines).

## Seven-hundred-and-fifteenth round: the party member boxes on the HUD

The HUD half of the party epic's last client lane. Built on `int/party` (`85e6c063`: S1 round
710, C1 round 711, S3 round 713, each with its review fixes) against `party_gui.md` §7, with
every rule re-read in `sro_client.exe` (the box's `/var/tmp/decomp_client`, objdump on the exe,
floats read from `.rdata`). Labels: READ (the binary), MEASURED (the archives / frames),
INFERRED, OURS, OPEN.

### What was built

- **`ui/hud/hud_quick_party.gd` (HudQuickParty)**, CIFQuickPartyWnd, built in code
  (`ifquickpartywnd.txt` is not loaded), each slot `resinfo\ifquickpartyslot.txt`:
  - **The board** (READ `0x6dae90`): at `GDR_QUICKPARTYBOARD`'s 4,137; one 122x40 slot
    (`0x6da110`) per member other than the player, in the party manager's order, skipping the
    player by name; slot n at (13 + column, row), the row stepping 73 with the buff option on and
    56 with it off; a new column 133 to the right when (screen height - board y - row - 73) <
    230. Out of a party: no slots, hidden.
  - **The slot's art**: `window_all.ddj`, u 0.723633..0.842773 x v 0.138672..0.216797 (READ
    from the four floats `0xda5438`/`0xda973c`/`0xda9740`/`0xda9738`) = the 122x40 round-faced
    box at 741..863 x 71..111 of the atlas (MEASURED, decoded). Round 709's spec had the pairs
    swapped (a 641x300 region of other panels): corrected in `party_gui.md`.
  - **Name, HP and MP gauges, the leader's red flag** (`0x6d9250`, `0x6d7db0`: the flag iff
    the party's leader id is the member's); the race mark stays hidden (never taken).
  - **Two mastery icons** (17x17 at -3,39 and 15,39) from the record's two mastery ids through
    `skillmasterydata.txt` (icon column 11, the name code resolved as the tooltip). Since the
    review: retail's rule exactly -- the second icon is hidden by the per-slot reset and shown iff
    its record exists; the first is never hidden once shown (a reused slot keeps it), a retail
    defect reproduced (READ, `0x6d8630`, `0x6d9495`, `0x6d951b`).
  - **The 3D portrait**: a PlayerPortrait at the slot's 64x64 buffer (`0x9edae0(0x40,0x40)`),
    the PMI camera (`0x6d8bf0`: Bip01 Head +1.0, yaw 0.2, distance 6.5, 30 deg), through the
    `qpt_face.ddj` disc. The body is the slot's own model built from the record's model id with
    ANI_POSE (`0x6d80d0`), so a member has a face spawned or not -- bare, since the model id
    carries no equipment. Re-rendered only when the model id changes (the dirty byte `+0x3dc`).
    The party window's member rows borrow it (`HudPartyPane.member_portrait`, `0x6dab10` ->
    `0x6d7f30`).
  - **The "far away" overlay** (READ `0x6db380`, `0x6d86e0`): each frame the squared 3D
    distance to the member's spawned body, else to the record's region/x/z **at y = 0**
    (`local_8` stays 0: the record's y is not used), stepped only in an exp-share party: level 5
    from 1e6 (double), 4 from 810000, 3 from 640000, 2 from 490000 (double), 1 from 360000, each
    `>=`; `qpt_face_faraway_60..100.ddj` on GDR_QPS_STATUS (MEASURED 28x28 discs, alpha
    130..241: five steps, no fade).
  - **The caution effects** (READ `0x6d90e0`): HP/MP below 0.3 (`0xd82f00`) with the record's
    byte `+0x58` = 0, then by the game option bytes +0x12 / +0x13; hidden at level 5. The 8
    frames (4x2 of 64x32) at one per 100 ms: "Speed 100" read as ms a frame is INFERRED.
  - **Buffs** (READ `0x6d9250`'s tail, `0x6d9010`): only for a member spawned in this client and
    with option +0x08 on; the member's skill buffs and abnormal states (the target window's own
    source), re-read every 1000 ms (`0xb93320(1, 0x3e8)`); otherwise cleared. The grid: 6 a row
