## Seven-hundred-and-fourteenth round: the party-matching client

The client side of party matching on the retail messages: the Party Matching window, the Form
party / Change entry dialog, the auto-match dialog, the delete question, the leader's join popup
and the requester's joining window. It sits on round 710 (S1, the party core), round 711 (C1, the
client party net and window) and round 713 (S3, the party-match server), with their review fixes
(`int/party` at `85e6c063`). Spec: `docs/protocol/party_gui.md` §3-§5, `party_protocol.md`'s
party-match rows and round 713's notes. Labels: **READ** (sro_client.exe), **MEASURED**,
**INFERRED**, **OURS**, **USER DECISION**.

### What is built

- **`net/party_match.gd` (`PartyMatchNet`)**: the codecs, one encoder and decoder per message:
  `0x7069`/`0x706a` entry, `0xb069`/`0xb06a` echo, `0x706b`/`0xb06b`, `0x706c`/`0xb06c` (page
  count, then index, then the rows: `c:0x8841f0` reads them in that order), S->C `0x706d` (job id,
  requester JID, entry, two masteries, job state, member record), `0x306e` and `0xb06d`. The
  window rules as pure functions: the `*name` alias, the Search filter, the job's allowed
  purposes, the auto-match candidate test, the default-title and label keys.
- **`net/party_match_state.gd` (`PartyMatchState`)**: registered on NetClient through round 711's
  `register_handler` hook (net_client.gd is untouched). It applies the replies:
  - a page (`c:0x8841f0`, READ): row 0 whose name is the key (the leader's name in a party, the
    player's own otherwise) becomes the player's registration (`0x97c960`); later rows with that
    name are skipped; every other row is a record. A `[2][code]` page is a coded line;
  - `0xb069`/`0xb06a` OK: the registration from the echo (`0x97c530`: race from the player's
    model, members 1 or the party's count), RECORD_COMPLETE / MODIFY_COMPLETE on the warning
    banner (`0x77b580` -> `0x7b3eb0`, GDR_WARNING_WND). The dialog closes on OK (`0x73f370`'s
    vslot `0xac`), not here: `0x73f300` is the `CPartyRegData` constructor (review D1, W4);
  - `0xb06b`: the own number clears the registration (`0x97c960(0)`); the line is DELETE_COMPLETE,
    or DELETE_COMPLETE2 when the client deleted it because the party filled (`DAT_00eeb8c8`);
  - `0xb06d` (`c:0x8847d0`): joined -> JOIN_COMPLETE_MASTER on the banner, the auto run ends;
    refused -> CREATE_PARTY_REFUSED, no reply -> JOIN_NOREPLY (type 4); `[2][code]` -> the coded
    line (`0x778190`); a running auto match then tries its next candidate (`0x786e70`) with
    AUTO_PROGRESS, or ends with AUTO_FAILURE; and the joining window closes (`0x884a0c` ->
    `0x7390b0`; the argument is INFERRED 0).
- **`ui/hud/party_match_window.gd` (`PartyMatchWindow`)**: the controller over HudPanels'
  GDR_PARTY_MATCH (built from ifpartymatch.txt as before) and the owner of the boxes. Each
  CIFPartyMatchSlot gets ifpartymatchslot.txt built into it; the columns as party_gui.md §3's row
  table; the own registration pinned in row 0 in (135,233,255); the gold bar
  (`com_bar01select_`) on the selected row; the enable rules (`0x7384a0`); Join (`0x739500`),
  Whisper, Auto match, Form party with its client refusals (`0x7397b0`), Change entry, Delete
  entry; Search (`0x73b780`); Refresh with its 2 s lock; the page spin; page 0 on opening; while
  the joining window is up, the spec's five are disabled (`0x7390b0`); `0x738890`'s seven are
  the auto-run disable (review D8, W3); the full party's own registration deleted by the client
  (`0x7387c0`).
- **The boxes** (`party_match_box.gd` the shared shell; caption at (10, 11), w - 21 x 12, READ
  `0x7400c0`):
  - `party_match_register.gd`: 314x373, caption RECORD / MODIFY, the objective radio READ in
    `0x73f820` (origin 0,0; pitch 0x42; label x 0x16, width 0x32; 4 across: 0xdb3ad0 Hunting,
    0xd9670c Quest, 0xdb3a70 Trade Union, 0xdb3a10 Thief Union), the job restriction, the level
    edits (3 digits, 1..0x6e, "1"/"110"), the type line, the title (max 50, the default by
    objective while a default), OK's two refusals;
  - `party_match_auto.gd`: 314x337, the four radios READ in `0x73e790` (objective as above; race
    origin 0,0, pitch 0x5b, x 0x16, width 0x64, CHN / EUR / Open; exp and item origin 2,2, pitch
    0x14, x 0x14, centred, width 0x64, SHARE / SELF), OK -> up to 10 candidates;
  - `party_match_confirm.gd`: the delete question, GInterface `0x788270`'s MsgBoxSimple (360x151,
    Yes at centre - 81, No at centre + 5, the text box at (30, 65));
  - `party_match_req_join.gd`: the leader's popup (screenshot 08), 360x315, every field from the
    `0x706d` as party_gui.md §4, the 10 s timer answering 2;
  - `party_join_progress.gd`: the joining window (screenshot 09), 365x149, the text with the two
    names, 200 ms ticks over 10 000 ms, closing itself at 10 s.
  The register, auto-match and joining boxes are centred on the screen (`0x798b70`, READ: screen
  w / 2 - w / 2, h / 2 - h / 2).
- **`ui/hud/party_match_qa.gd`**: OPENSRO_QA_PARTY's matching steps (World3D's `_qa_party_do`
  hands unknown verbs to it; the QA block's doc lists them).
- **`server/cmd/partybot`**: `-purpose`, `-min`, `-max`, `-flags`, `-title` for a `-register`
  bot, and `-silent` (leave join requests unanswered), for the renders.

### Strings (MEASURED, textuisystem)

The PML strings carry `<sml2>` markup: `<font color="255,239,218,164">[%s]</font>` and `<br>`.
They are drawn as BBCode in a RichTextLabel, the colour's fourth number dropped (INFERRED from
screenshots 08 and 09, which draw the names opaque).

- Full suite on the box (`RENDER_DIR=/opt/opensro-client-c2t`): 228 suites; the only failure was

## Seven-hundred-and-thirteenth round: party matching on the original's opcodes

The party-match server, built on lane S1's party core (round 710, branch `int/party`) against
round 709's specs (`docs/protocol/party_protocol.md` "Party matching", `party_rules.md` "Party
matching", `party_gui.md` §3-§5). Server only. Lane C2 builds the client windows against the same
golden fixtures.

### What was done

- **`server/internal/party/match.go`**, the ShardManager's half, `party.Matcher`:
  - **Entry numbers** come from a counter that only grows and skips 0. Numbers are never reused
    (SM `0x451290`, `0x44def0`, `manager+0x8c`).
  - **Who holds what.** The Hub records who holds which number with which flags
    (`SetListing`/`ClearListing`). It already moves a departing leader's entry to the new leader
    and drops a dissolved party's (SM `0x44e1a0`, `0x44eb30`). The Matcher keeps the rest of each
    listing (purpose, levels, title, time, the pending mark) by number. It finds the owner through
    the Hub, so the owner is always the current leader.
  - **Register** (SM `0x450680` -> `0x451290`/`0x451110`), in its order:
    `0x2c1b` already listed; then in a party `0x2c20` flags not the party's, `0x2c1d` not the
    leader, `0x2c08` full (the listing takes the party's flags); otherwise the listing carries the
    entry's flags.
  - **Change** (SM `0x450990` -> `0x4513c0`): `0x2c1c` the caller holds no entry; then the entry
    the request names is looked up: `0x2c1c` not found, `0x2c1d` not the caller's, bare 5 when the
    flags differ (fixed in review, finding 3). It replaces the purpose, levels and title and renews the time.
  - **Delete** (SM `0x450ba0` -> `0x451490`): `0x2c1c`, then `0x2c1d`.
  - **Withdraw**: a party-less owner's entry goes when it leaves the world (SM `0x4296f0` ->
    `0x451590`).
  - **Pages** (SM `0x451630`, `0x450d20`):
    - 23 to a page in number order, at most `0xfe` pages; a page past the end becomes page 0;
    - no listings at all gives `[1][0][0][0]`;
    - the requester's own entry, or its party leader's, heads every page and counts one more;
    - an entry whose owner is gone is deleted on the way.
  - **Join request ladder** (SM `0x44f850`), in its order:
    1. `0x2c18` the requester is in a party;
    2. `0x2c25` it holds its own entry;
    3. `0x2c1c` no such entry;
    4. when the entry has a party: `0x2c13`/`0x2c14` full, `0x2c1c` its leader is gone, `0x2c23`
       the leader's job does not match;
    5. `0x2c23` the job does not fit the purpose;
    6. `0x2c1e` level outside [min, max], inclusive;
    7. `0x2c1f` another request is pending;
    8. `0x2c0e` the leader is offline.
    
    On success the entry is marked pending, the requester's state byte becomes 1, and a job waits
    **15 s** (SM `0x79b018`; backstop answer 2, SM `0x420e10`).
- **`server/internal/session/partymatch.go`**, the GameServer's half:
  - **`0x7069`/`0xb069` register.** It runs `CParty::CheckCanCreateForMatch` (GS `0x514170`):
    - `0x2c09` not alive;
    - `0x2c24` a state byte other than 0 or 2;
    - `0x2c0a` level < 5 when in no party, `0x2c1d` not the leader when in one.
    
    Then the purpose rule `0x2c23` (GS `Party_PostRequest` kind 0xa -> `Party_UserMatches`), then
    the Matcher. The success echo carries the entry with the assigned number (GS
    `trs_sm_partyjob::vslot_002 0x46d3a0` reads it into the request's `+0x54`, which
    `0x5bf7d0` writes back) and the requester's party id (GS `0x5bf3ed`).
  - **`0x706a`/`0xb06a` change** (GS `0x514260`): `0x2c09`; `0x2c1d` in a party but not its
    leader; `0x2c1c` no own entry. Then the purpose rule, then the Matcher. The echo is the
    client's entry with the party id overwritten (GS `0x5bf870`).
  - **`0x706b`/`0xb06b` delete** (GS `0x5142c0`): `0x2c09`; `0x2c1c` no own entry. The echo is the
    number the client sent (GS `0x5bf900`, the request's `+0x24`).
  - **`0x706c`/`0xb06c` list**: no GameServer check; the reply is the Matcher's page.
    - Each row carries the owner's name and race, where race is the model's Country (SM
      `0x44f640`, `char+0x250`), via `character.RaceOf(Gender)`.
    - The member count is the owner's party size, or 1 without a party.
  - **`0x706d` join request.**
    - The GameServer's ladder runs first (GS `0x514300`), in this order:
      - `0x2c12` the requester is in a party;
      - success when the state byte is 0 and there is no exclusive interaction;
      - `0x2c1f` with state 1 or 3;
      - `0x2c25` with state 4;
      - `0x2c06` otherwise.
      
      A dead character may ask: the life test accepts 1 or 2.
    - Then the Matcher. A refusal from either half is `0xb06d [2][code]`.
    - On success the leader gets the relayed `0x706d`: job id, requester JID, entry, the two
      masteries, job state 4 and the requester's full record.
  - **`0x306e`**, the leader's answer, resolved as SM `0x44fbe0` and the GameServer's kinds
    0x11, 0xf and 0x10 do:
    - **0 cancel, 2 no reply**: the requester gets `0xb06d [1][answer]`.
    - **1, the requester gone**: the leader gets `[2][0x2c0f]`.
    - **1, the entry gone**: `[2][0x2c1c]` to both.
    - **1, a party-less entry**: a party of the leader and the requester with the entry's flags,
      the leader first (SM `0x44e9c0` -> `0x44e100`). The requester gets `0xb06d [1][1]`
      **twice** (see the correction below), then `announceFormed`.
    - **1, an entry with a party**: the requester and then the leader get `0xb06d [1][1]`, then
      `announceJoined`.
    - **an accept that fails**: `[2][code]` to the requester and to the leader (SM tail
      `0x44fe3b`).
  - **Disconnect**: `PartyMatchDisconnectHandler` withdraws a party-less owner's entry and clears
    a pending requester's state. It runs after `PartyDisconnectHandler` (whose removal moves a
    leader's entry, as SM `0x4296f0` does) and before `WorldDisconnectHandler`, which removes the
    session's character (fixed in review, findings 6 and 7).
  - **Expiry**: `RunPartyMatchSweep` deletes, every 60 s, each entry with no pending request that
    is more than 60 whole minutes old, telling nobody (SM `0x4504c0`; added in review, finding 1).
- **Wiring**: `cmd/server/main.go` builds a `party.Matcher` over the party Hub, adds the handler
  after `PartyHandler` and the disconnect hook before `worldDisconnect`.
- **`cmd/partybot`**:
  - `-mode match`, this round's acceptance run;
  - `-mode bot -register` (list an entry) and `-request NAME` (ask to join NAME's entry once it
    is on page 0). In bot mode, party-match join requests are answered by `-accept`.

### S1 files touched

- `server/internal/party/party.go` (9 lines):
  - a `requests` field on `Hub` and its init;
  - one test in `stateLocked`: a pending join requester is state 1. The GameServer writes 1 when
    it forwards the request (GS `0x5bf570`) and 0 when it fails (GS `0x5bfac0`,
    `MsgHandler_3c01`).
  
  The new `Hub` methods (`ListingOwner`, `setRequest`, `clearRequest`) live in `match.go`.
- `server/internal/systems/orphans_test.go`: twelve round-710 orphan entries removed, because
  they now have callers. `PartyByID` and `ItemShare` stay.
- `server/cmd/partybot/main.go`: the match opcodes added to `isParty`/`describe`, the bot-mode
  options, `-mode match`. The scenario itself is in a new file, `match.go`.
- `session/party.go`, `wire.go` and the fixtures are unchanged. Every encoder S3 uses already
  has a golden fixture: `b069_ok`, `b06b_ok`, `b06c_page`, `b06c_empty`, `706d_to_leader`,
  `b06d_*`, plus the generic `[2][code]` refusal. `0xb06a`'s success has the same layout as
  `0xb069`'s, so no fixture was added. Adding one would change the fixture count that both
  sides' tests check.

### Choices of ours (OURS), each labelled in the code

| what | choice | why |
|---|---|---|
| the job id the popup echoes | a counter that skips 0 | the ShardManager's transaction id; its numbering is its own |
| who may answer a job | only the entry's leader at request time | the engine finds the job by id and does not compare the sender; without this, anyone could accept for a party |
| the pending mark | cleared on every outcome | SM `0x44fbe0` stores 0 to `+0x34` at only three places: a party formed (`0x44ffa8`), a requester joined (`0x45029e`), and answer 0 or 2 with the requester present (`0x4504a4`). It stays set when an accept's requester is gone (`0x44fc64`), its leader is gone (`0x44fcfc`), the formation fails (`0x44ff05`), the leader's party is missing (`0x4500e6`), the join fails (`0x4501a7`), answer 0 or 2 comes with the requester gone (`0x450413`), or the answer is outside 0..2 (`0x44fc0e`). Outside `0x44fbe0` it stays set when SM `0x420e50` drops a gone leader's answer and when authorization fails (`0x421ec0`). Left set, the entry refuses every later request `0x2c1f` and is exempt from expiry |
| an answer whose requester JID is not the job's | dropped silently; the job stays pending | the check itself is READ (SM `0x421ec0`, `cmp [ebx+0x8],esi` at `0x421f3f`). The engine then releases the job and leaves the mark set; ours waits for the real answer or the backstop |
| an expired entry's owner | its state returns to 0 at once (the Hub derives it) | the engine leaves the GameServer's byte at 4 and `pc+0x1cd0` set until a relog, refusing that character `0x2c25`/`0x2c24`. A bug not replicated; on the coordinator's deviation list for the user |
| pages | built at each request from the live state | the engine serves snapshots rebuilt after each change (SM `0x451630`), so its counts can lag. Its builder can also leave an empty trailing page when the last entries are dropped as owner-gone (`[1][1][0][0]` when all were). Neither shows in normal play |
| an answer outside 0..2 | ends the job, no reply | SM `0x44fbe0` asserts and returns |
| an entry moved to a new leader before the answer | the accept is refused `0x2c1c` | the engine keeps the job's original leader (`+0x10`) and would act on that character's party state |
| the requester's two masteries | `topMasteries` (S1's choice) | the engine's pick, GS `0x5a1890`, is OPEN |
| refusals that cannot happen here | the lock (`0x2c06`/`0x2c09`), job mode with an empty alias (5), instances (`0x2c28`), `0x2c26` | OpenSRO has none of those states. `0x2c26` reads `chardata+0x13`, which is OPEN (spec) |

### Corrections to existing records

| record | says | what is true |
|---|---|---|
| `party_protocol.md`, "Party matching", the accept result | "Both requester and leader get `0xb06d [1][1]` (the leader's copy INFERRED from the second send in `0x44fbe0`)" | READ, two cases. **Party-less entry** (SM `0x44ffb3..0x4500a1`): both copies carry the **requester's** JID (`[ebx+0x78]` at `0x44ffc6` and `0x45003d`, `ebx` the requester from `0x44fc3e`). The second goes to the leader's GameServer (`[esp+0x10]+0x1c4` at `0x450081`). That server finds the requester by JID, so with one game server the requester gets it twice and the leader gets none. **Entry with a party** (`0x450333 mov ebx,[esp+0x10]`): the second copy is the leader's. **A failed accept** (`0x44fe3b`): `[2][code]` to the requester, then to the leader |
| `party_protocol.md`, "Party matching", register | the success reply carries the entry | READ: GS `trs_sm_partyjob::vslot_002 0x46d3a0` (kind 10) reads the ShardManager's u32 number into the request's `+0x54`, which `0x5bf7d0` echoes in `0xb069` and stores at `pc+0x1cd0` |
| `party_protocol.md`, "Party matching", join request | the requester's state goes to 1, the error comes back on the relay path | READ in full: a ShardManager refusal reaches the requester through `MsgHandler_3c01 0x4169d0`, which also writes the state byte back to 0 when the inner opcode is `0x706d`. A GameServer refusal never set it |
| `party_protocol.md`, Implementation lanes, S3 row | the register ladder "`0x2c1b`, `0x2c20`, `0x2c1d`, `0x2c08`, level 5" | That list is the ShardManager's half only. The GameServer's `CheckCanCreateForMatch` runs first, in its order: `0x2c09`, `0x2c26`, 5, **`0x2c24`**, then `0x2c0a` (no party) or `0x2c1d` (in a party), then `0x2c28` (GS `0x514170`); then the purpose rule `0x2c23` (GS `0x5bf2a0` kind `0xa`). The code has this order. The ShardManager's in-party order is `0x2c20`, then `0x2c1d`, then `0x2c08` |
| `party_protocol.md:231` (list entry, second u32) and OPEN 2 | "INFERRED a timestamp ... its use is OPEN" | READ: `_time32` seconds since the epoch. The expiry sweep (SM `0x4504c0`) subtracts it from `_time32` (`0x6e3cbc`; difference `0x6c1d40`) and divides by 60 (`0x6c1c40`). Only the client's use (`c:+4`) is OPEN |
| `party_protocol.md`, "Party matching" | nothing on expiry | an entry with no pending request expires after more than 60 whole minutes since its register or change (SM `0x40c703` 60 000 ms timer -> `0x40dd10` -> `0x4504c0`, `cmp eax,0x3c; jle` at `0x45055c`). The engine sends `0x386f [owner JID]` to the owner's GameServer, which has no case for it, so the client is never told |
| `party_protocol.md`, the `0x306e` row | the GameServer reads u32, u32, u8 | and the ShardManager authorizes the answer by the echoed requester JID (SM `0x421ec0`): a mismatch is dropped with no reply |
| `party_protocol.md`, "Party matching", change | change edits the caller's entry | SM `0x4513c0` looks up the number the request names: not found is `0x2c1c`, another owner's is `0x2c1d` |

### Review fixes (independent review `d73f314a`, `docs/rounds/party713_review.md`)

Applied after `git merge int/party`, which brought in S1's review fixes (`991bb1c2`). The one
conflict, in `orphans_test.go`, was resolved to the merged list. S1's `sample` now takes a
previous sample and a time; the `0x706d` record uses its `fullMask`.

| # | finding | fix | test |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | entries never expire | `Matcher.Sweep` and `session.RunPartyMatchSweep`: every 60 s, entries with no pending request older than 60 whole minutes are deleted silently (READ, SM `0x4504c0`). The owner's state returns to 0 through the Hub (OURS; the original leaves it stale until relog) | `TestSweepExpiresAfterSixtyWholeMinutes`, `TestMatchSweepExpiresSilently` |
| 2 | the `0x306e` requester JID is unchecked | an answer whose echoed JID is not the job's requester is dropped silently (READ, SM `0x421ec0`); the leader-only check stays (OURS); the job stays pending (OURS) | `TestMatchAnswerWithTheWrongRequesterIsDropped` |
| 3 | change ignores the number sent | `Change` looks up `e.Number`: `0x2c1c` when it is missing, `0x2c1d` when it is another owner's; the caller-has-no-entry `0x2c1c` stays first | `TestChangeLooksUpTheNumberSent`, `TestMatchChangeNamesTheEntry` |
| 4 | the pending-mark label under-counts | `TakeJob`'s comment and the OURS table list the engine's three clears and every path that leaves the mark set | (labels) |
| 5 | the second u32 is READ seconds | `Listing.Time` is relabelled READ; the spec row and OPEN 2 are in the corrections table | (labels) |
| 6 | a page could delete a logging-out leader's entry | `cmd/server` runs `partyDisconnect`, then `partyMatchDisconnect`, then `worldDisconnect`, the original's order. `rowLocked` also skips, without deleting, an owner out of the world who is still in a party | `TestPageSkipsAPartyLeaderOutOfTheWorld`, `TestMatchLeaderLogoutMovesTheEntry` |
| 7 | a requester's mark survived its logout | `Matcher.Disconnect` clears it; the job stays, so an accept answers the leader `[2][0x2c0f]` | `TestDisconnectClearsTheRequestMark`, `TestMatchRequesterLogoutClearsTheMark` |

### For lane C2 (the client matching window)

- **Expiry.** An entry expires silently after 60 minutes without a register or change (review
  finding 1). The client still holds its number (`this+0x7c0`); a later change or delete of it
  gets `0x2c1c`.

- **The page.**
  - The requester's own entry (or its party leader's) is row 0 **and** appears again in its
    numbered place; skip the second copy, as `c:0x73a770` does.
  - Rows come in entry-number order, 23 to a server page against the window's 12 rows; the
    scroll covers the rest (`party_gui.md` §3).
- **Race** is 0 China / 1 Europe, drawn as text "CHN"/"EUR" (the user's decision). **Count** is
  the party size, 1 without a party; draw `%d/8` or `%d/4` by flag bit 0.
- **A party-less entry's accept** gives the requester `0xb06d [1][1]` twice, and the leader no
  `0xb06d` at all. The leader learns of the join from the formation (`0xb060`, `0x3065`, kind 2).
  An accept into an existing party gives the leader `0xb06d [1][1]` too. The client shows
  `UIIT_MSG_PARTYMATCH_JOIN_COMPLETE_MASTER` for each `[1][1]`, as `c:0x8847d0` does.
- **The popup's answer** must echo the `0x706d`'s job id and requester JID. The server takes an
  answer only from the entry's leader, and only while the job is pending: a late answer after
  the 15 s backstop is dropped.
- **Timers.** The leader's popup answers 2 at 10 s and the requester's bar fills at 10 s; both
  are client-side. With a stock client, "no reply" arrives at about 10 s. The server's 15 s only
  covers a leader client that sends nothing.
- **Register echo.** `0xb069 [1]` carries the assigned entry number: keep it as the player's
  registration (`this+0x7c0`). Change and delete send it back.
- **No server-side search.** Name, purpose and level filtering is the client's, over the held
  rows.
- **Entries that drop.** An entry whose party fills is not removed by the server; the leader's
  client deletes it (`UI_PARTY::FUN_007387c0`). An entry also goes when its party dissolves or its
  party-less owner logs out.
- **Live tests.** Use `partybot -mode bot -name X -register [-accept=false]` as an entry owner,
  or `-request NAME` as a requester.

## Seven-hundred-and-twelfth round: the kill pays the party, the party shares its loot, and party monsters hit and pay as the original's

Built on `int/party` (dev + round 710, the party server core), from `docs/protocol/party_rules.md`
and its round-709 review. Server only; no client change, no perf gate.

### What changed

**The kill reward is the monster's death distributor** (`session/killshare.go`,
`leveldata/killreward.go`), replacing the killing blow's private award. READ, GS
`CGObjMob::vslot_399` `0x4c44a0`:

1. **Grouping.** The damage list is grouped. A player in an Exp Auto Share party groups by
   party; anyone else (no party, or an Exp Free-For-All party) is his own group.
2. **Kill credit.** The group with the most damage has the kill credit: its biggest hitter.
3. **Exp Auto Share group, the party share** (`FUN_005bca60`):
   - Who shares: members alive, in the reference's zone, and within 1000 (horizontal, inclusive)
     of the kill credit, damage or not. The kill credit may sit outside the party.
   - The split is `s_i = level_i / Σlevel`, as a float32.
   - The bonus is `1 + (others−1)·0.2 + chinese·0.1`, or `1 + (chinese−1)·0.1`.
   - Damping: a member with `s_i > 0.7`, in a party of 3 or more eligible whose top level is 21
     or more, keeps half the bonus.
   - Penalty: ×0.5 for a party monster below the eligible members' average level (integer
     division).
   - Each award is for the whole group's damage.
4. **Any other group, the individual award** (`FUN_004c4820`): the player's own damage,
   ×(1 + (n−1)·0.03) in a party (n = every member). It is halved for a party monster below the
   receiver's level.
5. **Per receiver**, `Formula_ExpRewardForContributor` `0x410110` and `Formulae::FUN_004106b0`
   `0x4106b0`, re-read in the asm this round:

   ```
   EXP = ftol(float32(base·slot359) · share · Window · lag1cd8 · Diff), floor 1
   SP  = base·slot359·100/expUnit(rcv) · share · Window · lag1cdc · Diff, floor 1, ftol (int32)
   ```

   - `base` is the victim's **ExpToGive**, characterdata col 79, for every receiver (slot 332;
     see "The base EXP" below). Without the column it falls back to the old `KillBase`.
   - `share` is damage/MaxHP clamped to [1e-6, 1] (`0xb45c84`).
   - `Window` and `Diff` are evaluated at the engine's float32 steps (`ExpWindowScale32`,
     `ExpDiffScale32`).
   - `slot359` is `leveldata.MonsterExpFactor`: 7.5 for a party monster, × the rank's factor
     (champion 2, giant 15, rank 5 60, elite 4, rank 7 30). A rank outside the table drops even
     the party factor.
   - `lag1cdc` is `MasterySPScale`, the mirror of the EXP lag scale, **clamped to [0.1, 1.9]**
     like its twin (`0x4e31af`-`0x4e31e9`). A lagging mastery earns more SP, up to x1.9.
6. **vslot_420** (`0x4ea6a0`):
   - EXP and SP are stored to a float32, × the multiplier (itself a float32 argument,
     `fld DWORD [ebp+0x10]`), and truncated. The SP formula's product is stored to a float32
     before its floor and ftol (`0x41083e`).
   - The rate bonus applies only at a rate of 1.01 or more (`0xb46178`). It adds `EXP·(r−1)` and
     `SP·(r−1)`. The rate is ExpRatioParty for a receiver in any party, otherwise ExpRatio.
   - Then GainExpAndLevel: SP through `skills.AddSkillExp` (the guild-points wrapper still sees
     it), EXP through the level table, with a level-up for any receiver.
7. **Every kill pays SP**, by the formula above. The old "a kill pays its own EXP as SP" (M = 1)
   is gone; round 709 had already corrected the census that justified it.

**Party monsters.**
- **Arming:** the nest is armed only from the share path's count: the last exp-share group's
  eligible members, against `nest.PartyArmCount` 2 (`session/nestkill.go`). A free-for-all kill
  writes 0. The measurement is from the kill credit, not the dead monster.
- **Attack:** a party monster's attack value is ×1.2 before defence, and an **elite's (rank 6)
  ×1.5, party or not** (`combat.MonsterAttackFactor`, READ `FUN_0040da20`), applied in
  `monsterBlow` to the range, or to the flat attack.
- **HP and rolls:** HP ×10, the 50/101 roll, the level clamps and the species-rarity coverage were
  already right (`combat.ScaleHPForMonster`, `nest.RollClass`, `nest.ClampClassByLevel`, checked
  against the review's corrections).

**Items and gold** (`session/itemshare.go`, `session/grounditem.go`, `grounditem`, `party`).
- **Pick-up rights:** someone else's drop needs the party's **Item Auto Share** flag, not just the
  same party (`samePartyFunc`).
- **Item Auto Share item, the round robin** (`FUN_00525dc0`):
  - The next member of the party's rotation (`party.Hub.NextInRotation`, `FUN_004d4840`: the front
    goes to the back, a joiner is appended, a leaver removed) who is found, alive, in the zone and
    within 1000 of the picker in 3D.
  - With the EBX fallback quirk: the last member tried keeps the item when he failed on alive or
    zone; a distance failure clears him and the picker gets it.
  - Owner-only items (3/3/9 but not `ITEM_QNO_RM_ARCHEMY*`) stay the picker's.
  - A full bag on the chosen member refuses the picker **`0x18da`** and leaves the item on the
    ground.
- **The notice `0x3068`** goes to the party's members (`party.ItemNotice`):
  - u32 recipient JID, u32 RefItemID, then a u16 count for an expendable (TypeID 3/3) or the
    constant u8 1 for anything else. READ, GS `FUN_005bdc80`, client `c:0x873990`.
  - The gold branch is 8 bytes (OURS, the client's width). It is encoded and fixtured but not
    sent, see the OPEN list.
- **Gold under Item Auto Share** (`FUN_005bc7f0`): the picker and the members in the zone within
  1000 in 3D (alive or not) take `amount / n` each. The picker takes the remainder, or everything
  when `amount / n` is 0.
- **The aggro link** now needs the party's Exp Auto Share flag, the real bit
  (`monsterai.linkAggro`).
- **The unique-kill notice** groups by the exp-share flag (`partyGroupOf`).
- **A kill by a state's tick whose killer has left the world** still pays everyone else its damage
  list earns a share (`status.go settleKill`). The distributor does not depend on who landed the
  last tick.

### Review fixes (`docs/rounds/party712_review.md`)

#### The base EXP: col 79, ExpToGive. The review is right, and the record is overturned

Re-read with objdump on `/var/tmp/SR_GameServer.exe` and the raw PE. Every step of the chain from
a monster's death to the field:

1. **The death distributor calls the PC award.** `CGObjMob::vslot_399` `0x4c44a0` calls `0x5bca60`
   (party share, `0x4c4777`) or `0x4c4820` (individual award, `0x4c4786`). Both call `[vt+0x690]`
   on the receiver (`0x4c48b4`, `0x5bceb4`). Slot 420 of CGObjPC's vtable (`0xaf59fc`, RTTI
   `.?AVCGObjPC@@`; the only place `0x4ea6a0` appears in the image) is `0x4ea6a0` = vslot_420.
2. **vslot_420 calls the two contributor formulas**: `0x410110` at `0x4ea7a8` and `0x4106b0` at
   `0x4ea7d4`. The other callers are a twin at `0x4fcbcc`/`0x4fcbf5`.
3. **Both formulas call `[victim vt+0x530]`**, slot 332 (`0x4101e8`, `0x4107f8`). CGObjMob's vtable
   `0xaeddac` (RTTI `.?AVCGObjMob@@`; slot 359 `0x4c15c0` confirms the table) has slot 332 at
   `0xaee2dc` = **`0x4a68b0`**:

   ```
   4a68b0: mov ecx,[ecx+0x34]   ; the object's instance
   4a68b3: mov eax,[ecx]
   4a68b5: mov edx,[eax+0x34]   ; instance slot 13
   4a68b8: jmp edx
   ```

4. **Slot 13** is **`0x449340`** in every CInstanceChar-family vtable. Its five references in the
   image are exactly these vtables' `+0x34`:
   - `CInstanceChar` `0xae3724`, `CInstanceCOS` `0xae3494`, `CInstancePC` `0xb0d12c`;
   - `CInstanceSiegeFortressStruct` `0xb0d1e4`, `CInstanceSiegeFortressObject` `0xb0d86c`.

   It reads:

   ```
   449340: mov eax,[ecx+0x18]   ; the reference row
   449343: mov eax,[eax+0x250]
   449349: ret
   ```

5. **`CRefObjChar+0x250` is col 79.** This is the project's anchored map (col 78 `+0x24c`, col 82
   `+0x25c` = KO_RecoverTime 3000).
   - The package's DB `_RefObjChar.csv` names the column **`ExpToGive`**, between `CHR` (78) and
     `CreepType`, `Knockdown`, `KO_RecoverTime` (80-82).
   - The fresh export agrees: MOB_WC_GUNPOWDERGHOST L28 carries 749 = exp_unit(28);
     MOB_EU_KERBEROS 40000.

**And the other formula is PvP.** `0x4105d0` (`Formula_MonsterExpReward`, the min-level rule) opens
with `call [eax+0x1c]` on both ESI and EDI and returns unless both are PCs (`0x4105d9`-`0x4105f3`).
Its only callers are `0x4e6a09` and `0x4e6d88`, in the PC death code.

**Why the 2026-09-14 probe missed it.** It looked for integer readers of `+0x250` by
**intersecting** the readers of `0x250` with the readers of the proven MaxHP field `0x19c`, as a
proxy for "is this CRefObjChar". `0x449340` is a ten-byte accessor that reads `0x250` and nothing
else, so the intersection could not keep it. It is also reached only through the slot-332 vcall
thunk (no direct caller), and the decompile files it as `CInstanceCOS::FUN_00449340`, which reads
like a pet-only helper. **Lesson: an intersection with a "type marker" field filters on function
size, not on type. An accessor reads one field.**

**What changed:**
- `species.ColExpToGive` = 79 is exported as the monsters CSV's appended `ExpToGive` column. It is
  optional on read, so an older CSV still loads, with `HasExpToGive` false.
- It is carried on `monsterSpec`, `combat.Species` and `combat.Monster`.
- It is used as the base for every receiver.
- `Table.KillBase` remains only as the fallback.
- `party_rules.md`'s OPEN row is closed; WORLD_ISSUES' round-175 col-79 note and its kill-EXP note
  carry "(Round 712)" corrections; `combat.ExpFor` and `leveldata.go` have the same correction.

**For the memory note `reference_characterdata_columns.md`** (the coordinator updates the file).
Two claims are wrong:
- "No function reads CRefObjChar+0x250 as an integer ... col 79 is dead data" is false: `0x449340`
  reads it, through slot 332.
- "MOB EXP SOLVED: a kill is worth leveldata col 5 at min(killerLevel, victimLevel)" is false for
  monster kills. That is the PvP formula. A monster kill's base is the victim's col 79, ExpToGive,
  which for an ordinary monster equals leveldata col 5 at the **monster's own** level, and is
  larger for uniques.

What the note still has right: the column map itself, the 95.3 % match and the death penalty's use
of col 5.

#### Fixes table

| # | finding | fix | test |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | SP lag `0x1cdc` clamped [0.1, 1.9] | `MasterySPScale` clamps; comments in `leveldata.go` and this page corrected | `TestMasterySPScale` (level 20, ref 0: 1.9); live solo SP 327 -> **207** |
| 2 | base = ExpToGive (col 79) | verdict and evidence above; export, carry, use, fallback | `TestKillShareReviewThreeMembers` (36/35/39 EXP, 83 SP, the review's hand numbers); `TestKillShareExpToGiveFallback`; `species.TestExpToGiveColumn`; the sentinel-line test reads col 79 |
| 3 | lost updates on the row | `character.LockLeveling` around every GetByID -> SetLeveling: the kill award, the stat spend (`stats.go`), the death penalty (`monsterstrike.go`, the EXP re-read under the lock) and `/level` (`gm.go`) | `TestKillShareNoLostUpdate` (50 concurrent awards, none lost) |
| 4 | float32 steps | `ExpWindowScale32`/`ExpDiffScale32` (the asm's stores) used by both formulas. The party bonus, the damped bonus, the penalty and the multiplier are float32 (`0x5bcd62`/`0x5bcd6a`/`0x5bcea3`/`0x5bcec8`). The free-for-all multiplier is a float32 | `TestLevelScalersFloat32` (14 vs 7: 0.39999998); the worked examples at float32 |
| 5 | `0x3068` recipients and gate | sent to every member but the recipient (`0x5bb770` skips him); sent for owner-only items too; never for gold | `TestItemNoticeSkipsTheRecipient` |
| 6 | attack-factor labels | the truncation is OURS (the engine keeps a float32); applying to a skill's range is INFERRED | -- |
| 7 | three rows upgraded | the not-found candidate is READ; the group order is READ as address order (OURS kept); the gold split sends no `0x3068` (READ) | -- |
| 8 | `party_protocol.md:191` | "recipient JID", with the addresses; and "to every member but the recipient" | -- |
| 9 | berserk party share | listed in the gaps above | -- |

**Live again** (`partybot -mode share`, the real server binary, the monsters CSV re-exported with
col 79 on the box and deleted after):

```
[psSolo] killed chakji #25 (HP 1031): EXP +51, SP +207
    killer +28 EXP, mate +28 EXP; want both trunc(51 x 0.55) = 28        (SP +113)
    killer +52 EXP, idle member +0 EXP; want trunc(51 x 1.03) = 52 and 0  (SP +213)
--- all share steps passed
```

The same run against MOB_WC_GUNPOWDERGHOST (L28, ExpToGive 749) with level-20 bots:
- **Solo: EXP +99.** That is 749 x 0.1 x 1.33, where the old base paid 62. **SP +402.**
- **Exp-share party: +67 each.** That is 749 x 0.1 x 1.63 x 0.55. From 5 levels up an exp-share
  member also earns the party gap bonus +0.30, so the share mode's x0.55-of-solo check (which
  failed as designed there) holds only below a 5-level gap. The mode's help now says so.

#### What players will notice

**Skill points from kills drop sharply; EXP rises for anyone fighting above his level.**
- **Before round 712**, a kill paid its own EXP again as skill EXP (OpenSRO's disclosed M = 1).
- **Now** it pays the engine's own skill formula: `ExpToGive x 100 / your level's EXP unit`. That
  is about **109 skill EXP for an even-level kill at any level** (0.27 skill points at 400:1),
  rising to 207 for a character whose masteries lag his level by 9 or more.
- **EXP is unchanged at or above the monster's level.** It rises against a monster above you,
  because the base is now the monster's own value. Uniques pay their own, larger values.

Solo kills of an ordinary monster, real leveldata, computed with the round's functions (EXP / SP;
"before" SP was the EXP):

| player | monster | masteries | before EXP / SP | after EXP / SP |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| L10 | L10 | at level | 256 / 256 | 256 / 109 |
| L10 | L15 | at level | 291 / 291 | 437 / 186 |
| L10 | L10 | none | 26 / 26 | 25 / 207 |
| L50 | L50 | at level | 2212 / 2212 | 2211 / 109 |
| L50 | L55 | at level | 2516 / 2516 | 2988 / 147 |
| L50 | L50 | none | 221 / 221 | 221 / 207 |
| L100 | L100 | at level | 10178 / 10178 | 10178 / 109 |
| L100 | L105 | at level | 11579 / 11579 | 13424 / 143 |
| L100 | L100 | none | 1018 / 1018 | 1017 / 207 |

So a level-100 player who kept his masteries up earned about 25 skill points a kill and now earns
about 0.27, roughly 90x less. This is what the original's formula pays (READ, `0x4107f0`-
`0x41082c`). Before release the user should hear it, since it changes everyone's SP income.

**Review** (kept beside the notes): `docs/rounds/party712_review.md` (the independent review: SP mastery-lag clamp, the kill base EXP is characterdata col 79 ExpToGive via slot 332 -- overturning the 2026-09-14/15 record and v0.1.155's min-level base, now the PvP formula -- an EXP write race, float32 rounding, 0x3068 recipients; all fixed).

No perf gate: server-only round.

## Seven-hundred-and-eleventh round: the client's party messages on the original's opcodes, and the party window

The client half of the party epic's first implementation pair (S1 = round 710 is the server).
Built against round 709's specs (`docs/protocol/party_protocol.md`, `party_gui.md` §1, §1b,
§2, §6) and round 710's golden fixtures, which are copied unchanged into
`client/scripts/net/fixtures/party/` (no disagreement found: every S1 message decodes and
re-encodes byte for byte).

### What was built

- **`net/party.gd` (PartyNet)**, every party message both ways, on the retail opcodes:
  `0x7060`/`0xb060`, `0x7062`/`0xb062`, `0x3080` (invitation and answer), `0xb067`, `0x3065`,
  `0x3864` kinds 1/2/3/6/9, `0x7061`, `0x7063`, with the masked member record (field and dungeon
  positions, signed). OpenSRO's `0x0080`-`0x0089` are gone from the client.
- **`net/party_state.gd` (PartyState)**: the client's party manager (`0xeeebd8`): the settings
  block (exp/item/anyone) the next `0x7060` sends, in-party, leader, own JID (from the
  `0xb060`/`0xb067` OK and from OpSelfId per round 710's id decision), the member list with the
  leader kept at index 0, the job-party flag `+0x0c`. It applies every message and emits
  `changed`, `notice` (system-window lines), `invitation`, `invitation_closed`.
  - invitation rules (`c:0x88aa60`): the "accept invitations" option off auto-declines with the
    kind's code; an inviter not spawned in this client is dropped unanswered;
  - `0xb067` with an error (the `0x2c10` timeout among them) closes the box (`c:0x880120` closes
    request kind 6 on its error branch, asm);
  - refusals with a code go to the system window as type 0, the client's error path
    `0x778190` (READ in all three ack handlers, `c:0x880010`/`0x8800b0`/`0x880120`); joins and
    leaves are type 4 (`UI_PARTY 0x886b10`); a code with no client message shows nothing.
- **`net/net_client.gd`**: `NetClient.party`, the senders `party_create/invite/leave/kick/answer`,
  and `register_handler(opcode, Callable)` -- the hook through which C2's `party_match.gd`
  registers its own opcodes (checked in the dispatcher's default branch).
- **The party window, `ui/hud/hud_party_pane.gd` (HudPartyPane)**, filling ifparty.txt as
  `IFParty 0x6d6640` (in a party) and `UI_NO 0x6d6d00` (out of one) do:
  caption with the anyone-invite suffix; type line and its colours; leader row (name, Lv,
  level, race mark from the model, guild rule, live HP/MP for the player, tenths for others,
  red flag); seven `CIFPartySlot` rows built from ifpartyslot.txt; Banish on every row for the
  leader, Leave on the player's own row otherwise; Dismiss = leave; the kick target is list index
  row + 1; Invite / Set / Party match enable rules; the player's own portrait borrowed from the
  player block's render. Party match toggles the matching window, as its key does.
- **The settings dialog, `ui/hud/party_settings_dialog.gd`** (CIFSetPartyMode, child 70 at
  32,85, 300x200): the two radio groups built as `CIFRadioButton` builds them (dots 16x16 at

  `0x657910..0x657960` as Create calls them, `0x6db980`), the "anyone may invite" check box,
  Yes writes the block (no request), No closes.

  round (party_gui.md OPEN 7 closed in part):

## Seven-hundred-and-tenth round: the party server core on the original's opcodes

The first implementation round of the party epic, built against round 709's three specs
(`docs/protocol/party_protocol.md`, `party_rules.md`, `party_gui.md`). Server only: lane C1
rewrites the client side at the same time, against the same golden fixtures.

### What was done

- **Golden byte fixtures** (milestone 1, commit `fd9da906`):
  - 57 payloads in `client/scripts/net/fixtures/party/`: every S1 message in both directions, the
    member record with each mask (field and dungeon positions), and the S3/C2 party-match records
    (`0x7069`, `0xb069`, `0x706a`-`0x706d`, `0xb06c`, `0x306e`, `0xb06d`);
  - `gen_fixtures.py` builds them straight from the spec tables, independently of either codec.
    The README lists every field value and the id decision below.
- **`internal/party` rebuilt** on the original's rules:
  - the flags byte, with the cap of 8 or 4 by bit 0 alone and `0x2c13`/`0x2c14` for full;
  - leader at index 0, then join order;
  - a party is formed from an accepted invitation with two members at once; there is no party
    of one any more;
  - a party of two dissolves when one leaves, and leadership passes to the longest-standing member
    with the leader's listing;
  - the person-to-person job table `0x2c23` (no job = 4, 0 matches nobody) and the
    person-to-purpose table for S3;
  - the state byte, derived;
  - invitations with the 30 s timeout (`0x2c10`);
  - party ids from a counter that skips 0;
  - formation and join refusals in the ShardManager's order.
- **`party/wire.go`**: every codec. The two HP/MP formulas are both READ and differ:
  - a full record's tenths are `trunc(cur/max x 10)` (GS `0x5baf96`);
  - an update's (GS `FUN_005bb0c0`) are `0` for 0 HP, else `1 - ftol(float32(r) x -10.0)`, i.e.
    `1 + trunc(10 r)`, which is **11 at full HP**. MP is `ftol(float32(r) x 10)`. Re-read in asm
    this round (`fmul QWORD 0xb45f78` = -10.0, `_ftol2` `0x9fbb40` = `cvttsd2si`).
- **`session/party.go` rewritten** on retail opcodes:
  - `0x7060`/`0xb060`: CheckCanCreate (alive, busy plus state, level 5), a self-target dropped
    silently, the 600-unit 3D range, the PC test, CheckTargetAvailable, then `0x3080` kind 2;
  - `0x7062`/`0xb062`: CheckCanJoin, whose first three tests fail silently; the full cap;
    range/PC/availability; and the `0xb060 [2][2]` quirk when posting fails;
  - the `0x3080` answer: a decline gives `0x2c0c`/`0x2c17`, a gone inviter `0x2c0e`, a timeout
    `0x2c10`. Each goes out to both sides, the inviter on `0xb060`/`0xb062` and the invitee on
    `0xb067`;
  - formation and join announced in the GameServer's order. The inviter gets `0xb060 [1][own JID]`,
    then a `0x3065` of itself, then the invitee's kind 2. The invitee gets `0xb067 [1][own JID]`,
    then the `0x3065` of both. A joiner's existing members get kind 2 before the joiner's
    `0x3065`;
  - `0x7061` leave (reason 2) and `0x7063` kick (reason 4, leader only, silent otherwise). Kind 3
    goes to every member, the leaver too; kind 9 goes out when the leader left; kind 1 `0x2c0b`
    when a party of two dissolves;
  - logout: reason 1 to the rest;
  - **kind 6 member updates**: level, HP/MP, position, guild, masteries, name and model, sent to
    every member but the one updated, each only when it changed.
  - OpenSRO's `0x0080`-`0x0089` party messages are retired.
- **Party chat**: delivered to every member, the sender included, and nobody else (GS `0x5bef50`
  excludes no one).
- **`cmd/partybot`**: characters on the real wire against a running server. `-mode scenario` is
  this round's acceptance. `-mode bot` keeps one character online as the other side of a live
  client test.
- **Callers converted** from the removed `Create`/`Join` to `Form`/`Add`: chat, friendlycast,
  round666, nest660, uniquenotice, monsterai and partyexp tests; `uniquenotice.go` (the party id
  is now u32). Test behaviour is unchanged: every converted party is exp-shared, as OpenSRO's
  parties were.

### Choices of ours (OURS), each labelled in the code

| what | choice | why |
|---|---|---|
| **JID and world id** | `uint32(characterID)` for both | It is already the u32 object id OpenSRO sends for a player (`motion.go`'s `0x30BF`). A client maps a party JID to the spawned player whose 64-bit `CharacterID` has those low 32 bits, and learns its own from `OpSelfID` (0x00F9). Monster ids overlap character ids, so a party target is resolved among players only; an NPC uid (>= `0x7f000000`) answers 3; anything else that names no player answers 0. **Consequence:** a monster id sent as a target names the player with that character id, and if that player is in the same zone within 600 units, that player is invited; retail answers 3 there (the `0x26` TypeID filter, `gs:0x4a8eb2`). The client must send player ids only |
| world id in the record | 1 | `_RefGame_World` `INS_DEFAULT` (EXTERNAL); one field world |
| masteries shown | the two highest-levelled above level 0, lower id first on a tie, 0 when empty | The engine's pick `GS 0x5a1890` is OPEN. A new character shows none, as screenshot 08 does |
| member-update cadence | a 1 s sampler (`partyUpdateInterval`) | Retail raises an event at each change (`vslot_323`), and how often position fires is OPEN. Each field still goes out only when it changed. HP/MP is evaluated only when a raw HP/MP/max moved since the last sample, standing in for the HP event. Without that, a full record's HP 10 would turn into the update formula's 11 with nothing having happened |
| logout trigger | the gateway's disconnect, reason 1 | Reason 1 is READ; retail's trigger is the ShardManager's user cleanup (`SM 0x4296f0`) |
| a stale answer | an answer with no invitation pending is dropped | Nothing names its inviter any more |
| accepting a formation | only an answer byte of 1 accepts, for both kinds | This GameServer accepts a formation on any non-zero byte (`test bl,bl`, `gs:0x5be41c`; a join on `cmp bl,1`, `0x5be39f`), which would make the stock client's "no" (`[2][0x2c0c]`) form the party (`party.DecodeAnswer`) |
| "state not 1" on an answer | refused 2 when the invitee got into a party meanwhile | the only way the derived byte leaves 1 with an invitation pending |
| an invitee who leaves the world | its invitation no longer holds it; the timeout still runs and reaches the inviter (`Hub.DetachSession`) | Whether the original's logout cancels the transaction was not read. READ: the transaction finds both sides by id at its answer and its timeout (`gs:0x5be350`, `0x46ce44 -> 0x46cec0`), and the state byte lives in the character object a relog replaces |
| a race past the ladder | a second invitation slipping past `CheckTargetAvailable` is refused `0x2c1f` | what the single-threaded engine's ladder would have said |
| guild and masteries in the sampler | re-read every 10 s (`partySlowRefresh`); a join reads them fresh | the engine announces them on their events (0x10, 0x20); two store reads per member per second saved |
| a zone with no region frame | the record carries no position (mask without `0x20`) | rather than region 0 with world coordinates cut to u16; no zone hits it today |
| refusals that cannot happen here | the slot-0x244 test (`0x2c19`), the character lock (`0x2c06`/`0x2c09`), arena opponents (`0x2c28`) | OpenSRO has none of those states. The exclusive interaction (INTERACTMODE) is `trade.Hub.Busy` |
| state byte | derived, not stored | It agrees with the writers' table for every single invitation |

### What C1 must know

- **The client's party messages are dead from this round on.** `client/scripts/net/party.gd`'s
  `0x0080`-`0x0089` get no answer, so World3D's debug party panel and `OPENSRO_QA_PARTY` do
  nothing until C1 lands. Merge S1 and C1 together (the plan releases them as a pair).
- **Party chat now echoes to the sender.** The client must drop a type-4 line carrying its own
  name, as retail's `c:Chat_OnChatUpdate 0x877810` case 4 does. Today `World3D._on_chat_update`
  would show it twice.
- **Ids.** The client's own JID is the low 32 bits of `OpSelfID`'s character id. A member or
  inviter is the spawned player whose `CharacterID & 0xffffffff` equals the JID. Send a player's
  id as the `0x7060`/`0x7062` target, not a monster's.
- **HP/MP tenths: two decodes** (READ in the client, round 710's second review).
  - A full record (`0x3065`, kind 2) carries `trunc(10 r)` per nibble. Draw HP n/10 and MP n/10
    (`push 0xa; push 0xa` before `c:0x99a2e0`).
  - A kind-6 update calls `c:0x991f60(jid, hp, 10, mp, 10)`. An HP nibble of 0 means dead (the
    flag at `+0x60`, HP 0). Any other HP nibble n draws as (n-1)/9 (`c:0x991fd1 lea ecx,[ebx-1]`,
    `lea edx,[ebp-1]`), so the server's full-bar 11 is 10/9; whether the gauge clamps that was not
    traced. MP is n/10.
- **Fixtures** are in `client/scripts/net/fixtures/party/`. `README.md` lists every value.

| 2 | "1 accepts" was READ only for kind 3 | labelled OURS with the `test bl,bl` evidence in `wire.go` and `party_protocol.md`; test that `[2][0x2c0c]` declines |

## Seven-hundred-and-ninth round: the party system specified from all three binaries -- every party and party-match message with its byte layout, the ShardManager that owns the party, the EXP/SP and item sharing formulas, the job rule, party monsters, and every window and HUD box -- checked by two adversarial reviews, and the plan for six implementation lanes

The user started the party epic (2026-10-04): "Let's get the party system fully working ... make
sure all the party features match the client/server opcodes exactly. Make no mistakes." They sent
12 screenshots of the original's party windows (from their server's client, "Esro Online"). This
round is **docs only**: a specification to build against, made by three parallel lanes (party709a
protocol, party709b rules, party709c GUI). Two adversarial reviews followed, one on protocol + GUI
and one on rules, and a fix-up pass applied their findings. No code behaviour changed (code
**comments** were corrected) and there is no perf gate. Labels: READ, MEASURED, INFERRED, OPEN,
OURS, EXTERNAL.

**The specification** is in three new pages:
- `docs/protocol/party_protocol.md`: 26 messages both ways with exact layouts, nearly all read
  identically from the client and the server, plus the implementation lanes;
- `docs/protocol/party_rules.md`: types and caps, EXP/SP and item sharing, jobs, party monsters,
  party matching;
- `docs/protocol/party_gui.md`: the party window, the settings dialog, the invitation, party
  matching, the leader's join popup, the join progress bar, and the HUD member boxes.

The reviews are `docs/rounds/party709_review_pg.md` (12 findings, ~90 READ claims re-checked) and
`docs/rounds/party709_review_rules.md` (15 findings, 48 claims re-checked).

**What is settled (READ unless marked):**
- **Who owns the party.** `SR_ShardManager.exe` owns parties and the party-match list
  (`CPartyManager`, `0x7866`/`0x3864`); the GameServer mirrors it and talks to the clients. This
  round decompiled the ShardManager in full (16,634 functions, `/var/tmp/decomp_shardmgr`).
  OpenSRO keeps it all in one process (OURS).
- **None of OpenSRO's party messages is retail** (`0x0080`..`0x0089`, by name, 64-bit ids). The
  retail set:
  - create+invite `0x7060`, invite `0x7062`;
  - the invitation `0x3080` and its answer;
  - acks `0xb060`/`0xb062`/`0xb067`;
  - the party info `0x3065` and events `0x3864` (kinds 1 dissolved, 2 joined, 3 left with reason
    1 logout / 2 leave / 3 server move / 4 kicked, 6 member update, 9 new leader);
  - leave `0x7061`, kick `0x7063`;
  - party matching `0x7069`..`0x706d`, `0x306e`, `0xb069`..`0xb06d`;
  - the item-share notice `0x3068`.

  One masked member record serves `0x3065`, `0x3864` and the join popup, cross-binary exact. There
  is no change-type, change-leader or disband message.
- **Party types.**
  - Flags byte: bit 0 EXP share, bit 1 item share, bit 2 anyone may invite. Set at formation, never
    changed.
  - **The cap is 8 or 4 by the EXP bit alone** (three binaries). That corrects the user's "all
    sharing off makes a 1/4 party": only the EXP setting matters.
  - "Set" is client-side and only outside a party; its values ride the next create request.
- **EXP and SP.**
  - EXP free-for-all: each contributor gets his own damage share × (1 + 0.03 per member past the
    first).
  - EXP share: the members alive, in the world and within **1000** (horizontal) of the kill credit
    split **by level**, × (1 + 0.1 per extra Chinese member, 0.2 per extra European). A member
    taking over 70 % keeps half the bonus.
  - SP follows EXP under every rule. The kill pays SP; an old census had missed the virtual call.
  - The ExpRatio bonus is additive and pays SP too, only at a rate of 1.01 or more; EXP and SP pass
    through float32 first (review).
- **Items.** Round robin by a rotation list within 1000 (3D); when no member qualifies, the last
  candidate keeps the item unless he failed on distance (review). Gold is split equally among
  members within 1000, the remainder to the picker.
- **Jobs.**
  - The job state is 1 trader, 2 thief, 3 hunter, **4 not in job mode**; 0 is invalid, three
    binaries (review; corrects `jobs.md` for this slot).
  - Trader and hunter party together; a thief only with thieves; no-job only with no-job (`0x2c23`).
  - Purposes: 0 Hunting, 1 Quest, 2 Trade, 3 Thief ("All" is search-only). There is no hunter
    purpose and no hunter icon, as the user guessed.
- **Party monsters.**
  - Not "after 4 or 5": an exp-share kill with **2 or more** eligible members arms the nest. The
    next hatch is a party monster 50 times in 101, by the level clamp table, and in an instance
    world only where `PARTYMONSTER_SPAWN` is ON (review).
  - HP ×10, EXP/SP ×7.5, attack value ×1.2.
- **Ranges and timers.**
  - The invite range is **600** for a player, 3D. The `0x26` that `party.md` read as "38" is a
    TypeID filter (both reviews).
  - The invitation waits 30 s (`0x2c10`).
  - A party-match join request is **ended by the leader's client at 10 s** (answer 2). The
    ShardManager's 15 s is a backstop, and the requester's 10 s bar is display only (review).
- **The GUI.**
  - Built from `ifparty.txt`, `ifsetpartymode.txt`, `ifpartymatch*.txt` and the decompiled CIF*
    classes, against the screenshots.
  - The HUD boxes' "far away" blue is **five steps** at 600/700/800/900/1000, exp-share parties
    only. Buffs show only for members spawned in your client.
  - The select glow is teal and follows the target; selecting yourself lights the player box
    yellow. The two mastery icons are whatever the server sends.
  - **User decision (2026-10-03): the matching list draws Race and Purpose as text**, as this exe
    does, not as the screenshots' icons. The level boxes default to the exe's 110, following the
    binary (not asked).

**Corrected records** (each marked "(round 709)"):
- `party.md`: range 38 → 600; `0x061` is leave, not a teleport; `0x06e` is the party-match
  leader's answer; state bytes 3/4; the ShardManager; the flags never change; `0x2c26`.
- `jobs.md` (no job = 4).
- `recovered_names.tsv`: four rows corrected, three placeholders renamed, 11 names added. The
  derived tables follow, and two rows leave `described_but_unnamed.tsv`.
- `client_senders.tsv`, `handler_payloads.tsv` (six layouts now exact), `TODO.md`, `UI_TODO.md`,
  `monster_ai.md`, `RE_COMPLETION.md`, `SYSTEMS.md`.
- The comments in `leveldata.go` (the 3 % is free-for-all only), `session/combat.go` (kills do pay
  SP; a party of two dissolves) and `session/nestkill.go` (measured from the kill credit).
- One spec claim was wrong in a way worth naming: the rules draft said `ArmParty` had no caller,
  from a grep of `internal/session` alone. It is wired through `cmd/server` (round 660). The
  `party=0` in the nest log counts party monsters hatched so far.

## Seven-hundred-and-eighth round: the server spawns the NPCs as the original does -- the retail group spawn 0x3017/0x3019/0x3018 per message block, each NPC at its nest and facing its nest's wInitialDir -- and the client builds none of its own

The user asked whether the NPCs could now be placed, cardinal direction included, without guessing,
and then decided the transport: "match how the original game does it down to the exact opcodes".
Labels: READ, MEASURED, INFERRED, OURS, EXTERNAL (the user's shard database, never committed).

**The chain, READ end to end** (`docs/protocol/npc_spawn.md` has every address):
`Nest_Hatch` 0x5607b0 turns `Tab_RefNest.wInitialDir` (+0x1c) into radians `a` (0x560a1b..0x560a3c:
/65535, *360, *pi/180) for every TypeID shape but the field monster's, so for every NPC; the angle
travels as the 7th argument through `FUN_005f6eb0` and the game world's slot 6 (`FUN_005eb9a0`) into
`CGObj::EnterWorld` 0x485360 as its 14th, which calls SetHeading (slot 230, 0x48ba10: heading vector
`(cos a, 0, sin a)`) and then `SetLifeState(1)`. The spawn record writes `atan2(+0x2c, +0x24)`
(0x487ce0 -> the CRT atan2 at 0x9fc1aa, its table naming "atan2") as `round(a * 57.2957.. / 360 *
65535)` (0x488050) -- wInitialDir again, within one unit on every u16 (`TestWireAngleRoundTrip`). The
client (`FUN_009c3a70`) makes radians of it and adds pi/2 (`FUN_009c40b0`): heading `h = a + pi/2`,
facing `(sin h, 0, -cos h)` = `(cos a, 0, sin a)`, the server's own vector. So **wInitialDir 0 faces
east, 16384 north, 32768 west, 49152 south**, and the long-open question of round 637 -- whether
wInitialDir goes through the same +pi/2 -- is settled: it does, because every spawn angle does.

### Review (round 708)

The review checked the wire layout, the opcodes and the facing against both binaries and found them
right. It found one HIGH and four LOWs, all fixed:

- **HIGH, NPCs lost at login (a race, confirmed by code order).** `enterOwned` forgot the NPC window
  and called `hub.Enter` before sending `OpEnterWorldResult`, with database reads in between. An area
  of interest tick in that gap sent the whole window before the result, recorded it as sent, and the
  client cleared its roster on the result: no NPCs until the next block line. Now the entry forgets
  the window again right after the result's Send, so the next tick spawns it after the result; and
  `World3D._on_npc_spawned` leaves an identical record (`Record.same_placement`: uid, RefObjID,
  region, position, angle, angle source) in place instead of rebuilding it, so the double send cannot
  close a talk window. `TestNPCWindowSurvivesATickBeforeTheEntryResult` puts a tick in the gap through
  a hook (`enterWorldBeforeResultHook`) and requires the window after the result; it FAILS with the
  second forget removed and passes with it. `npc_spawn_test.gd` holds `same_placement`.
- **LOW 1:** a delivery whose `SendBatch` fails now clears the session's mark, so the window is sent
  whole next tick.
- **LOW 2, the nest-less rows:** all 29 have `Tab_RefTactics` rows (EM1 is 1027 beside EM2's 1028,
  nest 51; nest ids 47-50 are missing -- INFERRED deleted by the shard). Four have own-species nests:
  `NPC_CH_EVENT_KISAENG1` (region 26265, 58 units) and `NPC_BATTLE_ARENA_MANAGER` (the same region,
  178), and the two gacha NPCs (other regions only). **Chosen: a second pass (OURS, INFERRED)** --
  a row with no nest at its spot takes the nearest unclaimed own-species nest in its region within
  200 units, since the original's NPCs are its nests. MEASURED: it places exactly those two; no other
  row has one in its region at any distance. 230 from a nest, 27 fallback; Jangan unchanged (17/2).
  Recorded as OURS: the NPC list comes from npcpos, not the nests (six custom world-1 nests in
  Donwhang have no npcpos row and are not spawned; TODO). Recorded from the review's reading: retail
  has no "no angle" form (`_RefGameWorldNPC` instance NPCs hatch with angle 0, `FUN_00609970`; the
  teleportdata row for `GATE_NPC_CH_SOLDIER_EM1` holds only an arrival point).
- **LOW 3:** the interaction set's ascending order is READ, not INFERRED (`_Left` start, values at
  node+0xc, in-order successor `FUN_004885c0`).
- **LOW 4:** `client/tools/README.md` says that a `--server` run given `npcpos.csv` /
  `monsters.csv` also changes where the roster monsters stand.

## Seven-hundred-and-seventh round: Compatibility's black frames with the Bloom row on were Godot 4.2.2's GLES3 back buffer, made by WorldFog's depth read without a colour texture -- a 3D anchor gives it one, the Compatibility bloom is computed per pixel from texelFetch, and a box check fails if the frame goes black again

Round 705 found every Compatibility frame with Bloom on (0, 0, 0) on the box, on base 1bcbd825
too, with nothing in the log. Middle, the default, has Bloom on, and Compatibility is the fall back
for machines without Vulkan and `opensro-compatibility.bat`.

### 1. Reproduced (MEASURED, the box, Compatibility on the RX 7600 through VirtualGL)

- **The game, not the movie writer.** The Jangan spawn (97/168 at 1002, 1020), `OPENSRO_QA_VIDEO_
  STEPS` frames saved from the viewport's own texture (no `--write-movie`): Bloom on mean RGB
  (5.8, 5.5, 5.2) with the HUD drawn over it, Bloom off (78, 86, 88); Texture Filtering (MSAA)
  on or off changes nothing.
- **Round 702's measurement could not see it.** `tools/measure_retail_bloom.gd` draws a canvas
  picture with no 3D view. Run as it was, Compatibility passed (mean 1.6/255). With a camera and a
  transparent 3D quad that reads the depth texture, as WorldFog's pass does, the same shader drew
  luma 0.0 against 123.2 (MEASURED). That is the whole difference.

### 2. The cause (READ, Godot 4.2.2's gles3 sources; tag 4.2.2-stable)

- `RasterizerSceneGLES3::render_scene`: a frame whose 3D materials read the screen or the depth
  texture calls `TextureStorage::copy_scene_to_backbuffer(rt, used_screen, used_depth)` after the
  opaque pass. It creates `rt->backbuffer_fbo`; it creates the colour texture `rt->backbuffer`
  only if a material reads the SCREEN. WorldFog reads only the depth, so the back buffer framebuffer
  gets a depth attachment and no colour.
- `render_target_copy_to_back_buffer` (the canvas, for any `hint_screen_texture`) creates its own
  back buffer (`_create_render_target_backbuffer`, colour with a mip chain) only `if
  (rt->backbuffer_fbo == 0)`. It is not 0, so the canvas copies the screen into a framebuffer with
  no colour, and `canvas_begin` binds `rt->backbuffer` -- 0 -- as the screen texture. Texture 0
  samples black. RetailBloom's Compatibility pass wrote an opaque colour, so the frame was black.
- Order matters: if a canvas reads the screen before any 3D depth read after the target is made,
  the canvas makes the back buffer with colour and all is well (the measurement's case). In the
  world, the 3D pass always runs first in the frame, and the target is re-made on every resize or
  MSAA change.
- Found on the way, same cause: **the brightness pass** (VideoOptions, layer 120, a screen read
  over the whole window) with Bloom off from the start and Brightness 3: the frame's mean 0 --
  wholly black, the interface too (MEASURED, `OPENSRO_QA_VIDEO=bloom=0,brightness=3`). Once the
  bloom had been on, the colour texture existed and the pass worked until the target was re-made.

The suspects named for the round, checked: `hint_screen_texture` with mipmaps and `textureLod` are
not it (the same shader passes with no 3D depth read); the layer -1 placement and the premultiplied
blend are not it (the pass is a plain opaque rect under Compatibility); no shader error -- there is
no screen to read.

### 3. The fix (`RetailBloom`, under Compatibility only)

- **The anchor** (`ANCHOR_SHADER`, `anchor_node()`): one triangle whose spatial material reads
  `hint_screen_texture`, every vertex outside the clip volume (covers no pixel), never culled
  (a 2e6 box), no shadow. It makes Godot's 3D pass create the colour texture whenever it creates
  the back buffer. It shows while the bloom or the brightness pass shows (`_sync_anchor`, each
  frame), so with both off nothing is copied.
- **The pass reads level 0 by texelFetch** and filters bilinearly itself: the back buffer the 3D
  pass makes has one level and NEAREST filtering, the one the canvas makes a mip chain and LINEAR,
  and the pass must read both alike (READ: `copy_scene_to_backbuffer`, `_create_render_target_
  backbuffer`). It asks for no mipmaps: `rt->mipmap_count` is set only when the canvas makes the
  back buffer and is never reset, so a mip request over a later one-level texture would leave it
  incomplete (`gaussian_blur` sets MAX_LEVEL from it) -- black again (READ).
- **The pipeline per pixel** (`COMPAT_SHADER`, the same READ constants as the grid): each pixel's
  point of the 512 x 512 target, the 25 taps at 0 / +-2.6 / +-5.2 texels with weights 80/70/50 of
  255, each tap one bilinear sample of the screen at that point x 128/255, thresholded at 40/255
  before the horizontal sum, each row clamped at 1, the vertical sum clamped at 1, composited by
  the blend (premultiplied alpha: Blur x 192/255 + S x 198/255), as the Forward+ grid. Why not
  the grid: GLES3's canvas declares the screen texture (`color_buffer`) in the fragment section of
  canvas.glsl alone (READ), so a vertex stage cannot read it (round 702's MEASURED "no light").
  OURS method: retail mixes two 512 texels' samples between texels and magnifies its target
  bilinearly; this samples the screen at each tap and evaluates every pixel.

Why not round 702's mip path with the anchor: the mips need the canvas-made back buffer, which the
world never gets first, and the mip-count trap above. Why not BackBufferCopy: it is the same copy
into the same colourless framebuffer. A multi-pass 512 chain inside the canvas has nowhere to keep
the target: GLES3's canvas writes only the window and copies only window -> back buffer, and both
must hold the screen at the composite.

### 4. Measured

**Against retail's 512 pipeline** (`measure_retail_bloom.gd`, now with a depth-reading 3D pass in
the scene, 4000 pixels x 3 channels; BAND = smooth ramps vs 41- and 7-pixel random blocks):

| | mean | p99 | max | ramps mean / p99 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Compatibility 1280 x 720 | 0.95/255 | 6.57/255 | 13.66/255 | 0.28 / 1.08 |
| Compatibility 1920 x 1080 | 1.54/255 | 9.54/255 | 15.52/255 | |
| Compatibility 3840 x 2160 | 2.13/255 | 13.18/255 | 24.46/255 | 0.32 / 2.87 |
| Compatibility, round 702's mip path, 1280 x 720 (no 3D) | 1.6/255 | 7.7/255 | 11.9/255 | |
| Forward+ 1280 x 720 (unchanged) | 0.24/255 | 0.56/255 | 1.52/255 | 0.23 / 0.50 |

Within round 702's documented Compatibility figures at 1280 x 720 on mean and p99; the single worst
channel is 1.8/255 over its max, in the 7-pixel blocks. At larger sizes fine detail (blocks 41: mean
2.4 at 4K, blocks 7: 4.8) is where per-pixel taps part from retail's sparse samples (7.5 pixels
apart at 3840); smooth content stays close. No echo peak at any size (a white bar's added light falls
39/255 -> 0). With the depth reader and without it the figures are identical (texelFetch: the
back buffer's filter does not matter).

**The game**: the box check below, Bloom on keeps the spawn's picture: mean grey 81.3 against 87.9
off (base 65e5d8a8: 0). The brightness pass, started with Bloom off and Brightness 3, then stepped
Bloom on and off: before the anchor followed it, mean grey 0 -> 104.5 -> 115.3; with it, 115.0 -> 104.5 -> 115.3 (Bloom and Brightness both off then: 84.6).

**Cost** (`time_retail_bloom.gd`, the root viewport's GPU time over a synthetic picture, with a
camera and the depth reader, RX 7600, ms a frame):

| 1280 x 720 | 0.069 | 0.392 | **+0.32** | +0.04 | +0.015 |

| 3840 x 2160 | 0.481 | 3.377 | **+2.90** | +0.60 | +0.10 |

(Repeat runs within 0.01 ms.) The anchor's own cost is the 3D pass's copy of the screen. Most of
the rest is the 25 taps x 4 texel fetches per pixel; a one-fetch (nearest) variant measured 0.18
and 1.40 ms at 720 / 2160 but read worse at 720 (max 20.7/255, p99 9.6) and was not kept. Against
Forward+'s grid (+0.69 ms at 4K, round 702) the Compatibility pass is dearer at 4K, where few
Compatibility players run (the renderer of machines without Vulkan); recorded for the user, not

**Perf gate** (`perf_gate.sh --base 65e5d8a8 --sites jangan --frames 12000 --renderer
gl_compatibility --env 'OPENSRO_QA_VIDEO_STEPS=quality=0|quality=1'`, both sides Compatibility on
Middle, median of 3). Note the base's bloom draws black, so the base side pays a broken pass, not
none:

|---|---|---|---|---|
| jangan 1280 x 720 | 2.43 -> 2.63 SAME (+0.2) | 9429 -> 9485 SAME | 3189 -> 3211 SAME | 5 -> 5 SAME |
| jangan 3840 x 2160 (`--size`) | 13.40 / 13.62 -> 15.83 / 15.89 (**+2.3**) | 9502 / 9528 -> 9424 / 9454 | | |

Exit 0 at 1280 x 720. At 3840 x 2160 the gate twice stopped on a head run with "the run's renderer

### 5. The guard

- `client/tools/retail_bloom_box_test.sh <client dir> [out dir]` (new; on the box, under the
  caller's lock): `measure_retail_bloom.gd` under Compatibility at 1280 x 720 with the
