### Review (round 707 review)

**M1 -- the in-game check passed with the anchor broken (the reviewer's MEASURED finding).** The new
pass blends instead of writing opaque, so a pass that reads a black screen leaves the frame x
198/255 (0.776 of the plain one), not black; `a >= 0.5 b` in the box test and `lum_b < 0.25 lum_s`
in the measurement passed that (anchor forced off: game 68.2 against 87.9, FRAME 95.6 against
123.2). A ratio cut such as 0.88 would also fail a legitimately dark view, where retail's bloom
itself keeps 198/255. **Now both test the light the bloom ADDS over S x 198/255** -- zero for a pass
that read nothing, whatever the scene:
- `measure_retail_bloom.gd`: FAIL if the added mean luma is under 5/255 (OURS). MEASURED: 32.4 with
  the anchor, -0.1 without.
- the box test's game check: FAIL if mean grey on minus off x 198/255 is under 5 (OURS). MEASURED:
  81.3 on / 87.9 off = **+13.1** with the anchor, 68.2 / 87.9 = **-0.1** without.

**M2 -- the brightness pass was not in the box test.** A second boot, Bloom off from the start (so
nothing has made the colour texture), stepped to Brightness 3: FAIL under half the plain frame's
mean grey. A boot of its own because the colour texture, once made, lasts until the target is
re-made. MEASURED (interface hidden): 119.3 against 87.9 with the anchor, **0** without.

**Self-test** (new): `OPENSRO_QA_BLOOM_NO_ANCHOR=1` (a QA hook in `RetailBloom`, OURS) never shows
the anchor. With it, every check FAILS (the three above); without it, ALL PASS (MEASURED, this
tree, the box).

**L -- a possible black frame when the brightness pass appears.** The anchor followed the
brightness layer only from `_process`, so the frame the layer first drew in (it is added deferred,
after the nodes' `_process`) could read a colourless back buffer. Now `RetailBloom` connects the
root's `child_entered_tree` and the brightness layer's `visibility_changed` and syncs the anchor at
that moment (its own `visibility_changed` already did for the Bloom row); `_process` stays as a
fallback (a layer freed). `retail_bloom_test.gd` checks the anchor follows the layer's entry, hide
and show with no `_process` call between.

**Recorded, no code change:**
- The anchor makes Godot's 3D pass copy the opaque screen into the back buffer every frame the
  anchor shows, which the canvas's own copy then overwrites: +0.015 / +0.03 / +0.10 ms at 1280 x
  720 / 1920 x 1080 / 3840 x 2160 (MEASURED, section 4). Godot 4.2.2 offers no way to make the
  colour texture once and skip the copy (`copy_scene_to_backbuffer` blits whenever a screen reader
  is in the list, READ).
- Cheaper Compatibility paths for the 4K cost (+2.3-2.9 ms), none built: (a) one texelFetch a tap
  (nearest) -- MEASURED 1.40 ms at 4K against 2.90 (with a uniform branch), its 4K error about the
  same (mean 2.25 against 2.13) but worse at 720 (max 20.7, p99 9.6); (b) choosing (a) only above a
  width, by swapping the shader on the CPU when the viewport is resized (OURS, unmeasured); (c) a
  real 512 chain, which needs somewhere to keep the 512 target -- GLES3's canvas has none (section
  3) -- so it would mean rendering the world into a SubViewport under Compatibility (a World3D
  change, not this lane's); (d) Godot's mip path, ruled out by the colourless-buffer order and the
  stale mip count. The user decides whether 4K Compatibility merits (a)/(b).

Checks after the review: `remote_godot.sh check` ALL LOAD; `tests` 223 suites, 0 failing; the box test ALL
PASS, and FAILURES with `OPENSRO_QA_BLOOM_NO_ANCHOR=1` (above).

## Seven-hundred-and-sixth round: objects and characters lit as the original lights them -- its own vertex-shader formula with the zone's READ light, the layer's second colour, 0.6 per object and a character's shadow tile, in display values with the tone map undone -- and the camera's 60-degree field of view; the gate wall now reads 82 against the original's 81

The user (after round 705): "A lot more fog and less vibrant. Let's try to match the original game
as best as possible." Round 705 measured the main cause of "less vibrant" at their spot (Jangan
X:6432 Y:1148 = 97/168 local (965, 1885), looking north at the dragon and the gate): placed objects
and characters 2-2.8x darker than the original, from our object lighting. Lane `light706`, client.
Labels: READ (`sro_client.exe`: the box's decompile and `sro_client.asm`), MEASURED, INFERRED, OURS.

### 1. What the original does (READ)

`client/scripts/assets/object_light.gd` carries every address; in short:

- **The formula.** Every object and character draw is `CObjRendererVS` (static `vslot_024`, skinned
  `vslot_038`) with `vertexshader0.c` / `vertexshader2.c`: `oD0 = saturate(c10 + max(0, N.c9) x
  c11)`, then stage 0 MODULATE2X (flag 0x1000). In display values, no tone map.
- **c10 = the object's colour x the light's Ambient** (round 705). The "raw colour" branch of
  vslot_038 (renderer+0x120 bit 0) is dead: the field's only writers store 0 (0xbf769d, 0xbf5891).
- **c11 = the material's +0x10 x the light's Diffuse** (`FUN_00bf0e20`), and that is the layer's
  SECOND colour: `CPrimMtrl::vslot_001` passes `this+0x10` to `FUN_00bf9270`, which stores the
  file's first colour at the record's +0x10 and the second at +0 -- a D3DMATERIAL9 (Diffuse,
  Ambient, ...) filled from a file in Ambient, Diffuse order; the flag word lands at the record's
  +0x60 = the material's +0x70, where the draw reads it. The layer's FIRST colour (BmtReader
  `ambient`, our albedo until now) is in no object lighting. `ResObject::FUN_00bc7ff0` ->
  `FUN_00bf8610` returns that material pointer from the object's material vector.
- **c9 = the light's Direction x -1** (`vslot_025`, renderer+0x130..0x138) times the object's
  inverse world matrix, not renormalised (a scaled object's N.L scales by 1 / scale).
- **The light** (`Map::FUN_00a19160`, every world draw, then vslot_025): Direction = DAT_01109510,
  written only by `Map::FUN_00a2f370` at world creation -- normalize(-1, -1, 0) (the constants
  -1.0 at 0xe1b878 and the folded 2.0 at 0xe1b898) -- so not the environment and not the time of
  day; to-light (0.707, 0.707, 0) in the file's coordinates, the same in Godot's (the mirror is
  z). Ambient = world+0x6853, channel 3 clamped (round 635). Diffuse = channel 2 clamped x
  world+0x68c3, which is **0.8** (0xde4c64) while world+0x2e54 is set and 0.6 (0xd86fc0) otherwise
  (0xa1d19b..0xa1d20b), halved under water (0x26bb). world+0x2e54: set to 1 by the world's
  constructor (`param_1[0xb95] = 1` in FUN_00a2f370), cleared by `Map::FUN_009fb180` (from
  `SWorld::vslot_005`) when the bloom's screen target world+0x27c3 is missing -- **0.8 with the
  Bloom row on, 0.6 off**. Its only writers are those two (once cleared it stays clear until the
  world is rebuilt; not reproduced, the row decides).
- **The object's colour** (+0x14..+0x1c): CCompoundObj's constructor (`ResourceMgr::FUN_00c32e50`,
  0xc330ed..0xc330fc) stores **0.6** for all three classes built on it -- CCompChar, CCompBldg (the
  map's buildings), CCompSimple (their constructors 0xc1f080, 0xc1fb80, 0xc1fc00, vtables
  0xe0cd3c / 0xe0ce8c / 0xe0cfd4). Round 705 had INFERRED white. The setter (slot 21,
  `CCompChar::FUN_00c255e0`) has two callers (a census of every 3-argument call through +0x54):
  `Map::FUN_009f6de0`, the region's 0x5d-byte decoration records (record+0x55 = the shadow byte
  / 382.5, 0xa27c0c; not drawn here), and **`GlobalDataManager::FUN_009cf530`, every character's
  position setter** (CIObject slot 37): 0.6, unless the character's nav cell is a terrain cell
  (vtable+8: CRTNavCellQuad returns 1, CRTNavCellTri 0) -- then `FUN_00aa1030`: 1.0 in a dungeon
  region (id bit 0x8000), else `SWorld::vslot_041`: the byte of the region's .t ShadowMap (read
  into region+0x73 by FUN_00a31d20 at 0xa31e40) at column x / 20, row z / 20, **divided by 384.0**
  (0xde4c48); 1.0 where no region is found. So 153..255 -> 0.398..0.664. No fade, berserk or
  selection writes it; berserk replaces the colour in c10 and c11 with its pulse (round 651, READ).
- **Characters** use the same formula (vslot_038, vertexshader2.c). **Terrain** is separate (its
  own shader and light terms) and keeps its baked lighting. **Specular**: none -- no oD1, and c14
  (material x the renderer's second light) is uploaded only when renderer+0x14 is 1, which the
  world's light clears. Metallic Sheen is an environment-map pass, not drawn here.
- **Field of view**: 60 degrees vertical at any aspect -- the camera constructor `FUN_00bae0a0`
  stores 60.0 (0xd89ddc) at +0x50 and sets +0x44 (perspective); `CGFXVideo3d::FUN_00bae810` hands
  +0x50 x pi/180 (0xe1b8d8) and width / height (0xed836c, from the viewport's Width and Height) to
  `FUN_00aa4ef0`: m11 = cot(fov x 0.5), m00 = m11 / aspect, a PerspectiveFovLH. Godot's Camera3D
  under KEEP_HEIGHT is the same.

### 2. What changed

- **`ObjectLight`** (new): the READ constants, the light as global uniforms (`srr_obj_light`,
  `srr_obj_ambient`, `srr_obj_diffuse`, `srr_obj_tonemap`, project.godot), `light_colors`,
  `character_color`, `shadow_byte_at`, the CPU `shade()`, and the shared GLSL: oD0 per vertex from
  `MODEL_NORMAL_MATRIX x NORMAL` (the inverse transpose, unnormalised, as c9's inverse world),
  `object_color` (instance uniform, default 0.6), `object_tint` (berserk), and `srr_obj_present`,
  which undoes Godot's Filmic so the screen shows the formula's value.
- **Every object material** is unshaded and computes it: `object.gdshaderinc` (was the foliage
  include) for solid layers (was a StandardMaterial3D with the FIRST colour, lit by the sun at 0.3
  and the Forward+ x4), alpha-tested and two-sided layers (the foliage shaders, whose authored
  normal on both faces now falls out of one vertex colour), their fade twins; and the MTRL mod
  shader (DIFFUSE was "lit by Godot" with L x first colour / 2; now c.lit x oD0 + c.unlit, whole).
  `ObjectLoader.object_shader(kind, fade)` builds them at run time: **GL Compatibility in Godot 4.2
  cannot compile an instance uniform** (MEASURED: "Uniform instances are not supported in
  gl_compatibility shaders") and has no renderer define (MEASURED: `#if CURRENT_RENDERER == ...`
  is a preprocessor error), so the builder defines `OBJECT_NO_INSTANCE_UNIFORMS` there and
  `object_color` is a plain uniform at 0.6.
- **`CharacterLight`** (new, Forward+): visits 12 bodies of CharacterBlobs' group a frame, reads the
  tile and footing under each (`_nav_graph_for`, `NavGraph.surface_at`, the ShadowMap the terrain
  commit leaves on the region's group) and sets `object_color` on its meshes; skips a body that has
  not moved a unit, rescans its meshes every 8th visit (OURS cadence). `OPENSRO_QA_CHARLIGHT=1`
  prints `QA CHARLIGHT` lines. At the user's spot: both soldiers and the player on terrain tiles
  of 153 -> 0.398; the plaza's NPCs on the deck object -> 0.6.
- **World3D**: the light from the zone's channels 2 and 3 and the Bloom row (`_apply_object_light`,
  logged `World3D: object light (READ): ...`; re-applied when Bloom changes); the tone map with the
  fog; `CAMERA_FOV_DEG = 60`, KEEP_HEIGHT (and the scene's camera). The sun stays for Godot-lit
  surfaces and Detail's character shadows on the terrain; objects no longer receive it, so those
  shadows do not fall on object floors (the plaza deck) -- as the original, which projects them
  on ground cells only (READ, round 702).
- **Consumers**: `BerserkLook` sets `object_tint` (c10 and c11 both = the pulse, READ);
  `AppearFade` takes the object shaders' fade twins (`appear_fade_shader`, the warm-up list);
  `PlayerPortrait` (and through it the paper doll, the select stage, the create preview) reads the
  material colour from `albedo` -- now the SECOND colour, which is what c11 uses -- injects its own
  light in place of `OD0_LINE` in a mod pass (before vertex(), where the uniforms must be) and
  strips the tone-map undo (its environment is Linear); its diffuse scale follows the Bloom row.
  `QaShotEnv`: `objtm=0|1` (the undo), `objdiag=1|2` (diffuse term alone / ambient term alone).
- Docs: BMT_FORMAT.md (which colour lights an object), SHADER_FINDINGS.md, OPTION_VIDEO.md (the
  Bloom row and the diffuse), TODO.md.

### Review (round 706)

The review confirmed the READ chain (the shader sources in the archive, the c9/c10/c11 uploads, the
0.8 / 0.6 bloom factor, the fixed light direction, the object colour 0.6, ShadowMap / 384, the
plaza deck) and found:

- **H1, fixed: the instance uniform overflowed Godot's instance buffer under Forward+** (the
  review MEASURED about 1,093 "Too many instances using shader instance variables" a boot at the
  Jangan spawn; the meshes that missed out drew with no ambient term, the far horizon band at luma
  30-41 against 65-81 with the buffer raised). `object_color` is now a plain material uniform
  (0.6) in `object.gdshaderinc` and `ObjectLight.SHADER_FN`: placed objects are always 0.6 (READ),
  so none of them carries a per-instance value. A character's tile is drawn with **per-level
  copies of its materials** (`ObjectLight.with_object_color`: one copy per material and level,
  shared by every body at that level, held by the meshes that draw it; the material itself at
  0.6), which `CharacterLight.set_on` swaps in -- leaving a mesh that draws an AppearFade twin or a
  BerserkLook copy to those (they put the copy back when they end). World3D visits a body when it
  is placed (`_light_character`: NPCs, other players, monsters before their fade starts, the
  player on every dress), so no body draws a frame at 0.6 first; a body whose region is not
  loaded yet is left for the next visit, not drawn at the original's "no region" 1.0.
  `object_light_test.gd` fails if the include, `SHADER_FN`, any object shader kind (fade twins
  included) or any MTRL mod shader declares an instance uniform. MEASURED after the fix: **0**
  "Too many instances" lines in every boot of the round on the box (Forward+ at the user's spot and
  at the spawn, both at radius 2; Compatibility; the perf gate's runs), 0 shader errors.
- **Found while fixing it: `Resource.duplicate()` of an object material draws its diffuse term
  brighter.** MEASURED (Forward+, the user's spot, bloom off, `OPENSRO_QA_CHARLIGHT_VALUE`
  forcing every character's value): the soldier's red cloth 57.6 with its own material at 0.6 and
  71.2 with a duplicated copy at 0.598; with the diffuse term alone (`objdiag=1`) 25.4 against
  39.0, with the ambient term alone 47.9 against 47.8 -- the copy's `object_color` was right, its
  diffuse was not. Copies are now built by setting each of the source's parameters by name
  (`ObjectLight.copy_material`): the same frame then reads 25.4 / 57.5, and a placed object forced
  through a copy at 0.601 reads the same as its own material (dragon 94.8 / 94.8, wall 82.0 /
  82.0). AppearFade's twins of an object material are made the same way (a fade drew its diffuse
  brighter for its 2 s); BerserkLook's copies replace the colour with the pulse and are left as
  they were. Why `duplicate()` does this was not read in Godot's source.
- **M3, fixed by the above:** the copies work in both renderers, so Compatibility draws characters
  by their tile too. The soldier at 0.398: luma 50.7 Forward+, 48.6 Compatibility (bloom off).
- **M1, filed:** the dragon is still about 1.3x (gold pixels (127, 97, 30) Forward+ / (132, 101,
  25) Compatibility against (91, 79, 33); R 1.40, G 1.24, B 0.91), and the user confirmed Bloom was
  OFF in their original. Checked this round: the dragon's `.bsr` carries **no mod** --
  `tools/probe_bsr_mods.gd` (new): `cj_jang_gate_dragon.bsr` env_map_flags -1, 0 material mods,
  materials `cj_jang_gate01.bmt`, mesh `cj_jang_dragon.bms` -- so `CRTModEnvMap::vslot_004`
  (0xc83690) and its 0x10000000 that would keep the previous c11 never run for it; and its layer's
  flag word is 0x140, without bit 3, so `FUN_00c42a60`'s MODULATE 1x / lighting-off branch (flag 8
  with FUN_00bc0fd0) does not apply either. TODO.md has what is left.
- **LOW, fixed:** `player_portrait_test` and `inventory_pages_test` put `ObjectLight.current_bloom`
  back; new bodies take their value when placed (above).
- **Recorded (no change):** M2 -- the terrain still goes through Filmic while objects undo it;
  switching the world to Linear needs a terrain round first, and the seam is not measured. The
  sky (220 against 190) is filed as its own sky / fog item (TODO.md).

  (wall 35 vs 81, dragon's gold 32 vs 90, soldier 37 vs 62) and the sky is brighter and paler.

### 2. The near fog

**On the box it does not happen.** At the user's spot, Forward+, Middle (the default), 1280 x 720:

**What was ours and wrong: Forward+ mixed a half-fogged pixel in linear light.** Direct3D 9 fogs in

  a frame (4.79 -> 6.16, SLOWER; +0.0 at 1280 x 720)** -- Godot's copy of the 3D buffer.

## Seven-hundred-and-fourth round: the project is renamed from srrevamp to OpenSRO -- the code, the tools, the deploy files, the docs and every environment variable -- and a player's saved settings follow the client to its new user folder

The user's decision (2026-10-03): the project is **OpenSRO**. A rename only; nothing a player or
the server does changes, apart from the names below. Labels: OURS = this project's choice.

**The names (the user's decisions, followed as given).**

- `OpenSRO` is the display name and the executable: Godot's `config/name`, the window title,
  the Windows product name, `OpenSRO.exe` (and `OpenSRO.console.exe`, `OpenSRO.pck`), and the
  Linux `OpenSRO.x86_64`. The `.pck` must share the executable's base name for Godot to find it,
  so it follows the executable rather than the lowercase rule.
- `opensro` everywhere else: the zips `opensro-windows.zip` / `opensro-linux.zip` (their top
  folders `opensro-windows/`, `opensro-linux/`), the Go module `github.com/OpenSRO/OpenSRO/server`
  (the repository's path is `OpenSRO/OpenSRO`), the Rust crate and library `opensro_native`
  (`opensro_native.dll`, `libopensro_native.so`, `client/opensro_native.gdextension`), the
  Compatibility launchers `opensro-compatibility.bat` / `.sh`, the log `user://logs/opensro.log`,
  the updater's own files (`opensro_update.zip`, `opensro_update_staging`,
  `opensro_update_relaunch.bat`, `opensro_update.log`, `opensro_update_cleanup.txt`), the
  databases `opensro`, `opensro_test`, the compose project and volume, the systemd units
  `opensro-update.service` / `.timer`, the CI runner label `opensro-pve`, and the box paths
  `/opt/opensro-client*`, `/opt/opensro-server`, `/opt/opensro-re`.
- **Environment variables, a clean break**: all 266 `SRREVAMP_*` names (server flags and the
  client's QA hooks) are `OPENSRO_*`. Nothing reads the old names.
- **The updater** asks `https://api.github.com/repos/OpenSRO/OpenSRO/releases/latest` for
  `opensro-*.zip`. A client from before the rename asks for `srrevamp-*.zip` and finds nothing,
  so it does not update itself: the user accepted that, and players download the new zip once.

**What stayed.** "Silkroad", SRO and every name of the original game's own; the `srr_` prefix
of the two shader globals (`srr_fog_params`, `srr_fog_color`) and similar internal
abbreviations, which name nothing a player or operator sees. docs/LEGAL.md had no mention of
the old name and is unchanged.

**A player's saved settings (UserDataMigration, OURS).** Godot keys the user folder by
`config/name` (the project sets no `use_custom_user_dir`), so the rename moves it:
`%APPDATA%\Godot\app_userdata\SRRevamp` becomes `...\OpenSRO`, and the same under
`~/.local/share/godot/app_userdata/` and macOS's `~/Library/Application Support/Godot/app_userdata/`.
`client/scripts/setting/user_data_migration.gd` is the project's first autoload -- before the
Audio autoload reads its options from `settings.cfg` -- and, when the new folder has no
`settings.cfg` and the old sibling folder exists, copies the old folder's files once
(`settings.cfg`, `quickslots.cfg`, `screenshots/`; never `logs/`, `shader_cache/` or `vulkan/`,
and never over a file already there), writes `migrated_from_srrevamp.txt` so it never runs again,
leaves the old folder as it was, and logs `UserData: copied N file(s) from ... to ...`. The
marker is written only when every file copied; a failed copy leaves
`migrating_from_srrevamp.txt`, and the next start copies what is missing even though
`settings.cfg` arrived the first time (review L4). The shader cache is left behind on purpose: on
the box it is 70 MB of the old folder's 87 MB (MEASURED, `du`), and the cost is one slower start
while the engine rebuilds it.
`user_data_migration_test.gd` builds an old and a new folder and checks the copy, the skipped
folders, the untouched new log, the once-only marker, a new folder already in use, and a fresh
install. It also ran for real on the box: the first run of this branch logged
`UserData: copied 1 file(s) from /home/ghidra/.local/share/godot/app_userdata/SRRevamp to
.../OpenSRO` (the box's `settings.cfg`).

The two files beside the executable are unaffected by the user folder: `override.cfg`
(RendererChoice) is only written, never recognised by its header, so an old one keeps working;
`setting/config.yaml` (ClientConfig) is not shipped in the zip and a private server's file may
say `type: srrevamp`. ClientConfig still reads that word, as `opensro`, with a warning naming the
server (`OLD_TYPE_NAME`; a new case in `client_config_test.gd`) -- the one place the old name is
still read, because skipping the entry would leave a player's login screen without its server.

**Production** is moved by hand, once: deploy/README.md, "Moving an install from srrevamp to
OpenSRO" (stop the old timer before the rename reaches `dev`; `ALTER DATABASE srrevamp RENAME
TO opensro`; copy `srrevamp_srrevamp-postgres-data` into `opensro_opensro-postgres-data`; rename
the variables, DSN and paths in the override; swap the systemd units). It runs in three parts:
A as the old user (the database and the volume, `-p srrevamp`), B as root from outside that
user's session (the user and host rename -- `usermod` refuses a user with live processes, and the
cloud-init sudo rule in `/etc/sudoers.d/90-cloud-init-users` names the user, so it is renamed too
and checked with `visudo -c`; `/etc/hosts`; `preserve_hostname: true`), C as the install's user
again (the folders, the remote after checking for an ssh alias or key, the override, the units). `docker-compose.yml` now
names its project (`name: opensro`), so the volume's name no longer depends on the checkout's
folder. Left running, the old updater would pull the rename and start a second stack beside the
first, on an empty database.

**Also in the round.** Five compiled Go binaries had been committed by accident and carried the
old module path inside them: `server/server` (15 MB), `server/heightat`, `server/o2sectors`,
`server/whatishere`, `server/wherecoord`. They are out of the tree (kept on disk, `git rm
--cached`) and in `.gitignore`. `AGENTS.md` says in its opening lines that the project was called
srrevamp until 2026-10-03.

**What is left with the old name (`git grep -i srrevamp`).** Only the intentional mentions:
this entry, AGENTS.md's note, deploy/README.md's migration section and the `docker-compose.yml`
comment pointing at it, `UserDataMigration` (the old folder name, the marker) and its test,
`ClientConfig.OLD_TYPE_NAME` and its test, two lines of `client/docs/RELEASE_NOTES.md`
(`bundle_docs.sh` copies them verbatim from the messages of tags cut before the rename),
`docs/RENDER_BOX.md`'s box-migration table, `client/tools/README.md`'s note on a stale
`srrevamp_native.gdextension` -- and the facts about the past, which the review (L2) put back as
they were: the backup `~/backups/srrevamp-20260919T065504Z-before-warehouse-per-account.sql.gz`,
the CI cache's `_work/srrevamp/srrevamp`, the tester's `SRREVAMP_*_PK2_PATH` and his
`srrevamp-windows.zip` (the second round of 2026-08-26), the zip listings, log lines and test
output measured in past rounds (667-668 among them), the v0.1.0-v0.1.5 release assets
(PROGRESS.md), a user's quote, a panic trace's path on the workstation, a screenshot path in
RE_COMPLETION, the lane directories `/opt/srrevamp-client-<lane>` and
`/var/tmp/<lane>/srrevamp-server` that past rounds ran in (the box keeps them under those names),
and `/root/srrevamp`, the local checkout, whose path stays.

**Checks.**

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `go build ./... && go vet ./... && go test -count=1 -p 1 ./...` against `opensro_test` | all packages ok (the first run caught `internal/systems`' import probe still matching the old lowercase path; fixed) |
| `cargo test --release --locked` (native/) | 45 passed; Cargo.lock carries the new crate name |
| `remote_godot.sh check` | 575 scripts and 9 scenes, ALL LOAD |
| `remote_godot.sh tests`, with `libopensro_native.so` built from this branch | 223 suites, 0 failing; `NativeAssets: native readers ON (library loaded, opensro_native 0.1.0, API 5, .../native_bin/libopensro_native.so)` |
| a QA run on the box through `qa_shot.sh` with the `OPENSRO_QA_*` hooks | `qa_shot.sh --region '97\168.m' --at 1002,1020` from `/var/tmp/rename704` on Vulkan (RX 7600): the log builds `97\168.m`, which only `OPENSRO_MAPM_PATH` names (the default is 98/168), and 20 frames were written |

**A test export** (after the review; MEASURED on the box with round 668's 4.2.2 templates in
`/var/tmp/ship668/templates`, set as the presets' `custom_template/release` in a scratch copy, and
both libraries built from this branch): `--export-release "Linux"` wrote `OpenSRO.x86_64`,
`OpenSRO.pck` (8,281,600 bytes) and `libopensro_native.so`; `--export-release "Windows Desktop"`
wrote `OpenSRO.exe`, `OpenSRO.pck` and `opensro_native.dll` (no console wrapper in a release
export, as in round 668's listing). The `.pck` carries `res://opensro_native.gdextension`. The
Linux export, run headless with a scratch HOME holding an old `app_userdata/SRRevamp/settings.cfg`,
logged `UserData: copied 1 file(s) from .../SRRevamp to .../OpenSRO`, `OpenSRO log file:
.../app_userdata/OpenSRO/logs/opensro.log` and `NativeAssets: native readers ON (library loaded,
opensro_native 0.1.0, API 5, .../build/linux/libopensro_native.so)`, and the new folder held the
copied `settings.cfg`, the marker and `logs/opensro.log`. The zips themselves were not assembled
(the box has no `zip`); release.yml's packaging and `check_release_zip.sh` name the same files.

The perf gate was not run: no world, drawing or loading code changed (World3D.gd's changes are

## Seven-hundred-and-third round: the notice band is drawn as the original's CIFStretchWnd lays it out -- the fill over the text, 40-pixel fades outside it -- the notice text is bold, and walking into a named area raises CIFRegionView's banner from regioncode.txt and textzonename.txt

The user (2026-10-03), with three pictures: ours, "You have advanced to level [101].", a hard-edged
blue rectangle hugging the text with broken streaks and gaps to its right (a long-standing bug, the
same under Compatibility as under Forward+); the original's "[Smile] has killed [Tiger Girl
(EU-STR)].", a wide translucent band with soft ends; and the original's town banner over Donwhang.
"Remember there are different color banners for notices, it's like a pinkish redish color I think
but whatever the game files say."

Labels: READ = read from `sro_client.exe` or the data; MEASURED = counted; INFERRED = follows from
what was read; OURS = OpenSRO's choice. `docs/protocol/notice_banner.md` has every address.

**What the original does (READ).**

| Kind | Instance | Band | y | Text | Timing |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| GM notice, guild created, arena, `0x887330` (`0x777bf0`'s four callers) | GDR_NOTICE | fill (128, 45, 67) + `com_notice_*` frame -- the pink-red one | 100 | 12 px, weight 600, white, no shadow | 7000 ms, last 2000 fading |
| level-up, unique appeared/killed, recall point, siege, training camp, error codes (`0x77b580`, ~70 sites) | GDR_WARNING_WND | fill (0, 52, 92) + `com_warning_*` -- the blue one | 130 | the same | the same |
| a named area entered (`0x783610` every move, `0x786f30` at world set-up) | GDR_REGION_INFO_VIEW (`#ifdef EUROPE_SYSTEM`) | `area_deco.ddj` 744 x 104 | 95 | title 20 px x1.5 weight 600 cyan (61, 253, 255) + shadow; line 2 15 px white + shadow; line 3 11 px (255, 255, 92) + shadow | 0.5 s in, held to 3 s, 0.5 s out |

There is no third notice colour: the pink-red the user remembers is GDR_NOTICE's fill.

- **The band** (CIFStretchWnd `0x8182e0`, drawn by `0x819d80`): the fill quad over the text's rect
  at alpha 128, and eight frame quads **outside** it, each its texture's own size -- corners
  mirrored to the four corners, edge2 (40 x 8) left and right, edge (4 x 8) above and below
  (vslot_010 hands `0x819690` edge2, edge, edge2, edge). MEASURED: the frame textures are one colour
  each (their fill), edge2's alpha 0 -> 127 over 40 columns, edge's rows 51, 89, 128... So the band
  is (w + 80) x (h + 16) with 40-px soft ends -- the reference measures the same (2x picture: 28.5 px
  tall over 12 px text, a two-row top ramp, fading past the text both sides).
- **Text flags** (`0x8b44b0`/`0x8b4400`): flag 2 picks the face's lfWeight-600 variant (`0x8b39e0`,
  variants made in `0x00baa110`), flag 1 is a one-pixel drop shadow (`0x8b2290`). The notice text
  has flag 2 only -- bold, no shadow. MEASURED on the reference: 2-px strokes, no dark pixel beside
  them.
- **One at a time per instance**: a second show replaces the first (`0x7b3eb0`), no queue; the GM
  notice and the warning are separate windows, up together.
- **The area banner** (CIFRegionView): the region id's code from `textdata\regioncode.txt` (rows
  with a non-zero service and a code other than "xxx"); an unnamed region clears the remembered
  code, the same code shows nothing, another code shows code_01 / code_02 / code_03 from
  textzonename.txt ("xxx" blanked). Every one of the 147 codes, not only towns: fields, dungeons,
  ferries. Layout 744 x 104 at (W/2 - 372, 95), the title at W/2 - trunc(w x 0.75),
  119 - trunc(h x 0.375).

**Why ours was broken (READ, in every renderer).** Round 634's `_draw` put the fill over the text's

## Seven-hundred-and-second round: the original's own distance fog -- linear, nothing before the zone's start plane -- replaces Godot's haze from the camera, with a temporary Video row to compare; the saved Video settings reach the world at start-up; Circle shadows under every character and none in Detail

The user (2026-10-03): "this has been a long term problem but I believe there's a fog effect around
the camera. When I zoom in and out I see shadows come and go. Can we get rid of that fog? I want the
game to be as vibrant and bright as the original and that fog seems to wash everything out." Asked
whether to keep fog the original has: "If the original game has it then make a temporary toggle in
the video settings so I can compare and make a decision." And: "When you do detailed shadows it
still shows the simple circle shadow when it shouldn't. The no shadow mode works fine." Lane
`fog702`, client. Labels: READ (`sro_client.exe`, the box's decompile and asm), MEASURED, INFERRED,
OURS.

### 1. What the client applied (READ in our code, MEASURED on the box)

- **Godot's exponential fog from the camera**: density 0.00005 (OURS, "a disclosed rendering choice"),
  sun scatter 0.1 and aerial perspective 0.5 (OURS), the zone's fog colour. The READ planes
  (round 229) were computed and logged but not drawn.
- **Filmic tone map** (tonemap_mode 2, OURS since the 2026-08-26 atmosphere pass), exposure 1.
- **Glow** (the Bloom row): intensity 0.8, bloom 0.2, threshold 0.85 (round 693's guess). SSAO off.
- **The sun's shadow map at Godot's default reach**: `directional_shadow_max_distance` 100 from
  the camera, faded from 80. The camera sits 20-90 units from the player.
- **The saved Video record was never applied at start-up** (found this round). The first
  `apply_video_options` call compared each row against the record in force, which was the record
  being applied (`video_options()` had just made it so), so no row "changed": every start drew the
  scene's own settings -- **the sun's shadow map ON even in Circle (Middle, the default)**, glow off
  although Bloom is on, no MSAA, no mip bias -- until the player changed a row in the window, and
  then only that row.

So the user's ordinary state was: Filmic, no glow, the exponential fog, the shadow map on with a
100-unit reach, and the player's circle on top of it.

**Measurement** (`qa_shot.sh` shots with the new `|key=value` per-viewpoint settings and
`OPENSRO_QA_PATCHES`, QaShotEnv; Jangan spawn (1002, 1020), yaw 0, pitch -30, camera at 20 / 45 /
90; ground squares of the plaza 15 and 40 units beyond the player and 40 to each side; Forward+,
1280 x 720; L = mean Rec. 709 luma of the square, c = its standard deviation, the contrast;
identical-settings shots differ by <= 0.5):

| before this round (dev 34286d92) | nz2 at z20 / z45 / z90 (L, c) | nz at z20 / z90 | horizon shot, sky band |
|---|---|---|---|
| as players had it (Filmic, no glow, shadow map, exp. fog) | 91.0 c20.9 / 90.2 c18.0 / 88.4 c15.9 | 70.1 / 74.2 | 205.5 |
| tone map Linear | 82.0 c16.0 / 81.0 c13.6 / 79.8 c12.1 (and glow on) | 66.4 / 68.4 | 191.2 |
| tone map Linear, no glow | 72.4 c15.4 / 71.7 c13.3 / 70.3 c11.7 | 56.7 / 59.9 | 180.4 |
| glow on | 100.7 c19.8 / 100.1 c17.8 / 99.2 c16.2 | 81.9 / 84.3 | 214.6 |
| glow on, Godot fog off | 102.3 / 100.2 / 97.2 | 79.5 / 81.5 | 217.2 |

- The exponential fog changes the near ground by at most ~2 luma (the spawn's patches lie 40-130
  units from the camera, where it is 0.2-0.7 %); it is a distance haze, 10-30 % from 2000 units out.
- **Glow is the wash**: +10-12 luma on every patch with the contrast unchanged in absolute terms,
  so contrast relative to brightness falls ~15 % (nz z20 c/L 0.32 -> 0.27).
- **Filmic is not**: Linear is 13 luma darker with the same relative contrast (0.32 / 0.30).
- **The shadows that came and went**: with the 100 reach, the player's square at z90 (feet, 98 from
  the camera) is 2.5 luma lighter than with a 4000 reach -- the player's own shadow fades out as the
  camera pulls back; with 100 vs 4000, 4-6 % of the frame's pixels change (distant buildings'
  shadows; frame_ab-style diff, MEASURED).

### 2. What the original does (READ)

**Fog** -- `Map::FUN_00a26f60`, the landscape step: FOGENABLE (0x1c) = 1 at 0xa27549, FOGCOLOR
(0x22) = world+0x67e6 (sqrt of channel 9, round 628) at 0xa2755c; the range at 0xa27568..0xa2765e:
world+0x26e1 == 0 -> start = end = 10000.0 (0xd82efc), but its only writer, the constructor, sets it
to 1 (0xa2f76a); world+0x26bb == 0 -> start / end = world+0x68af / +0x68b3 (DAT_011081ff /
01108203), channels 10 / 11 x the view distance (round 229); else (set at 0xa2ce1a for a flagged
cell, INFERRED indoor) start -200.0 (0xde4db8), end far / 10. FOGDENSITY 0.005 (unused by linear),
RANGEFOGENABLE 0 (0xa276b0: view depth, not radial), table fog LINEAR or vertex fog LINEAR by
world+0x237e bit 15 (0xa276fc..0xa27735), and the same start / end to the object renderer's fog slot
(vslot_014, c16; vss0.c's LINEAR fog). **So the original does have distance fog**, at the zone's own
planes, and nothing before the start plane: it darkens or hazes nothing near the camera. The spawn
block's record (EnvironmentID 15, "Env7") has channels 10 / 11 = 0.759 / 1.000: fog from 1897 to
2500 at the default view distance (MEASURED from the archive, logged).

**Shadows** -- `SWorld::vslot_024` (0xa182f0) draws by the Shadow Detail value at SWorld+0x2e58:
1 (Circle) draws `skybox\shadowsphere.ddj` (world+0x2a3f, loaded by `Map::FUN_00a0d1b0`) through
`SWorld::vslot_022` for each object that IsKindOf CICharactor (runtime class 0xef1a5c,
`CICharactor::vslot_000`) -- players, monsters and NPCs -- at most ten (`9 < count` break), size
`FUN_009c75c0() + 5` = the reference record's +0x118, BCRadius (teleport_network.md, 0x972ce2), colour
0xa8000000 (alpha 168); vslot_022 projects it over the ground cells (MODULATE TEXTURE x TFACTOR,
SRCALPHA / INVSRCALPHA; the TFACTOR is a stack argument at 0x9f44cd, INFERRED to be that colour).
2 (Detail) draws only the projected per-character shadows (`Map::FUN_009f35f0` per slot of
`SWorld::vslot_025`, 0xa17ab0: up to ten characters, each rendered into the 96 x 96 target and kept
as a 32 x 32 texture, the list walked while its key is <= 3000) -- **no circle**. 0 draws neither.
Neither mode depends on the camera's distance (the 3000 key, INFERRED a distance, is past every
zone's fog end). The original's scenery casts no real-time shadow: its building shadows are baked.

**Bloom** (partly read, not changed): `Map::FUN_00a1d790` -- screen copy x 0.776 (TFACTOR alpha
world+0x690c = 0xc6) + 512 x 512 blur x 0.753 (BLENDFACTOR +0x690d = 0xc0); OPTION_VIDEO.md.

### 3. What changed

- **`WorldFog` (new): the original's linear fog.** A full-screen quad parented to the camera, its
  vertex shader putting it over the view, first in the transparent sort (render priority -1),
  reads the opaque depth, turns it into view depth (both renderers' NDC) and blends the fog colour at
  `(depth - start) / (end - start)`; the sky (no depth) is left to its own fog. Start / end =
  channels 10 / 11 x the Background Sight Range's view distance (READ rule; before, a density factor,
  OURS). The colour is pre-inverted through the tone map (`pass_color`), so a fully fogged pixel
  shows the READ colour. The terrain's feathered overlays and both water surfaces are drawn before
  the pass (priority -2) and so fogged with the ground they lie on; a blended MTRL mod, drawn after,
  fogs itself from the same values (`srr_fog_params` / `srr_fog_color` shader globals in
  project.godot; Godot's FOG built-in). Godot's own fog is kept enabled at density 0 (Compatibility
  applies a shader's FOG only while it is on) with the OURS sun scatter and aerial perspective
  removed. The log line `World3D: environment fog (READ): ...` names each zone's planes.
- **"Fog (temporary)"** (VideoOptions.FOG = 18, OURS, the user's request): on by default (the
  original); off draws no fog. Not in any preset, saved as `fog_temporary`; listed after SSAO.
- **The first `apply_video_options` applies every row.** A default record now draws Middle from the
  first frame: Circle (no sun shadow map), glow, MSAA 2x, mip bias 1 (Forward+).
- **`CharacterBlobs` (new): Circle as the original draws it** -- under every character kind (the
  player, other players, monsters and NPCs register), the ten nearest the camera (INFERRED order),
  size BCRadius + 5 (READ; taken as the diameter, INFERRED -- 9 for the default body, the size drawn
  before), alpha 0xa8 / 255 (READ; before: the texture's full alpha). **Detail and Nothing draw no
  circle** for any of them. Until now one circle followed the player alone, in Circle and Detail.
- **Detail's shadow map reaches 3000 from the camera** (`SHADOW_MAP_DISTANCE`, READ-anchored to the
  original's 3000 key) instead of Godot's 100. *(Corrected in the review: the key is 10 x the distance
  from the player, so 400.)*
- QA: `QaShotEnv` (`|tonemap=,sdist=,glow_bloom=` or any Video row per viewpoint),
  `OPENSRO_QA_PATCHES`, `QA BLOBS` lines; `OPENSRO_QA_NOFOG` now turns the pass off.

### Review

The review found two blockers and several corrections; all are fixed here (commit after cf7b7d14).

**H1 -- the start-up fix made "washed out" worse.** It turned on Middle's Bloom, which was Godot glow
at round 693's guessed values: the near ground went 91.0 -> 102.3 luma with less contrast (section
4). The reviewer read the original's bloom in full (`Map::FUN_00a1d790`, constants from the
constructor `Map::FUN_00a2f370`; OPTION_VIDEO.md has every step): downsample to 512 x 512 at
x 128/255; a horizontal blur with a 40/255 threshold (this pass only) and weights 80 / 70 / 50 (/255)
at 0 / +-2.6 / +-5.2 texels of 512; the same vertical blur without the threshold; composite
`clamp(S x 198/255 + Blur x 192/255)` in display values. A flat field crosses over at 0.5: darker
below, brighter above -- it raises contrast.
- **`RetailBloom`** (new): that formula as one canvas pass on layer -1 (above the 3D view, under every
  interface layer and the brightness pass), in both renderers; the Bloom row shows it. Godot's glow
  is always off and round 693's glow values are gone from World3D.tscn. The Bloom row is no longer
  greyed under Compatibility.
- **Formula check** (`tools/measure_retail_bloom.gd`: ramps and seeded 7-pixel blocks, 4000 pixels x
  3 channels, the CPU formula from the bloom-off frame against the bloom-on frame): Forward+ max
  0.62/255 (mean 0.24), Compatibility max 0.95/255 (mean 0.27); 100 % within 1/255.
- **The same squares** (Jangan spawn, z20 / z45 / z90; L, c):

| | nz2 | nz z20 / z90 | nz2 c / L at z20 | horizon sky band |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| dev before the round (as players had it) | 91.0 c20.9 / 90.2 c18.0 / 88.4 c15.9 | 70.1 / 74.2 | 0.23 | 205.5 |
| the round's first version (Godot glow on) | 102.3 c20.3 / 100.0 c16.6 / 96.3 c13.5 | 79.0 / 81.4 | 0.20 | 215.7 |
| **now: the original's bloom (default)** | **80.3 c21.0 / 76.7 c14.5 / 72.3 c11.6** | **55.8 / 56.0** | **0.26** | **226.5** |
| now, Bloom off | 91.2 c20.9 / 89.9 c17.2 / 86.8 c13.9 | 69.7 / 72.0 | 0.23 | 204.7 |

  The paved ground (luma 70-90, under the crossover) is drawn darker and with more relative contrast
  and saturation (nz2 s 21.4 -> 26.5); the bright sky brighter. That is the original's look by its
  own arithmetic (READ), not a tuning.

**H2 -- Detail cost +2.2 ms, and the 3000 was misread.** The list key is `(int)(|object - player| x
10)` (CICPlayer::vslot_005 0x9d6f19..0x9d6fad), so `key <= 3000` is 300 units from the PLAYER.
- `SHADOW_MAP_DISTANCE` is 400 (300 + the camera's farthest 90 + a margin, OURS).
- In Detail only characters cast: the terrain patches and every placed-object template (so every
  placed copy) have casting off -- the original's scenery casts none, its shadows are baked.
- **Detail on terrain** (the review's M2): `ShadowCatcher`, a next pass on each terrain base
  (`blend_mul`, no ambient / specular / fog, `light()` adding `mix(k, 1, ATTENUATION)` for the sun),
  Forward+ only. k: READ in `FUN_009f2f80`, which builds the redrawn ground's vertices -- DIFFUSE black
  with alpha `round(150 - clamp((h - ref - 12) x 9, 0, 150))` (0xd83058, 0xd89248, 0xdd7ca8,
  0xdb8d74), so the ground keeps 1 - 150/255 = 0.412 of its colour under a solid silhouette; the
  catcher multiplies in linear light, so k = 0.412 decoded (INFERRED conversion). The fade with
  height is not reproduced. Render priorities: overlays and water -3, catcher -2, fog -1.
- **Placed floors: no catcher.** They are shaded, so they receive the shadow map natively (MEASURED
  at the spawn plaza: Detail darkens 2,502 / 533 / 150 pixels of the player's square against
  Nothing); a catcher there would darken twice.
- **Terrain, MEASURED** (farmland 96/168 at (960, 960), Forward+; the player's square): Detail
  against Nothing -5.1 / -6.0 / -6.5 luma at z20 / z45 / z90, 3,141 / 701 / 173 pixels darker by
  more than 8 (Circle: 7,647 / 1,635 / 375); before the review, Detail had no ground shadow there.

### Rework review

**H2 + M2 -- the bloom's 4K cost and its edge echoes.** Taps at full resolution, at the 512-texel
offsets, land 19.5 / 39 px apart at 3840 wide: sharp echoes of every edge, and +0.82 ms there.
- A first fix took the taps on the screen's mip level log2(width / 512): no echoes, but Godot builds
  those mips by a Gaussian blur of every level and the trilinear taps run per screen pixel -- the
  4K gate measured **+2.0 ms** (4.03 -> 6.07 ms, SLOWER). Dropped for Forward+.
- **Now (Forward+):** retail's pipeline at retail's resolution. A 514 x 514-vertex grid, one vertex
  per texel of the 512 x 512 target, whose vertex shader computes that texel exactly as retail's
  three passes do (81 screen samples: D at the texel centres, the horizontal taps between texels
  thresholded, the vertical taps); the fragments interpolate across the grid (linear within each
  half-cell where retail magnifies bilinearly -- OURS) and the composite is the blend itself
  (premultiplied alpha: Blur x 192/255 + screen x 198/255), as retail's.
- **Compatibility** reads nothing from the screen texture in a vertex stage (MEASURED: the grid
  added no light under GL 4.6), so there the pass keeps the 25 taps on the 512-wide mip.
- **Against retail's own pipeline**, computed on the CPU from the same frame (the rewritten
  `tools/measure_retail_bloom.gd`; 4000 pixels x 3 channels):

| | mean | p99 | max |
|---|---|---|---|
| Forward+ 1280 x 720 | 0.24/255 | 0.56/255 | 1.5/255 |
| Forward+ 3840 x 2160 | 0.30/255 | 1.43/255 | 5.8/255 |
| Compatibility 1280 x 720 (mips) | 1.6/255 | 7.7/255 | 11.9/255 |

  A white bar 1/64 of the width wide: the light the bloom adds beside it falls from 47-50/255 to 0
  with **no echo peak** at either size, in both renderers.
- **Cost at 3840 x 2160** (`perf_gate.sh` gained `--size`): Bloom on against off on this head
  (`--base HEAD --env OPENSRO_QA_VIDEO=bloom=1 --base-env ...=0`, jangan, median of 3):
  **4.03 -> 4.72 ms, +0.69, SLOWER**. Against the base build on the same Video rows (base Middle =
  round 693's Godot glow): 4.37 -> 4.79, +0.42, SAME. Where it goes (`tools/time_retail_bloom.gd`,
  the root viewport's GPU time at 4K over a synthetic picture): nothing 0.14 ms; a stub that only
  reads the screen once and writes it back 0.74 ms; the bloom 1.18-1.21 ms. So about 0.6 ms is Godot
  4.2's full-screen back-buffer copy that any canvas pass reading the screen pays at 4K, and ~0.45 ms
  the grid's work. **Recorded for the user, not fixed:** the remaining +0.7 ms at 4K is the
  Bloom row's (Middle turns it on; off restores it).

**H1 -- overlays were bloomed.** Retail draws its world, then the bloom, then the lens flare
(`SWorld::vslot_005` -> `FUN_00a1d790` -> `FUN_00a21280`), and its names as 2D text over that.
- **`OverlayView`** (new): name plates, damage numbers, party marks and name boxes go on their own
  render layer (bit 16), which the main camera leaves out; a transparent SubViewport of the window's
  size, sharing the world, renders that layer through a camera copying the main one each frame, and
  shows it at canvas layer 0 (over the bloom at -1, under the world's UI at 1). All of them draw
  with no depth test, so leaving the scene's depth behind changes nothing; their colours go through a
  linear tone map there (retail draws text colours as they are).
- **MEASURED** (the Jangan spawn at z90, an NPC's plate in view): pixels within 6 of the plate colour
  (255, 240, 184): 123 with the bloom on, 124 with it off, 123 the same pixel -- the plate is no
  longer touched by the bloom (before, (1.0, 0.94, 0.72) came out near (204, 191, 148)).
- **Not moved (OURS, disclosed in TODO):** the lens-flare sun sprite (depth-tested against the
  scene) and the character-select characters are still bloomed.

**M1 -- the catcher's k.** The decoded 0.141 assumed a linear tone map; the world is Filmic. Fitted
on the screen: the shadow core's displayed ratio (Detail over Nothing, farmland 96/168 top-down,
ground at luma ~98) measured 0.38 at k = 0.219 (Filmic's own prediction for 0.412 at luma 95), so k
= **0.25**; at 0.25 the core measures **0.414 / 0.429** (median, z45 / z90) and the histogram's mode
**0.413** -- the READ 0.412. FITTED, labelled so in ShadowCatcher.

**L4:** `_terrain_patches` drops freed patches whenever a patch is added.

**M3 (record):** on High (Detail), buildings and hills no longer cast real-time shadows -- only the
baked ones remain, as in retail, whose scenery casts none; characters cast, on objects and (through
the catcher) on the terrain. *Release note:* "High (Detail) shadows: only characters cast real-time
shadows now, as in the original -- building and hill shadows are the baked ones."

**L1, L2, L5:** BerserkFlash after the bloom (PLAUSIBLE), the character-create preview not bloomed
(PLAUSIBLE), and CLAMP against a possible WRAP at the target's edges are in docs/TODO.md.

### Final review (the overlay view)

- **H1 (CONFIRMED, fixed): at a UI scale other than 1 the overlay was shown magnified from the
  top-left corner.** The TextureRect kept Godot's default `EXPAND_KEEP_SIZE`, so its minimum size
  was the texture's, the window in physical pixels; under `content_scale_factor` 2.0 the full rect is
  half that in UI units, and the stretch doubled the rest. The review's GPU render put a plate that
  projects to window (640, 360) at (1251, 715). Fixed with `EXPAND_IGNORE_SIZE`;
  `world/overlay_view_test.gd` checks the shown rect against the window at 1.0 / 1.5 / 2.0 and fails
  on c3769753 at 1.5 and 2.0 (got (64, 64) for (42, 42) and (32, 32) in the headless window).
- **L1 (fixed):** the front-end's backdrop (title, select, create) has nothing on the overlay layer;
  `OverlayView.set_rendering(false)` stops the viewport there.
- **L2 (MEASURED, synthetic):** at 3840x2160 the overlay SubViewport costs ~0.26-0.29 ms GPU and the
  composite ~0.09 ms (400 boxes, a shadowed sun, 30 plates; not measured in the real world).
- **Checked fine by the review:** input passes through to the world (a push_input probe: left/right
  press and release, wheel, right-held motion all reach `_unhandled_input`); the copied camera
  matches the main one every frame; the viewport is the window's pixel size at 1.0 / 1.5 / 2.0 and
  follows a resize; nothing else needs the overlay layer.
- **Open (PLAUSIBLE):** text edges with partial alpha may tone-map slightly brighter than in the main
  view (L3); a camera moved by a Tween would leave the overlay one frame behind (L4; no such writer
  today).

## Seven-hundred-and-first round: a press of the left button is one click -- holding it moves neither the ring nor the walk, as in retail -- the ring lies on Jangan's plaza deck (the user's decision), and a far NPC or gate is walked to before it talks, a monster selected before it is attacked

The user (2026-10-03): "if you click and hold down the click the circle will fluidly move around
with your cursor and your character will follow. The original game places the circle where you
first clicked but doesn't follow the cursor if you hold it down. You have to reclick to move the
circle. Your character also doesn't follow the cursor, they go to circle instead." And, having
checked a live retail server, that retail draws no ring on Jangan's central plaza deck: "That seems
like a bug we should fix" (a USER DECISION: ours, an improvement over retail). Lane `move701`,
client, a world round. Labels: READ (`sro_client.exe` on the box: the decompile and
`sro_client.asm`), MEASURED, INFERRED, OURS. `docs/protocol/ground_markers.md` has both records
("Holding the left button", "On a placed floor").

### 1. What holding the left button does in retail (READ)

Nothing after the press.

- **WM_LBUTTONDOWN** (0x201) in `CGInterface::vslot_017` (0x77c260) calls 0x793570 at 0x77c4a7:
  the pick under the cursor (`FUN_0078ee20`), then the object click `FUN_00792f00` or the ground
  click `UI_SILKMALL::FUN_0078f8d0` -> `FUN_009ec570` (the 20-unit NPC test, the destination, the
  5-unit filter `FUN_009ec240`, the ring `FUN_00a631e0`), or a sky run `FUN_009ebec0`. The only
  place a left click walks.
- **WM_MOUSEMOVE** (0x200), the same handler: turns the camera when the right byte +0x25a is down
  (swap flag +0x4f9 clear) or the middle +0x259 (flag set). It never reads the left byte +0x258.
- **WM_LBUTTONUP** (0x202) -> `FUN_0078e5d0`: only ends process modes 0xae / 0xaf. No pick.
- **Timer 7** (500 ms, `FUN_00777b90`): set after a sky click and by the per-frame `FUN_009ec380`
  while a heading run lasts, killed by a ground click (`FUN_00777ba0`); its case in
  `CGInterface::vslot_005` runs `FUN_009eb8e0`, which re-plots the run from the player's own
  position and heading and reads no mouse. **Round 698's protocol line "a held button repeats the
  click (timer 7)" was wrong** and is corrected.
- The button bytes are written by `gfxmainframe::FUN_00ba7240` (+0x258 left, +0x259 middle, +0x25a
  right) and read through `FUN_00ba6240(i)`; its only index-0 (left) reader is the hover code's
  cursor choice (0x9a instead of 0x99 over a ground item while held). The 0xB021 heading echo
  (`FUN_008a5750`) hides the ring for heading moves only.

So: a press puts the ring down and sends one move; the character walks to the ring; a drag moves
neither; a new press does. No camera drag on the left button.

### 2. What changed

- **The click is the press** (`World3D._unhandled_input`): `_dispatch_left_click(event.position)`
  on the press; the release does nothing; the held-button steer (`_left_steering`,
  `_left_dragging`, `LEFT_DRAG_THRESHOLD_PIXELS`, the per-frame re-pick in `_physics_process`) is
  gone. Until now the click went on the release, and a drag past 6 pixels re-picked the
  destination -- and the ring -- under the cursor every physics frame. One log line a press:
  `CLICK: left press at (x, y) -> walk to (x, y, z)` (or attack / talk / pickup / ignore).
  The right button's orbit, the 5-unit filter, round 698's 20-unit NPC rule and the wall root
  are untouched. HELP_PLAYING's "hold the left button to steer" is rewritten.
- **The ring on a placed floor** (`GroundMarkers`, all OURS): a point more than 1.0 above the
  drawn terrain whose short ray down (0.5 above to 1.0 below, layers 0b1001) meets a body without
  the terrain-only bit takes a drape sampled by vertical rays on a 2-unit grid of the region's
  frame, from 2.0 above the point to 2.0 below; a triangle with a missed or out-of-span corner, or
  corners more than 1.0 apart, is left out. The same shader, texture and origin uniform as the
  terrain ring, lifted 0.05. Rebuilt only when the point enters another 6 x 6 cell or moves 0.25
  in height; samples cached per region and height. On terrain the drape is retail's, unchanged.
  The region-key lookup is now remembered per group name, which made the terrain path cheaper
  than before.

### 7. The click side of NPCs, gates and monsters (READ; added mid-round)

The user, from playing the original: "Monsters seem to show the sword far away and it will have
your character walk to the monster and then attack. NPCs are a little different where I think it
shows as far as you can see them but it will put the circle not where you clicked exactly but
where the furthest spot to talk them in the same direction. Currently it seems like we can talk to
NPCs from any distance." `docs/protocol/ground_markers.md`, "Clicking an NPC, a gate or a
monster", has the full record.

- **The distance** 0x793570 reads is the object's +0x24c, the 3-D distance from the local player
  that `CICPlayer::vslot_005` writes for every object each frame (0x9d6f19..0x9d6f7e).
- **An NPC** within 240.0 (double 0xdb9888) is selected at once (0x7045, `FUN_0078f5f0`); the
  0xB045 reply opens the talk window. Beyond, `FUN_009ec6b0(id, 20.0, 240.0, 0)` walks to
  `npc + d * unit(player - npc)` with `d = rand() / 32767.0 * 220 + 20`, moves the ring there
  with the ground texture, and `FUN_009ec380` fires the select when the mover has started and
  stopped. So the user's "furthest spot to talk, in the same direction" is the line and the ring
  is right; the distance is random in 20..240, not always the farthest.
- **A gate**: 800.0 (double 0xd83080) and a walk to 20..640 (float 0xdb9890) short; no follow ring.
- **A monster**: no distance test and no walk on the client. The first click selects (ring,
  target window); `FUN_00792f00` sends the attack 0x7074 only with Ctrl, or when the monster is
  already the selection with the target window up, or on a double click (`FUN_00792190`). Who
  walks into reach is the server (READ in the review: the attack tick 0x4ad8e0 calls
  `GObjPC::MoveTowardObject`); OpenSRO's client walks (OURS, as
  before).
- **Cancelling**: a ground click clears the pending id (`FUN_009ec570`: +0x20 = 0). Ours drops it
  on any new click, death, a zone change or the target going (OURS beyond the ground click).
- **The server**: the select handler (0x50faf0) refuses beyond `IsWithinInteractionRange` (300 for
  an NPC, 800 for a structure), silently on the client. OpenSRO has no select request: the
  arrival applies that limit itself. The teleport request has applied it since round 642; the shop
  and storage requests name no NPC, so the server cannot (TODO). No server code changed.

**Built**: `World3D._start_talk_approach`, `_step_talk_approach`, `talk_needs_approach`,
`talk_approach_point`, `_walkable_point` (the graph's landing height under the point, OURS),
`monster_click_attacks`; `_dispatch_left_click` answers `approach` and `select_monster`. QA:
`OPENSRO_QA_CLICK_STANDOFF` ("npc=330,gate=880:-x,monster=280") stands the QA click's player
that far short on a chosen side.

### Review

The review found nothing HIGH. Fixed here:

1. **M1, the help text** (CONFIRMED): HELP_PLAYING said "Click a monster once to attack it" and
   that the client does not walk back into reach. It now says the first click selects and a second
   click, a double click or Ctrl+click attacks; that a far NPC or gate is walked to first; and that
   the character walks back in (retail's server does, and this client does). `bundle_docs.sh`
   re-run (its RELEASE_NOTES snapshot picked up v0.1.483).
2. **L2**: the server's walk into reach is READ, not INFERRED -- SR_GameServer's attack tick
   0x4ad8e0 calls `GObjPC::MoveTowardObject` when the target is out of reach
   (docs/protocol/auto_command.md, rounds 247 / 256).
3. **L3**: a click on an NPC now moves the selection off a monster (`_select_for_talk`: retail's
   0x793570 calls `FUN_00778650` for any CICharactor, in reach or before an approach); a gate does
   not. Before, a later single click on the old monster attacked at once. With it,
   `_target_window_shows` now compares the window's own target (`HudTarget.shown_key`, set by
   `show_target` / `show_player`, cleared by `clear`) with the clicked monster, not only that the
   window is up.
4. **L4**: a typing or motion lock no longer reads as an arrival: the approach pauses
   (`_step_talk_approach(locked)`) and walks on to the same point when the lock lifts (OURS; not
   while a wall roots the player).
5. **L5**: a double click's second press is routed as retail's WM_LBUTTONDBLCLK
   (`_dispatch_double_click`, `FUN_00792190`): a monster under the cursor is attacked; the ground,
   an NPC and a gate get nothing, so a far NPC's approach is not re-rolled.
6. **L6**: the dead `_try_attack_monster` is replaced by `_monster_at` (the double click's pick);
   the comments that named it now name `_pick_character`.
7. **L7**: objects streaming into a region (`_objects_commit`) drop the floor samples and re-run

## Six-hundred-and-ninety-ninth round: the developer toggles move from Ctrl+F1-F3 to Shift+F1-F3, because macOS keeps Ctrl+F1-F3 for itself

The user (2026-10-03, on v0.1.481 under CrossOver on macOS): "can switch the ctrl+f1-f3 menus to
shift+f1-f3? It's not working on macOS for some reason. I wanna be able to test DPI"

**Why Ctrl failed there.** macOS binds Ctrl+F1 (turn keyboard access on or off), Ctrl+F2 (move focus
to the menu bar) and Ctrl+F3 (move focus to the Dock) by default (System Settings, Keyboard
Shortcuts, Keyboard). The system takes them before any application, so the client under CrossOver
never saw them. INFERRED from those defaults; not traced on the user's Mac. Shift+F1-F3 have no default
binding there. A Mac keyboard may also need Fn for the F keys, unless "Use F1, F2, etc. keys as
standard function keys" is on.

**The change** (OURS; retail tests no modifier for an F key, `KeyMap.resolve`'s reading, 0x778310
and 0x780610):
- `KeyMap.resolve` takes Shift (a new last argument, default false). Shift+F1 opens the
  developer tools, Shift+F2 the debug tabs and Shift+F3 the debug panel.
- Ctrl+F1-F3 now select pages 1-3, as plain F1-F3 and every other modifier do, which is retail's
  behaviour.
- Both callers pass `shift_pressed`: KeyInput, and HudPanels' window keys.
- Shift+F1-F3 still run while a text line has the keyboard (`runs_while_typing` is by key code).
- Every player-facing mention is updated: the controls line, the developer-tools and debug-panel
  lines, the unstuck hint, HELP_PLAYING, DEBUG_TOOLS and NATIVE_ON_WINDOWS. The older rounds' entries keep
  the key they had then.

**Follow-up (the user, 2026-10-03, later the same day).** "that worked but I think dxvk was the proper
fix to pick up fn key. Let's keep it at shift for now though." So the cause given above is
UNCONFIRMED: with DXVK switched on in CrossOver the F keys reached the game. Whether Ctrl+F1-F3 also
reach it with DXVK on was not tried. The keys stay on Shift (the user's choice).

**Checked:** `keymap_test.gd`:
- Shift+F1/F2/F3 toggle their panel.
- Ctrl+F1/F2/F3 select their page.
- Shift+F4 selects page 4.
- Alt+F1 still selects page 1.
- With a text line focused, Shift+F1-F3 still run.

### Review

The review confirmed the account, the terrain-only drape included (`CIODecal::vslot_010` is
`SWorld::vslot_022`'s only caller; the vertices come only from the `.m` height record). Not to be
merged until the user, who believes the ring shows on the Jangan plaza, has checked a live server.
Fixed here:

1. **The height cache kept dropped regions alive** (MEDIUM). It held `[ParsedRegion, heights]`
   per group, never evicted, pinning 36 x 289 Vertex objects a region past
   `RegionGridState.prune_heightmaps()`. It now holds a WeakRef and the plain
   PackedFloat32Array; `step()` drops an entry whose region left the grid (or was parsed again);
   `zone_changed()` (called from `_reload_zone_assets`) clears it. Tested: a pruned region leaves
   the cache on the next step and its ParsedRegion is freed.
2. **A ground click near an NPC does nothing in retail** (LOW, READ). `FUN_009ec570`
   0x9ec5a0..0x9ec5eb walks the object list (`0xec4d98`, nodes at object+0x78c) and returns --
   before the destination, the click filter and `FUN_00a631e0` -- for a CICNPC (0xef1ac4, which
   CICGuard derives from; not monsters, players or CITeleportGate) under 400.0 squared (double
   0xd878a8: 20 units, `FUN_009ed1e0`'s 3-D distance) from the click whose +0xc4 is not 0.0.
   +0xc4 is READ as the object's model scale: `FUN_009c4510(scale)` stores it (0x9c451d) and
   resizes the model's box; the spawns pass the scale (CICNPC::vslot_025 0x9d487d; CICMonster's
   rarity x ref scale, 0x9d3a53); the CIObject constructor sets 1.0 (0x9c4909). Built in
   `_move_by_pick_ray` (`GroundMarkers.npc_blocking` over the holders tagged `npc_name`, not
   gates): no walk, no ring, and one line, `CLICK: ground at (x, y, z) ignored -- d from NPC
   <name> (retail walks nowhere within 20 of an NPC)`, for a tester who cannot walk next to one.
   Tested at 10 (blocked), 25 (walks), exactly 20 (not under 400), a gate, scale 0.
3. **The drape was rebuilt every tick under a moving body** (LOW). The mesh is now built for the
   3 x 3 cell window in the region's own frame (the instance takes the group's transform), and a
   ShaderMaterial (`RING_SHADER`) projects the UV from the vertex's region-local xz with the
   centre as a uniform -- the same UV `drape_arrays` computes, unshaded, blend mix, opaque-only
   depth, no culling, linear filter without repeat, sRGB art: StandardMaterial3D's settings. The
   still-water quad spans the window (with clamp and the transparent border it draws the same
   12 x 12 square). MEASURED with `client/tools/measure_ground_ring.gd` (a body at 50 units/s,
   1,200 ticks, headless on the box, three runs each): **116.5 / 117.4 / 116.6 us a tick with a
   new mesh on every tick before; 13.1 / 13.3 / 13.3 us with 49 new meshes (4.1 % of ticks)
   after.** The look, MEASURED in the same crops as runs 5 / 6: Compatibility's rerun of the
   same scene counts 281 pale-cyan ring pixels (283 before) and 168 orange (168 before); the
   Forward+ rerun drew in 97/168's frame (the zone frame differed between runs), 304 and 191,
   the rings as before in its frames. The drape lines are unchanged (+0.050 over the terrain
   ray at every centre).
4. **Docs.** Round 697 also rewrote docs/TODO.md's line on retail's ground-pick cursor and decal;

## Six-hundred-and-ninety-seventh round: the game's own cursors on every screen -- gold arrow, red sword, speech bubble, glove, blue gate disc -- found wherever a player keeps sro_client.exe, scaled with the UI, chosen by the original's class rules on its 250 ms timer; and the Option combos' open list in retail's translucent black

The user (2026-10-03, from memory, no screenshots): "there's a golden cursor that's the default.
Then when you hover a teleporter it shows a blue teleporter icon. If you hover an npc it shows a
chat looking icon. If you hover over an enemy it shows a red sword. If you hover a stall (not
implemented yet) it shows a chest or something like that. Add that feature but make sure you follow
the code exactly." And: "those dropdown menus that you fixed, the actual dropdown background needs
to be a transparent black." Later: "hostile mobs count for the red sword and circle too btw", and
"Scale the cursor with the dpi scaling, just like the rasterized images. It doesn't look great but
it's authentic and usable."

### 1. Why the user never saw a cursor

Round 206 already read the cursors out of the exe, but `World3D` looked for it only at
`$OPENSRO_PK2_PATH`'s folder. A player's build finds its archives in the `pk2` folder by
`Pk2Config` WITHOUT that variable, so the path was empty and the system arrow stayed -- for every
player, on every screen. And the user's install is a bare `pk2/` folder with no exe in it.

### 2. What the client does (READ; the full table is docs/protocol/CURSOR.md)

Every direct caller of the three cursor entry points was read (the manager `0xba6260` x4,
SetHoverCursor `0x777ec0` x16, ForceCursor `0x777e70` x20; asm call sites, the decompile's
argument-less calls resolved from the pushes):

| Id | Art (MEASURED) | When |
|---|---|---|
| 0x95 | gold arrow | default, every screen from `CPSVersionCheck::vslot_011` (0x86d150) on; nothing / a window / a friendly under the mouse |
| 0x97 | sword, red edge | attackable CICMonster / CICMonsterNPC; enemy guild in fortress war; another team |
| 0x98 | speech bubble | CICNPC (exact class) |
| 0x99 / 0x9a | open / closed glove | a CIItem; closed while the left button is held (input +0x258, WM_LBUTTONDOWN) |
| 0xa0 | sword, bright red edge | a player (or another's COS) outside the party whose IsHostile(Alt held) is true |
| 0xa1 | blue disc | CITeleportGate |
| 0xa3 | pouch | a stalling player (+0x471 == 4, set by the 0x30b8 broadcast 0x873c10) -- the user's "chest" |
| 0x96, 0xa6, 0xae, 0xaf | hammer, bright arrow, socket tools | forced by the store's repair, an item applied to a slot, the socket window |

0x9d, 0x9e, 0x9f, 0xa2 are in the exe and never passed. **Nothing sets a cursor for a
ground-targeted skill.** The hover is CGInterface's **timer 1, every 250 ms** (`push 0xfa; push 1;
call 0xb93320`, 0x787294) -- `vslot_005` is the timer handler -- not mouse motion.

**The golden default is the resource 0x95, not the tga.** `Media.pk2`'s
`cursor\cursor_normal1.tga` decodes to a 32x32 glowing golden hand with alpha (looked at -- art
identification only); no string in the exe names it (ASCII and UTF-16) and no archive text does
(raw grep of Media.pk2 and Data.pk2: 0 hits). The manager only ever calls `LoadCursorA` with a
resource id. The live check below reads the X server's cursor on the login and select screens:
0x95's own 359 opaque pixels and mean colour.

**Hostility (the user's hostile mobs and players), exactly:** a monster is attackable when its
vslot 0xdc says so (CICMonster `0x9d3160`: by job mode against the monster's TypeID4, 1 for a
jobless player -- see Review, M2; CICMonsterNPC: `!(+0x7c8 & 2)`) and the
interface's set +0x500 holds key 5 (INFERRED "attack allowed") -- except that a player whose job
mode (vslot 0xac) is 4 (INFERRED: no job) gets the arrow over TypeID 1/2/1/2 and 1/2/1/3, the thief
and hunter NPC monsters. A player: IsHostile (`0x9de780`) is, in order, another team (+0x81d); the
base character test (job modes, murder state 0x9c7a40); fortress war enemy guild; differing job
bytes (+0x824); then -- when not both in job suits -- **Alt held**; then PK flags and a name list
(0x992a90, unread). Guards and fortress structures are hostile only in fortress war. This client
has none of teams, fortress war, jobs, murder state or that list, so **Alt over another player is
the only hostile player** here (0xa0; INFERRED: every other branch tests a state that never
reaches this client).

### Review

No HIGH findings. Fixed in this round:

- **M1 (READ): retail does not hide the cursor while the camera turns by default.** The hide and
  `SetCursorPos` in `CGInterface::vslot_012 0x77b140` run only while +0x82d is set; `vslot_017
  0x77c260` sets it only when the option byte settings+0x1c is non-zero (`0x77c535`, `0x77c6c1`),
  the Option window's UIIT_CTL_CAMERA_ROTATE_METHOD1 / METHOD2 choice (`0x5fcf40`), 0 by default
  (`0x7776c0`). So under method 1 the cursor stays visible and free -- what this client does. The
  first draft's "retail hides it" was wrong; CURSOR.md and TODO.md now record method 2 as an unbuilt
  Option.
- **M2 (READ): CICMonster's vslot 0xdc (`0x9d3160`) is conditional, not "always 1"**: 0 for job mode
  1 over a TypeID4 3 monster, mode 2 over one `0x779dd0` matches, mode 3 over one `0x779e20`
  matches, else 1 -- so 1 for a jobless player, this client's only state. Labels fixed
  (CURSOR.md, `GameCursor.monster_kind`); nothing to model without job state.
- **L1 (MEASURED by the review): a PE-signed garbage file stalled the parser** (1120 ms, 240k error
  lines): `_parse_pe` trusted the section count, `_dir_entries` the directory counts. Now the
  section count is capped at 96 and the table must fit the file, every directory's entries must fit
  (and at most 4096), each type directory is walked once, and every offset is checked before a
  read. `cursor_set_test` writes seven 1 MB PE-signed garbage files -- section counts 0xffff, 3, 1, 2
  over fills 0xff / 0x00 / 0x41, and three with one sane section mapping the resource table onto
  junk (fills 0x41, 0x00, 0x01; a type directory of 300 entries all claiming type 12 and pointing
  at themselves): each gives no cursor, in 0 ms and 22 ms respectively, with one log line each.
- **L2: retail's pick passes over dying characters** (FUN_0078ee20 skips a character whose +0x65c
  bit 0, alive, is clear). The hover's character ray now passes over a dying monster and goes on
  to what is behind it (up to 4 bodies), where it used to stop with the arrow.
- **L3: the hover follows the mouse while the camera turns** (retail method 1 reads the live
  position every tick); it used to keep the press point. The orbit itself is untouched.
- **L4:** the window frame and resize borders show the OS's shapes (retail sets its own there; Godot
  leaves the non-client area to the OS) -- a doc note.
- **Scaling filter:** the user chose nearest-neighbour (2026-10-03, "pixel-sharp is gonna be more
  clear"); recorded in CURSOR.md.
- **6a:** the ground pick's cross stays. Retail sets no cursor for a ground cast and shows a ring
  decal instead (`select_02` in range, `select_04` out of range, `FUN_00629fa0`, from lane 698);
  without that decal the cross is the only cue. Marked OURS until the decal is built.

over dying monsters, the hover position during an orbit, and documentation.

## Six-hundred-and-ninety-sixth round: in a window the chosen resolution sizes the OS window (a maximised window is restored first), and every Option combo draws the original's black value box

The user (2026-10-02, on v0.1.480, Windows at about 4K, UI scale ~1.95, window mode at 3840 x 2019):
"when you change the resolution in window mode please have the window size change with it.
Currently if you set a lower resolution it will leave a black area around the game inside the
actual game window." and "great start on the video settings but the drop downs need a black box
in them." Lane `ui696`, client, UI-only (no perf gate: no world, map, object, terrain, effect,
animation or loading code). Labels: READ (`sro_client.exe` on the box; Godot 4.2.2's source),
MEASURED, INFERRED, OURS. `docs/protocol/OPTION_VIDEO.md` has the record.

### 1. The black border (root cause, READ)

3840 x 2019 is a maximised window on a 3840 x 2160 screen. Round 694's `apply_display` set
`window.size` and moved it. In Godot 4.2.2:

- `Window::set_size` stores the size and calls `_update_window_size`, which asks the display
  server for the size and then sizes the viewport from the stored value (`_update_viewport_size`,
  scene/main/window.cpp);
- `DisplayServerWindows::window_set_size` and `window_set_position` both begin
  `if (wd.fullscreen || wd.maximized) return;` (platform/windows/display_server_windows.cpp).

So on Windows the OS window kept its maximised 3840 x 2019, no WM_SIZE came back to correct the
node, and the game drew a 1280 x 720 (or whatever was chosen) viewport in the corner of the
window: the rest black. Choosing a larger size again drew a viewport larger than the window.

### 2. What the original does (READ)

- The Video tab's store `0x5fdae0` calls `FUN_00835510(mode)` when the Resolution changed. In a
  window (`video+0xa0`) it ORs WS_CAPTION | WS_SYSMENU (0xC80000) into the style, turns
  {0, 0, w, h} into the frame with `AdjustWindowRect`, and `MoveWindow`s the frame to
  ((SM_CXFULLSCREEN - frame w) / 2, (SM_CYFULLSCREEN - frame h) / 2); then `FUN_004694d0` and
  `FUN_008354c0` reset the device to w x h. In full screen `CGFXVideo3d::vslot_020` (`0xbad590`)
  changes the display mode (`ChangeDisplaySettings`, CDS_FULLSCREEN) and `SetWindowPos`.
- The full screen <-> window toggle (`CGFXVideo3d::vslot_000`, `0xbad910`) does the same centred
  MoveWindow on the way into a window.
- Retail's style has no WS_THICKFRAME or WS_MAXIMIZEBOX: its window is never maximised or
  resized by hand. Ours can be, which is how the user met this.

### 3. The black value box (READ)

`CNIFComboBox::vslot_010` (`0x486d30`, asm `0x486d6e..0x486ee1`) takes the combo's own W x H rect
and makes: the arrow button {W-20, 0, 20, H} (`com_qst_downarrow_button.ddj`, 20 x 20); a
CNIFStretchWnd {0, 0, W-20, H} on `com_blacksquare_` (corners, `left_side` x2, `right_side` x2,
`0x49b040`) with +0x1c4 = 0xff000000; and the value CNIFStatic {5, 0, W-30, H}.
CNIFStretchWnd's draw (`0x49aeb0`) fills its rect with the +0x1c4 colour when it is non-zero
(`0x46d2a0`) and draws its frame over it -- the black box. Round 694 read that child as the list's
frame and drew no field. MEASURED in the box's Media.pk2: optionwnd.2dt has 14 CNIFComboBox
records, all on the Video pane (Resolution / Set Brightness 156 x 18, the rows' 217 150 x 20) --
no other Option tab has a combo; the six `com_blacksquare_` pieces are 4 x 4 (a near-black
top-left edge 0x080808..0x100c10, a grey bottom-right one 0x6a656a / 0x7b797b); `mid_up` /
`mid_down` do not exist.

### 4. What changed

- `VideoOptions.apply_display`: a maximised, minimised or full-screen window is restored
  (`MODE_WINDOWED`) before it is sized (`restore_for_size`); the client size is the chosen one cut
  to the usable area of the window's screen LESS the window's own frame (`frame_insets` from the
  display server's with/without-decoration rects; round 694's clamp, now counting the title bar);
  the frame is centred in that area (`window_placement`; retail centres it on the primary screen's
  full-screen area); afterwards `sync_window_size` makes the node's size the OS window's if they
  still differ (on Windows `window_get_size` is the real client size, so a size the OS refused can
  never again leave a viewport smaller than its window). One log line per apply names the node's
  size, the OS window's and the view's render target (for a tester's log), and one more each time
  the view changes size later ("view resized": a full-screen switch or maximise the window
  manager finishes after the call returns, a drag), at most one a frame.
- `OptionWindow` is centred again whenever the view changes size while it is open (OURS). Found
  by this round's live run: after Apply took the game window from 1920 x 1056 to 1024 x 768 the
  Option window kept its position, its right half and its Cancel / Apply off the screen. Retail
  sends its UI message 0x80a (w, h) after a resolution change (`CGFXVideo3d::vslot_020`); what its
  windows do with it is not read. The HUD's anchored pieces (minimap, hotbar, portrait) re-laid out
  by themselves (the shots); other open windows keep their positions (OPEN).
- `OptionVideoPage._make_combo`: the field (`ComboField`: the READ black fill and the
  `com_blacksquare_` pieces), the arrow (`ComboArrow`, the texture at its 20 x H button rect) and
  on top the OptionButton drawing only the text, centred in {5, 0, W-30, H} (a transparent 20-wide
  arrow icon keeps the arrow's room; 5 px style margins; no separation). The text is now sampled
  NEAREST (round 672's crisp text) -- the button draws nothing else; the field and arrow are its
  siblings and keep the art's filter. The top and bottom edges are the side pieces TRANSPOSED:
  MEASURED against the user's picture (one continuous row of the pieces' outer-column colour), the
  six-piece UVs (`0x49a140` / `0x49a7d0`) not read. A trap on the way: Godot 4.2.2 swaps a
  transposed rect's SIZE as well as its UVs (`canvas_item_add_texture_rect`, READ), so the first
  live run drew each top / bottom edge as a 4-wide dotted column hanging below the field; the size
  now goes in swapped.
