### Review (round 696's review: no HIGH; M1, L1, L2, L4 fixed in a second commit; L3 noted)

- **M1 (MEDIUM): the resolution list and clamp ignored the UI scale.** At 1.95 a 1280 x 720 window
  is a 656 x 369 view; the 700 x 500 Option window pinned at (0, 0) with Confirm / Cancel / Apply off
  the screen, and Boot re-applied the saved size at every start. Retail lists no mode narrower than
  800 or shorter than 600 (READ, 0x5fef70); here that minimum is the VIEW, window / scale
  (`VideoOptions.MIN_VIEW`, `min_window`, `view_fits`): `resolution_choices` lists only sizes with
  at least an 800 x 600 view at the window's content scale (on a screen with none, the largest that
  fits -- OURS, never an empty list), and `window_placement` raises a smaller asked size to
  `min_window(scale)` before the screen's clamp, which wins, so a size saved by an older build or at
  another scale cannot strand the player at start-up. Tests at 1.95 and 2.0 (the user's scale): on
  3840 x 2160 the list starts at 1600 x 1200 (no 1280 x 720, no 1920 x 1080 -- a 985 x 554 view at
  1.95); a saved 1280 x 720 becomes 1560 x 1170 at 1.95 and 1600 x 1200 at 2.0; at 2.0 a 1920 x 1080
  screen offers only 1920 x 1080 and a 1920 x 1040 work area gives 1600 x 1040.
- **L1: re-picking the stored Resolution while maximised did nothing** (the combo shows the stored
  value and Apply resized only on a change). The Resolution combo now takes a re-pick
  (`allow_reselect`), which marks `resolution_touched`; `store` hands the mark on once and clears it;
  World3D also applies the display when `VideoOptions.needs_resize` -- the row was touched and the
  window is maximised / minimised or not the size the placement gives. Moving the window is not a
  resize, so Apply on another tab still never snaps a moved window back (round 694's review).
  Live on the box (real X input, xfwm4, GL; `/var/tmp/ui696/runs/gl_L1`): 1024 x 768 confirmed,
  the window maximised by the window manager (1920 x 1056), 1024 x 768 picked again and confirmed:

- **L2: a drag-resize logged a line a frame.** The "view resized" line is now written once the size

## Six-hundred-and-ninety-fifth round: cut-out textures are see-through again under Forward+ -- tree leaves, hair, fences -- and the inventory's character renders at the screen's own resolution

The user (2026-10-02, on v0.1.480, the first release drawing with Forward+ by default; Windows,
3840 x 2019, UI scale 2.0, Video preset High): "there's a ton of textures now that aren't
transparent including even some hair" (a screenshot in the Dunhuang/Hotan desert: the trees' leaf
cards drawn as solid dark quads) and "the preview character in the inventory is much lower
resolution than the game. Can you make that the same resolution as the actual character please?"
Lane `alpha695`, client. Labels: READ (Godot 4.2.2-stable source), MEASURED (the render box, RX
7600), INFERRED, OURS.

### 1. The cut-outs: Forward+ uploads DXT1 without its alpha

**The cause (READ, Godot 4.2.2-stable).**
- A DXT1 block whose colour0 <= colour1 is in three-colour mode, and its index 3 is a transparent
  black texel (RGBA 0,0,0,0) -- the format's own rule.
- GL Compatibility uploads `Image.FORMAT_DXT1` as `_EXT_COMPRESSED_RGBA_S3TC_DXT1_EXT`
  (`drivers/gles3/storage/texture_storage.cpp` 418-426): the transparent texels stay transparent.
- The RenderingDevice renderers (Forward+, Mobile) upload it as `DATA_FORMAT_BC1_RGB_UNORM_BLOCK`
  with `swizzle_a = TEXTURE_SWIZZLE_ONE` (`servers/rendering/renderer_rd/storage_rd/
  texture_storage.cpp` 1721-1735): alpha is 1 everywhere, and BC1_RGB decodes index 3 as black. The
  client's alpha test (`ObjectLoader._mod_shader`'s discard below ALPHA_TEST_REF) then keeps every
  texel, so the card draws as its whole quad, black where it should be empty.
- Nothing in rounds 693/694's shader work touched this: the shaders sample the texture's alpha as
  before. It is the texture upload, and only under Forward+ -- which is why it appeared with the
  first Forward+ release. The other suspects (round 693's `ShaderColour`, Texture Filtering's
  MSAA, Texture Detail's mip bias, the native readers) are not involved: the card measurement
  below fails and passes with none of them in play.
- There is no way to keep it DXT1: 4.2.2 has no Image format for BC1 with alpha, and
  `texture_rd_create` cannot wrap a `BC1_RGBA` texture (`_texture_format_from_rd`, 2184-2194, has
  no entry for it; `texture_rd_initialize` fails on FORMAT_MAX).

**How many (MEASURED, `native/examples/dxt1_alpha_census.rs`, every mip level):** 4,024 of the
archives' 24,493 DXT1 textures mark a texel transparent -- Data.pk2 3,971 of 12,091 (183.8 MB;
2,468 of them lightmaps -- which no client code loads (review, L1) -- 388 monster, 252 building, 210
NPC, 183 item, 67 character textures, the hair among them), Media.pk2 44 of 11,640, Particles.pk2 9 of 9, Map.pk2 0 of 753. 23 have
their transparent texels only below mip 0 (seen only at a distance).

**The measurement (MEASURED, `client/tools/measure_alpha_cards.gd`).** Nine real cut-out textures
(the Hotan tree's leaf and branch cards, four hairs, a willow leaf, a ship's planking), each built
by DdjReader as the game builds it, drawn 1:1 with the client's alpha test over magenta; the cut
fraction read back from the frame against the engine's own CPU decode of the same payload:

| Texture | expected cut | Compatibility | Forward+ before (DXT1) | Forward+ after |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `w_cd_hotree_leaf01` | 0.7115 | 0.7115 | **0.0000** | 0.7115 |
| `w_cd_hotree_al01` | 0.5193 | 0.5193 | **0.0000** | 0.5193 |
| `w_cd_hotree_al02` | 0.8780 | 0.8780 | **0.0000** | 0.8780 |
| `chinaman_bogy_hair` | 0.0140 | 0.0140 | **0.0000** | 0.0140 |
| `chinawoman_scholar_hair` | 0.2140 | 0.2140 | **0.0000** | 0.2140 |
| `chinawoman_fighter_hair` | 0.2100 | 0.2100 | **0.0000** | 0.2100 |
| `europewoman_angel_hair` | 0.1666 | 0.1666 | **0.0000** | 0.1666 |
| `tre_willow03_leaf01` | 0.7984 | 0.7984 | **0.0000** | 0.7984 |
| `ruin_takl_wood_07` | 0.0513 | 0.0513 | **0.0000** | 0.0513 |

**The fix.** Under a RenderingDevice renderer, DdjReader decodes a DXT1 with at least one
transparent texel on the CPU with the engine's own decoder (squish), one mip level at a time
(`DdjReader.dxt1_to_rgba8`; see the review's M1 below), and hands Godot an `Image.FORMAT_RGBA8`,
whose upload keeps alpha. It is the RGBA8 format that keeps it, not the decompress: Godot's own RD
fallback for an unsupported BC1 (1725-1731) decompresses too but still sets `swizzle_a = ONE`
(1735) and would lose it the same way. Alpha then matches Compatibility texel for texel,
transparent texels (0,0,0,0) included; the colours are within a few levels of a GPU's DXT1 decode
(squish interpolates the middle colours in integer arithmetic; GPUs differ from it, and from each
other, by about 1-3/255). Every other DXT1 stays DXT1, and every DXT1 under Compatibility
(`ddj_reader_test.gd` checks both). The scan is native (`native/src/core/dxt.rs`,
`SrNativeParsers.ddj_dxt1_has_transparent`, called behind `has_method`, interface number still 5):
all 24,493 DXT1s of the four archives in 0.053 s (MEASURED); a GDScript loop is the fallback without
the method. `native_parity.gd` compares the two scans on every DXT1 of the real archives.

**A DXT3 re-encode was tried first and rejected (MEASURED).** It would cost a quarter of RGBA8's
memory (8 bits a texel against 32), but a four-colour palette cannot hold a three-colour block's
two colours, its midpoint and its transparent black at once. Fitted block by block over the
archives: alpha exact, but 1,256,345 of 1,278,659 midpoint blocks inexact, 0.42 % of opaque texels
off by more than 8/255 and up to 37/255, and the transparent texels lose their black -- which an
alpha-blended edge, a lightmap (2,468 of these textures) or an opaque material samples.

**The world (MEASURED, region 102/154, Hotan trees `w_cd_hotree01`, 1280x720, Middle):** each
Forward+ frame against the same frame under Compatibility, the fraction of pixels off by more than
32 levels (`frame_ab.py`):

| View | Forward+ before | Forward+ after |
|---|---|---|
| tree (close, behind the player) | 0.044 | 0.000 |
| far (the trees against the sky) | 0.040 | 0.002 |
| side | 0.044 | 0.001 |
| the player close up (body 1920) | 0.009 | 0.009 (its hair has no transparent texel; the rest is round 693's blending, unchanged) |

Sky-blue pixels in the upper 45 % of the far view: 0.4645 before, 0.5342 after, 0.5327 under
Compatibility. The run decoded 44 such textures to RGBA8 (QA ENTRY's `dxt1_alpha_rgba8`):
12.8 MB as RGBA8 against 1.6 MB as DXT1, so 11.2 MB more video memory there.

**At the user's preset (High: Texture Filtering On = MSAA 2x under Forward+, Texture Detail High,
`OPENSRO_QA_VIDEO=quality=2`) the result is the same:** pixels off by more than 32 against
Compatibility 0.044 / 0.040 / 0.044 before, 0.000 / 0.002 / 0.001 after; the far view's sky
0.4645 before, 0.5343 after. And the card measurement with the SubViewport at MSAA 2x
(`--msaa=2`): before 0.0000 for all nine, after all nine MATCH. So MSAA, the mip bias and the
preset play no part; the DXT1 upload is the whole cause.

Shots on the box (1280x720): `/var/tmp/alpha695/head-fplus-keep/` (before),
`head-fplus/` (after), `head-compat/` (Compatibility), `head-fplus-high-keep/` and
`head-fplus-high/` (High); the views are frames 16 (tree), 44 (far), 72 (the player) and 100
(side).

**Every alpha path** goes through this one reader: object and building cards (the MTRL mod
shader's alpha test), characters' hair and cloaks (the same materials), the appear/disappear fade
twins (they share the textures), the `.efp` particles (Particles.pk2's 9), the interface art
(Media.pk2's 44), and the water (Map.pk2: none). No path draws a DXT1 any other way
(`Image.FORMAT_DXT1` is created only in `ddj_reader.gd` and in `mapt_reader.gd`, the `.t` ground
tiles, which hold no transparent texel and are decompressed on the CPU anyway).

### 2. The paper doll: rendered at the UI's units, magnified by the UI scale

**The cause (READ, our code).** `PaperDoll.use_equipment_view` renders a fixed 176x318 -- the
pane's rect in UI units, READ in round 633 -- and HudPanels draws it in a 176x318 TextureRect. The
UI scale is the window's content scale (`ClientSettings.apply_ui_scale`: the canvas is the window
divided by the scale and stretched back up), so at the user's 2.0 the picture covers 352x636
screen pixels and each rendered pixel was drawn 2x2. Not a fractional-scale artefact: at 2.0 it is
exactly half resolution. The same held for the customize screen's model (its SubViewport took the
screen's size in UI units, 1920x1010 at 3840x2019 and 2.0). The player block's portrait was not
affected at 2.0 (below).

**The fix.** `ViewportPixels` (new, `client/scripts/ui/viewport_pixels.gd`), a child of the
TextureRect, keeps the SubViewport at the rect's size on screen in physical pixels -- the rect's
size through its canvas transform and the window's stretch -- and follows the rect's resizes, the
window's size and the UI scale (the window's `size_changed`, which `Window::_update_viewport_size`
emits for both). Applied to the paper doll, the customize preview and the portrait (retail's
128x128 buffer, READ, kept as the floor: the buffer is a square of max(128, the picture's longer
side)). The cameras keep their height (`KEEP_HEIGHT`) or the portrait's square, so the picture is
the same, with more pixels. The doll's pose log stays in the 176x318 picture's pixels
(`PaperDoll.pixel_scale`). Each size change logs one `ViewportPixels:` line with the filter the
picture is drawn with. Round 672's crisp text is untouched: it sets NEAREST on text nodes only,
and the doll's TextureRect inherits the viewport's default, LINEAR (MEASURED in the game's log
line below). At 1:1 the filter no longer magnifies anything; NEAREST is not wanted for a 3D picture.
(`CharacterPreview` has no user in the game and keeps its fixed size.)

**MEASURED (headless, `inventory_pages_test.gd`, the real HudPanels):**

| UI scale | picture on screen | doll renders (before) | doll renders (after) | texels per pixel before / after |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1.00 | 176x318 | 176x318 | 176x318 | 1.000 / 1.000 |
| 1.50 | 264x477 | 176x318 | 264x477 | 0.667 / 1.000 |
| 1.95 | 343x621 | 176x318 | 343x621 | 0.512 / 1.000 |
| 2.00 | 352x636 | 176x318 | 352x636 | 0.500 / 1.000 |

**MEASURED in the game (Forward+, 3840x2160, `OPENSRO_QA_UI_SCALE=2.0`, the inventory open at
the Jangan spawn, the China fighter in the starter set):** the log says `ViewportPixels: PaperDoll
(176, 318) -> (352, 636) for (176, 318) UI units x (2, 2) on screen (drawn with filter linear (the
viewport's default))`. In the frame, over a 200x520 box on the doll's body: mean |Laplacian| of luma
9.67 before (v0.1.480 with the same QA hook) against 23.39 after, 2.4x the detail. Side by side:
`/var/tmp/alpha695/doll_before_after.png` on the box (frames `base-doll/f00000038.png`,
`head-doll/f00000052.png`). The portrait's picture covers 96x96 screen pixels at 2.0 (MEASURED,
the `portrait dressed` line), under retail's 128x128 buffer, so it was never magnified and its
buffer stays 128: the follower only matters there at a scale above 2.67. Cost: the doll's buffer is 352x636
RGBA8, 0.9 MB (INFERRED from the size); the customize preview at 3840x2019 renders 4x the pixels
it did at 1920x1010 (its memory: L5 under OPEN; its frame time is not measured).

A QA run dresses the player before the HUD exists, and `_refresh_paper_doll` returns without
panels, so a QA run never had a doll; the panels' creation now builds it for a body already
dressed, as the player block already did for the portrait (round 635).

### Review

- **M1 (MEDIUM, MEASURED by the review): a non-square texture's smallest mip levels were blank or
  leftover memory.** The first version called `Image.decompress()` on the whole DXT1 chain. Godot
  4.2.2's squish loop (`modules/squish/image_decompress_squish.cpp`) halves width and height with
  no floor of 1, so once the short side reaches 0 it decodes nothing, and the remaining levels
  keep whatever the buffer held (`Vector::resize` does not zero it). The review's probe: 256x64
  levels 7-8 came out (0,0,0,0); 64x256 levels 7-8 held a leftover (0,200,0,77). 520 of the
  transparent DXT1s are non-square with mips. Fixed: `DdjReader.dxt1_to_rgba8` decodes each level
  as its own Image -- width and height floored at 1, the block-padded slice
  `ceil(w/4) x ceil(h/4) x 8` bytes that `Image._get_dst_image_size` lays out -- and joins the
  levels into one RGBA8 Image with mipmaps. `ddj_reader_test.gd` now checks every level's colour
  of a 256x64 and a 64x256 texture. Against this round's first commit (59ef1aa7):
  ```
  FAIL 256x64: every level opaque blue at texel 0, only blue or clear texels ["level 7 (2x1): texel 0 (0, 0, 0, 0), 0 texel(s) neither blue nor clear", "level 8 (1x1): texel 0 (0.0078, 0, 0, 0), 1 texel(s) neither blue nor clear"]
  FAIL 64x256: every level opaque blue at texel 0, only blue or clear texels ["level 7 (1x2): texel 0 (0, 0, 0, 0), 0 texel(s) neither blue nor clear", "level 8 (1x1): texel 0 (0.0078, 0, 0, 0), 1 texel(s) neither blue nor clear"]
  ```
  The nine real cards measured again after the change: all nine MATCH under Forward+, with and
  without MSAA 2x, and under Compatibility; the forced-DXT1 rows still 0.0000.
- **L1:** the memory notes counted lightmaps no client code loads; corrected above and in TODO
  (the 1,503 others, 976 MB as RGBA8 if all were loaded; items and avatars the target).
- **L2:** "exactly what the RD path does where BC1 is unsupported" was wrong -- that fallback still
  swizzles alpha to ONE (1735); the RGBA8 format is what keeps it. Corrected in `ddj_reader.gd`,
  `dxt.rs`, DDJ_FORMAT.md and above.
- **L3:** RGB is no longer claimed texel for texel: alpha is equal, colours within a few levels.
- **L6:** the interface number stays 5. `ddj_dxt1_has_transparent` is an added method, called only
  where `has_method` finds it, so a library left from before this round (an update whose DLL swap
  rolled back) keeps every other native reader and only this scan falls back to GDScript. The bump
  was not needed.
- L4 and L5 are recorded under OPEN.
- After the fixes: `remote_godot.sh check` ALL LOAD; `tests` 212 suites, 0 failing; `cargo test
  --release --locked` 45 passed; `native_parity.gd` PARITY PASS (24,493 DXT1 scans, 4,024 with a
  transparent texel, 208 s); `perf_gate.sh --sites jangan --frames 12000`:
  ```
  jangan  frame ms   base 1.65  head 1.64  (-0.0)  SAME
  jangan  entry ms   base 9263.50  head 9365  (+101.5)  SAME
  jangan  freeze ms  base 3257.50  head 3320  (+62.5)  SAME
  jangan  hitches    base 4.50  head 4  (-0.5)  SAME
  ```

### OPEN

- The RGBA8 textures cost 8x their DXT1 (11.2 MB more in the Hotan desert at radius 1, MEASURED).
  The 2,468 lightmaps are never loaded (no client code reads `Prim\LightMap`; the ground's are
  Map.pk2's `.t`), so the cost is the other 1,503: 122 MB as DXT1, 976 MB as RGBA8 if every one
  were loaded at once (monsters 327, items 209, NPCs 132, world 109, characters 35 MB -- the
  review's census). The largest are items and avatars: the four 2048x2048 `avatar_w_*arctic*`
  textures have no mips and are 16 MB each as RGBA8. If memory matters, the target is those --
  for example decoding only textures an alpha-tested or blended material uses, which needs the
  material's alpha use to reach the loader.
- L4 (the review): at a fractional UI scale the doll's picture lands at a fractional screen
  position, so LINEAR filtering softens it by up to about half a texel; 1:1 is exact only at
  whole-number scales. The user is at 2.0.
- L5 (the review): the customize preview's video memory at 4K (about 120-150 MB with its depth
  buffer) is an ESTIMATE from its size, not a measurement.

## Six-hundred-and-ninety-third round: the game draws with Forward+ (Vulkan) by default, looking as it did under Compatibility -- the same colours, ground, sky, portrait and select screen -- with Compatibility one launcher away for a PC without Vulkan

The user (2026-10-02): "Let's make forward+ the default build. Can you switch to it and test?" Earlier
the same day they asked whether Forward+ could return "without the ground textures issues we had
before", and about shipping a Compatibility build beside it. Labels: READ (Godot 4.2.2-stable
source, sro_client.exe's dump), MEASURED (the render box, RX 7600, real archives), INFERRED, OURS.

### 1. Vulkan on the render box (docs/RENDER_BOX.md, "Vulkan (Forward+)")

- **MEASURED:** RADV was already installed; `vulkaninfo` (vulkan-tools, installed here) lists
  `AMD Radeon RX 7600 (RADV NAVI33)`.
- **Plain Xvfb cannot take a Vulkan frame** (no DRI3). Godot then silently picks `Vulkan Device #1:
  llvmpipe`, the CPU. `MESA_VK_WSI_DEBUG=sw` reaches the GPU, but every frame is copied back
  through the CPU: an empty scene costs 17.5 ms a frame at 1280x720 and 4.7 at 640x360.
- **New `client/tools/xwl_run.sh`:** a private headless weston (GL renderer on the GPU) with
  Xwayland, which has DRI3. The same empty scene draws in 0.24 ms.
- **Installed:** weston and xwayland, `--no-install-recommends`, 49 packages. The list and the
  selections from before are saved on the box; the revert is in RENDER_BOX.md.
- **Nothing else changed:** no group, X configuration, service, or host change.
- **Headless runs** use the dummy rasterizer under either renderer (READ, main.cpp 1164-1167), so
  the suites, `--import` and CI's exports are unaffected.
- **Tooling:**
  - `qa_shot.sh`: `RENDERER=`; it repeats Godot's banner and warns on llvmpipe. `QA_SHOT_REAP=0`
    skips the box-wide kill for lane use. It now passes `-chargen-csv`; without it, a `--server`
    run has had no character to start since round 682 (S1027 "no creatable catalogue").
  - `perf_gate.sh`: per-side renderers from each copy's project.godot, `--renderer` and
    `--ab-renderer`. A run on the wrong renderer or on llvmpipe fails the gate. Separately,
    `$([ ... ] && echo _fp)` in an assignment had ended the gate silently under `set -e` (fixed).
  - New measuring tools: `frame_ab.py`, `measure_blend_space.gd`, `measure_lit_space.gd`,
    `measure_appear_fade.gd --instance`, `renderer_choice_cli.gd`.

### 2. The switch

- **`project.godot`:** `rendering_method="forward_plus"`. The `.mobile` key stays
  `gl_compatibility`; no mobile build is exported. `.web` is the engine's default,
  `gl_compatibility` (READ, main.cpp 1962).
- **No automatic fallback without Vulkan (READ):** Godot 4.2.2 does not fall back to OpenGL by
  itself. `DisplayServerWindows::create_func` shows "Unable to initialize Vulkan video driver",
  naming `--rendering-driver opengl3`, and Main fails. `fallback_to_opengl3` arrived in 4.3. With
  no `--rendering-method`, `--rendering-driver opengl3` alone implies gl_compatibility (main.cpp
  1911-1916).
- **`RendererChoice` (new, OURS):** the per-install choice lives in `override.cfg` beside the
  executable. An exported game reads that file over project.godot (READ, project_settings.cpp
  590-591). The file is written:
  - from `setting/config.yaml`'s new `display.renderer: forward_plus|compatibility`, which wins at
    every start;
  - by a start with `--rendering-driver opengl3` when no choice is recorded yet, so plain starts
    and the updater's argument-less relaunch stay on Compatibility. The release zips now carry
    `opensro-compatibility.bat` / `.sh` for that first start. **Corrected by the review below:**
    that cut looked for the flag in `OS.get_cmdline_args()`, which never holds it, and never wrote
    the file. It now decides from the renderer running.
  - Boot prints `RENDERER: running=... adapter=... override=... chosen=...`.
  - **MEASURED end to end:** a project with the file RendererChoice wrote, and no renderer flag,
    starts `OpenGL API ... - Compatibility`. Choosing forward_plus deletes the file, and the next
    start is `Vulkan API ... - Forward+`.
- **For the Options lane:** `RendererChoice.chosen()` / `choose()` and `WorldPostEffects.apply(env,
  ssao, glow)`. World3D's only environment change is one call at the top of `_ready`. The
  `ssao_enabled` / `glow_enabled` lines left World3D.tscn, and `fog_sky_affect = 0` was set beside
  the fog (section 4).
- **SSAO and glow are off.** Both were OURS guesses (2026-08-26) and invisible from round 581 to
  692, because Compatibility has neither.
  - READ: retail's option page (FUN_005fef70) has a "Bloom effect" switch (UIIT_STT_BLOOM_EFFECT),
    whose default and look are not read.
  - MEASURED: no SSAO or ambient-occlusion string in the exe.

### 3. What broke under Forward+, and the fix (READ, then MEASURED)

**The colour rule.** Compatibility samples every texture and colour parameter as stored, ignoring
`source_color`. It decodes the shader's ALBEDO and EMISSION from sRGB, unshaded included
(gles3/shaders/scene.glsl 1368-1370), and encodes after tone mapping (1590-1593). Forward+ differs:
- It decodes `source_color` textures as it samples them (storage_rd/material_storage.cpp 912).
- It turns EVERY vec3/vec4 parameter set from a Color into linear, whatever its hint (449 / 1375,
  variant_converters.h 211). MEASURED: Color(90,120,50) read back (26,48,8) once decoded again.
- It takes ALBEDO as linear.

So the project's gamma-space arithmetic drew too bright, or mixed. MEASURED before the fix, select
screen at 14:00, Bram's body / his customize preview: Compatibility 89 / 94, the same as round 688.
Forward+ drew **162 / 149**; at 23:00, 138 / 121 against 57 / 59.

**`ShaderColour` (new):** raw samples, Color parameters read through `srr_color(v, OUTPUT_IS_SRGB)`,
and ALBEDO and EMISSION decoded where `OUTPUT_IS_SRGB` is false. It covers:
- the mod shader (the D3DTOP emulation);
- the portrait, and the select screen's tone-mapping undo through it;
- the particles, the cloud layer, the water reflection and the mirror terrain;
- every StandardMaterial3D that multiplies by a vertex colour (terrain, water, the hit and level-up
  effects), which now sets `vertex_color_is_srgb`, decoded only where the output is linear (READ,
  material.cpp 973-976).

MEASURED along the way: `OUTPUT_IS_SRGB` is a stage built-in that a user function cannot read
("Unknown identifier in expression"), so the caller passes it. A decode-function parameter named `c`
collided with a uniform `c`. Setting a Shader's code twice compiled the half-made first version.

**The sky.** Compatibility mixes ProceduralSkyMaterial's gradient in display values and never fogs
the sky (READ, gles3 sky.glsl). Forward+ mixes in linear and fogs the sky by `fog_sky_affect`.
`GammaSkyMaterial` (new) is the material's own code with Compatibility's arithmetic, and
`fog_sky_affect = 0`.

**MEASURED after:**

| Check | Compatibility | Forward+ before | Forward+ after |
|---|---|---|---|
| Select, 14:00: Bram / Aria body (preview) | 89.4 (94.0) / 138.6 (141.1) | 162.3 (149.1) / 196.9 (185.6) | **89.0 (93.4) / 137.3 (139.5)** |
| Select, 23:00: Bram / Aria | 56.9 (59.4) / 89.7 (91.4) | 138.2 (121.1) / 169.5 (151.8) | **57.9 (59.9) / 89.2 (90.5)** |
| Portrait calibration (portrait_shot.gd) | 160 | -- | **160** (d8 0.000) |
| Portrait raw128, man / woman | -- | -- | dluma -2.1 / -2.7, d32 2.2 % / 2.9 % |
| Terrain flat base, `unfix_inverted` p50 | 98 | 144 | **95** |
| Jangan sky band, no fog: mean R, d32 | 69.5 | 87.8, 20.4 % | **69.2, 0.3 %** |
| Opaque quad (measure_blend_space) | exact | -- | **exact** |

**Compatibility is unchanged.** Every world shot of the Compatibility runs before and after all of
this (13 viewpoints, 4 places) differs in at most 0.6 % of pixels by more than 8 (animated water
and clouds); the rest are pixel-identical.

### 4. The A/B (frame_ab.py; Compatibility = a, Forward+ = b, the final build)

**Whole frame:**

| View | d8 | d32 | dluma | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Jangan spawn | 0.750 | 0.036 | -11.3 | lit objects; see "shadows" below |
| Jangan grass (unshaded terrain) | 0.058 | 0.005 | -3.4 | terrain, overlay blending |
| Jangan overview | 0.411 | 0.008 | -10.5 | lit objects |
| Jangan sky (fog on) | 0.731 | 0.296 | -1.8 | the cloud layer blended linearly (top band +16) |
| Jangan sky (no fog) | 0.339 | 0.013 | -7.8 | the sky band matches (-0.8); the rest is lit objects |
| Ferry dock / river / up (water, reeds) | 0.146 / 0.280 / 0.171 | 0.002 / 0.008 / 0.012 | -0.4 / -0.9 / -2.4 | water within 1-3 |
| Dunhuang reeds / reeds2 (foliage) | 0.407 / 0.535 | 0.068 / 0.092 | -7.1 / -6.4 | foliage, lit; shadows |
| Login title at 120 / 300 / 600 / 899 | 0.53-0.59 | 0.12-0.24 | -7.1 / -7.7 / -4.6 / -4.3 | the title's lit world; clouds |
| Create, China / Europe | 0.41 / 0.28 | 0.09 / 0.01 | -4.5 / -2.6 | |
| Select at 14:00 / 23:00 | 0.25 / 0.19 | 0.012 / 0.005 | -2.3 / -1.0 | |

**Shadows: the darker lit objects are Compatibility over-brightening.**
- MEASURED (measure_lit_space.gd, a lit quad with nothing occluding it): the two renderers agree
  within 1 level on ambient, sun, both, and Filmic.
- With the sun casting shadows (World3D.tscn's `shadow_enabled`) and ambient 0.7, Compatibility
  reads **(225,176,127)** against **(159,128,95)** without shadows. Forward+ reads (158,128,95)
  either way.
- READ: GLES3 draws a shadowed directional light in an additive pass, tone-mapped and encoded on
  its own, then added in display values (scene.glsl 1805-1808). So with shadows on it adds enc(a) +
  enc(b) rather than enc(a + b).
- In the world (new `OPENSRO_QA_NOSHADOW`): Jangan spawn's lower band is GL 70.7 with shadows and
  58.7 without, against Forward+ 56.9 either way. With shadows off the gap is -3.6 instead of
  -14.6.
- So the look Compatibility showed since round 581 includes that over-brightening. Forward+ draws
  the single-pass sum. Neither is retail's lighting (the world's objects use Godot's tuned light,
  OURS; TODO). Not changed: whether to retune the sun's 0.3 is the user's call.

**Blending space (MEASURED, measure_blend_space.gd).** Forward+ blends in a linear buffer:
`|read - linear|` is 0-1 on every case. Compatibility blends in display values, as D3D9 does:
`|read - gamma|` is 0-3. They differ by:
- 11 / 13 / 8 levels at a 25 / 50 / 75 % sand-over-grass feather (the terrain overlays);
- 12 for water at 50 % over dark;
- 21 for water's 200/255 over sand;
- 9 for an additive glow.

This cannot be fixed per material without the colour underneath; it stays OPEN, a user decision.

**The fades.** measure_appear_fade.gd, mangnyang, the share of the model on screen at t = 0.5 /
1.0 / 1.5 s of the 2 s fade-in:

### Review (round 693's review: two HIGHs, two MEDIUMs, three LOWs)

**HIGH 1: the Compatibility launcher's choice was never saved.**
- Godot 4.2.2's `Main::setup` consumes `--rendering-driver` / `--rendering-method` (main.cpp
  1020-1035), so `OS.get_cmdline_args()` never holds them. The reviewer MEASURED `ASKS=false`,
  nothing recorded.
- **Fixed:** `RendererChoice.boot_decision(config_word, running, current)` records Compatibility
  when the start is RUNNING it, nothing is recorded, and the project default is Forward+. Headless
  ("none (headless)") writes nothing.
- When the folder cannot be written (Program Files), the RENDERER line now says so in plain words,
  and the README says to install in a folder you own.
- **Windowed box test** (new `client/tools/renderer_fallback_box_test.sh`: real starts of the game's
  own main scene on xwl_run.sh, `OPENSRO_OVERRIDE_CFG` set). This tree: ALL PASS.
- **NEGATIVE** (c18419dc's client with the same library):
  - `FAIL 1. ... and records it for the next start ()`
  - `FAIL 3. ... the native probe says why ()`
  - `FAIL 3. ... and records Compatibility`

**HIGH 2: the auto-update moved every player to Vulkan with no fall back.**
- Godot 4.2.2 has none of its own. The native library now supplies one (native/src/vk_fallback.rs;
  native/README.md, "The Vulkan -> OpenGL fall back").
- It is loaded at Core for the game, so it runs in `register_core_extensions` (main.cpp 1647),
  before the renderer is read (1966). No Godot API is usable there on 4.2: ProjectSettings and
  Engine register in setup2. So rather than set the renderer, it:
  - asks the system's Vulkan loader (opened at run time) for an instance with the surface
    extensions and a physical device;
  - on failure, starts the game again with `--rendering-driver opengl3` (before any `--`) and ends
    this start (exec on Linux; spawn + TerminateProcess on Windows).
  - `OPENSRO_VK_PROBE` carries the result: Boot logs it, and RendererChoice records the
    Compatibility start.
- **MEASURED on the box** (the editor binary running the project windowed, plain start, no
  renderer flag):

| Start | Renderer | Probe |
|---|---|---|
| Vulkan present | Forward+ (RADV) | `ok 2 device(s) in 28.0 ms` |
| `VK_ICD_FILENAMES=/dev/null` (no driver) | **Compatibility, no alert** | `fallback to OpenGL: vkCreateInstance failed (-9) (0.3 ms)` |
| the same, without the library | none: "Could not initialize Vulkan", then the alert blocks until killed | -- |

- **A trap found on the way, MEASURED:** at Core the library made a first `--headless --import
  --quit` (a fresh `.godot/`) hang. It was still running after 180 s, against 15 s with the library
  at Scene. CI imports exactly that way. `min_level` is now Core only when the command line has no
  `--editor` / `-e` / `--import` / `--project-manager` / `--export*`, and the fresh import finishes
  in 15 s.
- **Checks:** `cargo test` 43 passed (5 new for the fall back's rules and arguments).
  `native_parity.gd`: PARITY PASS. `check_native_library.sh` on the new DLL: stands alone (kernel32
  imports only).
- No binding changed, so `core::API` stays 5.
- **NOT RUN:** the Windows restart (spawn + TerminateProcess). It is compiled, but no Windows
  machine has run it. The startup cost there is not measured either; on the box it is 28 ms.
- **The shipped README** (copied into both zips) said "OpenGL 3.3". It now describes Forward+, the
  automatic fall back, the launcher, `display.renderer`, `override.cfg`, a non-writable folder, and
  what happens without the library.

**MEDIUM 3: the clouds.**
- Under Forward+ the cloud layer blended into the sky in linear space.
- **Fixed:** the sky behind it is analytic, so `cloud_dome.gdshader` (fed by
  `GammaSkyMaterial.feed_clouds`: the sky's colours, the sun it draws, the tone mapper) computes
  Compatibility's own result: both colours tone-mapped and encoded, mixed in display values, and
  the inverse of that, drawn opaque. Only under Forward+; Compatibility blends as before.
- **MEASURED** (Jangan sky shot, fog on, top band, Forward+ minus GL): **+16.4 luma (77 % of pixels
  off by more than 32) -> -0.55 (0.6 %)**. The whole frame went from +5.6 to -1.1.

**MEDIUM 4: `display.renderer` cannot rescue a machine without Vulkan.** True on its own (Boot never
runs there). It is now said in ClientConfig's and RendererChoice's headers and in the README, and HIGH 2's
fall back makes it moot whenever the library is there.

**LOW 5: Program Files.** See HIGH 1: the log line and the README.

**LOW 6: xwl_run.sh** now clears its own user's `/var/tmp/xwl-run.*` older than 120 minutes before
it starts. A SIGKILLed run can leave one behind.

**LOW 7: the paper doll** (the equipment window, signed in, `--panels equipment`, the window at
(446,156) 388x408, frame 359, MEASURED): the window's pixels differ by more than 8 in 0.1 % between

## Six-hundred-and-ninety-second round: a new character starts with its race's own masteries, basic skills and first quests, as the shard's `_AddNewChar` gives them -- and the shard's own list of creatable ids is exactly the 104 the rule picks

The user approved the shard DB export (2026-10-02, "yes ct 104"); the four `_RefCharGen` /
`_RefCharDefault_*` tables and the text of six lobby procedures were exported to
`/opt/sro-files/db/csv/charsel/` on the render box (EXTERNAL, a private shard's; nothing entered the
repo). This round reads them and closes charselect.md's EXTERNAL OPENs (lane `defaults692`,
server only). The user, mid-round: "euros probably have their own quests too, make sure you consider
that."

### 1. The catalogue (MEASURED)

`_RefCharGen` holds 104 rows, all Service 1. Their RefObjIDs against the rule's:
- the server's (`chargen.csv` from `cmd/export-refdata -mode chargen` on the box's archive,
  `/var/tmp/lobby682/chargen.csv`): **identical**, 104 = 104, none missing, none extra
  (`TestRefCharGenAgreesWithTheRule` with `OPENSRO_TEST_CHARGEN_CSV` / `OPENSRO_TEST_REFCHARGEN_CSV`
  set: `rule 104 ids, _RefCharGen 104 ids, missing 0, extra 0`);
- the client's (`CharCatalog.from_archive` on the box's Media.pk2, a throwaway script run through
  `remote_godot.sh script`, not committed): **identical**, `CATIDS 104 ...`, `diff` empty.

So the rule is the shard's list, id for id. The server now also compares them at boot when
`_RefCharGen.csv` sits in `-chardefaults-dir` (`the creatable catalogue agrees with the shard's
_RefCharGen ids=104`).

### 2. What the procedures do (READ, this package's; charselect.md sections 2 and 5)

- **`_AddNewChar`** (20 parameters, the order section 5 READ from the ShardManager's pushes): refuses
  4 characters (-2), scale > 68 (-3), a taken name (-4); inserts `_Char` with **Strength 20,
  Intellect 20, CurLevel 1, HP 200, MP 200, InventorySize 109**, RemainGold 2,000,000, RemainSkillPoint
  5,000,000, region 25000 (97/168) at (993, 0, 130), AppointedTeleport 2094 (`STORE_CH_GATE`) -- the
  position and gate parameters are ignored, every race starts in Jangan on this shard; equips the
  items (the ammunition into slot 7 **with 250**); then, by `_GetObjCountry(RefObjID)`:
  `_CharSkillMastery` every `_RefCharDefault_SkillMastery` row of that Race or 3 **at Level 0**,
  `_CharSkill` every `_RefCharDefault_Skill` row of that Race or 3 (Enable 1), `_CharQuest` every
  `_RefCharDefault_Quest` CodeName of that Race or 3 **with RequiredLevel 1 and Service 1** (Status
  1) -- of the codes that have a `_RefQuest` row (its join; `_RefQuest` was not exported, so that every
  code passes it is INFERRED). It is **edited by the shard's operator**: an `_A_RARE` starting-kit swap ("Initial Equip Edit
  by LemoniscooL"), nine `_RoyalAddItems` grants, `ANTHEIA` calls, silk rows, and a commented-out
  level-110 variant of the INSERT.
- **`_DeleteCharTemporal`**: stamps `_DeletedChar` with GetDate() and sets Deleted 1 (refusing id 0
  and an already-deleted character); no guild or time check. **`_DeleteCharPermanently`**: refuses
  before **6 days 23 hours** ("roughly 7 days ... an hour's error is allowed"). So the delay is 7 days,
  the ShardManager's timer, which OpenSRO's `DeleteDelay` (the user's 7 days) already is.
- **`_ReviveChar`**: needs the `_DeletedChar` row and Deleted 1; removes the row, Deleted 0. No time
  check. OpenSRO's restore is the same. `_RecoverDeletedChar` is disabled in this package.
- **`_IsExistingCharName`**: `=` against `_CharNameList` (pending characters' names included) and
  `_CharNickNameList`. Case follows the DB collation, not exported (INFERRED case-insensitive);
  OpenSRO compares without case, as before (OURS until settled).

### 3. What changed

- **Defaults at create** (`session/lobbyhandler.go` `giveDefaults`): after the items, the race's
  masteries at level 0 (`skill.SeedMasteries`, new in `skill/defaults.go`), its skills

## Six-hundred-and-ninety-first round: Europe characters see, learn and cast their own masteries -- Warrior, Rogue, Wizard, Warlock, Bard and Cleric, laid out as retail's window lays them -- and neither race can learn or raise the other's

The user, 2026-10-02: "Euro needs added to the actually game with full skin support, animations, and
skills." This lane (euroskill691) is the skills; skin and animation are world689's.

### 1. What retail does (READ unless marked)

- **Which masteries a character has is the server's list, and the list is the race's.** The shard's
  `_AddNewChar` (`/opt/sro-files/db/csv/charsel/proc__AddNewChar.sql`, the retail DB export on the
  render box) seeds `_CharSkillMastery` with `SELECT MasteryID FROM _RefCharDefault_SkillMastery
  WHERE Race = @country or Race = 3`; the table's 13 rows are Race 0: 257 258 259 273 274 275 276,
  Race 1: 513 514 515 516 517 518 (no Race-3 row). `_RefCharDefault_Skill` gives Race 3 skill 1
  (the punch), Race 0 the three CH base attacks, Race 1 the nine EU base attacks (8419 8420 8421
  9354 9355 9944 10625 11162 11526) -- OpenSRO already picks the base attack by weapon
  (`combat.BaseAttackSkillFor`), so those need nothing.
- **The game server refuses another race's mastery by the list, not by a race test.**
  `FUN_0059d6f0` looks the id up in the character's mastery map (+0x234) and answers 0 for one it
  does not hold (or holds in status 3). `Mastery_LevelUp` (0x0059c4e0) refuses that with 0x3801
  before anything else; the learn check `FUN_0059e450` (called by `Skill_HandleLearn` 0x0059bfe0)
  with 0x3401 for each of the skill's two masteries (+0xa0/+0xa4), then 0x3402 for a level below
  +0xa8/+0xa9, 0x3403/0x3404 Str/Int (+0xaa/+0xac), **0x3405 when ReqLearn_Race (+0xc4) is neither 3
  nor the character's Country (`*(ref+0x18)+0x88`)**, 0x340c/0x3406/0x3407 the chain and the
  prerequisites, 0x340a the skill points (`pc+0x80 < +0xc0`, ReqLearn_SP) -- and 0x3409 up front for
  a row whose ReqLearn_SP is 0.
- **The cap**: the server's Country rule (round 483) is unchanged; the CLIENT shows the same:
  CIFSkill `FUN_006aa3e0` reads the player's ref race byte (+0x9c) and for 1 does
  `fild [player+0x868] ; fadd st,st` -- twice the level -- keeping it below 0xf0 (240), else 240
  (0x6aa474..0x6aa4a8); for 0 it uses 0x14a = 330 (0x6aa4ba..0x6aa4c3); then `"%d/%d"`.
- **The window**: the same function copies the server's mastery map and files each mastery under a
  tab manager keyed by the mastery record's +0x5c byte, adding a 0x44 x 0x1c mastery tab per
  mastery (`FUN_006a0400`). +0x5c is skillmasterydata's TabID: the record keeps GroupNum at +0x20
  (`GlobalDataManager::FUN_00945ee0` sizes the board's group vector from it) and the icon strings
  at +0x64/+0x80 (the board loads them), and with MSVC's 0x1c-byte strings between, column 5 lands
  at +0x40 and column 6 at +0x5c (INFERRED from that layout, not from a loader read). The table
  (READ) gives Europe three tabs: `UIIT_CTL_EU_SKILLWND_PHYSICAL` (Melee) 513 Warrior, 515 Rogue;
  `_MASICAL` (Caster) 514 Wizard, 516 Warlock; `_ASSIST` (Buff) 517 Bard, 518 Cleric. Within a tab
  the map's order, ascending id. GroupNum (READ) is the board's row count: 8, 8, 6, 9, 7, 11 -- and
  skillgroup.txt has exactly that many rows per Europe mastery (MEASURED).
- **Names**: China's mastery names are in textuisystem.txt, Europe's (`UIIT_STT_WARRIOR`...) only in
  textdata_equip&skill.txt (MEASURED).
- **Skill rows (MEASURED, the box's Media.pk2)**: 3,242 Service-1 rows have a Europe mastery, every
  one ReqLearn_Race 1; 2,942 China rows are 0 and the three CH `_BASE_01` rows 3. They spread over
  eleven skilldata files; 15000, 10000, 35000, 9000, 12000 and 22000 cover every id. Board rows
  (UI_SkillColumn < 250) per mastery: Warrior 47 base skills, Rogue 48, Wizard 40, Warlock 45,
  Bard 43, Cleric 47 (270 skill groups; 284 distinct Basic_Code stems, a few groups holding
  more than one).
- **SP**: a level's learn cost is skilldata col 46 for both races; the mastery raise cost is
  leveldata col 2 for both (Mastery_LevelUp has no Country branch in the cost loop).
- **Weapons (MEASURED, ReqCast_Weapon1/2 or the `reqi` list of each mastery's level-1 rows)**:
  Warrior 7/8/9 (sword, two-handed sword, axe), Rogue 12/13 (crossbow, dagger), Wizard 11, Warlock
  10, Bard 14, Cleric 15. skillmasterydata's own weapon columns differ for Rogue (11, 12) and Cleric
  (10) and are not a cast rule anywhere this round reads.
- **Cast clips**: `Prim\Ani\Char\Europe\man` holds 122 clips and `...\woman` 119 (228 of the 241 named
  `skill_eu_*`), but only 33 of the 284 Europe board Basic_Code stems have a clip named after them. Retail picks the body motion through skilleffect.txt's `skillaniset2` row (e.g.
  SKILL_EU_WARRIOR_ONEHANDA_STRIKE_A: AniGroup ONEHAND_SWORD, SHOT ANI_SKILL_4) in the body's .bsr --
  the per-body lookup of the world lane.

### 2. What changed

Server -- `internal/skill/race.go` (`DefaultMasteries`, `HoldsMastery`, `LearnRaceAllows`, the
mastery ids); `session/skill.go`: LearnSkillHandler refuses a skill of a mastery the race does not
hold ("not your race's mastery", 0x3401) and a ReqLearn_Race that is neither 3 nor the Country ("not
your race's skill", 0x3405), in FUN_0059e450's order; RaiseMasteryHandler refuses an unheld mastery
first (0x3801) and sums only held masteries into the total; SkillStateHandler sends every held
mastery, level 0 included, and nothing of the other race. Not modelled, disclosed: 0x3409 (a
ReqLearn_SP of 0 cannot be learned -- the own-design catalog and test rows are learned free), the
Str/Int clauses, the second mastery slot (refdata carries Mastery1 only).

Client -- `MasteryReader.parse_all/for_race/race_of_masteries` and `RACE_MASTERIES`; HudPanels
takes the race from the server's mastery list (`set_skill_state`; `set_skill_race`; QA
`OPENSRO_QA_SKILL_STATE=race=1`), reads that race's skill files (`SkillDataReader.tables_for_race`;
the other race's only on a lookup miss), shows the total against `mastery_total_cap(race, level)`,
falls back to Melee/Caster/Buff (OURS words, the archive's own English) for an unresolved Europe tab,
resolves Europe mastery names through the skill-name table, and adds the cast weapon to a skill's
tooltip ("Weapon: Light Staff"; OURS labels for READ codes; a `reqi` list's requirement is not
shown -- OPEN). `SkillDataReader` reads SKILL_EU_ rows and europe\ groups, `cast_clip_path`
puts a Europe body's clip under `Europe\<sex>`, World3D's two clip paths call it (an adapter: see
§6). SkillAudio/SkillEffects read both races' files (`all_tables`). QA: `OPENSRO_QA_KIT=body,chest,
legs,feet,weapon` creates the sign-in character with those ids (the gender kit has only China's).

### Review (round 691's review: no regression for China characters; one HIGH, predating 691 and live on opensro-01, and three LOW -- fixed in a follow-up commit)

The review tested pre-692 and 692-shaped characters, crafted mastery ids and a trial merge onto dev
d6205fc (green). origin/dev d6205fc is merged in (WORLD_ISSUES by `wi_resolve.py`).

- **HIGH: any character could learn a monster's skill for free, and cast it.** The review counted
  26,699 rows with no mastery, ReqLearn_Race 3 and ReqLearn_SP 0 (this lane's census of its
  re-export: 26,646 MSKILL_/CSKILL_/PSKILL_/TSKILL_/HSKILL_/GSKILL_ rows with no mastery and no learn
  cost, plus 47 SKILL_ event/mall rows), so the held-mastery check was skipped, the race clause passed,
  there was no prerequisite and nothing to pay; 14,621 deal damage (the review's count) with no weapon requirement, among
  them id 31825 (MSKILL_EVE_STRONG_CH_STRONG_MANGNYANG_ATTACK02, 300 %, a 99,999 maximum). The cast
  path checked only that the skill was known. Fixed three ways:
  - **Learn**: FUN_0059e450's outermost test (READ) -- its whole body sits inside
    `if (... && *(int *)(skill + 0xc0) != 0)` and falls through to `return 0x3409` -- is now the
    learn handler's first real-skill check ("this skill cannot be learned"). It also refuses the 205
    class-board chain links with no cost (SKILL_CH_SWORD_KNOCKDOWN_E2_01 ...), as retail does, and
    the skill window no longer offers their "+". Round 692's default skills are written by
    `giveDefaults` straight into the store (`Skills.Learn`), not through the handler, so the base
    attacks a new character starts with are unaffected (READ in lobbyhandler.go).
  - **Cast**: `playerHoldRefusal` (session/playerskill.go) applies the learn check's rules to a
    held skill -- the race clause, the held mastery, and for a mastery-less row its learn cost, with
    the thirteen base attacks (ids 1, 2, 40, 70, 8419, 8420, 8421, 9354, 9355, 9944, 10625, 11162,
    11526; `combat.BaseAttackSkillFor`) exempt. A refused cast answers "you cannot use this skill"
    and costs nothing. A class chain link the old gate let through is still castable (it is its
    race's own class skill, and the learn gate now refuses it).
  - **Purge**: the refused skill is dropped from the store (`skill.Forgetter`, both stores),
    logged `dropped a learned skill no player may hold` with the character, skill and reason; the
    skill-state request the client sends on entering the world does the same for every held skill
    (`SkillStateHandlerWithRefs`, wired in cmd/server). The check query for opensro-01 is in
    deploy/README.md, ROUND 691'S REVIEW.
- **LOW: another race's skills learned before 691 stayed castable.** The cast now re-checks the race
  clause and the held mastery (the same `playerHoldRefusal`) and drops a refused skill, logged.
- **LOW: a stale comment in skill/race.go** said OpenSRO stores only raised masteries. It now says
  the held list is the Country's, that round 692 seeds the race's masteries as level-0 rows from the
  same table, and that the two agree; the deploy note says the same.
- **LOW: a lookup miss parsed the other race's ~10 MB of skilldata on the main thread mid-game**
  (`skill_reach` / `skill_icon_path` / `skill_level_ids`). A miss now answers "unknown" from the
  tables already read, and HudPanels takes the race from the enter-world result's body (its
  gender) when it is built, so the hotbar restore and the first cast read the player's own race's
  tables at world entry; the skill state confirms the race as before.
- Tests: `TestLearnRefusesRowsWithNoLearnCost` (the 31825 shape and a chain link, 0x3409, nothing
  spent or learned), `TestPlayerHoldRefusal` (monster rows, all thirteen base-attack shapes, both
  races' class rows), `TestCastOfAnUnholdableSkillIsRefusedAndDropped` (a China character holding

## Six-hundred-and-ninetieth round: a Hotan return stands on the plaza, the Alexandria North teleporter is clickable, and a town gate is clicked where retail clicks it -- its own box around the stone, not the whole building

The user (2026-10-02): "when I set Hotan as my default spawn and die I get resurrected back in hotan
but im clipped half way through the ground. This didn't seem to happen at other towns. Also the
Alexandria north teleporter has been broken since you added teleporters but I'm just telling you now.
When I had jangan as my spawn and I died it seemed like the teleport hit zone was off to the right and
not on the actual stone or around so I couldn't easily click it."

Labels: READ (the decompiles and asm on the render box), MEASURED, INFERRED, OURS, OPEN. The full
reading is in `docs/protocol/teleport_network.md`, "The gate's pick box and the arrival's height
(round 690)".

The live runs used the render box, lane `tele690`, with real X input through the Login route:
- the server was dev's, with opensro-01's flags: `-full-map` (so `-single-frame`), `-monster-ai
  -monster-strike-push -monster-spawn-push -monster-battle -monster-aggro -player-dead-state
  -persist-position`, `-regions-csv` and `-chargen-csv`;
- the box's exports were loaded: teleport, npcpos, monsters, the nest DB, regions and chargen.

The harness is `/var/tmp/tele690/inter.sh`, `x.sh`, `gate.sh`, `hop.sh` and `relog.sh`. The runs were:
- **i2**: dev's client with only the probe hook added (no behaviour change), which reproduced the
  bugs.
- **i4**: this tree's client: all seven gates clicked, and a revive at Alexandria North.
- **i5**: this tree's client: a Jangan revive, a Hotan revive and a dead logout at Hotan.
- **i6**: dev's client again, at Alexandria North.

A new QA hook, `OPENSRO_QA_ARRIVAL_PROBE=1`, takes the measurements:
- `QA ARRIVAL`: the feet against the terrain-only ray and the walkable graph's landing, after every
  entry, zone change and GM move;
- `QA GATEPICK`: a gate's pick body against the placed object drawn there, with a sweep of the talk
  ray (`GatePickProbe`);
- `QA GATEAIM`: the screen point to click.

### 1. Hotan: the return was 12.19 under the plaza

**Cause (MEASURED).** The server sends a revive's return like a gate teleport: the gate's point at
height 0 (`teleportArrival`, round 686). The client stood a gate teleport on its walkable graph
because a receipt came first (round 576), but a return has no receipt. It took the plain zone
change's branch:
- In Jangan that branch moved the player to the square spawn (`ZONE_SPAWN_LOCAL`), 350 units from
  where the server had the character. Run i2, `QA ARRIVAL #3`: local (1002, 1020).
- Every other town kept the server's 0, and `_snap_player_onto_terrain` only lifted it to the bare
  terrain.

Hotan's gate point is on the castle plaza, so the result there was wrong. Run i2, `QA ARRIVAL #8 zone
change to hotan`:
- feet 234.59;
- terrain 234.25;
- walkable graph landing 246.78;
- **feet - landing -12.19** (the screenshot `hotan_revive_base.jpg` shows only the head above the
  plaza).

The graph's own step-up limit (`SURFACE_REACH_UP`, 12) then refused the plaza, which is 12.19 up, so
the character stayed underneath.

**Why only Hotan (MEASURED, every point).** `walk_probe.gd --column` was run at the 64 open-world
teleport points.
- At 61 of them the landing is within 1.6 units of the terrain.
- Three are more than 12 above it: `GATE_KT` +12.19, `GATE_TOMB_GATE_IN` +355.79 and
  `GATE_ARABIAN_COAST` +366.84.
- Only `GATE_KT` is a return point, an id-7 town gate.

The other six town gates measure: CH +0.56, WC, EU, CA, SD1 and SD2 0.00.

**Retail (READ, partial).** The server copies the teleportdata record's x/y/z as they are
(`FUN_00407760`; `ResolveRevivePoint` `0x4e08a0`; `GObjPC::Revive` -> `vslot_222` `0x4df590`). No
height function is called on that path. The re-entry's consumer and the client's placement are
unread (OPEN).

**Fix (client).** These arrivals now keep the server's point and stand on the walkable graph, as a
gate teleport does:
- A zone change that finds the player dead, or that this client did not ask for, is a move to the
  return point (`World3D.arrival_keeps_server_point`). Every request goes through
  `_request_zone_change`, which counts it. Both are OURS, from the server's own order: option 1
  warps a dead character, then revives it.
- A restored entry within 1 unit of a town gate's point is stood on the graph as well
  (`_land_restored_return_point`, `TeleportReader.return_points`). That is a dead logout, which the
  server saves at the return point (`savedPlace`).

**After (MEASURED, run i5):**
- Hotan revive: feet 246.78, landing 246.78, feet - landing 0.00 (`hotan_revive_fixed.jpg`).
- Jangan revive: at the gate's point local (969, 1369), feet - landing 0.00. It is no longer moved to
  the square.
- Dead logout at Hotan, then a fresh login: `the restored entry is GATE_KT's point (a return point) --
  stood on the walkable graph there`, feet - landing 0.00.

Run i4:
- Alexandria North revive: feet - landing 0.00.
- All seven gate-teleport arrivals: feet - landing 0.00. Their heights: CH -30.12, SD2 1539.99, SD1
  865.82, WC -104.27, KT 246.78, EU 86.23, CA 182.49.

### 6. OPEN

- The pick's 3 x 3 ray grid: retail casts nine around the cursor (step INFERRED to be 1.6 % of the
  screen); OpenSRO casts one.
- A ray starting inside a gate's box does not take it. Retail's triangle test's back faces are
  unread.
- A structure's spawn position is INFERRED to be its teleportbuilding row.
- Retail's arrival height after the server's unchanged y is unread.
- The two non-return points 355 and 366 units under their objects (`GATE_TOMB_GATE_IN`,
  `GATE_ARABIAN_COAST`) land on the graph as teleports. Nothing returns a character there.

### Review (round 690's review: no HIGH, no MEDIUM; five LOW -- fixed in a follow-up commit)

The review confirmed the READ claims and found layer 10 clean and the click paths and masks right. A
trial merge onto dev d6205fc passed, with 205 suites. The follow-up:

1. **Requests are matched, not counted.** `_request_zone_change` remembers each zone label it asks
   for (`_note_zone_change_request`). `_on_change_zone_result` asks `_zone_result_requested`:
   - a gate teleport's arrival is this client's and takes no request;
   - a refused change answers the oldest request;
   - an accepted one answers the oldest request for its own label, unless it lands on a teleport
     point. No zone's landing is a teleport point: the landings are the centres' middles, and none
     of the 64 open-world points is there.

   So a flag-off kill's return to Jangan's gate, arriving between a zone-box "jangan" and its answer,
   is the server's own move and leaves the request for its answer. The point test runs before the
   zone loads: `region_local_to_world` is `TerrainCollision.place_group`'s transform for the
   region's cell in the result's frame. It is checked against the server's own numbers: GATE_CH
   (9, -409) and GATE_KT (-63182, 10407) in frame 97/168.
2. **The QA rays exclude layer 10**: `QA NPCBODY` (it had no mask), `QA RIG`'s column and the ground
   lattice probe (both had `0xFFFFFFFF`).
3. **The pick's rays, worded right** (`teleport_network.md`, `World3D._bind_region_gates`, TODO).
   `FUN_0078ee20` casts a 3 x 3 grid and keeps a hit when `d < best || (best_idx != 4 && idx ==
   4)`: any nearer hit replaces the best, and a centre hit replaces a best from an outer ray whatever
   its distance.
4. **A logout where a teleport left the player** (pre-existing). The restored-entry landing matched
   id-7 town gates only. A logout right after a teleport to `GATE_TOMB_GATE_IN` or
   `GATE_ARABIAN_COAST`, without moving, re-entered 355.79 / 366.84 under the object there. It now
   matches every point in a world region (`TeleportReader.world_points`, `_teleport_point_at`), and
   no longer needs the region loaded.
5. **Tests for the wiring** (`arrival_landing_test.gd`):
   - `_request_zone_change` remembers the zone;
   - a refused change takes the oldest;
   - with nothing asked, a move is the server's;
   - the interleave: a return first, at a point, takes nothing, then the answer at the landing takes
     the request;
   - two requests answered out of order;
   - an unasked label takes nothing;
   - a teleport arrival leaves the requests alone;
   - the frame conversion, and a non-gate point matched.

   FAIL against 4465783: `FAIL World3D.region_local_to_world exists`; `FAIL
   TeleportReader.world_points exists`; `FAIL World3D._teleport_point_at exists`; `FAIL
   World3D._note_zone_change_request / _match_zone_change_request exist`.

No perf gate: none of this is per-frame code. The matcher runs once per zone change, over 64 points.

## Six-hundred-and-eighty-ninth round: every character is drawn from its own model -- a Europe man is a Europe man, a Kangsi a Kangsi, at its Height and Volume -- for the player, the other players, the paper doll and the portrait, and no body T-poses

The user (2026-10-02): "Euro doesn't seem work once you load in. I'm the default chinese male skin
and I t-pose. When I do chinese female it goes to the default woman skin too. Euro needs added to
the actually game with full skin support, animations, and skills. Same with the rest of the chinese
characters too. Some float and have different ways to sit or hold weapons."

charselect.md's lane W. Europe *skills* are lane euroskill691's; this round is drawing and animation.
Labels: READ (sro_client.exe's dump and asm on the box), MEASURED, INFERRED, OURS, OPEN.

### 1. Why (the before, MEASURED)

- **The T-pose is our code, not the data.** World3D animated the local player only under
  `_character_assets.has(_player_gender)`, and only `china_man` / `china_woman` were ever loaded. A
  Europe character's gender (`europe_man`, round 682) fell back to the China fighter's body for the
  build and failed that test every frame. The base client (bf25e7e, plus a box-only print) signed in
  to this round's server as a Europe noble man: `POSECHECK player gender europe_man body (default)
  posed TPOSE` on **21 of 21** samples, drawn as `chinaman_fighter.bsr` wearing 4 of its 5 items
  (the Europe heavy legs need a bone the China body lacks).
- **"The default skin":** every China Figure was drawn as the fighter (`GENDER_BODY_CODE`), the
  Figure, Height and Volume the player chose were never sent to the world.
- **129 clips played nothing** (`body_anim_probe.gd --lookup=old`, all 52 Figures x every core
  action x every weapon group of their race, 4,056 lookups): the Europe bodies' `onehand_sword` types
  16/17 and `onehand_staff` types 5/16/17 are entries that name no file, and our lookup returned the
  empty entry instead of falling back -- a 1H-sword or staff user's 2nd-4th swing froze.

### 2. What retail does (READ, addresses)

- **Group:** `CObjCharacter::RefreshAnimationGroup` 0xa5bd10: no weapon in visual slot 6 ->
  `default`; else `FUN_00a5a7d0(TypeID4, race)` (race = char data +0x9c); `cart` while pulling a
  transport. The switch is the table we had, plus the fortress weapon 16: race 0 `sword`, race 1
  `onehand_sword`. **No sex test.**
- **Entry:** `CCObjCharacter` slot 3 `FUN_00a5faf0` -> `CCObjAnimation::FUN_00a5b550` ->
  `CCompChar::FUN_00c2bbb0` -> `AniMixer::FUN_00c551a0`: the group by name (`FUN_00bd68e0`), the
  entry by type (`AniMixer::FUN_00c0e950`), a non-null clip; failing any, the same in `default`;
  failing that, nothing. `ResObject::FUN_00c0f500` stores a NULL clip for file index -1, and
  `FUN_00c0f470` overwrites a type in place, so **the last entry of a type wins** and an entry naming
  no file falls back. The avatar group (+0x190) is tried first, without fallback, when set (not
  modelled, OPEN).
- **Nothing race-specific:** the chain reads only the body's own `.bsr` maps. The Europe bodies'
  `default` group names `chinaman_*` / `chinawoman_*` stand, walk and sit clips (MEASURED, round 684's
  review and here) and retail plays them; all 52 Figures use the two Europe skeletons.
- **Sitting:** 0xa5a270 plays type 14 (and 13 from standing), 0xa5a160 type 15 (or 65,
  `_a_wakeup`, after a knock-down: not modelled), through the same lookup.
- **Root and Height:** a driven bone's local matrix takes the keyframe's full translation, x, y and
  z (`RTSkeleton::FUN_00c49f20` / `FUN_00c4bcb0`); the root's world matrix is its local one. Height
  (`CCompChar::FUN_00c25460` -> skeleton +0xa4 -> `FUN_00c4bcb0`) multiplies the root's whole local
  matrix: the model scales about its origin, the feet. **No per-body ground offset** was found in the
  clip / skeleton chain (the position -> compound matrix step, vt+0x54 0xc255e0, was not traced: OPEN).
- **Weapons:** `CObjCharacter::FUN_00a5f4f0` -- the `_l`/`_r` pair for TypeID4 9/13, `_f` for a
  harp on a vslot-0x34 body, else the plain model; the bone comes from each item's own `.bsr`. No
  per-race, per-sex or per-weapon bone table, no hold offset. CharacterAppearance already did this;
  the world did not (it drew no dual axe, round 683).

### 3. What changed

**The wire (OURS layout, trailing, backward compatible; charselect.md lane W has the bytes):**
`OpEntityEntered` appends the model (u32 RefObjID, u8 scale) after its wire angle; `OpEnterWorldResult`
appends the own model and a per-other models list after the own wire angle (making Restored, Seated,
the headings tail and the angle always written, as the field doc's trap requires);
`OpChangeZoneResult` appends the models list after its headings. A row with no model is sent as
`LegacyModelFor(Gender)` at 0x22. The base client read this round's server and entered the world
(section 1's run) -- the tails reach it unread. No migration.

**The world** (`World3D.gd`):
- `_build_assembled_character(equipped, body, scale)` builds through `CharacterAppearance`
  (`from_catalog`: a bodies-only `CharCatalog` from the characterdata parts the world already reads,
  39 ms MEASURED, and the world's item table). Height goes on the skeleton node, Volume on the bone
  groups, `_l`/`_r`/`_f`, the missing-palette-bone rule, round 685's default wear and round 687's hides
  -- select, create and the world now draw a character the same way. The player, every other player,
  the paper doll and the portrait use it.
- The body key is the Figure's code name (`WorldBodies.body_key`: the model's, else the gender's
  legacy body, else the China fighter). Speed (column 47), sound object, BCRadius and Country are the
  body's own rows. The animation gate tests the body, not a gender.
- `BodyAnimations` (new, `scripts/assets/body_animations.gd`): the group switch with the fortress
  weapon by race and the lookup above; `BsrReader.ParsedObject.animation_for` / `_entry_for` /
  `_group_for` implement the last-wins and null-clip fallback. CharacterAppearance and World3D share
  the one table. charselect.md "Animations per body" is the contract for euroskill691.
- The skill-clip folder (`Prim\Ani\Char\China\<man|woman>`) now follows the body's sex; the path
  rule itself is the skill lane's.

**QA:** `OPENSRO_QA_BODY=<id>[:<scale>]`; `OPENSRO_QA_LINEUP` (`scripts/world/qa_lineup.gd`: the
Figures spawned through the other-player path and measured per action phase -- `posed yes|TPOSE`
from the bones against their rest, `feet` as the lowest CPU-skinned vertex against the walkable
surface); `OPENSRO_QA_CREATE=ref:scale:chest:legs:feet:weapon` in QaSignIn; `tools/body_anim_probe.gd`.

- **MEDIUM, a held run speed dropped back to the body's at entry.** `_apply_player_speed` ran at the
  first dress (`_player_body` was still ""), after `_replay_held_buffs("world entry")` had applied the
  server's speed (`BuffRoster.run_speed_of`): a GM under `/speed 2`, or a buffed player, reconnected

  printed `FAIL world entry: the body's own row (run 50), applied at the first dress, keeps the held

- **LOW, Height in the paper doll and the portrait.** Both reset the skeleton's transform to identity.
  READ: the equipment page's avatar (+0x36c, the one the portrait borrows) is dressed by
  `FUN_00a619e0`, which ends with `FUN_00a5b960(info +0x30)` -- the scale byte -- called from
  `IFItemMall::FUN_007c08e0` on `IFMainPopup::FUN_006a1d50`'s page +0x36c and from 0x6abc50 on a +0x36c
  avatar (INFERRED to be the equipment page's own refresh, from the offset). So both now keep the
  skeleton's scale, and the portrait reads the scaled head for its camera.
- **LOW, the encoder's heading.** `EnterWorldResult.Encode` wrote the own wire angle whenever a model
  followed, even with `HasHeading` false; it now encodes such a result as the same result with

  makes the rule explicit rather than fixing a wrong byte).

walked in from below the frame, grew to a 480x270 px patch by the idols, then jumped back off-screen
and walked in again. Its meshes were visible in the tree on every frame and the cull box agreed with

### 2. The select screen's brightness: retail's random hour, not a lighting fault

**MEASURED** (`OPENSRO_QA_SELECT_LUMA`: 1.5 s after the list is up, the frame's mean Rec. 709 luma
over the 3D band less the characters, and over the characters' projected boxes, with the light the
backdrop was given):

| Hour (title phase) | Backdrop | Characters | Light (x 0.30) | Ambient |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 5:00 (0.2083) | 136.1 | 108.6 | (0.63, 0.64, 0.68) | (0.63, 0.66, 0.62) |
| 14:00 (0.5833), visits 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 in one process | 141.1 each | 112.0 each | (0.62, 0.61, 0.56) | (0.79, 0.71, 0.66) |
| 18:00 (0.75) | 138.5 | 109.2 | (0.91, 0.87, 0.74) | (0.79, 0.57, 0.43) |
| 23:00 (0.9583) | 107.4 | 89.8 | (0.48, 0.50, 0.65) | (0.42, 0.46, 0.55) |

At one hour every visit is identical to the decimal: nothing left over from a previous screen, no
late light, no first-visit difference. What changes is the hour: 23:00 is 24 % darker than 14:00
(backdrop) and 20 % (characters). Region 105/81 is environment 33 in all 36 blocks (MEASURED), so
the block-0 environment the world applies is the camera's too. As a picture only, the reference
`fe_ref1.jpg` (a private server, hour unknown) measures 115 over its 3D band, our 14:00 frame 127
over the same crop and 23:00 99 (`luma_montage_before.jpg`: 14:00, 23:00, 5:00, 18:00).

**READ, the hour** (closing charselect.md's INFERRED): SWorld is one global (0x1101950) built once
by the static initialiser 0xd768f0 -> `Map::FUN_00a2f370`, which sets the day phase +0x26a3 to 0.5
and the clock flag +0x2f18 to 0. The phase's only writers are that constructor, `vslot_020` and the
world clock at 0xa2d130 (phase += the float 0x110f7fc x 0.0005, wrapping at 1.0), which runs only
while +0x2f18 is non-zero -- and nothing but the constructor writes +0x2f18 (no other
`[reg+0x2f18]` store, no absolute 0x1104868 store). `CPSTitle::OnCreate` calls `vslot_020` with
`rand() & 3` of its four phases unconditionally (0x86b278). The environment graphs are read at the
phase itself (`Map::FUN_00a1baf0`, 0xa1bb0c). So retail's select and customize show the hour the
title last picked -- 5, 14, 18 or 23 o'clock -- and a new one each time the title is shown, which
is what the user saw: "very dark" at a 23:00 title, "a bit brighter" after returning to the title.
Within one title visit ours already kept the hour (`CharSelectHandoff.day_phase`).

**Changed (OURS, small):** when no title set the hour (a screen opened directly: QA runs), select
and customize each picked a NEW random hour on every visit; `CharSelectHandoff.front_end_phase()`
now picks it once and keeps it, as the title's would be.

**Decided, not changed:** the hour stays retail's. Pinning the front end to a daytime hour would be
OURS against READ; it is recorded as decision 13 for the user (charselect.md section 8). The review
(below) found the darkness this round missed: the bodies themselves drew 1.3-1.8x darker than retail's
character formula, at every hour.

### Review (round 688's review: all three fixes held, the READ confirmed; one HIGH and two LOW, fixed in a follow-up commit)

**HIGH: the select bodies were lit about 1.8x darker than the same character on the customize
preview at the same hour** -- the user's "probably not as bright as it should be". The select screen
hung its bodies in the backdrop with Godot's lit materials under World3D's DirectionalLight3D at its
tuned energy 0.3 (OURS since round 43); the customize preview (round 685), the equipment window and
the portrait draw characters with PlayerPortrait's materials, retail's own formula (READ, its
header: vertex colour = 0.6 x ambient + max(0, n.l) x material x diffuse, diffuse = environment
channel 2 clamped x 0.6, ambient = channel 3 clamped; then texture x colour x 2, MODULATE2X).

- **Changed:** `CharSelectStage._dress` gives each body PlayerPortrait's materials fed the backdrop's
  zone light (`_portrait_zone_light`), as `CharCreatePreview` does, after the body is built -- so the
  round 687 hides and the round 685 default wear are untouched (MEASURED: 7/6, 10/4 and 8/5 meshes
  shown/hidden on the three bodies with either light; every mesh in the character light after).
- **The backdrop's tone mapping:** the first after-run came out 13-37 % BRIGHTER than the preview.
  READ (Godot 4.2.2 `drivers/gles3/shaders/scene.glsl` 1369 and 1590-1593, `tonemap_inc.glsl` 42-58
  and 96-108): an unshaded ALBEDO is decoded to linear, times exposure, Filmic-mapped over the mapped
  white, and encoded again -- World3D's environment is Filmic (tonemap_mode 2), the preview's
  SubViewport linear (PlayerPortrait: no change, MEASURED round 635). So the characters' colour is
  pre-inverted through that chain in their shader (`_undo_tonemap`: the Filmic quadratic solved
  exactly, the decode cubic by Newton's method; OURS on READ source), and the frame carries the
  client's value.
- **MEASURED** (`OPENSRO_QA_SELECT_LUMA`'s per-body line: each body's own pixels -- those that change
  when it is hidden, its shadows off for that mask -- against the same character, same items, built

## Six-hundred-and-eighty-seventh round: the body's own skin no longer shows through worn armour -- each item hides the body pieces it covers, as retail's client does

Round 683 built the bodies and found the body's own skin showing through worn armour on 2-21 % of
an armour's pixels. Its review searched the visual-change masks for a way the client hides a body
piece, found none, and left the rule out as uninvented. A research pass then READ it in the
`.bsr` files, and this round implements it in `CharacterAppearance` (the builder no lobby screen uses
yet), the create screen's preview (`CharacterPreview`, added by the review) and the world.

### 1. The rule (READ, sro_client.exe; the decompile on the box)

- **The block.** Every `.bsr` ends with an attachable block, which `BsrReader.attachable_tail_end`
  only stepped over. `CResAttachable::vslot_007` (0xbe4b90) reads it right after the mod section:
  `u32` -> +0x314, `u32 kind` -> +0x318, `u32 flag` -> +0x31c, `i32 n`, then n x `{u32 key, u32
  value}`. `vslot_008` (0xbda070) writes the same layout. A body (`CResChar::vslot_007` 0xc1efd0)
  then has `nComboNum`, asserted 0; an item ends there.
- **What it means.** In a body (type 0), key -> the index of the body's own mesh in its mesh list.
  In an item (type 5), the keys the item covers.
- **Attaching.** `CCompChar::vslot_067` (0xc1fa90) adds a part and, for a tag-5 resource
  (`CResAttachable`), calls `FUN_00c1f790`. Read again this round: when the item's flag
  (`*(res + 8)`) is 1, it takes part id 1 (`FUN_00c1f720(1)`, the body, INFERRED), and for every
  item key equal to a body key calls `FUN_00c35050(value, 0)` -> `FUN_00c33760`, which sets the
  body mesh's `+0x10 = 0`. The gather `FUN_00c38f50` skips a mesh with +0x10 == 0.
- **Removing.** `vslot_061` (0xc1fa00) and `vslot_064` call `FUN_00c1f890`: `FUN_00c392a0(1)` shows
  every body mesh, then the loop re-applies the hides of every remaining part whose id is not 1.
- **The keys (MEASURED by the research, all Figures):** body 0 hair, 1 face, 2 torso_upper,
  3 torso_lower, 5 arm_upper, 6 arm_lower/fore, 11 pelvis, 12 thigh, 13 calf, in a different mesh
  order per file. Items: helm `_ha` {0} (some heavy helms {0, 1}), chest `_ba` {2, 3, 5} and the
  like by set, legs `_la` {11, 12} (women's light/clothes {11}), feet `_fa` {13}, gauntlets `_aa`
  {6} with flag 1 on heavy but flag 2 on light and clothes, shoulders `_sa` {4} (no body piece).

### 2. What changed

- `BsrReader.Attachable` and `parse_attachable` / `attachable_block`: the block, with strict
  bounds (every word in the file, 0 <= n <= 1000, OURS bound). Bytes after it -- a body's combo word,
  or the leftovers 61 real files carry -- are counted in `trailing`, not refused. Read for type 0
  and type 5 through the header table only (`ParsedObject.attachable`), so scenery parses as
  before. `attachable_tail_end` now uses it.
- `SkinnedBsrAssembler`: each body mesh (and its front-pass twin, and a rigid piece's attachment)
  carries `BODY_MESH_META` = its index in the body file's mesh list, and is named after its piece.
  The meta survives the template duplicate (tested); the generated name of an unnamed node does
  not, which is the trap the research hit. `apply_body_hides(skeleton, body, items)` is
  `FUN_00c1f890`: show every tagged mesh, then for each item block with flag 1 and each key, hide
  the meshes the BODY's block maps that key to. Matched by key, never by position.
  `AttachedItem.attachable` carries the item's block.
- `CharacterAppearance`: `build()` applies it; `unequip(body, slot)` frees the slot's nodes and
  re-applies from what remains; `Body.hidden_body_meshes` counts. `set_scale_byte` touches no
  visibility, so the hides stay (tested). The item blocks are cached with the item templates.
- `World3D._build_assembled_character` (the local player, other players, the paper doll and the
  portrait) applies it after attaching the worn items. Every equipment change rebuilds that body,
  so retail's show-all-then-re-apply is the same call on the new set. Its log line now says how
  many body meshes were hidden.
- `tools/appearance_probe.gd`: `--showthrough=1` measures both "every body piece drawn" and "the
  hides applied" in one run, checks every Figure's block, and `--closeup=<dir>` renders the
  before/after pictures.
