## Six-hundred-and-seventy-sixth round: monsters and other players fade into existence over 2.0 s, as retail's CIDecoAppear fades them, instead of popping in

The user (2026-10-01): "Also another fix, mobs seem to fade in existence not pop. Check the
original game code to see how they do it. Players might do the same but it seems like a much
faster fade if it at all."

Labels: READ (the decompiled client, `/var/tmp/decomp_client` and `/var/tmp/sro_client.asm` on the
render box; constants read from `sro_client.exe`), MEASURED (the render box, GL Compatibility,
RX 7600), INFERRED, OURS, OPEN. The full table is `docs/protocol/appear_fade.md`.

### 1. What retail does (READ)

- **The deco.** A character is faded in by a decoration object, `CIDecoAppear` (class link
  0x110a770, registered at 0xd77090 with the name string 0xde5610 `CIDecoAppear`), found by its
  RTTI name beside `CIDecoDisappear`.
- **Who makes it.** Vslot 0x6c of a character, `FUN_009d17e0`: `cmp byte [esi+0x770], 0` (asm
  0x9d18f0), then `FUN_00ba36d0(0x110a770, 0)` and `CIDecoAppear::FUN_00a48a20(obj id +0x30,
  [0xd86ecc])` (asm 0x9d190b-0x9d191b). The body reader runs it: `CICMonster::vslot_025` (0x9d3850)
  calls vslot 0x6c, and both spawn paths run the body reader -- 0x3015 (`FUN_008a6ca0` ->
  `FUN_008a6bd0(stream, 1)`) and the group spawn (`FUN_008a6d20` type 1 -> `FUN_008a6bd0(stream,
  0)`). There is no separate "entering view" path: every spawn the client is sent fades.
- **The flag +0x770** is 1 from the CICharactor constructor (asm 0x9d2e50). Its one setter
  (`FUN_009c7b10`) is called with 0 only for objects the client makes itself: a game script's
  actor (0x518514), an icscriptobj (0x9e26de) and `FUN_0050f1b0` (0x50f24a).
- **Which classes.** Vslot 0x6c, read from each vtable: `FUN_009d17e0` for CICMonster, CICNPC,
  CICCos (pets), CICGuard and CICMonsterNPC; for CICUser (**other players**) `FUN_009dbcc0`, which
  ends in `FUN_009d17e0`. Ground items (CIItem) and teleport gates have `FUN_009c1890`: no fade.
  **Players fade exactly like monsters, the same 2.0 s** -- not faster. (The user's "much faster if
  at all" is not what the code does; what makes it look so in play is not known.)
- **Duration and curve.** The float at 0xd86ecc is **2.0**. `CIDecoAppear::FUN_00a48a20` sets the
  alpha to 0 and the rate to 255.0 (double 0xd83108) / 2.0; `CIDecoAppear::vslot_009` (0xa48ae0)
  adds rate x dt each frame (float 0x110f7fc: the frame's seconds, clamped to 3.0, 0xba40fb-0xba4136)
  and sets the sum **truncated** & 0xff (asm 0xa48b5f-0xa48b75: rounding control set to chop around
  the `fistp`) while the sum is <= 255, then 0xff, and deletes itself. **Linear**, 0 to 255 in 2.0
  s: 63 / 127 / 191 at 0.5 / 1.0 / 1.5 s. (This entry first said `round(sum)`; the review read the
  chop -- see Review below.)
- **What it writes.** `CCompChar` vslot 5 (0xc25590, vtable 0xe0cd3c): `+0x4c = alpha << 24`, on
  the character's compound model. The name plate is drawn at full alpha regardless
  (`FUN_008b4d90(point, 0xff)`, READ in round 673); whether the shadow or effects read the
  compound's alpha is not read (OPEN). Every frame the CICharactor update also writes 0xff (or 0/0x50 for stealth) through
  `FUN_009ce950`; the deco's write landing after it is INFERRED from the fade being visible.
- **The way out.** A despawn (0x3016 `FUN_008a6cc0`, group despawn type 2) calls vslot 0x4c with 0
  (`IGIDObject::FUN_009c32f0`, CICMonster `FUN_009d3c90`), which makes a `CIDecoDisappear`
  (0x110a790) of **1.5 s** (float 0xd819ec): 255 down to 0, then the object is deleted. Not drawn
  by this round (OPEN).

### 2. The engine trap (MEASURED)

The obvious way to draw it, `GeometryInstance3D.transparency`, does nothing in Godot 4.2.2's GL
Compatibility renderer: the measurement below, with transparency set to 1.0 on every mesh of
`mob\china\mangnyang.bsr`, read **covered 1.000** on every frame from the first (the model fully
drawn). So the fade is drawn with materials.

### 3. What changed (OURS, in how it is drawn)

- `client/scripts/world/appear_fade.gd` (new): `AppearFade.alpha_at` is the deco's curve;
  `AppearFade.Fades` runs the fades. While a model fades, each mesh draws with a **blended twin**
  of its own material -- a StandardMaterial3D duplicated with alpha blending, a ShaderMaterial
  duplicated onto its shader's fade twin -- at the cohort's alpha. Twins are **shared by every model
  whose fade started in the same frame** (they are always at the same alpha), so a list of 500 of
  24 species makes a twin per species material per build frame, not one per body. At 2.0 s each
  mesh gets its own material back -- the template's shared, opaque one -- and the twins are freed:
  nothing stays on a transparent material. Depth is written while translucent
  (`depth_draw_always`, OURS) so a model's near faces stay in front of its far ones.
- `foliage.gdshaderinc` gains an `APPEAR_FADE` block (the same alpha test made by hand, ALPHA =
  `appear_alpha`), compiled only by the new `foliage_fade.gdshader` /
  `foliage_one_sided_fade.gdshader`; the world's shaders compile without it, unchanged.
  `ObjectLoader._mod_shader` takes `fade` for the MTRL-mod shader's twin and tags each shader with
  its key; `ObjectLoader.appear_fade_shader` maps a shader to its twin. A material with no twin is
  left as it is (that piece pops, counted in `unfadable`); the census below found none.
- `World3D`: a monster body built (`_build_monster_body`) and another player's body built
  (`_spawn_or_update_other`) start a fade; `_physics_process` steps them. The name plate (Label3D),
  the party mark (Sprite3D) and the collider are not meshes and are not faded; effect meshes (under an
  `EfpEffect`) are skipped. A refresh of a body already drawn does not restart it. A body rebuilt
  when its region loads fades again, as an object re-sent by the server would.
- `BerserkLook._take_meshes` copies `AppearFade.original_material(mi)`, so a berserk starting
  mid-fade keeps the real material (the piece then shows at once); the fade leaves a material
  someone replaced in place.

Census (MEASURED, `measure_appear_fade.gd --census`: the 155 of the 156 models the `MOB_` rows
name that assemble, every surface): 72 StandardMaterial3D, 269 `foliage.gdshader`, 244
`foliage_one_sided.gdshader`, 17 MTRL-mod shader; **with no fade twin: 0**.

### 4. The measurement (MEASURED, `client/tools/measure_appear_fade.gd`)

A real monster model from Data.pk2, held in its rest pose before a plain background at 320x240,
added and faded with a fixed 1/60 s step; every frame read back. Covered = how much of the model's
final colour difference from the background the frame shows (0 = absent, 1 = opaque).

| t (s) | asked alpha | mangnyang (StandardMaterial3D) | tiger (foliage shader) | nachal (MTRL mod) | mangnyang, no fade (base) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0.000 | 0 | 0.000 | 0.000 | 0.000 | **1.000** |
| 0.017 | 2 | 0.010 | 0.012 | 0.015 | 1.000 |
| 0.500 | 64 | 0.265 | 0.303 | 0.368 | 1.000 |
| 1.000 | 128 | 0.518 | 0.566 | 0.638 | 1.000 |
| 1.500 | 191 | 0.758 | 0.794 | 0.839 | 1.000 |
| 1.983 | 253 | 0.992 | 0.994 | 0.995 | 1.000 |
| 2.000 | 255 | 1.000 | 1.000 | 1.000 | 1.000 |

Rising monotonically from nothing to the whole model in 2.0 s. The multi-piece models read above
the asked alpha mid-fade (worst +0.064 tiger, +0.139 nachal; +0.016 mangnyang): overlapping
translucent pieces composite (INFERRED). After the fade, the last frame is **pixel-identical** to
the never-faded model's for all three (0 of 76,800 pixels differ), and every mesh has its own
material back.

- **Shadow, effects**: whether retail fades them with the model is not read; this client leaves
  them as they were. (The name plate stays at full alpha in retail, READ in round 673.)
- **NPCs, guards and pets** fade in retail (vslot 0x6c is `FUN_009d17e0` for CICNPC, CICGuard and
  CICCos), but ours are not: NPCs are built from the map's data when a region loads, not from a
  spawn, and guards and pets are not drawn yet; they appear at once.

  own interpolator; whether it shows a spawn fade is not settled. Not faded here.

  Review below) -- the base pays it when the monster appears, this client when its fade ends. Not
  this round's; warming the opaque monster shaders too is the same trick.
- **An MTRL mod shader first made after the world loaded** has its fade twin compiled on first
  sight (the warm-up covers the mod shaders made by then; 17 of 602 monster surfaces are mod).

### Review (on the integration branch with rounds 673-675): one MEDIUM, six LOWs, fixed in a second commit

1. **MEDIUM, retail truncates (READ, confirmed).** `CIDecoAppear::vslot_009` at 0xa48b5f-0xa48b75:
   `fnstcw; movzx; or eax, 0xc00; fldcw; fistp` -- rounding control "chop", MSVC's float-to-int
   idiom. So the alpha is the sum truncated: 63 / 127 / 191 at 0.5 / 1.0 / 1.5 s, not 64 / 128 /
   191. `AppearFade.alpha_at` now returns `int(a) & 0xff`; §1, the code comment and
   docs/protocol/appear_fade.md say so. The measurement table in §4 was taken with the rounded
   alpha (one step of 255 higher at most); the review's re-runs below are on the truncated one.
2. **LOW, a StandardMaterial3D twin multiplied in its texture's alpha.** The opaque original ignores
   texture alpha; the blended duplicate did not. MEASURED with the review's own probe
   (`measure_appear_fade.gd`, `mob\oasis\redeyeghost.bsr`, whose body textures average alpha
   0.890 with 11.0 % of texels under 0.5 -- `--census`): on 555cfc0, at 1.0 s **804 of 8,082 model
   pixels (9.9 %) showed under half the asked alpha** (holes), and the twin at alpha 255 differed
   from the opaque model in **2,799 pixels, by up to 166/255** -- a snap at 2.0 s. Now a plain
   StandardMaterial3D (`AppearFade.is_plain_standard`: opaque, colour and texture, every other
   setting Godot's default -- every monster StandardMaterial3D surface and the capsules) fades on
   `AppearFade.STANDARD_FADE_CODE`, a small shader with the generated standard lighting and ALPHA
   the fade's alone: **0 holes**, and the twin at 254 differs from the opaque model in **0 pixels
   by more than 2/255 (at most 1)**. Any other BaseMaterial3D keeps the duplicate. The player's
   default body (`char\china\chinaman_fighter.bsr`): 10 surfaces, all foliage-shader (whose twin
   keeps the alpha test and ignores texture alpha), none StandardMaterial3D.
3. **LOW, a stale berserk copy.** `original_material` returned the fade's original while a berserk
   end had put the template's material back; it now returns it only while the mesh still draws
   with a twin (twins carry `TWIN_META`).
4. **LOW, wording.** The HP bar (removed by round 673) is gone from the comments, docs and test
   labels: "the name plate and party mark (Sprite3D)". The name plate at full alpha is READ (round
   673: `FUN_008b4d90(point, 0xff)`), no longer OPEN.
5. **LOW, `Fades.finish_all()` was never called**: deleted (the bodies it would restore are freed
   with the world).
6. **LOW, the first-sight shader compile (MEASURED).** `measure_appear_fade.gd` with **empty Godot
   and Mesa shader caches** for every run (`XDG_DATA_HOME`, `MESA_SHADER_CACHE_DIR`), frame times at
   60 Hz vsync:

   | model | no fade (base): first frame | fade: first frame / at the fade's end | fade + warm-up: first frame / at the end |
   |---|---|---|---|
   | redeyeghost (StandardMaterial3D) | 238.8 ms | 198.9 / 234.0 ms | **31.0** / 232.0 ms |
   | tiger (foliage) | 176.7 ms | 159.2 / 162.9 ms | **31.3** / 166.4 ms |
   | nachal (MTRL mod) | 132.7 ms | 134.8 / 134.8 ms | **30.1** / 118.4 ms |

   So the fade added a compile of its own (135-199 ms) on the first monster of each material kind.
   `AppearFade.warm(camera)`, called while the world loads, draws a 0.01-unit quad per twin shader
   at alpha 0 in front of the camera for 3 frames: the first fading frame drops to 30-31 ms. What is
   left is the opaque material's own first compile -- the base pays it as the monster appears, this
   client 2 s later when the fade ends -- recorded OPEN. (A warm Mesa cache hides all of it: the
   same runs with the caches kept read 16-20 ms.)
7. **OPEN recorded:** NPCs (CICNPC), guards (CICGuard) and pets (CICCos) fade in retail and not
   here. The dt label is upgraded to READ: [0x110f7fc] is the frame's seconds, clamped to 3.0, at
   0xba40fb-0xba4136, set with the milliseconds at 0x110f7f8 (0x84c343).

## Six-hundred-and-seventy-fourth round: towns are safe from monsters -- a monster that follows a player into a town disappears at the town's region line, as the original server removes it

The user (2026-10-01): "There should also be safe zones in towns but I had a mob follow me into town
and attack me. I think the usually disappear if they follow you into safe zone but check the game
logic." The game logic says the guess is right: the original server removes a monster the moment
its move takes it into a town region. OpenSRO had no towns at all on the server, so a monster
chased a player through Jangan's gate and kept swinging.

Labels: READ (SR_GameServer.exe: `/var/tmp/decomp_server`, `srv.asm`, the exe's vtables read with
a PE reader on the box), MEASURED (the render box, the client's own Media.pk2), INFERRED, OURS.
The full reading is in `docs/protocol/monster_ai.md`, "Towns: a monster that walks into one is
removed (round 674)"; the essentials:

### 1. What a town is (READ, MEASURED)

- The server's town is the `_RefRegion` row's **IsBattleField** byte. The row parser `0x6a2e40`
  stores wRegionID at `+0`, skips X and Z, reads ContinentName and AreaName, and stores the sixth
  column's byte at `+2`. A field region keeps its row at `region+0x10`; every town test in the
  binary reads `*(region+0x10)+2`.
- NOT regioninfo.txt: the server parses it (`RegionManagerBody::FUN_0098be30`), but the region
  manager's town query (slot 23, `0x98d040`) is never called -- the global `DAT_00cc387c` is called
  through slots `0xc`..`0x7c`, never `0x5c`, in the decompile and in the asm.
- MEASURED: the client's `server_dep\silkroad\textdata\refregion.txt` (UTF-16, 21 columns) equals
  the server package's `SR_GameRefData\refregion.txt` byte for byte after decoding (diff empty):
  3,194 regions, **103 with IsBattleField 0**, all town areas (`Town_Jangan` 6 -- 97/167-169 and
  98/167-169 --, `Town_Dunhwang` 4, `Town_Khotan` 7, `Town_Cons` 21, `Eu` 2, `Town_Samarkand` 4,
  `Town_Thief` 1, `TOWN_ARABIA`/`TOWN_` 22, `town_Alex` 36). This is the data source: the
  operator's own archive, exported by `export-refdata -mode regions`. No row is in the repo.

### 2. What a monster does there (READ)

- `CGObjMob::SetCurRegion` (vtable `0xaeddac` slot 235, `0x4c1270`) is
  `this[0x4a] = region; if (region == 0 || region.row[+2] == 0) SetLifeState(3, 0xff, 0)`.
- Life state 3 is **removal**: `CGObjChar::SetLifeState` (`0x4a9c80`) broadcasts only 1<->2, and
  the main loop (`CMainProcess::FUN_00413b30`) hands a non-player in state 3 to `FUN_00417090`,
  which deletes it -- the same end as a monster's lifetime (`CGObjMob::Update` `0x4c1700`). No
  death, no experience, no drop.
- Slot 235's one call site (`0x485ad4`) is in the region change of `FUN_004858e0`, reached only
  from the object's MoveTo (`FUN_00485740` <- `0x48b660`, CGObjMob's slot 231), which
  `CGObj::EnterWorld` also calls. So a monster is removed whenever its walk crosses into a town
  region, and when it is placed in one. The veto before it (slot 220) is `return 1` for a monster
  (`0x9856e0`).
- **Nothing else protects a player in town.** CGObjMob's attack check (slot 394, `0x529110`), the
  AI's target validity (`0x540de0`) and its nearest selector (`0x5464e0`) read no region. A monster
  that stops on the field side of the line still hits a player standing just inside it.
- The byte's player-side uses (READ, not built, TODO): PvP refused `0x3018` when either side is in
  a town (CGObjPC slot 394, `0x5293a0`), offensive skills refused from a town (skill gate row 13,
  `0x58e186`), the thief's cart (`0x0c01`, CGObjPC slot 220, `0x4eb220`).

So the answers to the brief's four questions: a town is a region with IsBattleField 0 (a table);
a monster chasing a player into it **disappears** at the line; it cannot attack a player inside
because it cannot be inside -- but one outside can reach a player at the edge; monsters are not
kept from spawning or wandering there, they are removed on arrival.

### 3. What changed (OURS where said)

- `internal/safezone` (new): the table, read from the CSV `RegionID,ContinentName,AreaName,
  IsBattleField`; `SafeAt` is IsBattleField 0. OURS: a region the CSV does not list is not a town.
- `cmd/export-refdata -mode regions`: refregion.txt -> regions.csv, refusing a short or non-numeric
  row, loading its output back. On the box's archive: `wrote 3194 regions to regions.csv, 103 of
  them towns (IsBattleField 0)`.
- `cmd/server -regions-csv` (env `OPENSRO_REGIONS_CSV`): loads it, fatal when it does not load,
  `session.SetSafeRegions`. Without it nothing changes.
- `session` (monster AI, `monsterai.go` step 1b and the new-brain path, `safezone.go`): after the
  mover's step, each monster that crossed a cell line (a region line is always a cell line) and each
  monster met for the first time is removed when it stands in a town region: `combat.Hub.Remove`
  (new; no death, no credit; booked on the death log so the nest re-arms as for a loss, INFERRED),
  `OpMonsterLeft` to the players whose window holds it (OURS: retail's despawn is `0x3016`; the
  client already drops a body on `OpMonsterLeft`), its states and blocking streak forgotten, and an
  INFO line `monster removed: it entered a town ...` with its state, target, region and area.
- Docs: `monster_ai.md` "Towns", `server/README.md` (`-regions-csv`), `deploy/README.md` (the export
  line, the compose line, "Towns (round 674)" with the opensro-01 steps), `TODO.md` "Towns".
- No client change: the removal reaches the client as the area-of-interest leave it already handles.

### 4. Tests

New: `internal/session/safezone674_test.go` (with `safezone674_shim_test.go`, the one new-API call),
`safezone674_unit_test.go` (the region in each bucket's frame), `internal/safezone/safezone_test.go`,
`internal/combat/remove674_test.go`, `cmd/export-refdata/regions_test.go`. The rows in every test
table are SYNTHETIC.

## Six-hundred-and-seventy-third round: no bar over a monster's head, every monster's name shown within 300 of the player from any camera angle in the original's white-on-dark look, and every monster turns to face the way it runs

The user (2026-10-01, on v0.1.467): "There's a legacy healthbar above mobs that's needs removed (for
now) [...] There's a toggle in the original game to see mob and player health bars above them but
it's much smaller but let's ignore it for now. Also the mob name is only visible with certain
angles and it should be visible at all times [...] Also mobs should face the way the run, I've seen
mobs come at me sideways to attack me." Two screenshots: two Earth Ghosts with big red bars over
them near Donwhang, and, from a steep camera, an Earth Ghost with no name beside the player whose
name shows.

### 1. The bar (OURS, removed)

`World3D._hp_bar` built it in 2026-08 (rounds 146-149): a 64 x 8 red/black texture on a fixed-size
billboarded `Sprite3D` at 0.9 of the model's height, its colours and size "a disclosed choice". It
was hung on monsters only (`_build_monster_body`; players and NPCs never had one) and repainted on
every health change (`_set_hp_bar` from the list refresh, `_paint_monster_hp`). All of it is gone
-- the node, the per-hit texture rebuild, the constants -- and nothing replaces it per frame. A
monster's health still goes into its snapshot and the target window (HudTarget), and a damage
number still starts where the bar sat (`MONSTER_TEXT_UNDER_NAME`, 0.9 of the name's height, OURS,
unchanged).

What retail has (READ, not built, as the user asked): `CICharactor` vslot 38 (0x9d0da0), the name
pass's sibling, draws a small HP (and MP) gauge only under the option flags it tests
(`FUN_00b94b90` on 0xeef6f0 / 0xef1a84 / 0xef1bc0) and only within the name's 300 of the player
(`FUN_009cef40`). docs/TODO.md.

### 2. The name (READ the rule; MEASURED the cause)

**Retail (READ, sro_client.exe; docs/protocol/monster_ai.md "The overhead name").** The name is
drawn by `FUN_009d0a80` (CICharactor): it projects the head point through the camera, runs the
object's vslot 15 with pass 4 (CICMonster's 0x9d3e70, the party mark) and draws the text with
`FUN_008b4d90(point, 0xff)` -- screen space, full alpha, no fade. Its one distance test, at
0x9d0ac3, returns when `300.0 <= object+0x24c` (float 0xd85224, read from the PE image) unless
`object+0xf0` is set. `+0x24c` is written at 0x9d6f7e by `CICPlayer::vslot_005` (0x9d6c80, message
0xd) in its walk over the entity list: `sqrt(dx^2 + dy^2 + dz^2)` between the LOCAL PLAYER's
position (+0x90..+0x98, loaded at 0x9d6ea1) and the object's. The constructor (0x9c2340) starts it at
1000.0 (0xda95ec). So a name shows while its owner is within 300 units of the player; the camera's
angle and zoom do not enter into it.

**Ours, before.** `_apply_name_plate_range` gave every plate `visibility_range_end = 80` with an
8-unit fade -- a distance from the CAMERA, "a project choice". The camera hangs up to 90 units out
on its arm, so a monster a few dozen units from the player sits 80-115 units from the camera, and
which side of 80 it falls on turns with the pitch and the zoom.

**MEASURED** (the render box, 1280 x 720, `OPENSRO_QA_MOBS=24` real species around the Jangan
spawn, `OPENSRO_QA_PLATES=1`, eight viewpoints at pitch -42 / -80 / -10 and zoom 45 / 75 / 90;
`client/tools/plate_pixels.py` counts the plate's cream-beside-black pixels at the point each
`QA PLATE` line says it projects to):

| | plates on screen | with plate pixels |
|---|---|---|
| dev (4104a11 + the round's logging) | 121 | 3 |
| this round | 121 | 121 |

The one monster near enough to straddle the cut, 73.4 from the player:

|---|---|---|---|
| pitch -42, zoom 75 | 87.3 | 97 px | 97 px |
| pitch -42, zoom 90 | 97.0 | 0 | 99 px |

**The fix.** `NamePlates` (client/scripts/world/name_plates.gd): `shown(owner, player)` is the

crowd is not free), so a name changes at most 0.1 s after its owner crosses 300. `_name_plate` no
longer sets a visibility range and registers the plate; the party mark, a child of the plate,
follows it. The debug panel's "Names within" slider now sets the distance from the player; its
saved key is new (`name_range_from_player`) so a value saved for the old camera range does not
keep hiding names. The look is 2b.

NOT read: what `+0xf0` is (it shows a name at any distance), the pass's other early returns, and
the global byte 0xec4b58 the overlay is drawn under -- one is likely the Option window's name

## Six-hundred-and-seventy-second round: text as crisp as the original's at every UI scale -- glyphs rasterised at the scale and drawn unfiltered, every in-game text node in the client's own face, and the old lost-last-glyph bug found in Buttons and guarded

The user (2026-10-01): "The text in the game seems blurry while it's nice and crisp in the original
game. [...] The text looks bad on pretty much any DPI scale too. Here's 1.95 at ~4k resolution."
Then: "Yah, 2.0 does look clear." The screenshot (the HUD's name, "Lv 140", the HP/MP numbers at
1.95) shows soft, dark-fringed text in crisp frame art.

Labels: READ (the decompiled client, `/var/tmp/decomp_client`; Godot 4.2.2-stable's source),
MEASURED (the render box, GL Compatibility on the RX 7600, 3840x2160 unless said, real
Media.pk2 -- the face resolved is the archive's Arial, `UIC_STT_FONTNAME`'s English column on this
archive), INFERRED, OURS.

### 1. What retail does (READ)

- **The fonts.** `FUN_00baa110` builds each FontIndex's HFONT: `lfHeight = -MulDiv(pt, 96, 72)`,
  `lfWidth/Escapement/Orientation = 0`, `lfWeight` 0 (FW_DONTCARE) for the regular face and 600
  for variant 2, `lfItalic` 1 for variant 1, `lfUnderline` 1 for variant 3, `lfCharSet` 1
  (DEFAULT_CHARSET), `lfOutPrecision` 0 (OUT_DEFAULT_PRECIS), `lfClipPrecision` 0, **`lfQuality`
  0 (DEFAULT_QUALITY)**, `lfPitchAndFamily` 0; `CreateFontIndirectA`, selected into the memory DC
  `DAT_0110fab0` (`CreateCompatibleDC(NULL)` in `CGame::FUN_00ba9f40`) for `GetTextMetricsA`. Only
  the regular variant is always made (`local_50[0] = 1`); the others when asked.
- **The glyphs.** `GFontChar::FUN_008b0a00` rasterises a character with
  `GetGlyphOutlineW(DAT_0110fab0, ch, 1, &gm, size, buf, &identity MAT2)` -- **format 1 is
  GGO_BITMAP, one bit per pixel** -- and unpacks the DWORD-aligned rows bit by bit into 16-bit
  texels, `0xffff` for a set bit and 0 otherwise, 128 texels to a row of its glyph texture.
  `GNFontChar::FUN_00492bc0` does the same through `DAT_01119ffc` (a DC made compatible with the
  first). So `lfQuality` does not matter: whatever the system's smoothing, the glyph that reaches
  the texture is one bit deep. This is why round 199 measured one luminance level in the reference
  screenshots (`{12: 162}`); it is now read, not only measured.
- **The scale.** The original never scales its UI (UI_TODO's "Scaling" note): its glyphs are drawn
  1:1. OpenSRO's UI scale has no retail counterpart; the target at scale s is the same look --
  one level, a 1-pixel edge -- with glyphs rasterised AT s, not a 1x bitmap magnified.

### 2. The measurement (MEASURED, `client/tools/measure_text_crispness.gd`)

The tool builds the HUD's text the way World3D does -- `HudPlayerInfo` (name "deadass3", Lv 140,
24936/24936, 90333/90333), `HudChat` and `HudSystemMessage` lines, the GM notice, the character
window from `HudPanels`, eight code-made Buttons like the dialogs' ("Register", "Buy", "Sell",
...), the 2026-09-11 login form (a VBoxContainer of LineEdits and Buttons in Godot's own font) and
a name plate from `World3D._name_plate` -- and for each scale renders a frame, renders it again with
one text kind invisible, and diffs. Each changed pixel is fitted as background + t x (ink -
background) over the kind's ink colours (text, shadow, outline). Per kind: **partial** = % of text
pixels with t < 0.9; **levels** = distinct t in 1/16 steps; **edge** = mean partial pixels at a
run's end + 1; **mass** = sum of t / s^2 (a glyph drawn as a block, or lost, shows here); and per
Button, ink width against the string's advance width, judged against its own ratio at 1.0 (a lost
glyph). Aliased text drawn 1:1 is 0 % / 1 / 1.00. The scales run in ONE process, changed live as
the debug panel's slider does; fresh starts at 1.25, 1.5, 1.95 and (in 1160x700) 2.35 were run
too.

### 3. Before (dev bf11666, the scale changed live 1.0 -> 2.5): partial % / levels / edge px

| text | 1.00 | 1.25 | 1.50 | 1.75 | 1.95 | 2.00 | 2.35 | 2.50 |

### 4. Two engine traps on the way (READ + MEASURED)

**Glyphs drawn as solid blocks.** The first probe turned the window's oversampling flag on by
hand after `apply_ui_scale` had set a fractional scale: every glyph drawn before it rendered as a
solid rectangle in the text colour (ink mass 2.6x that at 1.0, fill 0.86 of the ink box against
0.35). READ: `Window::_update_viewport_size` resizes the canvas -- `Viewport::_set_size`, which
returns early when nothing changed and otherwise calls `update_canvas_items()`, a `queue_redraw`
on every CanvasItem -- and only then sets the text server's oversampling, and
`TextServerAdvanced::_font_set_global_oversampling` clears every font's size cache (the glyph
textures). Oversampling changed WITH a size change: the queued redraws fetch new glyphs. Changed
without one (a flag flip at an unchanged scale): nothing redraws and the old draw commands point at
freed textures (INFERRED: drawn with GL's default white). So the flag is now on from start-up
(`project.godot`) and never toggled. The probe's glyph atlas itself was fine at every scale
(`font_get_texture_image`: 601 opaque texels at 1.0, 2,212 at 1.95, 0 partial).

**The 2026-09-11 lost glyph, reproduced and explained.** With oversampling on at every scale,
"Sell" drew as "Sel" at 1.25 (ink 20 px against 25; 23 against 26.2 now), a fresh start and a live
change alike, and the 2026-09-11 form's "Register" as "Registe" at 1.5 -- the bug the
whole-number rule was made for. It is a Button's alone. READ: a Button sets its TextLine's width to
the text's own width (`scene/gui/button.cpp`, `int text_width = MAX(1, ... text_buf->get_size().x)`),
which `_shaped_text_get_size` rounds UP (`.ceil()`), and `TextLine::draw` passes that width as the
right clip of `shaped_text_draw`, which stops at the first glyph whose end passes it
(`servers/text_server.cpp`, "Clip right"). At a fractional oversampling the advances are fractions
-- "Sell" at 1.25 shapes as 8 + 6.675 + 2.662 + 2.662 = 20.000 (MEASURED, TextLine) -- and when
they sum to a whole number the ceiling adds no room, and the running end passes the clip on the
last glyph (INFERRED: single-precision accumulation a hair over). At 1.0 advances are whole
pixels; at 2.0 they are halves, exact in binary. A Label draws without that clip: no Label lost a
glyph at any scale. Round 581's probe (a Label) could not reproduce it for that reason.

### 5. What changed (OURS, each measured)

- `client/project.godot`: `gui/fonts/dynamic_fonts/use_oversampling=true` -- the window
  rasterises glyphs at its content scale factor at every scale, from start-up.
- `client/scripts/client_settings.gd`, `apply_ui_scale`: keeps the flag on (never toggles it);
  after a live scale change, `_refresh_text` sends every Control a theme-changed notification (so
  Buttons and containers re-measure their text) and nudges every Label3D's font size and back (so
  a name plate rebuilds its glyph quads). Measured without it, in a running client: the Buttons'
  layout moved under the probe and the plate's ink grew 5-14x at 1.75/1.95; with it, a live change
  measures as a fresh start.
- `client/scripts/ui/ui_builder.gd`: **the one helper** -- `apply_ui_theme(root)`: a Theme with
  the client's face (`font_at(0)`) at FontIndex 0's 12 px as the default, so a Label, Button,
  LineEdit, RichTextLabel or ItemList made in code without a font of its own is no longer in
  Godot's anti-aliased default at 16 px; and `watch_text(root)`, which makes every text node under
  the root -- there now or added later, at any depth, one `child_entered_tree` connection per UI
  node, none in the 3D world -- draw unfiltered (`crisp_text`: `texture_filter = NEAREST`). Art
  keeps its filter: only Label/LineEdit/RichTextLabel/ItemList, Buttons without texture styles,
  and nodes marked `ui_text` are switched. `guard_button_font` gives every Button under the root
  its face as a FontVariation with `variation_embolden` 0.01: each advance grows by 0.01 x size /
  64 (`_get_extra_advance`), so a whole-number sum gets a fraction and the ceiling a unit of
  room; the outline is untouched (FreeType's embolden strength, embolden x size x 4 in 1/64 px,
  truncates to 0 below 25 px) and 1.0's advances still round to whole pixels.
  `TextLayer`: a full-rect child that draws a node's text unfiltered over its art.
  `_apply_font` (every layout label) calls `crisp_text` too, and `use_font_data` gives a tool or
  test a face without an archive.
- `client/scripts/World3D.gd`: `_ui_builder.apply_ui_theme(ui_control)` right after the builder.
- `client/scripts/ui/frontend_ui.gd`: the front-end's root is watched too (its own font sizes
  unchanged).
- `client/scripts/ui/hud/hud_chat.gd`: `ChatList` (the chat's and the system window's lines) is a
  text node; `ChatTab` draws its caption on a TextLayer over its tab art.
- `client/scripts/ui/hud/hud_notice.gd`: the banner's text on a TextLayer over its frame (the GM
  notice and the blue warning banner).

Weighed and dropped (MEASURED, oversampled): the linear filter as it was (60-70 % partial at 1.95,
33-43 % at 2.0); `snap_2d_vertices_to_pixel` and `snap_2d_transforms_to_pixel` on the root (no
change from the linear numbers -- 59-73 % at 1.95); NEAREST on the whole UI root (would switch the
art's filter too, which the user accepts as it is).

### 11. Review follow-up (round 672's review of d9708cd)

**H1, fixed: a dialog's nested Buttons kept Godot's default face.** `UiBuilder._watch_node` ran
from an ancestor's `child_entered_tree` and walked into descendants that had not entered the tree
yet, where a Button's theme font still resolved to Godot's default; `guard_button_font` pinned
that face as an override, and the Button's own visit later skipped it (the guard's meta). Every
HudPanels dialog is built off-tree and added in one go, so every dialog Button was hit -- buy,
sell, withdraw (-/+, the action, Cancel), the gold box (Deposit, Withdraw, Close), the revive
prompt, guild Create/Cancel, the buff-cancel OK/Cancel, the help window's X. Now `_watch_node`
handles a node only once it is inside the tree; a descendant still outside is handled when it
enters, from its parent's `child_entered_tree` (READ order in 4.2.2: a node enters, its parent
emits the signal, then its children enter). `watch_text` on a root not yet in the tree waits for
its `tree_entered`.

MEASURED at 1.95 with the reviewer's dialog probe (fresh start, 3840x2160), distinct colours
inside each control's content rect (4 units in from its edge):

| dialog control | d9708cd | fixed |
|---|---|---|
| buy '-' / '+' | 7 / 12 (godot-default+guard) | 2 / 2 (Arial+guard) |
| buy 'Buy' / 'Cancel' | 112 / 158 | 2 / 2 |
| revive's two Buttons | 237 / 233 | 2 / 2 |
| the Labels beside them | 2 | 2 |

All 25 dialog Buttons the probe builds now report `font=Arial+guard/12`.

New cases in `text_crispness_test.gd`: a PanelContainer > VBox > HBox dialog built off-tree with
two Buttons (text set before the add), one Button whose text is set after, and a Label, added in
one go; and a CheckBox and an OptionButton. On d9708cd:
`FAIL nested Button 'Buy' in a dialog added in one go draws in the client's face (got Godot's
default)`, the same for 'Cancel' and 'Withdraw', `FAIL a CheckBox keeps its icons' filter`,
`FAIL an OptionButton keeps its arrow's filter` (FAILURES 5). Fixed: ALL PASS.

**L4, fixed:** CheckBox, CheckButton and OptionButton are no longer text nodes for `crisp_text`
(they also draw theme icons -- the box, the switch, the arrow -- which keep their filter); their
text keeps the Button guard. None is under the UI root today.

**L2, fixed:** the debug panel's UI-scale slider applied the scale on every step of a drag, and
each application re-measures every Control (`_refresh_text`, 33 ms on the reviewer's 2,286-Control
tree, 40 ms frames while dragging). It now applies 0.15 s (OURS) after the slider's last change.

**Recorded:**

  its Markdown heading sizes, 26/22/19/17/16/15 px (`md_to_bbcode.gd`), are OURS, not retail's --

## Six-hundred-and-seventy-first round: the text tables in Rust -- the boot tables from 1,023 ms to 187 ms, the NPC tables in the entry's longest frame from 582 ms to 113 ms

The user (2026-10-01): "I'd actually like to start moving over the tasks you think are worth having
in rust so we can squeeze more performance out of this. Once that's done we can start looking into
caching and multi-threading." This round is the text-table lane of three (669 models, 670 terrain,
671 tables): the UTF-16 tables the client reads at boot and at entry, ported one to one into the
GDExtension. No caching, no threads, no API change. The module, its rules and the negative:
native/README.md, "The text tables". What is left: docs/TODO.md, "Native (Rust) readers".

Labels: MEASURED (render box, real archives at /opt/sro-files/client, perf_gate's `jangan` view --
97/168 at 1002,1020, loading screen forced, 1280x720 -- and its `mobs` view, the same spot with
OPENSRO_QA_MOBS=500), READ (Godot 4.2.2's source: core/string/ustring.cpp, ucaps.h,
variant_construct.h), INFERRED, OURS.

### 1. The profile, before porting (MEASURED)

parser, `text.items`, `text.shop_goods`, `text.teleport`, `text.skill_effects` -- and
`text.decode_split`, nested inside them: the FF FE strip, `get_string_from_utf16`,

the tables in GDScript; the Jangan run without another lane's Godot beside it (run 2), ms:

What it says:
- **The boot tables were all text tables.** 963 of the 1,023 ms are five readers over the seven
  characterdata parts and the seven itemdata parts; the two body `.bsr` parses are 34 ms.
- **The decode and the line split are the small part** (136 of the boot's 963 ms). The rest is
  per-row GDScript: `split("\t")` on every line, `strip_edges` and `is_valid_int` per field, and
  `_find_model_path` / `_find_name_key` / `_find_icon_path`, which strip, lower-case and test EVERY
  field of a 104- or 160-column row. Per phase and per reader: §5's table.
- **characterdata is read 21 times over:** four readers at boot, three at the centre cell, three
  at the first monster, one on the name-key task, each over the seven parts.
- **The entry's NPC tables sit in its longest frame.** The centre cell's `npcs [tables 582]` is
  part of the 1,678 ms frame 0.
- At the mobs site the first monster adds 1,087 ms of main-thread table parsing.

### 2. What was ported, and what was not

Ported, every reader over 20 ms an entry, one native function per GDScript function
(`native/src/core/tables.rs`, binding `native/src/gd_tables.rs`, class `SrNativeTables`; the
GDScript readers call it through `NativeAssets.table_rows`):
- NpcTableReader: `parse_positions`, `parse_codes`, `parse_models`, `parse_models_by_code`,
  `parse_org_codes`, `parse_speeds_by_code`, `parse_country_by_code`, `parse_bc_radius_by_code`,
  `parse_name_keys`, and `parse_names` / `parse_models_by_name` up to their `names.get_text`;
- `ItemTableReader.parse` up to `Item.new()`;
- `UiTextTable.parse` up to its keep-first insert;
- `SkillEffectReader.parse_all` up to its case folding and ANI_TYPES lookups.

Each returns ONE Dictionary of packed columns: the rows the GDScript loop keeps, in file order.
The GDScript then merges them into the caller's Dictionary in that order, so a later duplicate id
still overwrites an earlier one ("last wins", within a part and across parts) and UiTextTable's
"first wins" check runs as before. Objects (`Item`, `Spawn`, `Vector3`, `Vector2`) are still built
in GDScript: the readers' API is unchanged. So is every `to_lower`/`to_upper` whose result is kept:
a key like `parse_models_by_name`'s is formed by Godot's full-Unicode case tables (ucaps.h), and
is left to the engine that defines it rather than ported (OURS). Tests of a lower-cased value
against `.bsr`, `.ddj`, `.efp`, `xxx` and `none` are ported as ASCII case-insensitive compares,
which are exact: no code point outside ASCII lower-cases into ASCII in Godot 4.2.2 (MEASURED by
the review, over every code point). (This entry first said 4.2.2 lower-cases 'I' to U+0131. That
was wrong -- §8: the {0x0049, 0x0131} entry is commented out at ucaps.h:716.)

Godot's string rules are ported from the source (READ): `parse_utf16` (a second BOM after the FF
FE strip, FFFE byte-swapping, the stop at the first NUL unit), `strip_edges` (every code <= 32),
`split` (empty fields kept), `is_valid_int`, `to_int` (digits up to the first '.', other characters
skipped, a '-' while the value is 0 flips the sign, INT64 clamping), `is_valid_float`, and
`to_float`, which is `built_in_strtod` -- not a correctly rounded parse (18 mantissa digits,
powers of ten by squaring) and with a quirk: a dangling `e` returns the mantissa digits unscaled,
so `float("1.5e")` is 15.0. GDScript's `int(s)`/`float(s)` are `to_int()`/`to_float()`
(variant_construct.h, `VariantConstructorFromString`).

Handed back to GDScript (`{"fallback": why}`), so those inputs read exactly as before: an empty
UTF-16 decode (the readers then try UTF-8), an unpaired surrogate, a U+FEFF after the leading BOM
(added by the review, §8), a negative UI language column, and a float exponent that overflows the
C++ `int`. On a lone lead surrogate followed by another
character, Godot 4.2.2 itself is not deterministic: `parse_utf16` drops the lead but sizes the
string for it, so the last character is uninitialised memory (MEASURED: the first parity run
compared GDScript with GDScript on such files and got different rows from the same bytes, and the
log printed `Invalid unicode codepoint (6db3bc40)` for that character). None of the client's boot
or entry tables is handed back (§3).

Two implementation choices, both MEASURED on a synthetic 1.9 MB characterdata-shaped part (cargo,
release): decoding with an ASCII fast path writing UTF-8 bytes took 1.09 ms against 2.43 ms for
`char::decode_utf16`; and a byte scan for tabs took a reader from 2.94 to 1.75 ms against
`str::split('\t')`.

Not ported, each under 20 ms an entry (MEASURED above): `ShopReader.load` (18 ms with its six
reads), `TeleportReader.load` (4), `NpcServiceReader.parse_greetings` and `parse_shop_npcs` (under
1). The other text readers (skills, masteries, level data, world map, sound tables) are not on the
boot or entry path.

### 8. Review follow-up (round 671's review: one MEDIUM, two LOW)

The review found no HIGH. It held the ported string rules to Godot's own function bodies in a C++
harness (1,000,067 strings, 0 mismatches), fuzzed the readers (1.3M inputs, 0 panics) and
reproduced the gain (entry 10,186 -> 5,604 ms, freeze 3,463 -> 1,219).

**M1. A native string that began with U+FEFF lost it.** gdext 0.5.5 turns a Rust `&str` into a
Godot `String` through `string_new_with_utf8_chars_and_len`, which is `String::parse_utf8`, and that
skips a LEADING UTF-8 BOM (READ, ustring.cpp 4.2.2). The GDScript kept the character (`strip_edges`
leaves code points over 32). It shows when two UTF-16 files are run together and the second's BOM
starts a line. The decode now hands any U+FEFF after the leading one back to GDScript (it sits on
the non-ASCII path, so ASCII text pays nothing). No real table has one: the parity run hands back
the same 130 files as before, none for this reason. The new synthetic case `BOM mid-file`, against
d508562's library (MEASURED):

```
FAIL BOM mid-file: models agrees both ways
FAIL BOM mid-file: models_by_code agrees both ways
FAIL BOM mid-file: ui agrees both ways
FAIL BOM mid-file: ui last agrees both ways
FAIL a field that begins with U+FEFF keeps it ({"5":"mob\\a.bsr","6":"mob\\b.bsr"})
5 FAILURES
```

With the fix: ALL PASS. `cargo test` gained four decode/reader assertions for it.

**L1. A false READ.** §2 said Godot 4.2.2 lower-cases 'I' to U+0131. Its {0x0049, 0x0131} entry
is commented out (ucaps.h:716, `// { 0x0049, 0x0131 }, // dotless I`); the parse of ucaps.h that
produced the claim did not skip comments, and on the box `"I".to_lower()` is U+0069 (the review's
measurement). Behaviour was not affected: the folds whose results are kept stayed in GDScript for
that reason, and stay there now as a plain choice (OURS) -- a key formed by Godot's full-Unicode
case tables is left to the engine. The ASCII compares are exact for the reason the review
measured: no code point outside ASCII lower-cases into ASCII. Corrected in core/tables.rs,
native/README.md and §2.

**L2. The native suites under OPENSRO_NATIVE=0.** `native_tables_test.gd` decided "native" from
`library_usable()`, so with the library present and the switch off it called a null reader; round
667's `native_assets_test.gd` expected a native handle the same way. Both now ask whether the
readers are ON (`NativeAssets.new_tables() != null`; `library_usable() and available()`).

Re-run (MEASURED): `cargo test --no-default-features` 21 pass; `table_parity.gd` `TABLE PARITY
PASS`, 0 FAIL lines (680 files, 11,550 reader runs); the suites in all three modes -- with the
library, `OPENSRO_NATIVE=0` (the log says `forced off by OPENSRO_NATIVE=0`) and `NO_NATIVE=1` --
182 suites, 0 failing each; the Windows DLL still `stands alone, exports gdext_rust_init,
stripped`.

## Six-hundred-and-seventieth round: the terrain's lightmap loop in Rust, 28 ms a region down to 1.2; the `.m` and `.nvm` decodes ported and proven, but left off the load path because they gain nothing

The user (2026-10-01): "I'd actually like to start moving over the tasks you think are worth having
in rust so we can squeeze more performance out of this." This round is the terrain and navigation
lane. It covers `.m`, `.nvm`, the `.o2`/`.ifo` lists, and the terrain prepare's other loops. Rounds
669 (models) and 671 (text tables) ran beside it. The module: native/README.md, "The terrain
parsers". What is left: docs/TODO.md, "Native (Rust) readers".

Labels: MEASURED (the render box, real archives at /opt/sro-files/client, 1280x720, the loading
screen forced, `OPENSRO_PARSE_PROFILE=1`), READ (this repo), OURS.

### 1. Where the terrain time goes, ranked, native readers ON, before porting

Two profiling hooks were added for this (OURS, profiling only):
- every prepare lap (`_job_lap`) now also lands in the PARSEPROF table as `prep.terrain.*` /
  `prep.objects.*`;
- `MapmTerrainBuilder.lightmap_term` is timed as `mapm.lightmap_term`.

The 10-second `LoadTimings` summary now prints a PARSEPROF `window` table and resets it. At the
`cross` site the walk crosses into 97/167 during the loading drain, so its 30 cells (against
Jangan's 25) are all in the entry window.

The Jangan entry, round 667's build with the hooks (MEASURED, run p0; runs p1 and p2 within 3 %).
Times are main thread / workers in ms, with the call count for the workers:

| key | Jangan entry | cross entry | what it is | ported? |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `prep.terrain.mesh` | 90 / **2,878** (24) | 95 / 3,635 (29) | `build_full_region_surfaces_textured`: grid, normals, light, texture passes | no: geometry, not a parse (§4) |
| `mapm.lightmap_term` | 27 / **710** (24) | 28 / 863 (29) | a per-byte LUT loop over the `.t` lightmap's RGB8 bytes, 29.6 ms a region | **yes** |
| `mapm.parse` | 16 / 524 (24) | 17 / 633 (29) | 10,404 `Vertex` objects a region | ported, **not switched on** (§3) |
| `nvm.parse` | 12 / 460 (24) | 12 / 590 (29) | 9,216 `Tile` objects plus cells and edges | ported, **not switched on** (§3) |
| `prep.terrain.navgraph` | 18 / 188 | 18 / 199 | `NavGraph.build` over the parsed objects | no: not a parse |
| `prep.terrain.heights` | 2 / 89 | 3 / 109 | `TerrainCollision.heights_from_region`, reading `Vertex` objects | no: an object walk, not a byte loop (§4) |

| `prep.terrain.walls` | 0.1 / 9 | 0.2 / 19 | `NvmCollision` wall triangles | no: under the bar |
| `tile2d.parse` | 1.8 / 0 | 1.9 / 0 | `tile2d.ifo`, once | no: under the bar |

The bar is the brief's: under about 20 ms an entry is not ported.

### 2. What was built

- **`native/src/core/terrain.rs`** (plain Rust): `parse_mapm`, `parse_nvm` and `lightmap_add`.
  - They are one-to-one ports of `MapmReader._pp_parse`, `NvmReader._pp_parse` and
    `_parse_edges`, and of `lightmap_term`'s loop.
  - They make the same checks in the same order, with the same error messages.
  - Results are flat columns.
  - **Floats keep GDScript's bits.** `decode_float` widens a float32 to a 64-bit float, and the
    float32 fields narrow it back. On x86-64 that sets a signalling NaN's quiet bit, and
    `f32_gd` does the same.
  - No `unsafe`. Every offset is checked before it is read. Every allocation is fallible and
    clamped to what the remaining bytes could hold, so an `.nvm` declaring 4 billion cells is an
    error, not an allocation.
- **`native/src/gd_terrain.rs`**: the class `SrNativeTerrain`, with `mapm_parse`, `nvm_parse`
  (one Dictionary of packed arrays, or `{error}`) and `lightmap_add` (a PackedByteArray).
  `lib.rs` and `core/mod.rs` gained only their `mod` lines. **`API` is 3**, in both `core/mod.rs`
  and `NATIVE_API`.
- **`NativeAssets.terrain()`**: the shared instance, made under a mutex on the first call,
  because the first call may come from two terrain tasks at once.
- **`MapmTerrainBuilder.lightmap_term`** hands its loop to `lightmap_add` when the readers are
  on. It falls back to the GDScript loop on an empty answer.
- **`MapmReader.parse_native` / `NvmReader.parse_native`**: the native decode, then the reader's
  own `ParsedRegion` built from the columns (`_from_native`). They are **not called by `parse()`**
  (§3).

### 3. The `.m` and `.nvm` ports gain nothing while the readers keep their objects (MEASURED)

`_bench670.gd` (scratch, not committed) parsed the 25 Jangan-window regions three times each way.
All three repeats agreed within 0.3 ms:

| per file | GDScript `parse()` | native decode (the call) | building the objects from the columns |
|---|---|---|---|
| `.m` | 12.7-13.0 ms | **0.10 ms** | 12.9-13.2 ms |
| `.nvm` | 13.0-13.1 ms | **0.14 ms** | 11.7 ms |

The Rust decode is about 100 times faster than the GDScript one. But the GDScript parse's cost is
not the decode: it is the `Vertex`, `Tile`, `Cell` and `Edge` objects, plus a sliced `extra`
for every vertex. Built from packed columns, they cost the same.

The parity runs' interleaved timing (§5) put the native path behind:
- `.m`: 10.2 / 10.6 ms against 8.0 / 8.2 ms;
- `.nvm`: 9.8 / 11.5 ms against 9.0 / 9.3 ms.

So `parse()` stays in GDScript.

The port is kept, proven on every real file, as `parse_native`. It is the decode the next step
needs: keep the columns on `ParsedRegion` and move its readers onto them (docs/TODO.md, an API
change this round's brief left out). At stake: 524 + 460 + 89 ms of worker time a Jangan entry,
plus whatever the mesh build saves from reading packed arrays instead of `[height, extra]`
pairs.

### 4. The prepare's other loops

The brief asked whether the prepare's height, normal and lightmap loops are parse-like byte
loops.
- **The lightmap term is one**: a LUT over every byte of a 512x512 RGB8 image (262,144 pixels a term: 5,446,303,744 / 20,776 in §5; docs/protocol/MAPM_FORMAT.md). It is ported.
- **The height grid is not.** `heights_from_region` walks `Vertex` objects, so it moves with §3's
  column step.
- **The mesh is not.** It is geometry and lighting in float32 vectors and colours: normals,
  per-vertex light, the texture passes. At 2.9 s of worker time a Jangan entry it is the largest
  item in the terrain prepare, and it has its own TODO entry.

### 5. Parity on the real archives (MEASURED)

`client/tools/native_parity_terrain.gd` (new) compares the two paths on every file of each type.
Floats are compared by bit pattern: 64-bit for the readers' `float` fields, packed float32 for
vectors, heights and planes.

| type | files | compared | truncations refused both ways | mismatches | GDScript / native |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `.m` (Map.pk2) | **4,719** (0 refused) | 49,096,476 vertices: height bits and extra bytes; every block's 7 fields | 564 | **0** | 8.0 / 10.2 ms a file |
| `.nvm` (Data.pk2) | **6,543** (101 refused by both) | 50,580 objects, 2,769 linked edges, 1,700,356 cells, 3,745,298 edges, 59,369,472 tiles, every height and plane | 744 | **0** | 9.0 / 9.8 ms a file |

## Six-hundred-and-sixty-ninth round: the mesh, animation and skeleton readers in Rust -- the Jangan entry 1.0 s shorter and its longest freeze 0.3 s shorter than round 667's native build, a 500-monster entry 1.1 s shorter

The user asked (2026-10-01) to move into Rust the work that is worth having there, before any
caching or multi-threading. This round is the model lane: `.bms` first, then whichever of the
other model formats measured significant. The ports are one to one: the GDScript readers stay,
and they stay the reference. Build, API and safety rules: native/README.md, "The model readers".
What is left: docs/TODO.md, "Native (Rust) readers".

Labels: MEASURED (render box, real archives at /opt/sro-files/client, 1280x720, loading screen
forced, Jangan spawn 97/168 at 1002,1020), READ (the GDScript readers, Godot 4.2.2), INFERRED,
OURS.

### 1. The profile, ranked, before porting (MEASURED)

`OPENSRO_PARSE_PROFILE=1` on dev 520c44e, native readers ON (round 667's pk2 and ddj). A new
window, `after the entry`, reports at exit whatever loaded after the entry (World3D `_exit_tree`),
so a species or character met for the first time would show there. At both sites it held only a
few file reads: the mobs site's 24 species are all assembled during the entry drain (their
templates on WorkerThreadPool tasks, round 661), so the entry window is where first sight costs.

Model readers in the entry window, ms main thread / workers (calls), run 1 of the first profile:

| key | Jangan | mobs (500 monsters, 24 species) |
|---|---|---|
| `bms.parse` | 328 / 682 (330 / 652) | **341 / 1,723** (330 / 691) |
| `bms.to_arrays` | 58 / 66 | 59 / **308** |
| `ban.parse` | 53 / 15 (56 / 22) | 59 / **248** (56 / 36) |
| `bsr.parse` | 34 / 26 (90 / 200) | 34 / 79 (90 / 213) |
| `bms.parse_collision` | 6 / 38 | 6 / 43 |
| `bsk.parse` | 23 / 2 (55 / 22) | 24 / 18 (55 / 36) |
| `bmt.parse` | 4 / 16 | 4 / 22 |
| `cpd.parse` | 0.1 / 0.1 | 0.1 / 0.1 |

Before the entry, `bsr.parse` also takes 34 ms on the main thread for 2 calls (the player's own
models). No `inflate` call ran at either site: every `.bmt` read was uncompressed.

What it says:
- `bms.parse` is three quarters of the model time, and the monsters triple its worker share.
  The GDScript parse builds one `Vertex` object per vertex and slices 4 bytes for every float.
  `to_arrays` then copies the objects back into packed arrays.
- `ban.parse` is a quarter of a second of worker time at the mobs site (36 calls): monster clips
  are long.
- `bsk.parse` is 24 ms on the main thread: its name check is a per-byte GDScript loop.
- **Ported:** `.bms` (parse and `to_arrays`), `.ban`, `.bsk`.
- **Not ported:** `bsr.parse` (see §5), `parse_collision` (6 ms main) and `bmt.parse` (4 ms
  main), both under the round's ~20 ms bar on the main thread.

### 2. What was built (OURS)

- **`native/src/core/bms.rs`, `ban.rs`, `bsk.rs`**: plain Rust, no Godot types, each a line-by-line
  port of `BmsReader.parse` (with `_detect_vertex_rec_size`, `_parse_skin`, `_parse_vertex_motion`
  and `_parse_vertex_links`), `BanReader.parse` and `BskReader.parse`. Integer arithmetic is i64,
  as GDScript's `int`.
- **`native/src/gd_models.rs`**: the binding, one new class `SrNativeModels` with `bms_parse`,
  `bms_wound_indices`, `bms_skin_arrays`, `ban_parse` and `bsk_parse`. Each returns one
  Dictionary of packed arrays, or `{error}`. `lib.rs` and `core/mod.rs` gained only `mod` lines;
  `gd.rs` is untouched. `API` is 3, and `NATIVE_API` 3: an API 2 library is refused.
- **`NativeAssets.models()`**: the accessor, beside the others in native_assets.gd. It makes the
  object once, under a mutex, since the readers run on worker tasks too.
- **The readers.** Each `parse` asks the native reader first. On `{error}` it runs its own
  GDScript, which reports as it always has.
  - `{error}` is returned exactly where GDScript returns null (READ, every branch). It is also
    returned for the one input whose GDScript answer depends on Godot's negative indexing: a
    `.bms` header pointer at or above 2^31, which `PackedInt32Array` makes negative. So **no
    input gets a different answer natively**; at worst it gets the GDScript one.
  - **Bit patterns.** GDScript reads a float as f32 -> f64 (`decode_float`) -> f32 (`Vector3`,
    `PackedFloat32Array`), which quiets a signalling NaN. `gd_f32` does the same. Strings are
    `get_string_from_ascii`'s: up to the first NUL, each byte a Latin-1 code point.
  - **The partial skin.** `_parse_skin` returns early on a bad bone index, leaving the vertices
    before it skinned and the palette empty. The port keeps that exactly. 0 real files do it
    (§3), but a synthetic one does (§4).
- **`ParsedMesh.vertices` became a property.** A natively parsed mesh keeps its vertices as
  packed arrays. The getter builds the same `Vertex` objects on first access. `to_arrays` reads
  the arrays directly (the winding and skin loops are native too), and so do two new methods,
  `vertex_count()` and `positions()`.
  - The callers that only counted or summed vertices now use those methods:
    `SkinnedBsrAssembler._nearest_bone`/`_centroid` (every monster piece) and the three effect
    loaders' empty check. Each gives the same answer: the same sum, in the same order.
  - `CharacterAssembler._build_side_mesh` still builds the objects.
  - The GDScript `to_arrays` reads `mesh.vertices` once instead of per vertex, so the getter
    costs the fallback nothing.
- **`.ban` keyframes stay objects.** The native parse is flat, and `BanReader` builds the same
  `Bone`/`Keyframe` objects from it, with no byte slicing. A lazy getter there would be called on
  every frame by `MonsterCrowd` and `Skeleton3DBuilder`, which read `track.keyframes` per bone.
- **`.bsk`**: the same walk (announcement, resolution, Type A/B, the one-byte gap), returned as
  name and parent arrays plus one transform buffer that `BskReader` slices per bone.
- **Safety.** No `unsafe` beyond round 667's ExtensionLibrary impl. Every read goes through
  bounds-checked i64 offsets (`Bytes`), and an out-of-range read is an `Err`, never a panic.
  Allocations are fallible (`try_reserve`) and sized only after the data is shown to hold them:
  a `.bms` claiming 4 billion vertices, or a `.ban` with 4 billion bones or keys, is refused
  without allocating. Cargo tests feed every truncation and 3,000 randomly corrupted copies of
  each synthetic file.

### 3. Parity on every real file (MEASURED)

`client/tools/native_parity_models.gd` (new) parses every `.bms`, `.ban` and `.bsk` of the four
archives both ways in one process and compares them with `ModelCompare`
(client/scripts/bms/model_compare.gd):
- every field;
- every vertex's position, normal, uv (as bit patterns, via `var_to_bytes`), extra bytes, bones
  and f64 weights;
- every index, motion, link and order value; the bounds;
- every keyframe's quaternion and position; every bone record's bytes, name and parent;
- `vertex_count()`, `positions()`, and the whole `to_arrays` surface: the native one taken
  before the mesh builds its vertices, against the GDScript one, byte for byte.

| | files | parsed | null both ways (native `{error}`, then GDScript) | compared |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `.bms` (Data 24,984, Particles 268) | 25,252 | 24,820 | 432 | 12,824,385 vertices, 10,837,084 triangles; 6,654 skinned; 6,196 at 52 bytes a vertex; 801 with motion and links |
| `.ban` (Data 5,130, Particles 105) | 5,235 | 5,232 | 3 | 283,994 bones, 9,709,358 keyframes |
| `.bsk` (Data 1,250, Particles 1) | 1,251 | 1,232 | 19 | 33,195 bones, 483 of them parent-less (92-byte) records |

Map.pk2 and Media.pk2 hold none of the three. Result: **`PARITY PASS`, 0 mismatches.** The native
reader never answered `{error}` for a file GDScript parsed ("0 of them parsed there", every
archive). No real `.bms` has a skin refused part-way.

In the same pass, the readers' own time over every file (GDScript / native, the native including
the GDScript that builds the result objects): `.bms` 58,061 / 3,998 ms, `.ban` 19,435 / 8,739 ms
(the `Keyframe` objects are most of what is left), `.bsk` 407 / 57 ms.

**12 real `.bms` files make the GDScript reader stop on a script error** rather than return null
(MEASURED: 24 `Out of bounds get index '0' (on base: 'Array')`, two GDScript parses a file). Its
`_read_len_prefixed_string` answers `[]` where the callers test for `null`. The native reader
returns `{error}` for them, so GDScript fails as before. This round changes no GDScript answer;
the bug is in docs/TODO.md.

## Six-hundred-and-sixty-eighth round: the release ships the native readers in both zips, and the auto-updater replaces a DLL the running game has loaded

The user (2026-09-30): "Build and ship the DLL. Make sure the Game auto update feature grabs it
but I'm sure it does just fine. I'll add the SRREVAMP folder as an AV exclusion and test it. I'll
also rename the DLL extension to test the fallback too." Round 667's library now ships. The
updater did not "do just fine": it would have taken a loaded DLL only after robocopy's 30-second
retry, it hung for ever on a file antivirus would not release, and its Linux copy never ran the
command it was written with. The DLL and the updater are covered below.

### 3. The auto-updater, read before changing it

What it did (READ, `client/scripts/update/auto_updater.gd` at d7b4aba):
- **What it downloads:** the whole platform zip, the release's `opensro-<os>.zip` (lines 76-95).
- **Where it extracts:** in-process, into `opensro_update_staging` next to the executable
  (lines 129-148).
- **How it replaces the running exe:** it writes a helper script, starts it, and quits
  (lines 159-170). On Windows the script ran `timeout /t 2`, then
  `robocopy "<staging>" "<install>" /E /XD pk2`, then relaunched (lines 180-188). On Linux it ran
  `sleep 2`, then `cp -r <staging>/. <install>/ --exclude=pk2`, and fell back to
  `find … -exec cp -r` (lines 194-202).
- **Deleting files the new version lacks:** never.
- **Verifying the download:** HTTP 200 and the zip opening, nothing more.

What was wrong with that:
- **`timeout` does not wait.** Godot starts the helper with `CREATE_NO_WINDOW`
  (`os_windows.cpp:847`, READ), and `timeout` needs a console. That it returns at once is
  INFERRED, not seen. robocopy then met the exe and the DLL still locked by the quitting game.
- **robocopy's default retry is 30 s x 1,000,000.** A locked DLL was taken only after a
  30-second wait. A file antivirus never released held the copy, and the relaunch behind it, for
  ever.
- **GNU cp has no `--exclude`.** The first command always failed, and the `find` fallback copied
  over files in place after a fixed `sleep 2`.
- **One staged file failing to write aborted the whole update.** That is exactly what antivirus
  quarantining the new DLL does.
- **The release lists a SHA-256 for each asset that nothing checked.** v0.1.464's two assets
  carry `"digest": "sha256:…"` (MEASURED, `gh api …/releases/latest`).

What it does now (OURS): `client/scripts/update/update_installer.gd`, `update_fs.gd` and
`auto_updater.gd`.
- **The SHA-256 check.** The download is checked against the asset's digest
  (`UpdateChecker.find_asset_digest` / `digest_problem`). A mismatch deletes the zip and reports
  the update as failed. A release without a digest is logged as `NOT verified`.
- **The install runs inside the running game, by moving files aside.** For each file it renames
  the current one to `<name>.old-update`, then renames the new one into place. Windows refuses to
  overwrite or delete a running exe or a loaded DLL but allows the rename, because the loader
  holds the file with FILE_SHARE_DELETE (INFERRED from Windows' documented sharing rules; not run
  on Windows). On Linux a rename gives the new file a new inode.
- **Every step is bounded.** A rename or copy is retried 5 times, 200 ms apart, so no step waits
  more than 1 s.
- **The executable and the `.pck` are critical.** If either cannot be installed, every file
  installed so far is put back, and the game carries on with the old version.
- **Any other file failing, the DLL included, is logged.** Its previous version is restored, the
  update continues, and the client falls back to GDScript if it cannot use the old library.
- **Moved-aside files are deleted at once where possible.** The rest are listed in
  `opensro_update_cleanup.txt` and deleted at the next start.
- **The pk2 folder is never touched, and no file is ever deleted** that the new version lacks.
- **The relaunch waits for the old process.** It polls the old PID: `kill -0` on Linux, a batch
  file using `tasklist` and `ping` on Windows (no `timeout`), for at most 60 polls. Then it starts
  the new executable, so the two never write the same log. If the relaunch fails, the files are
  already installed.
- **The summary reaches the new log.** The old process writes `opensro_update.log`. The new one
  prints it as `OpenSRO update (last run): …` and removes it.
- **Only an exported build updates itself.** A run from source would have installed a release
  zip over the Godot editor's folder.
- **QA hooks** (OURS): `OPENSRO_QA_UPDATE_URL` (another "latest release" endpoint),
  `OPENSRO_QA_UPDATE_ACCEPT=1` (no dialog) and `OPENSRO_QA_QUIT_AT_LOGIN=1`.

**A stale library beside a newer client, for real** (`/var/tmp/ship668/stale_test.sh`,

So on Linux the library is replaced while the old process has it loaded: the install runs inside
that process. The renamed-DLL fallback test restores the library. Windows' locking is not part of
this run.

### 5. Windows' locks, simulated

`client/scripts/update/update_installer_test.gd` (62 checks) runs UpdateInstaller against a
FakeFs with these Windows rules:
- a running exe or a loaded DLL can be renamed, but not overwritten or deleted, and the lock moves
  with the file;
- a file open without FILE_SHARE_DELETE cannot be renamed;
- `busy:N` refuses N renames (antivirus scanning);
- quarantined content is removed by antivirus the first time it is moved or copied;
- `DirAccess.rename` deletes an existing target first (`dir_access_windows.cpp:301-305`, READ).

The cases:
1. The exe running and the DLL loaded. Everything installs, the two originals wait for the next
   start, and the next start deletes them.
2. The fallback test: the DLL renamed `.off`.
3. The new DLL removed from staging. The rest installs and the old DLL stays.
4. The new DLL quarantined while being moved into place. The old DLL comes back under its name.
5. The `.pck` held open. Everything is rolled back, at a cost of at most 1,000 ms of retries.
6. The new exe blocked. Everything is rolled back, and the running exe is back under its name.
7. A transient lock, taken after two 200 ms waits.
8. An earlier `.old-update` still locked, so the next free name is used.
9. Linux rules: no leftovers, and the exe stays executable.
10. Both relaunch scripts: the PID is polled, there is no `timeout`, no robocopy and no
    `--exclude`, and the path is passed as a parameter.
11. The digest checks.
12. A real-filesystem install on the box.

What this does NOT prove: that real Windows behaves like FakeFs. The rules are INFERRED.

### 6. The log lines (item 5 of the brief)

`Boot._ready` now calls `NativeAssets.available()` right after `OpenSRO version: …`, so exactly
one line is printed at startup:
- ON: `native readers ON (library loaded, <version>, <path>)`.
- OFF: `library not found: <path>`, `library failed to load: <path> is there but…`, or `forced
  off by OPENSRO_NATIVE=0`.

The OFF lines all end `-- using the GDScript readers`. The Ctrl+F3 debug panel's `== build` block
shows the same line. `client/scripts/pk2/native_status_test.gd` holds every form, and
docs/NATIVE_ON_WINDOWS.md quotes them for the user's test.

**The version check (item 6 of the brief) is round 667's follow-up** (d836348, merged here as a
fast-forward). It adds `API = 2` in `native/src/core/mod.rs`, exposed as `api()`, and
`NativeAssets.NATIVE_API`. A library speaking any other number, or one without `api()`, is
refused before anything calls it. Round 668 folds that refusal into the same startup line:

```
NativeAssets: native readers OFF (library REFUSED: API 0, this client needs API 2 -- a stale library, rebuild it with native/build.sh) -- using the GDScript readers
```

That line covers the partial update: a DLL the installer could not replace (`NOT installed
opensro_native.dll: … kept the previous one`) sits beside a newer exe. It is refused if its
interface differs and used if it does not; the number changes only with the interface.

### 9. Review follow-up (round 668's review of 41e0d85)

The review ran v0.1.464's own updater against this release on Linux, for real, with the actual
v0.1.464 binary. Every file arrived byte for byte, and the relaunch logged native ON. It also
confirmed the move-aside rules, the rollback order, the digest check failing open and the
tag-only steps. What it found, and what changed:

- **H1: a disk filling during staging installed truncated files** (CONFIRMED by the review on a
  120 MB tmpfs). Every file logged "installed", the exe was 30.7 of 62.2 MB, three files were 0
  bytes, and the next start crashed (exit 139). The cause (READ, Godot 4.2.2):
  `FileAccess.store_buffer` returns nothing on a short write, and `ZIPReader.read_file` returns
  an empty array on a CRC or IO error (zip_reader.cpp:98-124).

  New `client/scripts/update/update_stager.gd` unpacks before anything in the install is touched.
  It checks, in order:
  1. the zip's own central directory is read for every entry's size (ZIPReader exposes none);
  2. free space must cover the unpacked total plus 32 MB (OURS);
  3. every entry must come out of the archive at that size;
  4. every staged file is read back at its full length.

  A failure removes the staging folder, and the update reports `could not unpack …, nothing was
  changed`. The installer's copy fallback reads its length back too. Real runs on the box, with
  a 120 MB tmpfs as root and the client as ghidra (`full_test.sh`, MEASURED):

| run | outcome |
|---|---|
| **41e0d85**, the 41e0d85 export on the tmpfs (67 MB used, 54 MB free before the download) | all four files logged "installed"; afterwards `OpenSRO.x86_64` was 30,728,192 bytes, and the `.pck`, the `.so` and the notices were 0 bytes; the next start exited 139 (a segfault) -- the review's finding, reproduced |
| follow-up, as it ships | `SRRevamp update: refused: not enough disk space next to the game: the update needs 66.8 MB (plus 32 MB to spare), 29.3 MB is free`, then `update failed (could not unpack v0.0.1, nothing was changed (…))`; install **byte-identical** (sha256 of every file before and after); the next start exits 0 with `native readers ON` |
| follow-up, free-space check skipped (`SRREVAMP_QA_UPDATE_IGNORE_SPACE=1`, OURS) | `refused: could not write srrevamp-linux/srrevamp.x86_64 whole into the staging folder (disk full?)`; install **byte-identical**; the next start exits 0 |

- **M1:** ci.yml's check `grep -q "NativeAssets: native readers ON"` could not fail, because
  `native_status_test.gd` prints indented sample lines holding those words. It is anchored now
  (`'^NativeAssets: native readers ON'`). On the box (MEASURED):
  - with the library, both the old and the anchored grep pass;
  - with `NO_NATIVE=1`, the old grep still passes, while the anchored one fails (exit 1).
- **M2 / L3: the relaunch batch file holds no install path.** cmd.exe reads a batch file in the
  OEM code page, so `C:\Users\José\…` written as UTF-8 was mangled. Every path in the file is
  now relative to `%~dp0`, and the file is plain ASCII. cmd is started as `cmd /D /S /C
  "<path>"`, with the path in its own quotes. Godot quotes an argument only when it has a space
  or one of `& ( ) [ ] { } ^ = ; ! ' + , `` ` `` ~` (os_windows.cpp:656-663, READ). `/S` makes
  cmd strip exactly the outer pair, so a path holding `&` or `(` reaches it intact. INFERRED from
  cmd's documented /S rule; not run on Windows.
- **PRE-EXISTING, found by the review:** v0.1.464's own batch file has the same code-page
  problem. An install under a non-ASCII path probably never auto-updated, and will not get this
  release automatically (docs/NATIVE_ON_WINDOWS.md says to copy it once by hand).
- **L1:** putting a moved-aside original back is retried like every other step. A failure is
  logged as `COULD NOT PUT BACK <name>: the previous version is still at <path> …`.
- **L2:** the next start finds leftovers by name (`*.old-update[-N]`, pk2/ aside) instead of from
  a list a killed run never wrote. Where the original is missing, it puts the newest aside back.
  A missing exe or `.pck` stops the game from starting at all, so the docs give the hand repair.
- **L4:** the relaunch poll matches the quoted PID (`find """<pid>"""`), not any comma.
- **L8:** docs/NATIVE_ON_WINDOWS.md now says that the first update to this release is installed
  by v0.1.464's robocopy batch file. It shows none of the new lines, and is INFERRED to take up
  to ~30 s to come back. The new lines start with the update after that.
- **L9:** THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.txt carries the full licence texts:
  - every crate's, from cargo-about 0.9.2, pinned and SHA-256 checked;
  - the Rust standard library's COPYRIGHT and licences, in `native/licenses/`, from
    rust-lang/rust 1.98.1;
  - Godot Engine's own licence and every third-party notice built into it, read from the engine
    by `client/tools/print_godot_licenses.gd`.

  `check_release_zip.sh` fails a zip that lacks any of them. The file is about 120 KB.
- **L5, L6, L10:** recorded in docs/TODO.md, unchanged.

- **Each fix undone on its own** in a copy of the follow-up tree (`/var/tmp/ship668/mut668.py`),

The first pass of these mutations caught two test gaps:
