  round 241), and the field world is `INS_DEFAULT`, id 1: **none of them hatches in the field**, so
  all 90 temple rows (the SD elites and bosses) are left out. MOB_SD_APIS has no nest of its own in
  the DB -- its spot's only nest is the shard's DEADWARRIOR at cap 0 -- so it is not placed on a
  stand-in either. Rank 8 is never announced: both notice gates are `cmp al,3` (0x5f71d4 spawn,
  0x4c1ccb kill). So rank 8 is NOT placed "the same way as rarity 3", by the READ world rule and the
  data; the coordinator's note assumed field nests they do not have.
- **The selector**: `BindSkillsAndRanges` chooses Summon_A / B / C by TacticsID immediates
  (0x53f7bd..0x53f8cf); the shard's seven unique tactics ids are exactly seven of them. Summon_A
  files a summon skill by AI_AttackChance into four slots (0x562060), Summon_B lists them (0x562470);
  a skill with a `_RefAISkill` row is a trigger in every selector.
- **The summon's timing -- a correction to the brief.** Both PickSkills (0x5621b0, 0x562570) summon
  when the damage taken since the last summon (`ctx+0xb0`) reaches 10 % of MaxHP (float 10.0 at
  0xb45b44), picking the skill by the HP bucket (0x541d70: 0.2/0.4/0.6/0.8); slot 6 (0x562540)
  zeroes `ctx+0xb0` when an `ssou` skill is used. So a unique summons about nine times a kill, the
  bucket choosing which wave -- not once at each of 0.8/0.6/0.4/0.2. Summon_B throws `rand() % 1000
  < 500` for its R1/R2 set.
- **The executor** (0x596e50): tuples `{id, class nibble, min, max}` after the `ssou` word (the
  parser stores that cursor at +0x354 and returns, 0x5890cb..0x5890e5); per tuple a radius die, then
  `n = min + abs(rand()) % (max-min+1)`, over 50 logged and set to 50, under 1 nothing; each minion
  from the spawn routine at exactly unique BC + 30 + minion BC (the ring's radius is at most 2 pi,
  under the minimum), its own angle, the world's class clamp (0x5f6eb0 calls the world's slot 6),
  then command 0xb binding it to the unique (`CAIState` slot 14, 0x5591b0: `ctx+0x14c` = the
  unique, IDLE).
- **Minions are not cleaned up.** The executor keeps no list, and the unbinding command 0xc
  (slot 15, 0x559260) has one sender, the pet path (0x4d2109): two probes with different failure
  modes (the decompile's `0x1c))(0xc,` and an asm scan for `push 0xc` before a register call through
  `[..+0x1c]`; the second found 0x4d2109 and 0x440679, the latter a `+0x500` call, not a command).

  490 -> 1,367 ms (her 877 ms on a WorkerThreadPool task), her body built in 1.5 ms, and the window's
  summary `longest work frame 8 ms ... 0 over 100 ms; longest wall gap 26 ms`. A client that has
  met her already (r2, r1) built the respawn's body in 0.9 ms either way.

**The client change** (`MonsterDraw.Templates.request/poll`, `World3D._build_monster_body`): a
species' first body no longer assembles its model on the main thread; the model is assembled on a
WorkerThreadPool task (the Pk2 reader is locked since round 565; the object prepare already builds
meshes and materials off the main thread) and the monster waits for it, its snapshot kept; the pump
queues the waiters when the task finishes. `OPENSRO_SYNC_LOAD=1` keeps the old path, as do round
655's tests with their own assembler. This is every species' first body, not only a unique's.

## Six-hundred-and-sixtieth round: every field monster of the game stands in its nest, comes back on the nest's own timer, is aggressive or passive and gives up as its data says, and hatches champions, giants and party monsters

The user (2026-09-30): "Please add all monsters to the map like the original server would have it.
Make sure they can walk around like the original game and respect if they're 'aggro' or not. Also
make sure you add all the monster types like champion, giant, party, etc. ... Make sure monsters
respawn after awhile and also make sure the monsters follow for a certain distance like the
original game." The reading is `docs/protocol/monster_ai.md`, "Nests on the map (round 660)"; the
operator's side is `deploy/README.md`, "The full map (round 660)".

Labels: READ (SR_GameServer.exe / sro_client.exe), MEASURED, INFERRED, OURS, and EXTERNAL for every
number that comes from the user's shard DB (the "Eternity" backup, round 658). No DB row, CSV or
game data is in this commit; the tests use synthetic rows.

### 1. What shipped (MEASURED at boot on the render box, npcpos + characterdata of our archive, the shard's three tables)

`-full-map` (off by default) makes every field monster row of npcpos a nest (`server/internal/nest`,
`server/cmd/server/nest.go`), run by one scheduler goroutine (round 656's, now the nest scheduler):

| | rows |
|---|---|
| npcpos rows | 12,367 (257 not monsters) |
| dungeon monster rows (region >= 0x8000), not placed | 1,915 |
| uniques (rarity 3), not placed -- round 661 | 71 |
| custom species (ETERNITY / ANTHEIA / `_STR`) in npcpos | 0 (the guard is there) |
| **placed nests** | **10,124** |
| matched: the spot's shard nest hatches the npcpos species -- its numbers and tactics (EXTERNAL) | 4,082 |
| swapped, the species' own tactics row, stand-in nest | 2,346 |
| swapped, no tactics row left, stand-in nest and behaviour | 3,696 |
| matched nests with cap 0 (hatch nothing, in the shard too) | 132 |
| shard field nests (world 1, monster species) no row reaches -- never placed | 3,245 |

The swaps: MOB_ETERNITY_DEADWARRIOR 62584 at 4,734 spots, the SD swaps 38244/38191/38219/38223 at
511/348/290/159. **The join tolerance** (OURS): every placed row's nest stands within 0.00014 units of it.
(CORRECTED by the review, §9: this said "the nearest OTHER nest to any placed row 2.10 units off",
from a probe that only measured beyond the tolerance and so could not fail. Other nests do stand
inside it -- co-located nests at 0.000, two at 0.713 -- and the join now keeps one row per nest.) Of the matched rows 2,505 run an aggressive tactics row and 1,577 a passive one; with the
swapped rows' own rows, 4,718 aggressive, 1,710 passive, 3,696 stand-in. 2,552 nests can roll a
champion (a champion row and a chance above 0). 10 shard hives among the matched nests carry a
total cap (80-130) and run the capped pass. The most monsters alive at once: **34,678** (the
matched nests' caps, 28,636, plus one a swapped spot).

Without `-nest-db-dir` every row is a stand-in nest: one monster, 10 s at both ends of its window,
no scatter, the stand-in behaviour (all aggressive, sight 100, give-up 400, roam 200; OURS), no
champion roll -- and the boot log says so.

### 2. What was READ this round

- **Aggression: `btAggressType` 0 is aggressive, 1 passive.** `AI::CTactics::Init` 0x53f4d0 copies
  `row+0x18` to ctx+0x168 (mode 2: `pct <= rand() % 100` makes it 1) and `AITactics_AcquireTarget`
  0x5478f0 scans only while that byte is 0 or 3. This is round 552's recorded reading; **the round's
  brief read the DB the other way round ("aggressive (mode 1)"), and the code settles it.** The
  data agrees with play: Jangan's Mangyang nests run a passive row whose champion row is aggressive,
  and across the map a species' row is aggressive where its `_CLON`'s is passive (MEASURED on the
  matched nests, round 660's census). A passive monster still fights back: `CAIState::OnAttacked`
  0x558ea0 engages on any blow.
- **The hatch spot** (`nest.HatchOffset`): Nest_Hatch pushes col 10 `nGenerateRadius` (`fild
  [esi+0x24]` 0x560c51) into the spawn routine 0x5f6eb0, whose first call is 0x531240: 70 of 101
  hatches land in the outer third of the circle, 20 in the middle, 11 in the inner (constants 1e-6,
  3.0, 32767.0, float32 2pi, 0.0 read with objdump). The monster's home stays the nest's position.
- **The field world clamps the class by level** (`nest.ClampClassByLevel`; `CGameWorld_Default`
  slot 6 0x5eb9a0, asm 0x5eb9f3..0x5eba7e, jump table 0x5ebf14 read back): no giant at level 10 or
  below (it becomes a champion), no party monster below 10, and the party flag only on the ranks
  each ten-level band allows.
- **The party roll's species test** `FUN_00561020`: TypeID (1,2,1,4) never hatches a party monster
  (17 of the 249 field species).
- **The capped pass**: `AIHive::Init` 0x55e5b0 sets hive+0x30 when `dwOverwriteMaxTotalCount` is
  non-zero (0x55e73d), and such a hive runs `AIHive_HatchPass_TotalCapped` 0x55ec10: the pinned nest
  alone or each nest in turn, timer and alive-cap tests only, until the hive's cap.
- **The client** (a read-only lookup in sro_client.exe): the class scales the model (`fld1`
  0x9d38c9; switch 0x9d3995, table 0x9d3c70): champion 1.5, giant 3.0, elite 1.7. The overhead
  name's colour does not change with the class. A party monster draws
  `icon\item\etc\europe_partymob.ddj` 16 x 16, 20 px left of its name (vslot 15 0x9d3e70, test at
  0x9d3f2a), and its target window's rank row gets UIIT_STT_PARTYMOB_TARGET's "(Party)" appended with
  no separator (0x69b834). The wire is one byte, `rank | party << 4` (vslot_025 0x9d3850).

### 3. What was built

- `server/internal/nest`: the three CSV loaders (by the DB's column names, the smallints as u16,
  NULL y), the join, the READ rules with scripted dice (window, halving, offset, class roll, clamp),
  the scheduler (the plain and the capped pass, the first-loss timer, the party arming with a
  two-pass graveyard so a kill arms a nest the pass already buried) and the hive model round 661
  builds the unique rotation on (`Hive{TotalCap, Pinned}`).
- `combat.Hub`: `SpawnHatched` (the nest's home, the party flag at x10 HP, the tactics) and a death
  log the scheduler drains, so it learns of a loss without polling 34,000 monsters.
- The brain (`session/monsterai.go`) runs the monster's own row where it has one: sight (col 6),
  aggression (7/8), chase switch and give-up (35/36), roam rule (37) and the nest's radius, reach
  rule (40, `ai.TargetOutOfReach`), the scan's fast bits (42); the stand-ins, OURS, elsewhere.
- The kill's party count (`session/nestkill.go`): the killer's party members alive, in the zone and
  within 1000 units of the dead monster (READ range; the reference point INFERRED) arm its nest.
- The wire: the party flag in bit 8 of the list record's rarity word (OURS), in the list, the spawn
  push and the area of interest's enter, only for a session whose list request sets bit 1 of the
  capability byte (0x02). **An older client** is sent the rank alone and draws every rank at its
  species' size; it still needs round 656's paged list for windows this dense (the densest holds
  1,516 monsters with every nest full; an unpaged client gets the ~480 nearest).
- The client: the class scale (label, collider and cull radius grown with it), the party mark
  beside the name, "(Party)" in the target window, the capability bit.
- Flags: `-full-map`, `-nest-db-dir`, `-nest-respawn` (override every window, testing only);
  `OPENSRO_AI_TICK_STATS=1` logs the AI tick's p50/p99 once a minute.

| r6 | Europe starter field 108/77 (MOVOI, EDENP) | DB nests | 65,662 | 2.30-2.39 / 3.06-4.05 | 139 MB | 1,378 | **100** |
| r7 | same | stand-in | 34,343 | 0.52-0.62 / 0.85-0.99 | 107 MB | 208 | 16.7 |
| r5 | the densest window, cell -116/8 | DB nests | 65,669 | 4.73-4.97 / 5.98-6.42 | 161 MB | 2,412 | **143** |
| r8 | same | stand-in | 34,344 | 0.62-0.65 / 0.83-0.95 | 111 MB | 202 | 16.7 |

(16.7-17.2 ms is the 60 Hz frame; the Jangan runs hold it either way.) **The server carries the
decision** -- p99 under 6.5 ms at the densest window, RSS 124-161 MB. **The client does not, where
the swapped spots cluster:** 1,378 and 2,412 bodies take the Europe starter field to 10 fps and
the densest window to 7 fps. That is the data, not this commit's code (the perf gate below is
SAME), and it goes to the user with these numbers: until the client's monster drawing scales past
round 655's ~500-in-view budget, `-nest-swapped-stand-in` keeps those fields at 60 fps. The densest
window's list is about 320 KB: ten frames of the paged list.

The perf gate on this commit's code, `perf_gate.sh --base 4bcc2cf --sites jangan,mobs` (the
client change is a comment's place): SAME on all eight numbers --

-- so the fall in frame rate above is the swapped spots' density, which the gate's fixed sites

## Six-hundred-and-fifty-ninth round: monsters give and receive status effects -- a stun stops a monster, a bleeding kills it and pays its caster, a water ghost's bite poisons the player, and the target window shows each state

The user (2026-09-30), part of the monster request: "Also make sure monsters give and receive
status effects." Server and target-window UI; no world drawing changed, so **no performance gate**
(`World3D.gd` only gains a dictionary of masks and a log line). Labels: READ (the binaries),
MEASURED (the archives), INFERRED, OURS, OPEN. The full record is
`docs/protocol/status_effects.md`, "What OpenSRO does (round 659)".

### 1. The correction: value[1] is the chance (READ)

The freeze block of `Combat_ApplyStatusEffects` (`0x590756..0x590889`) loads **value[1]** (plus
the target's param 169, the disease gate) into EAX, `kind << 24` into ECX and `[esi+0xa30]` into
EDX -- ESI the CASTER (corrected by the review, §6: this entry first said the target's map), and calls `0x5a1a20` -- `GObjPC::RollChance`, whose `FUN_00599cc0` is the
chance-memory dice the critical already uses (`combat/chancememory.go`). Only then does it read the
resist percent and compute `ftol((100 - resist) / 100 * value[0]) - flat` into `record+0x1a`,
which `0x410b40` multiplies into the duration. So value[1] is the landing chance and value[0] the
strength. Rounds 249 and 276 had it as "level = value[1]" and "+0x1a is the chance -- the number
that decides whether a state lands decides how long it lasts"; `internal/statuseffect` and the
protocol doc are corrected. MEASURED on the retail skilldata through the exporter's new column 90
(33,698 rows): `MSKILL_CH_WATERGHOST_ATTACK02 ps:34,100,16` (always lands), `SKILL_CH_COLD_
GIGONGTA_A_01 fz:30,5;fb:30,25` (5 % and 25 %), `MSKILL_CH_TIGERWOMAN_ATTACK03 zb:72,100`. 11,551
rows carry a status run, 3,107 of them monster skills: bl 559, es 347, ps 245, bu 223, st 201,
dn 197, ds 189, fb 181, cssr 178, fz 170, cshp 168, fe 157, rt 147, my 142, and fewer of the rest.
The non-elemental blocks roll the same dice (sleep `mov ecx,0x7000000` at `0x59106f`, stun
`0xf000000` at `0x592051`) with round 277's chance; bleeding writes `+0x38 = value[3]`, `+0x40 =
value[4]`, `+0x10` = 'puls' or 2000 (`0x591bd7`).

### 2. What a state stops (READ, the vslots the brief left unread)

The two vtables were located by their known slot 342/344 entries in `SR_GameServer.exe` (CGObjPC
`0xaf59fc`, CGObjMob `0xaeddac`); both hold the same two functions:

- **vslot 0x55c** (slot 343) `GObjPC::FUN_004a9d00` is SetMotionState: freeze passes 10 FROZEN,
  stun 9 STUN, sleep 0x13, each back to 0 STAND on removal (freeze with a 1.5 s delay, the float
  at `0xb45c10`).
- **vslot 0x570** (slot 348) `GObjPC::FUN_004aa340` stops a moving object (`0x4c0` / `0x4b0`) and
  cancels its running action through the action queue at `+0xa30`.
- The movement handler `GObjPC::FUN_004b0ea0` (slot 377 of every mobile class) refuses a move for
  mask bits `0xc1` (freeze, sleep, root) and `0x4000` (stun).

So a frozen, stunned or sleeping monster stops at once and is refused moves; a rooted one only
moves no more. INFERRED: that no new attack starts under those motion states (the attack path's
test is not read). Frostbite writes walk/run speed at 50.0 and slow at 75.0 in the scale slot
(`0xb4603c`, `0xb45de0`), slow only while no frostbite bit is set; 100.0 on removal.

### 3. What was built

- **Export**: skill CSV column 90 `StatusParams` (every status run and 'puls', walked, not
  scanned), `refdata.Skill.StatusParams`, the `status_params` column, `species` -> 
  `combat.MonsterSkill.Status`.
- **`internal/statuseffect`**: `Resolve`/`ResolveAll` (both shapes, the engine's roll order),
  `Holder` (one record per slot -- each block fetches its slot's record, `0x5aa450(cl = slot)`, so
  a state replaces itself), `Step` (expiry first, then the ticks: poison and burn at >= 2001 ms,
  bleeding at > its interval; poison stops at 1 HP and credits nobody, a fatal burn or bleeding
  tick names its source), `CanMove`, `CanAct`, `SpeedPercent`, `DefenceCut`. 'tb' and 'csmp' are
  not applied (unread block / no applier).
- **`session/status.go`**: a player's cast lands its runs on the monster it hits (and a
  zero-damage cast -- the stun rows -- on its target); a monster's attack skill lands its runs on
  the character it hits, not when blocked, never on a dead one (OURS; §6 corrects the citation); `RunStatusEffects` steps every holder each 100 ms (OURS). A monster
  tick goes through round 656/657's `damageMonsterWatched` -- booked on the damage list to its
  source when the engine keeps one (corrected in §6: a living caster on every tick), so a unique killed
  by a tick credits its caster -- and a kill runs the SAME `grantKill` and `announceKill` a blow
  does (performAttack's kill branch moved into them unchanged), with `AnnounceUniqueKill`; the
  killer is sent `OpMonsterDied` too, having no attack result. A character's fatal tick is
  `finishKill`, monsterStrike's death tail moved out unchanged. A death ends the states (monster:
  `grantKill`; character: `finishKill`); a respawn is a new monster.
- **The AI**: `update` returns while a monster cannot act (`heldByStatus`, which also ends its leg
  when it cannot move); `startLeg` scales the leg's speed and refuses one for a rooted monster; the
  synchronous counter is skipped likewise; under `-monster-sleep` a held monster stays awake, as
  one in BATTLE does. Bleeding takes its flat defence off the monster in performAttack.
- **The wire**: `OpObjectStatus 0x3057` -- retail's number and its flag-4 block (u32 mask, then a
  level byte per set bit in `0x17fefc0`, READ in `0x8a9e30` / `0x9d2220`) after an OURS head (owner
  kind, i64 id). A monster's mask goes to its area-of-interest watchers under the monster wire
  lock, and with its enter message and the monster list; a character's to its zone.
- **The client**: `StatusNet` decodes it; `World3D` keeps each object's mask; the target window's
  buff viewer adds one icon per bit after the skill buffs, in the second list (`0x699480` ->
  `0x7fd2e0`), the icon from `0x7fdab0` (`icon\stateodd\s_<name>_icon.ddj`, the same 20x20 point
  sampling), the tooltip `0x7fc260` kind 2: `PARAM_<label>` text, ` <level><UIIT_STT_GRADE>`, then
  the category's text and `UIIT_STT_MACROPOTION_ABNORMAL`. The body effects and colour lerps
  `0x9cd5e0` applies per bit are READ in outline and NOT built (OPEN, TODO.md).

### 4. Tests, and the negative

- Go (`internal/statuseffect/apply_test.go`): value[1] is the dice's chance and value[0] the
  strength; resist cuts after the roll; stun's shape and falloff; unread states not applied; puls;
  one state per slot; poison ticks at 2001 ms, stops at 1 HP, expires before its tick; a fatal
  bleeding credits its source; mask, level bytes, speed, CanMove/CanAct.
- Go (`session/status_test.go`): the 0x3057 fixture byte for byte; **a DoT kill pays the killer
  exactly once** (gold +77 once over four passes, `OpMonsterDied` to killer and bystander, one
  `OpMonsterDamaged` for the non-fatal tick, the states gone with the monster); **a stunned monster
  does not counter** and does again once the stun is gone; **a stunned monster in BATTLE neither
  moves nor strikes** under the AI, and swings once released; **a monster's skill poisons a
  player** (mask 0x10 to the zone, 16 a tick, stops at 1 HP, a dead player is not poisoned). The
  export and CSV columns: `TestSkillStatusParamsColumn`, `TestSkillCSVStatusParamsIsAStrictSuffix`.
- Client (`net/status_net_test.gd`, 31 checks): the fixture, the level bits, the icon/label/category
  table, the tooltip, and the viewer's second-list icons and their diff.
- **The negative, against the base int/mob 345e375** (a second worktree): the Go tests do not build

      FAIL	github.com/OpenSRO/OpenSRO/server/internal/session [build failed]

  -- the export test in a form the base compiles fails at run time:

      FAIL	github.com/OpenSRO/OpenSRO/server/cmd/export-refdata

  -- and the client suite, run on the base's client on the box:

      FAIL the buff viewer takes abnormal states (abnormal_entries)
      2 FAILURE(S)

- `cd server && go build ./... && go vet ./... && go test -count=1 -p 1 ./...` on the tree merged with int/mob 345e375 (rounds 656 and 657 in): 61 packages ok, none failing.
- `remote_godot.sh tests` (lane dir `/opt/srrevamp-client-status659`): 176 suites, 0 failing;

### 5. Left (docs/TODO.md, "Status effects on monsters and players")

Burn deals 0 a tick until the operator supplies the `0xc63c94` table (not copied into the repo);
the client's body effects, colour lerps and the buff bar's own abnormal icons; character resists;
the params the mask does not yet move (myopia, dark, electric shock, the curses); the unread
halving loop in the slow/bleeding/stun blocks, 'tb', fear's AI message; a player's own speed; no
EXP line for a kill by a tick.

### 6. The review's follow-up (a second commit, after merging int/mob 1ea6b02)

The adversarial review of 9007108 found three HIGH and three MEDIUM defects and four LOW ones.
Each fix has a test in `session/status659r_test.go` (or `statuseffect/apply_test.go`) that fails on
9007108; the FAIL lines are quoted below.

- **H1, a stun on a moving monster sent no stop.** `applyToMonster` ended the leg on the hub itself,
  so the next AI tick found the monster standing and `heldByStatus` never queued the stop; clients
  kept drawing the leg. The applier no longer touches the hub: the tick ends the leg and sends the
  stop (vslot 0x570's stop, READ, as the AI's own push).
- **H2, a zero-damage status cast landed from any distance and in any zone.** A cast that resolves
  no blow but carries states for a monster now passes `statusCastRefusal` before its costs: the
  monster alive in the caster's zone ("target not found") and within `skillInReach` ("too far
  away"), and `applyToMonster` refuses a monster outside the caster's zone. INFERRED that retail
  measures it so (the gate's exemption for a zero-damage row, if any, is unread).
- **H3, a character killed by a tick was never told.** After `finishKill` the victim and her zone
  now get the `OpMonsterAttacked` a blow's death sends (TargetDied, the death's HP and EXP loss),
  flagged `StrikeStatusTick 0x08` (OURS; retail's message for this death is not read) so no client
  draws a swing. The client decodes `status_tick` and routes it to `_on_status_tick_strike`: the
  bar, the death line and the dead state for this player, the hit clip for another.
- **M1, the dice are the caster's.** In `0x590680` the map is `[esi+0xa30]` with ESI the SOURCE
  (`[esi+8]` goes to record+0x4c; ESI = `[esp+0x124]` at `0x58f412`, the object the critical roll
  uses at `0x58ed76`), and the key is `kind << 24` with no id bits. `statusRoller` now keys
  `chanceMemory` by the caster; §1 above is corrected.
- **M2, the source rule.** vslot 0xf8 is `CGObj::GetLifeState` (`0x485ee0`). While the record's
  latch `+0x6c` is clear, a caster alive (life state neither 2 nor 3) is named on EVERY tick,
  poison's included; a dead or gone one latches the record, after which burn and bleeding name it
  only on a fatal tick and poison never (READ). `statuseffect.SourceRule` / `CasterLookup`: every
  tick of a living caster is booked on the damage list (so DoT damage counts toward the unique
  notice) and is the monster's struck event -- both INFERRED: the appliers pass the named source
  to vslot 0x4fc, `CGObjChar::Char_ForwardToAttachedObject` (0x4a7500), which forwards to an
  object not read (the re-review's L2).
  This supersedes the first commit's "book only a fatal tick".
- **M3, `0x5906c0` is the blocked flag.** `cmp [edi+5],2` tests the hit record's blocked byte
  (`[ebp+5] = 2` after the block roll at `0x58f0ef`), so a blocked blow applies nothing, both ways.
  `performAttack` now reports `blowReport{Landed, Blocked}` and a cast whose every hit was blocked
  lands no state (938 species carry block 20). "Never on a dead character" is relabelled OURS.
- **L1**: fatal is decided against the HP the monster has at the damage call, and the kill is
  credited from its `died` result. **L2**: the pass reads the character store before taking the
  runtime's lock. **L3**: frostbite and slow restart a moving monster's leg at the new speed on the
  next AI tick (`heldByStatus`, `legPct`), as the appliers' vslots 0x4e8/0x4ec republish it at
  once. **L4**: the runtime's deps comment says what the code does, and a freeze that ends holds
  its monster from acting 1.5 s more (`Holder.CanActAt`, the float 1.5 at `0xb45c10`).

The tests against 9007108 (a worktree at that commit, the new files copied in):

### 7. The re-review (a third commit)

- **A death by a tick released no monster.** Without `-player-dead-state` (the default) she is back
  on her feet at once, and battleTick releases its target only on the strike worker's `a.kills` or
  on LifeDead -- so the monster whose bleeding killed her stayed in BATTLE on her.
  `dealCharacterTick` now marks the kill for every monster in BATTLE on her (`releaseTargetsOf`),
  as the strike worker marks it for its killer. (A blow's death still releases only its killer:
  unchanged, OURS either way.)
- **With `-monster-ai` off**, a stun on a moving monster ends the hub's leg in `applyToMonster`
  again (no AI tick exists to do it, and nothing draws the leg to stop).
- The damage-list and struck-event readings are relabelled INFERRED (vslot 0x4fc, above).

## Six-hundred-and-fifty-seventh round: a unique's appearance and its killer are announced to every player in the original's blue banner at the top of the screen

The user (2026-09-30), part of the monster request: "if you kill a unique make sure you announce it
in a blue banner in the top middle of the screen like the original game". Retail announces a
unique's appearance too (the monster epic's decision D8: both). UI and server only, so no
performance gate. The full reading is `docs/protocol/unique_notice.md`.

### 1. The wire and the server rules (READ, SR_GameServer.exe)

- Spawn: `0x5f6eb0` relays `0x300C` / `0x0C05` {u32 RefObjID} for a rank-3 object (`vtable +0x12c`,
  slot 75 -- the rank getter; round 657's review corrected "vslot 300", which was that byte
  offset in decimal).
  Kill: CGObjMob vslot 398 `0x4c1c80` sends `0x300C` / `0x0C06` {u32 RefObjID, name}, class 3 only
  (`cmp al,3` at `0x4c1ccb`), and **only when there is a killer** (`test ebp,ebp; je` at
  `0x4c1cd7`). A killer whose `vtable +0x1c` answers 0 is named `"???"` (`0xaedda4`,
  `0x4c1dd1`) -- a branch this caller does not reach, since vslot 399 drops those (review M1).
- The killer is vslot 399 `0x4c44a0` (called from the death path vslot 311 `0x4c42f0`): over the
  damage list `+0x1ca4` ({id +0x10, damage +0x14}), each id resolved through `0x485d90` and a
  missing object skipped, pets mapped to owners, non-players skipped,
  grouped by an experience-sharing party (`+0x72e*4`, flag bit 0) or the player alone, the group
  with the most damage and in it the member with the most. Both comparisons strict.
- The suppress key: `CONTROL_NOTIFY_SPAWN_UNIQUE_MONSTER_MSG` (read at `0x60936f`) equal to `"ON"`
  (`0xb012f4`) sets the world's `+0x108` (`0x6093b1`, getter `0x608350`); both notices ask the world
  (`0x5f9910`) and are skipped when set -- for the spawn, only a nest's hatch asks (review L2, §7).
  Absent: both are sent.

### 2. The client (READ, sro_client.exe `0x874ea0`)

- The line is chosen by the monster's SN_ key against five strings -- `SN_MOB_CH_TIGERWOMAN`,
  `SN_MOB_KK_ISYUTARU`, `SN_MOB_OA_URUCHI`, `SN_MOB_TK_BONELORD`, `SN_MOB_RM_TAHOMET`
  (`0xdda1f4`..`0xdda090`) -- **five named uniques, not seven**; any other takes the `_UNIC` lines.
- **ANYONE_DEAD vs DEAD is the killer's name against `"???"`** (`0xdda02c`): DEAD ("... has
  disappeared") for `"???"`, ANYONE_DEAD ("[%s] killed ...") for a player. It has nothing to do with
  whether this player made the kill. Tahomet has no DEAD_ line: `"???"` takes DEAD_UNIC with its
  name (`0x87572e`). The generic kill is ANYONE_DEAD_UNIC (killer, name). The `_L2`/`_L3` rows
  compare unequal and take the generic lines.
- Every line goes to the system window, type 0 (`0x7781b0`: colour `0xffdbc99b`), **and** to
  GDR_WARNING_WND (`0x77b580` -> child `0x23` -> `0x7b3eb0`).

### 3. The banner is blue (READ, then MEASURED)

The brief said the colour was not read and not to assume blue. It is blue, and the blue is not the
layout's `Color=` line (the resinfo parser reads no such field). CGInterface's setup configures
each CIFNotify after creating it (`0x78cbbe..0x78ce3b`):

| | GDR_NOTICE (0x14) | GDR_WARNING_WND (0x23) |
|---|---|---|
| y (`0x7b3d40`) | 100 (`push 0x64`, `0x78cbbe`) | 130 (`push 0x82`, `0x78cbed`) |
| frame | com_notice_* (the class's) | com_warning_edge / edge2 / corner (`0xdb977c`, `0xdb9750`, `0xdb9724`) |
| fill (`0x7b3d10`) | (128, 45, 67) | **(0, 52, 92)** (`push 0x5c; push 0x34; push 0`, `0x78cd00`) |

The class's render (vslot 13 `0x7b3cb0`) draws a quad in the fill colour at alpha
`-0x80 - (0xff - a) / 2` (128 at full) and then the frame. MEASURED on the box's Media.pk2: every
texel of the three `com_warning_*.ddj` (A8R8G8B8) is (0, 52, 92), alpha 0..128; every
`com_notice_*` texel (128, 45, 67). Text: GDR_NOTIFY_TXT's FontColor, white. **Correction to round
634:** GDR_NOTICE is at y 100, not 0 (the constructor's 0 is overwritten by the setup), and it has
the maroon fill; round 639's "GDR_WARNING_WND shares the notice's y (OPEN)" is answered: 130.

### 4. What was built

- Server (`session/uniquenotice.go`): `OpUniqueNotice 0x0110` (OURS) carrying 0x300C's payload;
  sent to every character on a class-3 spawn (roster spawn hook and GM `/spawn`/`/spawnunique`) and
  on its death (the combat kill; GM `/damage`/`/kill`). `combat.Hub` now keeps each monster's damage
  list (`ApplyDamageFrom`, first-hit order) and hands it to the killing blow; `UniqueKiller` is the
  vslot-399 rule over it (a party of two or more is a group; ties: the first in first-hit order,
  OURS). `-unique-notice-off` (env `OPENSRO_UNIQUE_NOTICE_OFF`) is the key, default off.
- GM tools (OURS): `/spawnunique <id|name>` (Tiger Girl 1954, Isyutaru 2002, Uruchi 1982, Lord
  Yarkan 3810, Demon Shaitan 3875, Cerberus 5871 -- level, HP, defence, radius and speeds READ from
  the box's characterdata; attack the disclosed curve, no attack skill); `/damage <n> [id]`, a blow
  booked to the GM; `/kill` with nobody on the list announces `"???"` (OURS: retail has no GM kill).
- Client: `UniqueNoticeNet` (decode, `line_for` exactly as `0x874ea0`, `sprintf` for swprintf's

## Six-hundred-and-fifty-sixth round: the server carries ten thousand monsters -- each player hears only about the monsters around it, the list comes in pages, and far-off monsters sleep

The monster-world epic (2026-09-30, the user: "Please add all monsters to the map like the original
server would have it..."). Round 657 places every npcpos field row -- about 10,200 monsters --
under `-single-frame`, whose one bucket is the whole world. This round makes the server able to
carry that. Server round, plus the client's list parsing and a leave handler. No world, map,
object, effect, animation, movement or loading code on the client, so no performance gate.

### 1. What stood in the way (READ from the code at ab66d9c)

- **The monster list was one frame.** `handleMonsterList` sent every monster of the bucket in one
  `OpMonsterListResult`. A frame carries at most 32,767 payload bytes (`proto.Write`, the Size
  field's 15 bits), and a record is ~64-68 bytes, so ~480 fit. Past that, `proto.Write` failed,
  the handler returned the error, and the gateway closed the session on every list request
  (TODO.md, "A hard guard on the monster list", round 571's review).
- **No area of interest anywhere.** Every monster push -- spawn, leg, stop, blow, damage, death --
  went to `EntitiesInZone(zone)`. Under the flag, that is every player in the world.
- **`combat.Hub` was one mutex over one map**, and `InZone` walked every monster.
- **The AI tick** copied `All()` (every monster: the base allocates 6.6 MB a tick at 12,000 in the benchmark below), sorted it, built a
  `seen` map, and pushed each leg to every player in the zone, on one goroutine. `acquire` copied
  the zone's entities for every scan, and `linkAggro` copied the zone's monsters.
- **`Send` had no write deadline**: one client that stopped reading held its writer, and so the
  tick, forever.
- **One goroutine and one 1 s ticker per placement** (`maintainMonster`).

### 2. What was built (OURS unless marked)

- **The cell index** (`combat/cells.go`). Each monster is filed under `(zone, floor((x+960)/1920),
  floor((z+960)/1920))`: one cell per region of the zone's frame, with the region lines as its
  edges (READ: `worldmap.ToWorld`'s measured transform puts the frame's centre region's middle at
  the origin). The spawn files a monster, `StepCells` re-files one whose step crosses a line and
  reports the crossing, and the kill removes it. The hub's lock is an RWMutex. Only monsters on a
  leg are stepped (the moving set).
- **The area of interest** (`session/aoi.go`). A player hears about the monsters within
  `AOIRadius` = 2 cells of its view cell on both axes: 25 regions. **OURS:** 2 is the client's
  `REGION_LOAD_RADIUS`, and retail's visibility rule is unread. The runtime (`RunMonsterAOI`,
  always installed by cmd/server) moves each player's view to the cell it stands in every 100 ms
  and on each list request. The list, the spawn push, the legs, the blows, the damage and the
  death go only to the players whose window holds the monster's cell. When a view moves, the player
  is sent the monsters its window gained, each as `OpMonsterSpawned` (with the monster's current
  facing) plus its leg if it is walking, and one `OpMonsterLeft` **0x00B5** (u16 n, n × s64)
  naming the monsters it lost. A monster that walks over a line enters or leaves the same way.
  Enter and leave are **checked at the send**, under the session's monster wire lock (alive and in
  the window, or not), and death and damage take the same lock. So two goroutines' messages
  cannot leave a stale body, whatever order they reach the socket in.
- **The paged list** (`session/monsterlist.go`). A list that fits a frame is byte for byte what it
  was. A bigger one goes as several ordinary `OpMonsterListResult` frames, each with a 4-byte
  trailer after its records (u16 page, u16 pages). The motion list is split at 1,560 legs a
  frame. The aggro scan and the aggro link's candidates read the cells their radius can reach
  (`CellsWithin`), which keeps exactly the candidates the radius test keeps.
- **The sleep** (`MonsterAIConfig.Sleep`, `-monster-sleep`, default ON; **OURS**, retail's rule
  is unread). A monster whose cell no player's window holds is neither stepped nor run. Its brain
  is made when a player first comes that near, and it keeps its state and its leg while asleep.
  With sleep off (the zero config, every earlier test), every monster runs as before.
- **One respawn scheduler** (`cmd/server`). One goroutine checks every placement once a second,
  with the old loop's timing: `respawnDelay` 10 s, disclosed. `maintainMonster` is gone; its
  test drives the scheduler with one placement.
- **The send deadline** (`gateway.SendTimeout` = 2 s, OURS; 10 s since the review, §7, and a
  per-session blocking budget since the second review, §8). A Send blocked that long closes the
  connection, and every later Send returns `ErrSendStalled` at once. A stalled client holds the
  tick at most 2 s, once.
- **`-qa-spread-monsters N` / `-qa-spread-radius R`** (QA only): N more placements of Jangan's
  roster species at fixed-seed spots over the (2R+1)² regions around Jangan, for load checks.
- **Client, list parsing only** (plus the leave handler). `combat.gd` reads the trailer (lines
  239-243, 619-622) and decodes `OP_MONSTER_LEFT` (28-31, 625-638). `net_client.gd` gathers the
  pages and emits `monster_list_result` once, on the last (73-79, 877-889), and emits
  `monster_left`. `World3D.gd` connects it (line 1350) and drops each body as
  `_sync_monster_bodies` drops one the list no longer names (`_on_monster_left`, 15376-15412, a new
  function after `_on_monster_list_result`). None of round 655's lines (`_spawn_or_update_monster`,
  the list pulls) are touched.

### 4. The benchmark (MEASURED, `BenchmarkMonsterAITick`)

One AI tick, its pushes written, at 12,000 monsters (testMangyang) spread evenly over 40 × 30
regions in one bucket. 50 or 100 players are connected over real TCP on localhost, each client
draining its socket. "spread" puts the players anywhere on the grid, "town" puts them all within
Jangan's 5 × 5 regions. "aggro" turns `-monster-battle` and `-monster-aggro` on. There are 50
warm-up ticks. The same file ran against ab66d9c with a no-op setup stub
(`aitick656_setup_test.go`). The branch installs the AOI runtime (its reconcile runs before each
tick) and the sleep. i7-13700K, 30 ticks (base) / 100 ticks (branch):

| players | layout | aggro | base ms/tick | base B/tick | base allocs | branch ms/tick | branch B/tick | branch allocs |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 50 | spread | off | 34.11 | 6,618,659 | 7,702 | 3.55 | 35,748 | 819 |
| 50 | spread | on | 50.20 | 30,017,093 | 25,660 | 3.33 | 53,947 | 1,532 |
| 50 | town | off | 33.06 | 6,618,659 | 7,702 | 0.57 | 20,303 | 328 |
| 50 | town | on | 56.43 | 30,021,487 | 25,677 | 0.53 | 24,776 | 485 |
| 100 | spread | off | 58.91 | 9,060,227 | 13,666 | 5.56 | 65,128 | 1,308 |
| 100 | spread | on | 95.64 | 57,418,539 | 33,750 | 6.47 | 97,603 | 2,483 |
| 100 | town | off | 73.33 | 9,060,228 | 13,666 | 1.18 | 38,939 | 575 |
| 100 | town | on | 195.0 | 57,391,116 | 33,680 | 1.57 | 43,541 | 733 |

The base's tick at 100 players with aggro on (195 ms) is longer than the tick period (100 ms), so
it falls behind. On the branch, "spread" keeps nearly every cell awake (100 windows of 25 cover
most of the 1,200 regions), so the gain there is the area of interest and the index. "town" also
sleeps the rest of the map. One earlier branch run of the same file gave 13.7 ms for 100/spread/off.
Localhost TCP timing varies between runs, so treat single figures as ±2×. **The players never move
in the benchmark**, so it measures no view moves, and no enters or leaves driven by a player's
walk (review follow-up).

### 5. Live on the render box (MEASURED, `/var/tmp/aoi656/live.sh r1`)

The server was built from this branch: `-in-memory -single-frame -monster-ai -monster-spawn-push
-qa-spread-monsters 5000 -qa-spread-radius 7`. The client came from this branch
(`/opt/srrevamp-client-aoi656`, World3D with the QA sign-in), `OPENSRO_QA_AT=1850,1020` (world x
890, 70 units west of the region line at 960) and `OPENSRO_QA_WALK=90` (east), for 180 s:

- `roster spawned monsters=5024` (the 24 roster anchors + 5,000 spread).
- The client's one list: `World3D: server reports 594 monster(s)`. That is the 25-region window. The spread
  cycles Jangan's ten roster species, whose records are 56-79 bytes (Weasel smallest; 68.5
  average), so 594 records are at least 33,264 bytes: more than one 32,767-byte frame. They came
  as pages and were gathered into one `monster_list_result` (one line, not two).
- The walk over the line: `aoi: view moved character=1 zone=world from=0,0 to=1,0 entering=118
  leaving=107`. The client printed 118 `spawned (push)` lines and 43 leave lines naming 151
  monsters: the crossing's 107, plus 44 that wandered out of the window during the run.
- One `session connected` at 09:17:37, and the only disconnect is at 09:20:35, when the script

### 6. Open (docs/TODO.md, "Monster scale: the area of interest (round 656)")

- An older client (no capability byte, §7) gets one frame of the nearest monsters and ignores 0x00B5.
  Round 657's full map is the first to show it.
- The AOI radius and the sleep rule are OURS. Retail's are unread.
- The client still asks for the whole window's list after every hit (round 655's lane).
- A slow or stalled client can hold its writers up to its blocking budget (§8; 10 s since §9). A
  per-session send queue would remove that.
- The respawn is still the flat 10 s; round 659 brings the nest rules.

### 7. The review's follow-up

The adversarial review found three MEDIUM ordering bugs with a stress test: four goroutines (a
player walking, jumping and listing; the view reconcile; the AI tick with forced legs over region
lines; kills and respawns) against a client model that applies every monster message. All three
are fixed.

- **A step and a view move could lose an enter or a leave.** The tick stepped, a reconcile moved
  the view and read the monster's new cell in its difference, and then the tick's crossings,
  computed against the new view, found nothing to answer for. Now the step and its crossings run
  as one step under the area of interest's read lock (`monsterAOI.step`), so a view move lands
  wholly before or wholly after.
  `TestAOIStepAndViewMoveKeepTheEnter` / `...KeepTheLeave` run the reconcile wholly before and
  wholly after the step. Both orders already passed on d3963cf, so they pin that neither regressed
  and do not test the fix. The second review's `TestAOIReconcileWaitsForTheStep` (§8) does.
- **A kill could leave a ghost.** The death went to the watchers of where the monster died, read
  after `ApplyDamage`. A view that moved off it in between had also missed the leave, because the
  dead monster was no longer in its lost cells. The death now goes to the watchers before the blow
  and after it (`damageMonsterWatched`; GM `/kill` the same).
- **The spawn push was a direct send** to the views whose window held the cell when it was read.
  It now goes through the checked enter (`deliverViewEvents`).

Also: a push's cell is taken from the monster's float64 position, not the wire's float32. A
monster in BATTLE or HOMING never sleeps (`TestHomingMonsterNeverSleeps`). `gateway.SendTimeout`
is raised from 2 s to 10 s, so a client busy loading is not dropped (OURS). §8 bounds the whole
session, not just one write. A per-session queue
was not built, because every Send caller relies on the frame being on the wire, in order, when
Send returns.

**The paged list is opt-in.** The `OpMonsterList` request carries one byte, bit 0 = "gathers a
paged list" (`MonsterListFlagPaged`; the client sends 0x01). A request without it, from every
older client, gets the old single frame, holding the monsters nearest the player that fit
(`TestMonsterListWithoutTheFlagIsOneFrameOfTheNearest`).

The stress test is kept, driving the production paths (`TestAOIStressClientMatchesTheWindow`).
Six runs in a row MEASURED 0 ghosts, 0 missing and 0 spawns of a dead monster, with 50,288-84,863
frames a run. One line:

```
frames 48401, view {jangan 2 1} stand {jangan 2 1}, client bodies 174, truth 174, ghosts 0 [],
missing 0 [], unknown moves 285, spawn-after-death 0, leave-unknown 1194, dead 127
```

"leave-unknown" is harmless: a leave for a body the client had already dropped. "Unknown moves"
are NOT harmless, as this section first claimed: the real client answers a leg for a body it does
not have by asking for the whole list. §8 checks legs at the send, and the stress test now asserts
none. `go test -race` on the AOI tests reports no race. The benchmark players never move (see §4).

### 8. The second review's follow-up

The re-review verified all three ordering fixes and found no new correctness bug. It raised two
MEDIUMs and three LOWs, all closed here.

- **One slow reader still stalled everyone** (MEDIUM). The deadline was set fresh on every write,
  so a trickle reader finished each write inside 10 s and was never closed. Meanwhile the AI tick,
  the respawn scheduler's spawn push and other players' blows each waited on it in turn. Now each
  session has a **blocking budget**: `gateway.SendBlockBudget` = **3 s**, draining 3 s per
  `SendBlockWindow` = 30 s, **OURS**. Every write's time on the socket adds to the session's debt,
  and each write's deadline is capped at what is left. At the budget the session is closed. A
  per-session queue was not built (§7's reason). `TestASlowSteadyReaderIsClosedWithinItsBudget`: a
  peer reading 16 KB every 10 ms, a fan-out writing 16 KB to it and to a fast peer. Budget 300 ms
  in the test: it held the fan-out 301 ms and was closed, and the fast peer was unaffected.
  **NEGATIVE against 7a92b1c** (a stub returns `SendTimeout` as the budget; MEASURED):

```
slowreader656_test.go:86: the slow reader held the fan-out 5.203s, then: <nil>
    slowreader656_test.go:88: the slow reader was never closed: it held the fan-out 5.203s over 5 s (budget 1s)
--- FAIL: TestASlowSteadyReaderIsClosedWithinItsBudget (5.22s)
FAIL
FAIL	github.com/OpenSRO/OpenSRO/server/internal/gateway	5.219s
FAIL
```

- **The two step/view-move tests did not test the fix** (MEDIUM). §7 is corrected. A test hook
  inside `monsterAOI.step`, between the hub's step and the crossings (`aoiStepHook`, nil in
  production), starts a reconcile on another goroutine. `TestAOIReconcileWaitsForTheStep` asserts
  that the reconcile waits until the step is done, and that the player then gets both messages:
  M1 walks from cell 3 into cell 2 and M2 from cell -2 into cell -3, while the player moves from
  cell 0 to cell 1. **NEGATIVE** against a shim of d3963cf's order (the step unlocked, then the
  hook, then the crossings under the lock), MEASURED:

```
aoistress656_test.go:354: the reconcile ran inside the step: nothing kept a view move out from between the step and its crossings
    aoistress656_test.go:358: entered [], want [1]: the monster that walked into the window was never sent
    aoistress656_test.go:361: left [], want [2]: the monster that walked out of the window stays a ghost
--- FAIL: TestAOIReconcileWaitsForTheStep (0.32s)
FAIL
FAIL	github.com/OpenSRO/OpenSRO/server/internal/session	0.320s
FAIL
```

- **Unknown moves** (LOW). `monsterAI.deliver` checks each recipient at the send (`mayShowLeg`:
  alive, in the window, no enter still owed), and a view move marks the monsters it gains as
  pending until their enter goes out. The stress test asserts 0 unknown moves, and six runs
  MEASURED 0. It had 285 in one run before the check, and 2-7 a run with the check but with
  respawns wandering. The remaining source was the test's own fake clock: it runs a 2001 ms IDLE
  dwell in a few milliseconds of wall time, so a brain could leg a respawn before the goroutine
  that spawned it had sent the spawn push. The stress test's respawns therefore do not wander on
  their own. In the server the push leaves at once and the first leg waits out the dwell in real
  time. With `-monster-spawn-push` off (the default) a respawn is never announced, and its first
  leg reaches clients that do not know it: the pre-656 discovery path, recorded in TODO.
- **Every monster-damage path goes through `damageMonsterWatched`** (LOW).
  `TestMonsterDamageGoesThroughDamageMonsterWatched` parses every non-test file. It fails on any
  call of the monster hub's `ApplyDamage(id, amount)` or `ApplyDamageFrom(id, attacker, amount)`
  (round 657's damage list), except the one inside `damageMonsterWatched` and the GM's `/kill` and
  `/damage` in `gm/gm.go`. The character stores' `ApplyDamage(ctx, ...)` is told apart by its
  `ctx`. A probe file calling both on the hub fails it (checked, removed). The merged signature
  (`id, attacker, amount` → `updated, died, ok, watchers, hits`) is in
  `docs/protocol/monster_ai.md` for rounds 659 and 660.
- **GM `/kill`'s before-watchers** (LOW). `TestGMKillReachesTheWatchersBeforeIt`: a hook after the
  command (`gmAfterRunHook`) moves Bram's view far off before the announcement, and Bram still
  hears the death. With the before-watchers dropped, MEASURED: `Bram, watching the monster when
  the GM killed it, was never told it died`.

Tests: `go test -count=1 -p 1` on session, combat, gm, gateway, systems and cmd/server: all ok.
`go test -race` on the AOI, stress, sleep, GM-kill and guard tests, and on gateway: no data race,
and 20 stress runs in a row pass. One earlier -race run showed a single ghost. The client model
had not yet read the server's last frames when the test's fixed 500 ms settle ran out (45,848
frames under -race, against ~80,000 without). The settle now waits until the reader has been quiet
for 300 ms.

## Six-hundred-and-fifty-fifth round: five hundred monsters in view build in a few frames each instead of freezing the game, and the Small-eyed Ghost, Old Weasel, Water Ghost slave and Tomb Stone Ghost are drawn as themselves

Part of the monster-world epic. The server will soon send hundreds of monsters per view: 10,195
field placements over the map, and about 500 in the densest 5 x 5-region window. Before this
round the client could not draw that many.

**Labels.** READ: recovered from `sro_client.exe` (the decompile on the render box). MEASURED:
counted or timed on the box. INFERRED: follows from what was read but was not itself read. OURS:
this project's choice.

### What the client did with a monster list (READ from World3D.gd at ab66d9c)

- **Every body was a fresh assembly.** `_spawn_or_update_monster` called
  `SkinnedBsrAssembler.assemble_from_archive` for each monster. That meant the `.bsr`, the `.bsk`,
  every `.bms`, the `.bmt` and its textures, per body, with no species cache. The NPC path has had
  one (`_npc_model_cache`) since round 157.
- **The whole list was built in the frame it arrived**, with a print line and a debug ItemList
  row for each monster.
- **A monster outside the loaded terrain was built anyway**, at the server's y. It then sat on
  the height retry list until its region loaded.
- **Every idle and one-shot clip was posed in GDScript every frame**, wherever the body stood.
- **A full monster list was requested** after every own attack result, every `OpMonsterDamaged`,
  every `OpMonsterDied`, and at the end of every death clip.

**What it cost (MEASURED, `client/tools/probe_monster_build.gd` on the box's archive).** One body
assembled from its `.bsr`:
- 4-14 ms for most Chinese field species;
- 133 ms for the first one (a cold archive);
- 791 ms for `MOB_CH_TIGERWOMAN` (69 bones, 7 pieces);
- a mean of **53 ms** over the 21 species tried.

A duplicate of a species template costs **0.33 ms**, 162 times less. So 500 bodies of 21
species cost about 26.5 s built the old way and about 1.3 s built from templates.

### What changed

- **One template per species model** (`MonsterDraw.Templates`). Each model is assembled once
  and kept detached. Every body is a `duplicate()` of the template's skeleton: the meshes, skins,
  materials and textures are shared, and so are the parsed `.bsr`, the idle clip and the
  per-model animation cache. A model that fails to assemble is remembered as failed. The
  templates are freed with the world.
- **Bodies are built over several frames.** A list queues the bodies it names. Each physics frame,
  `_pump_monster_builds` builds them until 3 ms is spent, and always builds at least one
  (`BUILD_BUDGET_USEC`, OURS). A species seen for the first time is still one assembly on the main
  thread, and the at-least-one rule lets it through (OPEN, below). A single push
  (`OpMonsterSpawned`) still builds its body at once.
- **Posing is culled** (`MonsterDraw.pose_wanted`, applied in `_tick_idle_animations`). A monster's
  or NPC's clip is posed only while:
  - its body is in range of the camera, meaning `dist - radius < 2020`;
  - its sphere touches the view frustum.

  Its sounds stop out of range, and a monster's model is hidden there (`MonsterDraw.META_HIDE`,
  OURS, as MapAnimation hides a map object; added after the review, since an unposed walking
  body slid without its gait). An NPC is only left unposed. The clock keeps running, so a
  one-shot still hands back to its loop on time. The player, other players and the character window's doll are never culled.
  - **The range is OURS.** It is the map objects' READ update range (2500 - 480, asm
    0xa2d961/0xa2d967, round 645) applied to characters. Retail's monster render slot
    (`CICMonster` slot 10, 0x9d20d0) has no distance test, and the object slot `FUN_009c4aa0`
    only tests the frustum (READ). The entity manager's per-frame tick was not read.
  - **The sphere is OURS**: centred on the feet, with a radius of the farthest mesh-bounds corner
    or the name-plate height, whichever is larger.
  - Bodies out of range are still drawn, just not posed.
- **No body outside the loaded regions.** A monster whose cell is not in `_grid.loaded_cells` keeps
  its snapshot and gets no body (`_monster_deferred`). The body is built when the cell loads and
  dropped when the cell unloads, which happens in `_monster_cells_changed`, run from the pump after
  `mark_loaded` or `unload`. A move for a monster that is listed but not yet drawn updates its
  snapshot and asks for no list.
- **No full list on hits.** The own attack result's `monster_remaining_hp` is recorded in the
  snapshot when the result arrives (in wire order with the zone's pushes) and drawn from the
  snapshot as the blow lands (`_record_monster_hp` / `_paint_monster_hp`), so an older result
  cannot overwrite a newer `OpMonsterDamaged` that arrived before the landing. Showing it at the
  landing is OURS; until now it came with the list reply. `OpMonsterDamaged` records and draws at
  once (`_apply_monster_hp`). **Only a result that reports a blow carries health** (damage > 0
  or died): the review found that a zero-damage hostile cast (`SKILL_EU_WARRIOR_DUALA_STUN_A_01..05`,
  and the debuffs this epic adds) was answered with `MonsterRemainingHP` 0 (session/skill.go's
  no-blow reply), which the list pull used to correct. The client now ignores health on a no-blow
  result, and the server fills the field with the monster's current HP there. A death removes its body when its clip has run (`_finish_monster_death`),
  or at once when there is none. The server gives a respawn a new id (`maintainMonster`), so a
  removed id never comes back. The zone-change list, the GM refresh, the refresh button, the
  QA hooks and the rate-limited list after a move for an unknown monster all remain. **One
  throttled pull stays** (review, item 3): until the zone's first `OpMonsterSpawned` is seen, a
  death that has played out asks for one list, at most every 10 s (`DEATH_PULL_SECONDS`, OURS),
  so a server with `-monster-spawn-push` off (the default) still shows respawns and GM spawns.
- **No per-monster prints or rows.** The build line, the "height resolved" line and the list's
  per-monster lines are printed only with `OPENSRO_QA_MOB_LOG` or `/wire`. A queue that drains
  prints one summary. The debug tabs' ItemList is filled only while the tabs are shown.

### The `_CLON` model rule (READ; docs/protocol/characterdata.md has the addresses)

- **`xxx` is stored as an empty string.** The client's characterdata parser (`FUN_00972910`)
  stores `xxx` as "" (`FUN_0097f860`/`FUN_0097f920`). It stores column 4, OrgObjCodeName, at
  +0x40, and after the file loads it links that to the Org row's ID at +0x5c (`FUN_0093fb50(5)`).
- **The pick.** At object creation `CICMonster::vslot_025` (0x9d3850, and three twins) takes the
  row's own model at +0x124 unless it is empty, and then the Org row's model. It goes one level
  only; nothing loaded means `res\mob\china\mangnyang.bsr`.
- **OpenSRO.** `NpcTableReader.parse_org_codes` and `model_with_org` implement the rule, and
  `_monster_model_path` resolves through it before the display-name join.
  - The Mangyang fallback is not taken. In the real table only the thief, hunter and guild-soldier
    classes reach it, and retail draws those from their own list (`ICMonster::FUN_009d3470`).
  - A column-52 cell that names several files now yields the first, as the parser keeps piece 0
    (asm 0x972f1d).
- **MEASURED on the box's archive.** 1,731 `MOB_` codes have their own model, and 159 more take
  their Org's model. 120 of the 142 `MOB_*_CLON` rows take their Org's model. The four roster
  `_CLON`s now draw as `bigeyeghost`, `gyo`, `waterghost` and `tombstone`. The world's own count
  at load: `5423 species resolvable by code, 161 more through their Org row`.
- **Still OPEN.** Column 48 (Scale, applied by CICMonster as scale / 100 from the row's own
  record) is not applied to any monster.

## Six-hundred-and-fifty-fourth round: the server knows every monster species in the game, and a GM can spawn any of them

The user (2026-09-30): "Please add all monsters to the map like the original server would have it
... Also make sure you add all the monster types like champion, giant, party, etc. Make sure this
includes uniques as well ..." This round is the base of that epic: the server's species came from
eleven hand-typed rows (`monsterSpecs`); it now loads all of them from the client's own table.
**Who spawns where does not change** -- round 657 places the nests.

Server and tooling only (no client file touched), so no performance gate.

### 1. What shipped

- `export-refdata -mode monsters` (OURS, `server/internal/species`): every characterdata row of
  TypeID (1,2,1,x), parts fed in `characterdata.txt`'s order, last definition of an id kept (the
  items/skills rule), into a 35-column CSV with a checked header: id, code name, Org code name and
  the id of the row it names, name key and its English (textdata_object, the client's own
  `UiTextTable` rule ported), TypeID4, rarity, level, HP, walk/run speed, BCRadius, cols 71-78,
  skills 83-92, the model or -- for an "xxx" row -- the Org row's (flagged `ModelFromOrg`), and the
  levelgold range at its level. The export loads itself back before it returns.
- Skill CSV column 89: AI_AttackChance, skilldata column 66 (READ, CRefSkill+0x164,
  monster_ai.md). An older export or database reads -1, UNKNOWN, never 0 (0 is a real "never
  drawn": `ai.SkillWeight` enters nothing for it). The store adds `skills.ai_attack_chance`
  (default -1).
- `cmd/server -monsters-csv` (env `OPENSRO_MONSTERS_CSV`): each roster species takes every
  species number from its row (`specFromRow`) and keeps its zone, anchor and placements; a
  difference from the hand-typed value is logged as a WARN; what the table cannot supply (no
  textdata_object, no levelgold, a skill store without AI_AttackChance) keeps the hand-typed value
  and says `kept`. The GM console's `/spawn` finds any species by code name, characterdata id or
  English name (`/spawn 1933 3`), with its level, rarity-scaled HP and rarity; `/goto` refuses a
  species the server does not place. The usage line names the roster and the table's count, not
  7,604 names.
- `monsterSpecs` is the fallback: without the flag the server is what it was.

Column labels (the full table is `docs/protocol/refdata_schema.md`, "`_RefObjChar` monsters"):
READ -- id, code name, Org position (col 4), name-key position (5), TypeID (9-12), rarity (15),
speeds (46/47), BCRadius (50), level (57), MaxHP (59), cols 71-78 -> params 5-12 with 71/73 and
the four tags read, skills (83-92), AI_AttackChance (skill col 66). INFERRED -- 72/74 as the
magical pair; levelgold as the kill gold (as before). OPEN -- TypeID4's use; whether the client
draws the Org's model (round 655); cols 75/77 per species in the hit roll.

Col 76 ('bri', block) is carried as data but **not** handed to combat: docs/TODO.md's "A blocked
hit with a skill percentage deals 1, not 0" says to fix that before any monster blocks, and 938
species read 20.

## Six-hundred-and-fifty-third round: a click on the sky, or on ground too far away, runs the character that way until a wall stops it, every other player sees the run and the stop, and every walk now stops at a wall instead of sliding along it

The user (2026-09-30): "Also add sky clicking to the game. If clicked out far enough or above the
land in the sky the character would run indefinitely in that direction until stopped or a
collision. Also when the character collides with a wall or something that stops it make sure you
stop the running as well and make the character stop in place like the original game."

The reading is filed in `docs/protocol/opcodes/movement.md`, "The heading move: a click on the sky".
The open items are in `docs/TODO.md`, "The sky click (round 653)".

### Before (MEASURED, dev 56e8e24)

- The click-to-move ray (`_ground_point_at`) ran 2000 units from the camera on the terrain layer,
  and a ray that met nothing returned null. **A sky click did nothing.**
- A click on ground 1000 to 2000 units away walked to that point.
- Both are the base's own behaviour through `_dispatch_left_click`: see the negative below.

### Retail's rule (READ, sro_client.exe; the full trace is in movement.md)

- **The click.** `UI_SILKMALL::FUN_0078f8d0` casts the pick through `SWorld::vslot_034`
  (`0xa01310`). That pick normalises the camera ray and scales it to **1000.0** (`0xd83268`, asm
  `0xa01333`), so it only answers within 1000 units of the camera.
- **No hit** (the sky, or ground farther than that): the ray's ground direction (y zeroed at
  `0x78fb07`) becomes a heading (`FUN_009ed130`), sent by `FUN_009ebec0(h, 1)` as the **heading
  form of 0x7021**: kind 0, the `+0x14` byte 1, and the u16 angle of h − π/2.
- **Not re-sent** while moving (state bit 9 of `+0x65c`, INFERRED "moving") when the heading is
  within 5° (`0xdb9828`) of the facing. The difference is raw, not wrapped.
- **The `+0x14` byte is the movement command** (the server's `CGObjMoverByCmd`):
  - bit 0 = forward (vslot_004 sets the stepping flag and vslot_003 steps);
  - 0x10 and 0x20 = turn at π rad/s (vslot_010);
  - the arrow keys send 1, 0x10 and 0x20 (`FUN_0077b070` → `FUN_009ebf40`).

  movement.md had it as "not read".
- **The run.** The echo's heading form sets the mover's `+0x80 = 2` (`FUN_009e08a0`). The tick
  `FUN_009e0e60` tests a destination only for `+0x80 == 1`, so a heading move steps along its
  heading for ever. Round 649's cut to the distance left does not apply.
- **The stop.** The tick copies back whatever point the collision query `CRegionManagerBody::
  vslot_012` (`0x412660`) left in the proposed record (asm `0x9e0fff..0x9e1027`).
  - The query's terrain walk (`0x4047a0`) answers a blocking edge with the crossing point, nudged
    at most 0.2 toward the cell centre (`FUN_004472d0`, `0xe1b850`), and **bit 0**.
  - Bit 0 ends the movement (`+0x84 = 0`, `+0x80 = 0`). **The body stops at the wall and does not
    slide.** This is the no-slide walk `NavGraph.step_tracked(..., false)` already follows (rounds
    616–618).
  - Nothing in the tick plays a collision clip. The body stands, as after any movement (INFERRED).
  - The client sends nothing at the stop.

### What shipped

- **Client** (`client/scripts/world/sky_run.gd`, `SkyRun`; `World3D`):
  - `_move_by_pick_ray` casts the walk's pick 1000 units (READ, was 2000 OURS). A hit walks as
    before. No hit calls `_start_heading_run`, which starts a run on the ray's ground heading and
    turns the body to it at 3π rad/s. The 5° no-resend rule is `SkyRun.click_rule`.
  - `_step_click_walk` steps a run at the full run speed, `/speed` included, with no destination.
  - `_move_on_nav_graph` walks a run with the no-slide walk and **ends it at the first blocked
    step** (`SkyRun.blocked_ends`). The order clears and the body plays its stand.
    - OURS: in the physics fallback (no `.nvm`) a run ends on `is_on_wall`.
  - A ground click, an attack's or friendly cast's approach, a pick-up walk and the QA retreat each
    set a point and clear the run. Anything that clears `_has_move_target` ends it too: death,
    typing, the sit transition, the wall root, a skill's move and the void recovery. A zone change
    or teleport ends it too since the review follow-up below.
  - Several requests do NOT end a run yet; they are OPEN, listed in the review follow-up below.
  - A click while holding an icon (round 652) never reaches the world: `HeldIcon.handle` swallows
    it, and `_on_held_dropped_outside` neither walks nor runs.
- **Wire** (OURS framing of a READ form). Each `OpMove` sent while a run is in effect sets bit 1 of
  the trailing flags byte. Retail's heading form follows it: kind 0, command 1, then the u16 angle
  (`WorldNet.encode_move`, `session.encodeMoveTail`). A walked position is still 12 bytes, and an
  older server reads bit 0 alone.
- **Server**:
  - `handleMove` faces the character the run's heading (`world.Hub.MoveHeading`,
    `world.HeadingFromWire`), not the step's direction.
  - It relays the heading form in `OpEntityMoved`. A relocation still wins and carries no run.
  - `proto.MovementCommandForward` names the command bit.
  - `DecodeMovement` now has a caller, so its `knownOrphans` entry is removed.
- **Watchers**: `_on_entity_moved` turns the body to the relayed heading at 3π rad/s instead of
  toward the next position. The stop is the last position, sent plain, and the body settles on it.

### Follow-up: every walk stops at the wall, as retail's does

The first commit (287e394) left click walks sliding (round 649, OURS) and asked the user. The
user's request decides it: "when the character collides with a wall or something that stops it
make sure you stop the running as well and make the character stop in place like the original
game". The reading above holds for **every movement kind**. The query answers a blocking edge with
the crossing point, nudged at most 0.2, and bit 0, which ends the move.

**What changed.**
- `ClickWalk.blocked_ends(blocked)` is retail's rule: any blocked step ends the order. Round 649's
  1 % threshold (OURS) is gone, and so is `SkyRun.blocked_ends`.
- `_move_on_nav_graph` walks every order with the no-slide walk (`step_tracked(..., false)`) and
  ends it at the first blocked step. Only the QA walk (`OPENSRO_QA_WALK`, no order) still slides.
- **Approaches.** An attack's or friendly cast's approach ends at the wall like any walk, but keeps
  its pending action.
  - The order's tick, `World3D._step_move_order`, was moved out of `_physics_process` so it can be
    tested. It runs while an approach is pending even with no move in effect, and re-issues the
    approach on the next tick. Retail's attack tick re-issues `MoveTowardObject` on every pass
    while out of reach (auto_command.md, phase 1, READ).
  - OURS: while the re-issued approach aims within 0.5 of where the wall stopped it (the target has
    not moved), the body stands at the wall facing the target, and the reach is tested every tick.
  - Without that hold, the body **crept along the wall**: each no-slide stop nudges it up to 0.2
    toward its cell's centre, which came to 22.7 units in 2 s at 60 re-issues a second (MEASURED,
    the synthetic fixture). How often retail's client shows a server-side re-issue (every 30 ms at
    most) was not read.
  - It walks on as soon as the target moves clear.
- **The pick-up walk** ends at the wall and asks for the item from there (`_ask_pickup_after_walk`,
  unchanged). The server judges the 10 units.
- **A doorway at an angle:** a walk whose line meets the door frame now stops at the frame. Round
  649's walk slid along the frame into the doorway and through. This is retail's behaviour, as
  read. A walk whose line passes through the gap goes through.
- The physics fallback (no `.nvm`) ends any order on `is_on_wall` (OURS; it was the heading run
  alone).

**Tests.** `client/scripts/world/click_walk_test.gd`:
- The fixture is now two cells split at x = 100 with the blocking edge on their boundary. That is
  the shape a real region has. The no-slide stop nudges toward the mover's own cell centre, which
  in the old one-cell fixture lay across the wall (MEASURED: x 100.141).
- It now checks:
  - a walk at an angle stops at first contact (z 110.2 of a point at z 120);
  - a steeper one at 200 u/s stops at its crossing (z 125.2, not the point's 150);
  - the approach is re-issued on 120 of 120 ticks, stays pending, and stands at x 99.988 with
    0.00000 drift after the stop;
  - it walks on when the target moves clear (z 100.20 → 132.88 in 10 ticks);
  - a walk into a door frame stops at the frame (z 90.2);
  - a walk through the gap goes through (x 128.0).
- Round 649's oblique check, which expected the slide, is replaced.
