### Review follow-up (the review of 287e394)

- **The 5° rule now tests the move kind (READ).** Retail keeps its heading only when `+0x6e8 != 1`.
  `+0x6e8` is the mover's `+0x80` (mover at `obj+0x668`): 1 is a walk to a point, 2 a heading.
  `FUN_009ebec0` returns early only when it is 2. So a sky click within 5° of the facing during a
  ground **walk** starts a run. Ours dropped that click; it now calls
  `SkyRun.click_rule(_has_move_target and _move_heading_run, ...)`.
- **An accepted zone change or teleport ends the run.** `_on_change_zone_result` now calls
  `_end_move_order_for_arrival`. Before, a heading run went on into the new zone.
- **Running off the loaded world (OURS).** When `_move_on_nav_graph` has no graph and there is no
  terrain above `WORLD_FLOOR_Y` under the next step, a heading run ends (`_end_run_off_world`).
  Before, it fell under gravity until the void recovery. `VoidCatchFloor` (top at y −1995) is
  below that line and does not count as ground. What retail's mover does at an unloaded edge was
  not read.
- **A sky click and a ground click drop a pending pick-up walk** (`_pending_pickup_id = -1`). Before,
  a later wall stop or arrival asked for the item from wherever the new order ended.
- **OPEN, not built.** These requests do not end a run: a self or ground cast, an attack sent with
  no walk (the `no_walk`, no-BCRadius and wall-root paths), a friendly skill on a monster, an
  in-reach pick-up, and an NPC talk. Retail's skill-start and pick-up-start paths were not read for
  a mover stop (`docs/TODO.md`).
- **Tests** (`sky_run_test.gd`): a walk plus a sky click 3.4° off gives "run"; both clicks drop the
  pick-up; the arrival ends the run; a run with ground ahead goes on, and one with none ahead (x
  2010.5, past the fixture's edge) ends. **NEGATIVE against d12fca6:**

```
FAIL walking to a point, a sky click 3.4 degrees off the facing starts a run (+0x6e8 == 1 is not kept) (keep)
FAIL a sky click drops a pending pick-up
FAIL and so does a ground click
SCRIPT ERROR: Invalid call. Nonexistent function '_end_move_order_for_arrival (via call)' in base 'Node3D (...)'.
```

  The base has no `_end_move_order_for_arrival`, so its run stops at that script error. On the
  branch: ALL PASS.
- **The suites.**
  - `remote_godot.sh check`: ALL LOAD.
  - `remote_godot.sh tests`: 173 suites, 0 failing.
  - The first run of `tests` caught two suites (`teleport_board_test`, `ground_probe_ab_test`).
    They drive `_on_change_zone_result` with no player, so the new stop now guards the velocity
    against a null player.
  - `go test -count=1 -p 1 ./...`: all packages ok. The server is unchanged.

### Open

- **What a retail body shows while its approach is held at a wall** was not read; OpenSRO's
  stands. Nor was retail's pick-up approach.
- **The server does not step the run itself.** OpenSRO is client-authoritative. Whether retail's
  server sends its own stop to the watchers was not read.
- The arrow keys' heading-form commands (READ) are not bound. `0x70c5` (the other sender) is not
  built.

### 9. The third review: the budget must not close a client frozen by a load

§8's 3 s budget could close a HEALTHY client. It reads its socket on the game's main thread
(`net_client.gd` `_process`), so it reads nothing while a load freezes that thread. The perf gate
measures a 3.3 s freeze at the Jangan world entry, and zone changes and model loads stall too. If
the kernel buffers fill meanwhile, writes block and the debt runs up.

**Measured on the render box** (`/var/tmp/aoi656/freeze.sh f1`). The server was built from
085d03f plus a debug line: every new peak of a session's debt past 50 ms is logged ("send debt
peak"), and every disconnect carries `send_debt_peak`, `longest_write` and `sent_bytes`. It ran
with `-qa-spread-monsters 6000 -qa-spread-radius 5` (50 monsters a region, denser than npcpos's
worst region of 35) and all six monster switches on (`-monster-ai -monster-strike-push
-monster-spawn-push -monster-battle -player-dead-state -monster-aggro`) under `-single-frame`. One
real client:

- entered the world at the Jangan spawn (`server reports 1286 monster(s)`);
- ran `/goto donwhang` and 45 s later `/goto jangan` (`server reports 1253`);
- then ran `/spawnunique` for Tiger Girl, Cerberus and Uruchi (model loads, each with its
  banner). The longest gap in the timestamped client log is 1.64 s, before Cerberus's spawn push
  was drawn.

The session's whole life, 3.5 min: **peak debt 1.3 ms, longest single write 75 µs, 1,314,696
bytes written**. No "send debt peak" line was logged (none reached 50 ms), and the session was
not closed until the script ended it. The loopback buffers never filled. At ~6 KB/s a 3.3 s
freeze leaves about 20 KB unread; the entry list (1,286 records, ~87 KB) is the largest single
burst.

Over a real link the buffers are smaller, so the rule must survive a freeze with full buffers.
`TestAPeerThatFreezesThenReadsIsNotClosed`: with the production budget (not shortened), a peer
stops reading for 4 s while a fan-out keeps writing to it, then reads everything; it must stay
connected and receive every byte. **NEGATIVE with §8's 3 s budget**, MEASURED:

```
freezereader656_test.go:69: the freezing peer was closed after 4245010 bytes: write tcp 127.0.0.1:39729->127.0.0.1:38000: i/o timeout (debt peak 3.001s, longest write 2.964s, budget 3s)
--- FAIL: TestAPeerThatFreezesThenReadsIsNotClosed (3.02s)
FAIL
FAIL	github.com/OpenSRO/OpenSRO/server/internal/gateway	3.019s
FAIL
```

**The rule now** (OURS): `SendBlockBudget` = **10 s**, draining 10 s per `SendBlockWindow` = 60
s, and each write's deadline is capped at what is left of the budget (up to `SendTimeout`, 10 s).
The same test passes: debt peak 3.997 s, longest write 3.963 s, all bytes received. 10 s is 3x the
measured 3.3 s freeze and 2.5x the test's 4 s. The steady slow reader is still closed: that test
shortens the budget to 300 ms, and it held its writer 301 ms.

The price: a peer that keeps reading, but slower than it is written to, can hold its writers up to
about 10 s in all before it is closed. A per-session send queue would remove that, and remains
OPEN.

**What a closed player sees:** `NetClient` finds the peer no longer connected on its next
`_process`. `World3D._on_disconnected` changes to `Login.tscn`, which shows its remembered server
and account fields and no reason. That is a clean return to the login screen, not a crash; the
missing "connection lost" line is recorded in TODO.

## Six-hundred-and-fifty-second round: every icon is picked up with one click and put down with the next, and a worn item goes into the bag as the original puts it

The user (2026-09-30): "When I try drag an item from my person into the inventory to a slot I want
it moves it to the next available slot instead. Please let me choose which slot to place the item
in the inventory. Also the click and drag method works differently in the original game. I left
[click] the item once and it sticks to my cursor then I click again to drop it in a slot I want.
This works for items for inventory, storage, npcs, and skills. Basically any icon I drag around,
that's how it's supposed to work."

UI only (no world, map, object, effect, animation, movement or loading code), so no performance
gate. The full reading is `docs/protocol/held_icon.md`; the names are filed in
`recovered_names.tsv`.

### 1. How retail holds an icon (READ, sro_client.exe)

- **One global, `0x0110f604`, is the held window.** `0xb9db10(wnd)` sets it: the old one's vslot 26
  is told it was let go, the new one's vslot 25 is asked whether it may be picked up (a
  `CIFSlotWithHelp` says no when empty, `0x667ab0`).
- **The pick-up is a left RELEASE.** CIFWnd's message handler `0x652540` sends WM_LBUTTONUP to
  `0xb9db10(this)` when the cursor is the normal one (`0x00eb6a48`), none of Ctrl/Shift/Alt is
  down (`GetKeyState 0x11/0x10/0x12`) and the window is pickable (`+100`; every CIFSlotWithHelp is
  created pickable, `0x673cf4`). The slot's press and mouse-move handlers return 0 (vtable
  `0xda18e4` slots 30 and 35, read out of `.rdata`): **there is no press-drag-release**.
- **While held, every mouse message goes to the held window first** (`0xba4450` → vslot 18,
  `0x6523d0`): moves and keys pass on; a left press is swallowed unless it is over a `CIFButton`
  (`0xee9828`) or a `CIFSelectableArea` (`0xee96c0`, the bag's page tabs); a left release offers the
  held window to the control under the cursor and each parent (vslot 28) and then **lets go
  whatever the answer**; a **right press cancels**; everything else is swallowed.
- So **retail carries an item to another bag page by clicking the tab while holding it** — round
  633's open question (TODO.md, inventory_window.md) is answered, and round 633's hover-turn (OURS)
  is gone.
- The icon is drawn centred on the cursor (`CGame 0x8423d0`: `mouse - size/2`).
- **The right button uses** (`CIFSlotWithHelp` vslot 33, `0x685ee0` → `0x682040`): a quick slot
  (kind `0x0c`) is used, a skill in the skill window (`0x19`) is **cast**, a bag item is used.
- The drops: `CIFInventory::vslot_028` (`0x6b5b80`), `CIFUnderBar::vslot_028` (`0x68dd10`: two
  quick slots swap; a skill or an item goes on), `CIFUnderBar::vslot_026` (`0x68d140`: a quick slot
  let go of off the bar is cleared — the `+0x3b1` flag's meaning INFERRED),
  `CGInterface::vslot_028` (`0x78abe0`: the world — a bag item asks the drop warning, a worn item
  says `0x186d` `UIIT_MSG_STRGERR_CANT_DROP_EQUIPED_ITEM_DIRECTLY`).
- **Shift+click on a stack** opens the split box (`0x6b3fa0`); its OK moves into the first empty
  slot (`0x6b62d0`). Not built (TODO).

### 2. Where the unequipped item goes (READ, both binaries)

- **The retail client names the clicked slot.** `FUN_007950b0`, the 0x7034 sender, case worn → bag
  (`0x47 → 0x46`): type 0, source the worn slot, destination `bag slot + 13`.
- **The retail server does not honour it.** `FUN_00523860` dispatches worn → bag to
  `CGObjPC::DetachEquipItem` (`0x5255e0`), which at `0x5258c6` does
  `push 0xd; call CGStorage::FindFirstEmptySlot; mov [edi+0x4],al` — the request's destination
  overwritten with the first empty bag slot — before `MoveItem`. The weapon branch does the same.
  **What the user reported is retail's own server behaviour.**
- The other direction swaps: `CGObjPC::AttachEquipItem` (`0x524cd0`) calls
  `CGStorage::SwapItem(bag, worn)`, so the displaced item takes the bag slot the new one left. Ours
  put it in the first free slot.

**Built: retail's rule, READ, by the user's choice.** The first build of this round honoured the
clicked slot (OURS, commit 9b40d12); shown the reading above, the user chose "Match original". So
the client sends the clicked slot as retail's client does (a trailing int32 on OpUnequip; a request
without it is the old one), and the server parses it and **does not use it**: the item goes to the
first free bag slot, as `DetachEquipItem` does, whether the clicked slot is empty or holds an
item (no swap). **Equip swaps** as AttachEquipItem does (READ), and no longer needs a free bag slot
to do it.

### 3. The client: one controller for every icon window

`HeldIcon` (`client/scripts/ui/hud/held_icon.gd`), owned by HudPanels and fed from its `_input`,
replaces round 633's hand-rolled bag drag and the skill window's drag:

| Window | Left click (release) | Put down on it | Right click |
|---|---|---|---|
| bag | picks up | bag → move/merge/swap (OP_MOVE); worn → unequip (the clicked slot sent, the first free slot used, as retail); store item → buy dialog; warehouse item → withdraw dialog | use (on the release since the review follow-up, READ) |
| paper doll | picks up | bag item → equip (a swap) | — |
| NPC store | picks up | bag item → sell dialog | — |
| warehouse | picks up | bag item → deposit dialog | — |
| skill window | picks up a learned skill | — | **casts it** (READ) |
| quick slot bar | **picks up** (was: cast) | skill/bag item → goes on; quick slot → the two change places; its page arrows and menu button take their click | **uses it** (READ; was the left click) |
| the world | — | worn item → the `0x186d` line; quick slot → comes off the bar | — |

A page tab or any button takes its click while something is held (READ). The source slot is dimmed
while its icon is held (OURS). The skill window's "click puts it on the next free slot" shortcut was
ours and is gone.

## Six-hundred-and-fifty-first round: a berserk character glows red, grows, burns and sounds as in the original, and every other player sees it -- including players who arrive while it lasts

The user's report: "my character doesn't glow red when I activate beserk so make all of the color
and other effects work when activating beserk including audio and extra damage and speed. Make
sure other players can see it too."

What activation did before this round (dev e5bf2ba): the server spent the five orbs, doubled
every blow for 60 s and broadcast 0x30BF kind 4 value 1 and, at the end, 0 (rounds 629/632); the
client used it only for its own orb display. Nothing was drawn on any body, no sound played, and
a player arriving while someone was berserk was never told.

### READ: what the original client draws (docs/protocol/berserk_look.md has every address)

- **On every body, not only the player's own.** 0x30BF kind 4 (`0x8a80a0`) calls the object's
  body-mode setter `FUN_009cf880(mode, 0, extra)` for any object in view; mode 1 ->
  `FUN_009dd620(1, ...)` -> the decoration factory `FUN_00a54020` with key 0x80000000, which the
  name table at `0x00ec73f8` maps to `SYSTEM_CH_HWANMODE` (hwan level 0; level > 0 uses
  `SYSTEM_CH_HWAN2MODE`, OPEN here).
- **Its rows** (MEASURED, Media.pk2 skilleffect.txt `#section skilleffectset`): ACT_S
  `system_hwan_motion.efp` at Bip01 + `player\hwanchange.wav`; seven ACT_L AT_LOOP rows
  (`system_hwan_keep.efp` at Bip01 Spine with `SCT_MAT,64,16,0,140,32,0,1000`,
  `system_hwan_keep_s.efp` at L UpperArm with `SCT_CHAR_SCALE,1.1,1000`, and at R UpperArm,
  L HandMid, R Finger2, L Calf, R Calf); DEACT `system_hwan_disappear.efp` + `player\hwanreturn.wav`.
- **The red is a material colour, not a particle.** SCT_MAT is script flag 0x800 (table
  `0x00ec7378`); the row parser `FUN_00a9d0f0` packs two 0xFFrrggbb colours and an int ms; the
  apply `IDecoSkill::FUN_00a513a0` hands both colours / 255 and the ms to the character's compound
  object (`CObjRendererVS::FUN_00c25800`, CCompChar slot 18); `CCompChar::FUN_00c26ff0` lerps
  colour 1 -> colour 2 over the ms and back (triangle wave, period 2 s); while it runs
  `FUN_00c27180` uploads c11 = light diffuse x colour, c10 = light ambient x colour, c14 = second
  light x colour in place of the mesh material's diffuse (`0xbf0ff1`). The end clears it
  (`FUN_00c258b0`).
- **The growth**: SCT_CHAR_SCALE (0x1000) -> scale target 1.1 over 1.0 s; the end
  (`IDecoSkill::FUN_00a4db00`) returns to the saved scale over the same 1.0 s. Linear, READ
  (review): each frame `FUN_009d1d60` runs `FUN_009c7bc0` on the `+0x72c` record (t += rate x dt,
  clamped at 1; base + t x delta) and hands it to the render object's scale.
- **The own flash**: for the own id, `0x8a827b` fades the weather manager's colour to
  (255, 255, 255, 128) in 0.2 s, then (vslot_009) back to alpha 0 in 0.5 s; vslot_010 draws it
  as a screen quad, TEXTUREFACTOR = the colour, SRCBLEND SRCALPHA, DESTBLEND SRCCOLOR. The fade
  starts from the manager's current colour (alpha 0 after any finished fade); the constructor's
  first RGB (`_DAT_00de523c`) was not read, so the starting RGB is OPEN -- OpenSRO draws white.
- **Arriving while someone is berserk**: the spawn state block carries the body mode (client
  `0x9d1300` -> `+0x470`; server `GObjPC::FUN_004a9b70` writes chardata[3]), applied by
  `FUN_009d17e0` with `FUN_009cf880(mode, 1, 0)` -- arg 1 skips the start effect.

### READ: the mechanics

- **Damage x2** was already right (round 223/`berserk.DamageNumerator`, applied after mitigation
  in `performAttack`, basic attacks and skills). `TestRound651DamageDoublesOnlyWhileBerserk` pins
  40 -> 80 while berserk and 40 again after the end.
- **Duration 60 s** + param 195, already right.
- **Death does not end it** (READ, review): `GObjPC_OnDeath` (`0x4e6980`) and `SetLifeState`
  (`0x4a9c80`) call no SetBodyMode; only `GObjPC::Revive` does (body mode 2) -- as OpenSRO does.
- **A teleport ends it** (INFERRED, unchanged): `GObjPC::HandleTeleportUse` (`0x513590`) calls no
  SetBodyMode; the world-entry setter `CGObjPC::vslot_391` (body mode 2 or 4) replaces mode 1, and
  the teleport reaches it through the re-entry chain (char-data save -> `CharDataSavingCompleted`
  -> 0x34b5 -> the client's 0x34b6 -> the entry rebuilt), whose first link from the teleport
  handler is still not traced. So the server keeps sending the mover 0 on a zone change's arrival.
- **Speed: OPEN.** `CGObjChar::SetBodyMode` (`0x4a9fc0`) entering mode 1 on a PC applies the
  `_RefHWANLevel` row of the byte `+0x1c58` (`FUN_004ac7d0`): `'SPDU'` v -> `SetParam(23/24,
  slot 3, v)` (the percent scale slot; the end, `FUN_004ab060`, writes 100.0 back), `'DABR'` v ->
  params 174-177 slot 2 minus v; then the speed republish (vtable `+0x4e8`). The values are DB
  rows; Media.pk2's `hwanleveldata.txt` is titles only and the box's server package has no
  database, so OpenSRO changes no speed and applies no DABR. The spawn block's third float is
  NOT a berserk speed: it is param 140 (InitStats 100.0), which the server's `FUN_005a1a40` uses
  as a time percentage.

### What changed

- **Server** (`session/combat.go`, `world.go`): `sendBodyModesInView` -- on world entry and on a
  zone change's arrival, a 0x30BF kind 4 value 1 for each other character in the zone that is
  berserk, under that character's berserk turn. OURS: the carrier (OpenSRO's spawn is not the
  retail state block); the content is READ.
- **Client**:
  - `effects/berserk_look.gd` (new): parses `SYSTEM_CH_HWANMODE`'s rows and Script cells from the
    player's own skilleffect.txt, and on a body: the burst + sound (not for a body drawn already
    berserk), the seven kept effects, the pulse colour on every piece of the body (each mesh gets
    a copy of its material with the albedo replaced; the original goes back at the end -- our
    albedo stands for both of the client's light terms, INFERRED mapping), the x1.1 over 1 s and
    back, the end's burst + sound; `flash_alpha` for the own flash.
  - `World3D._berserk_apply`: on every body mode, for the own body or another player's; the own
    flash (an additive screen quad under the HUD); the hwan swing sounds for another player too.
  - `NetClient.body_modes` (`WorldNet.note_body_mode`), cleared/dropped with the buff roster, so a
    body built later -- an arrival list, a relog, a rebuilt body -- takes the look without the burst.
  - QA: `OPENSRO_QA_BERSERK_PROBE=1` prints each drawn player's chest on screen and its tint.
  - Review follow-up: the mover's own 0 on a zone change's arrival (`_arrival_pending`) drops its
    look silently (`BerserkLook.end(host, true)` -> `drop`): no DEACT burst, no `hwanreturn.wav`,

## Six-hundred-and-fiftieth round: Donwhang's and Samarkand's Dimensional Gates can be clicked again

The user reported: "The donwhang teleporter seems broken now too." Labels: READ = recovered from a
binary, MEASURED = counted or run, INFERRED = argued from shape, OURS = this project's choice.

**What was broken (MEASURED).**
- **The tester's session.** The public server's log (opensro-01, the session of 2026-09-30) has
  one teleport, Hotan -> Donwhang at 06:06:19 (`gate=STORE_KT_GATE dest=GATE_WC`). After it, no
  `OpTeleportUse` (opcode 243) arrived and no refusal was logged. So Donwhang's gate never sent a
  request: the break is on the client, before the server.
- **The client.** A boot at GATE_WC's point (102/153 (957, 1508), radius 1) on dev e5bf2ba logs
  `teleport gate STORE_WC_GATE -- no placed object within 10 units of the table's point (962, 8)
  in 103/153; left unbound (not clickable)`. Round 642's own Donwhang run had bound
  `Obj_w_cd_portal_0` in `RealMapObjects_103_153`, 3.3 units off.
- **The cause is round 643, not round 642.** Round 643 made a map object exist once, placed by the
  first loaded region whose `.o2` lists its key, in that region's container and frame
  (`_placed_objects`). Donwhang's portal stands 8 units from the 102/153 edge and both regions list
  it. A player arriving at GATE_WC has 102/153 load first, so the portal is held in
  `RealMapObjects_102_153`. `_bind_region_gates` looked only in the building region's own
  container. The same boot logs `103/153.o2 ... 5 already placed by a loaded region`.
- **Every town (MEASURED, a boot at each gate's arrival point, radius 1, dev e5bf2ba):**

| gate | building region | arrival region | dev e5bf2ba | round 650 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Jangan `STORE_CH_GATE` | 97/168 | 97/168 | `cj_portal`, 3.6 | same |
| Donwhang `STORE_WC_GATE` | 103/153 | 102/153 | **unbound** | `w_cd_portal` in 102/153, 3.3 |
| Hotan `STORE_KT_GATE` | 92/135 | 92/135 | `oas_hot_portal`, 0.7 | same |
| Constantinople `STORE_EU_GATE` | 105/79 | 105/79 | `euro_esteuro_fountain01`, 2.6 | same |
| Samarkand `STORE_CA_GATE` | 107/107 | 106/108 | **unbound** | `samarkand_center_01` in 106/108, 1.0 |
| Alexandria S `STORE_SD_GATE1` | 90/48 | 90/48 | `alex_portal`, 8.4 | same |
| Alexandria N `STORE_SD_GATE2` | 92/50 | 92/51 | unbound | unbound: nearest `alex_portal` at 15.1 (OPEN) |

  Round 650's bound objects and distances are round 577's, when each region still placed its own
  copy.

**Candidates tested and ruled out.**
- **The server's range** (MEASURED). The request from GATE_WC's point to the gate structure
  crosses the region line: 5 on x and 8 + 1920 - 1508 = 420 on z, inside the structure's 800. The
  live run below was served from the arrival point with the player not moved on the server.
  `TestTeleportDonwhangGateFromItsArrival` holds it, with 820 away refused 4. It passes on the
  base too; it is coverage, not the negative.
- **WorldID / instance refusal.** GATE_WC reads WorldID 1. No refusal was logged, and no request
  was sent at all.
- **The talk box closing at once.** No box opened, because the gate was not clickable.
- **Data.** The box's export (`/var/tmp/teleports/csv`) and opensro-01's
  `~/opensro-data/teleport` have the same md5 for all three CSVs. The client reads its tables
  from Media.pk2.

**Why round 642's tests missed it.**
- Round 642's Donwhang and Hotan real-input runs were made on its own branch, before round 643 was
  merged; round 643 then went in beside it in int/r646.
- Round 642's review ran real input at the ferry and the harbour, not at a town gate.
- `teleport_reader_test.gd` (b)-(d) put the portal in the building region's own container, which
  was the only arrangement before round 643. No test put a gate's portal in a neighbour's
  container.
- Round 643 counted what it placed, not what the gate bind then found.

**Fixed (client, OURS within round 577's disclosed stand-in).**
- `_bind_region_gates` takes the table point into the world through the building region's
  terrain group and searches every loaded region's container in world x/z
  (`_bind_gate`, `_nearest_placed_object`). The radius is still 10.
- A gate left unbound is tried again after every later region's commit
  (`_rebind_pending_gates`). That retry is defensive for the real data (round 650's review,
  MEASURED): each of the seven gate portals is also listed by its building's own region, so
  whichever of the two commits first places the portal and the first bind finds it. Its only
  live work today is re-scanning for Alexandria North, which never binds. The review also found
  the live run's Hotan click landed off-screen, at (640, -34), clamped to y 0; it still hit the
  tall portal. The Donwhang click this round is about was on-screen, at (640, 313).
- An unbound gate's log line names the nearest placed object and its distance.
- QA: `OPENSRO_QA_CLICK` takes `wait:<ticks>` between two clicks; the `gate` target takes any
  bound gate, including `STORE_SD_GATE1`/`2`.
- Retail has no counterpart to read for this: retail's gate is a server-spawned structure, and the
  nearest-object bind is round 577's disclosed stand-in. The fix restores what that stand-in bound
  before round 643.

**Live, real input (xdotool on Xvfb, Login -> CharacterSelect; in-memory server built from this
branch with the WorldID export and opensro-01's npcpos; GM account `qa650`, level 40, `/goto
hotan`).** The run clicks Hotan's gate, "Select a teleport area" and "[Donwhang]", then after the

## Six-hundred-and-forty-ninth round: at a raised /speed a click lands the character on its point instead of flickering across it, for the mover and for everyone watching; a walk into an edge stops instead of running in place

The user's report: "when I increase my /speed sometimes when I click around my character starts
stuttering back and forth really fast and you can even see it happening from another player. When
I try to record it looks like I'm just running in place but flickers outside of video."

### The mechanism, measured first (MEASURED, dev e5bf2ba plus a trace hook)

**The trace.** `OPENSRO_QA_MOVE_LOG=1` (new, measurement only) prints one line per physics tick:
- `MOVE self`: this player's position, the click destination, whether the order is in effect, the
  run speed and the distance left;
- `MOVE send`: each `OpMove` sent;
- `MOVE recv`: each `OpEntityMoved` received;
- `MOVE body`: where each other player's body is drawn.

**The run.** Two clients on one Xvfb, each through Login -> CharacterSelect, with real X input:
- A = QaTester (GM) moves; B = QaFriend watches.
- The server is built from the branch, in memory, `-gm-accounts qa,qa2`.
- A typed `/speed 4`, `/speed 8` and `/speed 10` in the chat. After each, it made the same 12
  xdotool clicks around the Jangan spawn (97/168 local 1002, 1020), 1.8 s apart.
- The harness is `/var/tmp/speed649/sp649.sh` and the analyser `mv649.py`, both on the box.

Base, per speed (A's log; a "ping-pong tick" is a tick whose step and the step before it are both
over 1 unit long and point in opposite directions while an order is in effect):

| run speed | ticks | arrivals | ping-pong ticks | longest run |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 200 (/speed 4) | 1659 | 7 | 0 | 0 |
| 400 (/speed 8) | 1662 | 2 | 113 | 113 |
| 500 (/speed 10) | 1615 | 1 | 118 | 115 |

The 113-tick run, at 400 u/s:

```
MOVE self t=3304 ms=69033 pos=(39.018,1.404) dest=(36.849,3.857) order=true speed=400.0 left=3.274
MOVE self t=3305 ms=69049 pos=(34.602,6.399) dest=(36.849,3.857) order=true speed=400.0 left=3.393
MOVE self t=3306 ms=69065 pos=(39.018,1.404) dest=(36.849,3.857) order=true speed=400.0 left=3.274
MOVE self t=3307 ms=69082 pos=(34.602,6.399) dest=(36.849,3.857) order=true speed=400.0 left=3.393
MOVE send t=3304 ms=69033 pos=(39.018,1.404)
MOVE send t=3307 ms=69082 pos=(34.602,6.399)
MOVE send t=3310 ms=69132 pos=(39.018,1.404)
MOVE send t=3313 ms=69182 pos=(34.602,6.399)
```

B, watching (its own clock):

```
MOVE recv 1 ms=64033 pos=(39.018,1.404)
MOVE recv 1 ms=64084 pos=(34.602,6.399)
MOVE recv 1 ms=64134 pos=(39.018,1.404)
MOVE recv 1 ms=64183 pos=(34.602,6.399)
MOVE body 1 t=2995 ms=64078 pos=(37.203,3.512) target=(39.018,1.404)
MOVE body 1 t=2996 ms=64095 pos=(36.553,4.234) target=(34.602,6.399)
MOVE body 1 t=2999 ms=64145 pos=(36.529,4.237) target=(39.018,1.404)
```

Over the whole base run, B received 161 positions. 109 of them reversed the direction of the one
before, with 41 in a row at the longest. B's drawn body reversed 76 times.

**What that is.**
- The two points are 6.67 apart, exactly one step at 400 u/s and 60 ticks a second. The
  destination lies between them, 3.27 from one and 3.39 from the other.
- Both distances are above `MOVE_TARGET_STOP_DISTANCE` (2.39, OURS). The walk stopped only
  inside that distance, and it took a full step toward the point on every tick.
- So each tick jumped over the stop band to the other side, for as long as the order lasted. It
  ended only at the next click.
- The fault needs a step longer than twice the stop, 4.78 units: a run speed over about 287.
  That is /speed 5.74 alone. It is less under a speed buff: /speed 4 under Grass Walk's x1.53 is
  306.
- It then catches a destination whose distance on the final approach falls in a band. At /speed
  10 that band is (2.39, 5.94) of an 8.33 step, which is why it happened "sometimes".
- /speed 4 alone (200, a 3.33 step) cannot do it, and measured 0.

**Why a video shows a body running in place.**
- The body alternates between the two points every tick, 60 times a second. A recording at 30 or
  60 fps samples the same end on every frame, so the character looks still and runs on the spot.
  INFERRED from the tick period; the video itself was not measured.
- The position send goes out every third tick (MIN_SEND_INTERVAL 0.05 s). Three is odd, so each
  send carries the other end: the sends above alternate.
- The server relays each position and turns the heading toward it (`hub.MoveFacing`). Every other
  player's body is therefore pulled to and fro 20 times a second.

**What it was not** (each candidate from the brief, tested):
- *A server speed check.* There is none. `handleMove` stores and relays whatever position the
  client sends (`gm.go`: "the server does not police movement speed"). It sends the mover no
  correction; `rootedMoveAnswer` answers only a move made under the player's own wall. The
  mover's own trace shows the ping-pong before anything reaches the server.
- *The client re-predicting after a correction.* No correction arrives: A's log has no
  `MOVE recv` for itself.
- *The remote interpolation* (rounds 637/638). `lerp` with `min(k·delta, 1)` cannot overshoot.
  B's body followed what it received, and it received the ping-pong.

### Retail's rule (READ)

The rule is from the client decompile on the RE box. It is filed in
`docs/protocol/opcodes/movement.md`, "How the client steps a mover and stops it at its
destination":
- The mover's tick `FUN_009e0e60` runs every frame. It steps `speed × seconds`: `obj+0x444`, or
  the speed slot times mover `+0x8c`; the seconds are the global `0x0110f7fc`.
- For a mover walking to a destination (`+0x80 == 1`), it measures the ground distance to the
  destination (`FUN_009ecc70`). When that distance is **no more than the step**, it **cuts the
  step to the distance** and ends the movement (`+0x84 = 0`).
- So a retail mover lands on its destination and never passes it, at any speed.

### The fix

- `client/scripts/world/click_walk.gd` (`ClickWalk.step`), called by the new
  `World3D._step_click_walk`:
  - within the stop distance, the walk is over (as before);
  - when a full step would reach or pass the point, the velocity is cut to land on it this tick
    (READ, `FUN_009e0e60`);
  - otherwise, the full speed toward it.
- OURS: the early stop at 2.39 units is kept, because `CombatNet.approach_aim` is built on it.
  Retail lands on the point exactly.
- The other players are fixed by the same change. What they draw is what the mover sends, and it
  no longer alternates. The server is unchanged.

### After (MEASURED, the same harness, the same clicks, the branch)

| run speed | ticks | arrivals | ping-pong ticks | longest run |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 200 | 1660 | 7 | 0 | 0 |
| 400 | 1662 | 3 | 0 | 0 |
| 500 | 1614 | 2 | 0 | 0 |

The same click, to the same destination (36.849, 3.857), at 400 u/s. It lands in one tick with
0.000 left and stops:

```
MOVE self t=3332 ms=70007 pos=(34.602,6.399) dest=(34.462,13.284) order=true speed=400.0 left=6.887
MOVE self t=3333 ms=70024 pos=(36.849,3.857) dest=(36.849,3.857) order=true speed=400.0 left=0.000
MOVE self t=3334 ms=70040 pos=(36.849,3.857) dest=(36.849,3.857) order=false speed=400.0 left=0.000
MOVE send t=3333 ms=70024 pos=(36.849,3.857)
```

B receives one position and its body settles on it:

```
MOVE recv 1 ms=65027 pos=(36.849,3.857)
MOVE body 1 t=3028 ms=65038 pos=(35.249,5.765) target=(36.849,3.857)
MOVE body 1 t=3034 ms=65138 pos=(36.564,4.197) target=(36.849,3.857)
MOVE body 1 t=3049 ms=65388 pos=(36.845,3.862) target=(36.849,3.857)
```

Across the whole run:
- A: 0 reversals in 5,674 ticks (the base had 323).
- B's drawn body: 0 reversals (the base had 76).
- B's receipts: 33 reversals, at most 3 in a row. These are consecutive clicks in different
  directions: the clicks alternate sides of the screen.

**Seen in both runs, and fixed by the review follow-up below:**
- Most of the clicks landed beyond an edge north of the spawn. There the walk stopped and held its
  order: 630 to 1,226 ticks per speed stood still with an order in effect, in both runs alike.
  - The edge is at local z 953.6. The follow-up's trace names the footing: `cj_jang_gate`.
  - A first draft of this entry called it the dragon pedestal's edge. That was a guess and is
    withdrawn.
- Retail's tick ends a movement its collision query refuses (bit `0x10000000`, READ). Ours kept
  the movement, so the body ran in place against the edge.
- The base run also had small damped wobbles at that edge: 4-11 reversals of about 0.2 units, at
  400-500 u/s. The branch's run has none. They came with 5.6-6.9 units left, which is less than a
  step of 6.67-8.33, so they were the same overshoot with the edge clipping it (INFERRED). The
  slide itself was not changed.

### Tests

- `client/scripts/world/click_walk_test.gd` (new; the fixtures are synthetic):
  - it replays the pre-649 rule and shows the scenario IS the fault: 118 reversals at 500 u/s
    against a point 4 ahead, and at 306 u/s against 2.5;
  - it shows 200 u/s never reverses;
  - it checks the cut, the full-speed step and the stop;
  - it sweeps 9 speeds (x1 to x15.3) and 400 distances (0.05 to 40): 0 reversals, 0 overshoot,
    and every walk ends;
  - it drives `World3D._step_click_walk` at 500, 306 and 400 u/s: each lands in 1 tick with
    0.0000 left.
- **NEGATIVE, against dev e5bf2ba** (the base client on the box, `git archive`, with the new test
  copied in):

```

### Review follow-up: a walk into an edge ends there instead of running in place

The review measured 16 held episodes in one run, at /speed 1 too. In each, the order stayed in
effect, the body stood 4.7-7.2 short of its point for 59-219 ticks, and the run played on the spot.
This matches "running in place" in the user's report, so it is fixed now rather than parked.

**The rule (READ, `FUN_009e0e60`).**
- When the mover's collision query (`[0x111a02c]` vtable `+0x30`) returns bit `0x10000000`, the
  tick takes the failure path: `+0x84 = 0` and `+0x80 = 0`. The movement ends and the body
  stops.
- OpenSRO now ends a click walk the same way. `World3D._move_on_nav_graph` checks each step;
  when `NavGraph.step_tracked` reports it blocked, it calls `ClickWalk.blocked_ends`, and
  `_end_blocked_click_walk` clears the order.
- A walk to a ground item asks for it from where the walk ended, as an arrival does
  (`_ask_pickup_after_walk`). The server judges the 10 units.
- OURS: our graph slides along a wall and retail's query was not read to. So "blocked" means a
  step that covers no more than 1 % of what was asked. A slide that gets somewhere goes on.
- **An attack's or friendly cast's approach is exempt.** Retail's attack tick re-issues
  `MoveTowardObject` on every pass while out of reach (`docs/protocol/auto_command.md`, phase 1,
  READ), and `_step_pending_attack` re-aims every tick the same way. Their release-in-reach, their
  retry on a too-far refusal (`APPROACH_RETRY_CAP`), and the pickup request are untouched. What a
  retail body shows while its attack approach presses against a wall was not read (docs/TODO.md).

## Six-hundred-and-forty-eighth round: the "broken water" by the Donwhang teleports was the reed beds smeared into streaks, and the reeds stand up again

The user (2026-09-30): "the water in the donwhang region appears glitched or something by the
water ... It happens by all teleports in the region". Their screenshot shows a ferry dock on
stilts over sand. Near the shore the sand carries dotted, hatched lines, and there is a pale speckle
around the huts. The brief's guess was water and terrain z-fighting at near-equal heights. **That was
measured and is not the cause.** The streaks are the Dunhuang reeds, `fw_cd_reeds_l`, the most-placed
animated map object (444 placements), drawn through a skeleton whose root was never set. Since round
645 every clump's skin was bound 1e24 units away, and each clump was drawn as lines running off
toward infinity.

**Labels.** READ: recovered from `sro_client.exe` (decompile and asm on the RE box). MEASURED:
counted on the box. INFERRED: follows from what was read but was not itself read. OURS: this
project's choice.

### The place (READ from the teleport table)

`teleportdata` (the server's CSV) has five Donwhang-region points: `GATE_WC` 102/153 (957, 1508),
`GATE_NPC_WC_FERRY` 100/161 (636, 1482), `..._FERRY2` 98/156 (1025, 601), `..._FERRY3` 91/143
(583, 1858) and `..._FERRY4` 90/143 (464, 879). `whatishere` near FERRY4 lists the ferry dock
`naruter_buil` (173, -62.5, 933), two `w_cd_boat` and seven reed clumps within 500 units. The QA
view at FERRY4 looking west (`--shots w270@464,879:270,-10,45`) shows the user's dock, with the same
hatched lines on the sand. That this is the dock in their screenshot is INFERRED from the matching
buildings.

### The water is not it (MEASURED)

- **Heights.** `waterat -region 90/143`: water blocks in column 0 only, PlaneType 0, plane -60,
  ground -57 to -78. The sand the view looks over is blocks with PlaneType -1: no water is drawn
  there at all.
- **Water that only the depth test hides.** New `waterat -hidden`. The terrain and the water share
  one vertex grid and one triangulation, so the ground and the shoreline alpha are both linear
  across each triangle. The tool samples every drawn block at 0.5 units and adds up where the
  water's alpha is above 0 but the ground stands above the plane. For 90/143 that is **45 square
  units** in the whole region, 25 of them within 0.1 of the plane. A band that small cannot make
  the user's picture.
- **A pixel diff with the water on and off** (new `OPENSRO_QA_NOWATER=1`, same boot and views):
  - the dock view (frame 38): 1,328 pixels change, all at y 282-315 between the dock's piles, which
    is the river behind it;
  - the view back east over the sand (frame 66): **0 pixels change, and the streaks are still
    there**.
- **The reeds hidden** (`OPENSRO_QA_HIDE=reed`, 28 mesh instances): the streaks are gone. Against
  the normal run, 5,595 pixels differ in frame 38 and 891 in frame 66, and they are exactly the
  hatched lines and the speckle.
- **`OPENSRO_NO_MAP_ANIM=1`** draws the reeds as upright clumps: 60,567 pixels in frame 38 against
  the reeds hidden. **`OPENSRO_MAP_ANIM_NO_SHARE=1`** still draws the streaks. So the fault is
  round 645's skinning, not round 647's shared poses.

### Why the reeds smear (MEASURED, then READ)

New `client/tools/probe_map_anim_pose.gd` builds an object the way the world does and skins it on
the CPU. On the base:

```
[root]  rest (0, 0, 0, 1) / (3683467473916534645063680.00, 253813068042076160.00, 4504345567583976629993472.00) | key0 identity / (0, 0, 0)
piece W_cd_reeds_L  136 verts  still size (154.09, 22.15, 104.39)  posed size (3683467762146910796775424.00, 838098202786791424.00, 4504346144044728933416960.00)
```

`w_cd_reeds_l.bsk`'s root stores a local translation of (3.7e24, 2.5e17, 4.5e24) (`dump_bsk_raw`).
Its world bind and inverse bind translations are the same kind of value, so the root was never set.
Every bone on the root stores a world bind equal to its local, so the file itself puts the root at
the origin. The clip keys `[root]` at identity.

`Skeleton3DBuilder` composes each bone's rest from the locals, root included, and binds the skin to
the inverse of that rest. The bind therefore carried -3.7e24, the root's key did not, and each
vertex landed 1e24 away. The vertices weighted partly to the object-space bind drew the lines.

What retail does (READ, a sub-agent on the decompile; BSK_FORMAT.md, "How the client skins"):
- The skin matrix is `InvBind_file x W` in `RTSkeleton::FUN_00c49f20`, `CRTBone::FUN_00c48fe0` and
  `FUN_00c4bcb0`. That is the file's own inverse bind; nothing inverts a composed rest.
- A keyed bone's local comes from the keys alone: `RTSkeleton::FUN_00c49f20` copies the prim's
  stored local only when the bone's blend weight (+0x98) is 0, and builds it from the blended
  quaternion and vector otherwise (`AniMixer::FUN_00c54200` is the loop that blends the tracks;
  round 648's review corrected the attribution).
- So retail never reads the reeds' unset local. Their unset inverse binds are garbage too, so this
  holds only while no vertex is weighted to the root (INFERRED; the reeds' posed size matching
  their still size says it holds for them).

**Round 648's review (MEASURED):**
- Six monster species did not assemble at all on the base (`none of its 9 mesh piece(s) loaded`:
  every bone at 1e24 or NaN, so no piece found a bone) and were drawn as capsule placeholders:
  thief_boss, planar, elemental, uruchidragon, flame_spirit, venefica. They now build as their real
  models and pose sensibly (thief_boss's skirt at y 9.9-29.5 against a rest of 12.3-32.0).
- The reeds site's own gate, which the round had not run: frame 10.72 -> **4.50 ms (FASTER)**;
  entry 7,255 -> 7,236 ms, freeze 2,137 -> 2,116 ms, hitches 2 -> 2 (SAME). The streak triangles,
  1e24 wide, cost about 6 ms a frame at Dunhuang.

**The census** (new `client/tools/census_bsk_bind.gd`, every `.bsk` in Data.pk2, MEASURED):
- 1,208 skeletons; 11 have an unset root: a component from 2.7e20 to 7.7e31, or NaN.
- Those 11 are the reeds, the Tarim rope bridge `oas_tarim_rob_b_brid_01`, `sword_skill_c`, and the
  monsters `flame_spirit`, `thief_boss`, `venefica`, `elemental`, `penon_die`, `planar`,
  `planar_die` and `uruchidragon`.
- In all 11, every bone on the root implies a root at the origin.
- Every other root is within 4,767 units (`roc_event_cam`).

### The fix

`Skeleton3DBuilder.build_skeleton3d`: when the root's stored local is not usable (not finite, not a
unit quaternion, or a translation component over `ROOT_TRANSLATION_LIMIT` = 1e6), the root takes
the rest its children's stored world binds imply, `world_bind x inverse(local)`, from
`root_rest_from_children`.
- The limit is OURS, set in the measured gap between 4,767 and 2.7e20.
- The rule itself uses READ file data.
- A root that is set keeps its own rest. 376 set roots have children that imply something else,
  and they animate correctly from their own rest.
- `SkeletonPose.bone_world_bind` reads the record's second pair.
- The map objects and the character path (`SkinnedBsrAssembler`, `World3D`) both build through
  this function, so the monsters in the list are covered too.

After, with the same probe:

| object | t | still size | posed size |
|---|---|---|---|
| `fw_cd_reeds_l` | 0 s | (154.09, 22.15, 104.39) | (154.09, 22.15, 104.39) |
| `fw_cd_reeds_l` | 1.5 s | | (154.07, 22.32, 104.10), the sway |
| `oas_tarim_rob_b_brid_01`, piece 07 | 0 s | (586.85, 408.10, 383.40) | the same |
| `oas_tarim_rob_b_brid_01`, piece 07 | 1 s | | (586.85, 425.59, 405.20) |

`thief_boss` (`probe_skinning.gd`, group `default`, t = 0) puts its skirt piece at y 9.9-29.5
against a rest of 12.3-31.96.

The dock view after the fix draws the reeds as standing clumps: 59,223 pixels against the reeds
hidden, where the still reeds drew 60,567. The streaks are gone.

### Retail's depth, for the water (READ; not changed)

The world camera's projection has near **1.0** (`fld1` in the camera constructor `FUN_00bae0a0`,
never written again). Its fovy is 60 degrees and its far is the view distance, 3,500 by default.
The device asks for a 24-bit depth buffer (`CGame::vslot_007` raises the minimum depth bits to 24,
0x841ced), and the water pass writes no depth. This client keeps Godot's near of 0.05, which is
about 20 times less depth precision. That is real but small: the hidden-water census below shows
little water that the depth test alone keeps out. It is in docs/TODO.md with the reason not to flip
it blind (the camera's close-geometry clipping).

## Six-hundred-and-forty-seventh round: the Jangan spawn draws at 85 fps instead of 71 with every tree swaying exactly as before, and a zone change no longer leaves the old zone's animated objects behind

Round 645 made the map's skeletal objects move. The rounds 641–646 integration review MEASURED what
that cost at the Jangan spawn (97/168 local 1002, 1020, yaw 0, 1280×720, default radius,
`--print-fps --disable-vsync`, mean of the last 40 samples): 14.1–14.5 ms a frame against dev
8658370's 10.6–11.2 ms and 10.9–11.3 ms with `OPENSRO_NO_MAP_ANIM=1` — about 90 fps down to 70,
all of it round 645's. Round 645's own figure for Jangan (+1.4 ms, at 640×360) understated it; its
entry now says so and points here. This round cuts the cost without changing a pixel, fixes the
driver's zone-change bookkeeping, and records what is left.

### 1. Where Jangan's cost went (MEASURED, before any change)

`MapAnimationProbe` (round 645's split): at frame 3,600 every registered object is switched to one
state and the driver halts; each row compares the mean of the once-a-second frame times from frame
1,200 to the split against those from 2 s after it to the end (140 s runs, one per mode, the
c306c51 path). The same split with `OPENSRO_NO_MAP_ANIM=1` drifted **+0.69 ms**, so a row is good
to about ±0.7 ms.

| Mode after frame 3,600 | Change (ms/frame) |
|---|---|
| `halt`: the driver stops testing, nothing else changes | −0.26 (the driver's own bracket: 450–480 µs) |
| `manual`: the driver steps the 154 players itself | −0.03 (with the driver halted; the `advance()` calls bracket at 874 µs) |
| `strip_player`: players freed, skins and skeletons stay, still | −2.43 |
| `freeze_skel`: as `strip_player`, skeleton processing off | −2.57 |
| `strip_skin`: skins unbound, players and skeletons still running | −2.21 |
| `stripped`: players, skeletons and skins gone (the pre-645 object) | −3.20 |
| `share`: every running copy of a clip on one skeleton (21 poses, lockstep) | −2.29 |
| `unskin_hidden` | +0.60 (inside the drift) |

`census` (new mode, one line): **154 clips running, 222 skinned MeshInstance3Ds (no front-pass
twins), 610 skin binds, 717 bones, 21 distinct clips, 69 clip × sector pairs, and 21 clip × clock
pairs** — every running copy of a clip had the same clock, because the whole view starts in one
frame after the load. The top models are ground cover: `grs_weed02` 32, `c_pondflower` 22,
`grs_water_big` 18, `grs_weed04` 17, then the maples and ginkgos.

So at Jangan the cost is per skeleton, not per drawn instance: freeing the players, or unbinding the
skins, or putting one clip's copies on one skeleton each take away 2.2–2.6 ms of the ~3 ms, while
drawing the skinned instances (`stripped` against `strip_player`) is under 1 ms. The reeds' split in
round 645 had the drawing larger; §5 has it again after this round. Why each skeleton costs so much
is INFERRED from Godot's source, not split further: every changed skin's bone texture is
re-specified with `glTexImage2D` each frame and the skeleton's version bumped, which re-skins every
instance on it by transform feedback (`drivers/gles3/storage/mesh_storage.cpp`,
`_update_dirty_skeletons` and `update_mesh_instances`, 4.2.2).

### 2. Is sharing a pose exact? Retail pauses each object on its own (READ)

- **Per object.** `SWorld::vslot_004` tests each list-2 object's own fade state (obj+0x1e) against
  its own `dist - radius` (`SWorld::FUN_00a38a50`), then, only while that byte is not 0 (asm
  0xa2d9dd), calls the compound's update (slot 14, `call [vtable+0x38]`) with the one global
  `DAT_0110f7f8` for every object of the pass. obj+0x27 is stamped with SWorld +0x6720 so an
  object two sectors list is updated once (asm 0xa2d91b/0xa2da08).
- **So** two objects' clocks are equal exactly when they started in the same pass and were updated
  in the same passes since. A sector leaving the view pauses all its objects together; an object
  crossing the 2,020 edge pauses alone. `Map::FUN_00a1e530` (the draw) only reads the state. BSR_FORMAT.md's
  table has the row.

### 3. What was built (OURS on those READ rules)

`client/scripts/world/map_animation.gd`, `MapAnimation.Driver`, rewritten around three exact savings:

- **Shared poses (`PoseGroup`).** Clips of one Animation that start in the same frame at the same
  clock run as one group: one AnimationPlayer and one Skeleton3D (a copy of a member's, pooled per
  clip) under World3D's new `MapAnimationPoses` node, and every member's skinned pieces bound to
  that skeleton by absolute path, so a region hand-over (round 643) that moves a member keeps it
  bound. Godot skins a piece from the skeleton-space pose (`pose_global * bind`) and the piece's
  own transform, never the skeleton node's (READ, 4.2.2 `scene/3d/skeleton_3d.cpp`,
  `mesh_instance_3d.cpp` `_resolve_skeleton_path`), so a member stays where it is placed.
  - A member whose clock stops **leaves at once**: its own player is seeked to the group's clock
    (its own clock) and its pieces bound back. The group runs until its last member stops.
  - A start **never joins a running group** (OURS, conservative): joining would need the start's
    clock to equal the group's exactly, and the rule avoids having to prove it. The reason first
    given here (Godot copies the process list before the frame's first node, so a group would run a
    frame ahead) is wrong: the driver ticks from `_physics_process`, before the frame's idle
    processing, so a clip started in the tick advances in that same frame (the release review,
    2026-09-30). A group node released in a frame is pooled only at the next tick; that is
    conservative too, and no test pins it.
  - One-shot clips (`LOOP_NONE`, the horses) and object.ifo flag bit 0 objects keep their own
    player.
- **Per-sector range bounds.** With `rho` the farthest origin from a sector's centre and
  `rmin`/`rmax` its radii, every object is in range when `d + rho - rmin < 2020 - 1` and out when
  `d - rho - rmax >= 2020 + 1` (the 1-unit guard band is OURS, so rounding cannot flip a decision).
  A sector decided the same way as last frame is not visited; a sector wholly out of range whose
  objects are all hidden and paused (`quiet`, as registered) is not even view-tested. The plane and
  range tests are inlined, the same expressions as `sector_in_view` and `in_range`.
- **A camera held still** (the same eye and planes, nothing added or dropped) re-tests nothing.

Not done, and why:
- **(b) pausing objects not drawn this frame.** The world's DirectionalLight3D casts shadows
  (`World3D.tscn`, `shadow_enabled = true`) and the water reflection draws the scenery from a
  second camera, so an object outside the camera frustum can still be seen moving; "not drawn"
  cannot be proven from the frustum. Retail runs the clock of every in-range object of a sector in
  view.
- **(d) manual stepping.** No gain (§1: `manual` −0.03 against `halt` −0.26 alone).
- **One Skin per object** (instead of per piece): 222 skins on 154 objects before sharing; on 23
  poses it would save a handful of uploads. Left.
- The update rate is untouched: every running clip still advances every frame by the frame's dt.

`OPENSRO_MAP_ANIM_NO_SHARE=1` keeps every clip on its own player (the A/B, and what the probe's
cost modes need). The QA MAPANIM line gains `poses`, `groups`, `sectors`, `viewed`, `tested` and a
`frame_ms` averaged over every frame since the last line; `MapAnimationProbe` gains `census` and
`freeze_poses`. The synthetic tree the tests build moved to `map_animation_fixture.gd`, shared by
the two suites.

### 4. The zone change (Task 2)

`_clear_region_grid` cleared `_placed_objects` and `_object_containers` but not `_map_animations`.
Sectors are keyed by world position, and a zone change re-origins the world, so the new zone's
objects joined the old zone's sector records (stale centre, stale view and range state, freed
entries only pruned when a visited sector found them). Now `_clear_region_grid` calls
`Driver.reset()` (the records and the pose nodes go), and `_release_region_objects` calls
`drop_under(container)` after handing the survivors on, so what goes with the container leaves the
driver the same frame instead of sitting, freed, in a sector the bounds no longer visit.

### 5. Before and after (MEASURED)

So the reeds' remaining +4.9 ms is Godot 4.2's GL Compatibility drawing of 40 skinned instances,
even when their pose does not change: GPU time, not the pose. Each skinned instance draws from its

4.2 has no way to draw one skinned result at several transforms (a MultiMesh does not skin). It
stays OPEN (TODO.md).

## Six-hundred-and-forty-sixth round, review follow-up: a walled caster's teleport landing is one move to a point the server named, and players who arrive during a zone change's load are drawn

The review confirmed the client roster, the replay, the dedup and the READs (`0x9d1300`,
`FUN_009cf270` skipping the start effect, the server's `FUN_0059cdc0`). It found three things to fix.

### 1. The walled-landing window undid the root (OURS; walls.go, world.go, gm.go)

**What was wrong.** Round 646 took *any* relocated move for 2 minutes after *any* warp, while a
wall rooted the caster:
- it was not one-shot;
- it was not tied to a place;
- it outlived the wall and the session;
- it was armed by every `OpChangeZone` and every gate teleport, including gate teleports whose
  client never sends a landing (`_land_teleport_arrival` sets `_last_sent_pos`).

So a walled player had 2 minutes of free relocations.

**Now** the landing is the reviewer's prototype, tightened:
- **What arms it.** The warp notes the points the server itself sent the caster to:
  - the arrival (`noteZoneWarpLanding`), which is also the point the client stands a gate arrival
    on;
  - the client's spawn spot in the arrival's centre region, when it has one;
  - a GM `/tp` or `/goto` point.
- **The spawn spot is exact.** The ideal was for the server to hold the exact x, z the client uses.
  `worldmap.LandingSpot` now holds `World3D.ZONE_SPAWN_LOCAL`'s row (97/168 -> local 1002,1020),
  and `LandingSpotFor` names it in the arrival's frame. For Jangan in its own frame that is (42, -60).
- **What is taken.** One relocated move within **1 unit** on x and z (`warpLandingTolerance`,
  OURS) is admitted. The reviewer's ±RegionSpan/2 would have allowed a 960-unit jump.
  - The client stands the player on the named x, z. MEASURED in round 646: the gate's local
    957,1508 is exactly the server's -28803,-10148.
  - It is used up by that move (`CompareAndDelete`). A move elsewhere does not use it up.
- **When it is forgotten:**
  - when the wall ends (`wallsEnded`);
  - on logout (`WorldDisconnectHandler`);
  - after the grace.

**Not done: moving the server's own arrival onto the spawn spot.** That would change every entry
and zone-change result that the clients and `TestSingleFrame*` pin, so it is left OPEN for the map
lane. The server now knows the spot; it does not land there.

### 2. The stale `/unstuck` comment

`_unstuck_player` saved and restored `_last_sent_pos` around `_place_at_zone_landing`. That was a
no-op after round 646, and it has been removed, with the comment. `restored_entry_test.gd`'s stub of
`_place_at_region_local` now does what the real one does: it leaves `_last_sent_pos` and sets
`_relocated_pending`. Its "left for the move sync to report" check still passes, now on the real
behaviour.

### 3. The two cheap ones

- **Players who arrive during a zone change's load are now drawn.**
  - From the `OpChangeZoneResult` to the arrival list's layout, `OpEntityEntered` is kept
    (`_arrival_entries`) instead of being built on the old zone's list and freed.
  - `OpEntityMoved` updates the kept snapshot.
  - `OpEntityLeft` takes a player off the result's list (`_arrival_left`).
  - `_replace_others_for_arrival` lays out the result's list minus those who left, plus those who
    entered. Their auras come from the roster, as for everyone.
- **The `/speed`-only `OpBuffEnd` at entry is no longer lost.**
  - `BuffRoster` keeps each owner's last non-zero run speed (`run_speed_of`). A start's or an end's
    0 means unchanged, and leaves it.
  - `_replay_held_buffs` applies this player's own speed after the starts.

### Tests

- **`session/buffreplay646r_test.go`** (wire only, so it compiles on 8b59288):
  - under `-single-frame`, a walled Aria goes to Donwhang and back;
  - a relocation to (900, 900) is refused and does not use the landing up;
  - her landing on Jangan's spawn spot (42, -60) is taken;
  - a second relocation, to a step away or back to the arrival, is refused;
  - after the wall is cancelled and cast again, the old landing is not taken;
  - after a relog, the old landing is not taken.
- **`buffreplay646_unit_test.go`:**

- **`buffreplay646_test.go`.** The walled-landing test now lands on the arrival point (0.5, -0.5)
  rather than an arbitrary (120, -40), which the one-shot landing now refuses.
- **`world/buff_persist_test.gd`:**
  - the roster's run speed;
  - a `/speed` sent before the scene listened becomes this player's run speed;
  - Dave, who entered during the load, is drawn where his last move during the load put him;

## Six-hundred-and-forty-sixth round: other players' skills stay visible after a teleport, a relog or a zone change, where they really stand -- no recast needed

The user's report: "make all skills visible to all players on the server and that persist visually
through teleportation. If someone has a skill and teleports to where a player is, the player won't
see the skill until they recast."

### Reproduced first (MEASURED, dev 8658370, two clients, real input)

Setup (`/var/tmp/fxpersist/e2e/run.sh`, run `r1`):
- two clients side by side on one Xvfb, each through Login -> CharacterSelect, keys and chat sent by
  xdotool after `windowfocus --sync`;
- an in-memory server built from dev, `-single-frame -teleport-dir -teleport-free`, with the skills
  CSV exported from the box's Media.pk2 (deleted afterwards);
- A = QaTester (level 40, GM): Grass Walk 113, the cold imbue 90 and Fire Wall 136 on keys 1-3;
- B = QaFriend (level 40, GM): Grass Walk on key 1.

What the logs show, case by case:

| case | measured on dev |
|---|---|
| both cast at the Jangan spawn | fine. Each log has `EFFECTS aura on character:<other> token N` for every buff |
| A `/goto donwhang` and back, into the same bucket | the auras come back in B's log (`QaTester left/entered the zone`, then the two starts and their auras). **But B drew A and its Fire Wall inside the dragon pedestal at the square's centre, while A's own client stood at the spawn spot, local 1002,1020** (shot `base/03_A_back_in_jangan.jpg`: B's half shows only flames on top of the pedestal) |
| B relogs where a buffed A stands | **no aura**. B.log line 38 is `BUFF start: owner 1 ... skill 113` from NetClient, with no `BUFF start handled` and no aura |
| A relogs where a buffed B stands | **no aura**. A.log line 38 is the start, then nothing. Shot `base/05_A_relogged.jpg`: A sees B with no Grass Walk ring, and B's own view shows it |

Three causes:

1. **The world-entry replay reached nobody.**
   - The server sends the zone's buffs right after `OpEnterWorldResult` (round 616's
     `sendBuffsInView`).
   - NetClient dispatches everything a read delivers in one loop, while CharacterSelect is still
     swapping World3D in. `buff_started` has no listener then.
   - That is the arrival case of the report. World3D also cleared its target book when a zone
     change's loading screen finished, which could drop a replay that arrived during the await
     (timing-dependent; the box's synchronous centre-cell build happened to hold the packets back
     in both runs).
2. **The arrival placement was never reported.**
   - `_place_at_region_local` set `_last_sent_pos` to the new spot, so the send loop saw no
     displacement. Nothing went out until the player walked.
   - The server, and every other client, kept the character, and its buffs' auras, at the server's
     arrival point. For Jangan that is the square's centre, inside the dragon's pedestal (the 11.45
     solid AGENTS.md records at local 1002,917).
3. **A walled caster's landing was dropped.**
   - Round 640's root (OURS) drops every move while a wall stands, and a warp's landing is a move.
   - `/goto donwhang` answered A with `SKILL move: character 1 skill 136 to (-28800, 0, -9600)` and
     `ROOT: the server holds this player at ...`.

### READ: what retail does (both dumps on the RE box; `docs/protocol/skill_buffs.md` "Entering view")

- **A spawn carries the buffs.**
  - 0x3015 (`0x8a6ca0` -> `FUN_008a6bd0`) and the group spawn's 0x3018 reach the shared state
    reader `0x9d1300`.
  - It reads u8 count, then per buff: u32 skill id, u32 token, and a u8 creator for `efta` rows.
    For the self player only it also reads the remaining ms.
- **The spawned buffs are attached like live ones.**
  - `FUN_009cf270` turns them into `IDecoSkill`s on the new body through `FUN_00a54020(token, obj,
    skill, 1, 0, creator)`, then `FUN_009cd050`.
  - That is the factory and the per-object list (`+0x284`, which the target window reads) that
    0xB0BD uses (`0x8a5d49`).
  - The difference is arg4 1: `FUN_00a53850` skips the start effect and plays the lasting one
    (`0xa538e3..0xa538fb`).
- **The server writes the block.** `FUN_0059cdc0` writes it from the book at `obj+0xa30`. It
  counts records with Param1 3, in state 2, and not an `lnks` link. Observers get no remaining time.
- **OPEN:** whether a retail teleport re-spawns the object for observers. The view wrappers
  `0x534340` / `0x5344b0` were not traced to the teleport code.

### What changed

**Client:**
- `net/buff_roster.gd` (**new**, `BuffRoster`) keeps every owner's active buffs per connection:
  - OpBuffStart adds;
  - OpBuffEnd removes;
  - an owner's OpEntityLeft or a monster's death drops that owner;
  - a successful OpEnterWorldResult or OpChangeZoneResult starts it over, since the server re-sends
    after each;
  - connect and disconnect clear it.

  NetClient updates it before emitting each signal. A replayed start's time left is counted down
  from its arrival, and a run-out timed buff is not replayed (OURS).
- **World3D:**
  - `_replay_held_buffs` runs once the handlers are connected in `_ready`, over the ordinary start
    handler: auras, target book, own ownership and run speed.
  - `_build_buff_board` seeds the bar from the roster. The board keys by token.
  - `_fx_resync_owner` runs whenever a body is built: another player's in `_spawn_or_update_other`,
    a monster's, and every owner after a zone change's arrival list (`_replace_others_for_arrival`,
    split out of `_on_change_zone_result`, which now rebuilds the book and the DefenseEfp/wall table
    from the roster).
  - Only the ACT_L aura is put back, as retail's arg4 1 does.
- **`SkillEffects.ensure_aura`**: a re-sent start for a buff whose aura already draws on that body
  keeps it and moves only its time bound. Before this, each zone replay rebuilt the effect.
- **`_place_at_region_local`** leaves `_last_sent_pos` at the server's position. The spawn-spot
  placement then goes out at once as a relocated OpMove.
- QA: `OPENSRO_QA_CLICK_WAIT=<ticks>` delays the gate click, so a run can cast by real input first.

**Server (OURS, walls.go / world.go / gm.go):**
- A zone change, a gate teleport or a GM `/tp` or `/goto` marks the next relocated moves of a
  caster its wall roots, for 2 minutes (`warpLandingGrace`), as the warp's landing. It is taken,
  stored and relayed.
- A walk is still dropped, and a relocation with no warp is still dropped.
- The replay itself (`sendBuffsInView`) was already right. The new tests pin who is sent what on
  each event.

### Verified (MEASURED, the branch, run `r2`, shots in `fxpersist_shots/fixed/`)

- **Both cast, then A `/goto donwhang` and `/goto jangan`:**
  - B.log after each warp: `left the zone`, `entered the zone`, then `EFFECTS aura on character:1
    token 6: skill 113` and `token 7: skill 136`.
  - A.log after each: B's `token 5` aura. A's own auras are kept (no rebuild line: `ensure_aura`).
  - A's QA line ends at local 1002,1020. Shot `12_A_jangan.jpg`: **B sees A beside it, burning, at
    A's real spot**, not in the pedestal.
- **B relogs where the buffed A stands:**
  - B.log: `EFFECTS aura on character:1 token 6: skill 113`, `token 7: skill 136`, `EFFECTS resync
    character:1 (their body was built): 2 buff(s) held, 2 on a drawn body`, `BUFF replay (world
    entry): 2 buff(s) held for 1 owner(s)`.
- **A relogs where B (Grass Walk) stands:**
  - A.log: `EFFECTS aura on character:2 token 8`, then `BUFF replay (world entry): 1 buff(s)`.
  - Shot `14_A_relogged.jpg` shows B's ring in A's view. On dev the same case (`base/05`) had none.
- **The target window:** A's click on B gives `HudTarget: buffs of character:2 -- 1 main, 0
  second: 113@(0, 0)` (shot `15`).
- **A real gate:**
  - B `/goto donwhang`. A starts at the Jangan gate (local 1230,1380) with `OPENSRO_QA_CLICK=gate
    OPENSRO_QA_TELEPORT=2`, casts Grass Walk and Fire Wall by keys, then the gate's Move sends
    `1 -> 2`.
  - Server: `teleport ... from=GATE_CH dest=GATE_WC zone=donwhang`.
  - B.log: `QaTester left/entered the zone`, `EFFECTS aura on character:1 token 9: skill 113`.
  - A.log, at `RealTerrain_102_153` local (957, 1508): `EFFECTS aura on character:2 token 8`.
  - The wall had ended before the gate, when its MP drain ran out (`toggle: MP short of the drain,
    ended`), so only Grass Walk crossed.
  - The two stood ~550 units apart, so shot `17` shows each alone. The logs are the measurement.
- **Same-zone relocation:** under `-single-frame` every `/goto` and gate here is one. The body is
  rebuilt (left, entered) and the aura re-attached, as above.
- **Not applicable: walking out of view and back.** OpenSRO's server has no view range; a zone

## Six-hundred-and-forty-fifth round, review follow-up: the user's tentacles are the Tarim thorn vines, and they move; animated objects end at 2,020 as in retail; the view test is per sector

The review confirmed the first commit's reading of the clip, looping, speed, flag bit 0, the absence
of wind, the lockstep phase and the bounds, and that still objects are unchanged. It also found
errors, which this follow-up fixes.

### 1. The user's tentacles (MEASURED, then READ)

The report's screenshot shows a canyon with a rope bridge high overhead and curling, spiked
tentacles. That is not the Taklamakan pit round 645 showed. Only the first line of the report was
about tentacles; "animated assets in Taklaman too" was a second report.

**Finding the canyon (MEASURED).**
- The rope bridge is `res\bldg\china\dunhuang\field-obj\w_cd_bridge01_01.bsr`. It is placed at
  about y 1,015 in 94/145, 94/146 and 95/147.
- The tentacles are the Tarim thorn vines. `res\nature\oasis\tarim\oas_tarim_thorng01_01.bsr` is
  skeletal: 4 skinned pieces, 19 bones, and `oas_tarim_thorng01_01.ban` (10,000 ms, cyclic). Its
  `default` group has a type-0 entry.
- It is placed 10 times in 93/144–96/148, including three times in 95/147.
- A render at 95/147 local (700, 800), looking along +Z, reproduces the picture: tentacles on the
  canyon wall and the bridge overhead.
- With `OPENSRO_QA_HIDE=thorng01`, 28 mesh instances (the pieces `oas_tarim_thornG01_01..04`) were
  hidden, and most of the tentacles in the picture went with them.

**The ones left (READ against the census).** `thorng02_01`, `thorng04_01_01`, `thorng05_01_01` and
the `thornp*` vines remain. They have no skeleton, no mod section entries and no per-vertex motion
section.
- Retail builds an AniMixer only for a skeleton plus a clip (`CCompChar::FUN_00c2b930`).
- Retail has no wind or wave code.
- These models carry no TEXANI or DY* mod.

So nothing in the client moves them, and they stand still in retail too. The user's moving
tentacles are `thorng01`, which the first commit already plays.

**Motion (MEASURED).** Changed pixels with `compare -fuzz 3%` inside a rectangle on a tentacle's
body, excluding sky, against frame 200:

| Rectangle | +1 s | +2 s | +3 s |
|---|---|---|---|
| Right tentacle, this branch | 323 | 549 | 587 |
| Right tentacle, dev 8658370 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| Left tentacle, this branch | 139 | 206 | 238 |
| Left tentacle, dev 8658370 | 0 | 0 | 0 |

The ground control rectangle was 0 in every run. The Taklamakan pit (101/130) still measures 1,379
to 4,133 over 0.5–3 s. The whole upper rectangle does change on the base (1,545 at +2 s), but a diff
image puts all of that change in the sky.

### 2. The range is 2,020, measured from the placement origin, strictly (READ)

- **The range.** At asm 0xa2d961 the caller loads `DAT_00ec54b0` (2500.0). At 0xa2d967 it subtracts
  the double at 0xde4f58, which is 480.0. It passes the result to `SWorld::FUN_00a38a50`.
- **The test.** That function takes the object out of range when `range <= dist - radius`.
- **The distance** is from the camera (+0x20a6..) to obj+0x57/+0x5b/+0x5f, the placement origin
  (asm 0xa2d92a).

So `OBJECT_RANGE` is 2020, the test is strict, and the distance is measured from the node's placement
origin, not the meshes' centre. Per view-distance setting the range is 720 / 1,520 / 2,020.

The first commit said 2,500 and the mesh centre. That text is corrected in the round's own entry
below and in BSR_FORMAT.md.

### 3. Drawing ends where the range ends (READ; OURS for the fade)

**READ (`SWorld::FUN_00a38a50`).**
- State 0 is hidden.
- Entering range within two-thirds of it (`range >= 1.5 × (dist - radius)`, the double at 0xe1b7e8)
  goes straight to state 2, drawn at alpha 255. Farther out it goes to state 1, whose alpha rises by
  `512 × dt` (0xde5148) to 255 (0xd83108).
- Leaving range goes to state 3, whose alpha falls back to 0.

The object is updated only while its state is not 0 (asm 0xa2d9dd). It is drawn only then too:
`Map::FUN_00a1e530` checks the state beside its frustum test.

**Here.** The driver hides an animated object out of range: `visible = false` on its root, with its
clock paused.
- **OURS:** the 0.5 s alpha fade is not drawn; the object is switched.
- **Scope:** only the animated objects. Retail applies the rule to every list-2 object, and making
  still scenery end at 2,020 is a visibility change for the loading lane, so it is noted in TODO.md
  rather than made.

### 4. The view test is per sector, not per object (READ; the sphere is OURS)

The first commit tested each object's bind-pose sphere against the frustum. That froze clips whose
geometry travels far from their bind pose while they were in view: the hawk (up to about 880 units
away), the boats and the goldfish.

**READ.** Retail visits only the sectors whose +0xba2 flag the frustum rasterisation
(`Map::FUN_00a2b370`) sets, and it updates the objects of those sectors. A sector not visited keeps
its objects' state: their clocks stop, and their drawn state stays as it was.

**Here.**
- Each placement is filed under its `.o2` sector: its 320-unit cell of the region's 6 × 6 grid.
  That this is the same grid as the frame's sector list is INFERRED.
- The cell's X-Z circle is tested at the object's height against the camera frustum. That sphere
  is OURS; retail rasterises a ground footprint.
- The test runs once per sector per frame. That replaces the old slicing, so there is no lag of up
  to 4 frames.
- A sector leaving the view pauses its clocks and leaves its objects drawn, as retail does.

### 5. The rest

- **The LAST type-0 entry wins (READ).** `ResObject::FUN_00c0f500` reads each entry's type and file
  index, then calls `FUN_00c0f470`. On an existing key, that function overwrites the entry's clip
  pointer (asm 0xc0f4e6). A negative file index stores null (asm 0xc0f58d). `clip_entry` now takes
  the last type-0 entry and returns null when it has no clip. No placed model has two type-0
  entries (MEASURED over the census), so nothing on the map changes.
- **After a one-shot (READ).** The mixer unlinks the finished clip (`AniMixer::FUN_00c53e80`). With
  none left, `AniMixer::FUN_00c54200` only clears the bones' blend weights: `CRTBone::vslot_004`,
  asm 0xc47a20, zeroes +0x98 and +0x9c. The apply (`CRTBone::vslot_005`) and the skeleton update
  (`FUN_00c4c320`) run only when a clip was evaluated, so the body keeps its last pose. Holding the
  last key matches this. It is no longer OPEN.
- **`OPENSRO_NO_MAP_ANIM=1` now builds the pre-645 object.** `MapAnimation.prepare` returns before
  reading anything, so there is no skeleton, skin or player. It is a clean baseline: B measures like
  dev below.
- **The census is exact now.** `animates` builds the model with `ObjectLoader.load_object` and looks
  for its player. The corrected counts:
  - **144 models**, 92 of them placed, **2,275 placements** in 226 regions.
  - Two models name a type-0 clip and still build still: `cj_ferry_boat_old`, whose `.bsk` has a
    root and no other bone (`bsk: no bones parsed`, 1 placement), and `demon_air rock01`
    (0 placements).
  - The round's entry said 146 models and 2,276 placements; that counted these two.
  - 0 placements animated before round 645.

### 6. Cost (MEASURED)

**Method.** 640×360 movie runs with the HUD hidden and one held viewpoint. Each row averages 30
samples, frames 100–390. The box is shared with other lanes. The columns:
- process: `Performance.TIME_PROCESS`;
- render CPU / GPU: the viewport's measured render times.

**The variants and order.** A is this branch, B this branch with `OPENSRO_NO_MAP_ANIM=1`, and C is
dev 8658370 with only the QA print patched in. They ran interleaved A, C, B, twice at each site.

| Site | Run | Process ms | Render CPU ms | Render GPU ms | Sum ms | Draws |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Jangan maples (97/168; 456 registered, 123 running) | A1 / A2 | 14.37 / 14.38 | 4.84 / 5.10 | 4.56 / 4.79 | 23.77 / 24.27 | 4,777 |
| | C1 / C2 | 12.73 / 13.29 | 4.88 / 4.87 | 4.70 / 4.70 | 22.31 / 22.86 | 5,336 |
| | B1 / B2 | 13.96 / 12.86 | 5.41 / 4.87 | 5.20 / 4.67 | 24.57 / 22.41 | 5,336 |
| Dunhuang reeds (98/157 at 900, 900; 197 registered, 57 running) | A1 / A2 | 9.91 / 11.56 | 2.01 / 2.28 | 1.89 / 1.91 | 13.81 / 15.75 | 1,655 |
| | C1 / C2 | 5.85 / 6.42 | 2.11 / 2.26 | 1.50 / 1.82 | 9.46 / 10.50 | 1,641 |
| | B1 / B2 | 5.92 / 5.68 | 2.01 / 2.08 | 1.62 / 1.43 | 9.55 / 9.19 | 1,641 |

- **Jangan.** A costs about +1.4 ms against C, all in process time. Render time is equal or lower:
  559 fewer draws, because the animated objects beyond 2,020 are now hidden.
  **Corrected in round 647:** that understates it. At the Jangan spawn (1002, 1020, yaw 0) at
  1280×720 with `--print-fps --disable-vsync`, the rounds 641–646 integration review MEASURED
  14.1–14.5 ms a frame against dev 8658370's 10.6–11.2 ms and 10.9–11.3 ms with
  `OPENSRO_NO_MAP_ANIM=1` (about +3.3 ms, 90 fps to 70); round 647 MEASURED +2.86 ms (14.05
  against 11.19) and cut it to +0.60 ms. See round 647.
- **Reeds.** A costs about +4.8 ms at 640×360 in those runs, nearly all process time. At 320×180
  in the split runs below it is about +2.9 ms.

#### Where the reeds' cost goes (MEASURED)

The split was made with `MapAnimationProbe`: `OPENSRO_QA_MAPANIM_SPLIT=420` with
`OPENSRO_QA_MAPANIM_MODE=<mode>`.
- At frame 420 every registered object is switched to one state, and the driver halts.
- Each run compares the median process time of frames 100–420 against frames 440–800, per frame,
  at the reeds view (98/157 at 900, 900, 320×180, 197 registered, 57 running).
- An `OPENSRO_NO_MAP_ANIM=1` run (B) gives the drift across the two windows: 6.21 and 6.10.
- The earlier rapid in-run toggling was abandoned: switching skins and players back and forth
  every 12–50 frames swamped the differences.

| Mode (after frame 420) | Before (median ms) | After | Change | Motion after (px, f700 vs f760) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `stripped`: players, skeletons and skins gone (the pre-645 object) | 9.10 | 6.37 | −2.73 | 36 |
| `strip_skin`: skins unbound, players and skeletons running | 9.16 | 7.10 | −2.06 | 34 |
| `strip_player`: players freed, skins and skeletons stay still | 9.17 | 8.01 | −1.16 | 29 |
| `freeze_skel`: as `strip_player`, and skeleton processing off | 8.55 | 7.92 | −0.63 | — |
| `share`: every running copy of a clip draws from one skeleton | 8.66 | 8.08 | −0.58 | 26,950 (still moving) |
| `unskin_hidden`: skins unbound on the objects not drawn | 9.07 | 9.05 | 0 | 27,020 |
| `manual`: the driver steps the players itself, timed | 9.02 | 8.63 | — | 26,880 |

Brackets from the same runs: the driver's GDScript loop takes **0.20 ms** a frame (0.05 ms of it the
sector view tests). The 57 players' `advance()` calls take **0.53 ms** (`mix_us`, timed around
manual stepping).

**The split of the ~2.9 ms:**
- **Driver: 0.20 ms** (bracketed).
- **AnimationMixer: 0.53 ms** (bracketed).
- **Skeleton pose and skin-bone updates: about 0.6 ms.** This is what `share` saves, and it matches
  `strip_player` less the mixer.
- **Skinned mesh instances being drawn: about 1.6 ms.** That is `strip_player`/`freeze_skel`
  (8.0 / 7.9) against `stripped` (6.37). It does not depend on the skeleton processing
  (`freeze_skel` equals `strip_player`). It does not come from the skinned objects that are not
  drawn (`unskin_hidden` changes nothing), and the draw count is the same (1,655). So it is the
  cost of the visible skinned instances in Godot 4.2's GL Compatibility renderer, even when their
  pose does not change.
- That process time here includes the render step is INFERRED from these numbers: the monitor's
  split was not read from the engine.

**What was cut: nothing.**
- The largest part, about 1.6 ms, is inherent to Godot's skinned instances. Their pose is the
  object's animation, and drawing them skinned is what makes them move.
- Retail advances every map-object clip every frame by the frame's dt
  (`SWorld::vslot_004` → `CRTAniCyclic::vslot_002`), so a lower rate would change what the player
  sees.
- The one cut that keeps every pose is sharing a skeleton between copies whose clocks are equal.
  It is worth about 0.6 ms. The clocks are equal only while the copies have been in range and in
  view for the same frames, because retail pauses each object on its own. Clock-grouped sharing
  with re-grouping on every pause is left OPEN (TODO.md). The `share` probe itself runs every copy
  in lockstep, so it is not a candidate.
- **B against C.** B now measures like C (Jangan 22.4–24.6 against 22.3–22.9; reeds 9.2–9.6 against
  9.5–10.5), so the A/B switch is clean.

## Six-hundred-and-forty-fifth round: the map moves — trees sway, the Taklamakan tentacles writhe, and reeds, grass, flowers, lanterns, boats and grazing animals play their own animations

A player reported on v0.1.461 that "some map assets around the game world are animated, like these
tentacles", with a screenshot of spiked tentacles in the Taklamakan. They also said there are "more
parts of the map that you'll need to find". Round 625 had left the trees still: their `.bsk` and
`.ban` were read, but the pieces were placed rigid and the skinned leaves drew in bind pose. This
round counted what moves, read how retail plays it, and plays it the same way.

over all 4,050 regions' `.o` and `.o2` list-2 records, de-duplicated by model and position. The
classes:

| DYVERTEX/DYJOINT/DYLATTICE mod (cloth: tents, sails, banners) | 143 | 550 | 175 |
| per-vertex motion section in a mesh | 139 | 767 | 174 |
