## Six-hundred-and-thirty-seventh round, headings in the arrival lists: the players already standing where you arrive face the way they face, and you re-enter facing the way you left

Same user-visible bug, last case: the players listed in `EnterWorldResult` and `ChangeZoneResult`
(already in the zone when you enter it or change into it) were drawn facing heading 0. The follow-
up above sent a heading only on `OpEntityEntered`. Labels: READ, MEASURED, INFERRED, OURS.

**The tail (OURS protocol, READ conversion).**
- Both results carry a headings tail after `Seated`: a u16 count equal to `len(Others)`, and one
  u16 wire angle per other in list order. The angle is `proto.EncodeMovementAngle(world.WireAngle(h))`,
  as `OpEntityEntered`'s.
- `EnterWorldResult` then adds the entering character's own wire angle.
- `Seated` is always written when the tail follows (a zero count), and so is `Restored` before it,
  as `Seated`'s own doc comment asks of the next field.
- The tail is written only when a snapshot carries a heading (the server's always do,
  `entitySnapshotFromWorld`). So a result built without one is byte for byte the older payload,
  and the round-570/573/607 compatibility tests stand unchanged.
- Older decoders stop after the seated list. Checked on both sides: the b5911a1 client decodes the
  new payloads without an error (its "decodes" check passes; only the heading checks fail), and
  the Go test reads the new tail with the Seated reader, which stops before the headings.
  `decodeSeated` became `decodeSeatedRest`, returning what follows: the orphans probe
  (`internal/systems`) refused the old name once only a test called it.
- A count that does not match the list is a decode error, in Go and GDScript.
- The client reads each angle with `RemoteFacing.from_wire_angle` and places the listed body facing
  it (`_spawn_result_others` -> `_spawn_or_update_other`). That is the spawn's bare
  `FUN_009c4260`, READ in the follow-up above.

**Persistence (OURS).**
- `character.HeadingStore` is implemented by the MemStore and the SQLStore; the SQLStore adds a
  `heading DOUBLE PRECISION NOT NULL DEFAULT 0` column. It is kept off `Character`, as
  `InventorySizeStore` is, so the `_CHAR` mapping is unchanged. `_CHAR` declares no heading
  column, and whether retail keeps a facing across a logout is not read.
- `savePosition` saves the heading with the position.
- `handleEnterWorld` restores it when the position is restored (`restoredHeading`,
  `Hub.SetHeading`). It then sends it on the entering character's `OpEntityEntered`, in the lists'
  own tail, and to its own client, which faces it (`World3D`'s entry reads `result.heading`).
- With `-persist-position` off, an entry faces 0 as before.

**Tests.**
- Go `session/facing_test.go` `TestArrivalListCarriesTheHeadingsOfThoseStanding`, end to end:
  - Aria walks toward -z (the relayed moves are read first, so both are in the hub).
  - Bram changes to Donwhang and back.
  - His `ChangeZoneResult` ends `00 00 01 00 00 40`: no one seated, one heading, wire angle 16384
    (heading pi).
- Go `session/facing_codec_test.go`:
  - both results round-trip the headings and the own heading;
  - the tail is the older payload plus `Seated`(0) and the angles;
  - a Seated read of the new tail stops before the headings;
  - a mismatched count is refused;
  - `TestPersistPositionKeepsTheHeading`: a walk toward +x, a logout, the store holds pi/2, and the
    re-entry's own heading and the hub's are pi/2.
- Client `net/world_test.gd` `_test_decode_headings`: the enter-world tail (Bram pi, own pi/2),
  the zone-change tail with Bram seated (pi/2), a mismatched count, and an older payload (NAN).
- Client `remote_facing_test.gd`: a listed body with heading pi is drawn facing -z.
- NEGATIVE against b5911a1 (the follow-up's commit):

      --- FAIL: TestArrivalListCarriesTheHeadingsOfThoseStanding (0.19s)
          facing_test.go:129: the arrival list ends 39 37 2f 31 36 38, want the tail 00 00 01 00 00 40 (no one seated, 1 heading, wire angle 16384)
      FAIL Bram, standing there, faces heading pi (got nan)
      FAIL and this player re-enters facing pi/2 (got <null>)
      FAIL a zone-change result's tail seats Bram and faces him pi/2 (seated [42], heading nan, error )
      FAIL a headings count that does not match the list is a decode error
      4 FAILURES
      FAIL someone in the arrival list with heading pi is drawn facing -z (rotation 0)
      1 FAILURES

  (The older payload ends at the frame "97/168"; the older client decodes the new one without
  error.)

**Real input, measured (two clients on the box, this branch's server and client).**
- A signed in through Login -> CharacterSelect and walked by real clicks: east, then south-west.
  A stopped facing **124.17 degrees**, its own model and its last movement agreeing (124.16).
- Then B signed in. B's first sample of A, from `EnterWorldResult`'s list, faced **124.17
  degrees**, at A's own position (31.039, -65.343).
- A first attempt lost its Xvfb display partway (the X server on `:97` was gone when B started);
  the rerun is the measurement.
- Screenshot: `facing_shots/lists_B_enters_sees_A.jpg`. The numbers are the evidence.

**Checks.**
- `check`: ALL LOAD. `tests`: 157 suites, 0 failing.
- Go: every package ok, run with the shared cache.

## Six-hundred-and-thirty-seventh round, review follow-up: your own character turns as others do, an arrival faces the way it last walked, and a teleport turns nobody

The review confirmed the round's core: the 3 pi rate, the millisecond clock, the shorter way, the
1e-6 keep and no axis flip. It found no jitter in a real-input curve and zig-zag. It asked for six
things. Labels: READ, MEASURED, INFERRED, OURS, OPEN.

**1. The re-aim guard, corrected (READ).**
- `0xB021`'s reader aims when `obj+0x714 != 0`, or when the new destination is more than 5 units
  (squared 25.0) from the mover's CURRENT POSITION. The mover is at `obj+0x668`, so
  `obj+0x6bc/+0x6c0` is mover `+0x54/+0x58`. The round had called this the held destination.
- `obj+0x714` is mover `+0xac`, the movement order in effect:
  - `FUN_009e0550`, `FUN_009e04b0` and `FUN_009e08a0` set it;
  - the stop/position message (`FUN_008a4f80` -> `FUN_009e00f0`), `FUN_009e0150`, `FUN_009e11e0`
    and `FUN_009e0960` clear it;
  - arrival in the ordinary tick does not: `FUN_009e0e60` clears `+0x84` only.
- Fixed in `docs/protocol/opcodes/movement.md`, the round's entry below, and `docs/TODO.md`. The
  guard stays unapplied (OURS; the reason is in TODO).

**2. The local player turns at 3 pi (READ).**
- A ground click goes `UI_SILKMALL::FUN_009ec240` -> `FUN_009eb2a0`; a return of 1 sends the move.
  The server's echo, `0xB021` -> `FUN_008a5750` -> `FUN_009e0550`, turns the player's own mover as
  it turns anyone's.
- `FUN_009eb2a0` has two exceptions:
  - With no order in effect, a click under 5 units away (squared 25.0, `0xe1b8a0`) is not sent.
  - With an order in effect, a click that meets all three of these is not sent:
    - it is 100 or more units away (squared 10000.0, `0xd82efc`);
    - the order's destination (`obj+0x684/+0x688`) is 100 or more away too;
    - the angle between the two (`FUN_0045c590`, y zeroed) is 5 degrees or less
      (`0xdb9828` = 0.0872664600610733).

    Instead `FUN_009e04b0` re-aims the local mover and SNAPS the heading (`FUN_009e0050`).
- `RemoteFacing.click_rule` is that rule. `World3D._try_set_move_target` applies it: "ignore"
  moves nothing and "snap" sets `_player_turn_snap`. `_aim_local_player` and `_step_local_turn`
  replace `rotation.y = atan2(dir.x, dir.z)`.
- The turn runs while standing too, as `FUN_009e0e60` runs it when `+0x88 & 0x31`.
- `_player_move_order` is set by an accepted click and cleared by a zone change or the player's own
  skill move. Both mappings are INFERRED: OpenSRO has no stop message.
- A ground click still drops a pending attack or friendly cast even when the filter does not send
  it. That keeps round 622's behaviour (OURS: where retail drops a pending action is not read).
  `friend_cast_test` caught the first ordering.

**3. The spawn heading, end to end.**
- Server:
  - `world.Entity.Heading` holds the client's heading.
  - `Hub.MoveFacing` updates it from each walk's delta with `world.HeadingToward`, which is
    `FUN_009ed130` in OpenSRO's frame: +z is 0, +x is pi/2, and a step of 1e-6 or less keeps it.
  - `Hub.Move`, used for relocations and skill moves, leaves it alone.
  - `Hub.ChangeZone` carries it.
  - A fresh entry has heading 0; it is not saved with the position.
- The wire:
  - `EntitySnapshot.EncodeEntered` appends the u16 wire angle,
    `proto.EncodeMovementAngle(world.WireAngle(h))`, where the wire angle is `h - pi/2`.
  - It goes AFTER the snapshot rather than after x/y/z. An older client's
    `decode_entity_entered` reads one snapshot and stops. The same snapshot sits inside the
    `EnterWorldResult`/`ChangeZoneResult` lists, which have fields after them, so those lists carry
    no heading here. They do now, in a tail of their own (the entry above).
- Client:
  - `WorldNet.decode_entity_entered` reads the angle with `RemoteFacing.from_wire_angle`: READ
    `FUN_008a5640` + `FUN_009c40b0`, the wire angle times 360/65535 degrees, plus pi/2, wrapped
    with the float constants.
  - `_spawn_or_update_other` places a new body facing it and snaps a drawn one, ending any turn.
    This is READ: `FUN_009d17e0` stores the spawn's angle with a bare `FUN_009c4260`, and a new
    mover has no turn (`0x9e0cd0` zeroes `+0xa4`).
  - `FUN_009ca320` aims a body that spawned moving. OpenSRO's arrivals never do, so nothing aims.

**4. Snap or turn, per path (READ, then matched).**
- The stop/position message snaps to the server's angle AND ends the turn (`FUN_009e00f0` ->
  `FUN_009e0050`). OpenSRO's monster stop has no angle. It now snaps to the turn's own target and
  ends the turn (INFERRED: the server's heading is the last leg's).
- The angle-only message `FUN_008a4ec0` turns at 3 pi unless mover `+0x94` is set. `FUN_008a78b0`
  (a u8 angle) snaps with a bare `FUN_009c4260`. OpenSRO sends neither; both are documented.
- The skill action reader `FUN_00a54be0` snaps with a bare `FUN_009c4260`, which does NOT end a
  turn. So two snaps no longer cancel a turn:
  - the cast start's snap toward the target;
  - a standing monster's snap toward its target (`_face_monster_toward`).

  Labelled INFERRED as that path. The angle is OURS: it points at the target, where retail's
  comes in the message.
- The monster spawn heading still ends the turn (a new object, READ).
- "Each snap cancels a turn" in the round's entry is corrected there.

**5. A relocation turns nobody (OURS rule, READ reason).**
- Before this, the entry placement ((0,0) -> the first position) and the gap-recovery snap-back
  turned the puppet toward the jump. Measured in round 637's run: the entry leg read "move 145.0,
  face 145.0".
- Retail places an object at a message's source position (`FUN_009e11e0`) without aiming it.
- OpenSRO's `OpMove` now has a trailing flags byte, bit 0 = relocated. Older servers read three
  floats and ignore it.
  - `World3D._position_relocated` sets it when the sender knows (`_relocated_pending`: the gap
    recovery, `_place_at_region_local`).
  - It also sets it when the displacement since the last send exceeds the physics step's walk
    since then (`_walked_since_send`) by `RELOCATE_MARGIN` (1.0, OURS). This catches QA/GM
    placements and the unstuck landing.
- The server skips the heading on a relocated move and relays the flag on `OpEntityMoved`. Older
  clients read 20 bytes and ignore it.
- The receiver places the body at once and does not turn it.
- A skill's move already snapped (`OpSkillMove`).

**6.** A dying monster's turn is dropped (OURS). The player's own turn stops at death (OURS).

### Tests

      FAIL a stop mid-turn snaps to the turn's heading, +x (FUN_009e00f0 -> FUN_009e0050) (got (0, 0, 1))
      FAIL and ends the turn
      FAIL a standing monster turned to its target keeps its turn (a bare FUN_009c4260, INFERRED)
      FAIL World3D has no _aim_local_player

## Six-hundred-and-thirty-seventh round: other players face the way they run, and they and monsters turn toward it at the game's own rate

The user's report on v0.1.460: "when I see other players on the server it doesn't show them running
in the direction they're facing. So you'll see them running sideways or backwards." Labels: READ
(from `sro_client.exe`'s decompile or disassembly, or its PE image), MEASURED (on the render box),
INFERRED, OURS, OPEN.

### 1. Reproduced by measurement

- MEASURED: two clients on the box, through Login -> CharacterSelect with real X input, against a
  server built from dev 5a82339 (`-in-memory`, `-monster-ai`). A (QaTester) walked 8 directions by
  real clicks around its own body. B (QaFriend) logged A's puppet every 50 ms with the new
  `OPENSRO_QA_FACING_LOG=1`. Each line has the drawn position and the way the MODEL faces, read
  off the skeleton's global basis (the body's front is the skeleton's -Z, MEASURED in round 533).
  `client/tools/facing_measure.py` turns the lines into movement against facing.
- Before (dev 5a82339 plus only the log hook), per leg, the movement heading and the facing:

  | leg | move | face | off |
  |---|---:|---:|---:|
  | E | -76.4 | 0.0 | 76.4 |
  | W | 76.4 | 0.0 | 76.4 |
  | N | 0.0 | 0.0 | 0.0 |
  | S | 180.0 | 0.0 | 180.0 |
  | NE | -36.6 | 0.0 | 36.6 |
  | SW | 124.9 | 0.0 | 124.9 |
  | NW | 47.1 | 0.0 | 53.3 (mean) |
  | SE | -124.9 | 0.0 | 124.9 |

  The puppet always faced world +z, whichever way it ran: 18.1% of its moving samples were within
  2 degrees of the movement, and those were only the leg that happened to run +z.
- MEASURED, monsters (18 bodies, 24,987 moving samples after the first 3 s): 99.8% within 2
  degrees. Their longest stretch off by more than 2 degrees was 183 ms, a sample across a leg's
  corner. Monsters faced their path already; they were snapped to it at each leg's start.
- NPCs do not move in OpenSRO (they are placed statues, `NpcFacing`), so there was nothing to
  measure.

### 2. The cause

- READ in this checkout: `World3D._on_entity_moved` set only the body's walk target
  (`_other_body_targets`). Nothing ever set another player's `rotation.y` on a move, so the body
  kept rotation 0. The only turn was the cast start's snap toward a target (`_on_skill_cast`).
- The monster path differs: `_apply_monster_leg` set `rotation.y = MonsterMotion.facing_yaw(...)`
  at every leg. That is why monsters were right and players were not.
- OpenSRO's player protocol carries no angle. `OpEntityMoved` is a character id and a position.
  The mover's client streams positions (`MIN_SEND_INTERVAL` 0.05 s), not retail's destinations. So
  the angle-units question does not arise for players: there is no angle to convert.

### 3. What the client does (READ)

- **The message.** `0xB021`'s reader, `NetProcessInNavAndSkill::FUN_008a5750`:
  - reads the object id and the movement (`FUN_008a5640`);
  - reads an optional source position; when it is present, `FUN_009e11e0` places the object;
  - for a destination (kind 1), calls `FUN_009e0550(region, dest)` on the object's mover. It does
    this when `obj+0x714` is non-zero or when `FUN_009ed1e0`'s SQUARED distance between the mover's
    current POSITION (`+0x6bc/+0x6c0`, mover `+0x54/+0x58`) and the new destination exceeds 25.0
    (`0xe1b8a0`). Corrected by the review. This entry first called `+0x6bc/+0x6c0` the held
    destination; `+0x714` is mover `+0xac`, the movement order in effect (see the follow-up
    above).
- **The aim.** `FUN_009e0550`:
  - takes the vector from the object's position (`+0x74`) to the destination
    (`FUN_009ecc70`, which zeroes the y);
  - makes a heading of it with `FUN_009ed130`, starting from the current heading
    (`FUN_009e0020`, `+0x8c`);
  - calls `FUN_009e02f0(heading, 0)`.
- **The heading of a vector.** `FUN_009ed130` (0x9ed130..0x9ed1cd):
  - `len = |v|`;
  - if `len <= 1e-6` (`0xe1b848`) the output is left alone;
  - otherwise `a = acos(-z_local / len)`, and the heading is `a` for `x >= 0` and `2 pi - a` for
    `x < 0`.
- **The turn.** `FUN_009e02f0` (0x9e02f0..0x9e0461), from the disassembly, since the decompile loses
  the x87 stack:
  - `d = target - current`, and `sign = -1` (with `d = -d`) when `d < 0`. When `d > pi` (`0xd81948`)
    the sign flips and `d = 2 pi - d`: the shorter way.
  - `step = elapsed * 9.42477798461914 / 1000.0`:
    - the two doubles are at `0xde3128` and `0xd83268`, read out of the PE image;
    - `elapsed` is an unsigned int (`+2^32` when negative, `0xe1b7c8`).
  - It stores the target at mover `+0xa8` and points the travel direction (`+0x68`) along the
    TARGET at once (`FUN_009ec850`).
  - When `step <= d` (fcom, C0|C3 at 0x9e039d):
    - the heading becomes `current + sign * step`, wrapped into `[0, 2 pi)`;
    - the turn stays on (`+0x88` bit 0, `+0xa4 = 1`);
    - the turn's clock restarts (`+0xa0` = the object's `+0x3c`).
  - Otherwise the heading is the target and the turn is over.
  - Both paths store through `FUN_009c4260`, which wraps into `[0, 2 pi)` and writes `+0x8c`.
- **Every frame.** The mover's tick `FUN_009e0e60` (called from 0x9d1fac) calls `FUN_009e0c10`,
  which calls `FUN_009e02f0(+0xa8, obj+0x3c - +0xa0)` while `+0xa4` is set. It also runs for a
  mover that is not moving, when `+0x88 & 0x31`.
- **The clock.**
  - `obj+0x3c` is CObj's millisecond clock: the scene loop `FUN_00ba34e0` adds the frame's
    milliseconds (`DAT_0110f7f8`, which `FUN_00ba4020` sets each frame, clamped to 3000) to
    `+0x3c` after each object's update (0xba359b..0xba35a1).
  - Every character is a CObj (RTTI: CICUser : CICharactor : CIGIDObject : CIObject : CIEntity :
    CObjChild : CObj).
  - So the turn rate is **3 pi radians a second** (9.42477798461914 is 3 pi at float precision). A
    half turn takes a third of a second.
- **The heading-only form** (kind 0, `FUN_009e08a0`) goes through the same `FUN_009e02f0`, so it
  turns at the same rate. Its wire angle is converted by `FUN_009c40b0`, which adds pi/2
  (`0xe1b8f0`) and wraps. So the wire angle `a` is `h - pi/2`, which faces `(cos a, sin a)`
  region-local (x east, z north): counted from east toward north. The spawn reader
  `FUN_009c3a70` (0x9c3adf..0x9c3b0a) does the same conversion.
- **When it stops.** A body that stops keeps its heading: nothing but `FUN_009e02f0` writes it, and
  nothing calls that without a message.

### 4. The frame (READ, then checked)

- `0x9ec850` makes the heading's facing `(sin h, 0, -cos h)` region-local (round 630). The region
  group mirrors z (`World3D.minimap_facing`), so in world space the facing is `(sin h, cos h)`.
  That is where a node with `rotation.y = h` points its local +Z.
- Another player's front is its node's +Z (the skeleton is turned PI inside it), so its
  `rotation.y` IS the client's heading.
- A -Z-front monster's `rotation.y` is `h - pi` (`RemoteFacing.yaw_of`).
- The test checks it both ways: `(sin h, -cos h)` mirrored equals the direction the heading came
  from, and so does the node's +Z.
- There is no mirror between the two turn directions: yaw and heading are the same number. So the
  tie at exactly pi turns the way the client's does.

### 5. The fix

- `client/scripts/world/remote_facing.gd` (new, pure) is `FUN_009ed130` and `FUN_009e02f0` with the
  rate above.
- `World3D._aim_remote_body` is the aim (`FUN_009e0550`). `_step_remote_turns`, called every
  physics frame after the other bodies' lerp, is the tick.
- Another player: each `OpEntityMoved` (and a snapshot for a body already drawn) aims the body from
  where it is drawn toward the new position.
  - OURS: OpenSRO streams positions, so each position is treated as the destination.
  - The retail 25.0 squared-distance guard is NOT applied. Corrected by the review: it compares
    the new destination with the body's current POSITION, and only while no movement order is in
    effect (see the follow-up above). Applied to OpenSRO's stream, it would drop the first
    sample (about 2.5 units away) of each walk after a spawn or placement, and nothing after
    that.
- A monster's leg now turns at the same rate instead of snapping (`_apply_monster_leg`). The
  snapping turns stay snaps. Each cancelled a turn in progress; the review follow-up (above) now
  matches each path to the client instead:
  - the cast start's turn toward the target;
  - a standing monster turned to its target (`_face_monster_toward`);
  - a spawn heading (`_face_monster_heading`).

  Whether retail turns or snaps in those three cases is not read (OPEN).
- OURS: the elapsed time is the physics frame's float milliseconds, where the client uses whole
  milliseconds per frame.

### 6. Tests

- `client/scripts/world/remote_facing_test.gd` (new, 33 checks, ALL PASS). It covers:
  - the heading of 7 vectors;
  - the 1e-6 early return;
  - the frame check;
  - the rate (3 pi);
  - 100 ms turning 0.9425 rad;
  - a half turn not done at 333 ms and done at 334 ms;
  - the shorter way and its wrap both ways;
  - the tie at pi.
- On a bare World3D, it also covers:
  - 8 directions each walked for a second: the worst leg is 0.00 degrees off;
  - a half turn at 90.00 degrees after 10 frames and done at 21;
  - a stop keeping its facing;
  - a position on the body leaving the facing;
  - a monster's leg that does not snap: 54.00 degrees after 6 frames, on its destination once done.
- `monster_motion_test.gd`'s leg-facing check now steps the turn (0.5 s) before it looks. ALL PASS.
- `remote_godot.sh tests`: 157 suites, 0 failing. `go build ./... && go test -count=1 -p 1 ./...`:
  all packages ok (the server is unchanged).
- NEGATIVE: the same file run against dev 5a82339 (a clean worktree of the base, shipped to its own
  render dir):

      FAIL RemoteFacing exists
      FAIL World3D steps remote turns each frame
      FAIL after walking each of 8 directions the body faces its movement (worst 180.00 deg)
      FAIL 10 frames into a half turn it has turned 90 deg, at 3 pi rad/s (got 0.00)
      FAIL 21 frames (0.35 s) in it faces the new way (off by 180.00 deg)
      FAIL a monster's leg does not snap it round: it still faces +z as the leg starts (got 90.00 deg)
      FAIL 6 frames in it has turned 54 deg toward +x (got 90.00)
      7 FAILURES

### 7. After the fix, measured (the same two-client run, this branch's client)

- Per leg, with the steady part after the first 0.4 s:

  | leg | move | face | mean off | max off |
  |---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
  | E | -80.0 | -80.0 | 0.01 | 0.02 |
  | W | 80.0 | 80.0 | 0.01 | 0.03 |
  | N | 0.0 | 0.0 | 0.00 | 0.00 |
  | S | 180.0 | 180.0 | 0.00 | 0.00 |
  | NE | -47.2 | -53.9 | 0.61 | 5.44 |
  | SW | 124.2 | 124.2 | 0.02 | 0.03 |
  | NW | 83.2 | 85.9 | 1.36 | 3.96 |
  | SE | -124.2 | -124.2 | 0.01 | 0.01 |

- MEASURED: the NE and NW maxima come from A's own path bending near its end, from -40.7 to -83.2
  degrees on NE. The facing follows it within one 50 ms sample, which is the turn rate at work.
- The turn itself was MEASURED on B: 27.0 degrees per 50 ms sample (-162 -> -135 -> -108 -> -81),
  which is 540 degrees a second, 3 pi.
- The time to come within 2 degrees matched the angle turned. A 135-degree start was aligned after
  250 ms; 135 / 540 = 250 ms.
- After the first 3 s:
  - A's puppet's stretches off by more than 2 degrees were turns: 10 of them, longest 319 ms,
    median 272 ms.
  - Monsters were 98.4% within 2 degrees, with turns up to 423 ms (a 180-degree turn plus a
    sample).
- Screenshots (for a human only; the numbers above are the evidence): the session scratchpad's
  `facing_shots/`, before and after, B's view of A in each direction.
- Observed once, at world entry: a monster whose body the list moved mid-leg walked 7.4 degrees
  off its facing for 0.6 s until its next leg. The leg's facing is aimed once per leg, in the base

### Left open

See `docs/TODO.md`, "Other bodies' facing (round 637)":

## Rounds 633-635 integration review (int/ui2): nothing new lands past a lowered bag size, the portrait's ambient is clamped, the chat's penalty line sits where the client puts it, and the text table loads rows as the client does

The final review of int/ui2 (dev b9bbf07 + rounds 633-635 and their follow-ups, merged at 14c4889)
confirmed the follow-ups' READs against the decompiles and ran two clients with real input through
Login (the portrait in Jangan and after `/goto donwhang`, every window's frame, the bag's pages, a
drag across pages and to a quickslot, the doll's arrows, gold colours, every chat channel, the
notice, a global, the size modes). It found these; all are fixed here. Before is 14c4889.

**1. A lowered bag size placed new items past itself (OURS rule, tightened).** round 633's
`inventory.KeepHeld` raised the size every operation used to the highest held slot + 1, so with
`-inventory-size 32` and an item in slot 60, pickups, buys, trades and withdrawals filled slots
32..59 and any item could be moved to 59: the bag never came back to 32 (a throwaway test: 28
extra adds succeeded). Now the stores keep two bounds (`SetKeepHeld`): the REACH (size, raised to
the highest held slot + 1) for listing, removing, durability and moving OUT, and the configured size
for every NEW placement -- AddItem's stacking and free-slot search, a move's target, a swap into a
held slot (refused), and the trade's space check (`inventory.PlacementCapacityOf`, counting only
slots within the size). `TestKeepHeldReachesHeldSlotsButPlacesWithinTheSize` (both stores): 32
items fill 0..31, the 33rd is ErrNoRoom, moves to 32/59/60 and the swap into 60 are refused, a
stack of the held item goes to slot 1 rather than onto 60, and emptying 60 brings the size to 32.

**2. The bag expansion grew the reach.** `useExpansion` took `CapacityOf` (the raised reach) as its
base, so with no stored size it stored 61 + 32, or refused an expansion the configured 32 allows.
It takes `PlacementCapacityOf` now; `TestBagExpansionGrowsTheConfiguredSizeNotTheReach` stores 64
(and fails against the old base with the 0x18fe refusal). `/invsize` shows the configured size and,
when items are held past it, how far they stay reachable.

**3. The doll's measurement lines flooded the log.** Every 50 ms repeat of a held arrow printed the
yaw and a three-bone pose line (~40 lines a second, measured on the live run). They print on an
arrow's press and release and on the reset now.

**4. The portrait's ambient is clamped (READ).** `Map::FUN_00a1baf0` clamps world+0x6853..0x685b to
[0, 1] in the same block as the diffuse (0x00a1cc50..0x00a1cc88); `zone_light_colors` passed
channel 3 through. No change on the box's archive (its highest channel-3 component is 0.925); an
archive above 1 would have lit the face too bright.

**5. The chat's penalty line (READ).** 0x7ab1b0..0x7ab1d6 places +0x468 (ID 52,
GDR_CHAT_STA_PENALTY) at its own x and +0x464's (ID 15, the size button's) y + 3 (`add ecx,0x3`);
it was at + 2, the authored 380 - 378.

**6. The text table loads rows as TextStringManager 0x8cac30 does (READ).**
- The service column: a row is loaded only when column 0 reads 1 (`0xb9cc80(0, 1)`, `cmp eax,1`
  at 0x8cb110..0x8cb118). On the box's archive no real key changes; the rows skipped are the
  continuation lines of multi-line values (57 in textuisystem, 129 in textdata_object), which had
  been read as keys.
- A first row with no English: the loader reads ONE column, 0x8c5370(language) -- the CGame loads
  (0x849215..0x8493ad) pass -1 as the first-choice language, and 0x8cace6 sets that slot to -1, so
  0x8c6a90's compare with L"0" (DAT_00e1804c) never chooses -- and stores the field as it stands.
  So a key whose first row has no English holds that column's "0" filler (or blank) in the
  client. Ours fell back to the Korean column 2 or the token; it keeps the English column's own
  field now. The box's Rebecca Event Hats (SN_ITEM_ETC_E060823_SATGAT_INT3_M/F), whose first row is
  all "0" and whose English row comes after it, read "0", as in the client (were "??? ?? (?)").
  On the box's archive this is 450 textuisystem keys (313 of them "0"), 2179 object names (1849
  "0"), 490 speech lines; of the Jangan-area names, seven (event NPCs, two Tiger Woman variants
  and a Strong Mangnyang).

**7. Stale comments** in ui_text_table.gd (last row wins), ui_builder.gd (the archive's font is
Tahoma: its first row says Arial) and hud_panels.gd (the doll's turn direction is READ).

Not done: the dungeon light (`Map::FUN_00a255c0` gives the object shader an ambient-only light in a
dungeon). This client loads no dungeon, so there is nowhere for it to apply yet (OPEN).

The review of ff30b8b confirmed:

It found five things wrong or missing. Labels: READ, MEASURED, INFERRED, OURS, OPEN. The detail is
in `docs/protocol/skill_buffs.md`.

**1. The category end ran before the gate (READ; fixed).**

  stealth: a lower level of it, or a Grass Walk inside its re-use delay.

  0x4aced4).

  `FUN_0059b480`. That function runs the category end at 0x59b745, just before

  test.

  `TestRound636ReviewRefusedCastKeepsStealth`.

  - it gives the `qest`+`trap` pair.

**3. The target test's `FUN_0059dc80` (READ; built).**

**4. The 18 `dttp` rows with a state byte (READ; matched).** These are `SKILL_CH_FIRE_DETECT_*`

## Six-hundred-and-thirty-sixth round: Fire Protection no longer stacks, one Grass Walk runs at a time, and a GM's /speed makes testing faster

The user's report on v0.1.460:
- Fire Protection could be cast again and again, stacking;
- three different Grass Walks could run at once;
- they asked for a `/speed` command for testing.

Round 616 modelled only `FUN_0059d870`'s GroupID branch. This round read the whole function, its
bit test and the bit set behind it, and the category end. Labels: READ (`SR_GameServer.exe`, the
dump and `srv.asm` on the RE box), MEASURED (the retail export), INFERRED, OURS, OPEN. The detail is
in `docs/protocol/skill_buffs.md`, "The recast rule" and "Every row, by rule".

**1. Why they stacked (READ + MEASURED).**
- `FUN_0059d870`'s list walk passes over every record whose skill carries `cbuf` (0x59d908). All
  five Fire Protections (`SKILL_CH_FIRE_GANGGI_A..E`) carry it. So the GroupID branch never saw an
  active Fire Protection, and OpenSRO had nothing after the list.
- Retail has something after the list: the **bit test** (0x59dad2). `FUN_0059db10` tests the row's
  `ovl2` and Action_Overlap bytes against a 256-bit state set at `book+0x1b0`.
  - `SkillBook::SetGroupBits` (0x59dc00) fills that set. A buff's engage sets its bytes (0x5842ce)
    and its end clears them (0x582c8c).
  - Every Fire Protection carries Action_Overlap **3**, so the second one meets bit 3 and is refused

## Six-hundred-and-thirty-fifth round, review follow-up: the portrait is lit by the zone's light, as the client lights it, and every body layer draws

The review of acd31b6 confirmed the camera, the yaw, the mask, the dirty triggers, the re-render on
equip, the berserk overlay, the relog and the cost. It found the light wrong. It also read the
camera's rotation axes: the dispatch table at 0x00ec7840 resolves them to RotationX / Y / Z, and
`FUN_00bae580` forms `M0 = RZ·RX`, then `R = M0·RY`. They are READ now, not INFERRED. Labels:
READ, MEASURED, INFERRED, OURS, OPEN. Addresses are in `docs/protocol/player_mini_info.md`, "The
portrait".

**1. The portrait's own light never reaches the avatar (READ).**
- The render's D3DLIGHT9 (frontal, 0.7 / 0.3) goes to the DEVICE's SetLight (0x007b7a2b).
- `CGame::FUN_00bc13d0` always builds CObjRendererVS, and every object draw uses a vertex shader
  (`CObjRendererVS::FUN_00bf05e0`).
- The shader's light constants come only from `vslot_025` (0x00beecc0). Only the world draw
  (`Map::FUN_00a19160`) and the dungeon draw (`Map::FUN_00a255c0`) call it.
- So retail's avatar is lit by the zone's light as it stands when the portrait renders.

**The zone light (READ):**

| part | value | where |
|---|---|---|
| Direction | normalize(−1, −1, 0) (DAT_01109510; to-light (0.707, 0.707, 0)) | `Map::FUN_00a2f370`, 0x00a300c2 |
| Diffuse | world+0x6847 clamped to [0, 1], × 0.6 | 0x00d86fc0, applied at 0x00a1d1b6.. |
| Ambient | world+0x6853 | 0x00a19262 |

- I traced the two world fields to their environment channels in `Map::FUN_00a1baf0`:
  - +0x6847 comes from record+0xf0, **channel 2** (DiffuseColor), 0x00a1bbf3;
  - +0x6853 comes from record+0x124, **channel 3** (ObjectAmbientColor), 0x00a1bc29.
  - Both ease toward their targets by frame time.
- OPEN: the 0.8 factor when world+0x2e54 is set, the halving when world+0x26bb is set, and the
  constant targets when world+0x2eb4 == 1. All three are taken as clear.

**2. c10 multiplies the object's own colour (READ), not the material's.**
- The colour is `[[renderer+0xc4]+0x14..0x1c]` (0x00bf59ce..0x00bf5a04).
- CCompoundObj slot 21 (`CCompChar::FUN_00c255e0`) sets it.
- The constructor `FUN_00c32e50` stores **0.6** there (0x00d86fc0, at 0x00c330ed).
- c11 is the material colour (+0x10, MEASURED 0.588) × the diffuse (`FUN_00bf2360`, 0x00bf2504).
- The face is square to the camera, so it has n·l = 0 and gets `2 × 0.6 × channel 3 × texel`.
  The diffuse falls on the top of the head and the camera-right side.

**3. The plausible fixes.**
- Blended layers are now mapped. A StandardMaterial3D with alpha blending gets a blending variant
  of the portrait shader.
- MTRL mod passes are now mapped. The portrait keeps the mod's own shader (stage ops, alpha func
  and ref, blend) and injects its vertex colour as the DIFFUSE, unshaded.
- `unmapped_materials` is 0 on all four bodies.
- The mask shader takes the block's modulate.
  - The first try multiplied by fragment `COLOR`. That COLOR already holds the texture, so it
    darkened the picture.
  - MEASURED: the first r2 block renders came out visibly darker than their own buffers.
  - The modulate is now read in `vertex()`.

**4. The world's own directional light is not changed here.** Its angle is READ now, but changing
it changes the whole world's look. `docs/TODO.md` records it as a world-lighting item for the
user to see first.

**Shipped.**
- `PlayerPortrait.set_zone_light(channel 2, channel 3)` takes the zone light and re-renders a
  dressed portrait when the light changes.
- `World3D._apply_real_environment_lighting` pushes the zone's two channels at the same
  reference time the world uses (OURS: retail's day clock is not modelled). That function runs
  on a zone load, i.e. world entry or a teleport — when retail's `FUN_00786f30` → `FUN_006abc50`
  dirties the portrait.
- The block's creation pushes a light applied before it existed.
- MEASURED, in-world (Jangan): `portrait zone light at block creation: diffuse channel (0.7255,
  0.7214, 0.7165) ambient channel (0.6784, 0.6745, 0.6627)`, then `portrait dressed (...)`.
- The tool calibration now uses the zone light: expected 160, got 160.

**How bright it is now — the honest answer** (`portrait_shots/r2_*`, four bodies each in Jangan,
environment 15, and in environment 58, the darkest ambient in `environment.ifo`):
- The authentic result is **darker than acd31b6's**.
  - Jangan face: `0.81 × texel`, against `1.18 × texel` before.
  - MEASURED at the centre texel: CH man 0.627 against 0.773, and EU woman 0.690 against 0.894.
  - Buffer means are about the same (0.152 against 0.141). The top of the head and the right
    side now catch the diffuse.
- The comparison against retail is rough: a different zone (retail's is Hotan), a hat, and a

| | mean | median | 90th percentile |
|---|---|---|---|

| ours, acd31b6 (CH woman) | 96.7 | 77.6 | 180.1 |

## Six-hundred-and-thirty-fifth round: the player block's circle shows the character's own face, bright, the way the client renders it

The user asked for the black circle at the top left to show the character, bright and visible.
Retail's screenshots show a face there. Round 629 had read that `FUN_007b7740` renders the
player's model from the `Bip01 Head` bone into a 128x128 buffer, but not which camera float
did what. This round finishes the read and draws the portrait. Labels: READ, MEASURED,
INFERRED, OURS, OPEN. Addresses are in `docs/protocol/player_mini_info.md`, "The portrait".

**1. The model is the equipment window's avatar (READ).**
- `IFMainPopup::FUN_006a1d50` returns the CIFEquipment page (popup +0x7c0).
- Its CCObjAnimation at +0x36c is the model, the same dressed body the equipment window turns.
- The render plays animation 0x3c on it and steps it once (`FUN_00a5ac80(1, 0.0)`).
- 0x3c is 60, which is ANI_POSE in the client's name map.
- MEASURED (`client/tools/probe_portrait.gd`): every player body tested lists ANI_POSE in its
  `default` group only. CHAR_CH_MAN_FIGHTER and CHAR_EU_MAN_WARRIOR use `man_pose.ban`;
  CHAR_CH_WOMAN_FIGHTER uses `woman_pose.ban`.
- After the render, the model's yaw and animation 0 are restored.

**2. The camera (READ from 0x007b7875..0x007b790a and `CGFXVideo3d::FUN_00bae810` /
`FUN_00bae580`).** The render copies the game camera and changes these fields:

| field | value | address |
|---|---|---|
| +0x10, the look-at target | the head bone + (0, 1.0, 0) | 0x00e1b7f0 |
| +0x34 | 0 | |
| +0x38 | 0.2 | 0x00da95f8 |
| +0x3c | 0 | |
| +0x40, the distance | 6.5 | 0x00da95f4 |
| +0x50, the vertical field of view | 30.0 degrees | 0x00d82ef0 |

- The field of view goes through pi/180 (0x00e1b8d8) into `FUN_00aa4ef0`, a
  `PerspectiveFovLH`: `cot(fov/2)/aspect`.
- FUN_00bae580 builds `R = RotZ(+0x3c) * RotX(+0x34) * RotY(+0x38)`.
- The eye is `target - (0, 0, distance) * R`, and the up vector is `(0, 1, 0) * R`.
- So 0.2 is a yaw about the head, and the look is level.
- INFERRED: which D3DX rotation each dispatch pointer is. 0x00ec7798, 0x00ec779c and 0x00ec77a0
  are D3DX's X, Y and Z in its own order. The camera-mode presets in the same function only
  make sense that way: RotX(±pi/2) looks up or down, and RotY(pi/2, 3pi/2, pi) looks to the
  sides and back.
- The avatar is turned to 0.1 rad (`FUN_00a5a8c0(0.1)`, 0x00e1b7fc). The CCompoundObj yaw
  setter (slot 12, `CCompChar::FUN_00c26e70`) builds `[[c,0,s],[0,1,0],[-s,0,c]]`.
- INFERRED: the avatar object belongs to that family.

**3. The light (READ, 0x007b796d..0x007b7a64).**

> **Corrected by the review follow-up above.** This light is dead fixed-function state. The avatar
> is lit by the zone's light through `vslot_025`, and c10 uses the object's colour (0.6).

- A D3DLIGHT9 of type 3, set as light 0 and enabled:

| part | value | address |
|---|---|---|
| direction | (0, 0, 1) | |
| diffuse | 0.7 | 0x00d82f04 |
| specular | 0.58 | 0x00da95f0 |
| ambient | 0.3 | 0x00d82f00 |
| range | 1000 | 0x00da95ec |

- The render also sets LIGHTING on, z on and blending off.
- It sets fog start = end = 1000 through `CObjRendererVS::vslot_014`, vertex constant c16.
- The skinned-object vertex shader (`vertexshader2.c`, READ) lights with
  `oD0 = c10 + max(0, N.c9) * c11`.
- `vslot_025` stores the light direction times -1.0 (0x00e1b8e8) for c9.
- `vslot_038` multiplies the ambient by the material colour for c10 (0x00bf59e1).
- The object draw sets stage 0 to MODULATE2X (0x00bf5e1e).
- MEASURED: every player body material is ambient = diffuse = 0.588. A face square to the light
  therefore draws at `2 x 0.588 x texture`, brighter than the texture itself.
- INFERRED / OPEN: the portrait calls the DEVICE's SetLight. The vertex-shader renderer takes its
  light from `vslot_025`, which the world's environment code calls (`Map::FUN_00a19160`) and
  the portrait does not. On a vertex-shader device, retail may light the portrait with the
  zone's own light.
- We use the light the portrait's own code sets.
- One retail screenshot (`retail_eu.png`) shows a black circle, so retail itself does not
  always draw it.

**4. The clear and the mask (READ, MEASURED).**
- BufRender's begin (`FUN_009edb60`) clears to 0xff000000.
- `CIFStaticWithPictureClip::vslot_013` draws one quad over the control with both textures at
  full UV.
- Stage 0 takes its colour from the render. Its alpha comes from CURRENT, which is 1.0 with the
  FVF 0x204 (no diffuse).
- Stage 1 takes its alpha from `pmi_face.ddj`.
- MEASURED: that file is 48x48 ARGB8888, every texel black. Alpha is 255 on a disc of 1804
  texels and 0 on the other 500. It is a hard round mask, not a picture, so "the black circle"
  was an empty buffer.
- INFERRED: the UI's usual SRCALPHA blend and linear filtering (the draw sets neither).

**5. When it renders (READ).**
- The block renders only while its dirty byte (+0x38c) is set. `vslot_012` checks it every frame
  (0x007b83ef).
- The byte is set:
  - in the constructor;
  - on a device reset;
  - by `FUN_007b4c00`, which is called after the item-move reply (five sites in `FUN_0087ba20`,
    after the avatar's refresh `FUN_006ab690`) and by the avatar's reset `FUN_006abc50`;
  - again, when the avatar has not loaded yet.
- Nothing in the berserk code sets it. The berserk face is the HWAN_EFF_FACE overlay, not a
  re-render.
- So retail renders once per dress, not every frame.

**What shipped.**
- A new script, `PlayerPortrait` (`client/scripts/ui/hud/player_portrait.gd`), a 128x128
  SubViewport:

## Six-hundred-and-thirty-third round, review follow-up: the preview is lit by the zone and turns the right way with the weapon in the right hand, a drop after a page turn carries its item, tabs act on the press, and a lower bag size strands nothing

The review confirmed the frame fix, the pages and growth caps, the gold colours (all 11 boundaries
rendered), equipment slots 8–12, the camera rect and field of view, the arrow timing, and
BagCapacity on every write path. It found the following. `feat/portrait` (e2677e0) was merged
first. Labels used below: READ, MEASURED, INFERRED, OURS.

**1. The light was wrong: it is the zone's (READ).**
- `0x6ad9e8` is the device's fixed-function SetLight, and nothing draws with it.
- The model is drawn by CObjRendererVS (`vslot_038` `0xbf5830`). Its light constants
  (`0x1112e18`/`0x1112e28`) are written only by `vslot_025` (`0xbeecc0`), which only the world draw
  calls. This is round 635's portrait finding.
- PaperDoll now reuses PlayerPortrait's materials: the zone's channel 2 clamped × 0.6 as diffuse,
  channel 3 as ambient, to-light (0.707, 0.707, 0), object colour 0.6, MODULATE2X.
- World3D hands it the zone light with the portrait's.
- Round 633's 0.7/0.3 Godot light, its 0.89 calibration and `measure_doll_light.gd` are gone.
- **MEASURED** in Jangan, the median of the shirt in the preview: (101,100,96) before, (149,147,138)
  now.

**2. The direction and the hand (READ).**
- The yaw setter `CCompChar::FUN_00c26e70` has forward (sin, 0, -cos). So the right arrow
  (`0x6ab960`, yaw up) turns the face to the screen's right; ours turned it left.
- The doll also lacked the z → -z node, so it was a mirror image with the sword in the wrong hand.
- The fix is the portrait's approach: a (1,1,-1) node, the camera at (0,9,40), and rotation.y = -yaw
  under it.
- **MEASURED** (`World3D: doll pose`, real input):
  - at yaw 0, R hand x 55 and L hand x 133 of 176: the character's right hand, which holds the
    sword, is on the screen's left, as a model facing the viewer shows it;
  - with the right arrow held, a point in front of the face runs +1.2 → +23.1 px to the right as
    the yaw goes 0.024 → 0.510.

**3. Cross-page lookups.**
- `_bag_item_id_at_slot` and the icon now read the server's bag list (`_bag_slots`), not the shown
  page's cells.
- A drop carries the item the drag armed with.
- **MEASURED:** dragging bag slot 1 over the Page 2 tab and onto quickslot 1 logs
  `World3D: quickslot 1 <- item 11 from bag slot 1`. Before, the item id was -1, and the move and use
  sounds were lost for an off-page slot.

**4. Retail's cross-page mechanism: READ, and it is not one.**
- `0x6b4610` (message 0x8074) is a confirm box's answer after a drag between windows. It reads
  "DraggedTab", "DraggedPage" and "DraggedItemIndex" back to address a store slot
  (`index + (page + tab*8)*0x1e`).
- `0x6b62d0` (message 0x8076) is the split box's OK, moving into the first empty slot (`0x6b6280`).
- Neither turns a page, and the tab answers only a press and hover. So ours stays OURS, as labelled.

**5. Tabs act on the press.** `0x64cb80` answers 0x201, so the tabs use `ACTION_MODE_BUTTON_PRESS`.
**MEASURED:** with the button held down and not released, the log reads `bag page 2 of 3` (shot
`02_tab_pressed_not_released`).

**6. The preview renders only while shown.**
- `PaperDoll.set_active`, driven by the doll's visibility (`paper_doll_shown_changed`): UPDATE_ALWAYS
  while the pane shows, UPDATE_DISABLED otherwise.
- Its idle pose still steps while it is hidden (OPEN).

**7. A lower size strands nothing (OURS).** I chose to keep the size up, rather than letting
operations past capacity through, because it leaves every store bound untouched:
- `inventory.KeepHeld` raises the answered size to the highest held slot + 1, logged once per
  character and size.
- Once those slots are emptied, the configured size applies again.
- `/invsize` now checks the requested size itself, since the store's answer is kept up.

**8. Docs.** `docs/protocol/inventory_window.md` now has:
- that `0x6b45b0` matches the tab by handle (`+0x2c`) and acts on the press;
- the frame table's reason: GDR_COMMUNITY, GDR_STORE and GDR_ALCHEMYBOX carry Style 64 but are not
  registry-built here;
- the Light and the Direction sections, rewritten;
- the two drag handlers.

**9. The leader marks.**
- **Party (READ, built):** `IFParty::FUN_006d6640` shows GDR_PTY_PARTY_LEADER (ID 14, `+0x3a8`) and
  its race mark (ID 15, `+0x3ac`) while the party manager's in-party byte (`0x987070`) is set, and

  `HudPanels.set_party_marks` does the same, from World3D's party results. China is always used:

- **Academy (OPEN):** the rank mark (`+0x390`) is textured from the rank byte and shown at

## Six-hundred-and-thirty-third round: the inventory has its frame again, three pages of 32 slots, purse colours, the real equipment slot art and avatar view, and a bright preview that turns with the arrows

The user's report on v0.1.459 had five parts, and the coordinator added a sixth:

1. Inventory, Character, Party "aren't showing the border properly again".
2. Add the inventory's three pages.
3. The equipment slots are "visually inaccurate".
4. Fix the avatar slot page.
5. The preview character is badly placed and too dark, and should turn with the arrows and reset
   with the circle.
6. Colour the gold amount by its size.

Labels used below: READ, MEASURED, INFERRED, OURS. Every address and table is in
`docs/protocol/inventory_window.md`.

### 1. The missing frames: round 630's Style-64 rule hid the registry windows' own frames

**READ.** The builder's `0x8b5710` test hides any control whose Style has bit 0x40, whatever its
class (`0x652da0(0x40)`, then vslot `0x5c` ShowWindow(0)). `ginterface.txt` gives Style 64 to 43
registry entries, and those entries are windows, not controls. Among them are `GDR_MAINPOPUP`,
`GDR_STORAGEROOM`, `GDR_EXCHANGE` and `GDR_GAMEGUIDE`. The client creates these windows hidden,
and each one's ShowWindow(1) shows the window along with the frame it draws.

Our `HudWindow` builds the registry entry as a child, `RegistryFrame`, through `build_control`.
Round 630 therefore hid that child, and nothing ever showed it again.

**The fix** is in `hud_window.gd`: `_add_registry_frame` keeps the frame visible, and the window's
own visibility stays with HudPanels. The shared UiBuilder is not changed. A Style-64 control
inside a layout is still hidden at creation, as round 630 made it.

**MEASURED** with `client/tools/dump_visible_panels.gd`, which builds every window from the box's
Media.pk2 and lists its visible nodes. Diffing v0.1.458 (cfddf39), v0.1.459 (b9bbf07) and this
round shows the regression and what came back:

| Window | `RegistryFrame` nodes: 458 | 459 | 633 |
|---|---|---|---|
| inventory, character, skill, action, party, academy (the main popup) | 9 | 0 | 9 |
| storage, exchange | 9 | 0 | 9 |
| help (GDR_GAMEGUIDE) | 9 | 0 | 9 |
| quest, guild, community, store, system, party match, auto potion, NPC talk, alchemy, option, world map | unchanged | | |

The windows marked "unchanged" are either 2dt windows or registry entries without Style 64.

The only other differences between 458 and 459 were:

- the party and academy leader marks, which are hidden now and rightly so (Style 64 in their
  layouts, shown by code for a leader);
- round 630's text layout.

The before and after renders are in the round's `inv_shots/before_after_sheet.png`.

### 2. The bag's pages

**READ.** The character-data handler takes 13 off the inventory size (`0x9d9aee`) and calls
IFInventory `0x6b6620` with the result. That builds:

- `((size-1)>>5)+1` pages, asserting at most 3;
- one CIFSelectableArea tab per page:
  - (4,-23,60,24) using `com_tab_on/off`;
  - (64,-23,56,24) and (118,-23,57,24) using `com_short_tab_on/off`;
  - captions `UIIT_CTL_BELOINGING`, `_INVENTORY_EXTENSION_TEB` and `_TEB2`;
- 32 slots per page, 32x32 at each lattice cell's top-left;
- slots past the size drawn with `interface\pet\pt_block.ddj` and disabled.

`0x6b3d00` shows one page's slots, and a tab click reaches it through `0x6b45b0`.

**Built (client).** HudPanels code-builds the tabs on the inventory pane. The lattice's 32 cells
show the selected page, cell i being bag slot `page*32+i`. Locked cells show `pt_block` and take no
drop. Icons are now 32x32 at the cell's top-left; they had been stretched to 36.

**Built (server).** Each character now has its own bag size:

- `character.InventorySizeStore`, stored in the `characters.inventory_size` column;
- `inventory.BagCapacity`, which holds every bag operation to that size;
- the bag list and move replies carry the size as a trailing u16, the warehouse list's shape.

**The size settings.**

- `-inventory-size` / `OPENSRO_INVENTORY_SIZE` sets the size for any character without its own,
  clamped to 1..96. Its default is **96**, three full pages: OURS, the user's choice for testing.
- `/invsize [1-96|default]` is a GM command (OURS). It refuses to shrink the bag below an occupied
  slot.
- The inventory expansion item (+32) now grows the bag under the engine's kind-0 test, which
  counts the 13 equipment slots, against a ceiling of 64. So one item takes a 32-slot bag to 64,
  and a second is refused with 0x18fe and kept.

**Retail's starting size is not known.** It is a `_CHAR.InventorySize` database default, and
neither executable carries it; this was already recorded for the server and is re-checked here
for the client. The engine's growth caps (77, or 99 with the quest, both counting the 13
equipment slots) mean retail's third page is never full by its own means: at most 86 slots.

**Carrying an item to another page.** The retail mechanism is not read. Ours (OURS) turns the
page when a drag passes over a tab.

## Rounds 629-632 integration review (int/ui): the berserk display lasts as long as the berserk, a revive or a zone change ends it on the server, hit rate and parry are the item's own, and the panel follows every change of what is worn

The final review of int/ui (dev cfddf39 + rounds 629-632, merged at 1a7e84d) confirmed every READ
of round 629's follow-up (b0ce3bd) and ran the whole branch with real input. It found five
problems and three smaller ones; all are fixed here. Before is 1a7e84d.

**1. The display's drain step includes the scroll's bonus (READ).** `FUN_007b4f40(1)` fixes timer
2 at `ROUND((stones + player+0x20f8 + 60.0) * 1000.0 / 5.0)` ms. `player+0x20f8` is written by
`FUN_0089a0d0` -> `FUN_009d4e00` with the value of a timed job whose FourCC is `0x706874` (the
Energy of life job) while it has time left, and cleared by `FUN_0089a1a0` at its end; "stones" is
`FUN_006ac0a0`, the Hwan socket stones (OPEN, 0: none here). The client used 60 s whatever the
bonus, so with the scroll's +5 s the orbs were gone 5 s before the server's end. Now
`HudPlayerInfo.set_hwan_time_bonus` takes the composite state's bonus and its time left, and the
step is fixed when the display starts. MEASURED (real input: scroll, potion, Tab): "drain step
13.000 s (bonus 5 s)", the display ended at 02:34:56.278 and the server's body mode 0 arrived at
02:34:56.277, 65.003 s after the start (was 60 s against 65 s).

**2. A revive and a zone change end the server's berserk.**
- Revive, READ: `GObjPC::Revive` (0x4df290) ends with `SetBodyMode(2, 0, 6.0 or 11.0 s, 0)`
  (0x4df46c..0x4df484; 0xb45b78 = 6.0f, 0xb45bb8 = 11.0f), which replaces body mode 1.
- Zone change: world entry is READ -- `CGame::EnterWorld` (0x417240, reached from the 0x3012
  SR_READY_TO_PLAY handler `Game__EnterWorld`) calls `CGObjPC::vslot_391` (0x4df9e0) after
  `CGObj::EnterWorld` succeeds, and vslot_391 sets body mode 2 (with the world's timer) or 4. That
  a teleport is such a re-entry is INFERRED: 0x34b5 (SR_RESET_CLIENT, sent by
  `CMainProcess::CharDataSavingCompleted` 0x437de0) and its ack 0x34b6 (`FUN_00402e60` ->
  `FUN_00437e80`, which sends 0x7005 and destroys the lobby entry) were read; the path from the
  teleport handler to them was not traced.
- `berserk.Tracker.End` clears the active window (the activation's end timer then stands down)
  and `session.endBerserk` broadcasts body mode 0, from `ReviveHandler`, the auto-revive and
  `warpTo` (change zone and teleport). OURS: the value is 0, not the engine's 2 -- OpenSRO has no
  body mode 2 (the invincibility and its timer); the client's handler starts the display only on
  1 and does nothing else to the orbs on either value (0x8a80a0).
- MEASURED: berserk at 02:55:51.6, killed, Revive clicked at 02:56:06.1 -> body mode 0 at
  02:56:06.129, before "revived"; no second end at the activation's 02:56:51. Berserk at
  02:35:17 (65 s with the bonus), `/goto hotan` at 02:35:20.9 -> body mode 0 delivered once the
  zone had loaded (02:35:25.8), and no end at the activation's 02:36:22 (its timer stood down).
  Before, 1a7e84d's server kept the berserk through the zone change: a potion in Hotan 30 s after
  Tab was refused "during berserk mode".

**3. Hit rate and parry are each item's own (READ).** `Char_BuildAggregateStats` interpolates the
weapon's ref +0x288/+0x28c (itemdata 113/114, HitRateMin/Max) by variance group 3 (`mov esi,3` at
0x496376) into item+0x1d8, and the body armour's ER triple +0x1c8/+0x1cc (itemdata 68/69,
ParryRatioMin/Max) by group 5 (0x496062) into item+0x19c; `Char_PublishCombatStats` publishes
+0x1d8 as param 11 (0x497ace..0x497add) and +0x19c as param 9 (0x497920..0x49792f). All 2913
weapons in the box's itemdata have HitRateMin < HitRateMax, so the minimum was wrong for nearly
every instance. `combat.WeaponAttackRate` and `session.armourParry` apply the instance (the
weapon rule of `combat.WeaponRange`, the armour rule of `defenderDefence`), in the panel AND in
combat's centre roll and `monsterBlow`, so the two still agree; a broken weapon adds nothing. The
disclosure is restored: retail also adds buffs, masteries and the per-plus increments (columns
115 / 70). MEASURED: the starter sword (24..30) now reads hit 38 (10 + 1 + 27) on one character;
bare-handed 11.

**4. The refresh leaves the running display alone (READ, `FUN_007b4f40(0)`).** It hides the
flames, shows the ready circle at 5, steadies the orbs at 255 and shows one per charge -- and
touches neither timer, the face nor the glow. b0ce3bd's `_refresh_hwan` stopped the drain and
hid the face. `reset_hwan_display` (`FUN_007b5300`) now fades each SHOWN orb and its flame from
255, the face and the glow only at alpha 255 (`+0x12d == -1`; +0x12d is the control's current
fade alpha, 0xff at construction), and stops timer 2 only -- the flames' timer 1 runs on. A
visible consequence, READ and kept: a death in the first 3 s of a berserk leaves the face and the
glow fading in to full, and they stay until the next display ends (seen live: the portrait stayed
red after a death 2.6 s into a berserk).

**5. The stat panel follows every change of what is worn.** Round 629's review skipped empty
equipment lists as "acknowledgements", but the server answers an equip and an unequip with the
worn list itself (`sendWornList`); only a refusal carries no list. So taking off the last item and
equipping onto nothing were missed. MEASURED with real drags: four unequips gave refreshes #2-#4
(the last "player equipment {}" -> hit 11 parry 11), and the sword onto an empty character gave
refresh #5 (hit 38).

**Smaller:** a second activation while berserk is refused before the orbs are counted (READ:
`GObjPC_HandleBerserkMsg_0a7` 0x515b30, error 3 when GetBodyMode() is 1; its error 4 for body mode
2 is OPEN with body mode 2); `/hwan` takes the berserk turn; the end timer holds the turn across
its test and its broadcast. **chardata+5 is READ**: `SetBodyMode` stores its fifth argument there
just before broadcasting (the flag granting param 189's 0.3), and the activation passes 0
(`push 0x0` at 0x515cc6) -- labels upgraded in motion.go, world.gd and player_mini_info.md.

**Tests.** `hud_player_info_test.gd` against 1a7e84d's `hud_player_info.gd`:

    FAIL a refresh during the display leaves the drain running
    FAIL a refresh leaves the face and the glow
    FAIL the drain still ends the display after a refresh (orbs [2, 3, 4])
    SCRIPT ERROR: Invalid call. Nonexistent function 'drain_period_seconds' in base 'Control (HudPlayerInfo)'.

Go: `TestActivateRefusedWhileActiveAndEnd`, `TestBerserkActivationRefusedWhileBerserk`,
`TestReviveEndsBerserk`, `TestZoneChangeEndsBerserk`, `TestCharacterRatesUseTheInstance`.
`remote_godot.sh check`: 382 scripts, ALL LOAD; `tests`: 153 suites, 0 failing; `go vet ./...`
clean; `go test -race -count=1 -p 1 ./internal/berserk/... ./internal/session/...` ok; `go test
-count=1 -p 1 ./...`: 60 packages ok. Live: 0 SCRIPT ERROR in four logs, p95 work frame 4-9 ms.

## Six-hundred-and-thirty-second round, composite review follow-up: a grant's icon goes when the grant ends, the window has its Cancel, and a failed store changes nothing

The review of 5b362d2 confirmed every READ claim. It also confirmed, with real input, the GM
path, the non-GM path and the +5 s bonus. This follow-up fixes what it found. Labels: READ,
MEASURED, INFERRED, OURS.

**1. The grant's end is pushed (READ: 0x653e80 sends 0x315B; the client's FUN_008993b0 removes the
entry and the icon).**
- `CompositeKeeper.put` now starts a real-time timer for each grant. The timer and the last use
  both end the grant. Each end pushes `OpCompositeEnd` (0x0108, OURS) {item, scroll} to the
  session the character last used the keeper through.
- A generation stamp stops a stale timer from ending a newer grant.
- The last use pushes the end BEFORE its result, because vslot_007 ends the job before it
  answers 0xB15F.
- A refused fill is now followed by the state too.
- The client's `_on_composite_ended` removes the kind-5 icon.

**2. The Cancel button (READ: FUN_007af830 builds count + 1 buttons, and the extra one is
labelled from `UIIT_CTL_CANCEL` at 0x7afb57; FUN_007b03e0 hit-tests all count + 1).**
- `CompositeItemWindow` adds it one step below the last item button. Pressing it closes the
  window.
- The file's header now describes the count + 1 buttons.

**3. Leaks.**
- `BerserkDisconnectHandler` runs before `worldDisconnect`. It skips a character still live on
  another session. It calls:
  - `Tracker.Forget` (renamed from Clear; a method named Clear is on the orphan list for the threat table): drops the charges (they are persisted and reseeded), the active window, the
    turn (unless a request holds it; `TryLock`) and an expired bonus;
  - `CompositeKeeper.Forget`: drops the session binding, expired grants and the empty map.
- The berserk tracker was never cleared on logout before this round.
- A RUNNING grant or bonus stays until its own timer deletes it, because retail keeps timed
  jobs across a relog. So what stays in memory is bounded by the jobs still running.
- `SetDurationBonus` now takes (now, lasts) and deletes its entry on real time.

**4. No partial state on a store error.**
- The fill persists `SetHwanCount(after)` FIRST. On an error it answers "using failed" and
  leaves the grant, the bonus, the cooldown and the live orbs as they were.
- The bag potion does the same: on an error the potion is handed back and the orbs are
  untouched.

**5. The pieces that had been skipped.**
- *The FUN_00488db0 gate (READ, 0x488db0).* It answers 1 for TID bit 1 clear and TypeID
  3/3/3/10. On 0, `0x49fc94 je 0x49fd55` skips the type-10 job with no error. OpenSRO now skips
  such a UIU1 entry the same way.
  - The type-3 branch's class is `FUN_004929c0` (0x4929c0: TypeID 3/3/13) with TID4 4. This
    corrects the previous round's "TypeID4 4" to **3/3/13/4**. Such rows are still refused, as
    not modelled.
- *FUN_004a0600's vslot_300 (READ, OPEN).*
  - `CGObjPC::vslot_300` (0x4ef340) is `GObjPC::FUN_004a9430`. It calls
    `CGObjMobile::vslot_300` (0x48b730), which is both move controllers' +0x18. It may send
    0xB023, copies the position block, and resets the stance from body state 2/3.
  - That this is a movement stop is INFERRED. Not mirrored, labelled OPEN in code and in
    TODO.md.
- *board+0x390 (READ + INFERRED).*
  - At 0x800501 it guards the click. The board's grant map is the std::map at +0x388: its
    iterators compare against the head at +0x38c (FUN_008052f0 / FUN_00805430). So +0x390 is
    the map's size under MSVC's layout.
  - That means "some grant exists". Ours opens only for an icon whose grant it holds, which
    implies the same.

**6. Minor.**
- An `items_code_name_idx` index for `GetItemByCode`.
- 0x185b's authored text, `UIIT_MSG_STRGERR_WAIT_FOR_REUSE_DELAY` "Still have time to reuse the
  item.", now replaces OpenSRO's "wait for the reuse delay" on every item path.
- The client prints `World3D: use item refused: <text>`, so tester logs show refusals.

**7. deploy/README.md: the ROUND 632 note.** The item CSV grows to 72 columns (70 CodeName, 71

## Six-hundred-and-thirty-second round, review follow-up: the Energy of life scroll works as the game's does, and cooldowns of key 0 are per item

The review confirmed every READ claim of round 632 and asked for five changes. All five are
done here. Labels: READ (seen in the decompile, the asm or the data), MEASURED, INFERRED, OURS.

**1. A COOLTIME key of 0 is per item (READ).**
- `Item_HandleUseItem` hands ref+0x520 to `ItemCooldowns::IsReady` (`0x64c040`) in EAX
  (`0x510d8f`).
- Key 0 reads the per-item map at block+0x10. A non-zero key reads the group map at +0x2c,
  once for each non-zero byte of the key.
- `Arm` (`0x64c320`) always stores the per-item entry. It adds a group link for each non-zero
  byte.
- `itemcooldown.go` now has `ReadyItem`/`ArmItem` doing the same. Round 632's "group 0x00" was
  wrong: it let 22936 block every other key-0 row (37 of them, by the review's count).
- Skills keep `Ready`/`Arm` on the group map, which is the map they read.

**2. The refusal text has an authored source (READ).** textuisystem's
`UIIT_MSG_QUEST_ERR_USE_WHANITEM` is "Selected item cannot be used during berserk mode." The
new composite refusals also use authored texts:
- `0x1894`: "The selected item cannot be used together or the skill is already in use."
- `0x18c6`: "Exceeded one day use limit."
- `0x183e`: "The selected item is unusable."

**3. The Energy of life scroll is built (READ; the full chain is in `docs/protocol/ITEM_FORMAT.md`,
"The composite path, end to end").**
- *Which rows carry a list.* ExtractData parses a Desc as a composite list only for 3/3/13/14
  and 3/3/13/15, and only beside a Param of 1. The list is exported as item column 71,
  `CompositeDesc`. It is stored in SQL, and `GetItemByCode` resolves the parts it names.
- *The scroll's use.* `UseByKind` case 0xe → `FUN_0049f090`'s `0x1894` refusals →
  `FUN_0049f590`, which creates two timed jobs:
  - a UIL1 job: one use of 23937 for 3600 s (flag "A" → 0, read at `0xb12aa4`);
  - a UIU1 job: `ITEM_ETC_INCREASE_HWAN_TIME_0n`. Its Param1 is the seconds, Param2 the FourCC
    and Param3 the value.
- *The FourCC is traced.* `0x706874` is not a `Stat_ApplyTaggedModifier` tag. It keys
  `CTJ_CharParamKeeper`'s table (`FUN_006552d0`, `0x6552fe`), whose record is {index 0,
  **param 60**, slot 0}.
  - The apply is `vslot_012`, `0x655045` → `0x655430`, with EDX = param, calling
    `ParamKeeper_SetParam`. Removal is `vslot_015`.
  - Param 60 is the berserk duration's base (60.0 from InitStats; the activation reads
    60 + 195). So a 1st-degree scroll lasts **65 s** of berserk while its hour runs.
  - `berserk.Tracker.SetDurationBonus` carries it.
- *The fill.* The chain is `0x511640` → `CUsedItemLimit::vslot_007` → `FUN_004a05b0`
  (dead / berserk / five orbs). The last use:
  - ends the UIL1 job;
  - ends the `0x706874` job (`FUN_004dd620`, `mov ebx,0x706874` at `0x654310`);
  - arms 23937's COOLTIME (group 0xC9, 20 minutes);
  - then runs `AddHwanCount(Param1 byte)`.

  vslot_007 does not call IsReady. The 20 minutes block the next scroll, which shares group
  0xC9.
- *What the client shows (READ in the retail client, by a sub-agent this round).*
  - `0x3159` adds a kind-5 buff-bar icon: the SCROLL's icon, with a gauge over the scroll's
    Param1.
  - A left-click (`CIFMagicStateBoard::vslot_029`, `0x800430`) opens `CIFCompositeItemWnd`
    (`GDR_COMPOSITE_ITEM`, `resinfo\ifcompositeitemwnd.txt`).
  - The window's "%s(%d)" buttons, 150 × 25 on `sys_button.ddj`, send `0x715F`.
  - The UIU1 buff has no icon: Param4 is -1 on 23938-23941.
- *Built.*
  - Server: `session/composite.go` (`CompositeKeeper`, `useCompositeScroll`,
    `CompositeHandler`) on opcodes 0x0104-0x0107. The opcodes are OURS; retail uses
    0x715F/0xB15F/0x3159/0x315B.
  - Client: `CompositeNet`, `HudBuffBoard.add_item_state` (kind 5, left-click →
    `item_state_clicked`, right-click does nothing), `CompositeItemWindow`, and
    `ItemTableReader.Item.param1`.
- *OURS, the user's request:* a GM account neither checks nor arms the scroll's or the fill's
  COOLTIME.
- *Not recovered:*
  - the window's resize arithmetic for several buttons;
  - what a zero-count button looks like (ours is disabled);
  - which list FUN_00805a40 puts a kind-5 icon on (ours: the main list, INFERRED).

**4. The berserk turn.** `berserk.Tracker.Turn(characterID)` is a per-character lock. Four paths
hold it across the whole read, spend, change and `SetHwanCount`:
- the bag potion;
- the scroll;
- the fill;
- `handleBerserk`, plus the kill-earn block.

A potion can no longer be spent against a state that a concurrent activation is changing. The
engine needs no lock, because all of these run on the PC's own thread.

**5. Quest items 5921/10491 (READ).** No gate in the use path is specific to them:
- `0x185f` is `CGObjPC::QB_IsBlocked(8)` (`0x4ddd30`) over a quest-script block mask at
  `pc+0x217c`, set and cleared by `QB_SetBlocked`/`QB_ClearBlocked`.
- The event-0xc listener list (`FUN_0063d4a0` → `FUN_0063d190(0, 0xc)`) can veto a use with 3.

OpenSRO has neither state, so there is nothing to mirror: their fill works, as the bag path
reads. Who registers event-0xc listeners is not traced (OPEN).

**Tests.**

## Six-hundred-and-thirty-second round: a berserk potion fills the five orbs, so a GM can test berserk with `/give 23937`

The request: "allow me to use energy of life potions so I can test berserk. I think it usually has
a 30 minute cooldown on that but remove that limit for GMs." Before this round every berserk
potion was refused as "that cannot be used" (round 491 listed it as a disclosed gap).

**Which item (READ, Media.pk2 `textdata_object.txt` and `itemdata_*.txt`).** "Energy of life" is
`SN_ITEM_ETC_SECOND_HWAN_SCROLL_01..06` -> `ITEM_ETC_SECOND_HWAN_SCROLL_01..04` (ids 23944-23947,
TypeID 3/3/13/14; 05 and 06 have names but no rows). The scroll is not what fills the gauge. Its
Param2 descriptor is `[UIL1:ITEM_ETC_SECOND_HWAN,A,3600,1],[UIU1:ITEM_ETC_INCREASE_HWAN_TIME_0n]`,
and its tooltip reads "Option : During the Effect, 100% gauge charge can be used once. (After use
of 100% Gauge charge, extend time will be removed and unable to use Energy of life for 20 Mins)".
The fill it grants is `ITEM_ETC_SECOND_HWAN`, **id 23937, TypeID 3/3/1/8, "Hwan regeneration
fill"**: Param1 5 ("? ???"), then Param2 **1,200,000** with `COOLTIME:0x000000C9`. The scrolls
carry `COOLTIME:0x000000C9` too (1 ms). So **the retail delay is 20 minutes, not 30** -- the data
and the tooltip agree. The other 3/3/1/8 rows are the Berserker Regeneration Potions 24331, 24993,
33884 (no COOLTIME; tooltip "Fills berserk gage to 100%. Cannot be used during berserk mode."),
22936 Berserk Regeneration Potion (`COOLTIME:0x00000000`, 180,000 ms) and the quest items 5921
and 10491. Full table: `docs/protocol/ITEM_FORMAT.md`, "Berserk potions and Energy of life".

**What using one does (READ, SR_GameServer.exe).** `CGItemExpendable` slot 308 (`0x0049b710`),
TypeID3 1, TypeID4 8, in srv.asm `0x49b9a4..0x49b9e9`: `GetBodyMode()` (vtable `+0x100`) == 1
writes `0x18ce` and returns (DoJob keeps the item); otherwise `push 0; mov esi,0x5; call
0x4e4d00` -- `GObjPC::AddHwanCount(+5)`, which clamps at 5 -- and the answer is 1. It skips the
per-kind potion lock (`FUN_004eb410` is asked only on the other kinds) and never reads the orb
count, so a potion at five orbs is spent for nothing. The delay is the generic COOLTIME:
`Item_HandleUseItem` (`0x00510980`) asks `ItemCooldowns::IsReady` before DoJob (`0x185b`) and
calls `ItemCooldowns::Arm` after a success, for any item whose ref `+0x524` is non-zero.

The scroll's own path was read and is **not** built: `UseByKind` (`0x0049c2b0`) case `0xe` ->
`GObjPC::FUN_0049f590` walks the FourCC list (`'UIL1'` `0x55494c31`, `'UIU1'` `0x55495531`) and
queues timed jobs; the fill is then spent through `CUsedItemLimit::vslot_007` (`0x00654080`),
which additionally refuses five orbs (`FUN_004a05b0`, `0x183e`), arms group 0xC9, and adds the
row's Param1 byte (`FUN_004a0600`, `0x4a062b movzx esi,BYTE [esp+0x14]`). INFERRED: because the
scroll carries group 0xC9, the fill's 20 minutes also block the next scroll -- the tooltip's
"unable to use Energy of life for 20 Mins".

**Built.**
- `berserk.Tracker.Add` is `AddHwanCount`: clamp [0, 5], no gain while berserk.
  `berserk.PotionCharges = 5` is slot 308's literal.
- `session.useBerserkPotion` (`server/internal/session/berserkpotion.go`) runs the engine's order:
  COOLTIME gate, `0x18ce` while berserk (item kept), spend, +5 orbs persisted through
  `SetHwanCount`, arm COOLTIME. `UseItemHandler` takes the berserk tracker and the GM gate.
- **OURS, the user's request:** a GM account's berserk potion neither checks nor arms its
  COOLTIME. It is scoped to TypeID 3/3/1/8; every other cooltime item keeps its delay for a GM.
- `UseItemResult` gains an appended `HasBerserk`/`BerserkGauge`/`BerserkActive` tail (6 bytes
  after the 28). The client's `UseItemNet.decode_result` reads it when present, and
  `World3D._on_use_item_result` drives `set_berserk` with it. The refusal text "that cannot be
  used during berserk mode" is OURS: `0x18ce` has no case in the client's error switch, so it is
  taken from the tooltip.

**Tests.**
- Go (`server/internal/session/berserkpotion_test.go`, synthetic rows shaped like 23937/24331):
  - the gauge fills to 100 and persists 5;
  - a potion at full orbs is still spent;
  - Tab's `Activate` then works;
  - a potion during berserk is refused and kept;
  - a normal player's second fill 19:59 later is refused and kept, and at 20:00 it is used;
  - a GM's second fill goes through at once;
  - `Tracker.Add` clamps and refuses while berserk.
- Client (`client/scripts/net/useitem_test.gd`): the old 28-byte reply decodes without berserk
  state, and the tail round-trips.
- **Negative against dev cfddf39** (the gauge test cut to the old seven-argument handler, in a
  detached worktree):

      --- FAIL: TestBerserkPotionFillsTheGauge (0.10s)
          berserkpotion_neg_test.go:48: the berserk potion was refused: "that cannot be used"

  The test file verbatim does not compile there (`too many arguments in call to
  UseItemHandler`, `res.HasBerserk undefined`).

**Real input on the box (MEASURED from the logs).** Xvfb `:93`, the lane's own server build with
`-gm-accounts qa` and an items CSV exported from the box's Media.pk2 (deleted afterwards).
Signed in through `Login.tscn` (`OPENSRO_QA_RECONNECT_VIA_LOGIN=1`). Then, with xdotool:
typed `/give 23937` in the chat, pressed `i`, right-clicked the bag cell, and pressed Tab.

    World3D: berserk potion: gauge 100, active false
    GM REPLY: gave 1 x item 23937
    KEYMAP Tab -> berserk 8: berserk requested
    World3D: berserk result: activated true, gauge 0, active true

The orbs' drawing is round 629's lane. This round only checks the value in the log.

**OPEN.**
- The Energy of life scroll (3/3/13/14) and its UIL1/UIU1 composite are still refused.
