## Six-hundred-and-thirty-first round, review follow-up: a world-map name plate no longer frees itself mid-click or walks the player, a confirm box closes with its window, and the gold box moves the amount once

The review confirmed the round's fix for the seven store and warehouse handlers, and that it
works with real input. It found five more issues; all are addressed here.

### 1. The world map's name plates (MEASURED)

**Before (dev cfddf39).** A real click on the Jangan plate (M, the globe, the plate) did two
things wrong:
- It logged "freed or unreferenced while a signal is being emitted" for the same reason as
  the store boxes. The call chain is `_on_plate_input` → `_show_map` → `_build_place_labels`,
  whose `old.free()` deleted the plate's own layer while the plate was emitting.
- It walked the player.

**Two faults, found in two steps.**
1. The layer is now removed from the map and `queue_free`d.
2. With that alone, the real click still walked the player. The session log (fix 1 only) showed
   `PICK: click at (0, 0)`, a footstep sound, and the minimap moving from X:6436 to X:6447.
   - World3D walks on a left **release** that reaches `_unhandled_input`.
   - Godot sends a release only to the control that took the press.
   - Switching maps on the press removed the plate, so the release went to the world.

   The plate now takes both halves of the click (`accept_event`) and switches the map on the
   release. Doing it on the release is OURS; the plates are ours.

**The edit is small.** Two hunks in `hud_worldmap.gd` (`_build_place_labels`,
`_on_plate_input`), away from the player-arrow code that round 630 is changing.

**After, with a real click on the fixed build.** The regional map of Jangan opened. The minimap
stayed at X:6436 Y:1062. There was no PICK line, no footstep, and no error lines in the whole
log.

**Test.** `client/scripts/ui/hud/worldmap_plate_test.gd` uses worldmap_window_test.gd's
synthetic fixture; the town is given a one-region box so that it gets a plate. It pushes a
press and a release through the live viewport, with a recorder standing in for World3D's
`_unhandled_input`. On dev cfddf39:

```
ERROR: Object <Object#48167388722> was freed or unreferenced while a signal is being emitted from it. ...
FAIL the clicked plate is not freed inside its own gui_input
FAIL its PlaceLabels layer leaves the map and is deleted at the end of the frame
FAIL neither half of the click falls through to the world (1 press(es), 1 release(s) reached _unhandled_input)
```

The fixed tree prints ALL PASS.

### 2. A box outlived its window (MEASURED on base; the fix is OURS)

**The bug.**
- `open_shop` and `open_storage` never dropped an existing box.
- Escape, the window's X and `close()` only hide the window.
- So a sell box, which holds a bag *slot* rather than the item, came back stale on reopen and
  sold whatever had moved into that slot.

**The fix.** `_close_window_boxes` closes every box on the window (Buy, Sell, Deposit, Withdraw,
Gold):
- when the window hides (its `visibility_changed`; the window's own flag, so hiding the whole
  HUD with F10 keeps the box);
- when `open_shop` or `open_storage` reuses the window.

A closing box is also renamed at once, so a lookup never finds it and a new box keeps its plain
name.

**What retail does is OPEN.** The hide branch of `CIFStore::vslot_023` does not touch the box.
The storage, the inventory and ConfirmBuy have no ShowWindow override. No `[+0x390]` hide was
found in store, storage or NPC code (`docs/protocol/message_box.md`).

**Real input, fixed build.**
- The sell box was open when the store's X was clicked. Talking to the storage keeper and
  choosing Buy reopened the store with no sell box.
- A sell box, then Escape: the store and the box both closed.
- In the warehouse, the deposit box was open when the storage's X was clicked. Talking to the
  keeper and choosing Deposit reopened the storage with no deposit box.

### 3. The gold box closes on OK (READ, then matched)

**Retail.** CIFMessageBox's message map (`.rdata 0xd9b174`) sends every OK and Cancel to a
handler that posts to the owner and then hides the box. For the gold box these are OK 215 →
0x63d7f0 and Cancel 216 → 0x63bc50.

**Ours.** Deposit and Withdraw now close the dialog before sending.

**Real input.** A double-click on Deposit with 100 typed moved the stored gold 250 → 350,
once.

### 4 and 5. The protocol document

`docs/protocol/message_box.md` is rewritten for the **RENEWAL** branch:
- **Only RENEWAL controls.** MsgBoxStoreConfirm and ConfirmBuy's contents exist only under
  `#ifdef RENEWAL_SHOP_SYSTEM`. Their `#else` controls are gone from the tables.
- **The branch is INFERRED from the code.** It loads MsgBoxStoreConfirm at 0x640300. ConfirmBuy's
  control 400 is read without a null check. The only filler of the `#else`-only 44/45
  (0x7c2a20) is dead code. The resinfo parser's define map (0xeed4e0) was not traced.
- **Where the code puts Buy and Cancel.** Under RENEWAL, ConfirmBuy's buttons are 0,0,0,0 in the
  file. `FUN_007c3f70` adds a row per price type and moves Buy to (X+82, Y+H-40) and Cancel to
  (X+170, Y+H-40) (asm 0x7c47ef..0x7c4871).
- **The review's nits, fixed:**
  - modes 10-13 carry their MsgBox names;
  - the title is `UIIT_STT_CONFIRM_BOX` for purposes 1-10, 14 and 16-20, and other purposes
    have their own titles;
  - DEPOSITMONEY and WITHDRAWMONEY are NAME1's caption;
  - "exchange gold" and "drop gold" are INFERRED from their callers;
  - MsgBoxSimple is created at 280x144 and then resized to 360x151 by 0x643e50 (READ);
  - the +0x908 style byte is READ at 0x643e94.

### Tests

**New negatives in `confirm_box_test.gd`.** On dev cfddf39 they are among its 37 FAIL lines:

```
FAIL gold: GoldDialog closes by hiding and queue_free          (Deposit, then Withdraw)
FAIL hiding its window closes SellConfirm
FAIL showing the window again shows no stale SellConfirm
FAIL hiding its window closes BuyConfirm
FAIL showing the window again shows no stale BuyConfirm
FAIL hiding its window closes DepositConfirm
FAIL showing the window again shows no stale DepositConfirm
FAIL hiding its window closes WithdrawConfirm
FAIL showing the window again shows no stale WithdrawConfirm
FAIL hiding its window closes GoldDialog
FAIL showing the window again shows no stale GoldDialog
FAIL _close_window_boxes (called by open_shop / open_storage) closes a box left on the window
```

The fixed tree prints ALL PASS.

## Six-hundred-and-thirty-first round: confirming a sale, a purchase or a warehouse move no longer crashes the game, and the store's goods can be clicked again

The user reported this on v0.1.458: "when I try to interact with shops or storage and use the
native gui to confirm things it causes the game to crash." The crash was reproduced with a real
click. It is fixed at its root, and a test pins it. The same run found two more faults in the
same boxes and fixed them too. Replacing the boxes with the retail windows is the next round;
the retail equivalents were READ and are listed in `docs/TODO.md` and
`docs/protocol/message_box.md`.

### Reproduced with real input (MEASURED)

**Setup.**
- Box: Xvfb `:89`, the release route `res://scenes/Login.tscn` with
  `OPENSRO_QA_RECONNECT_VIA_LOGIN=1`, GPU through vglrun.
- Server: an in-memory server built from dev cfddf39.
- Client: the Jangan spawn (97/168 at 1002,1020), with `OPENSRO_QA_SHOP=NPC_CH_POTION` and
  `OPENSRO_QA_SHOP_BUY=1`. The hook buys a stack and leaves the sell box open.
- Input: a real `xdotool click` on the box's **Sell** button (screen 474,412). The script is
  `/var/tmp/confirmcrash/cc.sh`.

**Result.** The client exited with status 134. The log (`/var/tmp/confirmcrash/base_sell_crash.log`)
ends with:

```
ERROR: Object <Object#13437661318602> was freed or unreferenced while a signal is being emitted from it. Try connecting to the signal using 'CONNECT_DEFERRED' flag, or use queue_free() to free the object (if this object is a Node) to avoid this error and potential crashes.
   at: ~Object (core/object/object.cpp:2006)
handle_crash: Program crashed with signal 11
```

**Cause (READ in `hud_panels.gd`).** Seven handlers freed the box synchronously from inside the
`pressed` of one of its own buttons:
- Buy and its Cancel;
- Sell and its Cancel;
- Deposit/Withdraw and their Cancel;
- the warehouse gold dialog's Close.

The box is the button's ancestor, so `panel.free()` deleted the Button while BaseButton was still
emitting `pressed` and the Viewport was still routing the click. Godot 4.2.2 then touches the
freed button, which is a use-after-free.

The crash was reproduced on Linux. On Windows (the user's build) the same engine path is
INFERRED to crash the same way, as an access violation. It is not a Windows-only case: no
Godot `Window` is involved.

The first line above is Godot's own warning and goes to the log file. So if a crash like this
comes back, the tester's `logs/opensro.log` will end with that "freed ... while a signal is
being emitted" line.

### Two more faults in the same boxes (MEASURED in the same run)

**The totals were never shown.** The buy box's "Total" and the sell box's "Get" line stayed
empty. Every time a box opened, the log said:

```
SCRIPT ERROR: Invalid call. Nonexistent function '_grouped' in base 'Nil'.
```

The static `_grouped` was called unqualified from inside the refresh lambda. It is now
`HudPanels._grouped`. After the fix, the sell box reads "Get: 148 gold" and the buy box reads
"Total: 600 gold".

**No good in the store could be clicked.** Buying had never worked with the mouse.
- **Why.** `ifstore.txt` authors 30 `GDR_STORE_SLOT_100..129:CIFSlotWithHelp` controls, READ:
  slot 100 is at 21,71,32,32 and the rest step by 36. They sit exactly on the 30 cells of
  `GDR_STORE_LAT`. `ifstorageroom.txt` does the same with `GDR_STORAGE_SLOT_*`.
- **What happens.** The slot controls come later in the tree, so Godot hit-tests them first.
  With `MOUSE_FILTER_PASS` a click passes on to their parents, never to the cell underneath.
- **Measured.** A hit-walk debug print on a real click at 426,271 listed `GDR_STORE_SLOT_100`
  as the topmost hit. `_on_shop_cell_input` never ran. Every earlier "buy" was a QA hook.
- **Fix (OURS).** `_lattice_takes_clicks` sets those slots to `MOUSE_FILTER_IGNORE` when the
  store or the warehouse opens. The goods are drawn and clicked in the lattice cells, so the
  slots stay drawn but no longer take the mouse. Which of the two controls takes the click is
  this client's arrangement, not the original's.
  - The original clicks the `CIFSlotWithHelp` itself, READ: `vslot_029` 0x680fa0 handles
    Ctrl+click buying.

**A small error when two boxes close at once.** In that case `_message_box_sounds` connected
the same bound Callable twice ("Signal 'process_frame' is already connected"). It now checks
first.

### The fix

- `HudPanels._close_confirm_box` hides the box and `queue_free`s it. The engine deletes it at
  the end of the frame, after the click is done with it.
- The box's one-frame centring now checks `is_instance_valid(panel)` first. On base, 11
  `Invalid get index 'size' (on base: 'previously freed')` errors came from it.
- The guild prompts and the buff board's cancel box already used `queue_free`, and never crashed.

stayed alive after every click.

`grep` found none of these in any of the three logs: `SCRIPT ERROR`, `signal is being emitted`,

### The native-dialog question

The client has exactly one Godot `Window` dialog: `Boot.gd`'s `ConfirmationDialog` for the
auto-updater. It is embedded, because `embed_subwindows` is left at its default of true. It is not
part of the store or the warehouse.

presets set nothing that touches subwindows (READ `client/export_presets.cfg`).

## Six-hundred-and-thirtieth round, review follow-up: no seams or holes in the map, text sits in each control's ClientRect, the purse amount has its own field, and Style-64 controls start hidden

The review confirmed round 630's readings and traced the heading: `0x9ed130` / `0x9c4260` store it
at `player+0x8c` in `[0, 2 pi)` and `0x9ec850` turns it into `(sin h, 0, -cos h)` (re-read here:
`0xb44b40` is the sin, `0xb44a10` the cos). So the arrow's origin is now READ, not INFERRED. The
review also found seven problems, and this follow-up fixes them. Labels are as in round 630.

1. **1-pixel see-through seams** (MEASURED by the review's magenta probe). At every zoom level but
   64, 160 and 256 the tile size is fractional, and each tile's rect was snapped separately. Now
   `HudMinimap.tile_rect` floors every tile edge, so a tile's right edge is its neighbour's left edge
   (OURS; the client's float quads share their vertices). Re-run of the review's
   `zz_rv630_seam.gd`, first 630 commit against this one: before, 6 of 28 zoom/spot cases showed
   magenta, up to 176 aperture pixels (at S 179.2, spot (1919.9, 0.1)), with seam-band error up to
   0.708. After, 0 of 28, and the seam-band means (0.000..0.057) are the interior's (0.001..0.060).
2. **ClientRect.** READ: `0x652800` insets the text rect by `+0x18c..+0x198`, which `0x6527d0`
   copies from the parsed ClientRect (`0x8b566e..0x8b5674`) in the order left, top, right, bottom.
   CIFButton's draw is CIFStatic's (its slot 13, `0x655f30`, jumps to `0x64d940`; its slot 42 is
   `0x64d9b0`), and the builder sets every control's HAlign and VAlign (`0x8b5696..0x8b56b8`).
   `UiBuilder.place_label` now lays the text of every CIFStatic and CIFButton inside its ClientRect,
   by its own alignment. Button captions used to be centred both ways whatever the layout said.
   - Truncation: the client truncates the SCREEN coordinate (`cvttsd2si`). Windows sit at whole
     pixels and that coordinate is not negative, so the offset inside the window is floored, as
     before. Truncating the offset itself would be a pixel off whenever it is negative and
     fractional. Kept, and the reason is written at `place_label`.
   - MEASURED, the same census as round 630 plus storage and exchange, first 630 commit against this
     one (Arial fallback): storage's "Total Gold" moved from centred on the whole 236 px strip to
     x 16..71 (text rect x 17..71), left of the coin button; its "Gold" to x 210..237 (the round
     562 record's 210..237). Button captions' label boxes are now their ClientRect, and they keep
     their own alignment: party / academy Invite, Set, Party match and Matching (centred) go from
     the whole 24 px button to y 6..20. Party match's Join, Whisper, Auto match, Form party, Change
     entry, Delete entry, Search and Refresh, autopotion's Confirm and Cancel, and exchange's
     Confirm and Cancel are VAlign 0 and now start at y 6 instead of being centred on the button.
     These are node rects; the glyphs themselves were not diffed for these windows. Party match's
     column headers are unchanged.
     No window builds ifmessagebox's MsgBoxStore* sections, so their NAME / PRICE fields are not
     drawn anywhere yet.
3. **The purse amount.** READ from ifinventory.txt: the amount is `GDR_INVENTORY_STA_MONEY` (0,305
   176x28 over int_window_downbox, ClientRect 36,7,39,5, HAlign 2: right-aligned, ending at x 137),
   and the 24-pixel `GDR_INVENTORY_STA_GOLD` says "Gold". ifstorageroom.txt pairs
   `GDR_STORAGE_STA_MONEY` and `_STA_GOLD` the same way. HudPanels wrote the amount over "Gold" in
   both. It now writes `STA_MONEY` through the new `UiBuilder.set_static_text`, which puts text on
   an art static the layout gave none.
4. **Missing neighbour tiles.** READ: `0x661ce0` stores the null the loader returns, and the quad
   is drawn with no texture, which Direct3D 9 samples as black (the review's reading). MEASURED at
   region 80/78's corners, where 3 of the 9 regions have no file: before, 2,994 of 6,077 aperture
   pixels showed the window behind; after, 0, and 2,987 are black.
5. **Cost.**
   - `update_signs` no longer builds a dictionary or a log string every tick.
   - `World3D._refresh_minimap` keeps the region group and its parsed name until the player leaves
     it, and refills two kept lists for the signs.
   - The tiles stay out of the builder's unbounded cache (`load_texture(path, false)`): a bounded
     set of 25 (OURS), with missing names remembered.
   - MEASURED with the review's probe: 82.3 -> 44.0 us per `update_player` + `update_signs`; a
     crossing east (3 new tiles) 3.0 -> 2.4 ms; cold 3x3 7.5 -> 7.4 ms.
   - OPEN: decoding off the main thread. The archive reader is shared with world streaming and its

6. **Docs.**
   - `0x661ce0` has two callers: vslot_012 (`0x6625f4`), only while a zoom walks, and `0x777a70`
     (`0x777ac7`), which the review traces to CICPlayer::vslot_015(3) on a heading change. The
     per-frame refresh is ours.
   - Corrected in protocol/minimap.md and in `World3D._refresh_minimap`'s comment.
7. **Style 64.** READ (`0x8b5710`): `UiBuilder.build_control` now hides a Style-0x40 control at

## Six-hundred-and-thirtieth round: the minimap shows where the player stands, its arrow points the way the player faces, and it sits flush in the corner without the black ring

The report on v0.1.458: a black circle left of the globe; the map not matching the dirt road the
player stood on (HUD X:6450 Y:891, Grassland); the arrow (minimap and world map) not facing the way
the character faces; the NPC and monster dots misplaced; the zoom buttons outside their circles and
the text slightly off; and the minimap not flush with the top-right corner. Every value below was
READ from the client (`/var/tmp/decomp_client`, `/var/tmp/sro_client.asm`) or MEASURED; the full
reading is in [protocol/minimap.md](protocol/minimap.md).

### What was wrong, and the reading that fixes it

1. **The black ring** is `GDR_MINIMAP_DUNGEON_FLOOR_INFO` (id 10, `mm_dungeonfloor.ddj`, 1,42
   32x32). READ: its Style is 64, and the resinfo builder hides a style-0x40 control at creation
   (`0x8b5710..0x8b5726`); `0x661ce0` shows it only while the region id's top bit is set
   (`0x6620db..0x662101`), a dungeon region. The retail screenshot has no ring. Hidden now.
2. **The map was mirrored north-south inside each region.** READ (`0x661ce0`):
   `+0x408 = S * (1920 - z) / 1920` -- an image's rows run north to south. The minimap drew row
   `z / 1920` under the player instead. MEASURED three ways:
   - the harness (`--base` against this tree, 1024x768 on the RX 5700 XT): the pixel under the
     aperture's centre matches the tile's texel at `(x, 1920 - z)` within 0.005 (mean RGB, 0..1) at
     five of six spots, where the base matched `(x, z)`; at (960, 960), the region's middle row, the
     two rules agree, which is why the error was easy to miss;
   - against the terrain: over every navmesh tile of six regions (96/168, 97/168, 96/167, 95/168,
     96/169, 98/168) grass tiles sit on greener texels than the rest by 0.022..0.104 under the READ
     rule, and by -0.011..0.008 under the old one. At the report's spot, 96/168 local (1140, 1230),
     the terrain is `c_dust_fld_06` (dirt) and the READ texel is brown (114,84,32); the old rule
     read (1140, 690), which is `c_grass_fld_05`, and drew green (35,56,1);
   - the tiles' seams: `168x97`'s bottom row continues `168x96`'s top row (mean difference 13.8
     against 31.7 reversed), and `169x96` continues it to the east (10.0 against 24.8).
   Also READ: the client draws the **3x3** tiles around the player (`0x662271..0x6622a3`), so the
   neighbouring region shows near an edge (the map went blank past its own region), and one region
   is **160 px** (`0x660c42`), not 256. Zoom is the client's: +-19.2 a press between 64 and 256
   (`0x660620`, `0x660660`), walked at 0.05 per frame-timer count (INFERRED milliseconds).
3. **The arrow.** READ: vslot_013 turns the 16x16 arrow by `-(player+0x8c - pi/2)` through the
   clockwise rotation `0x8b5c50` (cos `0xb44a10`, sin `0xb44b40`). MEASURED: `mm_sign_character.ddj`
   points right. The minimap passed Godot's `rotation_degrees.y` straight through, so it pointed
   right when the player faced south: only 45 degrees came out right. It now turns the art by the
   angle of the facing's `(x, -z)`, the facing taken into the region group's frame
   (`World3D.minimap_facing`). INFERRED: that is the READ formula for a heading counted from south
   toward east (the heading's writer was not traced). The world map's marker is turned the same way
   (READ `0x6200de..0x620236`); it never turned before. The minimap is also updated every frame
   now, as the client's is, instead of every tenth.
   MEASURED with real movement (`qa_shot.sh --walk`, 96/168 at (1140, 1230), the new
   `QA MINIMAP` log line): walking world heading 180 moves local z up and logs facing (0.00, 1.00),
   arrow -90 (up); 90: (1.00, 0.00), 0 (right); 0: (0.00, -1.00), 90 (down); 270: (-1.00, 0.00),
   180 (left). The frames' arrow pixels fit the art turned 270 (260 at 5-degree steps), 0, 90, 180.
   The base walking north draws it pointing left (`minimap_shots/live/base_walk_180_minimap_3x.png`).
4. **The signs** were placed right relative to the player (world X right, world -Z up) but on a map
   that was mirrored and at 256 px a region. READ (vslot_013): 8x8 quads (+-4) whatever the art's
   size, drawn only inside `w/2 - 8` = 44.5 px. MEASURED (harness): signs at world offsets (192,0),
   (0,-192), (-240,120), (300,300), (400,0) land at 16.0, 16.0, 22.4, 35.4, 33.3 px from the centre,
   exactly the computed points, 8x8.
5. **The zoom buttons outside their circles**: `mm_window.ddj` is 140x184 (MEASURED) and ginterface
   gives the window 140x184; it was stretched to 136x175, which slid the art's circles and bars up
   and left of the children laid at their authored rects (the + circle by 3.3 and 7.1 px). Now 1:1.
   MEASURED: every child sits at its authored rect (zoom-in 107,136; zoom-out 90,152; X 8,32; Y
   67,32; area 12,9; map button 99,47).
   **The systemic text rule.** READ: CIFStatic lays its text out in `0x64d9b0` -- left / centred /
   right and top / centred / bottom within its rect by the text's extent, then truncated
   (`0xb42d10`, `cvttsd2si`) and drawn unclipped by `0x8b48b0` / `0x8b2290` with each glyph cell's
   top at the point. A Godot Label is never smaller than its text and grew right and down from the
   rect's corner, so a centred row shorter than the font's line drew low, and a right-aligned word
   wider than its rect started at the rect's left. `UiBuilder.place_label` now lays a CIFStatic's
   text label by the client's rule when its rect settles and whenever its text's size changes;
   captions of button and art statics get the matching grow directions. What it moves, MEASURED on
   the box (Arial fallback) across the minimap, player info, target, underbar and all twelve
   HudPanels windows: `GDR_PMI_TXT_HP` / `_MP` 1 px up (centred, 13-pixel line in 12);
   inventory's and equipment's `GDR_INVENTORY_STA_GOLD` "Gold" 2 px left (right-aligned, 26 wide in
   24); autopotion's `GDR_AUTO_POTION_ABNORMAL_QUICKSLOT_STA` 8 px left; party match's
   `GDR_PARTYMATCH_SLOTLIST_NUM_BTN` caption half a pixel left. Nothing else moved. Window captions
   (title strips) are not CIFStatic text and keep their rects (`hud_registry_frame_test.gd`,
   `hud_settle_test.gd` pin them).
   MEASURED against the retail crop (frame matched at scale 2.00, offset 26,2): with retail's own
   strings, "Hotan Kingdom" spans x 22..104 and starts at y 11 in both; "X:114" / "Y:244" caps start
   at y 34 here and 35 in retail. The box has no Tahoma, and the archive's Arial fallback has the
   smaller ascent (about 10.9 px at 12 against Tahoma's 12.0), which accounts for the pixel.
   INFERRED, not measured with Tahoma.
6. **The corner.** READ: `0x79f030` calls the minimap's SetPos with `(screen width - 0x81, 0)`. The
   art is opaque over columns 0..128 and rows 0..171 (MEASURED), so it is flush with the top-right
   corner and 11 transparent columns hang off the edge. It sat 14 in and 10 down (ours). MEASURED:
   the window's rect is (895, 0) 140x184 in a 1024-wide viewport.

## Six-hundred-and-twenty-ninth round, review follow-up: hit rate and parry show numbers, the stat panel no longer floods the server, and a berserk ends the way the client ends it

The review confirmed every READ claim of round 629 byte for byte and a real-X run of E, +, Tab and
the ready circle. It found six things; this follow-up fixes them. Labels as in the round.

**1. Hit rate and Parry ratio have numbers.** READ (the reviewer's): retail's server sends both in
0x303D -- the client's `FUN_00880f80` stores the u16 hit rate at +0x14 and parry at +0x16 of the
stats block both windows draw -- built by `CGObjPC::vslot_334` (0x4ebe30) from params 11 and 9.
OpenSRO already computes the two for combat (rounds 378/379): `combat.CharacterRate(level, the
weapon's HitRateMin)` and `CharacterRate(level, defenderParryRate)`. They are now the stats
packet's fifth and sixth tails (`characterRates`, rounded), decoded by `StatsNet` and drawn in
`GDR_PMI_TXT_HITDAT`/`PARRYDAT` and the character window's `GDR_PI_TEXT_HIT_DAT`/`PARRY_DAT`. The
stats.go comment that "the engine never reads these two" was wrong and is gone. OPEN: retail also
adds buffs and masteries to params 11 and 9; ours carries neither.

**2. No refresh storm.** The panel asked for stats on EVERY OpBuffStart/End in the zone, and zone
entry replays everyone's buffs; and every equipment list counted as an equip change, which opening
the bag also sends. Now: only this player's buffs (behind `SelfCast.claims_start/claims_end`), only
a real change of what is worn (an empty acknowledgement list is skipped and the next real list is
compared with the last), and every cause in one frame makes ONE request (a deferred flush).

**3. The berserk end.** READ: the client's 0x30BF handler (0x8a80a0), kind 4 (the body mode):
value 1 reads one more byte and, for its own player, calls `FUN_00778ae0(0, 1)` -- the display
starts; value 0 ends the body mode and does not touch the display. The server's side is
`CGObjChar::SetBodyMode` (0x4a9fc0) -> `GObjPC::BroadcastStateChange` (0x4a8340), which appends
chardata+5 for kind 4 value 1. `FUN_007b5300` -- which round 629 called "the end from the server"
-- is the reset run on DEATH (kind 0 value 2 -> `FUN_0077b000`) and on a ZONE RESET
(`FUN_00787860`). Now:
- the server broadcasts 0x30BF kind 4 value 1 (extra byte 0, OPEN what chardata+5 holds) at
  activation and value 0 when the activation runs out -- the tracker expires lazily, so a timer
  (`scheduleBerserkEnd`) pushes it, standing down if a newer activation moved `ActiveUntil`;
- the client decodes the extra byte, starts the display on its own value 1, ends it on its own
  timer 2 (the 12 s drain), and fades it out on death and on a zone change (`reset_hwan_display`);
- an AttackResult's `berserk_active` no longer starts or ends anything -- retail's attack packets
  carry no such flag -- and the berserk request's gate tests the count only, as 0x00778ac0 does.

**4. Fade conflicts.** Each item's running fade is kept and killed on a new fade, a refresh or a
start, so an old fade-out's hide callback cannot hide the orbs of a berserk started after it.

**5. The setter** is `FUN_00778ae0` exactly: `(0, 0)` refreshes nothing; a non-zero count without
the flag refreshes; the flag starts the display unless timer 2 is running.

## Six-hundred-and-twenty-eighth round, review follow-up: the reflection is as bright as the game's, clips at the water, leaves out characters, and the sky is the game's cloud layer

The review confirmed the mirror's geometry: its marker's reflection lands where predicted, within
retail's own 14 px bias. It found six problems, and this follow-up fixes them. Labels are as in
the round.

### 1. The reflection was tone-mapped twice

The target holds what the screen shows, already tone-mapped. The water pass sent it through the
tone map again, so a reflecting lake came out about 1.27x too bright.

**How the output is transformed (MEASURED).** A grey ramp written as an unshaded ALBEDO was read
back from the screen.
- This renderer shows `srgb(T(lin(a) * exposure))`, where T is Godot 4.2's filmic curve (A 0.88,
  B 0.6, C 0.1, D 0.2, E 0.01, F 0.3). The fit is 1.7/255 rms over 19 steps.
- The candidates without the sRGB legs fit at 7.5/255 or worse.

**The fix.** The shader now samples the target raw and writes `srgb(T^-1(lin(s x WaterColor)) /
exposure)`. The screen therefore shows s x WaterColor: retail's MODULATE of displayed values,
with WaterColor as the gamma-space texture factor.

**The deep-water pixel fit** (lake, from above, no fog, bump zeroed; screen against the target at
retail's mapping):

| Output | rms against s x WaterColor | Ratio of screen to s x WaterColor (R, G, B) |
|---|---|---|
| The displayed value written straight, the double tone map | 23.7/255 | 1.23, 1.28, 1.28 |
| After the fix | **0.7/255** | 0.98, 1.00, 1.00 |

Hooks: `OPENSRO_QA_WATER_DUMP=<dir>:<frame>` saves the target and the screen, and
`OPENSRO_QA_WATER_NOBUMP=1` zeroes the bump. `OPENSRO_QA_WATER_OUTMODE` = 1 writes the
displayed value straight and 2 writes the ramp.

### 2. The sky is the game's cloud layer

The curved band was our CloudDome, a finite 3000-unit hemisphere over the player, showing its rim
in the sky and in the water.

**What retail draws (READ).**
- **The sky step** (`FUN_00a26f60`) zeroes the camera's position, sets the far plane to
  5,000,000, and turns Z and lighting off before drawing. The cloud layer is drawn by
  `FUN_00a19330` -> `FUN_00a3f570`.
- **The mesh:** the vertex buffer built in `FUN_00a3de90` is a flat 5x5-vertex grid at y = 20000.
  x and z run from -4,000,000 to 4,000,000 in 2,000,000 steps, and u and v from -32 to 32 in steps
  of 16. That is one `cloud1.ddj` repeat per 125,000 units.
- **Scrolling:** u scrolls by `frac(GetTickCount() / 500000)` (texture matrix _31, TTFF COUNT2).
- **Colour and alpha:** colour is MODULATE(texture, TFACTOR), whose RGB is environment channel 4
  (`FUN_00a3eb40`'s sixth argument, world+0x685f from record+0x158). Alpha is MODULATE(texture,
  TFACTOR alpha), where TFACTOR alpha is world+0x68c7 = (channel 12 + 1) / 2.
- **Fog:** linear from 90,000 to 200,000.

**What changed.**
- `cloud_dome.gdshader` places the layer relative to the eye (view rotation only) and pins it to
  the far plane with the depth test on.
  - That draws it behind everything. OURS: a transparent material cannot be ordered before
    Godot's opaque pass.
  - It is drawn in both the main view and the mirror.
- `World3D.cloud_layer_mesh` builds the grid.
- The scroll is READ; the old 0.008 UV/s drift is gone.
- The colour and alpha come from channels 4 and 12, sampled at the reference time. Jangan
  measured colour (1.00, 1.00, 1.00) and alpha 0.755; environment 1 measured (0.91, 0.99, 0.99)
  and alpha 0.743.
- Pictures (`water_shots/r628rv_{before,after}_jangan_main.png`): the arc is gone, and clouds
  cover the sky.
- The sun glow billboard is still OURS.

### 3. The clip plane

`FUN_0045e0d0` builds a plane through three points, with the points' order swapped between the
two cases: above water it keeps y >= h, underwater y <= h. The round's text is corrected.

Godot 4.2 has no user clip planes, no custom projection, and no public way to get a
StandardMaterial3D's generated shader (`get_shader_rid` is absent, MEASURED on the box). So:
- **Terrain:** each region's terrain gets a mirror-only copy, `MirrorTerrain`. It is the same
  mesh on layer 18, which the main camera now excludes.
  - Its surfaces use `WaterReflection.clip_material`: a shader that reproduces what the terrain's
    StandardMaterial3D uses (albedo texture, vertex colour, the MUL lightmap detail layer on UV2,
    shaded or unshaded, blend, render priority).
  - It discards fragments on the wrong side of `global uniform vec4 water_clip_plane`, which is
    set each frame.
  - The main view's terrain is untouched.
- **Scenery objects** are drawn into the mirror unclipped (OPEN): their materials are
  ObjectLoader's.
- **Measured**, at the reviewer's view (lake, yaw 90, pitch -45, distance 300, no fog): non-sky
  pixels in the top 85% of the target went from **2.01%** (the lake-bed strips and the player
  under the water) to **0.31%**. What is left is the far bank's poplars, which stand above the
  water.
- **The WRAP strip.** With retail's squeezed mapping, `v = 0.48 + 0.8 y/z` stays inside
  [0.018, 0.942] across the screen, so only the bump (at most +-0.057) can reach past an edge. That
  wrap is retail's own (stage 1 is WRAP, READ).

### 4. What the reflection draws, and when

**READ.** While world+0x26c3 is set, the reflection render skips the game's draw callback
`DAT_01101920`, which is `LAB_0084c700`. It is registered through `SWorld::vslot_040` (0x009f7040, which stores it) from the client's startup, `Client_LoadAllRefData` at 0x00844cd0.
- Stage 1 of that callback calls vtable +0x28 of the object at `[0xeecea4]+0x120`.
- Stage 2 calls the world's vtable +0x60 and +0x30 with 0xec24c0 and 0xec24e4.
- Which objects these are is INFERRED: the characters and the effects. The landscape pass keeps
  the sky, the terrain and the scenery.

**What changed.**
- The mirror's `cull_mask` is `MIRROR_TERRAIN_BIT | REFLECTED_BIT`.
- The cloud layer and the scenery containers (`mark_reflected`) are on REFLECTED_BIT.
- Characters, NPCs, monsters and effects stay on layer 1, which the mirror leaves out.
- The plane is now chosen, and the target enabled, only among water blocks **in the camera's
  frustum**: a bounding sphere per block, against `Camera3D.get_frustum()`. This matches retail's
  view-tested list. With none in view, the target is `UPDATE_DISABLED`.
- The block list is cached and rebuilt only when a region registers, leaves or moves; it was
  rebuilt every frame.
- The bump sampler CLAMPs, as retail's stage 0 does (sampler state (0, 1/2, 3), READ).

**Frame times.** Averages of 15 ten-frame windows (frames 59-199), main + target in ms per frame,
reflection on in both. Before is 1b2d317.

| Spot | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Lake, shallow | 2.80 + 2.52 = 5.31 | 3.35 + 1.73 = **5.09** |
| Moat, along it | 4.56 + 5.36 = 9.93 | 6.04 + 3.52 = **9.56** |
| Jangan square | 5.88 + 7.67 = 13.55 | 7.30 + 5.64 = **12.94** |

The target's share falls by about 30% without the characters and effects. Jangan's square keeps
the reflection on because the plaza pool (plane -33, under the paving) and the moat are in the
frustum. Retail's list is view-tested, not occlusion-tested, so it would keep it on too.

### 5. Doc fixes

The mirror fields are the orbit camera's look-at y (0x221a) and orbit angle (0x223a), and the
v mapping is squeezed (0.8 against 0.866). The round's text is corrected in place.

**Tests:**
- `water_reflection_test.gd`: 30 ok, ALL PASS. New checks cover the clip plane both ways, the
  clip shader's code, the mirror's layers, and the cloud mesh.
- `remote_godot.sh check`: ALL LOAD.
- `remote_godot.sh tests`: 145 suites, 0 failing. Go tests: green.

**Still OPEN:**
- Clipping the scenery objects in the mirror.
- The identity of the two skipped callbacks' objects.
- The cloud layer's draw order against Godot's opaque pass.

### Rounds 623-628 integration review (int/visual): seven fixes, each measured

The final review of int/visual merged rounds 623 to 628 and found seven problems. All are fixed.
Before is b50a400.

**1. Video memory leaked with Water Reflection on.** `WaterReflection.clip_material` cached
the mirror terrain's materials by the source material's id. Every region commit makes new
terrain materials, so the cache only grew. It held every streamed region's lightmap and ground
textures.
- MEASURED: the same tour, 8 regions west and back (about 230 cell builds), then texture memory
  back at home:
  - before: 322.7 and 325.6 MB with the reflection on, against 111.3 MB with it off;
  - after: **112.7 MB on**, 111.3 MB off.
- The cache is gone. Each copy lives and dies with its MirrorTerrain node, and the four shader
  variants are still shared.
- Load cost of the copies: main-thread terrain for the first 25 cells is 2225 ms on against
  1967 ms off (+13%).

**2. Two-pass MTRL front faces drew over nearer transparents.** The material review follow-up
gave the front pass a higher `render_priority`. Priority is global, so every such pass drew
after every priority-0 transparent in the scene.
- MEASURED with a GPU probe: a two-pass object 20 units behind a nearer blue transparent quad
  painted over it. The single-pass control did not.
- The front pass is now a twin MeshInstance3D (`ObjectLoader.add_front_pass`). The twin has the
  same mesh, skin and transform, priority 0, and `sorting_offset` 0.01 (OURS). This is wired at
  every build site: `_commit_node`, `attach_rigid`, and the skinned body and item pieces.
- After: the nearer quad stays on top.
- A two-pass box with depth writes off draws its front faces (green) over its back faces (red).
- Negative: the twin at -0.01 turns the box centre red, so the probe can see a wrong order.

**3. The cloud layer covered distant geometry.** At `z = 0.99999 w`, with a 0.05 near and an
11,520 far, the clouds sat at a view depth of about 5,400.
- MEASURED: opaque quads at 6,000, 8,000 and 11,000 units were painted over.
- They now sit at `z = w` (depth 1.0).
- After: quads at all eight distances (1,000 to 11,000) keep their colour, and the open sky is
  still cloud.
- Retail draws the layer first with Z off (READ). This gives the same result.

**4. The fog colour is the square root of channel 9 (READ).**
- The chain: `FUN_00a1baf0` clamps channel 9 into world+0x68a3..ab, then stores
  `sqrt` of each into world+0x68b7..bf. `FUN_00b42de0` is the CRT sqrt, with `fsqrt` at
  0xb42e1c; the calls are at 0xa1d164, 0xa1d17b and 0xa1d192. `FUN_00a26f60` then sets those
  as D3DRS_FOGCOLOR before the landscape draws.
- Both the cloud layer's fog and the main Godot fog now use `EnvironmentReader.render_fog_color`.
  `OPENSRO_QA_FOG_RAW=1` restores the old colour, for comparison.
- Jangan: channel 9 is (0.357, 0.580, 0.677), which now renders as (0.598, 0.762, 0.823).
- Size of the main-view change, MEASURED on one build with and without the hook, over the world
  area of the frame (the HUD excluded), at four spawn viewpoints:
  - mean |Δ| 2.0 to 6.4 /255;
  - 4.7% to 20.8% of pixels change by more than 12/255, most on the distant wall and hills;
  - the largest change is 54/255.
  - For example, looking at the south gate the mean goes from (116, 128, 126) to (123, 135, 132).
- The fog's density (a disclosed choice) is unchanged.

**5. The cloud fog is measured in view depth.** Range fog is off in the sky step (READ,
render state 0x30 = 0), so the fog runs on view depth, not radial distance.

**6. MTRL stage coverage.** The mod shader now evaluates:
- ADDSIGNED2X (9);
- MODULATEINVALPHA_ADDCOLOR (20, colour);
- BLENDTEXTUREALPHAPM (15, alpha);
- TEMP as 0;
- the D3DTA ALPHAREPLICATE and COMPLEMENT modifiers.

That covers every op in the census. Any other op is drawn as MODULATE, and
`stage_ops_handled` reports it. The SRCCOLOR pairs 3/6 and 3/14 are relabelled "given": they
are exact only for an unlit stage result, since a lit one is drawn light × L², not
(light × L)².

**7. Mirror terrain shader and stale comment.**
- The mirror terrain shader now blends its detail layer by the detail texel's alpha, as
  BaseMaterial3D does.
- It carries the untextured fallback's AO lightmap. The lightmaps are RGB8, so the alpha is 1
  and the picture does not change.
- The stale dome comment in `_try_add_real_sky` is replaced.

**Tests:**
- object_loader_test: the twin and priority 0, with a negative for a single-pass material; the
  ops, with a negative for op 12; the modifiers; the relabels.
- water_reflection_test: no cache, the material freed, AO present, the unshaded negative, and
  the detail alpha.
- environment_reader_test: the square root, the raw-channel negative, and the clamp before the
  root.
- `check` and `tests` pass, and the Go suite is green (see the commit).

## Six-hundred-and-twenty-eighth round: water reflects the sky, the banks and the trees, as the game's own Water Reflection option draws it

The shipped `Setting\SROptionSet.dat` has Water Reflection ON (round 627's follow-up), and the user
wants the authentic look. This round implements retail's reflection pass, `Map::FUN_00a2df70`, and
makes it the default. The plain animated water of round 627 stays behind the same option.

**Labels.** READ means recovered from `sro_client.exe` (decompile, asm, constants read out of the
exe). MEASURED means counted on the box. INFERRED follows from what was read but was not itself
read. OURS is this project's choice.

### What FUN_00a2df70 does (READ)

- **When it runs.** `FUN_00a2b370` sets the reflection plane (world+0x26c4) to the PlaneHeight of
  the first drawn-list block that has water: PlaneType != -1 and state != 0. The list is ordered
  by block distance from the camera's block.
  - world+0x26bf ("reflect this frame") is set when option 6 (world+0x2e68) is on and such a plane
    exists.
  - world+0x26bb ("underwater") is set when also `eye.y - 0.5 < plane` and the camera's own block
    has water. 0.5 is `_DAT_00e1b7d0`.
  - With 0x26bf clear, the function draws nothing.
- **The reflection render, `FUN_00a2dc20`.**
  - Target and depth: the 512x512 target world+0x27bb, with its own 512x512 D16 depth buffer
    +0x27bf. Both are created by option case 6. Only depth is cleared (Clear flags 2).
  - The camera: above water, the orbit camera's look-at y (world+0x221a) becomes `2h - y` and its
    orbit angle (world+0x223a) is negated, which mirrors the camera in the plane (corrected in the
    review follow-up; this first said "eye y" and "look vector"). Underwater, the camera is left as
    it is.
  - Clipping: a user clip plane is enabled (SetClipPlane, D3DRS_CLIPPLANEENABLE 0x98). It is built
    by `FUN_0045e0d0`, a plane through three points, with the points' order swapped between the two
    cases: above water it keeps y >= h, underwater y <= h. (Corrected in the review follow-up: this
    first read `_DAT_00e1b878` = -1 as the normal's y.)
  - What is drawn: the landscape pass `FUN_00a26f60`, the same routine as the main view (sky,
    terrain, objects), over the block list the mirrored camera sees (world+0x2793). World+0x26c3
    is set during the render; the water pass's caller skips water when it is set.
- **The bump map** (world+0x68df, `FUN_009f2050(0x3c)`): `skybox\waterbump3.ddj` converted to
  D3DFMT_V8U8. du = (left - right) / 2 and dv = (row above - row below) / 2 on byte 0 (blue),
  wrapping at the edges, C division.
- **Stage setup, above water, PlaneType 0 (pass A).**
  - Stage 0: COLOROP BUMPENVMAPLUMINANCE, ARG1 TEXTURE (the bump). BUMPENVMAT00/01/10/11 are
    world+0x2c10/0x2c14/0x2c20/0x2c24, LSCALE 1, LOFFSET 0.
  - The bump matrix is `[[0.04 cos, -0.04 sin], [0.04 sin, 0.04 cos]]` of `t * 0.5 * 9`. 0.04 is
    `_DAT_00de4f70` as a double, and t is `*(float*)(DAT_0110f7d0 + 0xa0)` (`SWorld::vslot_004`, 0x00a2cf60).
  - Stage 1: MODULATE(TEXTURE = the reflection target, TFACTOR). Its texture coordinates are
    TCI_CAMERASPACEPOSITION with TTFF COUNT3 | PROJECTED, through the texture matrix
    `u = 0.65 x/z + 0.5`, `v = 0.8 y/z - 0.52`, sampled WRAP. So v is 0.48 + 0.8 y/z: the screen
    position, flipped, 0.02 off.
  - The texture factor is `0x8C | WaterColor x 255`. Its alpha 0x8C is read by no stage.
  - Stage 2: colour SELECTARG1 CURRENT, alpha SELECTARG1 TEXTURE (the block's 17x17 shoreline
    alpha, texcoord set 1).
  - Result: colour = reflection x WaterColor, alpha = shoreline. **The water1NN frames are not
    used** in this path.
- **PlaneType 1 above water (pass B).**
  - The texture factor is `0xC8000000`. Stage 0 is SELECTARG1 TEXTURE (water201), with alpha
    SELECTARG1 TFACTOR.
  - Stage 1 is BLENDCURRENTALPHA(CURRENT, reflection). Stage 2 was disabled after pass A.
  - Result: colour = 0.784 water201 + 0.216 reflection, alpha 0.784, no bump.
- **Underwater (world+0x26bb).**
  - Texture matrix `u = 0.65 x/z + 0.5`, `v = -0.8 y/z + 0.52`, which is not flipped.
  - Texture factor `0xC8 | WaterColor x 128` (`_DAT_00d8e480` = 128.0). Alpha is SELECTARG1
    TFACTOR = 200/255.
  - Drawn over every block with PlaneType != -1 and state != 0.
- **Render state:** cull NONE, SRCALPHA/INVSRCALPHA, ZWRITE 0 during the pass (set back to 1
  after it). The stage-0 to stage-2 samplers are LINEAR.
- **Water Reflection is option 6.** Video control 4, `UIIT_STT_WATER_REFLECTION`, stored as
  SROptionSet.dat tag 5. The shipped file has it at 1 (the round 627 follow-up).
- **`wave1..3.ddj`** are not used by either water pass. They are loaded to world+0x295b and handed
  out only through `SWorld::vslot_027`, whose callers were not traced.

### What changed

- **`client/scripts/mapm/water_reflection.gd` (new, class `WaterReflection`).** It holds the rules
  above.
  - A SubViewport and a Camera3D render the mirrored view; the camera is `mirror_transform`, with
    the up axis negated so the camera stays a rotation.
  - `pick_plane` chooses the nearest water block's plane; `is_underwater` is world+0x26bb.
  - `bump_image` and `bump_matrix` build the bump.
  - The target updates only while a plane exists; with no water loaded it is `UPDATE_DISABLED`.
- **`water_reflection.gdshader` (new).** It samples the target at the flipped screen position
  (plain underwater) plus the bump offset, with the v bias of 0.02. It draws the three cases above.
- **`World3D`.** It reads the option once per world scene:
  - `ClientSettings` `[world] water_reflection`, default **true**;
  - `OPENSRO_WATER_REFLECTION=0/1` overrides it for a run.
  - With the option on, each region's water gets the reflection materials and registers its drawn
    blocks for the plane choice.
  - Water meshes sit on visual layer 20, which the mirror camera leaves out. Off draws round 627's
    animated water, unchanged.
- **`MapmWater.Built.drawn`** lists each drawn block's (x0, z0, plane).
- **`OPENSRO_QA_WATER_TIMING`** prints the main viewport's and the target's measured render time
  (CPU + GPU) every 10 frames.

### What is OURS or INFERRED

- **No user clip plane (OURS).** Godot 4.2 has none. Geometry under the plane stays out of the
  mirror only when it is back-face culled; the terrain is, a two-sided prop is not.
- **The target's width (OURS).** It is 512 rows by `512 x aspect` (910 at 16:9), not a stretched
  512x512. A Godot camera cannot stretch its frustum into a square target, so the same projection
  needs the screen's aspect.
- **Sampling (corrected in the review follow-up).** Retail's fovy is 60 degrees, so its
  projection's P22 / 2 is 0.866, not 0.8. The texture matrix's 0.65 is exact for u at 4:3, but its
  0.8 squeezes the reflection vertically to 0.924 and shifts it 0.02. That misregistration is now
  reproduced. This first sampled the exact flipped screen position.
- **The bump (OURS / INFERRED).** V8U8 is read as `s / 128`. The bump time is Godot's seconds, and
  that retail's t is seconds is INFERRED.
- **BUMPENVMAPLUMINANCE (INFERRED).** Its luminance term is left out, because V8U8 has no L
  channel and stage 1 never reads stage 0's colour.
- **The plane choice (OURS).** It ignores retail's view test and picks among the loaded water
  blocks.

### Measured

- **Tests:**
  - `water_reflection_test.gd`: 22 ok, ALL PASS. It covers the option, bump derivation and
    wrapping, C division, the bump matrix at 0 and a quarter turn, the mirrored camera (eye,
    determinant, look direction, straight down), the plane choice, underwater, and the shader and
    material.
  - `remote_godot.sh check`: ALL LOAD.
  - `remote_godot.sh tests`: 145 suites, 0 failing.
  - Go tests: green.
- **Negative:** the same test file on a68a03a:

```
note: res://scripts/mapm/water_reflection.gd is missing -- checking what the tree draws instead
FAIL a Water Reflection option exists and is ON by default, as the shipped SROptionSet.dat has it
FAIL the default water surface samples a reflection (got StandardMaterial3D)
2 FAILURES
```

- **Pictures** (`water_shots/r628_{before,after}_{lake,moat}_{above,shallow}.png`; before is the
  option off, which is round 627's water). Numbers are the mean colour of the band under the HUD
  (800x250 at 420,320).
  - **Lake 98/159, from above:** before (0.30, 0.38, 0.25), after (0.43, 0.58, 0.44). That is the
    sky mirrored and tinted by environment 1's tan WaterColor.
  - **Lake, shallow angle:** before (0.41, 0.38, 0.15), after (0.67, 0.60, 0.25). The far bank's
    poplars now stand upside down in the water. The strip under the bank has a standard deviation
    of 0.093, against 0.041 without the reflection.
  - **Moat 96/168, looking along it:** the water strip goes from (0.23, 0.37, 0.33) to (0.24, 0.45,
    0.45), the sky reflected in Jangan's teal.
- **Cost:** the average of 15 ten-frame windows at the held viewpoint, frames 59-199, in the
  box's GL Compatibility on its RX 5700 XT. Numbers are main + target, in ms per frame.

| Spot | Option off | Option on |
|---|---|---|
| lake, shallow | 3.33 | 2.67 + 2.64 = **5.31** (+2.0) |
| moat, along the moat | 6.49 | 4.91 + 6.05 = **10.96** (+4.5) |
| moat, first viewpoint (wall and field) | 4.15 | 3.43 + 3.35 = **6.78** (+2.6) |

  The reflection roughly doubles the scene's render cost, as retail's does, because it draws the
  landscape twice. One moat run beside the wall measured 12.7 off against 25.7 on.

### Still OPEN

- The clip plane: an oblique projection would need Godot 4.3's `Camera3D` projection override, or
  a shader discard.
- Whether `FUN_00a26f60` in the reflection render draws characters. `CIFCharacterWnd::FUN_0080beb0`
  runs after it, which was not traced.
- The option's default when SROptionSet.dat is absent.
- Retail's time base t.
- The `wave1..3.ddj` callers.

## Six-hundred-and-twenty-seventh round, review follow-up: the shoreline truncates, a deep block is one quad, and the water's colour follows the camera's block

The review confirmed that the olive lake is authentic for the path without reflection. 98/159 is
environment 1, whose WaterColor is tan all day, and stage 1 is a plain MODULATE with the texture
factor. The review also found the items below. Labels are as in the round.

- **The shoreline nibble truncates (READ).** At 0x9fb338-0x9fb34e, `fnstcw` / `or eax,0xc00` /
  `fldcw` / `fistp` sets RC=11 (chop) for the conversion. The nibble is therefore
  `clamp(trunc((PlaneHeight - h) * 0.5), 0, 15)`, not round-half-to-even as the round inferred.
  - Fixed in `MapmWater.shoreline_nibble`, `waterat`'s `nibble()`, MAPM_FORMAT.md and the round's
    text.
  - The test now expects 3 deep → 1, 7 deep → 3 and 29.9 deep → 14.
  - The block states do not depend on the conversion, so the census's 39,486-of-39,510 match
    stands.
- **Dead code:** `World3D._load_region_navmesh` is deleted. Its only caller was the old water.
  The orphaned navmesh-walls doc comment above it moved to `_add_navmesh_walls`, where it
  belongs.
- **A block deep at every vertex is one quad (OURS, a mesh economy).** Its alpha is 1 everywhere,
  so 2 triangles draw what 512 did.
  - MEASURED, `waterat -census`: 22,284 of the 33,056 drawn type-0 blocks are deep at every vertex
    (67.4%).
  - A fully flooded, fully deep 5x5 window of loaded regions goes from 25 x 36 x 512 = **460,800**
    triangles to 25 x 36 x 2 = **1,800**.
  - The real map's worst 5x5 window was 460,800 triangles, centred 111/230. Its worst is now
    **243,292**, centred 89/140, where most water is shore.
  - The reported lake's 3x3 load went from 119,296 triangles to **47,386**. 98/159 alone went from
    18,432 to 2,622.
- **Dungeon worlds draw no block water (READ).** In `FUN_00a220b0`, `world+0x237e & 0x8000`
  selects the object-water branch, which jumps past both block loops.
  - world+0x237e is the current region id: `SWorld::vslot_001` sets it and hands bit-15 ids to the
    dungeon manager.
  - `MapmWater.draws_block_water(region_id)` mirrors this, and `_try_add_real_water` skips such a
    region.
  - MEASURED: Map.pk2's 4,721 `.m` files top out at x = 127. So no field region has the bit;
    dungeons are `.dof`.
- **WaterColor follows the camera's block.**
  - READ: `Map::FUN_00a1baf0` takes the environment from `**(world+0x2783) + 4`, the EnvironmentID
    of the first block in the drawn-block list. `Map::FUN_00a2b030` copies that list in order from
    an ordered map. `Map::FUN_00a2b370` fills that map with every block that passes the view test,
    keyed by `dx^2 + dz^2` from the camera's block (world+0x6914/0x6910).
  - INFERRED: that block comes from the frustum's apex, the camera eye at world+0x220a/0x2212.
  - So one environment drives the whole world's water; it is not one per region.
  - What changed:
    - `_try_add_real_water` keeps each region's 36 block EnvironmentIDs as group metadata.
    - `_water_env_tick` runs on the zone label's 10-tick throttle. It finds the block under the
      camera and re-samples channel 14 into the shared material when the EnvironmentID changes.
  - MEASURED in the lake run: from the "above" viewpoint the camera stood over an environment-5
    block. The log read `water colour follows the camera's block, environment 5: (0.8928, 0.5766,
    0.2321, 1)`. At the shallow viewpoint it read environment 1 again.
- **The region flag at +0x2475 stays OPEN.**
  - READ: `FUN_00a361b0` copies it from byte 0 of the region's entry in the world's runtime map at
    world+0x7b64. Only `SWorld::vslot_046(1, regionId)` sets that byte. `SWorld::vslot_045` (a
    named object added to a region at run time) creates the entry with the byte at 0.
  - It is game state, not map data. No call to slot 46 was found through the world pointer.
- **The reflection path is the Water Reflection option (READ); it is not implemented.**
  - The chain:
    - `CIFOption_Video::Create` labels video control 4 `UIIT_STT_WATER_REFLECTION`.
    - `FUN_006f4210` stores control *i* at settings-record byte 4 + *i*, so byte 8.
    - `CGame::FUN_00835000` passes byte 8 to `SWorld::vslot_043(6, v)`, whose case 6 creates the
      reflection target (`FUN_009f2050(0x3c)` into +0x68df) and two 512x512 textures.
    - `SWorld::vslot_037` passes `param_1[0xb9a]`, which is +0x2e68.
    - `FUN_00a220b0`'s caller takes `FUN_00a2df70` when +0x2e68 and +0x68df are both set.
  - Storage: `<client>\Setting\SROptionSet.dat` (`FUN_00502680`). It is a u32 13, then tagged
    fields.
    - Tag 9999 is one byte, the record selector.
    - Tag 5 is two bytes: record 0's byte 8, then its byte 0x18. Tag 105 is the same for record
      1.
  - **The shipped file on the box** is identical in `/opt/sro-files/client/setting` and the
    pserver client. It has selector 0 and tag 5 = `01 00`, so **reflection ON**. Record 1 has it
    at 00.
  - The client's default with no file is not found. `CGInterface::FUN_0077c190` does not
    initialise the struct when the load fails. Whether the launcher writes the file is not
    checked.

## Six-hundred-and-twenty-seventh round: water is seen from above, drawn where and how the game draws it

**The report (v0.1.457).** "Water has mostly been working but you can't see it from above, only
from underneath." The tester's screenshot reads X 4680, which is region y 159, local x 720. From
the lake bed, a teal sheet hangs overhead and the banks sit below it. From above, there is no
water.

**Labels.** READ means recovered from `sro_client.exe` (decompile at `/var/tmp/decomp_client`,
constants read out of the exe). MEASURED means counted on the box's real archives or a real run.
INFERRED follows from what was read but was not itself read. OURS is this project's choice.

### Why it was invisible from above (MEASURED)

`NvmWater.build_water_mesh` wound every quad `base, base+2, base+1`. By Godot's own front-face rule,
`Plane(a, b, c)`, all 512 triangles of a flooded block face **down**. The terrain is wound
`i00, i10, i11`, and its triangles face up. The material culled back faces, which is the default.

The world group's `scale.z = -1` mirror does not change which side is the front. Godot flips its
cull test for a negative-determinant transform, and the terrain proves it: the terrain has the
opposite winding to the water and renders from above. So a player saw the water only from below.
This is the negative:

```
FAIL every drawn water triangle faces up, the side a player above sees (got 0 up, 512 down)
FAIL every vertex carries the shoreline alpha
FAIL the frame repeats 4 times across a block, 0..4 (READ _DAT_00e1b860; got max (1, 1))
FAIL MapmWater exists (the rest of this suite needs it)
4 FAILURES
```

This is `mapm_water_test.gd` run on dev b22edf5, with only the test file copied in. There, the
"drawn water" checks fall back to NvmWater, the builder World3D drew with. The same file passes
all 34 checks on this branch.

### The height was right (MEASURED)

`waterat -region 98/159` gives the height for all 36 blocks of the reported region: PlaneType 0,
PlaneHeight **50**. The `.nvm` plane map carries the same 50. At local (720, 500) the ground is
-22.80, so the water there is 72.8 deep. At (720, 640) it is 53.5 deep.

The tester was standing on a lake bed about 70 units down, under a correctly placed surface. The
banks sit below the plane only as seen from under it. Walking on the bed is authentic, per the
user, and this round leaves movement alone.

### How retail draws water (READ)

- **Where the fields live.** `FUN_00a35c50`, the block loader, seeks to `index * 0xa0f + 0xc` and
  reads the block's 0xa0f bytes straight into its record. So PlaneType is at block+0x7ed, WaveID at
  +0x7ee and PlaneHeight at +0x7ef. That is +6 for Flag and EnvironmentID, then 289 7-byte
  vertices.
- **The block's layout.** Block index = col + row*6. The block's origin is (col*320, row*320), with
  `_DAT_00e1b908` = 320.0.
- **A region flag.** The same loader forces PlaneType to -1 on every block when a region flag at
  +0x2475 is set. `FUN_00a361b0` sets that flag from the first byte of a per-region object list.
  What that list is remains OPEN.
- **The shoreline.** `Map::FUN_009fb280` handles PlaneType 0 only; it returns early for any other
  type. For each of the 17x17 vertices it computes
  `nibble = clamp(trunc((PlaneHeight - height) * 0.5), 0, 15)` (truncated: see the review follow-up), with `_DAT_00e1b7d0` = 0.5 and
  `_DAT_00d878a0` = 15.0. `FUN_009f6ef0` is only the plane height here, because all four corners
  are set to it. The nibble goes into a 17x17 texture: A8R8G8B8 `n << 28` when
  `DAT_0110f728 < 3`, otherwise A4R4G4B4 `n << 12`.
- **The block state.** The same function overwrites +0x7ee with the block's state:
  - 0: every vertex is dry; the block is not drawn.
  - 1: no vertex is dry.
  - 2: some vertices are dry and some partial.
  - 3: some vertices are dry and some fully deep.
- **The draw** (`Map::FUN_00a220b0`, the path without reflection; `FUN_00a2df70` is the other path):
  - Geometry: ONE flat quad over the whole block, drawn as a triangle fan at PlaneHeight.
  - Stage 0 is the alpha texture: colour SELECTARG1 CURRENT, alpha SELECTARG1 TEXTURE.
  - Stage 1 is the frame `water\water1NN.ddj`, index `(GetTickCount() / 100) % 30`, so **10 fps**.
    Colour is MODULATE(TEXTURE, TFACTOR) and the alpha op is disabled.
  - The texture factor is `0xB4RRGGBB`. Its RGB is world+0x688f/93/97 x 255.
  - Stage-1 UV runs 0..4 across the block (`_DAT_00e1b860` = 4.0), so one frame repeats every 80
    units. Stage-0 UV runs 1/32..31/32.
  - Render states: ALPHABLENDENABLE 1, SRCBLEND SRCALPHA, DESTBLEND INVSRCALPHA, **CULLMODE 1
    (NONE)**. CULLMODE goes back to 3 and ZWRITE back to 1 after the pass.
- **PlaneType 1 blocks** are drawn only when their own WaveID byte is non-zero. They use
  `water\water201.ddj` for colour, SELECTARG1 TFACTOR for alpha (0xB4), the same UVs, and no
  culling.
- **The water colour.** world+0x688f is environment channel **14** (WaterColor).
  - The record reader `FUN_00a1b650` reads channels 0-6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12 and then, for version
    >= 1002, the ColorGraphs at record+0x1f4 and +0x228 and the FloatGraph at +0x36c. So +0x228 is
    channel 14.
  - `Map::FUN_00a1baf0` evaluates +0x228 into world+0x688f..0x6897 and clamps it to [0, 1].

### How often each case occurs (MEASURED; `waterat -census`, 4,704 regions, 169,344 blocks)

- **PlaneType:** -1 on 128,879 blocks, 0 on 39,510, 1 on 955. The type-1 blocks sit at plane 800,
  filling whole regions around 88-92/124-129.
- **Shoreline state:** the state recomputed from the heights matches the file's own WaveID on
  39,486 of the 39,510 type-0 blocks. The tool that authored the maps ran the same rule, which
  checks the reading of FUN_009fb280.
- **The navmesh plane map disagrees with the `.m`:**
  - It marks 3,846 blocks as water where the `.m` has -1.
  - It marks 6,259 drawn type-0 blocks as not water.
  - The two sources disagree on plane height 217 times.
- **Frame alpha:** `water101.ddj` and `water115.ddj` are 64x64 A8R8G8B8 with every alpha 255.
  `water201.ddj` is 512x512 DXT1.

### What changed

- **`client/scripts/mapm/mapm_water.gd` (new):** builds water from the `.m` blocks by the rules
  above.
  - Each drawn type-0 block is its 17x17 vertices at PlaneHeight. Each vertex's alpha is its
    nibble / 15. OURS: this is the A4R4G4B4 branch; which branch a machine takes is OPEN, and the
    other gives at most 240/255.
  - The mesh is wound so the front faces up, and the material draws both sides anyway, as retail
    does.
  - The conversion truncates (READ in the review follow-up: RC=11 at 0x9fb338; this entry first said
    round-half-to-even, an INFERRED x87 default that the code overrides).
  - The per-vertex alpha stands in for the 17x17 texture (OURS). The two agree at every vertex.
- **The materials** (`MapmWater.water_material` / `still_material`) are unshaded: stage 1 never
  reads the diffuse, so lighting cannot reach the water. They are alpha-blended with
  `CULL_DISABLED`.
  - The animated material's albedo is WaterColor, sampled at `ENVIRONMENT_REFERENCE_TIME`. Its
    alpha comes from the vertex colour.
  - The still material is water201 at alpha 0xB4.
  - World3D keeps one of each per world. The player's environment writes WaterColor into the shared
    material, as retail writes one texture factor.
- **The frame rate** is 10 fps (READ), replacing the 8 fps guess. The frame repeats 4 times a block
  (READ), replacing a repeat every 5 units.
- **Logging:** World3D logs, per region, the drawn and skipped blocks, the plane heights, and the
  triangles facing up and down. It also logs the environment's water colour.
- **`server/cmd/waterat` (new):** per-block fields and shoreline state, the `.nvm` comparison,
  `-census`, `-column`, and a `-dump` of one Map.pk2 file.

### Verified

- **Tests:**
  - `mapm_water_test.gd`: 34 ok, ALL PASS.
  - `remote_godot.sh check`: 365 scripts, ALL LOAD.
  - `remote_godot.sh tests`: 144 suites, 0 failing.
  - `go build ./... && go test -count=1 -p 1 ./...`: green, after adding `waterat` to
    server/README.md's tools table (the README probe caught it).
- **Runs** (lane box copies, `--shots`, radius 1; the frames are in the session's
  `water_shots/`):
  - **98/159 at the reported spot (720, 500), X 4680 in the HUD:**
    - The log reads `98\159.m -- water: 36 animated block(s), 0 still, 0 dry skipped, plane
      height(s) [50], triangles 18432 up / 0 down`. Environment 1's water colour is (0.64, 0.56,
      0.38).
    - From above, frame 41, the band under the HUD averages (0.26, 0.28, 0.13), which is the lake
      bed, before the fix. After the fix it averages (0.30, 0.37, 0.24), which is the water.
    - The shallow-angle shots show a lake surface to the far bank.
    - From under the water, the view is unchanged, as the report described.
  - **97/168 with the farmland moat in 96/168 (640, -380 from 97/168):**
    - Before the fix, `96\168.m -- no real water surface built (30 real water plane cell(s))`: the
      navmesh tiles carry no water texture, so the moat was dry.
    - After the fix, `96\168.m -- water: 6 animated block(s) ... [-20], triangles 3072 up / 0
      down`. The moat's pixels go from (0.32, 0.29, 0.26), which is stone, to (0.22, 0.39, 0.35),
      which is teal water. Jangan's environment 15 water colour is (0.36, 0.69, 0.62).
  - **The Jangan square:** the pool quad at -33 lies under the plaza. The fountain's own water is
    the fountain model's, and the frame is identical before and after.
- **The parked "Moat water" item is resolved by the `.m` (MEASURED).** In 96/168, only block row
  4, which is the moat band, is PlaneType 0 at -20.
  - Rows 0-3 are the farmland at -43 to -80 that the plane level would have flooded. The `.m` marks
    them -1, although the `.nvm` marks them type 1.
  - Row 4's blocks are state 2: dry and partial.

### Still OPEN

- **The region flag at +0x2475**, which hides every block's water. Its source list is not
  identified.
- **Which alpha-texture format a machine gets:** `DAT_0110f728`.
- **The reflection path:** `FUN_00a2df70`, taken when option +0x2e68 and +0x68df are set.
- **The per-object water branch:** when `+0x237e & 0x8000`, lists of water quads come per object,
  with their own fog.
- **The `wave1..3.ddj` textures** are loaded to world+0x295b, but their draw was not traced.
- **The two environment special modes** (+0x2eb4 == 1, +0x2e5c == 2/3) that replace or damp the
  colours.
- **Time of day:** WaterColor is sampled at the fixed reference time, like the sky.
- **Depth writes:** whether retail writes depth during the water pass is INFERRED. ZWRITE is set
  back to 1 after the pass, so it was presumably off. Godot's alpha pass does not write depth
  either.

## Six-hundred-and-twenty-fifth and -sixth rounds, material review follow-up: blended canopies keep their leaves at distance, and the MTRL shader draws what the mod says

The combined review of c1bc28a confirmed every READ claim. Performance was flat: 864 materials,
8 shaders, the same draw calls. It found real bugs in the MTRL mod shader, fixed here.

**1. Blended canopies vanished at distance.** The mod shader discarded on mipmapped alpha, so the
72 tree models that blend their leaves lost them as they receded. The test now reads mip 0
(`textureLod(albedo_texture, UV, 0.0)`), as `foliage.gdshaderinc` does; the blend still uses the
filtered alpha.

MEASURED with the new `tools/render_material_distance.gd` (non-background pixels, dev c1bc28a →
now):

| Model | 1× | 8× | 16× |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tre_bamboo01` | 2234 → 2273 | 20 → 48 | **0 → 11** |
| `tre_maple01` | 5781 → 5781 | 89 → 89 | 26 → 26 |

The maple's leaves are not an MTRL layer, so it is unchanged. Renders:
`equip_shots/material/bamboo01_cmp.png`, `bamboo01_far_zoom.png`, `maple01_cmp.png` and
`maple01_far_zoom.png`; the top row is dev.

**2. The stage bytes.** `_mod_pass` skipped zero values, so D3DTA_DIFFUSE (0) never reached the
shader, and MODULATE(DIFFUSE, TEXTURE) computed texture × texture. All six bytes are now sent
whenever the mod blends.

DIFFUSE is the lit vertex colour. READ from `Shader\vertexshader0.c`:
`oD0 = saturate(N.L) · c11 + c10`, where c11 = material Diffuse × the D3DLIGHT9 Diffuse (READ:
`FUN_00bf0e20` and siblings, from the globals `CObjRendererVS::vslot_025` copies from the light
it passes to `SetLight(0)`). Its alpha is 1, because both registers' w is 1.0 and oD0 saturates.

The shader splits the stage result:
- the part that multiplies DIFFUSE is drawn as ALBEDO, lit by the scene like every other
  material;
- the part that does not is drawn as EMISSION, unlit, as a SELECTARG1 TEXTURE draw is.

OURS: DIFFUSE × DIFFUSE is drawn as DIFFUSE, and TFACTOR is white.

**3. MODULATE2X.** READ: the renderer seeds flag 0x1000 on every object draw (`vslot_024`,
`vslot_038`), and `FUN_00c42a60` turns it into stage-0 COLOROP MODULATE2X, so the client's
object colour is texture × lit diffuse × 2. Both paths now agree with each other:
- the flag-word path draws ALBEDO = layer ambient × texture for that MODULATE2X;
- the MTRL shader draws a lit coefficient L as L × ambient / 2 (OURS: the anchor), so its
  MODULATE2X equals the flag-word path and its MODULATE is half of it.

A mod that only tests keeps the renderer's MODULATE2X. Whether the flag-word path matches the
client is **not changed and not settled**:
- Its brightness was tuned by eye: `light_energy` 0.3 against a Dunhuang wash (round 43), with
  ambient energy 1.
- The client's formula is read only in part. c11 is READ. c10's product (the object's own colour
  × the light's Ambient, built in `vslot_024`) is INFERRED. The env record → D3DLIGHT9 mapping
  was not traced.
- A measured comparison needs those values. No global change was made.

Jangan before and after (`jangan_cmp.png`): 2–3% of pixels differ by more than 12/255, and the
means move by under 1/255. Those pixels are the MTRL-drawn pieces.

**4. Pass order.** Godot 4.2 does not keep a `next_pass` after its material in the transparent
sort. A two-pass object's front-face pass now has a higher `render_priority`, so the back faces
draw first.

**5. Alpha funcs.** Every D3DCMPFUNC is compared exactly, on the alpha byte against the ref
byte. The census has 5 NOTEQUAL (for example `khotanshop_designer`, `arabia_malak` and
`rocmountainquest_youngwoman2`, at 128) and 1 LESSEQUAL (`samarkand_potion_etc01`, 148). An
MTRL mod that tests without blending now draws through the mod shader in opaque mode, with its
own func.

**6. Blend pairs.** The census has 18 D3DBLEND pairs, not one unmapped pair. Godot 4.2's GL
Compatibility has mix, add and mul (`rasterizer_scene_gles3.cpp`). Each pair is drawn through
them by what the shader writes as colour and alpha, and labelled (`ObjectLoader.BLEND_EMULATION`,
BMT_FORMAT.md):
- 8 are exact;
- 5 are exact given BLENDFACTOR white or a destination alpha of 1. The client sets BLENDFACTOR
  only in `Map::FUN_00a1d790`, and whether that is live for objects is OPEN;
- 7 are OURS, with the dropped term named.

The dungeon water is unchanged in shape (`water_cmp.png`, frames 20/48/76): 0.4–1.1% of pixels
differ by more than 12/255.

**7. Minor.**
- A new `Skeleton3DBuilder.is_skeleton_bone` excludes `OBJECT_SPACE_BONE` from the loops that
  measure a body by its bones: the paper doll's framing, the QA feet report, the NPC bounds
  fallback and the monster label height.
- `census_item_envmap.gd` counts MTRL-governed layers apart.

**Tests** (`object_loader_test.gd`, "review 1–6"):
- the mod shader tests mip 0;
- a DIFFUSE byte of 0 reaches the material;
- lit is ALBEDO and unlit is EMISSION, anchored to the flag-word brightness;
- the front pass has the higher `render_priority`;
- each of the six funcs is kept exactly on an unblended mod;
- all 18 pairs are labelled.

The distance behaviour is measured by the render tool above; the headless test runner cannot
rasterize.

## Six-hundred-and-twenty-sixth round, review follow-up: hats and fringes are cut again, armour stays whole, and the reason is READ

The review confirmed round 626's chest and legs fix and the comma split. It also found a
regression: "draw every item layer solid" drew 95 DXT1 hat and flag layers as opaque black
cards, and 590 formerly cut layers solid (`rv626_shots/hats_zoom.png`). Round 625 had made the
same inference the other way, "items draw untested", and drew 91 avatar cutouts solid. This
follow-up merges feat/foliage (4f65715) and replaces both guesses with the client's rule.
`ObjectLoader.layer_draw_rule` is now the only material rule; round 626's `equipment_material`
is removed.

**How retail spares armour (READ).** The mechanism is the item's own **ENVMAP mod**.

- `CRTModEnvMap::vslot_004` (0x00c83690) ORs `0x60000000` into the draw flags, which switches
  off the material's own `0x200` test. It then sets its own test from the mod's flag word:
  ALPHAREF 1 / GREATEREQUAL when bit 1 is set, no test otherwise.
- It does this before it compares its material index, so it covers every material. The index
  only decides where the reflection texture is bound. Round 625 read the index as the scope.
- Items write index `0xFFFFFFFF` and header word 1 = 1. `CObjRendererVS::vslot_038` runs
  word-1 = 1 mods once per part, before any material, through `FUN_00c45110` → `FUN_00c7b4e0`
  with index −1.
- Per-material mods (word 1 = 2) run through `FUN_00c451e0` → `FUN_00c7b540` in every draw
  path, also before `FUN_00c42a60`.
- `CRTModBumpEnv` sets no alpha state.
- `CRTModProgEquipPow` (the `0xe21f0000` override) is the +N glow. It is attached only through
  `CObjCharacter::FUN_00a5f3e0`, for a non-zero per-slot byte with a matching row, so it does
  not explain plain gear.
- MTRL mods (kind 0) appear on no item checked.
- Stage-0 alpha is the texture's (`FUN_00c42860` sets `ALPHAARG1` = TEXTURE). So without the
  mod, the gloss alpha really would be cut.

**MEASURED** with `tools/census_item_envmap.gd`, over all 1,421 item `.bsr` files the table
names:

| ENVMAP flag word | Item `.bsr` files |
|---|---|
| 1 | 602 |
| 3 | 465 |
| 0 or 2 | 3 |
| none | 351 |

Of the 2,890 bit-9 layers on item models:
- 1,315 are under a no-test mod;
- 1,220 are under a ref-1 mod;
- 355 keep their own 0x80 test.

Those 355 are the 1-bit hats, Santa hats, mittens and flags. Joined with the review's
`itemalpha.tsv`, only 2 of the 85 that join have mostly graded alpha: `light_02_ha` and an
`_ef` layer (OPEN in TODO).

Examples:

| Item | Layer flags | ENVMAP word | Drawn as |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sword_01` | 0x0340 | 1 | solid |
| `spear_11` | 0x0141 | 1 | solid, two-sided |
| `heavy_11_la` | 0x0341 | 3 | cut at alpha 0 only |
| `clothes_04_ha` | 0x0341 | none | cut at 128 |

The code change is `BsrReader.ParsedObject.env_map_flags`, the object's last ENVMAP flag word.
`layer_draw_rule(flags, env_map)` applies it to every layer, and the `item` argument is gone.

**The skin rule, finished (READ).** The review traced the path: `CompoundObj::FUN_00be7640`
passes 1 for object types 0, 1 and 5, which reaches `ResObject::FUN_00be3540`, which builds
with `FUN_00be2f80`. That builder resets the palette entries to 0/0 per vertex, skips a 0xFF
slot, and blends slot 0's weight over the sum; a zero sum gives blend 0.

So an empty slot, or a weightless vertex, lands on entry 0, which is not a bone. Both slots
empty occurs: `heavy_15_ba` 14 vertices, `sd_t_area_smith_part1` 7. The reader now mirrors
this. Entry 0 becomes `BmsReader.OBJECT_SPACE`: `to_arrays` puts it one past the palette, and
`Skeleton3DBuilder.build_skin` binds that index to a parentless bone that never moves. That
entry 0 is the object's own transform is INFERRED. `FUN_00be28d0`, used for other object types,
keeps the previous vertex's entry instead; that difference is recorded in BMS_FORMAT.md.

The review's sweep counts **158 meshes** made skinned by the 0xFF change: NPCs, monsters, pets
and carts, not only armour. MEASURED with `tools/probe_skinning.gd` at the idle's 0.5 s, dev →
now:

| Model | Skinned pieces | Pieces that were missing their skin on dev |
|---|---|---|
| NPC `sd_t_area_smith` | 3 → 4 | `sd_t_area_smith_part1`, 717 vertices: the whole lower body, posed y 0.02..13.51, feet on the ground |
| monster `immotal` | 5 → 7 | two parts |

The unchanged pieces pose identically. Renders are in `equip_shots/followup/`
(`npcs_cmp.png`, `gear_cmp.png`, `gear_zoom_3.png`, `hats_zoom_3.png`; rows are dev b22edf5,
round 626 d345414, now):
- the hats' spikes and fringe are cut again, as on dev, where round 626 drew their cards solid;
- the Degree-11 set is whole, with its cloak cut only at alpha 0;
- `spear_11` is solid.

**Tests.**
- `skinned_bsr_assembler_test.gd` is rewritten on `layer_draw_rule`, using the measured flag
  words, and the foliage shader at scissor 0 or 1/255.
- `bms_reader_test.gd`: both slots empty → OBJECT_SPACE, one past the palette, bound to a still
  bone.
- `bsr_reader_test.gd`: `env_map_flags` is object-wide.
- `object_loader_test.gd`: round 625's cases without the item column.

`probe_equipment.gd` now walks `Item.model_paths` instead of re-splitting `model_path`, which
had become dead code. `render_lineup.gd` takes a `.bsr` path as a body.

**After merging round 625's follow-up (87b5066).** Round 625's reader and rule now carry the
object's input. The item branch is gone; `env_map_flags` is the last ENVMAP mod in the ambient
set with word 1 of 1 or 2; the MTRL mod and the two-pass flag are added. Re-run under that
reader, the census is unchanged (`envcensus3.log`):

| ENVMAP flag word | Item `.bsr` files |
|---|---|
| 1 | 602 |
| 3 | 465 |
| 0 or 2 | 3 |
| none | 351 |

The bit-9 layers are unchanged too: 1,315 no test, 1,220 ref 1, 355 own test.

- The item ENVMAP mods have two shapes. 1,041 are ambient-set, word 1 = 1, material
  `0xFFFFFFFF` (once per part). 29 are word 1 = 2 on a named material (per material). The
  reader counts both, as READ.
- 32 item `.bsr` files carry an MTRL mod, which the merged rule applies. No item is two-pass.

Checked after the merge:
- `probe_equipment.gd`:

| Piece | Drawn as |
|---|---|
| `spear_11` | foliage shader, scissor 0 (two-sided, uncut) |
| `heavy_11_la` | scissor 1/255 |
| `heavy_11_ba`, `sword_01` | standard, opaque |
| `clothes_04_ha` | scissor 128/255 (its two-sided `_2s` card and the one-sided brim) |

- `probe_skinning.gd`: the smith and `immotal` pose exactly as they did before the merge.
- Renders: `hats_zoom_4.png`, `gear_zoom_4.png` and `npcs_cmp_merged.png` in
