## Five-hundred-and-seventy-fifth round: the server loads the teleport network, with the grounded fee, waiver and restriction rules

The first round of the town teleporters. `cmd/export-refdata -mode teleport` turns the client's
`teleportdata.txt`, `teleportlink.txt` and `teleportbuilding.txt` into three CSVs in one directory;
cmd/server's `-teleport-dir` loads and joins them at boot (`msg="teleport network loaded"
dir=... points=222 links=292 buildings=77` on a retail export); `internal/teleport` holds the lookups and
the rules the next item's handler will call. Nothing a player sees yet. The full record is
`docs/RE_COMPLETION.md`'s round 575.

- **The fee** is the link's second word, waived below level 21 (`cmp al,0x14` at `0x5136de`,
  `GObjPC::HandleTeleportUse`); GM accounts and a testing flag are two more waivers, own design.
- **The level gate is real, and it is not columns 8/9 alone.** Columns 7-21 are five (type, data,
  data) triples, and the server's `FUN_00513a70` walks them before the fee on
  `CMainProcess::FUN_004f2b50`'s teleport path: type 1 is a level range (`0x1c15`), 2 and 7 a trade
  cart, 3 the character's PvP state against a mask of barred states (`0x1c19`; no retail link uses
  it, and OpenSRO, with no PvP state, passes NEUTRAL -- a stand-in), 4 and 5 a held item, 6 a job
  state. The evaluator enforces them only when a mode byte on the link is 0, and what fills it was
  not read; OpenSRO enforces them (a stand-in). Jangan's links to Hotan, Constantinople and Samarkand
  carry `(1, 1, 110)`, so a level-111 character is refused there.
- **`0x1c14` is "already teleporting"** (`GetTeleportState`, tested first), not the range test the
  record called it; the range test refuses with its own return value.
- The client's link parser reads one leading column fewer than the file has; the data (the Roc
  link's type-4 item, 23973 `ITEM_QNO_RM_MEETROC_6_01`) fixes where the triples start.

## Five-hundred-and-seventy-second round: a monster whose height ray found no ground at spawn keeps retrying until the ground commits

The user, 2026-09-25: "Mangyangs are now floating". The full record -- the logs, the change, the
tests and the live runs -- is `docs/RE_COMPLETION.md`'s round of the same title.

**Cause, measured.** The monster list is asked for in `World3D._ready` and applied whenever it
arrives; `_spawn_or_update_monster` fires one terrain ray per body, and a miss left the body at the
server's y -- 0 for every Jangan monster -- for good, since nothing re-rays a standing body. Whether
the ray misses is decided by the **loading-screen drain**, the real player's path
(`_should_show_loading_screen` is true whenever `OPENSRO_MAPM_PATH` is unset). Of the render box's
63 first-entry logs with monsters (rounds 558-569):

- the 47 that took the loading screen (`OPENSRO_QA_FORCE_LOADING=1`, directly or through
  `--reconnect`) all float monsters: the 14 on rounds 558-561's code the four Mangyangs (the list
  lands after the centre, before its neighbour 96/168), and the 33 on round 562's code and later --
  which awaits the screen's frame between the request and the centre's build -- all 23
  (`/var/tmp/r562/entry.log` is the first);
- the 16 without it -- the QA path, which commits the whole grid in one frame before the list is
  applied (`/var/tmp/r567/rays{,2,3}_{entry,cross}_{hf,tri}.log`, `/var/tmp/r569/*.log`) -- are the
  counter-case: the Mangyangs stand on the ground (e.g. `130,-37,2280`), and only the 7 vertex
  bodies where the plain ray misses (below) are at 0 on the heightfield (none on the trimesh). So
  a default QA render does not show the float.

The "why now" (the public server's latency used to let 96/168 commit first, and rounds 565-567 took
that away) is NOT confirmed: the in-memory server floated the Mangyangs in every loading-screen
entry since round 558.

**Fix.** A miss now puts the body on a wait list (`_monster_heights_pending`), and
`_step_monster_bodies` retries it every physics frame inside the existing 32-a-frame budget until
the ground is there; `World3D: monster <id> <name> height resolved after <n> frame(s): <y>` says
when. Ground items had the same race and get the same retry (`GroundItems.resolve_pending`), with a
fair share of the budget: the monsters may take it less the items' want, up to half
(`MonsterMotion.monster_height_share`), so bodies that never resolve can no longer starve the items.
`OPENSRO_QA_MOB_LOG`'s 10-second line counts the waiting bodies' retries apart from the walking
legs' resolves. Other players, NPCs and the player's own placements were checked and are not the
pattern.

**And two things the retry alone left in the air, both fixed in the same round:**

- **Round 567's heightfield has no answer on its own grid lines.** Read from Godot 4.2.2's source:
  a vertical ray tests only the one cell `floor()` picks, with Moller-Trumbore's closed bounds, so
  a point on the cell's edge misses about as often as not and the neighbouring cell is never tried.
  Measured (`terrain_collision_test.gd`'s grid probe, committed; a synthetic height field, no game
  data): plain vertical rays miss at 6,909 of the 9,409 vertices of the region at the frame origin
  and 50,391 of a radius-2 grid's 235,225 (13 of its 25 regions). On Jangan's real ground the plain
  ray missed at 7 of the 9 monsters standing on 97/168's grid vertices (it answered at (-300, -880)
  and (-300, -760), and at all 10 on exactly one grid line); those 7 never came down -- four of
  them about 30.6 above the ground. The trimesh answered at all 23 monster columns, 19 of them on
  grid lines. Every vertical terrain ray now goes through `TerrainCollision.vertical_ray`, which
  steps a column within `RAY_GRID_EPSILON` (0.01, an own engineering choice: 0.001 and 0.01 both
  miss none of the 235,225 in the probe, 0.0001 misses 3,416) off the line, trying the other side
  if the first misses; 0 misses anywhere in the probe. The height it reads can be off by at most
  0.01 times the steepest triangle's |dh/dx| + |dh/dz|: 19.165 over Jangan's 25 regions (99/170),
  so 0.19 at worst, 0.033 in 97/168. Round 567's "every vertical ray hits both" is corrected in
  place below: its 1,600 columns all sat inside quads.
- **The scene's placeholder `Ground` answered the ray.** It is on the terrain-only layer until the
  first terrain commit, so a body listed within 100 of the origin before the centre commits was
  placed on it (0.898) for good; `VoidCatchFloor` did the same for a body listed at y -995 or
  lower. The placement ray (`_terrain_hit_height`) now passes through both; the player's own body,
  ground check and snap still see them as before.

**Measured, not pictured** (`OPENSRO_QA_MOB_HEIGHTS`: each body's drawn y against the game's own
terrain ray, a plain ray at the exact column, and the drawn mesh from the parsed heightmap; a
server-backed Jangan entry with the real loading drain, radius 2, on the heightfield):

- Fixed: all 23 bodies wait at spawn; the 19 in 97/168 come down the frame after its commit
  (frame 15), the 4 Mangyangs the frame after 96/168's (frame 20). At the last report every one of
  the 23 is drawn 0.40 above its terrain ray -- the placement's lift -- the ray answered by 97/168's
  or 96/168's collider and equal to the drawn mesh; the plain ray has no answer at 7 of the 9
  bodies on 97/168's grid vertices -- it answers at (-300, -880) and (-300, -760) -- and answers at
  all 10 on exactly one grid line. 0 `terrain ray none`, 0 `SCRIPT ERROR`.
- The helper bypassed (live): those 7 stay at y 0 -- 30.51 to 30.67 above the drawn mesh for four,
  3.50 for one, 2.45 and 2.49 under it for two. Round 569's code with only the report added (the
  first pass's run): the Mangyangs stay at y 0, 37.13 to 49.42 above the ground.
- The "-30.27" several bodies resolve to is -30.67 ground plus the 0.398 lift: the drawn mesh reads
  -30.67 at those columns.

**Landed on round 571's code** (full record: `docs/RE_COMPLETION.md`'s step 9):

- *One terrain placement.* `_terrain_commit` places the group through `TerrainCollision.place_group`
  only. Round 570's `_group_position` stays, for the grid's corner. `region_grid_state_test.gd` now
  holds the two equal for 16 cells (Constantinople's -single-frame corner, world x -175,680,
  included) at four anchors. Its NEGATIVE: `place_group`'s half set to 970 gives 16 FAILURES.
- *Float32.* Under `-single-frame`, world x reaches -175,680. There the 0.01 nudge is stored as
  1/64 = 0.015625, which is still off the line. Above 262,144 it would round back onto the line.
  The grid probe fires at that corner cell and misses none.
- *Runs, repeated on the combined code.* The acceptance run: all 23 bodies are drawn 0.40 above
  their own ray at tick 340, with 0 `terrain ray none` and 0 `SCRIPT ERROR`. 96 suites pass, and
  so do 58 Go packages. The README's crossing (b): the tick-600 summary's longest work frame is 85
  ms (round 567: 86), with 0 over 100 ms.

## Five-hundred-and-seventy-first round: one world frame and one bucket behind `-single-frame`, default off

With each zone in its own frame and its own broadcast bucket, a player who walked out of Jangan
toward Donwhang stayed in Jangan's bucket and never met Donwhang's monsters, which stood in
Donwhang's frame. `-single-frame` (env `OPENSRO_SINGLE_FRAME`, **default off**) names every framed
zone in Jangan's 97/168 frame and keeps every player and roster monster of those zones in one bucket.
The full record is `docs/RE_COMPLETION.md`'s round 571.

- **The landing moves with the frame.** A zone change lands at the middle of the town's centre, as
  it always has, now named in the one frame: `worldmap.Landing`. Donwhang is
  `ToWorld(102, 153, 960, 960, 97, 168)` = (-28800, -9600), not (0, 0, 0), which would be Jangan's
  middle and off the grid a Donwhang client builds.
- **Heights, measured, not assumed.** Every vertex of the five town centres and their radius-2
  neighbours was read from the box's Map.pk2 (125 regions), read-only.

Measured by the Go suite (the flag-on and flag-off world tests over TCP, the roster placement and

## Five-hundred-and-seventieth round: the server names the coordinate frame on the wire, and the client builds its grid inside it

A world coordinate means something only once you say which region the frame is centred on. Until
this round that was implicit: the server converted into `worldmap.ZoneCentre`, and the client built
around `_resolve_zone_region`. Now `OpEnterWorldResult` and `OpChangeZoneResult` end with a
**FrameRegion** ("x/y", after the entity list, where a tagged client stops reading). The client
builds the zone's grid inside it. The full record is `docs/RE_COMPLETION.md`'s round 570.

- **A no-op today, checked first.** All six labels' server frames equal the client's centres:
  jangan 97/168, dunhuang and donwhang 102/153, constantinople 105/79, hotan 92/135 and samarkand
  106/107. So every zone builds with its centre at cell (0, 0), and the grid is the one it was.
- **Two offsets, not one.** `World3D._cell_offset` is the offset BEFORE the mirror.
  `_group_position` (moved out of `_terrain_commit` unchanged) negates its z, and the group carries
  `scale.z = -1`. The world-space offset, after the mirror, is
  `RegionGridState.cell_world_offset`. The test puts local points through the real placement and
  compares them with `ToWorld`'s own rows. It uses the measured table in the 97/168 frame, and the
  same points in the 98/157 frame, generated by Go. A point moved from 97/168's frame into
  98/157's shifts by **(+21120, +1920)**; the plan's "(21120, -1920)" was wrong.
- **Nothing assumes centre == frame any more.**
  - `_grid_origin_region` is the frame.
  - `_grid_centre_region` is new; the ground-rays wait and QA TEXPROBE read it.
  - Cell keys and `_last_stream_cell` are relative to the frame.
  - `_grid_origin_world` is the frame region's corner.
  - The minimap, the placements and the QA hooks work through group transforms.
- **Not reachable yet (the single-frame item's job):** a frame other than the centre.
  - The server would then have to send a position inside the centre region, because (0, 0, 0)
    would be the frame's middle, off the grid.
  - The height anchor would be the frame's own near-row vertex. Under 97/168's (-2.49), the five
    town centres draw between -151.7 and 254.2, inside the +-1000 snap ray and above
    `WORLD_FLOOR_Y`. Their radius-2 neighbours were not measured.

Measured by the headless suites (94, 0 failing; `check` ALL LOAD) and the Go suite. No live run:
this item kept the box read-only apart from `remote_godot.sh`. A live run should look for the new
line `is built in its own frame -- the server's FrameRegion 97/168`.

## Five-hundred-and-sixty-ninth round: every town's centre is the same on the server and the client, from the game's own NPC rows and gates

The frame-on-the-wire item aborted because the server's `worldmap.ZoneCentre` and the client's
`*_ZONE_REGION` constants named different regions for constantinople (server 100/98, client
104/80), hotan (87/118, 92/135) and samarkand (88/130, 106/107). This round makes them agree, and
the full table, evidence and tests are `docs/RE_COMPLETION.md`'s round 569.

**The rule.** A town's centre is the region where its own NPC rows (npcpos's first column, the
NPC's id, joined to characterdata's second, its ID -- "on the first column" until round 574;
counted by the town's code: CH, WC, KT, EU, CA) and its dimensional gate
(`teleportdata.txt`'s `GATE_<code>`, `SN_ZONE_22001..22005`) agree. Where they disagree, the
server takes the client's constant and the disagreement stays open.

- **Donwhang 98/157 -> 102/153**, both sides: 15 of 26 `NPC_WC_*` rows and `GATE_WC`.
  `textzonename.txt` names 98/157 "Donwhang Ferry" and 102/153 "Donwhang". The density pick of
  2026-08-24 had called 102/153 a ferry crossing near the town; it is the town.

- **Hotan 92/135**: the client was right; the server moves from 87/118 ("Aircraft dock").

  106-107/107-108 corner and `GATE_CA` lands in 106/108, so the server takes the client's 106/107
  (from 88/130, "East-Karakoram"). The plan had read `NPC_SD_*` as Samarkand's; `SD` is Alexandria
  (the text tables name its NPCs, its gates `GATE_SD1`/`SD2` and its regions 90/48-94/48
  "Alexandria").
- **"donwhang"** -- the server's spelling, on the /goto list and the Earth Ghost's roster zone --
  resolves on the client now; until this round it fell through and a `/goto donwhang` left the
  placeholder ground.

**Measured, not pictured.** Each centre's heightmap, read over all 10,404 vertices against its own
anchor (the near-row vertex the client sets to y = 0; the frame is the centre, so each town
calibrates itself): 102/153 draws -55.0 .. 12.4, 105/79 -221.2 .. 32.4, 92/135 -243.8 .. 7.9,
106/107 0.0 .. 6.4 -- inside the +-1000 snap ray and above `WORLD_FLOOR_Y` (-500) everywhere. The
server lands a player at (0, 0, 0), the centre's middle; `walk_probe.gd` from local (960, 960) finds

The QA runs on the box (`/var/tmp/r569/<town>.log`, a GM `/goto <town>` from Jangan with this

| town | centre built | landing (local, the walkable graph) |

## Five-hundred-and-sixty-seventh round: the terrain collides as a heightfield cut the way the ground is drawn, and a streamed cell's collision lap goes from ~25 ms to under 1

The hundred-and-fifty-sixth round named `terrain_mesh.create_trimesh_shape()` the load's
bottleneck and proposed a `HeightMapShape3D` from the height grid instead -- a reading from before
the hundred-and-sixtieth round's archive fix, which took most of the terrain phase with it. So this
round was gated on a fresh measurement: after rounds 565-566 moved the prepare off the main thread,
the trimesh's `collision` lap (`ConcavePolygonShape3D.set_faces`, the BVH build) was 27-30 % of the
streamed cells' main-thread commit (22-39 ms a cell, over half of each cell's terrain commit), in
round 566's shipped-code logs and in today's BASE alike. Over the 25 % bar, so done.
`docs/RE_COMPLETION.md`'s round 567 has the grounding, every log line and the tests; in short,
anchored by function:

- `TerrainCollision` (new): `heights_from_region` lays the region's 97x97 grid out as the shape's
  `map_data` on the prepare's task; `make_shape` and `shape_transform` build and place the shape in
  `World3D._terrain_commit`. `OPENSRO_TERRAIN_TRIMESH=1` builds the old trimesh for A/B.
- **The plan's layout would have been wrong, and a picture would not have shown it.** Godot
  4.2.2's heightmap (read from the 4.2.2-stable source) cuts each cell along the diagonal from
  (x + 1, z) to (x, z + 1); the drawn mesh cuts each quad from (r, c) to (r + 1, c + 1). Laid out
  row for row, as the item proposed, every vertex is in place and every quad is split the other
  way, so inside a non-planar quad the collision is not the drawn ground -- on the suite's
  synthetic hills that layout's rays miss the drawn triangles by up to 17.4 units, and on the real
  Jangan grid 252 of 1,600 probed quads are non-planar enough for it to be off by over 0.5. The
  rows are stored reversed and the shape's z axis flipped back, which also cancels the terrain
  group's mirror: the shape's global basis is a plain (20, 1, 20) scale.
- Benchmark (the README's two commands; BASE / round 567 / the A/B flag): the streamed cells'
  `collision` 657 -> 0 -> 656 ms over the entry's 24 and 791 -> 0 -> 780 over the crossing's 29
  (0 on every cell line: under 1 ms each); the crossing's column, in commit order 97, 96, 98, 95,
  99/165 (so the 85 is 98/165's; labelled `95..99/165` until round 568), 50/45/85/49/49 ->
  29/21/60/23/22 ms a cell, its longest work frame 106 -> 86 ms (113 with the flag), 1 -> 0 frames
  over 100 ms; the entry drain's frames over 100 ms 9 -> 5 (9 with the flag), and its p95 950 ->
  914 ms, inside run-to-run spread (957 with the flag). The round-567 and flag runs ran the code
  before `OPENSRO_QA_GROUND_RAYS` was changed to wait for the grid (a QA-only hook they do not
  enable); the ray runs below ran the committed code.
- **Measured, not pictured** -- a new `OPENSRO_QA_GROUND_RAYS=n` probes the terrain collision on
  an n x n lattice of every loaded region and holds each hit to the drawn mesh's own triangle. On
  1,600 real columns, heightfield against trimesh: every vertical ray hits both, the heightfield's
  within 0.0009 of the drawn triangle and 0.001 of the trimesh's (steepest probed quad edge 5.43 a
  unit) -- **corrected in round 572**: every one of those columns sits inside a quad, 9 and 11
  units off the grid lines, and a vertical ray exactly ON a grid line of the heightfield often
  finds nothing (round 572's grid probe, a synthetic height field -- not 97/168's real heights --
  in the frame origin's region slot: 6,909 of that slot's 9,409 vertices; on Jangan's real ground,
  the plain ray missed at 7 of the 9 monsters standing on 97/168's grid vertices, and the trimesh
  answered at all 23 monster columns, 19 of them on grid lines), so "every vertical ray hits" held
  only off the lines; round 572's `TerrainCollision.vertical_ray` steps every vertical terrain
  ray off them; slanted rays agree within 0.004 (the same 4 missing on both); the camera arm's
  sphere swept down stops at the same travel on 1,594 and within 0.352 on the rest; the snap's ray
  at the server's spawn lands at -54.394 on both; the crossing walk's lines are identical tick for
  tick.
- **One behaviour did change, and it was a latent bug.** The player's own body moved down with
  `body_test_motion` -- move_and_slide's query -- touched the heightfield at 1,600 of 1,600 columns
  and the old trimesh at **0**. The trimesh was one-sided under the world's mirror, the trap the
  sixty-first and sixty-third rounds found (and fixed with `backface_collision`) for the objects'
  navigation-mesh collision; the suite shows the same trimesh unmirrored, or two-sided, is
  touched. So when no walkable graph covered the player, `_physics_process`'s move_and_slide
  fallback sank into the terrain (3.26 units in the suite's 2 s walk) and relied on
  `_recover_if_below_terrain`; on the heightfield it stands on it. Not yet measured in-game on a
  region without a navmesh.

## Five-hundred-and-sixty-sixth round: a streamed cell's objects prepare on its worker task too, and the alpha probes measure the decoded Image instead of reading the texture back

Round 565 moved a streamed cell's terrain onto a `WorkerThreadPool` task and left its objects on
the main thread, in the commit's frame: 26-83 ms a cell at the crossing and 5,346 ms over the
entry's 25 cells on round 565's code. `docs/RE_COMPLETION.md`'s round 566 has the grounding,
every log line and the tests; in short, anchored by function:

- `ObjectLoader.load_object` is now `commit_object(prepare_object(...))`. `prepare_object` is the
  plain-data half -- the `.bsr`/`.cpd`, `.bmt` and `.bms` parsed, each piece's surface arrays
  (`BmsReader.to_arrays`) and trimesh faces (`_piece_faces`, the list `create_trimesh_shape()`
  read back out of the mesh, equal to it element for element), each texture decoded to an Image
  and each material's alpha classified on that Image. `commit_object` builds the ArrayMeshes,
  textures, materials, shapes and nodes on the main thread.
- The three alpha probes take the Image instead of calling `Texture2D.get_image()` (a readback of
  the uploaded texture), same rules and thresholds, measured once per texture and kept in the
  world's texture cache. `OPENSRO_QA_ALPHA_LOG=1` prints each probe consulted. On the entry
  benchmark the count is **0 before and 0 after**: every real layer the 25 cells build is decided
  by its flag word, so the readback path was never reached there. Forced with `OPENSRO_QA_MATS=1`
  as a control: 690 readbacks before, 0 after, the same 341 texture statistics -- 327 identical,
  14 within 0.0002, and on those the readback gave two different values for the same texture
  where the Image gives one.
- `World3D._objects_prepare` (static) runs on the cell's task after the terrain
  (`_cell_prepare`): the `.o`/`.o2` merge, the ownership test -- whose neighbour heightmaps it
  reads under Pk2Reader's lock rather than pre-parsing them on the main thread, since their parse
  is what that lap costs -- and `prepare_object` for every model the world holds no template for.
  `_objects_commit` uploads the textures and places the copies; `ObjectTemplateCache` still owns
  one template per model, now committed from the prepared model.

Measured, the README's two commands, BASE against the shipped code (the pump finishing before it
dispatches, below; `fix2B_*` on the render box -- until the second review these figures were the
first write's dispatch-first run): the crossing's column, in commit order 97, 96, 98, 95, 99/165
(`95..99/165` until round 568), went from 108/123/123/70/69 ms a cell to 50/46/87/51/49 (objects 26-83 -> 5-11 ms on the main thread), its longest work frame from
140 ms to 118 (109 in the review fix's earlier run of the same order; 1 frame over 100 ms, from 3).
The entry: the 24 neighbours' main-thread objects 3,360 -> 460 ms (2,857 ms now on the tasks), the
cells' main-thread sum 10,517 -> 7,457 ms, p95 1,848 -> 990 ms (947 in the earlier run), the drain
19.8 s -> 18.1 s. Every placement is the same -- the entry's 58 map-object lines and the crossing's
67 are identical, and the synthetic objects' node trees, surfaces, faces and materials match
fingerprints taken from round 565's `load_object`. Not better: the entry's NPC phase (692 ms at
BASE, 728-876 over the round's five entry runs -- three dispatch-first, 876/839/840, two
finish-first, 728/743; "four" until round 568 -- unattributed), a reconnect mid-load waits 497 ms
for the dropped tasks (18.8 in round 565's run; measured on the round's first write, which still
dispatched first -- the shipped order's wait was not re-measured; now a `docs/TODO.md` item), and the centre cell is still
5.1 s by design. The crossing's longest frame is now the terrain commit (`collision` 25 ms), the
NPCs (35 ms) and the frame's other work, not the objects; the objects' largest main-thread lap is
`place`, the duplicates.

The round's review found one orchestrator note neither done nor answered: `_pump_cell_jobs`
dispatched the next cell BEFORE committing the finished one, so the next job's snapshot missed
everything that commit cached and its task prepared it again. It now commits first. Counted, not
inferred -- `_finish_cell_job` prints `cell x/y prepared again what an earlier commit had cached --
N ground tile(s), N navmesh(es), N object navigation mesh(es), N heightmap(s) the objects read, N
model(s), N object texture(s) decoded` (`_prepared_again`, before the commit merges anything).

The second review found that count wrong as first committed, and the numbers this round first
gave for it with it: it took every texture a job's prepare named for one it had DECODED, but a
texture the job's snapshot already held is named, not decoded -- the render box's own log had
`cell 97/169 prepared again ... 0 model(s), 2 object texture(s)` for the first streamed commit
after the centre, where nothing could have been cached twice -- and it counted the region's own
heightmap, which the objects take from the terrain prepare's parse. Corrected (a texture counts
only with an Image and a key its snapshot lacked; the `here` parse is not counted; two new
negatives in `objects_prepare_test` fail on the first counter) and the pair re-run: over the
entry's 24 streamed cells, dispatch-first against finish-first, 67 -> 28 things prepared twice
(tiles 10 -> 3, object navmeshes 8 -> 4, heightmaps 2 -> 1, models 16 -> 7, textures 31 -> 13),
and the sum of the `decoded now` tile lines 58 -> 51, the same 7; the crossing 102 -> 32. (The
first counter's 103 -> 66 and 145 -> 84 are withdrawn.) Per cell, what finish-first still counts
follows one commit each -- the cell that was preparing beside it when it was dispatched (97/167
beside 97/169, both dispatched from the snapshot after the centre: 19 of the entry's 28; then
96/168, 96/166, and at the crossing 96/165), from the cells' dispatch and commit frames; the
pump's order cannot hand a job what a job preparing at the same time has not committed yet. The
frames a player sees show no order effect beyond run-to-run spread at one run each (this pair:
crossing longest 114 -> 118 ms, entry p95 954 -> 990 ms; the first pair: 111 -> 109, 1,004 ->
947); the drain's frames over 100 ms fell in both (13 -> 8, 13 -> 7). The cost is the overlap
given up while a cell commits -- one more awaited frame in the entry, 1.1 s more waiting in the
QA drain. The count also corrects the round's first reading of `own` (894 ms at BASE, 1.1-1.2 s on
the tasks): only 2 and 1 heightmaps were read twice, so that difference is not duplicate parses
-- it stays unattributed. `OPENSRO_SYNC_LOAD=1` restores the schedule only: its objects
still go through the split `ObjectLoader` and the prepared trimesh faces.

## Five-hundred-and-sixty-fifth round: a streamed cell's terrain prepares on a worker thread, and a boundary crossing's frame falls from 334 to 144 ms

The hundred-and-fifty-fourth round left this open ("it does not thread the build, so a very heavy
cell can still hitch -- threading the region build off the main thread is the next step if it is
still felt"; its last words restored in round 568), and
round 561's benchmark put a number on it: one ~300 ms frame per streamed cell, five in a row, ~250
of each the terrain. `docs/RE_COMPLETION.md`'s round 565 has the grounding, every log line and the
tests; in short, anchored by function:

- `World3D._try_load_real_terrain` is split into `_terrain_job` (main thread: the one-time tables
  and a snapshot of every cache the prepare reads), a static `_terrain_prepare` (the `.m` read and
  parse, the `.t` lightmap and ground tiles as Images, the mesh surfaces and the collision faces as
  arrays, the navmesh, the wall triangles, `NavGraph.build`) and `_terrain_commit` (the textures,
  the ArrayMesh, the nodes, the shapes, the water, the graph's registration). A streamed cell runs
  the prepare on a `WorkerThreadPool` task (`_dispatch_cell`, two at a time -- an own tuning
  choice) and `_pump_cell_jobs` commits finished ones, one a frame in play and two a frame under
  the loading screen, which now owns the pump while it runs instead of sharing the queue with the
  physics step. The grid's centre still builds whole on the main thread.
- The prepare-thread rule, written at `_terrain_prepare` and in `client/tools/README.md`: no Node
  and no RID-owning Resource off the main thread, no tree, no server, reads only through
  `Pk2Reader` -- which takes a per-handle lock since this round (without it, 4 tasks x 200
  concurrent reads of one entry got 10-13 of 800 wrong) -- and caches reach the task as snapshots.
- The trimesh is no longer read back out of the mesh: `MapmTerrainBuilder.surface_faces` builds
  the same face list from the arrays (equal to `create_trimesh_shape().get_faces()` element for
  element, measured on off-grid heights, which shows the engine's 0.0001 snap), so the commit's
  `collision` lap is `set_faces` alone -- 25-33 ms a cell, from 52-61.

## Five-hundred-and-sixty-third round: the streaming unload forgets the region -- NPCs respawn on return, and a freed group no longer aborts every position lookup

The third item of the map/loading epic (2026-09-25); the full record with every line is
`docs/RE_COMPLETION.md`'s round 563.

- **What the unload left behind.** `_maybe_stream_regions` freed a region's terrain and objects
  nodes, released its scenery templates (round 559) and erased its `_loaded_cells` key -- and kept
  its `_npc_regions_done` mark (so `_try_spawn_region_npcs` returned at its first line when the cell
  streamed back in: the NPCs are the terrain node's children and had gone with it), its
  `[NavGraph, group]` pair, and its entries in `_navmesh_cache`, `_parsed_region_heightmaps` and
  `_object_collision_cache`, none of which anything ever pruned.
- **Measured at BASE, not the plan's failure first.** A `--shots` tour that hops one region a
  viewpoint (`-30,1020` west, `1950,1020` east; a viewpoint is local to the region under the
  player) at `--radius 1` produced the first `region 97/169 unloaded -- 32 scenery templates only
  it placed freed` lines of any log and then 687 x `SCRIPT ERROR: Trying to assign invalid
  previously freed instance. at: _nav_graph_for (World3D.gd:2452)`: the freed group's pair was
  still in the list, the typed `var group: Node3D = pair[1]` raised on it and aborted the function
  on every tick for every region after it, so every later viewpoint and `QA <tick> local` read
  `off-region` and the run went nowhere. A town walked away from and back to came back empty
  only if the walk survived this.
- **The fix is one object.** `RegionGridState` (`client/scripts/world/region_grid_state.gd`) holds
  the seven per-region members; `unload(x, y)` drops the region's cell, NPC mark, nav graph,
  navmesh and heightmap, then the heightmaps of regions neither loaded nor next to a loaded one
  (the ownership test parses neighbours that are not cells: 28 heightmaps for 12 cells) and the
  object collision meshes no cached navmesh lists; the lookups test `is_instance_valid` before
  any typed assignment; `clear_all()` is the zone change. The unload loop prints `region x/y
  forgotten -- <what>; N NPC holder(s) freed with its terrain`, and each viewpoint a `QA GRID
  <name> frame <n> at <x/y> local <lx>,<lz>: cells=.. navmesh=.. heightmaps=.. collisions=.. ...
  objects=.. orphans=.. static_mem=..` line.
- **Measured after.** The same tour: `97/169 forgotten -- ... 30 object collision mesh(es); 7 NPC
  holder(s) freed with its terrain` at the third hop, `7/7 NPC(s) placed in 97/169` (and `2/2 in
  98/169`) again when the row streamed back at the fifth; 0 script errors in 311 lines; `cells=12
  npc_regions=12 nav_graphs=12 navmesh=12` at every viewpoint, `heightmaps` 28 -> 21 and
  `static_mem` 1,040 MB -> 967 MB across the tour, against a growing-only BASE. The first hop of
  the tour does not stand (the player is at `97_168 local 90,1020` at frame 13) -- a QA-harness
  interaction at the first tick, not chased.
- Tests: `region_grid_state_test.gd`, 28 checks, its negative a `FAIL` on the pre-change tree;
  `monster_motion_test.gd` injects through the state; `check` 264 scripts ALL LOAD.

## Five-hundred-and-sixty-first round: the load measured per cell, per phase and per frame -- and the benchmark the map epic is measured on

The first item of the map/loading epic (2026-09-25) is the instrument, not a fix: before anything
about loading changes, what a change is measured with and the BEFORE it is measured against. The
full record with every line and the per-phase sums is `docs/RE_COMPLETION.md`'s round 561; the
benchmark's definition and its two commands are `client/tools/README.md`, "Load benchmark".

- **The metric is main-thread work time per frame, not `delta`.** Every benchmark runs under
  `qa_shot.sh`, which always passes `--write-movie`; Godot's movie writer forces `--fixed-fps`,
  which "disables real-time synchronization" (Godot 4.2, command line reference), at the project's
  60, so `delta` reads 1/60 s on every frame however long it took, and a hitch metric built on it
  would read 16.7 ms for ever. `LoadTimings` (`client/scripts/world/load_timings.gd`) sums, per
  drawn frame, each cell's build time and `World3D._physics_process`'s own step, and reports the
  longest, the p95 and the count over 100 ms (a reporting bucket, not a game value); the wall gap
  between steps goes beside it and carries the writer's per-frame floor (about 0.33 s a frame,
  AGENTS.md; the entry run's longest in-play gap was 368 ms -- a longest, not a typical frame;
  round 564 reworded this from "~0.37 s").
- **The lines.** One `World3D: cell x/y built in N ms at frame f (terrain T [read, parse, env,
  lightmap, tiletable, textures, mesh, collision, walls, water, navgraph], objects O [parse, own,
  templates, place], npcs P [tables])` per cell, the centre included (it was never timed); `region
  grid loaded in N ms (...) at frame f -- C cells S ms, D ms outside the cells over A awaited
  frames`, whose check is `S <= N` (under the loading screen `D` is the screen's build, the UI init
  and the awaited frames, so equality cannot hold); `World3D: longest work frame ...` at the end
  of each drain, every 600 physics ticks (`_qa_step` runs for every player, so a real player's log
  carries it too) and on leaving the tree, each covering the window since the previous one. The
  three accumulators the split summed since round 156 were never reset (round
  559's review); the drain totals now start with the drain's clock.
- **The BEFORE** (`--radius 2`, the real awaiting drain, HUD hidden, a server behind it). Entry:
  the centre cell **5,373 ms in one frame** before the loading screen exists (tile index 944, NPC
  tables 925, templates 1,670 for 69 models, the eight neighbour heightmaps 319 -- 2.6 s of it is
  one-time or first-time work no neighbour pays); the 24 neighbours 231..1,120 ms, mean 417,
  **three a frame** at frames 14-21 (three `built in` lines per frame in the log, 8 x 3 = 24):
  `_drain_initial_load`'s `LOADING_CELLS_PER_FRAME` = 2 per awaited frame, plus the one the same
  frame's physics step pops through `_process_stream_queue` (`STREAM_CELLS_PER_FRAME`) from the
  same `_load_queue` -- nothing gates the in-play pump on the drain, so a change to the constant
  alone changes two of the three; `region grid loaded in 22,752 ms`, cells 15,388, 7,364 outside
  over 9 awaited frames (the screen's one plus 8 batches); longest work frame 5,374 ms, p95 2,844
  (frame 14's three cells: 1,120 + 1,109 + 609), 9 over 100 ms (the centre plus 8). In play: p95 6
  ms, longest 6 ms.
  Crossing (`--at 120,1020 --walk 270`, the edge at tick 147): the new column 95..99/165 streamed
  one cell a frame, 270..323 ms each, longest work frame 328 ms, 5 over 100 ms, p95 5 ms.
- **Where the 15.4 s of cell work goes** (25 cells): terrain 7,987 (mesh 3,177, collision 1,433,
  tiletable 944, navgraph 749, walls 389, parse 386, water 302, textures 199), objects 5,022
  (templates 3,356, own 1,069, place 460), npcs 2,351 (tables 925; the centre's spawning 746).
  The textured mesh build is now the largest terrain lap and `create_trimesh_shape` second, the
  other way round from round 156's reading (round 160's archive fix lies between; re-measured, not
  re-derived).
- The crossing start (120, 1020) was picked with `walk_probe.gd` (terrain, no wall to -280; (150,

tester's log decides that report. The full record is `docs/RE_COMPLETION.md`'s round 560.

  `_environment_table` and its flag) -- one value per loaded script, so entry 2 started with entry

## Five-hundred-and-fifty-ninth round: one scenery template per model per world, freed with the world

Round 558 measured what a reconnect costs -- orphan nodes exactly doubled, texture memory x1.69 --
and named the cause: `_try_load_real_map_objects` kept its built object templates in a dictionary
local to each call, so every region built its own copy of every model it placed (the `cj_s.bsr`
wall five times over five regions) and none was ever freed. The templates now live in one
`ObjectTemplateCache` per world (`client/scripts/world/object_template_cache.gd`): built once per
model path, duplicated per placement, released when the last region placing them streams out, kept
across a zone change (the same models recur; a 600-template cap, an own safety limit, bounds them),
freed in the new `World3D._exit_tree` and again if the cache itself is deleted. `ObjectLoader`
takes a per-world texture cache with it, so two models naming one `.ddj` upload it once. The full
record is `docs/RE_COMPLETION.md`'s round 559; the same reconnect command as round 558, before (this
change absent) and after:

| | before, entry 1 -> 2 | after, entry 1 -> 2 |
|---|---|---|
| texture memory (MB) | 139.96 -> 237.58 (x1.70) | 78.38 -> 92.49 (x1.18) |
| video memory (MB) | 186.41 -> 294.20 (x1.58) | 121.95 -> 137.78 (x1.13) |
| orphan nodes | 3,770 -> 7,540 (x2.000) | 2,757 -> 2,981 (x1.08) |
| templates built per entry | 358 (the nine cells' distinct models summed) | 226 (132 placements reused a neighbour's) |
| exit census: Mesh / Material / Texture / Body / Shape | 2468 / 2468 / 2469 / 2114 / 2114 | 354 / 354 / 355 / none / none |
| `region grid loaded` (ms) | 16,963 / 16,978 | 15,665 / 14,656 (objects 2,260 / 2,104) |
| lower-40% mean of the `square` shot | (0.271501, 0.260978, 0.249704) | the same, to six decimals |

- Every leaked Body/Shape was a template piece: the 2,114 drop per type is exactly what leaves the
  Mesh, Material and Texture counts, and what stays (354 / 354 / 355) is the leaked pieces that had
  no `StaticBody3D` -- consistent with the skinned NPC templates in `_npc_model_cache`, which
  `map-reconnect-fix` frees, together with the static caches. Consistent with, not proven from the
  census.
- Two things the tests caught before the final run: a `free_all()` called from a RefCounted's
  `NOTIFICATION_PREDELETE` is a call on a null instance (no reference left to make `self` from), so
  the freeing is inlined there; and a `replace_all` that turned the new `four_cc = parsed_tex.four_cc`
  into `four_cc = four_cc`, named by the existing DXT3 cutout test.
- The box: an orphaned re-run of round 558's command was holding `/var/tmp/godot-lock/lock` in a
  `flock` inside `flock` (qa_shot.sh takes the lock itself; wrapping it in another one deadlocks it
  before any Godot starts). It runs nothing and was not this lane's to end; this round used a
  lane-local `GODOT_LOCK` after checking no Godot or Xvfb was alive. A human should end PIDs
  1203107 / 1203108 / 1203110 / 1203113 on 192.168.5.78.

direct route (World3D -> World3D, which isolates `World3D.gd`'s `static var` caches) and the

at tick 200 and mid-load (`drain`). Each entry prints its renderer memory, object and orphan
counts, the static caches, the viewport's `debug_draw`, and one texel probe per surface material
of the centre cell's terrain; the frame is measured as the lower-40% mean of the same `--shots`
camera on both passes. The full record is `docs/RE_COMPLETION.md`'s round 558; the numbers:

  errors, then `data.tree` null, no `previously freed`): it builds one more batch of two cells into

  `_drain_initial_load` -- the one at the bottom of its loop -- with `SCRIPT ERROR: Invalid get
  index 'process_frame' (on base: 'null instance')`. That await is what `map-reconnect-fix`
  guards (the five-hundred-and-sixtieth round).
- On 42 of the 48 texture passes the baked vertex colour is exactly 1.000, so the texture is the
  ground's only colour source there: a sampler resolving to GLES3's default white draws exactly the
  tester's picture, a missing texture draws the 0.5-grey fallback. The tester's own
  `user://logs/opensro.log` -- the second `character/item/NPC tables loaded` block's `ground
  textures for 97\168.m -- N ids, N resolved` line, any `pk2: could not open`, any `SCRIPT ERROR`
  between the blocks, and whether buildings and water were white too -- tells the two apart.
- Found on the way: `QaSignIn.run` compared the wanted name against `Summary` objects, so every
  sign-in after a server's first stopped at `name already taken` (fixed); a `--shots` frame armed
  at tick 0 was named during the sign-in, before any world existed (the shots now wait for the
  entry drain).

## Five-hundred-and-thirty-third round: a monster the server moves walks, faces its path and is not teleported back by the next list

No server moves monsters yet. This round built the client half so that one can: OpenSRO's own
`OpMonsterMoved 0x007C` and `OpMonsterMotionList 0x007F` are decoded (`CombatNet`) and drawn
(`MonsterMotion`, `World3D._on_monster_moved` / `_on_monster_motion_list` /
`_step_monster_bodies`). The table, fixtures and stand-ins are in `docs/protocol/monster_ai.md`,
"OpenSRO's own monster protocol (placeholders)". Nothing changes in normal play.

**The mover is the engine's, re-read on the box (2026-09-24).** `CGObjMoverByDest::FUN_0048bff0`
(SR_GameServer.exe) returns the owner's unit direction times min(|speed(+0x174) x dt|, cap). The cap
is the .rdata float at `0xb45ea8`, bytes `00 00 20 43` = 160.0f, read out of the PE. Its caller
`vslot_003` (`0x48c4e0`) takes dest - position from `FUN_00430ad0` (`call` at `0x48c5a9`). It
compares the two lengths (`fcompp` at `0x48c622`, `test ah,0x41 ; jne`), and when the step is longer
it copies dest - position over it (`0x48c62b..0x48c63c`). So a body lands exactly on its
destination and never overshoots. The mover also zeroes a component under 0.01f (`0xb45df8`, bytes
`0a d7 23 3c`); that is not modelled.

**The list no longer teleports a walking body.** `_spawn_or_update_monster` set
`existing.position = pos` on every refresh. That line moved into `MonsterMotion.reconcile`, still
returning the list's position, and the new NEGATIVE (`reconcile(Vector2(100,0), Vector2(97,0),
true)` must return (100,0)) ran red: `FAIL ... (got (97, 0))`. Now a walking body keeps where it is
drawn unless it has drifted more than 32 units (`RESYNC_DISTANCE`, OpenSRO's own) from the list.

**Which way the bodies face: measured, not assumed.** `client/tools/probe_monster_front.gd`
assembles each roster species as World3D does and reads, in skeleton space, the mean toe-minus-foot
vector and the head-minus-pelvis offset, at the bind pose and at the walk clip's first frame. The
control is the player's body, whose front World3D already turns by PI.

- **The first run did not count.** The rule then was that every reading had to name the same axis.
  The control failed it: an upright body's head sits over its pelvis (bind (-0.00, 0.15)), and its
  walk-pose foot reading is short ((0.08, -0.37)). Neither names an axis, and under that rule
  they vetoed the clear bind-pose foot reading (0.00, -1.23). Mangyang, Water Ghost and Earth
  Ghost failed the same way.
- **The rule was changed** so that a reading naming no axis abstains. That is what a head-over-hips
  reading means for a biped. Conflicting axes still unsettle a model. The control then reads -Z,
  and the probe counts.
- **All seven roster models read -Z**, and no reading named a conflicting axis. The per-model
  numbers are in the monster_ai.md table. The strongest are Stone Ghost's head (0.00, -10.00) and
  Weasel's head (0.00, -8.15). The weakest settled model is Earth Ghost, whose only readings are
  its bind feet (0.00, -1.28) and its walk-pose head (0.21, -1.97).

So `MonsterMotion.FRONT_BY_MODEL` lists the seven as -Z, and `facing_yaw` turns a body by
`atan2(dir.x, dir.z) - PI`. That is the player's convention with the PI moved from the skeleton to
the yaw. `NavGraph.godot_yaw` (map objects' negated yaw) is not involved: a leg's direction is a
world-space vector, not an engine yaw.

**Found on the way: four roster species have no model.** `MOB_CH_BIGEYEGHOST_CLON`,
`MOB_CH_GYO_CLON`, `MOB_CH_WATERGHOST_CLON` and `MOB_CH_TOMBSTONE_CLON` carry `xxx` in cols 52-56
of the box's `characterdata_5000.txt`. Their display names ("Small-eyed Ghost", "Old Weasel",
"Water Ghost slave", "Tomb Stone Ghost") resolve to no row that has a model. They are drawn as the
capsule, which has no front, and the probe says so. docs/TODO.md has the item.

**Live, on the render box.** `OPENSRO_QA_MOB_MOVE=40,0,8,0 OPENSRO_QA_MOB_LOG=1 qa_shot.sh
--server --frames 600 --size 640x360`, hardware GL, with the box's default `SERVER_BIN` (a
2026-09-19 build; this check only needs its monster list):

	QA MOB MOVE: monster 18 at 231 from the player, leg (40.0,0.0) at 8.0/s mode 0
	World3D: monster 18 walk from (70.0,-220.0) to (110.0,-220.0) at 8.0/s yaw -1.57
	World3D: monster 18 at (74.0,-220.0) 36.0 to go
	...                                       (every 30 frames: 32, 28, 24, 20)
	QA MOB MOVE: asking for the monster list at half the leg
	World3D: server reports 23 monster(s)     (Yeoha at 70, 0, -220 -- 20 behind the drawn body)
	World3D: monster 18 at (94.0,-220.0) 16.0 to go

**The review's blocking point: the approach walk against a moving target.** Round 519 released an
