(id 3675) has `Param2 = 420744970 = 0x19140F0A` with `Desc128_2 = "1,2,3,4"`, `Param3 =
168430090 = 0x0A0A0A0A` with `"5,6,7,8"`, `Param4 = 168101125 = 0x0A050505` with
`"9,10,11,12"` -- the descriptors list the plus levels each dword packs, high byte first,
exactly as `alchemy.BaseRate`'s `tier = n/4 + 1, within = n % 4` reads them: **+1 25 %, +2 20 %,
+3 15 %, +4 10 %, +5..+9 10 %, +10 and beyond 5 %** for the A-grade elixirs. Shield, armour and
accessory elixirs carry the same dwords; their `Param1` differs by target type (by shape the
TypeID3 set, not read at a use-site -- said so).

**Shipped:** `refdata.Item.ReinforceRate1..3` as export columns 61-63 (a strict suffix -- the
public server's 61-column file still loads and reads zeros, which is a 0 % base rate rather
than an invented one), the SQL columns and round trip, `Item.ReinforceRates()` in the shape
`alchemy.Inputs.Tiers` takes, and `TestBaseRateFromTheRetailElixirRow` pinning the fourteen
percentages. No handler runs `alchemy.Rate` yet, so no player-visible value changed and there
is no release; the public server's items export is refreshed when alchemy is wired.

## Two-hundred-and-sixty-first round: HOMING -- the way home, and the window in which a returning monster ignores you

The RE tick for 2026-09-19 18:02 read the last unread state body of the monster machine.

`CAIState_HOMING::OnEnter` (`0x55a540`) arms a timer, takes the 50 s dwell, starts `MoveHome`,
and stores **`round(detectionRadius / runSpeed x 1000)` ms** in the state: for that long
(`ReaggroWindowPassed`, HOMING's 49th vtable slot) the update does NOT run the acquire scan, so
a monster walking home ignores players for the time it would take to run its own detection
radius, then notices them again and can go straight back to BATTLE. `MoveHome` (`0x545c50`)
aims at the nest's position (or the spawn record) displaced along the home-to-monster line by
`rand % (1 + ftol(R/3)) - R/9` -- between -R/9 and +2R/9 with `R` the nest or roam radius
(`-3.0` at `0xb45e08` and `3.0` at `0xb45ab8`, both doubles). The step (`AITactics_HomingStep`,
behaviour `+0x118`) runs on a context timer: **arrived within 5.0 units** (`fcomp DWORD
0xb45b28`) -> IDLE; otherwise, while still outside the roam radius, the direction is blended
with the current heading scaled **0.50..1.50** (`(rand % 101 + 50) x 0.01`, `fmul QWORD
0xb46068`), a blocked probe, and a move along it; a destination that would be farther from the
spawn than the monster already stands ends the state too.

Recorded: `monster_ai.md` "HOMING: the way home"; `ai.HomingArrivalRadius`,
`ai.HomingScatterRange`, `ai.HomingReaggroDelayMs`, the wobble bounds, with a test; six names
including the context's timer table (`AITactics_ArmTimer`/`TimerDue` -- shape read, the
meaning of each index not). With this every state the loop runs is read; the build is next.
No shipped value changed; no release.

## Two-hundred-and-sixtieth round: the skill choice -- triggers first, then a weighted draw, and three columns settled

The RE tick for 2026-09-19 17:49 read `AI::CAISkill_Basic::PickSkill` (`0x561b00`), the
selector BATTLE's attack step asks, and with it the three `_RefAISkill` columns that had no
reader since round 241.

**Two lists on the selector.** `RegisterSkill` (slot 3, `0x5614d0`) files each of the owner's
skills by whether `FindAISkillRow` (`0x6ab1d0`) knows it: a skill WITH a `_RefAISkill` row
becomes a 24-byte **trigger entry** `{skill, row, enabled, lastFired, phased}`; one without
joins the plain **attack list** (three branches on `AI_SkillType`, column 67, that all end in
the same push -- the difference unread).

**The pick.** `CheckTriggers` (slot 12) first: the first enabled entry whose condition holds is
armed at once. The conditions are the columns: **column 3 (`+0x20`) is the trigger type** --
0 = `Trigger_HPBelow`: the owner's `CurHP*100/MaxHP` (slots 66/68, floats) at or below
**column 4**, firing ONCE (the entry is disabled); 1 = `Trigger_Periodic`: every **column-4
milliseconds**, the first evaluation arming the timer (or firing at once when **column 5 bit
0** is set), phase-aligned once after that. Otherwise the attack list is drawn from at random
in proportion to `weight = AI_AttackChance (column 66) + max(0, ftol(Range + ownerBC +
targetBC - distance))` -- a skill whose reach covers the target by more units is likelier --
and the pick goes to `ArmNextAttack` (round 259's jittered interval). A monster with one
attack skill always swings it, which is the whole Jangan roster.

Recorded: `monster_ai.md` "The skill choice" and the `_RefAISkill` table's columns 3-5;
`ai.SkillWeight`, `ai.TriggerHPBelowHolds`, `ai.TriggerHPBelow/Periodic` with a test; ten
names (`PickSkill`, `CheckTriggers`, `TriggerHolds`, `Trigger_HPBelow`, `Trigger_Periodic`,
`OwnerHPPercent`, `RegisterSkill`, `GetArmedSkill`, `FindAISkillRow`, `NoTriggers`). No shipped
value changed; no release.

## Two-hundred-and-fifty-ninth round: the threat table -- two seats, three rules, and a jittered swing

The RE tick for 2026-09-19 17:44 read the attacker accounting behind behaviour `+0xec`, the last
rule the monster BATTLE loop needs before it can be built: whom a monster fights when several
things hit it.

**Two seats, not a list.** The context keeps a TARGET seat (`+0xbc..+0xcc`) and one CHALLENGER
seat (`+0xd0..+0xe0`), each `{id, damage, hate, hits, lastHitTick}`, plus the total damage taken
(`+0xb0`). `AITactics_CreditAttacker` (`0x5473c0`) books a blow `{attacker, damage, hate,
hatePercent}` into whichever seat is empty or already the attacker's -- code 0 the target, 1
the challenger, **2 nobody: a third attacker is not tracked** -- as `hate = clamp(hate +
hate*pct/100 + delta, 0, INT_MAX)`, and returns "drop" when the target's hate ends below 1.
An immobile monster credits only attackers within its detection distance.

**Three retarget rules**, the tactics row's `+0x20` (column 9), applied in BATTLE by
`Handler_0fc`: **0** keep the first attacker; **1** face the latest (the seat keeps its
history: only the id and tick change -- the engine's, kept); **2** by hate through
`AITactics_ResolveTarget` (`0x545680`; round 238 had it as an owner lookup): the challenger
overtakes when its hate exceeds the target's **or** the target has not hit for **two attack
intervals**; an invalid target is replaced by the challenger outright; an untracked third
attacker takes the seat **only when it stands farther than the target** (`fcomp` at
`0x545720`, keep on `d_candidate <= d_target` -- the flags checked), the old target moving
down to the challenger seat.

**The swing has jitter.** `AI::CAISkill_Basic::ArmNextAttack` (`0x5619e0`) arms the next
attack at `ReuseDelay + rand % (J + 1)`, `J = clamp(previous interval / 5, 500, 2000)` ms: a
Mangyang swings every 3000..3600 ms, and round 254's "cadence = ReuseDelay" is the window's
floor. The idle window above is twice this interval.

Recorded: `monster_ai.md` "The threat table" and column 9 relabelled; `ai.ThreatTable`
(`Credit`, `Face`, `Resolve`, `FaceAfterHit`), `ai.AttackIntervalRange`/`AttackJitterMs`, with
four tests; six names. No shipped value changed (OpenSRO's monsters still only counter-strike);
no release.

## Two-hundred-and-fifty-eighth round: the aggro link -- what the ten nearest monsters are for

The RE tick for 2026-09-19 17:36 closed round 257's open thread. The list of monsters a
monster gathers when it enters BATTLE is the **aggro link**, and that is the engine's own word
for it: the config key is `MONSTER_AGGRO_LINK_DECREASE_RATIO`.

**The route.** Being hit reaches a monster as command 2 through its command source -- and
`AI::CTactics` IS the monster's command source (its vtable shares `CCmdSrcNet::PostCommand`
at slot 1; slot 7, `DispatchCommandToState`, hands a command to the current state's slot 5,
`CAIState::DispatchCommand`, `0x558bb0`, whose switch maps command codes to state slots: 2 ->
slot 6, 0xe -> slot 29, and thirteen more). Slot 6 is **`CAIState::OnAttacked`** (`0x558ea0`)
for IDLE, WANDER, FLEE and HOMING:

	raw = record.damage
	behaviour +0xf0 (record)                         ; the link
	record.damage = ftol(raw * 1.15)                 ; 0xb46300, double, used nowhere else
	if attacker accounting (+0xec) == 0: SetTarget(1); ChangeState(BATTLE)   ; edi = 3, EBX zeroed

**The link**, `AITactics_ExtRoutine::LinkAggroToNearbyMonsters` (`0x547570`, behaviour `+0xf0`;
its CLAMP assert cites `AITactics_ExtRoutine.cpp` line 0x662): the attacker must be a player in
a party whose `+0x10` word has bit 0; `AITactics_CollectNearbyMonsters(attacker)` gathers the
ten nearest monsters inside `LevelScaledRadius(BCRadius + detection, attacker)` (round 257's
list); `n` = party members within **1000.0** units of the attacker (`0xb45c68`, double), the
attacker counting; `CLAMP(n, 0, gathered)`; then the first `n` gathered monsters each receive
`cmdsrc->slot7(0xe, record, 0)` and the record's damage is multiplied by
`g_MonsterAggroLinkDecreaseRatio` (`0xc8252c`) and `ftol`'d between them. Command 0xe is slot
29, **`CAIState::OnAggroLinked`** (`0x559bb0`): attacker accounting, `SetTarget(1)`,
`ChangeState(BATTLE)` -- the same entry a direct hit makes, minus the link, so it never
cascades. So: **a party's blow on one monster pulls in as many of its neighbours as the party
has members on the spot, credited 100 %, 50 %, 25 % ... of the blow, while the victim itself
books the attacker at 115 %.** A solo player links nothing.

**The knob, and the block it lives in.** `CMainProcess::LoadServerConfig` (`0x427050`) reads
`MONSTER_AGGRO_LINK_DECREASE_RATIO` as a percentage over 100 with **default 0.5** (`0xb45b68`,
`fld DWORD`) and no floor -- alongside the gain knobs `internal/rates` already mirrors. Two
corrections to that package's comment fell out of reading the whole block: `PCSpeedRatio`
(`0xc8253c`, cap 3.0) exists and scales the player's speed params in `GObjPC_InitStats`; and
**`HwanGainFactor` is a knob with no consumer** -- its pre-config value is 100.0 (`0xb45e10`),
the clamp turns that into 10.0, and no instruction outside the loader reads `0xc82528` (the
`ds:0xc82528` census over the whole image has only the loader's stores). The berserk earn was
right not to multiply by it. The full key vocabulary (25 keys through `ServerConfig_Get`,
`0x426b00`) is in the names table.

Recorded: `monster_ai.md` "The aggro link" (round 257's "unread" note now points at it),
`ai.AggroLinkMaxHelpers/MemberRange/DecreaseRatio/VictimDamageFactor`, `ai.AggroLinkCount`,
`ai.AggroLinkDamage` with a test, the `rates` package comment corrected, nine names. No
shipped value changed -- OpenSRO has no monster BATTLE loop yet, and this is one of the rules
it will run on. No release.

## Two-hundred-and-fifty-seventh round: how a monster notices you -- the detection radius, and where the level term really is

The RE tick for 2026-09-19 17:20 turned to the monster's side of round 256: OpenSRO's monsters
strike only when struck because nothing ever picks a target. The acquisition rule is now read,
and one row of the tactics table changes meaning.

**The radius is `BCRadius + _RefTactics.+0x14`.** `AI::CTactics::BindSkillsAndRanges` (`0x53f780`)
ends with three instructions Ghidra did not show -- it rendered the store as `= 0` and cut the
function at a misread noreturn:

	53fa2b  call [vtbl+0x560]          ; GetBCRadius (slot 344, characterdata col 50)
	53fa46  fst  DWORD [ctx+0x158]     ; = BCRadius
	53fa4c  fiadd DWORD [row+0x14]     ; + the tactics row's column 6
	53fa4f  fstp DWORD [ctx+0x15c]     ; = the detection radius

Round 238 had column 6 as "a distance" that installs the acquire behaviour; it is the DETECTION
DISTANCE, and the radius the scan uses is the body's radius plus it.

**The scan takes the nearest player, and nothing about levels.** `AITactics_AcquireTarget`
(`0x5478f0`, behaviour `+0xf8`, WANDER/HOMING/WATCHOUT/EMOTION) rounds `ctx+0x15c`, picks a
kind mask and a selector from the row's flag word (players and "nearest" by default), and
`AITactics_ScanForTargets` (`0x5405b0`) walks the regions within the radius handing every object
to the selector at `ctx+0x128 + selector*4` -- a second eight-entry table the constructor
`AI::CTactics::CTactics` (`0x53ea60`) fills. Selector 2 (`0x5464e0`) keeps a candidate that
passes the kind mask (`GObj_MatchesKindMask`, `0x540b90`), stands within the radius by the
region-aware distance and is nearer than the best so far. A player's summoned objects get a
detour (`GObjPC::FUN_004fc160(pc+0x1ce8)`; a pet may be picked instead -- shape only). Then
`SetTarget` and 2, which the caller turns into BATTLE. **No level comparison anywhere in it.**

**The level term is at BATTLE entry, and it is not about the player being noticed.**
`CAIState_BATTLE::OnEnter` -> `AITactics_CollectNearbyMonsters` (`0x540580`): the same base
radius scaled by `AITactics_LevelScaledRadius` (`0x541e00`) against the TARGET's level --
**x1.4** when the monster is 4+ levels above it, **x1.2** at 1..3 above, 1.0 from 3 below to
equal, **x0.8** at 4..6 below, **x0.6** at 7+ below (doubles at `0xb45c08/c00/bf0/bf8`; `fmul
QWORD`, checked) -- bounds `AITactics_GatherObjectsWithin` (`0x540860`, kind mask 2), which
moves the **ten nearest monsters** (never a `MOB_AUTOMOB`) into the vector at `ctx+0x80`. What
that list drives is unread this round: its readers share `+0x84` with a position record and
the census was polluted; the shape is recorded, not interpreted.

**Where the numbers would come from, checked rather than assumed.** The per-species column-6
distances live in `_RefTactics`, a shard-database table. The server package on the box has no
shard backup: its `SR_GameRefData` folder is the client-side text tables plus shop, teleport
and quest files (no tactics, nest, hive or AI-skill file), `smc.bak` is the manager's own
database, and the three `SR_GameServer_*.dmp` files are 2 MB minidumps with eight streams
(threads, modules, a small memory list, exception, system info) and no heap -- `MOB_CH_` occurs
in none of them. So the RULE is grounded and the per-species distance will be disclosed when
OpenSRO's monsters learn to notice a player.

Recorded: a new section in `docs/protocol/monster_ai.md`, column 6 relabelled, `ai.DetectionRadius`
and `ai.LevelScaledRadius` with a test (`internal/ai`), the build item in `docs/TODO.md`
("Monsters do not move, chase or notice anyone" -- every rule it needs is now listed with its
round), ten names. No shipped value changed; no release.

## Two-hundred-and-fifty-sixth round: one click fights to the death -- the keep-up, read and built

The RE tick for 2026-09-19 16:34 took round 255's TODO: the real server repeats the plain
attack on its own, OpenSRO wanted a click per swing. Reading the "keep-up" phase properly
turned over more than the repeat.

**The machine has a name.** The action queue behind attacks, skills, pick-ups and traces is
`CGCharAutoCommandActor` -- the binary's own RTTI class (vtable `0xaecd0c`, ctor `0x4ac9f0`).
Its constructor stores a handler table by action kind: `[1] 0x4ad8e0` attack, `[2] 0x4ae0c0`
pick up, `[3] 0x4ae3d0` trace, `[4] 0x4ae590` use skill, `[5] 0x4ae520`. So **`0x4ad8e0`, which
round 247 named `GObjPC::ActionTick_UseSkill`, is the plain-ATTACK tick**; the skill tick is its
sibling `0x4ae590`, which computes the same approach band from the skill's own `Range` (plus a
`+0x250` param when that is 0). The rule round 247 read stands for both; the name is corrected
(`recovered_names.tsv`, forced). `CGObjChar::Update` ticks the actor at most every 30 ms.

**The keep-up, phase by phase** (`docs/protocol/auto_command.md` has the whole thing):

	phase 1  PrepareAction: ctx.skill = the weapon's DEFAULT ATTACK (re-resolved every pass),
	         target check, gate 0x24; out of reach -> MoveTowardObject(stop), in reach -> gate 0x81
	phase 2  serialise the ctx into a 0x7070 command and POST IT TO THE CHARACTER'S OWN COMMAND
	         SOURCE (CCmdSrcNet::PostCommand, the queue the client's packets arrive through);
	         accepted -> phase 3, refused (queue full) -> the action ends
	phase 3  [HANDLE_ATTACK-KeepUp]: the ctx skill must still resolve, else log and end;
	         Skill_CheckUseConditions mask 1 = THE COOLDOWN TEST ALONE -> wait while it refuses;
	         a second queued action (depth 2) -> end; target gone or dead (slot 6) -> end;
	         recompute the band -> phase 1

So the cadence is the base attack's `ReuseDelay` by construction (round 255's guess at the
mechanism was right), the server walks back into reach on every repeat, and what ends it is the
target's death, the player's next action, or the client's cancel.

**The skill side.** The skill tick's phase 3 waits `CastingTime + ActionDuration` after the
post (`CastingTime` already carries `PreparingTime`: `SkillGlobal` adds it at load), re-enters
phase 2 for a chain link (`ChainCode`), and otherwise -- when the row's **`AutoAttackType`
(`CRefSkill+0x90`, skilldata col 19) is 1**, the target is a live monster and nothing else is
queued -- **pushes a brand-new kind-1 ATTACK action carrying the same context** (`0x4ac910`,
phase 5, `Push` at `0x4ad630`). That is why a sword skill leaves the character swinging.

**The default attack is the engine's table, not a name convention.**
`SkillGlobal::PostLoadSkillTable` (`0x5893e0`, `SkillGlobal.cpp`) walks the loaded rows once
and fills `g_DefaultAttackSkillByTID4` (`0xc82638`, 32 dwords) by comparing each `Basic_Code`
with literals: `[1] SKILL_PUNCH_01`, `[2][3] SKILL_CH_SWORD_BASE_01`, `[4][5]
SKILL_CH_SPEAR_BASE_01`, `[6] SKILL_CH_BOW_BASE_01`, `[7] SKILL_EU_SWORD_BASE_01`, `[8]
..TSWORD..`, `[9] ..AXE..`, `[10] ..WAND_WARLOCK..`, `[11] ..STAFF..`, `[12] ..CROSSBOW..`,
`[13] ..DAGGER..`, `[14] ..HARP..`, `[15] ..WAND_CLERIC..`, plus the two `FORTRESSWEAPON` rows
by race. Resolved against the retail skilldata on the box the ids are 1, 2, 40, 70, 8419, 8420,
8421, 10625, 9944, 9354, 9355, 11162, 11526 -- **row for row what round 255's
`combat.BaseAttackSkillFor` derived from the `ReqCast_Weapon1` bytes**. It is grounded now; no
value changed. `SkillBook::DefaultAttackSkillIDForWeaponTID` (`0x59e650`) reads it: no weapon
is TID4 1 (bare hand), the row must also be learned.

**Free with it: the whole CRefSkill fixed-column layout.** `0x6ab5a0` copies a record field by
field at each field's own width -- Service u8 .. ID +4, GroupID +8, three strings, Original
+0x60, Level +0x64, Activity +0x65, ChainCode +0x68 .. ReuseDelay +0x7c .. Interruptable +0x88,
Overlap +0x8c (its high byte +0x8f is the COOLDOWN GROUP `SkillCooldowns::IsReady` keys a shared
map on), AutoAttackType +0x90, InTown +0x91, Range +0x92, the twelve Target bytes +0x94..+0x9f,
the requirements +0xa0..+0xc8, the four costs +0xca..+0xd0, **Consume_WHAN +0xd2**, UI bytes,
five UI strings, AI +0x164/+0x166, Param1..50 at +0x168 -- ending exactly where
`RefSkill_ParseParams`' memset begins (+0x230). Recorded in `skill_fields.md`; it agrees with
every offset the gate, the ticks and `SkillGlobal` already used.

**Built (v0.1.406).** `server/internal/session/keepup.go`: one accepted click arms a per-character
run that swings again every base-attack `ReuseDelay` (falling back into step if a manual click
landed in between), a cast with `AutoAttackType` 1 arms it after `CastingTime + ActionDuration`,
and a cast, a move, a zone change, death, disconnect, or the target's death ends it. Two
departures are written where they live: the server cannot walk the player, so a repeat that
finds the target out of reach ENDS the run (the reach test is the engine's, `keepUpInReach`);
and the retail client's explicit cancel on a move click is stood in for by `OpMove`, which
OpenSRO's client only sends for a real move. `Session.Send` gained a mutex: it was two writes
per frame with broadcasts already arriving from other goroutines, and the repeats made that
routine. Tests: the tracker's replace/cancel semantics, the reach band (sword vs Mangyang lands
from 18, not 19), the hand-off rule, and a TCP round trip where a single `OpAttack` produces
three results and a kill, then a move stops the next run. `go test -p 1 ./...` green. Names: 21
(`CGCharAutoCommandActor::{Tick_Attack,Tick_UseSkill,Update,Push,PrepareAction,FinishFront,
RunInstantSkill}`, `SkillBook::{ResolveUsableSkillRef,FindLearned,DefaultAttackSkillID,
DefaultAttackSkillIDForWeaponTID}`, `SkillGlobal::PostLoadSkillTable`,
`CRefSkill::CopyFixedColumns`, `CCmdSrcNet::{PostCommand,NewCommand,ReleaseCommand}`,
`SkillCooldowns::IsReady`, `GObjPC::{HandleCharacterActionRequest_7074,SendActionResult_B074}`,
`Action_OverrideBandForRangedVsFlying`).

## Two-hundred-and-fifty-fifth round: a plain swing is a skill with a re-use delay -- the player's attack cadence

The RE tick for 2026-09-19 16:19. The server accepted an `OpAttack` per click with no cadence
at all: a fast clicker swung several times a second. In the real game the plain attack IS a
skill -- each weapon type's `_BASE_01` row, named by its `ReqCast_Weapon1` byte (the itemdata
TypeID4) -- and it runs through the same action machine as any cast (round 247), so its
`ReuseDelay` (= its `ActionDuration`) is the swing rate. Read from the retail table:
`SKILL_CH_SWORD_BASE_01` (types 2/3) **1200 ms**, spear/glaive 1166, bow **840**, EU sword 1333,
two-hander 2000, axe 1500, crossbow 1333, dagger 1000, the staff/wand bolts 1666, harp 2000,
`SKILL_PUNCH_01` (bare hand, type 1) **1500**. `AutoAttackType` is 1 for every melee and bow
base and 0 for the three magic bolts.

**Wired (v0.1.405):** `combat.BaseAttackSkillFor(typeID4)` keeps only the row ids (structural);
the delay is read from the imported skill table at run time; `session.swingReady` drops a swing
inside the equipped weapon's delay (a broken weapon swings bare-handed on the punch's), exactly
as the engine ignores a use while the action runs, and records the swing under the base skill's
id in the existing cooldown store. Tests on the map and the gate; full suite green (57). Not
built, and now in `docs/TODO.md`: the **keep-up** -- the real server repeats the swing on its own
(`ActionTick_UseSkill` phase 3, `[HANDLE_ATTACK-KeepUp]`); OpenSRO still wants a click per blow.

## Two-hundred-and-fifty-fourth round: a monster's attack cadence is its skill's re-use delay

The RE tick for 2026-09-19 16:04. BATTLE's attack step is `AITactics_Handler_0e8` (`0x5472a0`,
behaviour `+0xe8`): it waits on the tactics timer, takes the AI-skill selector's pick (ctx
`+0x9c`, slots 4/7) and runs Execute (slot 8) -- the skill goes through the same action machine
a player's cast does (round 247's `ActionTick_UseSkill`), so **a monster cannot strike more
often than its attack skill's ReuseDelay**, and on a landed blow it stamps ctx `+0xcc`, the
5000 ms window the give-up check reads. The species' attack skills (characterdata col 83) carry
the numbers in skilldata columns 13/14/21: Mangyang `MSKILL_CH_MANGNYANG_ATTACK01` action 2400
/ reuse **3000** / range 10; Gyo 1700/**2000**/7; Yeoha cast 1070 + action 830 / **2500** / 7;
Tomb Stone ghost **2500** at range **100** (a ranged monster); Earth Ghost 1533/**2000**/7.

**Wired (v0.1.404):** `combat.Species/Monster.AttackReuseMs` and `AttackRange` on the roster
from the table, and `combat.Hub.CounterattackReady` -- a monster's blows are at least its
re-use delay apart; the session skips the counter-blow inside the window. OpenSRO's monster
still strikes only when struck (there is no BATTLE loop of its own yet), so this is a ceiling
on its cadence, not the cadence -- said in the code. Before this a player swinging once a
second took a Mangyang blow once a second; the real Mangyang swings every three. Test on the
gate; full suite green (57 packages). One name.

## Two-hundred-and-fifty-third round: every roster species stands where the game puts it

Follow-up to the playtest report "why are there Yeohas in town" (round 250). Only Mangyang had
its real placements (four embedded rows); the other ten species stood at own-design anchors a
few hundred units from Jangan's square -- Yeoha, a level-10 monster, among them. The data was
always there: `npcpos.txt`, 12,367 placements keyed by the species' characterdata id with a
packed region and a local position, converted by the transform this project measured for it.

Wired (v0.1.403): `export-refdata -mode npcpos` streams the table to a CSV (rows are not
id-unique, so nothing is de-duplicated -- a species with 55 placements gets 55 rows); the new
`internal/spawn` loads it; `cmd/server -npcpos-csv` gives every roster species with rows ALL of
them, replacing embedded rows and anchors alike (a configured path that fails to load is fatal,
not a silent fall-back). The roster now carries each species' numeric id (`RefObjID`, read from
the retail table: Mangyang 1933 ... Yeoha 1943, Earth Ghost 1963), test-checked distinct. The
public server's compose command passes the flag and its data directory holds the CSV. The
anchors stay only as the fallback when no file is configured or a species has no rows -- and
the roster comment says so. Full suite green (57 packages).

## Two-hundred-and-fifty-second round (world lane): the Alexandria "white ground" report, and the zone label that never moved

Reported from a real playtest: after the debug panel's **Alexandria** button (zone target
`90/48@663,526`), "the ground is all white" while buildings, sky and the character drew
normally, and the minimap still read **Jangan**. Both halves were measured on the render box
with the retail archives there; one reproduced and is fixed, the other did not reproduce and
now logs the numbers that would settle it.

### 1. The zone label / minimap name -- reproduced, cause read, fixed

**Measurement.** The label and the minimap's area name come from
`_update_zone_label_for_region` -> `RegioninfoNames.display_for_region`, which resolves a
region through `Data.pk2`'s `Shader\regioninfo.txt`. That file, extracted and counted, has
**15 zones** -- 장안/Jangan through 중앙아시아/Central Asia, the pre-Egypt world -- and **no row
for any Alexandria region**. `display_for_region` therefore returns `""` for 90/48 and the
function returns early, leaving `_current_zone_name` (and the minimap header fed from it every
tick) at whatever zone the player came from. Reproduced in one `qa_shot` run booting Jangan and
reloading for `90/48@663,526` through `OPENSRO_QA_ZONE`: the frame at the Alexandria spot
(world X -16638, Y -332 -- the reporter's own screenshot reads X -16608, Y -337) still showed
**Jangan** over the minimap.

**The game's own table.** `Media.pk2`'s `server_dep\silkroad\textdata\textzonename.txt` is a
per-REGION zone-name table: 4,176 rows shaped `<service> <regionId> <korean> 0 0 0 0 0
<english> <...>`, keyed by the packed region id this project already uses everywhere
(`(x << 8) | y`: Jangan's 97/168 is 25000; 90/48 is 23088, whose row reads `Alexandria`). The
full `textdata\regioninfo.txt` (3,242 lines, 65 zones, `48 90 ALL` under `#TOWN Alexandria`)
agrees, but the per-region text is the simpler and more complete source and carries the real
localized names rather than this project's transliterations.

**Fix.** `TextZoneNameReader` (new, `client/scripts/regioninfo/`) parses that table with the
UI text tables' own language-column rule (`UiTextTable._pick_language_column`, column 8 with
its documented fallbacks); `World3D._zone_name_for_region` prefers it and falls back to the
15-zone Shader table, and `_update_zone_label_for_region` now also pushes the name straight to
the minimap. Headless test `text_zone_name_reader_test.gd` (synthetic rows, no game data)
covers the packing, the column fallback, service-0 and short rows. **Verified**: the same run
after the change loads `3460 regions` of names and the Alexandria frame's minimap reads
**Alexandria**.

### 2. The white ground -- NOT reproduced; the chain is measured intact

Every step the client takes to texture 90/48 was checked against the archives on the box:

| step | measured |
|---|---|
| region file class | `90\48.m` is 92,712 bytes -- the 7-byte-vertex class, same as `97\168.m` (so the per-vertex `TextureInfo` decode is the one Jangan uses) |
| texture ids in the row data | 90/48 uses **13 distinct ids** (263 `alex_stone00.ddj` on 7,984 of 10,404 vertices, then 380, 0, 262, 362 ...); 89/48 22 ids, 90/47 15, 91/48 14, 90/49 26 |
| `tile2d.ifo` entries | 719 entries, ids 0..718; **every id of every checked region has an entry** (0 missing) |
| files in `Map.pk2`'s `Tile2D\` | 725 files; **every referenced filename is present** (0 missing) |
| the `.ddj` files themselves | `alex_stone00/01`, `alex_grass_04`, `esteu_godgarden_*`: 20-byte DDJ header + DDS, **DXT1, 512x512, 10 mips -- byte-for-byte the same format as `c_marble_jang_02.ddj`**; a 256x256 one decodes the same way |
| brightness of the paving | decoded DXT1 top mip: `alex_stone00` mean sRGB (0.63, 0.58, 0.48), luma mostly in the 0.5-0.75 bins; Jangan's `c_marble_jang_02` (0.40, 0.38, 0.31). Brighter, nowhere near white |
| the client's own load | the new per-region line reads `ground textures for 90\48.m -- 13 ids, 13 resolved, 0 without a tile2d.ifo entry, 0 files missing or undecodable`, and likewise for all nine regions of the grid |
| the frame | the Alexandria spot renders the real paving (`alex_stone00`), not white, in both runs |

So with these archives and this code the ground is textured. What is left is on the reporting
machine: either its own `Map.pk2`/`Data.pk2` differ (an archive whose `Tile2D\` lacks the
`alex_*`/`esteu_*` files, or whose `tile2d.ifo` is shorter -- the untextured fallback draws a
flat material whose albedo is white when the zone's minimap image is also missing), or the
render differs (the Windows build on that GPU). The two are now distinguishable from the
client log written beside the executable: `World3D: ground textures for 90\48.m -- ...` says
how many ids resolved, and ends in `NOTHING resolved, the region draws the flat fallback`
when the archive is the cause. **Ask for that line** before doing anything else about it.

### 3. A log line that never printed

Every environment application raised `ERROR: unsupported format character`: the fog-planes
diagnostic used `%g`, which GDScript's `%` operator does not support, so the line documented
in `World3D.gd`'s QA block was silently lost on every zone. Now `%.5f`; the line prints
(`near 1697, far 2500` at Alexandria, `1897/2500` at Jangan).

### Files

- `client/scripts/regioninfo/text_zone_name_reader.gd` (new) and its `_test.gd` (new)
- `client/scripts/World3D.gd`: `_load_text_zone_names`, `_zone_name_for_region`,
  `_update_zone_label_for_region` (minimap push), the per-region ground-texture diagnostic in
  `_load_real_ground_textures`, the `%g` fix
- transient extracts under `/var/tmp/maplane` on the box were deleted; nothing from the
  archives is committed

The RE tick for 2026-09-19 15:04 read `Combat_ApplyStatusEffects` (`0x590680`) with a

ca cssr`; each asks the target's active-effect map whether the state applies at this level,
keyed by **kind << 24** where kind = the client's icon bit + 1 (freeze 1 ... myopia 11 ...
decay 18); the six elemental blocks roll `chance = (100 - resist%)/100 * value[0] - flat`

burn 30/148, poison 31/149, zombie 32/150 -- which settles the per-tag question

the tick interval from the skill's `puls` value or **2000 ms** by default, and a word from
the table at `0xc63c94` indexed by `value[2]` (unread, by shape a duration). The function
opens on param 169, the Disease applier's param: disease gates the whole roll. Recorded in

## Two-hundred-and-forty-eighth round: the status-effect vocabulary -- one bit numbering on both sides, and param 183 is Myopia's range cut

The RE tick for 2026-09-19 14:53 closed round 247's two unread terms and found a vocabulary
behind one of them. The reach formula's percent, param 183, has one writer: the server's
abnormal-state applier for slot 10 (`0x4a4c60`, `pc+0xe0c + 4*10`), which stores the
effect's value at param 183 while the state is on and removes it on expiry. Which state is
slot 10? The client answers: its icon switch (`sro_client.exe` `0x7fdab0`) maps the
abnormal-state MASK to icon files, bit by bit -- `0x1` freeze, `0x2` frostbite, `0x4`
electricshock, `0x8` burn, `0x10` poisoning, `0x20` zombi, `0x40` sleep, `0x80` root, `0x100`
blunting, `0x200` fear, **`0x400` myopia**, `0x800` bleeding, `0x2000` dark, ..., `0x1000000`
incubation -- and the server's applier table is indexed by the same bits. Six independent
agreements hold the alignment: slot 3 lowers parry / bit 3 is burn; slot 8 lowers speed /
blunting; slot 10 cuts range / myopia (short sight); slot 17 cuts physical defence / decay;
slot 18 cuts magical defence / weakness; slot 13 cuts attack rate / dark. So **param 183 is
the Myopia state's attack-range reduction percent**, and `range * (1 - p/100)` in the action
tick is short sight doing what its name says.

The other two terms, the skill fields `+0x50c`/`+0x4e8`, are the params `CBRA` and `WIRU`
(`skill_fields.md`): the action tick looks each one's first value up in the caster's
active-effect map (`pc+0xa30`, the same `FUN_005a0330` the damage formulae and
`Combat_ApplyStatusEffects` use) and adds the found record's `+4` to the range -- a
conditional range bonus while a named state is active. What the two states are is unread.

Recorded: `docs/protocol/status_effects.md` (the 25-bit table with each applier and the
params thirteen of them write), the 22 appliers renamed with their state
(`AbnormalState_Myopia_Apply10`, ...), param 183 in the registry, a new PARTIAL row in
SYSTEMS.md (headline 12/22/0 of 34), and the comments in `combat/reach.go`. No shipped value
changed: OpenSRO has no status effects, so its myopia percent is 0.

## Two-hundred-and-forty-seventh round: the attack-distance rule -- read on the server, where it lives

The RE tick for 2026-09-19 14:37 took the parked item with the route round 234 left, and
the route was wrong in one respect that mattered: the client sends the action at once, and
the SERVER walks the attacker into reach. Round 232's "the client walks into range before it
sends" is corrected.

**The rule**, in `GObjPC::ActionTick_UseSkill` (`0x4ad8e0`, the action state machine
switched on `action+0x1c`), phase 0:

	base  = caster.BCRadius + target.BCRadius       ; IGObj slot 344 = ref +0xee, characterdata col 50
	range = skill.Range (CRefSkill+0x92)            ; 0 for every basic attack, so:
	      | round(param 33)                         ; = the weapon's Range column, itemdata 94
	range += two skill range modifiers (skill+0x50c/+0x4e8; unread)
	range *= 1 - param183/100                       ; unread percent
	reach = base + range                            ; action+0x18
	stop  = base + f(range)                         ; action+0x14
	f(r)  = r (r <= 4) | r - 2 (4 < r < 10) | 0.7 r (r > 10) | 0 at exactly 10 (the engine's hole)

Phase 1: `Action_IsTargetWithinReach` (`0x4ad4a0`) = `int(distance) <= reach + 2` on the
region-aware separation; when false, `GObjPC::MoveTowardObject(target, round(stop))`
(`0x4b0350`); when true, the conditions are re-checked and the blow executes (phase 2 sends
`0x7070`). Param 33 is the weapon's Range: `Char_PublishCombatStats` publishes the item
ref's u16 at `+0x224` (itemdata column 94 -- sword 6, spear 18, bow 180, dagger 3 across
every weapon row of each type; 0 while broken), and `Char_GetAttackRange` (`0x4ac890`)
rounds it back. The comparison takes the table's tenths-of-a-metre numbers as world units
with no conversion: the use-site round 233 asked for -- **1 world unit = 0.1 m**.

**A layout correction on the way.** Slot 344 returns `ref+0xee`, which the common-record
map had as one past `BCRadius`. Re-reading the parser: `Scale` at `+0xe8` is a DWORD
(4-byte advance), so `BCHeight` is `+0xec` and `BCRadius` `+0xee` -- column 50, as the TODO
predicted. Real values: every playable body 4; Mangyang 6, Gyo 10, Yeoha 11, Tomb Stone 4.
So a sword against Mangyang lands from 16 (+2), and the walk stops at 14.

**Wired (v0.1.400):** `combat.ApproachBand`, `EffectiveRange`, `InReach` with the cited
constants and tests (the three bands, the hole, the slack); `combat.Species.BCRadius` on the
roster from the table; `refdata.Item.Range` as CSV column 60 / SQL `attack_range` (the
public server's items re-imported). **Not yet built:** the behaviour -- OpenSRO's server does
not drive player movement, so the walk has to be the client's, and monsters need their BATTLE
approach; recorded in `docs/TODO.md` with the rule. Six names.

## Two-hundred-and-forty-sixth round: where gear aggregates -- the shield's defence counts

Continuing from round 245's open item. The question was whether a worn shield's own
physical/magic defence (its block's `+0x198/+0x1a8`, computed by the shield branch of
`Char_BuildAggregateStats` with variance groups 4/5) reaches the character's params 5/6, and
the answer is the site that folds equipment into the character:

- `Char_PublishCombatStats` (`0x497830`) takes the equipped **item** as its first argument
  (RE_COMPLETION had this open since 2026-09-15): it requires the item to answer vslot 33
  (equipment), `item+0x14c != 0` and the broken flag `item+0x190 != 1`, then publishes the
  item's block into the PC's keeper **keyed by the item** -- `+0x198` -> param 5, `+0x1a8` ->
  6, `+0x1a0` -> 7, and the rest of the table already recorded. While broken it publishes
  zero defence; `GItemEquip::SetBrokenFlag` (`0x495980`) is what sets `+0x190`.
- `GObjPC::PublishEquipItemParams` (`0x4e3760`) calls it after `CheckEquipRequirements`; it is
  the re-add half of the pair `ChangeItemDurability` uses around the broken flag, whose remove
  half is `RemoveParamKeeperItemEntry`.
- `CGPCInventoryOP::RefreshEquipParamEntryForPC` (`0x4bb3e0`, vtable slot 31) walks equipment
  slots **0..12** and publishes every item that is equipment and not an expired rental.

Slot 7 is the shield, and the shield branch stores `+0x198/+0x1a8`, so **a worn shield's
defence counts exactly as armour's does**. Wired (v0.1.399): the defence walk includes the
shield with its own groups (PD 4, MD 5 -- not the armour's 3/4, and not its own block group
3), a weapon still adds nothing (its branch never stores `+0x198`), broken and Untracked
rows behave as before; a test pins all three. Full suite green. Five names.

## Two-hundred-and-forty-fifth round: the shield's block rate reads the instance

The RE tick for 2026-09-19 14:19, the third piece of the item-instance thread. `defenderBlock`
returned `BlockRatioMin` -- "the low end, so a shield is never overstated", a choice from
before instances carried a variance. The shield branch of `Char_BuildAggregateStats`
(`0x496623..0x4968a4`) settles it: `mov esi,3` at `0x4967b0`, then `BR_L + q*(BR_U-BR_L)`
from the ref row's `+0x1e0/+0x1e4` (itemdata 74/75) into item `+0x1a4` -- the field
`Char_PublishCombatStats` publishes as param 10, `'bri'`, the blocking rate the block roll
reads (round 236's `Formula_...` chain). Wired (v0.1.398): `defenderBlock` interpolates by
`durability.ShieldBlockGroup`, keeps the low end for an Untracked row, rounds for
`RollChance`'s whole percent, and a broken shield still blocks nothing; a test pins the
group, the interpolation and both edge cases. Full suite green.

**Open, and said plainly:** the shield branch also stores the shield's own physical and
magic defence (groups 4/5 -> `+0x198/+0x1a8`), and OpenSRO's `ArmorSlots` do not count the
shield in the defence sum. Whether a worn shield's `+0x198` reaches the character's param 5
is decided at the site that folds an equipped item's block into the character's params,
and that site is unread -- the two callbacks `param_writers.md` records for param 5
(`0x4a4cc0`, `0x4a5160`) are timed effects, not equipment. Until it is read, the shield's
defence stays out.

## Two-hundred-and-forty-fourth round: a worn weapon's damage and reinforce read the instance -- eight hi-end columns exported

The RE tick for 2026-09-19 14:04 finished what round 243 started on the other half of the
item. `combat.WeaponRange` read every weapon stat at its variance FLOOR: the export carried
only the lo end of each (lo, hi) pair (columns 95/97, 100/102, 105/107, 109/111), so a sword
hit for its worst possible roll whatever its instance said.

**The read.** The weapon branch of `Char_BuildAggregateStats` (`0x4960b7..0x496586`) is six
interpolation blocks after durability, and one `mov esi,N` serves a PAIR of stores each:
group 4 (`0x4963f0`) computes physical damage min from `+0x228/+0x22c` and max from
`+0x234/+0x238`, both with the increment at `+0x23c`; group 5 the magical pair
(`+0x240/+0x244`, `+0x24c/+0x250`); group 1 the physical reinforce pair; group 2 the
magical; 3 attack rate; 6 critical. `RefObjItem::ExtractData` lays the block out with a
synthesized zero between the min and max pairs (`+0x230`), which is why column 97 is the
max's LO end and 98 its hi, not a continuation of the min.

**Wired through (v0.1.397):** eight strict-suffix columns 52-59 in the item CSV
(`PhysAttackMinHi` ... `ReinforceMagMaxHi`, itemdata 96/98, 101/103, 106/108, 110/112),
through `refdata.Item`, the SQL schema (`ALTER TABLE ... IF NOT EXISTS`, default 0) and the
exporter; `combat.WeaponRange(item, inst, str, intel, atk)` takes the instance and
interpolates each pair by its group, reading the lo end alone for `NoInstance`, an Untracked
row, or an older export whose hi ends are zero -- the previous behaviour, kept as the
fallback. Tests pin the groups, the pair-per-group rule, and the old-export path; the full
suite is green. The public server's `items.csv` is re-exported and re-imported below.

## Two-hundred-and-forty-third round: a worn piece's defence is its instance's white stat -- and the variance group is not the triple index

The RE tick for 2026-09-19 13:49 went after a shipped value with a weak reason:
`defenderArmor` summed `PhysDefenseMax` over the worn armour, a stand-in from before item
instances carried a variance. They do now (the durability round), and the engine's rule for
what a worn piece contributes was already read in `durability.md`:
`Char_BuildAggregateStats` (`0x495d60`) stores `L + q*(U-L)` (+ `Inc*plus`, zero here) with
`q = ((Variance >> 5k) & 31)/31`. What was NOT right was `k`.

**The correction.** `refobj_binary_format.md` said the variance group is the stat's triple
index in the ref row ("durability's `xor esi,esi` is read on the asm; the rest is the same
block repeated"). Reading every `mov esi,N` in the 3334-byte function says otherwise: the
group is the ORDER of the interpolation blocks per item kind. Armour: 0 durability, 1 PDStr,
2 MDInt, **3 physical defence** (ref `+0x1bc/+0x1c0/+0x1c4` -> item `+0x198`, param 5), **4
magic defence** (`+0x1ec..` -> `+0x1a8`, param 6), 5 ER. A shield inserts block rate at 3
(`+0x1e0..` -> `+0x1a4`, param 10) and shifts the defences to 4 and 5; a weapon's six groups
are its two damage triples, attack rate, critical and two more. Had the wiring used
"triple 1 = group 1", every armour piece would have read its PDStr bits as its defence.

**Wired through (v0.1.396):** `durability.WhiteStat(lo, hi, variance, group)` and the group
constants; `defenderArmor` / `defenderMagicArmor` share one walk that interpolates each worn
piece by its instance (an Untracked row -- no instance to read -- still counts at the top,
as before; a broken one still counts nothing) and rounds the float sum once for the int32
wire field. Tests pin the groups, the interpolation and the Untracked/broken cases;
`go test -p 1 ./...` is green (56 packages). The shop listing keeps `PhysDefenseMax`: an
unsold item has no instance and a listing shows the range's top.

What this changes for a player: a fresh instance's white stat is the minimum of three
uniform draws (mean about 25 %), so defence on the public server drops from the range's top
to roughly a quarter of the way up it -- which is what the real game gives a freshly
dropped or bought piece.

## Two-hundred-and-forty-second round: the reference-table census was short by 39 -- 124 tables, not 85

The RE tick for 2026-09-19 13:34. While tying parsers to tables, the `_RefQuestReward`
reader (`Can not find QuestRewardData : QuestID [%d]`, `REFDATA_MGR+0xb40`) pointed at a
table that `refdata_tables.md` did not list -- and that page, `persistence.ReferenceTables`
and `quest_scripting.md` all called their 85 **proven complete**, on the strength of two
probes that agreed. They agreed because they shared a blind spot: both matched an upper-case
`_REF` pattern. The count that is actually complete is the number of loaders that build a
table name through `FUN_00401fc0(name, len)`: **124** -- the 85, the ten `TAB_REF*` tables
(the AI's four and six job rankings) and **29 mixed-case `_Ref*` tables** the census never
saw: `_RefQuestReward`/`_RefQuestRewardItems`, `_RefEventReward`/`Items`, four
`_RefServerEvent*`, `_RefRentItem`, two `_RefCollectionBook_*`, `_RefUIString_Mt`, three
`_RefGameWorldGroup*`, and the twelve `_RefTrigger*` tables behind `CGameTrigger*`. Every one
has a `CRef*` descriptor in the table at `.rdata 0xadda70` and the same 503-byte loader
shape; none has a client `textdata` file.

**Wired through** (v0.1.395): `persistence.ReferenceTables` carries 124 names in the binary's
own spelling; the 39 join `ServerOnlyOtherTables` (17 -> 56); the doc-drift test compares
names case-insensitively and without the `TAB_`/underscore prefix; the counts in the three
tests moved (85 -> 124, 17 -> 56). `refdata_tables.md`, `persistence.md`,
`quest_scripting.md` ("exactly four" quest tables -> six, the two new ones being rewards,
which strengthens "objectives are code") and SYSTEMS.md carry the correction. The 35 unnamed
loaders are named `DB_Load_RefX`.

The lesson is the one the rules already state, applied to a census: two probes that share a
regex are one probe. What would have caught it earlier is the descriptor table -- 121
classes against 85 names is a 36-row gap that was visible in round 238 and not counted.

## Two-hundred-and-forty-first round: the AI-skill and hive rows -- and a correction to round 238

The RE tick for 2026-09-19 13:19 closed the last two of the Monster AI's four tables and
corrected a reading two rounds old. Full text in `docs/protocol/monster_ai.md`.

**The correction.** Round 238 said the tactics row's trailing string is "the AI-skill code
names, whitespace-tokenised (`FUN_0067ef90`)". The disassembly at `0x6ab085` says
otherwise: after the string is stored at record `+0x94`, the parser calls `FUN_0067ef90`
with `REFDATA_MGR+0x25c` and the record itself -- and that function is a
`std::multimap::equal_range` on the record's first dword, the TacticsID. The skills come
from **`_RefAISkill` rows** (parser `0x6ab4b0`: u32 TacticsID, string `Basic_Code`, u8, u32,
u32) inserted into that multimap keyed on TacticsID (`mov eax,[edi]` at `0x6b55f4`); each
hit's code name is then looked up in `m_RefSkillByCodename` (`+0x894`), whose builder
`RefInstanceGenerator::FUN_006f68f0` names itself in its own assert
(`m_RefSkillByCodename.end() == m_RefSkillByCodename.find(pRefSkill->m_Basic_Code.c_str())`).
So a monster's AI skills are ordinary **skilldata rows**, the `MSKILL_*` ids characterdata
column 83 already pointed at; the tactics string has no reader. A use-site settled it, as
the rules say -- the earlier reading came from the decompiled shape alone.

**`_RefHive`** is the 9-column, 0x30-byte parser `0x6aa960` at `REFDATA_MGR+0x250`, settled
by `CMainProcess::CreateHivesForWorld` (`0x54b8d0`), which walks that container building an
`AIHive` per row whose `+0x1a` is the world id (kind `+0x1c` 1 then 2), and by
`AIHive::Init`/`AdjustHatchRateByPopulation`: `+0x00` HiveID (a nest row's `+0x04` must
equal it -- nest column 2 settled too), `+0x04` mode (1 = population scaling), `+0x08` the
hive-wide count cap, `+0x0c` a float divisor, `+0x10` rate and `+0x14` its cap
(`AIHive.cpp:0x23c`'s `CLAMP`). The hive sets every nest slot's percentage to
`round(sample / (sum of caps / divisor)) * rate`, capped, and the hatch fires after
`interval * (1 - pct/100)`: busier hives hatch sooner. The `sample` is a per-region word read
at each nest's position (`FUN_005347c0`) -- by shape a population count, not read as such.

Fifteen names, including `RefInstanceGenerator::BuildRefSkillByCodename` from the engine's own
assert. No shipped value changed. Open: the tactics `+0x94` string's reader (none found),
`_RefAISkill` columns 3-5, and the region word's writers.

## Two-hundred-and-fortieth round: the row-parser catalogue -- 66 positional parsers, 19 tied to their tables, 34 functions named in one pass

The RE tick for 2026-09-19 13:11 took the systematic lever the last two rounds exposed:
every reference table reaches the game through a positional stream parser, and the parsers
share one shape (a cursor at `+0x1c`, a column counter at `+0x28`). `/var/tmp/parsers3.py`
on the box harvests all of them with their read widths, the inserter that allocates their
record (and its size), and the list loader `CGameServer::LoadReferenceData` calls.

**Which table is which** was settled three ways, never by column count (the client's
textdata files carry more columns than the server reads -- `refshoptab.txt` has 7, the
parser reads 5): (1) a parser's own assert names it -- `can't find %s from _RefShopTabGroup.
check _RefShopTab` names the table being loaded, the one to "check"; (2) a **family
inserter's case number** -- shops, shop tabs, shop groups and package items travel as one
stream whose rows carry a kind byte, and `RefShop_InsertFamilyRow` (0x6b4590) switches
0 -> `_RefShop` (0xd4), 1 -> `_RefMappingShopWithTab`, 2 -> `_RefAccessPermissionOfShop`,
3 -> `_RefTreatItemOfShop`, while `RefPackageItem_InsertFamilyRow` (0x6b41b0) switches
0 -> `_RefPackageItem` (0x188), 1 -> `_RefScrapOfPackageItem` (0x110), 2 ->
`_RefPricePolicyOfItem`, 3/4 -> the sell-package reward/condition rows; (3) structure --
the teleport parser reads `d d S d w w w w w b b w b`, teleportdata.txt's 14 columns minus
its client-only zone-name string, beside its `[tel id: %s]` assert.

Nineteen parsers now carry their table (`RefX_ExtractData`), plus nine inserters and eight
list loaders: 34 names. The catalogue -- all 66 rows, 47 of them still blank -- is in
`docs/protocol/refdata_tables.md`, so the next table anyone needs (the hive, the AI skills,
the drop-class selectors) is a lookup by record size and assert rather than a rediscovery.
No shipped value changed.

## Two-hundred-and-thirty-ninth round: the `_RefNest` row and the hatch scheduler -- how the real game respawns

The RE tick for 2026-09-19 12:58, the follow-on the last round named. The nest table has no
string column, so its parser is not a `RefData_ReadStringField` caller; it was found by the
cursor-advance shape every positional parser shares (`/var/tmp/parsers.py` on the box now
lists all of them). Full write-up in `docs/protocol/monster_ai.md`.

**The row.** `RefNest_ExtractData` (`0x6ab230`): 17 columns into a 0x3c-byte record --
NestID (engine string), u32, TacticsID (the tactics lookup), RegionID u16 (engine string),
position x3, direction u16 (`/65535 * 360 deg` for rarity-3 species, random otherwise),
the roam radius `Attach` already used, u32, champion percent, **delay-min s, delay-max s,
alive cap**, u8, **respawns**, **scheduler-off**. Column names are DB-only, as before.

**The scheduler, exactly** (`AIHive_HatchPass` 0x55ea90, `NestSlot_RollHatchDelay`
0x560380 read from the asm because the decompiler dropped the roll): a nest hatches one
monster per pass when `col17 == 0 && (col16 != 0 || budget > 0) && stamp + base <= now &&
alive < col14`; the delay is **uniform between col12 and col13 seconds**, re-rolled at
every hatch; the stamp is set on a hatch and -- by `AI::CNest::OnHatchedRemoved` -- only
when a FULL nest loses one, so the timer runs from the first loss, not every death; a
failed placement halves the base with a 1000 ms floor. `col16 == 0` turns the cap into a
finite budget. The champion roll: `rand()%101 < col11` when the tactics row's column 41
is non-zero, then `rand()%101 > GiantMonster_SpawnRatio` (the engine's own config key,
`.rdata 0xae0a04`, default 14) for a champion (x2) else a giant (x20), running under
tactics column 41's row.

**What moved for OpenSRO:** nothing numeric -- `respawnDelay = 10 s` is now disclosed
against the mechanism it stands in for (comment in `server/cmd/server/main.go`): the real
window is per-nest data the project does not hold (`npcpos.txt` carries only id, region
and position). Seventeen functions named. Open: the hive row (`refHive+0x08` caps a
hive-wide count, `+0x08 == 1` selects a mode), column 10's use inside the spawn routine,
and `OnHatchedRemoved`'s caller.

## Two-hundred-and-thirty-eighth round: the `_RefTactics` row read off its parser -- 43 columns, and the ones the AI consults settled at their use-sites

The RE tick for 2026-09-19 12:34 took the Monster AI row's own next probe: the tactics
table's layout. Full write-up in `docs/protocol/monster_ai.md` (two new sections); the
shape of the finding here.

**Where the columns are.** Not in the DB loaders. `PTR_s_CRefTactics_00adde58` is one entry
of a 121-record descriptor table (`0xadda70..0xade3bc`: class name, `new` size, factory,
shared fn, table pointer), and the `0x30` every loader stores is that wrapper's `new` size
-- which is why `refdata_tables.md` found it constant. The rows come in as a byte stream
and each table has a positional parser; the tactics one is `RefTactics_ExtractData`
(`0x6aaab0`): **43 columns** (u32/u8 by read width) into a 0xbc-byte record, then the
trailing string tokenised as AI-skill code names and bound by name (`Invalid AIRefSkill is
bound!!`). Its caller chain runs up to `CGameServer::LoadReferenceData` (`0x6bd920`),
which calls one list loader per table in a fixed order -- the lever for naming the other
55 parsers next.

**What the AI reads, and what it means** (three probes over the AI namespace: direct,
nested and aliased access to the row pointer at context `+0x2c`):

| col | offset | settled by |
|---|---|---|
| 7/8 | `+0x18` u8, `+0x1c` u32 | aggression mode 0/1/2 and its percent: the flag they set (ctx `+0x168`) is what gates `AITactics_AcquireTarget` (`0x5478f0`), the only path to `SetTarget` from WANDER/HOMING/WATCHOUT |
| 6 | `+0x14` u32 | a distance; non-zero installs the acquire behaviour at all, feeds the max-skill-range, and bounds attacker credit for an immobile monster (`FUN_005473c0`) |
| 9 | `+0x20` u8 | retarget-on-hit rule 0/1/2 (`AITactics_Handler_0fc`) |
| 36 | `+0x7c` u32 | the give-up distance: `BATTLE::OnUpdate` -> `AITactics_BattleGiveUpCheck` (`fild [+0x7c]; fcompp`, `0x54842a`) -> `0x2a(1)` -> IDLE at `Distance >= +0x7c`; and `AITactics_TargetOutOfReach` -> `0x27` -> IDLE (the "no sender" row of the message table was wrong -- the id travels in a register) |
| 37/38 | `+0x80` u8, `+0x84` u32 | the roam-radius rule (1 -> x1.5, >= 2 -> never home) and the nest-less radius (fallback 200.0 at `0xb45d68`), through `AI::CTactics::Attach` and `AITactics_IsWithinRoamRadius`, whose false sends `0x26` -> HOMING from IDLE::OnEnter and WANDER::OnUpdate |
| 35 | `+0x79` u8 | 0/2 switch the chase tests off; 2 has its own branches |
| 40 | `+0x89` u8 | 1/2 make the reach test fail at once; 3 makes it fail under 40% HP (`GetCurHP/GetMaxHP` buckets 0.2/0.4/0.6/0.8) |
| 42 | `+0x90` u32 | flags: bits 2/7/8 pick the target-kind filter pair and bits 2/7 swap two behaviours and shorten the first action delay |

Fifteen functions named for it (`recovered_names.tsv`), among them `GObj_DistanceBetween`
(`0x53d7a0`, region-aware, 1920 a region) and `AI::CTactics::InstallBehaviourTable`
(`0x53fc00`), the sixteen-pointer table at ctx `+0xe8` the states call instead of reading
the row. One dead branch: the low-HP request behaviour (`+0x10c`) tests the HP bucket for
`< 0` (`jge` at `0x54898d`), so it never fires in this build.

**Not settled:** 27 columns have no AI reader in the three probes; column NAMES are in the
database only (the package on the box has no shard DB). No shipped value changed --
OpenSRO's server does not move monsters yet (`docs/TODO.md`); the roam and give-up rules
above are what that work implements first.

## Two-hundred-and-twenty-seventh round: how long a drop lies on the ground -- DecayTime, read and wired per item

The RE tick's step for 2026-09-19 09:49, from the disclosed census: `grounditem.Lifetime`
was a 3-minute own-design value ("the sweep that deletes stale items was not located").

### Read

- `CGItem::Update` asserts a ground item is in life-state 2; `CGObj::Update` (`0x484d10`)
  accumulates the frame delta for a state-2 object at `obj+0x3c` and, once the float at
  `ref+0x18 -> +0x84` is exceeded, fires slot 218 = `SetLifeState(3, 0xff, 0)` -- removal.
  `CGObj::EnterWorld` puts the object into state 2 with the accumulator at zero (slot 226
  -> `SetLifeState(2, 0xff, 0)`; the base setter *adds* its third argument to the
  accumulator, which `FUN_004181d0` exploits by pre-loading the full value to remove an
  object on the spot).
- `+0x84` is field 14 of `RefObjCommon_ExtractData`: nine inline counter bumps, four string
  reads and one schema skip precede its bump; the value is `fild`ed, unsigned-fixed and
  divided by the 1000.0 at `0xb45c68` before `fstp [esi+0x84]` -- **milliseconds in the
  text, seconds in the record.** Field 14 -> text column 13 (`refobj_binary_format.md`'s
  rule, anchored again by field 41 = column 40 = the regen amount). `fields.py` had
  mis-attributed it because it matches `mov` stores only; noted in the doc.
- The player's own table: 10000 for 6,494 of 15,338 rows (gold, potions, weapons, armour),
  180000 for 8,402, 20000 for 383, 1800000 for 55, 3600000 for 1, 1000 for 2.
- Consequence the data forces: an ordinary drop (10 s) vanishes before its 30 s ownership
  window ends. That is the game's rule.

### Wired (v0.1.393)

`DecayTime` is column 52 of the items export (a strict suffix), `refdata.Item.DecayTimeMs`,
`items.decay_time_ms` in PostgreSQL, and `grounditem.Hub.SetDecayLookup`: each drop's
`ExpiresAt` is fixed from its own row at drop time; `FallbackLifetime` (the old 3 min,
still disclosed) applies only to a row with no value. Tests cover both. The public server's
items were re-exported from the user's Media.pk2 and re-imported (15,338 rows); the render
box's `items.csv` for `qa_shot --server` was refreshed. `deploy/README.md` says to re-run the
export when the exporter grows a column.

## Two-hundred-and-twenty-sixth round: the retail sky is fixed at midday -- ENVIRONMENT_REFERENCE_TIME = 0.5 is the client's own value

The RE tick's step for 2026-09-19 09:34, the second and last budgeted on the day/night link,
and it closed the other way round: there is no cycle to reproduce.

- `SWorld` keeps a day/night phase at `+0x26a3`. Its constructor (`Map::FUN_00a2f370`) sets

- `SWorld::vslot_004`, the per-frame update, advances the phase only under that flag:
  `phase += dt * 0.0005` (`_DAT_00de4f88`; `dt` is the seconds frame delta -- clamped to 3.0
  beside a millisecond twin clamped to 3000), wrapping at 1.0 with a 30-day counter -- a
  **2000 s** day, dormant. Nothing in this build sets the flag, and the setter
  `SWorld::vslot_020` has no time-passing caller.
- The environment update `Map::FUN_00a1baf0` evaluates every graph at the RAW phase through
  `FUN_004e55e0` (16-byte keyframes, time at `+0xc` -- the ColorGraph evaluator); the sun
  and its shadow are drawn for `0.25 <= phase <= 0.875`.

So the retail client renders a fixed midday, exactly what OpenSRO has done since round 136
as a "flagged simplification". `ENVIRONMENT_REFERENCE_TIME = 0.5` is promoted from
disclosed to read; the day/night TODO closes as not-a-gap; the server's `0x34be` clock is
confirmed to feed nothing in the sky. The dormant machinery (rate, shift, sun angle) is
written down in `docs/protocol/game_clock.md` for the day a live cycle is wanted as our own
design.

## Two-hundred-and-twenty-fifth round: the sky does not read the game clock -- a negative result that reshapes the day/night probe

The RE tick's step for 2026-09-19 09:19, one tick on round 224's open link. Read: the
`S_SetWorldTime` handler (`0x54f6b0`) sets a calendar time on the clock and locks it. Found
by enumeration: nothing outside the clock module reads the clock's fields -- not the
hour/minute, not the synced `time_t`, not the seconds value (one alchemy timer), not the
elapsed counter (UI timers). So the environment sampler is not fed by this clock's fields;
either a value is pushed to it by a call, or `SWorld` runs its own day/night accumulator
with a period of its own. The probe moves to `SWorld`'s update slot
(`docs/protocol/game_clock.md`). No value changed.

## Two-hundred-and-twenty-fourth round: the game clock -- server time every ten minutes, real-time advance, and the four other periodic jobs named

The RE tick's step for 2026-09-19 09:04. Round 223's timer table left four jobs unnamed;
naming them found the clock. Spec: `docs/protocol/game_clock.md`.

- **10 s** (slot 365): `CGStorage::CheckRentalItemValidity`. **30 s** (slot 368): COS-only
  (silk pet / mercenary). **60 s** (slot 366): training-camp accounting (`AQ_TrainingCamp`,
  ops `0x3c86`/`0x3c87`) plus rent items in equip slots. **600 s** (slot 367): the clock.
- The clock: the server packs `GetLocalTime()` into 32 bits (year-16:6, month:4, day:5,
  hour:5, minute:6, second:6) and sends `0x34be`; the client's handler (`0x89a250`,
  registered in the opcode table beside `0x34aa`, `0x34d2`...) unpacks the same fields,
  `mktime`s them, seeds a millisecond clock (ms since the server-local week start) and
  advances it 1:1 with real time (`CGame::vslot_011`, published as seconds via the double
  `0.001` at `0xdd3020`), re-syncing every ten minutes with a 2000 ms drift reset. The scene
  command `S_SetWorldTime` locks it (`+0x931`); the console prints it as `ServerTime`.
- **Not read:** the sky/fog sampler's mapping from that clock onto the environment tables'
  0..1 axis -- its only located readers are the clock's own display and an alchemy timer.
  So no day/night cycle is wired; `ENVIRONMENT_REFERENCE_TIME`'s note, which said "no
  server-side game-time signal", now says the signal is read and names what is not.

No OpenSRO value changed. A `0x34be`-shaped sync is an additive op away once the mapping
is read.

## Two-hundred-and-twenty-third round: the PC tick is one second, read -- and it grounds three shipped units at once

The RE tick's step for 2026-09-19 08:49. Round 222 had parked the period of
`CGObjPC::vslot_415`. The repo's own `internal/mana` note held the mechanism (the regen job
is a TIMER registered with a vcall thunk and a `.rdata` interval); following it closes the
question and corrects two earlier rounds. Spec: `docs/protocol/character_state.md`.

### Read

- `CGObjChar::Create` (`0x4a6f40`) registers the character's periodic jobs on a timer
  vector at `this+0x18c` (0x18-byte nodes: elapsed, interval, callback), each callback the
  vcall thunk of a vtable slot. Slot 364 -- the job that calls `controller->slot11(pc)`,
  which is `CGObjPC::vslot_415` -- is registered three times with `fld1` = **1.0**. Beside
  it: slot 362 (regen) 4.0, slot 365 10.0, slot 368 30.0, slot 366 60.0, slot 367 600.0.
- The ticker `GObjPC::FUN_004ab690(dt)` adds dt to each node and fires the callback when
  it reaches the interval; it is called from `CGObjChar::Update(dt)` (slot 211, offset
  `0x34c`) -- the slot the main loop's fixed step `CMainProcess::FUN_00413b30` calls on
  every object, passing `_DAT_00d6a8ec`, the accumulator round 219 showed is in seconds.
- Therefore the intervals are seconds: `vslot_415` runs once per second; the battle
  stance reverts **20 s** after the last blow; berserk's float countdown (advanced 1.0 per
  `vslot_415` call) is **60 s**; regeneration ticks every **4 s**. Three shipped values whose
  unit was labelled "inferred" are read, and their code comments say so now.

### Corrected

Rounds 220 and 222 said slot 364 was dead because nothing referenced `0x4ac6b2`. That is
the thunk's `jmp`; the entry is `0x4ac6b0` (`mov eax,[ecx]` first), referenced three times.
The vcall-thunk search must take the entry. And the "parked" verdict of round 222 was
premature by one grep of the repo: the mechanism was already written down in
`internal/mana/mana.go` -- docs before dump, again.

No numeric value changed (20, 60, 4 were already shipped); labels and specs did.

The RE tick's step for 2026-09-19 08:19, on round 220's probe. A correction and a
